title: package_members: --out and --title default to the SHIPPED shelf, so a second-shelf push overwrites the first
description: Running 'package_members --roster comp/members2.roster' with no other flag writes the 2-member package into all_ours (the shipped root, rmtree'd first) and stamps it dataset-metadata id dimiturnt/kneemri-members. Pushing that put a 2-FILE version over the live 126-member shelf on 2026-09-07 02:06Z; every champion kernel mounts that dataset at its latest version. Restored by repackaging the full roster and pushing a version back (~10GB). The roster is the thing that decides WHICH shelf, so the destination and the title must be derived from it, or refused when they disagree: a roster whose name is not members.roster must not resolve to the shipped root by default.
close_reason: The roster declares its own shelf: RosterShelf reads a '# shelf:' / '# out:' header pair off the roster text, main derives destination and dataset id from it, and --out/--title survive only as flags that must AGREE. The incident invocation (package_members --roster comp/members2.roster --out .../all_ours) now raises 'contradicts the roster'. Both rosters carry headers; members_2 repackaged with two members and pushed; the 126-member shelf is restored and mount_check --live reads 108 ok, 0 refused.

title: Distilled fold-0 readings are leaky: OOF teachers trained on fold 0
description:
oof_fold_k (k=1..4) was fitted at --fold k, which trains on every OTHER fold, fold 0 included. Each teacher therefore memorised fold 0's labels. A student distilled from their targets on folds 1-4 and SCORED on fold 0 mimics four functions that carry fold 0 inside them: a label leak through function mimicry. The teacher never predicts fold 0 and does not have to.

WITNESSED BY THE BOARD, which is the un-leaked ruler. This family transfers offline->board at ~0.79 of the delta (spansolo 0.8545->0.921, holdsolo 0.8634->0.928). oof_teacher read 0.8681 offline, ABOVE holdsolo, and scored 0.926, BELOW it (ref 56065873). Pass-through 0.37 from the low anchor, negative from the high one.

AFFECTED: every *.holdout number produced under --teacher-targets teacher_oof_corpus.npz (and teacher_oof_full.npz, which is that file plus a fold-0 fill). Named: oof_teacher +0.0107, seat_distill_lr4e5 +0.0107 (0.8632). foreign_distill_mix07's 0.8656 uses a FOREIGN teacher - check whether its folds saw fold 0; if not, its +0.0061 is the cleanest distill term the project owns and the term is real at about half the claimed size.

FIX SHIPPED: --exclude-fold (ReportFolds.holdout's excluded), which drops a fold from TRAINING without putting it in the holdout. teacher_clean.sh refits the four twins with --exclude-fold 0; seat_clean_distill.sh re-reads the term against band_dense 0.8578 with the leak removed. Pre-reg >= 0.864 real / 0.860-0.864 knob / < 0.860 lever closes.

STILL OPEN: mark the affected ledger rows LEAKY (experiments/README.md); run the fold-0 sub-check (correlation of the student's fold-0 logits with the mean of the four teachers' IN-SAMPLE fold-0 logits, vs band_dense's correlation with the same) to witness the mechanism directly rather than by inference from the board.
notes: RESOLVED IN PART, 2026-09-07T03:20Z: the leak is REAL and it transferred ~ZERO AUC. seat_clean_distill (clean teachers, --exclude-fold 0) read 0.8634 peak e9, convergence_check clean, against its leaky twin seat_distill_lr4e5 0.8633 and the no-teacher control band_dense 0.8578. Removing the leak cost -0.0001, and it was NOT free to remove: the exclusion starves each teacher of ~900 of ~3500 studies and the four clean teachers priced -0.0067 mean on their own holdouts. So the clean student matched the leaky one out of a measurably weaker teacher set. Both the witness and the score are right: the student DID prefer the teachers that saw its holdout (+0.0127 diff-in-diff residual mimicry, control preferring the other set) and that preference bought no AUC. GENERAL SHAPE, worth more than the number: a leak visible in the RESIDUALS is not automatically a leak in the SCORE - the witness answers 'is it there', never 'is it the number', and only a re-run without it answers the second. CONSEQUENCE: seat_distill_lr4e5's +0.0107 is a treatment effect; retrain_six_distill (knee-ygi2k) is licensed and its kill switch did not fire; the five distilled members declined under the leak argument are ANSWERED rather than re-quoted (this reopens the TERM, not the seats - member axis stays closed on seven board flats). STILL OPEN: oof_teacher's 0.8681 and the oofsolo board inversion (0.926 from an offline read above holdsolo's 0.928) are a different corner and are NOT explained by this; the warning on that ledger row stands. seat_oof5_distill remains the only reading that prices the term at full teacher strength with the board as ruler. Ledger row + interpretation section written.

title: foreign_entry.SOURCE: one declaration read by both build_kit and kit_check
description: A foreign-fold entry declares its source in two places today, so a kit can be built from one spelling and checked against another. Make it a single SOURCE constant on foreign_entry that both build_kit and kit_check read, so a mismatch is impossible rather than merely caught.

title: A kit rebuild without --extra silently unships every foreign kernel
description: comp/build_kit.py copies extra files only when handed --extra <path>. The 18:18:55Z rebuild on 2026-09-06 omitted external/dinov3folds/bend_the_knee_to_dinov3_ensembled.py, so kneemri-foreignsolo died with FileNotFoundError: no their serving program, carried in our kit under /kaggle/input. Every foreign kernel mounts that same file through foreign_entry.mounts.one(SOURCE), so kneemri-foreignlogit (the registered 21:41Z fallback) was equally dead and would have spent a slot to discover it. Fixed by rebuilding with the flag and pushing a kit version at 20:19:48Z. The defect class: a kernel dependency declared in a hand-typed build flag, invisible to kit_check and to the kernel that needs it. Fix is for foreign_entry.SOURCE to be the single declaration, read by build_kit AND by kit_check, so a kit that cannot serve a foreign kernel refuses to push.

title: Every axis closed on a board FLAT may be UNRESOLVED, not closed - the public LB is ~400 studies
description: mastermind steer 13, 07:04Z. The public leaderboard is ~30 percent of 1,322 hidden studies = ~400 image-read studies. A board delta therefore carries a sampling half-width of its own, and the seat swaps the seven flats tested were priced OFFLINE at 0.001-0.003. If the board half-width at n=400 exceeds those deltas, the flats did not close their axes - they said the axes sit below the board's resolution, which is a different sentence and licenses different work. Axes closed on a board flat, from comp/board.jsonl: (1) seventh seat inert - sevengrade 0.931 vs sixfresh 0.931, reproduced by four later entries; (2) count 6 to 7 - dark7 0.937 vs dark6 0.937; (3) encoder FAMILY at seat seven - v3seat 0.936 vs two matched 0.937 controls; (4) member TYPE/regularisation - augseat 0.936 vs lastseat 0.937; (5) vote rule - votefit 0.938 vs dark6 0.937, one tick; (6) serving views/jitter - jitterfit 0.937 vs 0.937; (7) kit refresh - sixfresh_v2 0.931 identical to v1; (8) ordinal separation - accumseat 0.933 tie; (9) count with redundancy held high - sixstrong 0.930 vs sixfresh 0.931. Note (8) cross-family diversity via farseat is ALREADY void for a different reason (a member never loaded). Board scores are quantised to 0.001, so even a real 0.0005 effect is unreadable by construction. Instrument: kneemri.evaluation.paired_floor gives the paired bootstrap width; scale to n=400. Consequence already accepted by mastermind for slot policy: a slot is only spent on a candidate whose offline delta EXCEEDS the board half-width - reseatings and one-member swaps never qualify again.
notes: 2026-09-06 ANSWERED. Board resolution for a one-seat swap: 95% half-width 0.0011 at ~400 public studies (0.0007 at our 909), plus a 0.0005 rounding floor from three published decimals. Table of all nine flat-closed axes in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_board-flats-below-the-boards-resolution.md. Outcome: FOUR axes carry offline numbers and all four read under 0.0011 (closed on both rulers); FIVE are --fold -1 with offline:null and were closed on the only ruler that cannot resolve them (UNREAD, not closed). Nothing clears the pre-registered +0.003 reopen bar, so no stacking entry exists. What it licenses: no slot to a one-seat swap in either direction - a flat and a 0.001 win are equally uninformative.

title: Our holdout and the board disagree by 0.17 AUC on the only column both have measured
description: colmcl fixes MCL's board AUC at 0.980 (interval 0.968-0.992). Our 909-study fold-0 holdout scores the SAME ensemble's MCL column at 0.8104, the worst of our twelve. Same weights, same findings, 0.17 apart, and on the board it is nearly the best column while for us it is the worst. That 0.17 on one column is 0.014 of board, which is LARGER than the 0.009 gap to first place. Every seating decision this project has made - eight member declines, seven board flats, the honest12 baseline, seat_value's DISTINCT/SCALED/NOISY verdicts, the per-column headroom map that aimed the whole per-label lane - was made on that holdout. Four candidate mechanisms: label noise as TEST truth (our lexicon over-calls 108 FP to 32 misses per overcall_audit), prevalence variance (171/909 positives), case mix in the hidden test, or a definitional mismatch between our lexicon's MCL and the competition's. THE LOAD-BEARING SUB-QUESTION is whether a shared bias cancels in a PAIRED comparison between two members - my instinct is yes and the ordering survives, which is the only reason the seating decisions still stand, but that instinct is unverified and if it is wrong then eight declines and seven flats need re-reading. colbaker (Baker's, our strongest column at 0.9208) ships 04:56Z and colhalf (six-column set) ~09:32Z, giving a second and third point, but three of twelve will not give the shape. Put to Kimi as Q-RULER1-4 in .agent-runtime/inbox/20260905T0140Z-claude-ruler-disagreement.md.
notes:
DAWID-SKENE LATENT TRUTH PROPOSED AND CLOSED WITHOUT BUILDING IT (Kimi Q-RULER3, 2026-09-05T0143Z; audited and closed 0250Z). Kimi proposed treating the 58-study four-reader panel as a multi-annotator inference problem - Dawid-Skene EM for per-reader error rates and a latent true label per study - then scoring the model's MCL AUC against that latent truth, to test whether label noise or case mix drives the 0.17 board/holdout disagreement. The method is right and the panel cannot hear it.

core.data.labels.table_blend and kneemri.evaluation.table_separation already ran the experiment this proposal is a member of. Four blends of the same reader panel - the shipped one, the weakest reader dropped, a fourth reader added, and ours plus the single strongest reader - span 0.8894 to 0.8931 and EVERY pairwise interval among them covers zero, while the readers themselves separate cleanly (ours 0.8658, best foreign 0.8991, weakest 0.8352, all resolvably apart). The recorded conclusion: on 58 studies this ruler resolves about +/-0.008, and every blend recipe lives inside that; a better label table has to come from a better READER, not from a new weighting of the readers already here.

Dawid-Skene IS a new weighting of the readers already here - better motivated than a mean, per-reader error rates rather than equal votes, but inside the same +/-0.008 box. And the quantity it would feed is a per-column MCL AUC over roughly 18 panel positives, where Kimi's own Hanley-McNeil figure is SE 0.08-0.10. Both ends of the chain are wider than the effect being estimated.

So the 0.17 stays unexplained offline and that is now a closure rather than a to-do: Q-RULER5 established that case mix and definitional mismatch make identical offline predictions and cannot be separated without board labels or board cases, and this closes the remaining offline instrument. A per-column board map costs one slot per column, or group ablations under the sparsity assumption colhalf tests. What survives unchanged: label noise is the leading explanation with measured support, and paired member comparisons remain safer than absolute AUCs but are not immune where members differ in SUPERVISION - which is exactly the errors_* family.

title: MCL board AUC is 0.980 - the offline per-column map failed its only external check
description: colmcl (ref 56020054) read 0.904 against the champion's 0.944, outside all three pre-registered bands (0.918-0.928 expected). With colnull having fixed the metric as a plain unweighted mean of twelve per-column AUCs, MCL board AUC = (0.944-0.904)x12+0.5 = 0.980, rounding interval 0.968-0.992. That is 96 percent of the largest drop one column can produce. Harness checked first: run_check reads loaded 6 of 6 members, the scored submission carries exactly the twelve TARGETS columns with MCL at one unique value, and the kernel's chosen tuple and FOREIGN_WEIGHT are byte-identical to the champion's. CONSEQUENCE: MCL is our WORST column offline (0.8104, seven-member fold-0 rank pool) and very nearly our BEST on the board. The map does not transfer in LEVEL (board columns average 0.944 vs the pool's 0.8715) and on the one column with an external read it does not transfer in ORDERING either - it inverts. The +0.0196 bottom-three headroom in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-05 is priced on that map and must not be planned against. It also says WHERE the defect is: the model separates MCL almost perfectly against board labels, so the 0.8104 is our SUPERVISION - matching the 50.0 percent radiologist agreement that makes MCL the second-worst-labelled column we own.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-05T13:15Z. The label-noise explanation for MCL is REFUTED by our own module. supervision_gap scores the report label ITSELF as a predictor of the radiologist on the 58 annotated studies: MCL reads 0.9762, the SECOND BEST of twelve. Our MCL labels are among the cleanest we own, not the noisiest. The 50 percent agreement figure I argued from is a THRESHOLD statistic (v2 calls MCL positive 18 times where gold calls it 9, a two-to-one overcall) and AUC reads the RANKING, which the graded reader gets almost right. Denominator checked: MCL corpus positive rate 17.4 percent (767 of 4406), gold set 15.5 percent (9 of 58), so the gold set is not enriched and the 909-study read is not thin-positive noise. What is left: labels clean, model reads 0.8104 on our holdout and 0.980 on the board, and supervision_gap puts MCL on the MODEL-BOUND side at -0.0964. The only story fitting all three is that the board MCL column is a different and easier task - case mix or a definitional mismatch. Q-RULER5 listed that as the alternative; it is now the leading explanation. Written up in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-05_the-offline-column-map-ranks-our-labels-not-our-model.md, which keeps the wrong paragraph standing with the correction under it.

title: Per-label axis is priced: bottom three columns hold ~0.02 of board
description: colnull read exactly 0.500, so the board metric is a plain unweighted mean of twelve per-column AUCs. A column gaining d moves the board by d/12. The seven-member fold-0 rank pool reads MCL 0.8104, Fracture 0.8255, Lateral OA 0.8309 against a 0.8715 mean and a 0.9208 best. Bringing those three to 0.90 is +0.0196 board, above the 1.5 percent bar. Every ensemble operation moves all twelve columns together and has flattened seven times; this axis moves three and has never been tried. Blocked on choosing a mechanism - see the letter to Kimi 20260905T0005Z-claude-weak-column-lift. Offline map is scored on our supervision, so it gives ORDERING; colmcl (ref 56020054, scoring) gives the board-truth level for MCL.
notes: REFUTED 2026-09-05 by colmcl_v1 (ref 56020054) and colbaker_v1 (ref 56023244). The bead prices bringing MCL 0.8104, Fracture 0.8255, Lateral OA 0.8309 to 0.90 as +0.0196 of board. MCL now has an external read: its BOARD AUC is 0.980, not 0.81. Our worst offline column is nearly solved on the board, so the offline map ranks OUR SUPERVISION and not the model, and the bottom-three headroom does not exist as priced. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-05_the-offline-column-map-ranks-our-labels-not-our-model.md. Do NOT spend card on a weak-column lift chosen from the offline map. The axis it hands off to is knee-wko44 (the labeler), because label noise is what the two column reads measure.

title: THE LABELER AXIS: our labels are Wollek's 0.858 rule-based row, and the learned-labeler row is 0.939
description:
A NEW AXIS, which is what knee-m69u asks for, and the first one this week with a published number an order of magnitude above the 0.0062 holdout floor.

THE PUBLISHED RESULT. Wollek et al., 'Automated Labeling of German Chest X-Ray Radiology Reports using Deep Learning' (arXiv:2306.05997, Fortschr Roentgenstr 2024), found by Kimi as A-QEC and written up in research/2026-09-04_qec-parser-vs-label-noise.md. They train the SAME DenseNet-121 on the SAME internal chest X-ray dataset and change only the LABELER: public ChestX-ray14 labels 0.720, rule-based CheXpert-style labeler 0.858, DL-based labeler (German BERT trained on rule-based plus manual labels) 0.939, manual radiologist labels 0.934. The learned labeler beats the rule-based parser by +0.081 downstream AUC and passes the manual-label control.

WHY IT LANDS ON US. report_reader is a lexicon parser, so this project's supervision IS that 0.858 row. Every label arm queued today - errors_dense (prune the flagged cells, knee-teh4) and its pair knee-f8hv5 (re-label them to the pool's held-out posterior) - trains AROUND the parser's errors. This axis fixes them at the source, which is the difference between the two columns of Wollek's own table. It also matches the error PATTERN the project already measured: the Q-AB taxonomy (interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-02_what-label-correction-is-actually-worth.md) finds CONSTRUCTION errors - hedged negation, severity thresholds, BME to contusion - which is exactly what a parser targets and exactly what a noise-robust loss cannot see.

WHAT MAKES IT CHEAP, AND IT IS THE BEST PROPERTY IT HAS. The axis is measurable at ZERO card and ZERO slots. 58 studies carry radiologist annotation, so a candidate labeler is scored against radiologist truth directly, per finding and pooled, beside v2's own row - no training run has to happen to learn whether the labels got better. Only a labeler that WINS that reading ever costs a card hour.

THE BLOCKER, AND IT IS PLUMBING RATHER THAN SCIENCE. knee-8hyr6 (P0, open since 2026-09-03, Kimi's tree and Kimi's run): the Qwen3.8 candidate table has 687 of 696 cells at UNK (98.7%) against v2's 177 of 684 (25.9%) on the same studies, and per finding exactly ONE study carries a non-UNK verdict. The vocabulary it does emit is correct, so ReadingPrompt and ReportReading.parse work when handed a response - the endpoint returned nothing 57 times. Scored as-is it would read as 'the LLM is a far worse reader' and retire this axis on a measurement that never happened. Sent to Kimi as T-ED 2026-09-04T1543Z with the three hypotheses ranked (truncation with finish_reason == length, checkable by the prediction that the one study that succeeded has the shortest answer; swallowed per-request exceptions; a model alias returning an error object under HTTP 200), plus the denominator trap: the candidate has 58 studies and v2 has 57 of them, so score on the intersection.

WHAT THIS IS NOT, AND THE HONEST LIMIT. A-QEC also returned an honest null on the comparison I actually asked for: no published head-to-head exists where a parser repair is measured against an off-the-shelf label-noise method on the same corpus. So this axis is not established as BETTER than knee-teh4's, only as having a much larger published effect on its own. Wollek is chest X-ray, single-label pneumothorax, German reports; ours is knee MRI, twelve labels, English. The +0.081 is a mechanism floor, not our expected gain, and it must never be quoted as our number. Board transfer is UNKNOWN.

PRICE: the gold-58 reading costs no card and no slot. Only if a candidate labeler beats v2 against radiologist truth does a training arm follow, and that arm is ~4 h. P(a fixed endpoint produces a labeler that beats v2 on the gold 58) is genuinely unknown - the one attempt so far never ran. That is why the first step is a plumbing fix and a non-UNK-rate census, not a score.

Blocked on: knee-8hyr6.
notes: ARMED 2026-09-07 02:55Z: compose_v4b_clean.sh - the MIDDLE rule's own successor test ('the label axis composes with distillation or it is not worth a seat'), with the leaky teacher replaced by teacher_clean. One variable off labels_v4hybrid.sh: --distill-weight 0.7 --teacher-targets teacher_clean.npz. Matched control labels_v4hybrid_s2026 (v2 holdout 0.8524, gold 58 0.9063), both on disk. THE MECHANISM UNDER TEST is teacher PROVENANCE: every teacher block was fitted on v2, so a v4b student pulled toward them is pulled back toward the errors the table swap removed. Additive => the distill term is about images; cancels => it was mostly 'agree with v2 more'. The two predictions differ in sign, which is why a knob-sized delta is worth 1.2 h here. Queued behind seat_oof5_distill via experiments/after_compose.sh; costs zero slots. Kimi asked Q-PROVENANCE (02:55Z) for the published sign of the same interaction.

title: Encoder can load ZERO pretrained tensors and train silently — radiodino_corpus burned 62min of card on a random-init ViT
description: radiodino_corpus_s2026 ran 3 epochs (0.6501/0.6714/0.6813) with a RANDOMLY INITIALISED trunk. Its log reads 'Loading weights: 0it' and a ViTModel LOAD REPORT where every checkpoint key is UNEXPECTED and every model key is MISSING: Snarcy/RadioDino-b16 ships timm names (blocks.*, patch_embed, cls_token, pos_embed), transformers ViTModel wants HF names (layers.*, embeddings.*). Nothing refused. The arm pre-registers four outcomes about medical-corpus pretraining; all four are unreadable, and REFUTES (<0.80) would have blamed the corpus for a loader bug and retired MRI-CORE on it. Killed at 10:29Z. Denominator: of 232 run logs, 15 print a LOAD REPORT and exactly 1 reads 0it — this instance only. But a PARTIAL load is silent too, and medsam prints no report at all. FIX: refuse at load time, like run_setup.py:397 refuses --batch 1 with a nonzero ranking term. A --variant naming a pretrained checkpoint that matches zero (or few) of its keys must ABORT, not train.
notes:
SWEEP RUN 2026-09-04T11:07Z, CLEAN. python -m kneemri.models.load_check over the whole registry: 16 entries, every declared dim equal to the loaded trunk's own hidden_size, no refusals. radiodinob16 now reads 768 through TimmHubWeights. So RadioDino was the ONLY entry ever handing a run a randomly-initialised trunk — the question a single fixed entry cannot answer.

Shipped as ea12b3e7 (gates green, pushed): the gate (Encoder.refuse_unloaded at the seam both hub loaders pass through, exact via output_loading_info), the fix (kneemri/models/timm_trunk.py), the sweep (kneemri/models/load_check.py, by hand because it fetches every trunk).

Kimi Q-DO then read the actual weight keys of every remaining candidate: RadioDino s16 (vit_small_patch16_224, 384) and s8 (vit_small_patch8_224, 384) carry the SAME fault and load through TimmHubWeights unchanged; BiomedCLIP is timm-keyed nested under visual.trunk. and needs a subtree strip; RadImageNet is torchvision-keyed and our StateDictWeights row already loads it strict=True so it cannot under-load; MRI-CORE is not on HF at all.
close_reason: Gate, fix and registry sweep all shipped in ea12b3e7 (gates green, pushed): Encoder.refuse_unloaded aborts at the seam both hub loaders pass through, using output_loading_info so the check is exact rather than heuristic; kneemri/models/timm_trunk.py carries the fix; kneemri/models/load_check.py swept all 16 registry entries with no refusals and every declared dim equal to the loaded trunk's hidden_size. RadioDino was the only entry that ever handed a run a randomly-initialised trunk. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE, recorded here because it is the part that outlives the bug: radiodino_corpus's three epochs are VOID rather than negative - all four of its pre-registered outcomes were unreadable, and REFUTES would have retired MRI-CORE on a loader bug. The arm is re-runnable and stays queued behind errors_dense.

title: arm_check EXECUTES every arm script, so seven no-run_train arms (three on the GPU) run for up to 30s on every pre-flight
description: arm_check harvests each arm's flags by RUNNING the script against a stub lib (arm_check.py:196, [[str(arm)] for arm in sorted(self.arms.glob('*.sh'))]). The stub shadows run_train, so a normal arm prints its flags and does no work. after_ortho_encode.sh is not a normal arm: line 9 is 'timeout 21600 .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m kneemri.embeddings.build_ortho_embeddings --batch 4', a real command outside run_train, so the stub neutralises nothing and arm_check launches a six-hour GPU job. --only filters AFTER the harvest, so it does not prevent it. Observed twice on 2026-09-04 within twenty minutes: pids 25956 and 10020, each appearing on the card seconds after an 'arm_check --only band_pairmem', each contending with the live radiodino_corpus arm, each killed by hand after card_check reported OVERSUBSCRIBED. The pre-flight that exists to save card time spends it, and it does so silently - arm_check's own output says nothing about having started anything. This also means every arm_check run since after_ortho_encode.sh was added has been racing whatever held the card, and any timing read during one is suspect. TWO FIXES, not exclusive: (a) the stub should neutralise or refuse a script that invokes anything outside run_train, since executing arbitrary commands to read a declaration is the wrong mechanism - parse the invocation instead of running it, or run under a PATH where python is a no-op; (b) after_ortho_encode.sh is a DRIVER, not an arm, and does not belong in experiments/arms - it has no run_train call, no pre-registration and no reading, so nothing in the arms contract fits it.
notes:
REOPENED 2026-09-04 — the close was wrong and the defect was real.

The close rested on: 'exactly one arm names .venv/Scripts/python.exe directly (after_ortho_encode.sh) and it runs set -u against ${1}, so invoked bare it aborts before the line'. It does not abort. The expansion is inside a pipeline, so set -u kills the SUBSHELL and leaves the script running; tasklist then fails, the leading ! turns that failure into true, and the until loop exits on its first iteration straight into a six-hour build_ortho_embeddings.

Reproduced by running the file bare with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 and a 6 s timeout — exactly how invocations() runs it. Output: two 'line 7: 1: unbound variable' lines, then 'starting ortho encode', then 'loaded 3 plane denoisers', then 'encoding 4407 studies'. The encode was live within six seconds.

Cost, twice: a six-hour timeout-wrapped build on a card a live arm held. On 2026-09-04 it halved medsam_dense from 508 to 280 img/s and was six seconds behind an arm_check call, which is what finally attributed it.

FIXED in 33814d68 — explicit [ $# -ge 1 ] guard in the shell, and the watcher moved to experiments/ so the arms/*.sh glob no longer reaches it. The invariant to check on any new arm: nothing under arms/ may reach an interpreter without going through uv, because stub_lib.sh's no-op uv is the only thing making this lint inert.

title: The offline-to-board slope has never been fitted outside the DINOv2 family, and ortho_solo cannot fix that alone
description:
ortho_solo_v1 (ref 55994354) put the project's first non-DINOv2 point on the board: ortho_dense_s2026 alone, honest fold-0, offline 0.8452 -> board 0.907. board_transfer prices EVERY arm here, and every pair fitting it comes from a DINOv2-family trunk.

The point cannot be read yet and the row in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md says so. 0.907 against soloseat_v1 0.925 / calibsolo 0.923 / raptor_solo 0.923 is NOT a measured family penalty: all three are --fold -1 and saw every holdout study. The only honest-offline solo in the record is solo_v1 (0.8518 -> 0.868), 2026-08-12, a different kit and decode.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT A READING: two current-kit DINOv2 solos served alone at --fold 0, at separated offlines, giving the in-family solo line; the ortho point then sits on it or under it. Candidates already on disk with honest fold-0 records: calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634, small_batch6_s2026 0.8598, through_dense_s2026 0.8558, calib_span_s2026 0.8545 (record_mix, 2026-09-03). Two of those span 0.0089 offline, which is above the holdout's 0.0053 resolution floor.

COST: two slots, zero card. GATE IT ON ortho_stack: if the continued ViT-L does not clear band_dense the family may be dead anyway and the slope question is academic.
notes:
RAISED P1->P0 2026-09-04. The scope defect that hid this is fixed: four board.jsonl rows carried scope='included', a value in neither reader's vocabulary — green in board_check (which only tests != EXCLUDED), silently dropped by board_transfer (which fits == 'ensemble'). Corrected to 'ensemble': the fit goes 34 entries/436 pairs -> 37/530. Planning constant UNCHANGED (+0.97 at >=0.8678).

WHAT CHANGED IS THE INVERSIONS. Resolved-pair inversions went 0/276 -> 2/342, and BOTH have ortho_solo_v1 on one side (solo_v1 holdout +0.0066 board -0.039; onedecode_v2 holdout +0.0101 board -0.003). ortho_solo carries the LOWEST offline of all 37 (0.8452) and read 0.907 — about +0.02 board above where the DINOv2-fitted slope puts it.

ONE observation, not two, and the confound is TOTAL: offline level and date are collinear in this record (every low-offline entry is 08-12..08-24, every late entry is high-offline), so 'ortholarge transfers better than its holdout says' and 'the current kit transfers better than the August kits' predict the same thing. This bead's instrument — two CURRENT-KIT DINOv2 solos at --fold 0 at separated offlines — is the only thing that breaks that collinearity. It was speculative when filed; there is now a candidate effect worth +0.02 board on the table. Two slots, zero card.

IT ALSO TOUCHES ortho_stack, on the card now: its middle pre-registered branch (within 0.0062 of band_dense = close the in-domain trunk lane) assumes offline order transfers, which for this trunk family is the thing in question. Branch NOT moved — annotated as conditional on this instrument coming back null. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_the-ruler-had-four-rows-outside-it.md
close_reason: Both anchors scored and both are >=0.900: spansolo_v1 0.921 at offline 0.8545, holdsolo_v1 0.928 at 0.8634. That is the pre-registered branch — the KIT ERA explains ortho_solo_v1's +0.02, ortholarge is not special, and board_transfer's whole-record slope is era-contaminated and needs refitting within era. Reading in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_kit-era-not-ortholarge.md; both rows in comp/board.jsonl.

title: --batch 1 silently switches the ranking term OFF; ortho_stack ran 3 epochs void
description:
RankedObjective.ranking forms pairs WITHIN the micro-batch via pairs(batch, batch), and self-pairs drop out (objective.py:317-324, 346-349). At --batch 1 no pair forms, so the term contributes exactly zero. --accumulate does not repair it: it sums gradients of micro-batch losses each computed alone.

MEASURED, not argued. ortho_stack void run: step-80 loss 0.6785. Same arm with --pair-memory 66: 1.3774. Control band_dense (batch 12, term on): 1.3598 at step 29. The halved loss WAS the missing term.

WHY IT SURVIVED THE GUARDS. Objective.settings() reports the CONSTRUCTOR's weight, so the recipe line records rank_weight 1.0 whether or not a pair ever formed. objective.py:159-161 warns about precisely this failure mode ('a --rank-weight that never reached the constructor trains plain cross-entropy under a ranking arm name and reports a number that reads as a refutation of the mechanism') but only covers flag dispatch, not batch size.

COST. ortho_stack reached epoch 2 at 0.8010 vs band_dense 0.8197 and was killed there. Its middle branch CLOSES the in-domain trunk lane - the only open lever - and it would have closed it against a control training a different objective. v3large_stack was queued with the same defect.

FIXED in both arms with --pair-memory 66, derived: band_dense at batch 12 forms C(12,2)=66 pairs a label, so M=66 matches the pair mass; staleness is lower both in optimiser steps (5.5 vs 8) and epoch share (1.9% vs 2.7%).

STILL OPEN, and this is the actual bug to fix: nothing REFUSES a rank-weight arm at batch 1 with pair_memory 0. arm_check or run_setup should raise, the way run_setup already raises for --pair-memory without --rank-weight. Until then any low-batch arm can repeat this. Audit other arms in the ledger that combine --rank-weight with a small --batch.
close_reason: Guard landed (run_setup._check_pairs_can_form, raises before the card, names all four silenced flags). The AUDIT this bead asked for is done and split out: sixteen arms across the ConvNeXt, Swin, RadImageNet and raptor-feature families ran --batch 1 with no --pair-memory, so every one trained plain cross-entropy under a ranking arm's name. See the new P0.

title: rampsix pre-registered two readings and can produce neither - every refit is fold -1 dark
description: rampsix ran on 2026-09-02 (final_ws_ramp 20:18, through_dense_ramp 22:03, grade_ladder_ramp died 23:47 with no .pt) and was never written into experiments/README.md. Both finished members log auc: nan on all 12 epochs because the arm sets FIT='--fold -1 --ema', so there is no holdout. Its gate - 'the first two members must each clear +0.002 solo over their calibsix originals or the remaining three are not run' - is not merely unrun, it is unreadable by construction. So is its second reading: the offline ensemble over the champion's six contains five dark members, so every holdout study is in-sample for part of the pool and the number is null by construction, the same way corpusdose_v1 and corpusfull_v1 were unscoreable. A board slot was explicitly NOT pre-committed, which leaves the arm with no ruler at all. This is a live instance of knee-v78o1. The fix is not to add a fold - folds are banned - it is that an arm whose members are dark must pre-register a BOARD reading or declare itself unmeasurable before it spends 4.2h of card.

title: board_transfer slope quoted as +1.55 from prose; the tool says +1.25/+0.97/+0.71 and it inverted a verdict
description:
THE DEFECT. Every recent pre-registration, kernel docstring and board row prices arms with a board_transfer slope of +1.55 board points per holdout point. The tool has never said that. Run 2026-09-03 15:05Z with holdfive_v1 in the record, python -m kneemri.evaluation.board_transfer reports:

  compression: median +1.25 over the WHOLE record -- and the tool itself labels this 'the wrong number to price an arm with'
    among entries at or above 0.8678:  13 resolved pairs, median +0.97  [+0.94, +1.17]
    among entries at or above 0.8694:   3 resolved pairs, median +0.71  [+0.70, +0.89]

CLAUDE.md already records that this constant has been quoted wrong from prose twice. This is the third, and the first time it changed a conclusion.

WHAT IT INVERTED. holdfive_v1 pre-registered four bands against +1.55, which predicted 0.938-0.939. It scored 0.936, landing in the band labelled 'the offline gain does not survive to the board' -- and that verdict was written into comp/SUBMISSIONS.md and comp/board.jsonl. But holdfive's pool sits at offline 0.8729, inside the >= 0.8694 band where the fitted slope is +0.71. Its +0.0023 offline gap therefore predicts +0.0016 board = 0.9366. It scored 0.936. The gain transferred EXACTLY as the record says it must. The row has been corrected in place rather than rewritten, so both readings and the reason for the change stay visible.

THE REAL FINDING, WHICH IS BIGGER THAN THE ENTRY. Compression is not a constant. It is a decreasing function of where the pool already sits: +1.25 whole-record, +0.97 above 0.8678, +0.71 above 0.8694. Every arm this project priced with one number was priced at the exchange rate for a weaker pool than the one it would actually join, and the error grows as the pool improves -- i.e. exactly where the pricing matters most.

THE BAR IT SETS. BOARD_RESOLVABLE is 0.0015. At +0.71 an offline gain must exceed 0.0021 before it can move the board one resolvable quantum. So the 0.0005 hold-annotations term, the 0.0018 calibration term and the +0.0006 LogitAverage margin over flat are all PROVABLY under the board's resolution at this pool's position, not merely close to it. The owner's 1.5% bar would need ~0.021 offline -- two points of holdout AUC, which no knob or seating in this project has ever produced.

CORROBORATION. All 10 board-order inversions in the record are pairs the holdout left UNRESOLVED (gaps 0.0020-0.0037, under its own 0.0053 floor). 0 of the 276 pairs the holdout DID resolve were inverted by the board. The ruler is sound; it was being read below its resolution.

WHAT TO DO. (1) Grep every kernel docstring, interpretation and bead for 1.55 and correct or annotate each. (2) Any pre-registration that names a slope must READ it from the tool at write time and quote the banded value for the pool's own offline position, never a remembered scalar -- the same rule board_read already enforces for the leaderboard gap. (3) Consider having board_transfer refuse to report a single scalar, or print the banded table only, since the scalar is what keeps getting carried off.
design: Correction to the note above: one backtick pair was executed by the shell, so the sentence about the two-pair band lost a word. It should read: 'BoardTransfer.spread bootstraps whatever it is handed, so resampling two numbers reported a [+0.71, +0.89] interval that reads as a fit and is a restatement of its own input.'
notes:
2026-09-04 02:10Z. Items (1) and (3) done, (2) is now mechanical rather than a rule people must remember.

(3) BUILT THE GATE. board_transfer.PRICEABLE = 5 and BoardTransfer.priced(). Any cell holding fewer than five resolved pairs now prints ' - DIRECTION ONLY, too few pairs to price an arm with' inside its own line, at both cell sites (the regime table and --near). Live output today:

    among entries at or above 0.8678: 13 resolved pairs, median +0.97 [+0.94, +1.17]
    among entries at or above 0.8695: 2 resolved pairs, median +0.80 [+0.71, +0.89] - DIRECTION ONLY, too few pairs to price an arm with

That second line is the one that mattered: the top band the bead quotes as +0.71 now holds TWO pairs, and  bootstraps whatever it is handed, so resampling two numbers reported a [+0.71, +0.89] interval that reads as a fit and is a restatement of its own input. Committed aa65f625, pushed.

(1) THE 1.55 SITES, SORTED. Nineteen hits. Sixteen are HISTORY and stay: comp/SUBMISSIONS.md, the dated interpretations, kneemri-holdfive's docstring (which already says the constant was carried from prose), board_claims/claims_check (which name it as the defect). Rewriting those would destroy the record of the error. ONE was live and is annotated in place: experiments/arms/rampgate.sh line 25 priced a branch at '+0.004-0.008 offline x board transfer 1.55 = +0.006-0.012'; at the real +0.97 the same branch is +0.004-0.008 board, about two thirds. The annotation says do NOT repair it by editing the number - run the tool with --near at write time.

(2) The tool already had --near and already labels the whole-record median wrong in its own output. Added a docstring paragraph stating that EVERY number in the docstring is history and quoting one is the bug, with holdfive's inverted verdict as the worked example.

THE ANCHOR PROBLEM, FOUND WHILE DOING THIS AND BIGGER THAN THE ITEM LIST. I tried to re-price the owner's 0.953 target off the champion and could not: raptorweight_v1 carries offline: null, because six of its seven seats are --fold -1 and the row says so - 'no offline number exists or can exist for this pool'. THE PINNED CHAMPION CANNOT BE PRICED OFFLINE. So no 'how far is 0.953' arithmetic can be anchored on it, and any that appears to be is anchored on something else without saying so.

The only honest anchor is the best entry carrying BOTH numbers: holdfive_v1, offline 0.8729, board 0.936. To 0.953 is +0.017 board, and at the shipping band's +0.97 that is +0.0175 offline, target ~0.890. The remembered ~0.891 was correct - but it was correct by an anchor nobody had written down, which is the same failure mode as the constant itself. Recorded here so the next re-pricing does not have to rediscover that the champion has no offline number.
close_reason:
All three items landed and are committed: (1) the nineteen 1.55 sites sorted, sixteen kept as history and the one live site annotated in place; (2) the tool's docstring now states that every number in it is history and that quoting one IS the bug; (3) board_transfer.PRICEABLE=5 gates any cell with too few resolved pairs to price an arm with, which is what caught the top band being two pairs bootstrapped into an interval that read as a fit.

The anchor finding is carried forward rather than closed with this: the pinned champion has offline null (six of seven seats at fold -1), so no 0.953 arithmetic can be anchored on it. The only honest anchor is holdfive_v1 at offline 0.8729 / board 0.936, and at the shipping band's +0.97 the target is offline ~0.890.

title: Qwen3.8 candidate table is a failed run: 57 of 58 studies parsed nothing
description:
'.agent-runtime/scratch/report_labels_qwen38_annotated.csv' has 687 of 696 cells at verdict UNK (98.7%) against v2's 177 of 684 (25.9%) on the same studies. Per finding exactly ONE study carries a non-UNK verdict, and the same study is the only non-UNK on nine of twelve findings. The values it does emit are the correct vocabulary (0.08/0.28/0.82 at conf 0.85/0.95), so ReadingPrompt and ReportReading.parse work when handed a response - the endpoint returned nothing 57 times.

Scoring this through reader_upgrade or reader_agreement would have read as 'the endpoint is a far worse reader' and written off the axis on a measurement that never happened. Faulty PLUMBING, not a refutation.

Leading hypothesis: max_tokens ~320 against a twelve-finding JSON truncates, and a truncated JSON parses to nothing which falls back to UNK silently. Check finish_reason == 'length' on a failing request; the prediction is that the one study that succeeded has the shortest answer. Second: per-request exceptions swallowed into the UNK default. Third: model alias returning an error object with HTTP 200.

Also: the candidate has 58 studies, v2 has 57 of them - one candidate study is absent from v2.

Sent to Kimi as a P0 letter 20260903T1136Z (their tree, their run - not edited). Related: knee-pnwar.
close_reason: Resolved. The endpoint run was fixed by setting chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking: False} and max_tokens=4096. The output file now contains 58 studies with 30.2% UNK verdicts (210/696 cells), not 98.7%. Full result documented in research/2026-09-03_qwen38_reader_gate_result.md.

title: An arm's SECOND pre-registered reading can silently never be taken: recal_dense sat 4 days with its deciding number missing
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03. recal_dense.sh (knee-qxyj) pre-registers on GOLD FIRST and says so explicitly: 'PRE-REGISTERED, on GOLD first, because the proxy truth IS the report table and is biased against label-side movement.' Its three branches - REPLICATES / CORNER / COSTS - are all defined on the gold delta against band_dense_hold. The proxy is the secondary number.

The arm RAN. recal_dense_s2026 is on disk, converged, proxy 0.8610, on the roster at line 543. And the gold reading its own header names - a separate command, kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap - was NEVER RUN. recal_dense is absent from processed/.../annotated_predictions/, which holds 14 arrays over 8 checkpoints and not this one. So the arm's DECIDING number does not exist and its branch was never selected, while every gate reads green: the ledger has a row, convergence_check passes, roster_check passes, the member is packaged.

THE HOLE IS STRUCTURAL, not a lapse. A reading that lives in the arm's PROSE and requires a second command has nothing asserting it happened. ledger_check verifies a run reached the ledger; nothing verifies the ledger row answers the question the arm was armed to ask. The same shape is live for every arm whose header names a follow-up command - annotated_readings, supervision_gap, per-label reads.

PROPOSED CHECK, in the family of roster_check and convergence_check: an arm header declares its readings in a parseable line (the arms already carry 'deliberate:' and 'bead:' lines, so the convention exists), and the check asserts each declared reading has an artefact on disk for that run. Anything declared and missing is the defect. It guards a QUESTION rather than a shipment or a number, which is the one thing the fifteen checks do not currently cover.

The missing reading is being taken now (CPU, no card). Whatever it says, the check is the finding.
notes:
THE GOLD RULER HAS A FLOOR AND IT IS ~+/-0.015. I quoted deltas against it before measuring it, and that was wrong.

annotated_readings --against calib_dense_hold_s2026, paired 95% interval over the 58 studies:

  stackfit_s2026            +0.0101  [-0.0044, +0.0252]   spans zero
  labelwise_dense_s2026     +0.0054  [-0.0113, +0.0222]   spans zero
  recal_dense_s2026         +0.0011  [-0.0121, +0.0122]   spans zero
  stack_increments_s2026    +0.0005  [-0.0115, +0.0142]   spans zero
  (combined 5-member pool 0.9240, above every solo)

So the paired half-width on 58 studies is roughly +/-0.015, about 2.4x the 0.0062 the 909-study report holdout gives. That is what n=58 buys and it should have been measured before any gold delta was read.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. Two wakes ago I selected recal_dense's REPLICATES branch on a +0.0172 gold delta by comparing it to 0.0062. 0.0062 is the REPORT ruler's floor, measured on 909 studies. Applying it to a gold delta measured on 58 is a category error, and it is the exact 'faulty TEST' failure mode: a tolerance below the noise. The ledger entry written at 03:12Z carries that error and must be amended.

WHAT SURVIVES. Nothing about stackfit or labelwise_dense: +0.0101 and +0.0054 are inside the interval and are NOT pairwise claims. Their proxy readings (flat, and 'buys nothing') stand unchallenged. stack_increments and contrast_dense are unaffected — both were already null and are still null, now with an interval to say so honestly.

STILL OPEN. recal_dense's branch was pre-registered against band_dense_hold, not against calib_dense_hold, so the +0.0011 above is the wrong comparison for it. Its own paired interval against band_dense_hold is computing now (logs/gold_recal_paired.log). +0.0172 against a +/-0.015 half-width is marginal either way — if the interval excludes zero it is the project's only readable gold result, and if it spans zero the REPLICATES selection is withdrawn and v3 stays where knee-8wa0 left it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT KILL. The finding this bead sits on is unharmed: the pool beats the report ruler by +0.0516 with CI [+0.0296, +0.0729], which is 3.4x this half-width and never depended on member-vs-member resolution. The reader-is-the-weaker-half result is about a LEVEL, and knee-kddo already said the 58 are a level and not a selector. What today's number adds is the size of that selector's blind spot: the gold ruler cannot separate two members closer than ~0.015, which is most of the member field.
close_reason: reading_check built, committed c643d27a, live: 218 arms, 0 declared and missing. The check is the finding, as the bead said. recal_dense carries the first declaration; the twenty dark arms are knee follow-up above.

title: feature_probe compares trunks at a SHARED ridge penalty, and that mispriced at least two declines
description: Measured 2026-09-02 18:02Z. feature_probe reports every trunk at the same penalty (default 100). Trunk feature magnitudes differ ~17x (radnet121 max 0.173, v3large max 2.90), so one penalty is near-optimal for one trunk and far off for another. At each trunk's OWN best penalty: ortholarge 0.8249 @1.0, radnet121 0.8197 @0.003, v3large 0.8023 @10.0. At the shared 100: 0.7829 for v3large and 0.6746 for radnet121 - a 0.108 gap that inverts to a 0.017 LEAD when each is read at its own penalty. Two declines rest on the shared-penalty reading: OrthoFoundation-L (quoted 0.7387 vs v3large 0.7446) and the radnet121 trunk family. Both trunks BEAT the incumbent control when read fairly. CAVEAT before quoting: all three peaks were selected on the same 909-study holdout, so all three are inflated by selection; the RANK REVERSAL is the finding, not the levels. The fix is per-trunk penalty chosen by a nested split inside the probe, the same discipline stack_fit already uses. Until that lands, no trunk comparison in this project should be quoted.
notes:
FIXED IN CODE 2026-09-04 05:48Z, and the fix is a DEFAULT flip rather than a new capability.

--choose-penalty already existed; a bare feature_probe still printed the shared-penalty table, so the
reading this bead calls wrong was the one nobody had to ask for. It is now the opposite: per-trunk
nested-split choice is the default and --shared-penalty is the opt-out, kept only because every number
quoted before today was taken at it.

Two more things went with it:
- The four @focal-attend rows are deleted from TRUNKS. They named arrays byte-identical to their
  @focal-max siblings (knee-n647: --slice-read never reached the encoder), so every table this probe
  printed carried a duplicate of each row that read as two instruments agreeing. The arrays stay on disk;
  the fix for the readout axis is a cache written by an encoder that took the flag.
- The RIDGE docstring argued FOR the shared penalty. It now states the measurement that refutes it
  (0.108 gap inverting to a 0.017 lead) and says why the plausible argument is wrong: a shared penalty
  is not one instrument either, because feature magnitudes differ ~17x. The instrument is the PROCEDURE.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN and is NOT this bead: ortholarge probes best (0.8249) and serves worst (ortho_dense
0.8452 vs ~0.855 dinov2 seats). Probes best / serves worst is a RECIPE question. Tracked separately.

title: Q-AN: answer whether cross-corpus auxiliary segmentation gains survive
description: Claude restated Q-AN as a literature question: in published work on auxiliary segmentation for medical image CLASSIFICATION, does the gain survive when segmentation masks come from a DIFFERENT corpus than classification labels? This decides whether  (SKM-TEA masks + RSNA labels) is viable. Need a table of 5-6 papers with task, mask corpus, label corpus, same/different, classification metric before/after, and n. Also answer Q-AN.1 (where seg head attaches) and Q-AN.2 (loss weight / annealing).
acceptance_criteria: Literature table delivered to Claude; bead  updated with the answer; decision recorded (proceed / redesign / decline).
notes:
2026-09-02T1630Z Kimi preliminary literature table (4 of 6 rows). 1) Hooper et al., NeurIPS 2023 "A case for reframing automated medical image classification as segmentation": tasks pneumothorax/melanoma/cervical-fracture; masks and labels SAME corpus (CANDID n=19,237, ISIC n=2,750, SPINE n=2,018); AUROC gain +2.6% to +10.0% (limited data) and +0.6% to +6.1% (full data); seg head is shared trunk + decoder; no annealing reported. 2) Xia et al. 2026 HA-DLC: liver-lesion and BraTS tumour classification; SAME corpus; removing seg loss drops AUC 0.650 to 0.623; joint end-to-end segmentation + classification; fixed multi-task weight. 3) Li et al. 2024/2025 SuPreM: organ/tumour segmentation pretraining on AbdomenAtlas 1.1 (9,262 CT, 88 hospitals) -> fine-grained pancreatic tumour classification on proprietary dataset (1,869 train / 1,073 test CT, 3,577 tumours); DIFFERENT corpus/task; supervised seg init beats SSL init and needs 50% fewer classification annotations; seg head is U-Net decoder on shared encoder; pretrain then fine-tune, not joint. 4) Ma et al. 2025 Foundation X: 11 CXR datasets (some classification-only, some segmentation-only); MIXED same/different corpus; cross-dataset/cross-task learning improves over single-task baselines; shared Swin-B backbone + task-specific heads; cyclic Lock-Release pretraining; specific classification gains mixed. Need 1-2 more rows and exact Q-AN.1/Q-AN.2 details before answering Claude.
2026-09-02T1700Z Kimi final literature table (6 rows) and Q-AN.1/Q-AN.2 answers. TABLE: (1) Hooper et al. NeurIPS 2023 - pneumothorax/melanoma/spine-fracture; masks and labels SAME corpus (CANDID n=19,237, ISIC n=2,750, SPINE n=2,018); AUROC gain +2.6% to +10.0% limited, +0.6% to +6.1% full; shared trunk + decoder; fixed CE, no anneal. (2) Xia et al. 2026 HA-DLC - liver lesion and BraTS tumour classification; SAME corpus; removing seg loss drops AUC 0.650 to 0.623; joint shared encoder with seg/class branches; fixed multi-task weight. (3) Heker and Greenspan 2020 - liver lesion classification; MIXED (LiTS segmentation for transfer learning + target dataset joint learning); classification accuracy +10% vs baseline, +3% vs Y-Net; shared encoder joint framework; fixed joint loss. (4) Li et al. SuPreM 2024/25 - pancreatic tumour subtype classification; DIFFERENT corpus (AbdomenAtlas 1.1, 9,262 CT -> proprietary dataset 1,869/1,073 CT); supervised segmentation init beats SSL and halves annotation need; U-Net decoder on shared encoder; pretrain then finetune. (5) Ma et al. Foundation X 2025 - CXR disease classification; MIXED (11 CXR datasets, some classification-only, some segmentation-only); cross-dataset/cross-task learning improves over single-task baselines; shared Swin-B backbone + task-specific heads/decoders; cyclic Lock-Release (freeze/release), not loss annealing. (6) Zhang et al. MASS 2026 - unseen pathology classification; DIFFERENT corpus (5K CT/MRI/PET auto-generated masks -> downstream classification); frozen encoder matches full supervised training with fewer labels; in-context segmentation pretext; SSL only. Q-AN.1: shared encoder/trunk with segmentation decoder/head is the dominant architecture; classification head is parallel or added after pretraining. Q-AN.2: fixed multi-task weights dominate; no reviewed paper anneals the segmentation loss to zero; Foundation Xs cyclic lock-release is the only non-constant schedule and it freezes parameters rather than weighting losses. VERDICT: direct cross-corpus auxiliary-segmentation gain is NOT well established; most evidence is same-corpus. Cross-corpus support is indirect (pretraining transfer). knee-xhhj is therefore speculative and should be gated on a cheap encoder probe before a full multi-day build.

title: OrthoDiffusion smoke — download Kaggle weights and test as 3D member
description:
OrthoDiffusion (Lan et al. 2026) is a 3D diffusion foundation model pretrained on 15,948 knee MRIs with released Kaggle weights and reported macro AUROC 0.908 on 8 knee abnormalities. This task tracks the first smoke experiment:

1. Download the Kaggle dataset 'OrthoDiffusion Official Knee MRI Foundation'.
2. Verify license/terms allow competition use.
3. Inspect checkpoint structure (sagittal/coronal/axial 3D U-Net backbones).
4. Implement feature extraction: load volume, run diffusion U-Net to selected timestep/block, pool bottleneck features (SAP-style), fuse three planes.
5. Train a small 12-label head on a subset of RSNA studies and measure holdout AUC vs DINOv2/DINOv3 baseline.

If smoke reads positive, schedule a full member arm. If license blocks use, decline with reason.
notes:
2026-09-07 19:20Z, steps 1-3 DONE, card-free.
(1) DOWNLOAD: already on disk and has been for days, unrecorded. D:/data/external/orthodiffusion/ 1.6 GB: sagittal_model.pt, coronal_model.pt, axial_model.pt plus a HuggingFace cache dir, so it came from HF and not from the Kaggle dataset this bead names (prvsiyan/orthodiffusion-official-knee-mri-foundation, 1.12 GB, still available).
(2) LICENSE: MIT, stated in the weights README front-matter (license: mit). No non-commercial or research-only clause. Competition use allowed. Paper Lan et al. arXiv:2602.20752, code github.com/lt-0123/OrthoDiffusion.
(3) STRUCTURE, read off the checkpoints: all three planes identical in shape, same step 21499, 34.54 M params, 257 tensors. A DDPM 3D U-Net (denoise_fn), NOT a ViT. Top keys step/model/ema/opt, so the EMA copy is in the same file and the separate cemdusenkalkan/orthodiffusion-ema-weights dataset is redundant. The 1000-step schedule ships with it (betas (1000,) plus the alphas_cumprod family). Input conv (64,1,3,3,3): single channel, 3x3x3, base width 64. Four downsamples at input_blocks.{2,4,6,8}.0.op with widths 64,64,128,128, so channel mults (1,1,2,2,4) and the grid divides by 16 in every axis. Bottleneck middle_block is 256 ch with a self-attention block (qkv 768=3x256). NO positional embedding anywhere, so the net is fully convolutional and accepts any volume with all three dims divisible by 16 -- we are not locked to their crop.
FEATURE PLAN (step 4): noise to a chosen t, run the encoder half, take middle_block output, pool -> 256-d per plane, 768-d fused over three planes. A ridge head, not a training run.
STILL NEEDED before the encode, and NOT in the checkpoint: their intensity normalisation and the voxel spacing/crop the 15,948 volumes were resampled to. Take both from the GitHub repo; feeding a diffusion model an out-of-distribution intensity range is the one way this smoke reads a false negative.
PRE-REG (mastermind 19:15Z): frozen ridge on the 896 >= 0.85 -> full encode and seat read, target cell corr9 <= 0.85 at solo >= 0.87 (the raptor cell); 0.80-0.85 -> price a fine-tune arm before running it; < 0.80 -> closed as a trunk with the reason written down. Caveat to carry into the read: their reported 0.908 macro is FINE-TUNED on their own 8 labels, not a frozen-feature number, and a denoiser bottleneck is trained to predict noise rather than to be a discriminative summary.

title: Re-probe closed trunks with attention / patch-level readout before final closure
description:
Claude's trunk-closing readings (RadImageNet 0.6716, OrthoFoundation-L 0.8452 fitted / 0.7387 frozen, DINOv3-L 0.7446 vs DINOv2-L 0.7852) were all taken through the project's default max-pooled readout. Q-AL literature review (research/2026-09-02_trunk_vs_readout_quality_medical_volumes_qal.md) finds that the readout can hide trunk quality:

1. Muthyala et al. 2026: same frozen ViT goes from chance (CLS, AUC 0.50-0.52) to near-perfect (patch-local, AUC ~1.0) on chest small-lesion detection.
2. AnyMC3D: same frozen DINOv3 backbone, query-based attention pooling over slices beats max pooling by +0.016 AUC (up to +0.11 AUC in another setup).
3. DINOv3 ViT-L distilled is +0.7-1.1 pp better than DINOv2-L on ImageNet linear probe, and tied with DINOv2-L when AnyMC3D's adaptation is used.

Task: re-run the frozen-cache ridge probe for dinov2-large, v3large, and ortholarge using (a) the existing DepthAttention aggregator, and (b) a patch-token linear probe (e.g. average patch tokens or a learned query over patch tokens) as the readout. Measure whether the trunk ranking changes. Costs no new training; only a different head on existing frozen caches.
notes: CARD-FREE HALF DONE, negative. The slice-aggregation readout (knee-n647 detail) moves each trunk by at most +0.0043 and does not change the ranking, so the closed trunks were closed by the trunks and not by the max-pooled readout. The PATCH-LOCAL half (Muthyala) is untouched and still needs re-encoding: --pool collapses tokens before storage, and neither prior art here is patch-local (cls_mean_focal discards the topk INDICES; sided is a two-column split).

The 2x2 in the ledger says why it is not a closure either - continuation is worth ~+0.019, ViT-L costs ~-0.016 against the ViT-B on this recipe, and the two nearly cancel. title: Q13 hard and diverse example sampling - nothing in the repo does this today
description: Child of the 2026-09-01 direction epic. Answer in writing with numbers on disk, or state explicitly that nobody has measured it and what it would cost to.
design: Nothing in the repo does hard or diverse sampling; a grep for sampler, curriculum and hard_example hits only pretrain.py. With 62 Fracture positives on the holdout, uniform sampling is a live suspect. Design: per-example loss tracking first (depends on the metrics work), then small-loss selection, prevalence-balanced batches, or diversity sampling over the cached feature space. Gate on the published finding that neither reweighting nor selection dominates alone.
acceptance_criteria: A sampler landed behind a flag, smoked with arm_check --smoke, plus a pre-registered arm against a matched uniform-sampling control.
notes:
PRICE: 2 x 3.1 h = 6.2 h of card for one axis. P(clears +0.015) ~ 0.12 at the retuned tilt; P(clears the noise floor either way) ~ 0.5. Aimed at the ~70% split band from residual_split, the biggest block on the residual sheet, so a mechanism that works at all has room past the 1.5% bar. The null is the point as much as the gain: it closes the DRAW axis, the last untouched axis in the loop.

TILT RETUNED BEFORE ARMING, on the spread report rather than on taste. train_spread_honest12 reads mean 0.1244, median 0.1267, p90 0.1571, max 0.2128; bands: spread<0.05 ZERO studies, 0.05-0.10 699, 0.10-0.15 2175, >=0.15 624. At the original alpha 0.5 the split band drew 1.145 against the quiet band's 0.840 — a 1.36x contrast, which is a null by construction and the UNINFORMATIVE null, since a flat result could only say '1.36x does nothing' and could not close the axis. Alpha 1.0 gives 1.29 vs 0.68, a 1.9x contrast, same runtime, no code change. That is the most contrast this weight HAS, which is what makes a flat result a closure rather than a knob reading; a sharper weight (power on spread, rank tilt) would re-open it.

SEPARATE FINDING, belongs to Q3 (knee-f9rx) and not to this arm: the quiet band is EMPTY. Twelve separately-trained members never unanimously agree anywhere on the training corpus. The 24.3% unanimous block from residual_split is unanimous in VERDICT, not in confidence. Denominator: 3498 training studies, all of them in-sample for all twelve members.
Read-only audit complete. Disagreement sampler already implemented and pre-registered (see interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-01_q13_hard_and_diverse_sampling.md). Missing: diversity sampler, prevalence-balanced batches, and any loss-based miner (blocked on Q10 per-example loss). Child tasks: knee-nyqc.1 smoke/queue disagreed_sampler, knee-nyqc.2 diversity sampler, knee-nyqc.3 prevalence-balanced batches.

acceptance_criteria: A statement separating the measurable transfer constant and its spread from the unmeasurable, plus a rule for how much offline gain justifies a slot.
close_reason: Audit complete. Measurable: offline-to-public-board compression is a saturating curve (whole-record +1.23, champion regime +0.80 [+0.70,+1.19]); holdout has never mis-ordered a resolved pair on the public board. Unmeasurable: any claim about the 70% hidden-test population. No controllable bias visible in member count, date, offline score, or selection; fold -1 share could not be checked due to missing members_named. Slot rule: require offline delta >= 0.0053 and predicted board gain (0.80 x delta) to exceed the board gap. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-01_q8_shown_vs_hidden_test_bias.md.

Inputs: the cached held-out probabilities champion_uncertainty already reads.

notes: Cut (a) LANDED 2026-09-01 as a JOIN, and it is the payoff of the bead. The per-label deficit table already existed (research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md, annotation ruler, 58 gold studies). Joining it to cut (c)'s unanimity column: Spearman 0.952 (p=0.00027, n=8), Pearson 0.942. Lateral Meniscus (-0.20 deficit, 13.3% unanimity) and ACL (-0.10, 14.4%) are the two extremes on BOTH rulers; Effusion (+0.08, 29.7%) the other end. NOT prevalence: prevalence~unanimity is -0.105 over all twelve findings, and deficit~unanimity partialled on prevalence RISES to 0.981. Two rulers that share only the finding name -- external published AUCs on other corpora vs our members' internal agreement on our holdout -- order the panel the same way. Reading: the remaining gap is model-side and reachable, and it is concentrated in Lateral Meniscus + ACL. A new member should be judged on those two, not on the twelve-label mean that dilutes a real gain six-fold.
