title: Audit the 108 confident false positives for EXTRACTOR failure (negation, laterality, priors) vs genuine reader disagreement
description:
THE QUESTION. noise_binding measures 108 confident false positives over the 58 gold studies — all verdict YES, 15.8% of every annotated cell, against 32 misses — and supervision_gap measures 65.3% radiologist agreement where the report says YES. Every label mechanism this project ships treats that as READER error and responds by softening. Nobody has checked whether it is EXTRACTOR error instead.

WHY IT IS NOW A LIVE HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A GUESS (research/2026-08-31_report_label_noise_and_uncertainty_heads.md). Negation errors — 'no evidence of ACL tear' read as a positive — are the classic report-labeler failure mode, alongside laterality and interval-change errors, and recent work reports LLMs are specifically WEAK at detecting negated expressions relative to purpose-built models. A false positive produced by a missed negation is CONFIDENT BY CONSTRUCTION: the extractor saw the finding named in the text and had no reason to hedge. That is exactly the signature of our 108 — all verdict YES, all high confidence. Our labels are LLM-read, so this failure mode is available to us in a way it is not to a hand-labelled corpus.

WHAT TO DO. For each of the 108 cells, pull the report sentence it was extracted from and classify into: (a) missed negation, (b) laterality error, (c) hedge dropped (report hedged, extractor did not), (d) temporal or prior-study reference (finding described as historical or on a prior exam), (e) genuine radiologist-vs-image disagreement. Report counts with the denominator stated (108 of how many annotated cells, and how many of the 58 studies contribute). CPU only, no card, no slot.

WHY IT IS P0 AND NOT A CURIOSITY. The two answers send the project to different places, and both are actionable.
* If a material share are EXTRACTION failures, the fix is the extractor and it is CORPUS-WIDE — 4,407 studies, not 58 — and upstream of every member ever trained here. That is a bigger lever than any loss term and it is the only label lever that could plausibly clear 1.5% on its own.
* If they are genuine reader disagreement, then Rep-GLS-style sharpening stays contraindicated for us (see the sibling bead), the softening half we already ship is the correct half, and the label lane narrows to the confident-learning detector.
Either answer is worth having, which makes this an INSTRUMENT rather than a bet.

PREREQUISITE TO VERIFY FIRST: that the report text is on disk and joinable to the gold 58 by StudyInstanceUID. Report text is train-time only (test.csv holds one column) but it should be present for training studies. If it is not on disk, say so and stop — do not substitute the derived labels for the text, which would make the audit circular.

RELATED: this is the upstream half of the confident-learning detector (running 2026-08-31T15:25Z), which finds label errors from model disagreement. This one finds them from the text. They should agree on the same cells; if they do not, that disagreement is itself informative.
notes: ANSWERED. Precondition YES: raw/train.csv carries Report beside the radiologist columns, 58/58 annotated non-empty, 57 join to report_labels_v2 (684 cells / 57 studies). Built core.data.labels.{finding_mentions,negation_scope,overcall_audit}; located 101 of 108 (93.5%) against 44.1% for the English-only prior instrument. With the confident TRUE positives (n=203) as control: missed_negation 12/108 11.1% vs 3/203 1.5% (+9.6% [+4.4,+15.3]), laterality 2 1.9% vs 6 3.0%, hedge_dropped 2 1.9% vs 12 5.9%, historical 1 0.9% vs 11 5.4%, subthreshold 46 42.6% vs 48 23.6%, genuine 38 35.2% vs 106 52.2%, unlocated 7 vs 17. Clean extractor failure = 16/108 (14.8%), an UPPER bound; 84/108 (77.8%) is rubric mismatch + real disagreement. Three of four extractor categories fire MORE on agreed cells: style, not error. LANE: Rep-GLS sharpening stays contraindicated, the shipped softening half is correct; the negation slice is worth a targeted extractor pass priced at ~15% of the defect, not as the lane. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_the-overcalls-are-mostly-not-the-extractor.md

title: Per-cell label weight from MODEL disagreement, not reader self-report — confident learning over the OOF arrays
description:
THE DEFECT, already measured, not hypothesised. noise_binding: 108 confident false positives over the 58 annotated studies, ALL verdict YES, 15.8% of every annotated cell, against 32 misses the other way. supervision_gap: where the report says YES the radiologist agrees 65.3% of the time.

WHY EVERY EXISTING MECHANISM IS BLIND TO IT. Two label axes ship today:
  VALUE   Supervision.applied maps the reader's five levels to measured agreement 0.08/0.28/0.68/0.82/0.94.
  WEIGHT  weight_floor, CONFIDENCE_FLOOR=0.25, so the per-cell loss weight is 0.25 + 0.75*conf.
Both are functions of what the READER says about ITSELF — its level, its confidence, its finding. The defect is cells where the reader was CONFIDENT and WRONG. Under 0.25 + 0.75*conf those cells carry weight near 1.0. The current scheme UP-WEIGHTS precisely the cells that are wrong, by construction, and no refinement of a self-report can fix a self-report. finding_calib_dense (2026-08-27) is the same lesson one level shallower: per-finding offsets are also a function of reader-side quantities, and they read FLAT (+0.507 [+0.434,+0.579] vs +0.550 [+0.470,+0.630]). That ledger entry names this door itself — 'a per-STUDY confidence rather than a per-FINDING constant'.

THE INDEPENDENT SIGNAL. Confident learning ranks a cell by the MODEL's out-of-fold disagreement with its label. It never asks the reader, so it can see a confidently-wrong cell. Use cleanlab, not a hand-rolled version — this project's own captum result (knee-wgaa, 2026-08-31) is the argument: a mature library's faithfulness metrics found that our hand-built occlusion attribution was the LESS faithful readout on 12 of 12 findings, which nothing hand-written would have caught.

INPUTS ARE ALREADY ON DISK, NO GPU. paired_floor uses four seeds over five folds whose id-sets partition all 4,407 studies, so every study carries predictions from models that did not train on it — exactly confident learning's required input, over the whole corpus rather than the 58.

THE GATE, AND IT MUST RUN BEFORE ANY CARD IS SPENT. Detection runs on 4,407 studies; we hold 108 KNOWN radiologist disagreements on the gold 58. Do the flagged cells hit them? Pre-register it: state the hit rate a random flagger would get at the same flag count, and require the method to beat it clearly. If it misses the 108, the method is dead and it cost zero card. Report the DENOMINATOR: how many of the 58 fall in folds the OOF models held out.

THE ARM, only if the gate passes. ONE flag against the current scheme, same corner: a per-cell weight derived from model disagreement replacing 0.25 + 0.75*conf. weight_floor is already the plumbing for a per-cell weight, so no new training path is needed.

RULER CONTAMINATION. Supervision.moves_the_ruler() exists because a switch that changes the training table usually also changes the table the arm is SCORED against. Establish which side this one falls on BEFORE the arm, and re-read the ruler plain if it moves it. The floor does not move it; a per-cell reweighting might.

PRICE: detection CPU-only, few hours, 0 slots. The arm ~4 h card, only after the gate. Board transfer is UNKNOWN — --calibrated-targets moved noise_binding -0.145 at two corners and what that bought on the board was never isolated. Do not invent a transfer number for this.
notes:
2026-09-04T15:28Z. GATE SPENT AND GREEN, re-read from logs/label_errors.log: over 684 scoreable cells on 57 of 58 gold studies, the confident joint beats a random flagger of the same size 4.05x at budget 25 (precision 0.640 vs 0.158 random), separation AUC 0.7580 on the 108 confident false positives. Denominator stated: 57 of 58 gold studies carry held-out predictions; corpus is 52,872 read cells of 52,884, 5,360 flagged (10.138%). The FLAG TABLE, the one missing precondition, is now written: D:/data/volumetric/mri/processed/label_flags.csv, 5,360 rows, matching the log's 'corpus flagged' count exactly - the disbelief check errors_dense.sh's own header asks for. arm_check --only errors_dense: 1 checked, 0 refused, 0 uncached.

PRICE (restored - an earlier note on this bead replaced the field that carried it, and arm_check refused the arm as UNPRICED until it came back; the number is not new, it is the pre-registration's own): the arm costs ~4 h of card and 0 slots, detection was CPU-only and is already spent. P(clears 1.5% absolute) ~0.12. P(clears the 0.0062 holdout floor, i.e. >= 0.8640 against band_dense 0.8578) ~0.35. It is priced as an AXIS OPENER rather than as an improvement: the flags are real at 4.05x, so a null does not close the axis, it splits it - flat means the TREATMENT (prune) is wrong while the signal stands, which points at re-labelling. Board transfer is UNKNOWN and no transfer number is to be invented for it.

Queued next on the card ahead of the RadioDino trunk arms: the trunk family has ten priced members topping out at +0.0016 with not one reaching +0.0040, and this axis has never been priced at all.
2026-09-04T15:55Z. THE ARM HAD ALREADY RUN. errors_dense completed 2026-09-02 07:57, twelve of twelve epochs, best 0.8420 at e6 — and this bead, the arm header, and a letter to Kimi all spent 2026-09-04 treating it as unrun. It was re-queued on the card behind band_pairmem and would have burned ~4h re-running a known result; the watcher chain was killed and relaunched over the two RadioDino arms only.

READING, against the arm's own pre-registration: 0.8420 vs band_dense 0.8578 = -0.0158, the LOWEST branch (< 0.8516), IT COSTS, by 2.5x the 0.0062 floor. Ruler clean: moves_the_ruler() is True for a prune so Targets.pair scored against a PLAIN unpruned table (core/data/labels/targets.py:484). Converged, peak e6 then five epochs inside 0.0024.

PER-LABEL (the branch demands these first): eleven of twelve LOSE, broad not rare-concentrated. PF OA -0.038, Fracture -0.034, Baker's -0.024, MedMen -0.019, LatMen -0.017, LatOA -0.016, Contusion -0.016, Effusion -0.012, MedOA -0.009, Synovitis -0.007, ACL -0.002, MCL +0.003. Not BoMD's rare-class trap.

MECHANISM, priced against the data slope: half_data costs -0.0234 for 50% of cells; linear, 10.14% predicts -0.0047, and quarter_data's measured concavity makes the marginal prediction smaller still, and dropping cells while keeping the image should cost less per cell than dropping whole studies. Observed -0.0158 is 3.4x the linear estimate. The prune is not paying for volume: confident learning selects cells the MODEL disagrees with, a set enriched in HARD-BUT-CORRECT far more than in mislabelled at a 10.14% budget, and those carry the highest gradients in the corpus.

THE AXIS SPLITS, IT DOES NOT CLOSE. Flags real at 4.05x; PRUNE-AT-FULL-BUDGET is refuted. Survivors: knee-f8hv5 (re-label, now mechanism-backed by this arm rather than only literature-directional) and a new small-budget prune bead. Kimi's Q-EB was right that pruning loses; my 1535Z correction to them was wrong and is retracted.
2026-09-04T16:05Z. THE 4.05x IN THIS BEAD IS THE WRONG ROW. logs/label_errors.log reports a budget CURVE plus a separate row for cleanlab's own confident-joint mask, and the mask is what errors_dense actually ran on. On the 108 confident false positives the mask reads precision 0.258, lift 1.63x; the 0.640 / 4.05x quoted above and in the arm header is the plain ranking at a 3.7% budget the arm never used. On all 140 disagreements the mask reads 0.484. Scaled to the corpus, the arm pruned ~1,383 confident FPs, ~2,594 disagreements, and ~2,766 cells the radiologist AGREED with. That is the measured version of the mechanism this bead's previous note inferred from the data slope, and the two agree. It is also a denominator error of mine: an arm priced off the best row of a curve rather than off its operating point. The gate was never as strong as it was reported, and the strong number is still available - to a DIFFERENT selector (knee-jom26).

title: Split the 87% aleatoric mass: is it imaging ambiguity or LABEL NOISE? The gold 58 can bound it, no card
description:
FROM knee-qrtx (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_the_pool_is_redundant_not_the_task.md). The decomposition put 87.3% of the ensemble's remaining uncertainty in the ALEATORIC term — what no member knows. But aleatoric is only defined GIVEN THE LABEL, and our labels are report_labels_v2.csv: LLM-read findings from radiology report text. So that mass is imaging ambiguity PLUS annotation error, and nothing separates them.

WHY IT IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE OPEN QUESTION. The two readings imply opposite work:
 * genuine imaging ambiguity -> the task is near its ceiling, member search is over (knee-qrtx already bounds it at 12.7%), and the remaining game is vote mechanics and calibration.
 * material annotation error -> LABEL QUALITY is the untouched lever, and no architecture search can reach it. A better trunk fitted to a wrong label learns the wrong label better. Every arm this project has queued for a month has been optimising against a ruler with unmeasured error in it.
This is the only open question whose answer redirects the whole search rather than one arm.

THE INSTRUMENT WE ALREADY OWN. 58 gold studies with RADIOLOGIST annotations. The comparison is the aleatoric term computed against gold labels versus against report labels, on the same studies with the same members. 58 x 12 is too thin for a per-finding split — say so in the output rather than printing twelve numbers that cannot carry the claim — but it is not too thin for a POOLED one, and the SIGN and rough SIZE of the gap is the entire answer.

METHOD NOTE. Do not compute this as two independent numbers subtracted. The 58 are the same studies under both label sources, so it is a PAIRED read and the interval is far tighter than either term's own — kneemri/evaluation/paired_floor.py measured that tightening for exactly this reason and should be reused, not re-derived.

EXISTING CODE. kneemri/evaluation/uncertainty_split.py (UncertaintySplit / UncertaintyShare) does the decomposition; kneemri/evaluation/gold_rows.py and annotated_readings.py already handle the gold set. Audit both BEFORE writing — knee-qrtx was filed as a new module and turned out to be a K-way generalisation of a function that already existed.

COST: no GPU, no slot. Arrays are on disk.

STATE THE DENOMINATOR: how many of the 58 fall in a fold the members held out, since that is the number that actually carries the read — not 58.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-09-03 by interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-03_the-report-ruler-over-calls.md, in the LABEL-NOISE direction, with a sign and a size.

Instrument: eight members fitted with --hold-annotations (flag read off each recipe row, not off the name), scored against the 58 radiologist-annotated studies in train.csv. Card-free, cached arrays.

The report ruler is wrong on 145 of 696 cells (0.2083) and the error is ONE-DIRECTIONAL: 108 over-calls against 37 under-calls, 71 net positives on 240 gold. Synovitis is the single inversion (14 FN vs 4 FP) and that is the 84.2%-UNK silence, not a disagreement.

Our own members already beat the ruler: report-as-predictor 0.8658 mean AUC, eight-member pool 0.9174, paired delta +0.0516, 95% CI [+0.0296, +0.0729] over 4000 study-level bootstraps, P(delta>0)=0.9998. Every solo member beats it too (0.8932-0.9152), so it is not an ensemble effect - models trained on a noisy target average away part of that target's noise, and are then SCORED against a target that still carries it.

Mechanism, not coincidence: the per-label AUC-gain ordering matches the over-call COUNT ordering. Contusion (20 FP) and Effusion (16 FP) are the two hardest over-calls and the two biggest member gains.

DENOMINATOR, stated: 58 of 4406 studies = 1.3%, and they are MEASURABLY not representative - 44.7% positive cells here against 30.5% corpus-wide, 1.47x enriched. So 0.2083 is an UPPER BOUND on the corpus rate, never an estimate of it.

What it does NOT establish: which ruler the hidden test uses (provenance argument only), and any board number (board_transfer's slope was fitted on report-holdout points and does not transfer to a different ruler).

Closing this bead does not close the axis. The label-correction lever it opens is knee-kabn's direction, and the interpretation's own constraint stands: the correction must come from a MECHANISM (reader behaviour - the UNK level at 0.28, the over-call direction, the Synovitis silence), never from fitting twelve per-label thresholds on 58 studies, which would spend the only honest ruler this project owns.

title: Decompose the champion ensemble's uncertainty into aleatoric vs epistemic — is the plateau reducible at all?
description:
Systole (D:/personal_projects/cardiac-seg, same owner, different modality) hit the same wall we are at: a cross-vendor gap that augmentation, normalization and same-recipe deep ensembling all failed to move. It did not close the question by argument. It MEASURED how much of its error was reducible, with a BALD uncertainty decomposition over its ensemble members, and got ~15-18% epistemic on unseen vendors. That number is what licensed 'stop adding members, change model class' instead of it being a hunch.

MECHANISM. For K members with per-study probability vectors p_k:
  total     = H[mean_k p_k]        entropy of the ensemble mean
  aleatoric = mean_k H[p_k]        irreducible: the label's own ambiguity
  epistemic = total - aleatoric    reducible: what a better/different member could fix
Per finding and pooled. Binary entropy per target, since our twelve outputs are independent sigmoids, not a softmax.

WHY THIS ONE, NOW. It costs NO card, NO slot and NO training. 122 members already have cached holdout probabilities under holdout_predictions/ (one .npy + .json per checkpoint). This is numpy over arrays on disk, minutes.

WHAT IT ADJUDICATES — knee-nj4l (P0), directly:
 * epistemic fraction LOW -> the six champion members genuinely agree, more members of any kind cannot pay, and the reseating/diversity search is dead ground. The lever is model class or data. That is knee-nj4l's claim made quantitative rather than asserted from a 0.004 band across seven entries.
 * epistemic fraction HIGH -> the members DO disagree and the combiner is failing to exploit it. Then the lever is the combination rule (we rank-average) and not the roster at all — a cheaper and entirely unexplored axis.
Either answer redirects card time. Nothing else queued has that ratio.

TRAP TO AVOID, from systole's own writeup: TTA-flip variants share weights, so their epistemic term is a LOWER BOUND and under-counts. Only separately-trained members count as an honest sample. Our six are separately trained; do not fold TTA windows in as pseudo-members.

DENOMINATOR. State it: which studies, how many, and that they are the holdout the members were NOT fitted on. Cross-check member fold with the same seen = train u val logic foreign_overlap uses — an in-sample member makes the decomposition meaningless (this is exactly how raptor_solo's 0.8938 was voided on 2026-08-29).

DELIVERABLE. A committed module under kneemri/evaluation/ with a CLI, plus an interpretation under interpretations/kneemri/ carrying the number and which of the two branches above it fires.
notes:
AUDIT BEFORE DELEGATION, 2026-08-31 — this is SMALLER than filed, and nearly went out as a duplicate.

kneemri/evaluation/member_divergence.py ALREADY computes Jensen-Shannon divergence between two members' predictions read as Bernoulli beliefs, per study, per label, and seat_value already prints it. For a K-component mixture the identity is exact:

    JSD(p_1..p_K) = H[mean_k p_k] - mean_k H[p_k]

which IS the epistemic term. The reducible half of this bead is written and tested. Do not re-derive it and do not add a second entropy helper.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING, and it is only these two:
 1. K-WAY, not pairwise. member_divergence is a member-to-member distance used to price a seat. The question here is about a whole entry's members at once.
 2. THE ALEATORIC TERM REPORTED BESIDE IT. A divergence is a distance; it cannot say what FRACTION of the remaining uncertainty is reducible. epistemic / (epistemic + aleatoric) is the number systole acted on and the only number that adjudicates knee-nj4l. A large JSD in an already-uncertain regime means something different from the same JSD in a confident one, and pairwise JSD cannot tell those apart.

SO: extend beside member_divergence, same per-label-then-mean shape it already uses (one number over the flattened array is dominated by prevalence — its docstring says why). Same file or a sibling in kneemri/evaluation/; NOT a new subsystem.

FOLD / LEAK. The holdout_predictions cache .json records checkpoint, count, views, window, precision, bytes, mtime_ns, studies — and NO fold. count is 909, the whole corpus. So the cache alone cannot say which studies a member held out; join through HoldoutSlab / TrainerRecord, and apply foreign_overlap's default-is-guilt rule. An in-sample member makes the decomposition meaningless.

Cache state: 122 members present, each a (909, 12) float64 array.
close_reason:
Delivered, commit 78a54aef, gates clean. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_the_pool_is_redundant_not_the_task.md

POOLED REDUCIBLE FRACTION: 12.7% over honest12 (12 members), 8.3% over the 79-member roster, 909 held-out studies. Below cardiac-seg's 15-18%, and FALLING as members are added — the extra 67 members concentrated the pool's belief rather than widening it.

Both pre-registered branches resolve the same way. Member-hunting is bounded at 12.7% of remaining uncertainty; and the combiner branch is closed too, because there is only 0.0565 bits of disagreement in a 0.6807-bit pool for ANY vote rule to exploit.

CAVEAT THAT IS THE NEXT LEAD: aleatoric is measured against report_labels_v2.csv, which are LLM-read report labels. 87.3% aleatoric conflates imaging ambiguity with LABEL NOISE. Separating them is the next read and costs no card — see the follow-on bead.

title: Attribution has occlusion only: log the SLOT/SLICE attention and check it against anatomy.py
description:
OWNER ASKED 2026-08-31 whether attribution.py has captum's goodies. It does not. It implements three occlusion diagnostics (slot drop, border-vs-centre ring, depth-window profile) -- captum's Occlusion and FeatureAblation at a domain-chosen granularity. Absent: Integrated Gradients, DeepLIFT, GradientSHAP, KernelSHAP/LIME, LayerConductance, neuron attribution, GradCAM, TCAV, influence functions.

TWO PILES, and only one of them is a gap.

PILE ONE -- pixel-space saliency (IG, DeepLIFT, GradSHAP, GradCAM). Still declined, and attribution.py's docstring already argues why: nothing in the supervision says WHERE a finding is, so a heatmap has no ground truth to be scored against, and the model-randomisation sanity check (Adebayo) is exactly the failure mode of a map that looks right. Occlusion returns a number on held-out score instead. Adding captum does not change this.

PILE TWO -- the real gap, which the pile-one argument was wrongly allowed to cover.

(a) ATTENTION READOUT. The head is explicit attention over six NAMED slots and then over slices. Those weights are discrete and named, and core/data/corpus/anatomy.py already encodes which plane each finding is read on and whether it needs fluid weighting. So attention attribution here IS checkable against a prior, unlike a pixel map: mass on COR_T1 for a finding the anatomy table says lives on sagittal fluid-weighted is a falsifiable statement about the model. We do not log these weights anywhere. Cheap -- they are already computed -- and it belongs in TRAINING LOGGING (knee-579v.3 hook points), not as another standalone CLI.

(b) INFLUENCE FUNCTIONS. Which training studies drive a prediction. There is a live label-noise problem (reader disagreement, unsure cells, the hold_annotations ruler split) and influence is the standard tool for 'which labels are poisoning this finding'. Nothing in the tree does it.

WHETHER CAPTUM IS WORTH A DEPENDENCY is deliberately left open: (a) is likely fifty lines reading weights we already compute, and the answer should follow seeing the attention distribution rather than precede it. Do (a) first, then decide.
notes:
DELIVERED 2026-08-31, commit 860a99a2, gates clean (1x 'Session gates was successful'). Not pushed.

SHIPPED. captum is a real dependency now (pyproject extra attribution=['captum']). New: kneemri/evaluation/{attention_readout,attention_scan,attribution_faithfulness,slot_probe}.py + four mirror tests. SlotHead gained public projected()/slot_weights() because SlotHead.attention is a METHOD, not a submodule — a forward hook cannot reach it, so capture had to become an explicit read. forward()'s arithmetic is byte-identical and test_slot_weights asserts on/off logits agree by construction.

THE READ, attend_true_s2026 (dinov2-small, fitted WITHOUT the anatomical prior — so agreement with anatomy.py is a MEASUREMENT, not a restatement of a constraint it was trained under), fold-0 holdout, 200 studies:
 * 7 of 12 findings read most heavily on a slot the anatomy table calls primary. Mean off-table mass 0.259.
 * NO degenerate-attention collapse: top slot 0.24-0.31 against a 0.167 uniform, 0 of 12 findings exceed 50% on any one slot. The head spreads its mass.
 * Plane-sensible where it agrees: Baker's 0.415 on AX_FLUID_FS, Effusion dearest AX_FLUID_FS, both menisci and Contusion/Fracture dearest COR_FLUID_FS.
 * The clean disagreement is the three OA findings (Medial/Lateral/PF): all pull SAGITTAL (SAG_T1/SAG_FLUID_NOFS) where the table says COR_T1, PF says AX_FLUID_FS. ACL also chose SAG_T1 over the fluid-sensitive sagittals.
 * CAVEAT the agent stated itself and it is the right one: with peaks this close to uniform the orderings are shallow. Single member, single fold. A fact about this model, not yet about the architecture.

THE FINDING THAT IS ABOUT OUR TOOLING, NOT THE MODEL. captum's faithfulness metrics (24 studies, centred window) score ATTENTION against the occlusion attribution kneemri/evaluation/attribution.py has been producing:
    infidelity      attention 0.037-0.125   vs occlusion 0.052-0.188
    sensitivity_max attention 0.70-0.90     vs occlusion 0.88-2.41
Attention wins on 12 of 12 findings on BOTH metrics. An occlusion sensitivity_max above 1.0 means the explanation moves MORE than the signal does under small feature jitter — the diagnostic is noisier than the thing it explains. Nothing had ever checked this; the occlusion maps were trusted because they existed.

FOLLOW-ON, not done here: this prices attribution.py's occlusion diagnostics as the less faithful of the two available readouts. Any past reading that rested on an occlusion map should be re-read, and the module should either be fixed or demoted with a note. File separately.

Artefacts outside git under the processed root: attention_readout_attend_true_s2026.json, attribution_faithfulness_attend_true_s2026.json.

title: farseat_v1 closed the diversity axis on a member that never loaded; vjepa2-hf is uploaded without its vjepa2-vitl leaf
description:
farseat_v1 (ref 55758082, 2026-08-25, board 0.937) is recorded as the entry that CLOSED the
cross-family ensemble-diversity axis: "the seventh seat is inert even ACROSS architecture families and
the ensemble axis closes". It ran SIX members. Its own kernel log says so, in three lines nobody read:

  member vjepa_warm_s2026 (vjepa2l) would not load -- dropping it from this entry
  FileNotFoundError: no vjepa2l mount among [... dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf ...]
  ENTRY IDENTITY CHANGED: named [...7...] and ran [...6...] -- ['vjepa_warm_s2026'] would not load.
  Score this as the smaller ensemble, not as the entry that was designed.

So farseat_v1 WAS dark6, seat for seat, and it read dark6's exact number, 0.937. A flat read against a
matched control that is literally the same six members is not evidence about a seventh seat. The row's
conclusion is void, not weakened.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is a dataset layout, not code. backbone.py:626 declares the mount as
dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf/vjepa2-vitl, and Encoder.locates (backbone.py:308-309) requires the leaf
"vjepa2-vitl" to be a PATH SEGMENT. The uploaded dataset has config.json and model.safetensors at its
ROOT with no vjepa2-vitl directory (kaggle datasets files dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf, verified 2026-08-30).
DINOv3 is published correctly, one directory per variant -- the same log line lists dinov3-hf/vitb16,
dinov3-hf/vits16, dinov3-hf/vits16plus. V-JEPA2 was uploaded flat and never re-checked.

FOUND BY: building kneemri-vjepaseat for the same seventh seat and reading its save-run log before
submitting. It dropped the member the same way. No slot was spent, on either discovery.

WHAT THIS RE-OPENS. knee-avzz's 2.4x under-pricing argument and the whole distance program were
retired on this row. augseat_v1's row also leans on it. The owner's standing question -- "its about
diversity, not averaging 7 numbers that are the same number" -- has never actually been tested across
families on this board. It is open again.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RE-OPEN. dark7 (same-family control, flat) stands; it did not involve this mount.
vjepa_probe 0.7620 and vjepa_member 0.8343 stand -- those are local numbers, not kernel mounts.

THREE FIXES, in order:
1. Re-upload dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf with the weights under vjepa2-vitl/. ~1.3 GB.
2. mount_check has a hole: it verifies a kernel DECLARES the dataset, never that the dataset CONTAINS
   the leaf path the encoder resolves. Make it ask Kaggle for the file list and match the leaf.
3. Nothing reads a kernel log before a board row is written. "ENTRY IDENTITY CHANGED" is printed
   precisely so a human catches this, and it survived five days and a closed axis. board_check should
   refuse a row whose kernel log carries that line unless members_named is corrected to what RAN.
notes: ALL THREE FIXES LANDED 2026-08-30. (1) mount leaf -> vjepa2-hf; kneemri-vjepaseat v2 then loaded 7 of 7. (2) mount_check EncoderMounts: one live listing per encoder dataset, asks whether it publishes the path the mount names. (3) kneemri.kaggle.run_check: reads a completed kernel's log and refuses on the drop line, ENTRY IDENTITY CHANGED, and a census reading N of M with N<M. It is a PRE-SUBMISSION gate, not a board_check rule, because kaggle kernels output serves only the LATEST version's log - a historical row can never be re-checked. CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md conventions updated (fifteen checks). farseat_v1 voided on the board as a seven-seat reading.

title: Block discovery finds ONE stage on a staged trunk: Swin trained with its top frozen, and ConvNeXt did too
description:
EncoderSurgery.blocks() takes 'the longest ModuleList in the tree' as the encoder's blocks. That is
correct for a FLAT trunk and wrong for a STAGED one, and its own docstring names the failure it then
suffers: 'opening the wrong six modules trains something that is not the encoder's top and reports a
clean number for it.'

MEASURED, by grouping every non-empty ModuleList in each backbone by the TYPE of its elements:

  cnxbase    discovered 27   ConvNextV2Layer totals 36  (stages.0 3, stages.1 3, stages.2 27, stages.3 3)
  swinbase   discovered 18   SwinLayer       totals 24  (layers.0 2, layers.1 2, layers.2 18, layers.3 2)
  v3base     discovered 12   DINOv3ViTLayer  totals 12  (model.layer 12)
  vitin21k   discovered 12   ViTLayer        totals 12  (layers 12)
  raddino    discovered 12   Dinov2Layer     totals 12  (encoder.layer 12)

So on Swin the discovered blocks are layers.2.blocks.0-17 ONLY, and --unfreeze-last 6 opened
layers.2.blocks.12-17. Stage 3 — the final two blocks, the widest and highest-level features in the
network — was FROZEN for the entire run, as were stages 0 and 1. ConvNeXt has the same shape: 27 of 36
discovered, stage 3 never opened.

WHAT IT COSTS US, and it is not one run. Three arms were measured this way:

  swin_supervised_s2026  0.8331   (this is the arm that just finished; seat value -0.0012)
  cnx_own_recipe_s2026   0.8186
  cnx_dense_s2026        0.7927

All three are the project's architecturally DISTANT trunks, and all three are 'far end deaths' on the
knee-y59c distance curve that anti-correlates solo strength with distance-from-DINOv2. That curve is now
partly an artefact: the two families sitting at its far end are exactly the two whose top of network
never trained. The flat trunks that populate the near end are unaffected — discovery returns the same
12 blocks for them either way — so the curve's near end is real and its far end is not measured.

THE FIX. Group the tree's ModuleLists by their element TYPE, take the type with the largest TOTAL count,
and concatenate every list of that type in tree order. A flat trunk has exactly one such list and comes
back byte-identical (12 blocks, same objects, same order), which is the equality this refactor must be
checked against — every number in the ledger was measured under the old shape and only the staged
families may move. Ambiguity (two types tied on total) still raises rather than picking, keeping the
existing discipline.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not say Swin or ConvNeXt would have won. It says their numbers are facts
about a handicapped run, so they cannot be used to close the supervised-pretraining or the
architectural-distance question — which is precisely what they were being used for.
notes:
FIXED. blocks() now groups every non-empty ModuleList by the TYPE of its elements, takes the type with
the largest total, and concatenates its lists in tree order. Ambiguity is two TYPES tied on total, which
still raises.

Verified on the real trunks, CPU, card-free — flat unchanged, staged whole:

  small     12  last=encoder.layer.11          (unchanged)
  base      12  last=encoder.layer.11          (unchanged)
  v3base    12  last=model.layer.11            (unchanged)
  vitin21k  12  last=layers.11                 (unchanged)
  raddino   12  last=encoder.layer.11          (unchanged)
  swinbase  24  last=layers.3.blocks.1         (was 18, last=layers.2.blocks.17)
  cnxbase   36  last=stages.3.layers.2         (was 27, last=stages.2.layers.26)

So no member on disk was measured under a rule that has now changed, and the two staged families now
open their top. The unit test asserts the flat case comes back as the SAME objects, not merely the same
count, because that identity is what protects the ledger.

One deliberate behaviour change beyond the bug: several lists of the same type are now ONE family rather
than an ambiguity. That is the fix itself, and it costs the ability to refuse an encoder-decoder whose
halves share a block type. No trunk in the registry has one; the model.py double that did was rebuilt to
express its ambiguity as two types.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and it is the expensive half: swin_supervised (0.8331), cnx_own_recipe (0.8186) and
cnx_dense (0.7927) are all facts about runs whose top never trained. Re-running is ~3 h of card each and
priced separately.

title: board_transfer is ONE-FOR-ONE at the top, not 23% — and that re-opens the discarded increments
description:
QUOTED WRONG FOR THE THIRD TIME, and this time it changed a strategic conclusion. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_the-mixing-side-is-spent.md shipped the line 'pass-through is ~23%, so even a real +0.003 offline is +0.0007 on the board'. It was written from prose, never from the module. Refit 2026-08-30 05:38Z:

  compression: median +1.23 board points per holdout point over the WHOLE record
    at or above 0.8670: 16 resolved pairs, median +0.98 [+0.94, +1.08]
    at or above 0.8692:  4 resolved pairs, median +0.80 [+0.70, +1.19]
  inversions: 9/392 pairs, 0/252 of the pairs the holdout RESOLVED (gap >= 0.0053)

BoardPair.ratio() is board delta over holdout delta, raw AUC both sides. +0.98 is ONE-FOR-ONE. An offline +0.003 is +0.003 on the board — twice the board's own 0.0015 resolution, not half of it. The prior stale quote went the other way: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the_ensemble_axes_and_which_are_levers.md line 99 says '+0.0005 offline is +0.0023 board' (a slope of 4.6). Three quotes, three different numbers, none from the module.

WHAT IT CHANGES. Nothing about the mixing knobs: they are flat on the holdout and one-for-one transfer of zero is zero. It changes the OTHER branch. Every mechanism-sound increment this project measured and then discarded for sitting under the 0.0062 paired floor is worth approximately its own size on the board:

  distillation, architecture-distant   +0.0035
  label TABLE swap                     +0.0034
  specialist per column (ceiling)      +0.0043
  supervision policy (knee-fuhq)       +0.0034

NONE OF THEM HAS EVER BEEN STACKED. Each was measured alone against a control and filed as under-floor. Their sum is +0.0146, which is above the 0.0062 floor AND above the 1.5% bar's neighbourhood, and the gap to the live leader is 0.008. This is exactly the branch knee-m69u names as one of its two closing conditions ('the ceiling reading is accepted and the plan turns to banking increments instead') and the arithmetic that was thought to forbid it was an arithmetic error.

THE 0/252 IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE LICENCE. Where our holdout resolves a pair at all, the board has never once ordered it the other way. All nine inversions are pairs the holdout itself declared unresolved. So the offline ruler is trustworthy exactly where it speaks, and the correct move is to make it speak — build ONE member that stacks the increments and measure the STACK against the floor, rather than continuing to measure the terms one at a time in a band the ruler cannot see.

THE CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH IT. Additivity is an ASSUMPTION, not a measurement. The four terms may share mechanism (distillation and supervision both move ORDERING; the label swap and the supervision policy both act on the target table), in which case the stack is worth one term and not four. That is what the arm tests, and a null there is informative: it would say the increments are one increment wearing four names, which is the same shape of finding as the pool being 82 percent one number.

FIRST ACTION: fix the two interpretation files (mixing-side done, ensemble-axes line 99 outstanding), then build the stack arm.
PRICE: 72 min of card for arm stack_increments.sh (12 epochs at 336 px, 362 s an epoch measured on contrast_pool). No slot.

P(clears 1.5%) < 0.05 — it is not supposed to. P(clears the 0.0062 paired floor, the ADDITIVE branch) 0.30-0.40: the two deltas are +0.0034 and +0.0035, both reproduced against their own controls, and their mechanisms are prima facie disjoint (one moves the target TABLE, one adds an ordering term from a foreign teacher). Against that, the label delta was measured at 224 px on 12 slices without held annotations and is transported here to 336/20 holding them, which is the likeliest single reason it reads short.

The ensemble gain this arm aims at does not come from seating it. The 0.23 solo-into-seat dilution makes +0.0069 solo worth ~+0.0016 in one seat, under the board's 0.0015 resolution plus noise. It comes from RETRAINING THE SEATS on a landed recipe, which moves the entry's offline score directly and therefore transfers one-for-one. calibsix_v1 is the precedent: five members retrained under a different supervision policy, singles worse (0.923 vs 0.925), six-seat entry +0.002.

JUSTIFIED AS A GATE, not as an improvement. Both branches are worth the 72 minutes. ADDITIVE licenses a six-arm roster retrain (~7 h of card) with a measured reason. NULL says the increments are one increment wearing two names, closes the bank-the-increments branch of knee-m69u, and leaves the non-DINOv2 lane (owner-approved 2026-08-30) as the only one standing. Neither branch leaves the schedule where it is.
notes:
RESULT 2026-08-30: stack_increments_s2026 best holdout 0.8642 against control calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634 = +0.0008, against an additive prediction of 0.8703 (+0.0069). Paired floor 0.0062; this is an eighth of it. Pre-registered NULL band 0.8600-0.8668 — the run landed inside it.

NULL BRANCH TAKEN. The label TABLE swap (+0.0034) and architecture-distant distillation (+0.0035) do not compose: one term's worth arrived and not even that cleanly. Both act on what the model is asked to ORDER — the swap by changing the target table, distillation by adding a teacher's ordering — so they compete for the same headroom rather than stacking. This is the risk the bead itself named ('the increments are one increment wearing two names').

WHAT CLOSES. The bank-the-increments branch of knee-m69u. The two unstacked increments (specialist per column +0.0043, supervision policy +0.0034) are NOT re-armed on this reading — their sum with these two was the whole case, and the case required a composition that has now been measured absent. The six-arm roster retrain (~7 h of card) that the ADDITIVE branch would have licensed is not armed.

WHAT DOES NOT CLOSE. The individual increments are unharmed: each still reproduces against its own control and each is still worth about its own size on the board when it is the only thing changed. What is refuted is that they SUM. The board_transfer correction itself (+0.98 one-for-one at/above 0.8670, not 23%) stands — it was refit from the module, and the two interpretation files it corrected stay corrected.

Ledger: experiments/README.md, section 'stack_increments — the two banked increments do not compose'. Epoch trace 0.7525 .. 0.8642, peak at the last recorded epoch of ten under a twelve-epoch budget; the last three epochs moved 0.0033 total, so a longer fit does not reach the prediction.

title: annotated_readings and noise_binding reported each member's score under another member's name
description:
FOUND 2026-08-30 03:00Z. FIXED the same hour. The gold-ruler instrument -- the only one that scores members against the KIND of label the board actually uses (knee-9198) -- crossed names and values on every multi-checkpoint call whose cache grouping differed from argv order.

THE DEFECT. AnnotatedReadings.readings appends arrays in MemberReadings.slabs order, which groups members sharing a decode so the cache is paid once. It returned bare arrays. Both annotated_readings.main and noise_binding.main then re-paired them against their own --checkpoints list with zip(..., strict=True). strict guards LENGTH; the lengths always matched and the IDENTITIES were crossed. supervision_gap was the one safe consumer, because it only RankAverages them, which is order-insensitive.

HOW IT SURFACED, and it was nearly missed. A six-member --overlap read came back byte-identical to its plain read, while a three-member --overlap read of the same checkpoints gave different numbers. A flag that changes nothing in one call and everything in another is not a policy effect. Read order was band_dense, calib_dense, band_span, calib_span, blendhold, holdannot against a print order of band_dense, band_span, blendhold, calib_dense, calib_span, holdannot -- so five of six rows were wrong.

WHAT IT ALMOST COST. I had already written down a contradiction against knee-bs4l, a correctly-closed P1: its recorded calib_span_hold - band_span_hold = +0.0129 on the gold ruler read as -0.0165 under the crossed table. Un-crossed, the pair reads +0.0129 to the digit. bs4l was right the whole time and the reading was mine. It also produced a fake finding -- 'the gold ruler reorders members, Spearman 0.43, band_span_hold last on proxy and second on gold' -- which was an artifact of the crossing and would have been filed as a discovery.

THE FIX. readings now returns list[tuple[Path, array]]: each array carries the checkpoint that produced it, so the pairing cannot be re-derived by position anywhere downstream. Both crossed call sites consume the pair; supervision_gap takes [values for _, values in per_member].

THE PROOF, an equality rather than an argument. Each of the six was read ALONE, where crossing is impossible, and the fixed six-member table reproduces all six to four decimals:
  band_dense_hold 0.8956 | band_span_hold 0.9023 | blendhold 0.8952
  calib_dense_hold 0.9117 | calib_span_hold 0.9152 | holdannot 0.8932

SCOPE OF THE DAMAGE, to be checked and not assumed: any multi-checkpoint annotated_readings or noise_binding output recorded before today may be crossed. Single-checkpoint outputs cannot be. bs4l's numbers are confirmed correct. Whoever re-reads an old multi-member gold table should re-run it rather than trust it.

Same class as knee-y8y (a member scored as a function it was never read as) and as the SupervisionGap.reported/against column-by-position defect recorded in 2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md. Third time position has stood in for identity in this codebase.

title: After the contamination finding, every mapped axis is closed or knob-sized — name a NEW axis or stop arming
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-29 17:59Z, no card, no slot. Written because the card sat free for 40 minutes and the honest reason is that nothing on the board prices above the bar, not that momentum ran out.

WHAT knee-ie30 CHANGED. The +0.0304 foreign member gap was 896 of our 909 holdout studies inside their training set. On the gold 58 and on the board the best published member of this field and ours are LEVEL. So the six P0s resting on 'rivals hold a better single model' have no measurement behind them, and the search for the missing 0.010 cannot be pointed at member quality any more.

THE AXES, EACH WITH ITS OWN NUMBER AND ITS OWN CLOSER:
  ensemble COUNT        saturates from ~9 members, +0.0018 six->twenty-four (mix curve)
  ensemble SPREAD       -0.0088 vs quality-built, 1.4 floors (record_mix DIVERSE)
  per-label WEIGHTING   oracle 0.8590 vs plain average 0.8588 — headroom +0.0002 bounds EVERY scheme
  combiner              flat within 0.0005 (knee-qhzd)
  decode GEOMETRY       crop80_span -0.0099 against its own control; in-plane extent and through-plane
                        span are ANTAGONISTS (knee-nas5, closed)
  slice ORDER           depth_true seat value -0.0002 (knee-tqn)
  composition/STACK     seven of seven second terms below the calib_dense_hold control, p=0.008 (knee-orjq)
  recalibration         0.000 by construction — the board metric is a per-label rank AUC
  label TABLE swap      +0.0034 measured, every re-weighting of the readers on disk inside +/-0.008
  DISTILLATION          +0.0016 self-teacher, +0.0035 architecture-distant, both at weight 0.3, both
                        under the 0.0062 floor; and the seat ruler declined it 44th of 121 because
                        distillation moves ORDERING while the seat ruler prices PIXEL GROUP
  SPECIALIST per column  priced, not refuted: closing MCL and Fracture COMPLETELY is +0.0043 on the
                        twelve-label mean, a quarter of the bar, for 3.1 h of card (focus_mcl.sh)

CORRECTION THIS AUDIT OWES. focus_latmen's 0.4747 is an EPOCH-0 checkpoint of a run that never finished
— it is a dead checkpoint, not a verdict on specialists. It was briefly read here as evidence against
the specialist axis. The specialist axis is closed on PRICE (the +0.0043 ceiling above), which is a
different and weaker closure: a reason to re-open it would be a cheaper route to the same columns, not
a new argument that specialisation works.

WHAT REMAINS STANDING, and it is one thing: knee-fuhq's shared supervision ceiling. supervision_gap over
six --hold-annotations members reads labels - model: -0.0498 [-0.0742, -0.0255], the model beating its own
labels on ten of twelve findings, on models we fitted. Two independently-built systems landing on the same
0.923 board score is what that ceiling looks like from outside. The lane is confirmed LIVE and confirmed
SMALL (+0.0034 on the metric, +0.0070 on the six findings a reader can reach).

THE ACTUAL QUESTION, and no arm answers it: is there an axis nobody has mapped, or is 0.943 near this
data's ceiling under our supervision? Until one is named, arming a knob costs 40-50 min of card for a
term the ledger already prices under the floor. The card idling is the correct move, not a gap.

Blocks nothing. Closes when a NEW axis is named with a mechanism that could plausibly deliver 1.5%, or
when the ceiling reading is accepted and the plan turns to banking increments instead.

PRICE: mricore_corpus costs 80 min of card (12 epochs x ~400s). Prior is negative and measured - five medical-corpus trunks all cost: radnet_family 0.6716, radnet_pinned 0.7505, radiodino_s16 0.8108, radiodino_corpus 0.8214, raddino_dense 0.8137. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.03; P(solo >= 0.85) ~ 0.20; P(seat gain >= +0.0040, the board-resolvable step) ~ 0.05. It is therefore NOT sold as an improvement, it is an INSTRUMENT on two axes: (1) third point on a two-point corpus line, separating "medical corpus costs" from "PROJECTION corpus costs" - both existing medical points are radiographs, MRI-CORE is 6.1M MRI slices; (2) first test of the distance/quality frontier measured 2026-09-06 by seat_requirement, where every member below 0.90 agreement with the seated blend has NEGATIVE gain and best solo falls ~0.04 per 0.2 of agreement. A null lands on that curve and closes the corpus axis; anything above it re-opens external pretraining as the one route to +0.0117. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_one-more-member-cannot-close-the-gap.md
notes: PRICE (2026-09-06, added because arm_check refused to let it run unpriced): 80 min of card (12 epochs x ~400s). Prior is NEGATIVE and measured - five medical-corpus trunks all cost: radnet_family 0.6716, radnet_pinned 0.7505, radiodino_s16 0.8108, radiodino_corpus 0.8214, raddino_dense 0.8137. P(solo >= 0.85) ~20%. P(seat gain >= +0.0040, the board-resolvable step) ~5%. So it is NOT sold as an improvement - it is an INSTRUMENT, on two axes at once: (1) it is the third point on a two-point corpus line and separates 'medical corpus costs' from 'PROJECTION corpus costs', since both existing medical points are radiographs and MRI-CORE is 6.1M MRI slices; (2) it is the first test of the distance/quality frontier measured 2026-09-06 in seat_requirement - every member below 0.90 agreement with the seated blend has NEGATIVE gain, and best solo falls ~0.04 per 0.2 of agreement, so the question is whether a same-modality foreign trunk lands OFF that curve or on it. A null lands on the curve and closes the corpus axis for good; anything above it re-opens external pretraining as the one route to +0.0117. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_one-more-member-cannot-close-the-gap.md

title: Read A's whole-corpus pool is EIGHT members on disk, not three — the refit lane was pricing card time we do not have to spend
description:
AUDITED 2026-08-29T12:31Z by reading the OPTIONS of every .pt under processed/, not by reading arm scripts. Zero card, zero slots.

Eight checkpoints already sit at read A's exact decode cell (20 slices, band 0.1-0.9, 336 px, canonical, tie=first) AND are fitted --fold -1, i.e. whole-corpus, the fit trioseat_v1 (0.938) and fourseat_v1 use:

  base_dense_ff       DINOv2-BASE trunk        <- a different ENCODER inside read A's decode
  final_ws_cf         final weight-averaging   <- trioseat seat 1
  final_ws_e12        final weight-averaging, 12 epochs
  grade_ladder_cf     the grade ladder         <- trioseat seat 2
  grade_ladder_ff     the grade ladder, final fit
  small_batch6_ff     batch 6                  <- fourseat seat 4
  through_dense_cf    the through-plane read   <- trioseat seat 3
  through_dense_ff    the through-plane read, final fit

WHY THIS CHANGES THE LANE. greedy7_v1 (seven FOLD-0 members, 0.8712 offline) read 0.933 against trioseat's three WHOLE-CORPUS seats at 0.938, so the one-decode roster can only grow through whole-corpus members, and the plan was to REFIT the greedy walk's fold-0 picks at ~45 min of card each -- five of them, ~4 hours. Eight are already here. The refit lane is not wrong, it is partly REDUNDANT, and it was being priced in card-hours when the first four or five seats cost a kernel push and a slot.

THE MOST INTERESTING ONE IS base_dense_ff. It is a BASE trunk inside read A's decode: architecture diversity at ZERO extra decode cost, which is the one combination no entry on this board holds. raptorseat bought its +0.002 by adding an architecture AND a decode; fleettwo showed the second foreign decode adds nothing (0.942, flat). A trunk swap inside one decode separates those two terms on the cheap side.

THE TWINS ARE NOT SEATS, PROBABLY. grade_ladder_cf/_ff, through_dense_cf/_ff and final_ws_cf/_e12 are the same treatment at a different fit. Expect them to behave like raptor's v4_full x v4_full_swa pair (agreement 0.9955, one model twice). They cost nothing to test offline with RankAverage.agreement, which needs no labels and no slot -- do that before seating one.

WHAT CANNOT BE DONE. None of these has an honest holdout number: --fold -1 means the fold-0 studies are inside their training set, so RecordMix excludes them and neither seat_value nor decode_entry can price them. The only offline instrument that works on this pool is AGREEMENT (label-free), and the only quality ruler is the board. That is why this is a roster-DESIGN bead and not a greedy walk.

FIRST STEP, NO CARD, NO SLOT: pairwise RankAverage.agreement over the eight, to collapse the twins and rank the survivors by distance. Then a five- or six-seat one-decode all-whole-corpus entry, gated on fourseat_v1's score (still pending at the time of writing; its >=0.939 branch licenses exactly this).

PRICE: 0 card. ~20 min CPU for the agreement matrix. ONE slot for the entry, and only after fourseat lands. title: Two reads, many seats: the entry design the decode map implies
description:
THE DESIGN, stated before any number licenses it, so the pricing that follows is a gate and not a search.

Build one entry that fully seats BOTH of the reads we already own, instead of an entry that seats a few members across four reads.

  read A  canonical, 20 slices, band 0.1-0.9, centre image, crop 130mm   49 fold-0 members owned, 3 seated (trioseat_v1)
  read B  canonical, 12 slices, band 0.2-0.8, centre image, crop 130mm   ~30 fold-0 members owned, 1 seated (the champion's lr4e-5_ws_cf)

The pinned champion spends about four decodes to seat seven members. This design spends TWO to seat as many as price positive, and the two are reads the champion already pays for.

WHY IT IS NOT A KNOB. It is a change of unit. Every seat argument here has priced a member against a decode budget, on the premise that a different resolution is a different pixel group. Ensemble.reads keys a decode on (scheme, slices, tie, reading) and excludes size and both poolings by design; dry_run confirms it, serving 224, 336 and 448 from one read. The premise was wrong, so the budget those arguments were spending does not exist for these candidates.

WHY READ B IS THE BETTER READ despite being the smaller pool: all 49 of read A's members were fitted at 336, so its free diversity is treatment only. Read B carries 224, 336 and 448, so it offers treatment AND resolution diversity on one decode — and it is the read that is seated ONCE.

WHAT MUST BE TRUE, and the order to establish it:
1. The seats are worth something. experiments/arms/trio_seat_value.sh prices both pools offline against trioseat_v1 and against the pinned champion, queued behind merged_span_cf. Bar is the 0.0062 holdout floor and nothing else, because there is no decode budget to trade against. HONEST PRIOR: members from one cell are correlated and most price at zero; the expected outcome is a handful of seats per read, not thirty.
2. The decode count holds at roster scale. A 32-member dry_run reported two reads, splitting the tissue-centred members off correctly. The shipped roster must be dry_run again before a slot, because a member whose crop or tie disagrees silently adds a decode and turns an efficiency entry into a slower one.
3. Packaging. Only 7 of read B and 28 of read A are in dimiturnt/kneemri-members. The rest are a dataset push, no card.

WHAT WOULD KILL IT: every candidate inside the floor in step 1, which would mean the reads are already saturated at 3 and 1 seats and that trioseat's +0.013 was the whole effect of that axis. That is a real possibility and this bead is not written as if it were not.

Reads on: knee-z652, knee-vfnr. Write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-29_seats-per-decode.md
notes:
STEP 2 ESTABLISHED FROM METADATA, before any pricing (2026-08-29 13:58Z, zero card).

roster_reads over the FULL candidate universe of the design - read A's pool plus read B's pool -
reports 44 seats on exactly 2 decodes, 22.0 seats per decode:

  27 members at [224, 336, 448]  canonical / 12 slices / band 0.2-0.8 / centre image / 130mm / tie first / spread
  17 members at [336]            canonical / 20 slices / band 0.1-0.9 / centre image / 130mm / tie first / spread

The pinned champion seats 7 members on about 4 decodes, 1.75 per decode. So the design's COST claim
holds at roster scale and is not an artefact of the 32-member probe: nothing in either pool silently
adds a read.

Read A was checked the same way GROUP2 had been, and it found one splitter that had gone unnoticed:
band140_s2026 (crop 140mm, which lives inside reading) cost a second decode. It is dropped from
trio_seat_value.sh's CANDIDATES for that reason alone and stays a priceable candidate on the
decode-distance question. Read A is 336px throughout - its free diversity is TREATMENT only, which is
the measured form of the bead's claim that read B is the better read.

This bounds the design, it does not license it. Step 1 (does any of it price above the 0.0062 floor)
is still what decides, and runs behind raddino_dense.

title: The 224 pixel group is a complete second one-decode roster, already built and never read as a group
description:
FOURTEEN fold-0 checkpoints sit at (12 slices, band 0.2-0.8, 224px): adjacent224, base224, blendhold, confident224, holdannot, labelwise224, mixup224, mixup224_long, mixup224_strong, native224, native224_long, nocycle224_long, normcount224, tissue224. They were fitted as a RESOLUTION family, one arm at a time, and every reading of them was a member-quality reading against a 336 control. Nobody has ever asked what they are worth AS A GROUP.

WHY THAT IS NOW THE QUESTION. trioseat_v1 scored 0.938 by seating three members that share one decode, +0.013 over a single seat for one decode's cost — the first evidence in this project that a pixel group holds several seats. If that holds, a group of fourteen is not fourteen members; it is one decode with up to fourteen seats behind it.

WHY THIS GROUP RATHER THAN ANY OTHER. Its decode is the cheapest we own: 94 s/epoch against 336's 290, a measured 3.1x, at a member cost of -0.0023 (native224 0.8502 vs the 336 control lr4e-5_ws 0.8525) which is INSIDE the 0.0062 holdout floor — flat, not worse, and knee-s9cr already corrected the record that this was untested. Both rival self-reported singles above ours (0.942, 0.938) are at 224.

So it is the one lever that moves all three of the things being asked for at once: a new pixel group is the decode axis knee-nas5 measured transferring at 2.4x (SCORE), the cheapest decode we own is the efficiency-prize entry (EFFICIENCY, where our row is stale at 0.925 while accuracy shows 0.943), and a 3.1x epoch is the budget every future arm is fitted in (EXPERIMENT SPEED).

COST TO FIND OUT: ZERO CARD. All fourteen checkpoints are on disk. Only base224_s2026 and blendhold_s2026 are packaged in dimiturnt/kneemri-members; the other twelve are a dataset push and no fit. experiments/arms/trio_seat_value.sh (knee-vfnr) now prices this pool TWICE — against trioseat_v1, asking whether two one-decode groups compose, and against the pinned champion, asking whether a cheap decode earns a seat in our best roster at all. It is queued behind merged_span_cf.

A positive against the champion is a SCORE result and outranks everything else queued. A positive against trioseat with a negative against the champion is an efficiency-only play, which is still a prize we are entered for. Both negative kills the group as a group and leaves 224 as what it already was: a cheap fit for future arms.

2026-08-29 10:05 UTC — THE WHOLE-DISK MAP, measured by a tool rather than by hand, and it corrected the hand numbers.

`python -m kneemri.kaggle.roster_reads` (new; groups raw checkpoints by `Member.decode_key`, the SAME

    9 members at [336]            canonical / 12 slices / band 0.1-0.9
    3 members at [336]            canonical / 20 slices / band 0.2-0.8
    ... nine more reads of one or two members each
  188 seats on 13 decodes = 14.5 seats per decode

TWO LARGE READS, and they are NOT equivalent:

  read A — 20 slices, 0.1-0.9:  58 on disk, 27 packaged, 3 seated (trioseat_v1), 336 ONLY
  read B — 12 slices, 0.2-0.8: 108 on disk, 19 packaged, 1 seated (the champion's lr4e-5_ws_cf),
                               carrying 224 AND 336 AND 448

Read B is the bigger pool AND the only one holding several resolutions, so it offers treatment AND

WHAT IS BUILDABLE TODAY: 46 packaged members already ride those two reads, so an entry seating all of
them costs TWO decodes, no card time and no dataset push — a kernel edit and a slot. The pinned champion

STILL A COST RESULT. Nothing here says a seat is worth taking; correlated members from one cell most

title: Treatment diversity is a SEAT axis, not a decode axis: trioseat bought +0.013 from one pixel group
description:
OPENED 2026-08-29 by trioseat_v1 reading 0.938 against a pre-registered 0.925-0.929.

THE MEASUREMENT. final_ws_cf, grade_ladder_cf and through_dense_cf are matched on slices (20), band (0.1-0.9), image size (336) and backbone (dinov2-small). They differ only in SUPERVISION TREATMENT: final weight-averaging, the grade ladder, the through-plane read. Served at 1/3 each through one decode they read 0.938, +0.013 over `soloseat_v1` 0.925 -- level with onepair_v1's +0.011, which bought its bonus by crossing an architecture boundary and paying for a second decode.

WHY THIS IS A P0. Every roster decision in this ledger for the last week has been priced off knee-nas5's pixel-group collapse (0.0059 offline arriving as 0.014 board) and off the architecture-monoculture interpretation, both of which were being read as 'seats in one pixel group are redundant'. They never measured that. What they measured is that PIXEL GROUPS collapse. Treatment does not travel with the pixel group, and on this board it is worth as much per seat as architecture distance while costing nothing at inference beyond a head.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, AND WHY IT SERVES BOTH PRIZES AT ONCE. A roster maximising treatment diversity inside a SMALL number of decodes is simultaneously the accuracy play (more seats that actually disagree) and the efficiency play (few decodes). The efficiency track's top 20 span 0.925-0.948 with median 0.935; trioseat already clears that median at one decode.

THE OPEN QUESTION THIS DOES NOT ANSWER. Whether treatment diversity and decode diversity ADD or substitute. raptorseat 0.943 holds ~4 decodes and 7 treatments and cannot separate them. The clean next instrument is a roster with MORE treatments at the SAME one decode -- a quadruple or a quintuple inside the (20, 0.1-0.9) cell -- read against trioseat 0.938. If the count keeps paying inside one group, the decode axis is a smaller share of the champion's bonus than the ledger currently assumes, and the cheap lane is much longer than one entry.

FIRST STEP COSTS NO CARD: the pool holds 131 arms. Enumerate every existing checkpoint that already sits at (20 slices, 0.1-0.9) and differs by treatment, and greedy them offline on the fold-0 holdout. Only then spend a slot.
notes:
2026-08-29 14:24Z — CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT ON THE WHOLE POOL, and the arm built for it is retired.

The question was 'how many treatment seats does one decode hold?' It is answered, and not on a sample:
198 checkpoints enumerate to 191 members on 13 reads (14.7 seats per decode). Read B — canonical / 12
slices / band 0.2-0.8 / centre image / 130 mm / tie first / spacing spread — holds 108 members across
[224, 336, 448]; read A holds 59 at 336 only. Resolution is not in Member.decode_key and neither pooling
is, so one read serves three sizes.

ALL 41 SCOREABLE READ-B CANDIDATES were priced against honest12 (108 minus five smoke/other-fold, minus
confident224_s2026 which RecordMix refuses under a different label table, minus every checkpoint with no
holdout record). Best marginal +0.0003 (merged_blend_s2026), second +0.0001 (blendlabels_s2026),
everything else 0 to -0.0005. seat_value's own verdict: 'best is +0.0003, inside +0.0015: this ruler
cannot tell it from the incumbent.' The earlier 24-candidate pricing read the same number to the fourth
decimal, so this is the same null at 3.7x the denominator, not a confirmation of a sample.

THE PATTERN AT 41 IS THE FINDING, not the value. Every one of the 41 shares ONE best move — swap out
honest12's dud mae_matched_s2026 (0.6735 solo). Not a single candidate is a marginal ADDITION. A free
seat on a saturated read buys nothing; the only value on that read is not being the worst member already
sitting on it.

THE CONTROL BIASES THIS UPWARD, so the null is stronger than it reads. honest12 is 0.006 weaker on the
board than the pinned champion, and a seat is easier to earn in a weaker roster. It is also FORCED, not
preferred: every member of raptorseat_v1 and trioseat_v1 is fold -1, has seen every holdout study, carries
no holdout record, and seat_value refuses both rosters by name.

WHAT SURVIVES. The COST half only, as an efficiency-track lens (knee-7lyz): 44 seats on 2 decodes against
the champion's 7 on ~4 is a real runtime argument even though it is not a score argument.
WHAT IS RETIRED. experiments/arms/trio_seat_value.sh and experiments/arms/packaged_seats.sh, their
watchers killed and their after.sh markers deleted; queue_check reads clean.
WHAT IT POINTS AT. Decode DISTANCE, the lane the nulls left open — experiments/arms/crop80_tissue_full.sh
(knee-17kn), queued behind ARM DONE raddino_dense. It is confounded today because every distant member we
own is also a weak one, and crop80_tissue's weakness has a recorded cause that is not the mechanism
(--epochs 8 against everyone else's 12).

title: The champion is an architecture MONOCULTURE, and that is the mechanical cause of the 0.937-0.941 plateau
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-28 by dumping all six calibsix member configs. Every member of comp/champion.json is facebook/dinov2-small (DIM 384, 22M) at img=336, whole_stack=True, the SAME six slots (SAG_FLUID_FS, COR_FLUID_FS, AX_FLUID_FS, SAG_FLUID_NOFS, COR_T1, SAG_T1), the SAME head (pool=cls_mean token pool -> slice_pooling=max -> slot_pooling=attend SlotHead), encoder_layer=-1, lora_rank=0, crop_mm=130.0, head_lr=1e-3, backbone_lr=4e-5, rank_weight=1.0.

THREE THINGS VARY ACROSS THE WHOLE CHAMPION: slices (12 vs 20), band ([0.1,0.9] vs [0.2,0.8]), and through_plane (True on through_dense_cf alone). That is RECIPE diversity, not architecture diversity, and it is the direct mechanical explanation for seven differently-seated entries landing in a 0.004 band (0.937-0.941) against a 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor: seven ways of reseating six copies of one lens.

THE ROSTER'S ONLY NON-DINOv2 MEMBER is lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026.pt at 0.8215, too weak to have ever earned a seat.

THE SINGLE-MODEL CEILING IS NOT DINOv2's FAULT. calibsolo scored 0.923 and the foreign raptor_v4_swa (coatnet_rmlp_2_rw_384 at 384 px, different corpus, different decode, different head) scored 0.923 the SAME DAY. Two unrelated stacks, one number. That coincidence says the ceiling is not architecture-limited but PRETRAINING-DISTRIBUTION-limited: both trunks are natural-image pretrained. It also settles knee-9g28 in knee-3uje's favour — the claimed +0.030 foreign member-quality gap does not exist.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GOAL. knee-urvf's bonus law (board(ensemble) ~ board(best single) + 0.0143 mean over three clean pairings; calibsolo->calibsix_v1 is +0.018) puts 0.950 out of reach of any reseating: it needs a single near 0.9357 and nothing we own is within 0.012 of that. The remaining axes are (1) a trunk pretrained OUTSIDE natural images — knee-7l4e, armed, (2) per-finding member routing instead of one global rank average, (3) slice budget: 12-20 slices of a 30-40 slice stack, so thin findings (meniscal tear, cartilage defect) can miss the slice they live on.

DO NOT close this by reseating. It is closed by a member whose errors are somewhere else.
notes:
2026-09-03 04:38Z: two arms now attack this directly, both on the card axis rather than the combiner axis.

RUNNING ortho_pool_read - ortholarge (v3large continued on 1.25M knee images) at the pool's standard 336 px read, one variable moved from depth_regions_narrow_s2026 = 0.8554. Motivation is a frozen probe at each trunk's own ridge penalty (knee-x4yx's fix): ortholarge 0.8249 focal-max / 0.8170 mean_max against v3large 0.8046 / 0.7968 - the SAME +0.020 on both readouts, which is what makes it a trunk property and not a pooling artefact. Every previous ortholarge member was read at 224 px and landed 0.7537-0.7589, i.e. BELOW the frozen floor, which is a recipe fault not a trunk verdict. Epoch 0 landed 0.7540 at 1184s (contended; card since cleared). Pre-registration in the arm header, four branches.

QUEUED cnx_rate_ladder - gated on the arm's pid. 2 rates x 3 epochs, an INSTRUMENT that produces no member. It prices the fair-budget ConvNeXt arm the ledger records as 'attempted and left incomplete, not answered'.

Neither is a seating operation and neither wants a slot.

  strong-and-distant five (merged_labelwise_cf, labelwise_dense_s2026, small_batch6_s2026, finding_calib_dense_s2026, merged_blend_cf): 0.8754
  champion holdout twins (calib_span/grade_ladder/merged_blend/lr4e-5_ws/through_dense _s2026): 0.8700 — reproduces the ledger's 0.8701 exactly, so same ruler.

title: RAD-DINO cold re-run: the only medical-pretrained trunk we own was killed on a run with the wrong normalization
description:
ARMED 2026-08-28T04:51Z, queued behind the fleet teacher pass via await_free_card.sh (logs/arm_raddino_rerun.log).

THE DEFECT THAT VOIDS THE OLD NUMBER. raddino_dense ran 2026-08-23 and entered the ledger at 0.8137, -0.0375 against base_dense 0.8512, and the owner's ban list has carried 'do NOT re-queue raddino_dense (refuted)' ever since. The normalization fix landed 2026-08-25 in commit 3b74685 — TWO DAYS AFTER the run. For its entire twelve epochs RAD-DINO was fed the ImageNet constants while its own preprocessor_config.json declares 0.5307/0.2583 (greyscale, repeated over three channels): inputs 0.20 std off its pretraining distribution with a 12.8 percent scale error. The CONTROL was correct, because DINOv2-base does declare the ImageNet constants. THE BAN IS NOT BROKEN. The standing ban is on the WARM start and the RATE refit. This is neither: it is a COLD re-run from the HuggingFace checkpoint. A warm start is in fact impossible — the 2026-08-23 checkpoint carries the wrong constants baked into its own state dict as persistent buffers, which is what makes the owner's ban correct twice over. The arm file experiments/arms/raddino_dense.sh was already rewritten on 2026-08-25 to say exactly this and has been sitting unarmed since.

WHY IT IS THE BIGGEST LEVER ON THE BOARD. The champion is six DINOv2-small at 336 px with one head, one slot scheme and one slot list; only slices (12/20), band and one through_plane flag vary. title: Matched 58-study read: our member is LEVEL with Raptor (0.9152 vs 0.9167), and knee-rh4t's 0.017 member gap was a two-ruler artefact
description:
Both sides hold out the same 58 radiologist-annotated studies (our *_hold members train with --hold-annotations; their corpus is 4349 = 4407-58), so their published per-label 'aucs' and our cached annotated_predictions are on ONE ruler for the first time.

Macro: calib_span_hold 0.9152 vs raptor_ft_coatnet_v4_full 0.9167, delta +0.0016 against a macro SE of ~0.012. A genuine null.

CONSEQUENCE for knee-rh4t: the ~0.017 member gap was built by comparing our BOARD single (soloseat 0.925) to rivals' FORUM claims (0.938-0.942). Those are different rulers on different studies. On a matched ruler there is no gap. knee-rh4t is not refuted -- the board numbers are what they are -- but its MECHANISM sentence ('their member is better') is now unsupported, and the residual has to be explained by something other than member quality.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: n=58. Hanley-McNeil SE per label runs 0.031-0.072, so no single per-label delta clears. The per-label complementarity pattern (they win Medial OA +0.0884, Lateral OA, Effusion, Bakers; we win PF OA -0.1017, Lateral Meniscus, ACL, Medial Meniscus) is a HYPOTHESIS. The per-label oracle reads +0.0188 over the better single, and max-of-two-noisy-draws at this SE manufactures ~0.023 by itself -- so the oracle is fully explained by selection noise and is NOT evidence.

NEXT: knee-9g28 scores their checkpoints on our 909-study fold-0 holdout, 15x the studies, which is the test that can actually settle the complementarity claim.
notes:
2026-08-28 00:47Z — THE RE-SCORE THIS BEAD ASKED FOR IS IN, AND SELECTION IS NOT THE EXPLANATION.

foreign_ruler now takes --member, so a member can be FIXED IN ADVANCE instead of being the maximum over
the same 58 studies it is then scored on. Named in advance by the 909-study holdout (where
calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634 beats calib_span_hold_s2026 0.8565), read on the 58:

  member                        58-macro   vs raptor_v4_full   vs raptor_v4_full_swa
  calib_span_hold  (chosen ON the 58)  0.9152        +0.0016              -
  calib_dense_hold (named in advance)  0.9117        +0.0051           +0.0033
  macro SE ~0.012 either way — both are still nulls on 58 studies.

THE SELECTION TERM IS 0.0035, AND IT IS OVER SIX ARMS, NOT 105. The cache holds six *_hold members
(0.8932-0.9152), so this bead's own note overstated the search: max-over-6 at this SE, not max-over-105.
Measured, the maximum buys 0.9152 - 0.9117 = 0.0035.

CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE POINT. 0.0035 is a TENTH of the 58-vs-909 disagreement (+0.0016 against
-0.0350, a swing of 0.037). Removing the selection effect moves the 58 delta from +0.0016 to +0.0051 and
leaves the disagreement essentially intact. So the 58 and the 909 do not disagree because our member was
picked on the small set. They disagree because the SETS differ — the 58 flatter our member by 0.059 and
theirs by 0.025, and that asymmetry survives naming the member in advance.

A SECOND FACT, FREE FROM THE SAME READ: the two rulers ORDER our members differently.
calib_dense_hold beats calib_span_hold on the 909 (0.8634 > 0.8565) and loses to it on the 58
(0.9117 < 0.9152). n=58 cannot order two members 0.0035 apart against a macro SE of 0.012, so this is

WHAT IS STILL OPEN. Why the 58 flatter our members so much more than theirs. The 58 are radiologist-
annotated and both sides held them out, so the asymmetry is not a leak; the candidates are the LABEL
SOURCE (the 58 answer radiologists, the 909 answer report-derived labels our members were trained on —

WHAT HAS ALREADY BEEN RULED OUT as the source of the gap, by reading their notebook against our code and NOT by guessing:
  * SLICE SPAN. They take 6-94% of the stack and say cutting the ends cost them collateral-ligament and lateral-meniscus accuracy. We measured that axis with three trained points - 0.20-0.80 = 0.8525, 0.10-0.90 = 0.8565, 0.00-1.00 = 0.8427, an interior optimum - and every shipped member already passes --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9. Their operating point sits between our best and our worst. Consistent, not a gap. See core/data/corpus/band_coverage.py.
  * SLOT ROUTING. Their five slots are sag-fluid / sag-nonfluid / cor-fluid / cor-second / axial. Our canonical six already routes SAG_FLUID_FS, COR_FLUID_FS, AX_FLUID_FS, SAG_FLUID_NOFS, COR_T1, SAG_T1, with an extended nine and a multiscale twelve on top. Ours is the richer scheme.
  * mm-BASED CROP. They crop 140 mm by DICOM pixel spacing; we crop 130 mm the same way, with an 80 mm detail scale beside it.
What is left is BACKBONE (CoAtNet at 384), PER-FINDING ATTENTION (already an arm, knee-xuu5 / labelwise224.sh, whose own text cites this same author), and their soft labels (unmeasurable here - see the sibling bead).
