title: Per-diagnosis slice attention: our own head says it is next, and a 0.924 rival says it matters more than anything else
description:
FOUND 2026-08-26 23:52Z by reading the competition forum, not our ledger. Kaggle user dreaddevelopment published BOTH halves of the model behind a 0.924 public inference notebook: kernels 'knee-mri-twelve-findings-from-a-single-model' (84 votes) and 'knee-mri-training-the-twelve-finding-model'. Both are pulled to external/raptor/. Five fine-tuned checkpoints are also public as datasets (raptor-knee-arms, raptor-knee-arms-x, raptor-cnn336) across three architectures we do not have — ConvNeXt-v2-B@336, CoAtNet@384, EfficientNetV2-L@480. The author states in forum topic 737696 that the same set unblended scores 0.936-0.938.

THE LEVER, AND WHY IT IS A P0 AND NOT A KNOB.

Their head is an attention-MIL pool with ONE ATTENTION CHANNEL PER FINDING:

    self.att   = Linear(F, 256) -> Tanh -> Dropout -> Linear(256, 12)
    a          = softmax(att(h), dim=windows)
    pooled     = einsum('bkn,bkf->bnf', a, h)     # (batch, 12, F) — a separate pooled vector per finding
    logits     = (pooled * clsW).sum(-1) + clsb   # clsW is (12, F), a per-finding readout

Their own words for it: 'the windows are then pooled by an attention layer that has separate weights for each of the twelve findings. THAT LAST PART MATTERS MORE THAN ANYTHING ELSE HERE. A cruciate tear may be visible on two slices while osteoarthritis spreads across many, and one shared pooling weight forces those to compete; giving each finding its own attention lets each draw on the slices that actually show it.'

Ours is the same operator with a SHARED query — kneemri/models/slice_attention.py, gate width 64, Linear(gate, 1). And its docstring already names this exact successor: 'DELIBERATELY TINY: one gate of width 64 and a single shared query... A per-diagnosis query over slices is the obvious next step and is deliberately not taken until a shared one earns it.'

So this is a mechanism converged on from two independent directions: our own architecture note wrote it down as next, and a rival at 0.924 rates it above every other choice in their design. It is also the mechanism that predicts OUR OWN deficit pattern — the labels where we still trail our teacher are MCL -0.0465, Lateral Meniscus -0.0149 and PF OA -0.0071, and the first two are precisely the focal, few-slice findings that a shared pooling weight makes compete with the diffuse ones.

WHY THE SHARED ONE HAS NOT EARNED IT AND THIS SHOULD RUN ANYWAY. The docstring's gate was 'until a shared one earns it', and attend beat max by only +0.0002. But that null is EVIDENCE FOR this arm, not against it: if the shared query is being pulled in twelve directions at once, it should land on approximately the mean, which is approximately the max, which is what +0.0002 says. The shared-query null is what a per-diagnosis lever PREDICTS.

PRICE: WALL-CLOCK ~20 min at 224 (the native224 cell, 94 s/epoch x 12) plus maybe 2 h to build and test the head. GAIN: the author ranks it their top design choice and it is the only untried mechanism that explains the per-label deficit; plausibly 1-2% absolute. P(clears +0.010) ~ 0.45, P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.3. Best ratio on the board — better than adjacent224, which is queued and cheaper but explains less.

FOUR MORE MECHANISMS IN THE SAME NOTEBOOK, filed here so the read is not thrown away:
  1. Windows of 3 PHYSICALLY-CONSECUTIVE slices as RGB, with the window CENTRES spread by linspace across the valid range. Local contiguity, global extent — BOTH. This bears directly on knee-e6sj: our new Adjacent takes ONE contiguous run of 12 and pays for continuity with extent, which is that arm's own risk branch 4. Their geometry buys both and is the shape to test next if adjacent224 reads flat. We already own the local half as slice_pooling 'channels'.
  2. Soft LLM targets — twelve PROBABILITIES per report, a hedged 'suspected tear' emitted as ~0.8 rather than 1. Confirms our label lane and our --calibrated-targets independently.
  3. The 58 gold studies held out for validation and NEVER trained on — our --hold-annotations, priced at -0.0005 to -0.0015.
  4. Weight averaging over the best three epochs, written as a second checkpoint. Free at inference, unlike prediction averaging. Near our --ema but not the same operator.

DO NOT quote the 0.924 as replicated. Our own standing rule from biohub: a claimed number in a notebook is not a number until we reproduce it.
notes: MEASURED AND CLOSED 2026-08-27. labelwise224_s2026 = 0.8517 vs native224_s2026 0.8502, MEAN +0.0015, converged (convergence_check clean). Pre-registration asked >= +0.010 with MCL AND Lateral Meniscus among the movers; got +0.0015, MCL moved (+0.0126) and Lateral Meniscus did not (+0.0051). NO delta is marked significant - paired half-widths run to +/-0.0326. Lands squarely in the pre-registered 'within +/- 0.006' branch: per-diagnosis pooling is not the lever at 12 slices, and 58 image-read labels cannot supervise twelve separate attention channels. What DID hold is the mechanism's predicted signature - focal +0.0038 vs regional -0.0017, six model-bottlenecked findings +0.0037 - so the direction is right and the size is a fifteenth of what was asked. CAVEAT ON THE RIVAL: their 0.924 is a whole model (ConvNeXt-v2-B@336 / CoAtNet@384 / EffNetV2-L@480, five checkpoints, blended), not this head in isolation; nothing here says their number is wrong, only that the head alone does not carry it on our trunk. NOT DEAD AS A MEMBER: +0.0015 with a different internal structure is a diversity-seat profile and costs nothing to try in one. Follow-up it named (window geometry) ran as adjacent224 and came back -0.0040 - see knee-e6sj. Ledger: experiments/README.md '2026-08-27 - the per-diagnosis head and its own named follow-up, BOTH closed on one control'.

title: board_transfer is a whole-range fit and we are on the flat part: local slope 0.74-0.88, not 1.72 - every arm in the repo is priced at roughly double
description:
Measured 2026-08-26T16:58Z, CPU only, zero slots, from comp/board.jsonl as board_check now maintains it.

WHAT IS WRONG. kneemri/evaluation/board_transfer.py reports 'compression: median +1.72 board points per holdout point' as a single number over all 171 orderable ensemble pairs. That statistic mixes pairs spanning the whole history, from solo_v1 (offline 0.8518, board 0.868) to peak8_v1 (0.8731, 0.932). Transfer is not constant across that range - it saturates - and every arm we price today sits at the top.

THE MEASUREMENT, two independent estimators, and the whole-range setting reproduces the tool exactly (1.72), which makes the comparison like-for-like:

  regime                     estimator        value        interval (2000 bootstrap draws)
  all pairs, resolved gap    median ratio     1.72         [1.42, 1.89]   <- the pinned constant
  all ensembles              OLS              2.22         [1.21, 3.14]
  offline >= 0.860           OLS              1.45         [0.76, 2.10]
  offline >= 0.8648 (now)    OLS              0.83         [0.55, 1.47]
  offline >= 0.8648, any gap median ratio     0.88         [0.59, 1.11]
  offline >= 0.8648, resolved median ratio    0.74         [0.49, 0.85]

Both current-regime intervals EXCLUDE 1.72. Monotone decreasing across three nested regimes, on two estimators that do not share a functional form.

THE CAVEAT, and it is real. The top band spans only 0.0083 of offline while the offline noise floor is 0.0053-0.0062. Restriction of range plus errors-in-variables attenuates BOTH estimators toward zero, so the STRUCTURAL slope may well still be near 1.72 and the three regime intervals do overlap - saturation itself is NOT resolved. But the attenuated coefficient is the correct one for PREDICTION: we predict a board move from an OBSERVED offline reading that carries exactly that noise, and the regression of board on a noisy offline is what 0.74-0.88 estimates. For pricing arms, 0.8 is right whether or not saturation is real.

WHAT IT CHANGES. 0.939 -> 0.950 is +0.011 board.
  at 1.72 (what the repo assumes):  +0.0064 offline
  at 0.83:                          +0.0133 offline
  at 0.74:                          +0.0149 offline
  at the optimistic end 1.11:       +0.0099 offline
Our best offline ensemble ever recorded is peak8_v1 at 0.8731; gradeswap_v1 at 0.8694 reads 0.933. 0.950 wants an offline around 0.883-0.888. Nothing in the repo is within +0.010 of the best. The goal is roughly TWICE as far as every plan in this repo has been written to assume.

Every arm priced this session was priced at 1.72 and is overstated ~2x. knee-8yi5's blendhold-six (+0.008-0.010 board) becomes +0.004-0.005. calibsix's case halves. This also explains blendthree_v1 reading 0.939 dead flat at dose 3, and the ten-entry 0.936-0.939 band across every axis we have varied: small offline gains on the flat part of the curve read as nothing.

FIX. board_transfer.py should report the regime-local slope alongside the whole-range one, with its interval, and name the regime by the score being priced - the whole-range median is the wrong number to quote when pricing an arm against a 0.939 champion. The failure shape is the one CLAUDE.md already records twice: a constant quoted from prose while the instrument said otherwise.

Does NOT change: the ORDERING. 0/108 resolved pairs are inverted; the holdout still ranks correctly. Only the SCALE is wrong.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-27 08:24Z, zero card, zero slots. board_transfer now reports the regime-local slope WITH its interval alongside the whole-range one, and the priced line names the score it was asked about.

Three additions to BoardTransfer:
  ratios_above(floor)  -- the resolved pairs' ratios behind a regime median, so a thin cell is visibly thin
  spread(ratios)       -- a seeded percentile interval on the median (2000 draws, seed 2026, 2.5/97.5)
  regimes()            -- now (floor, pairs, median, interval), the interval per regime

The tool reproduces this bead's measurement exactly:

  compression: median +1.72 board points per holdout point over the WHOLE record -- the wrong number
  to price an arm with, see below
    among entries at or above 0.8661: 4 resolved pairs, median +0.74 [+0.49, +1.11]
    among entries at or above 0.8679: 0 resolved pairs, median +0.00 [+0.00, +0.00]
    PRICE AN ARM AT THIS ONE: at or above 0.8648 (asked for), 8 pairs, median +0.74 [+0.50, +0.85]

The interval is what stops the local number becoming the next 1.72: +0.74 [+0.50, +0.85] on 8 pairs is
a range, not a constant, and an arm priced at the upper end is priced at 0.85 rather than 1.72. Seeded,
because a gate that redraws its own answer is not a gate.

CONSEQUENCE UNCHANGED AND NOW MACHINE-READABLE: 0.939 -> 0.950 is +0.011 board = +0.0133 to +0.0149
offline at the local slope, not the +0.0064 the 1.72 constant implied. Ordering is unaffected (0/108
resolved pairs inverted), so this reprices arms and does not invalidate any seating decision.

Gates green (Session gates was successful in 3 minutes); mirror tests test_ratios_above and test_spread
added, test_regimes repaired for the 4-tuple.

title: Nothing has ever tested whether directional gains ADD - and the 0.950 plan assumes they do
description:
THE PLAN RESTS ON AN UNTESTED ASSUMPTION. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_what-0950-actually-costs.md prices first place at +0.010 offline on ONE member. Since raddino_dense ran and read -0.0371, the page names no single arm reaching that, and its own conclusion is that the route is a STACK of directional gains, quoting CLAUDE.md's 'increments below the bar still compose, and a chain of them that sums past it IS a result'. That sentence is a licence, not a measurement. In 110 arms this project has never once put two measured-positive flags in the same run. Every ledger row is one flag against a control, read alone.

THE ARM: experiments/arms/stackfit.sh. Dense corner (336 px, 20 slices, 0.1-0.9), --calibrated-targets AND --ema AND --hold-annotations.

THE TWO TERMS, both with singles landing in the same hours:
 - --calibrated-targets: knee-bs4l measured the matched pair at +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotated, the largest unrefuted directional gain we hold. calib_dense_hold reads it at this exact corner and its header predicts our first member above 0.860.
 - --ema: knee-56w5 pre-registered >=0.8640 against band_dense's 0.8578. A competitor's single-variable ablation of the same flag reads +0.003 (research/2026-08-26_the-ablation-table-a-competitor-published.md), so the honest prior is half the floor and directional. ema_dense reads it at this corner.
Mechanically independent - one changes what the targets say, the other changes which weights are kept - which is the precondition for a sum rather than a substitution.

CONTROL IS calib_dense_hold, so the arm moves exactly one flag (--ema) and the additive prediction is a subtraction with no correction terms:
    predicted = calib_dense_hold + (ema_dense - band_dense)
ema_dense carries no --hold-annotations and neither does its control band_dense, so its delta is internally matched and portable; the hold price cancels out of the difference.

GATED. Do not run until BOTH singles have landed AND both are non-negative, and read them through convergence_check first - under one_cycle a truncated score is a FLOOR and gating on a floor is gating on nothing. If either term is negative this becomes a two-variable arm with a known-bad term and diagnoses nothing.

PRE-REGISTRATION (full ladder in the arm header): >= predicted+0.0062 super-additive, suspect it and demand a second seed. Within 0.0062 ADDITIVE - the result the page needs, and it licenses stacking as a METHOD. <= predicted-0.0062 SUBSTITUTES NOT COMPLEMENTS, the depth_regions_span shape, which KILLS the stack route. <= band_dense_hold, suspect the harness first.

PRICE: ~85 min of card at 336 px / 20 slices, ZERO submission slots, fold-0 holdout, and --hold-annotations buys the second ruler in the same run (knee-9198 satisfied without a rerun).
P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.05 alone. That is not the case for it. The case is that it is a DECISION arm: P(it settles whether the stack route exists) ~ 0.8, and the stack route is the whole remaining plan for reaching 0.950. An 85-minute arm that can kill or license the entire strategy is the best ratio on the board, and killing it early is worth as much as licensing it.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY: two points do not fit a composition rule. Additive here is evidence about THESE two terms, not a law about the next three; each further term still needs its own single before it is stacked.
notes:
GATE RE-READ 2026-08-27T16:04Z, AND THE ARM IS NOW UNINFORMATIVE. DO NOT QUEUE stackfit.

Both singles have landed and both are non-negative, so the bead text says GO. Reading the actual numbers says otherwise:

  band_dense_hold   0.8573   (control for the calib term)
  calib_dense_hold  0.8634   --calibrated-targets = +0.0061
  band_dense        0.8578   (control for the ema term)
  ema_dense         0.8588   --ema = +0.0010

convergence_check lists neither ema_dense nor calib_dense_hold as TRUNCATED, so these are the recipes numbers and not floors.

--ema MISSED ITS OWN PRE-REGISTRATION. knee-56w5 pre-registered >=0.8640 against band_dense 0.8578. It read 0.8588. That is a null at this corner, not a directional gain, and the competitors published ablation reading +0.003 for the same flag is now the upper end of what we can claim rather than the honest prior.

WHY THE ARM CANNOT ANSWER ITS QUESTION ANY MORE. predicted = calib_dense_hold + (ema_dense - band_dense) = 0.8634 + 0.0010 = 0.8644, against a control of 0.8634. The ladder in the bead calls anything within +/-0.0062 ADDITIVE - but the SUBSTITUTES branch (<= predicted-0.0062 = 0.8582) and the additive branch both contain the do-nothing outcome 0.8634. A discriminating arm needs the two hypotheses to predict different numbers; here they differ by 0.0010 against a 0.0062 floor. The decision value P(settles the stack route) ~ 0.8 was priced when the ema term was expected at +0.0062; at +0.0010 it is ~0.05.

85 minutes of card, saved. The stack-route question is NOT closed - it is still open and still the whole plan. It needs a second term that actually measured over the floor, and --ema is not it. The candidates that remain are the ones whose singles read over +0.004 in the ledger; pair the calib term with one of THOSE, not with the largest available null.

LEDGER READ 2026-08-27T22:19Z — ZERO CARD, ZERO SLOT. THE STACK ROUTE IS NOT AWAITING A BETTER SECOND
TERM. IT HAS BEEN TESTED SEVEN TIMES AGAINST THE SAME CONTROL AND HAS NEVER ONCE LANDED NON-NEGATIVE.

The bead's own framing — "find a second term whose single measured over the floor, pair it with the
calib term" — assumes the failures so far were bad candidates. Grepping every arm in experiments/README.md
that runs `calib_dense_hold` (0.8634) as its control says the failure is the ROUTE, not the candidate:

  second term added to the calib corner        arm              holdout   delta
  --ema                                        stackfit         0.8631   -0.0003
  --slice-pooling labelwise                    labelwise_dense  0.8613   -0.0021
  --finding-calibration                        (offsets arm)    0.8595   -0.0039
  warm start from a converged parent           warm_calib_dense 0.8562   -0.0072
  --contrast-weight 1.0                        contrast_dense   0.8547   -0.0087
  --through-plane + attend + --pool sided      fuse_attend      0.8509   -0.0125
  --auc-margin 1.0 --rank-weight 0             margin_calib     0.8235   -0.0399

SEVEN OF SEVEN BELOW THE CONTROL. Three are inside the 0.0062 paired floor and are FLAT rather than
negative-with-confidence — but the SIGN is what this counts. Under a null-additive model (a second
mechanism-sound term is as likely to sit above the control as below), seven of seven on one side is
p = 2^-7 = 0.008. That clears any bar this project applies to a single arm, and it was free.

AND THE ORDERING IS MONOTONE IN HOW MUCH THE SECOND TERM CHANGES. A weight-averaging trick costs
0.0003; a pooling swap 0.0021; an auxiliary loss 0.0087; three pooling changes at once 0.0125; a
competing objective 0.0399. That is the shape of a LOCAL OPTIMUM, not of seven unrelated bad bets.
`calib_dense_hold` is not a member with room above it that the right flag unlocks — it is the top of a
basin our recipe cannot be pushed out of by adding terms to it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not say gains never compose — `2026-08-27_aggregation-beats-input`
still holds that four aggregation flags agree on a SIGN, and the running total 0.8272 -> 0.8523 is a
real chain. It says composition has not survived a single test AT THIS CORNER, where the first term is
already `--calibrated-targets`. A stack built from a DIFFERENT base has never been tried and is not
addressed here.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE 0.950 PLAN. The remaining lane for a better solo is not another flag on our
recipe. It is a genuinely different representation, which is knee-9g28 (`foreign_member`, built and
gates-clean, never run) and knee-tlba behind it. This bead's arm stays cancelled; what changes is that
it is now cancelled by a MEASUREMENT of the route rather than by one term's null.

DO NOT re-derive this. The seven rows are in experiments/README.md; grep for the string 0.8634.
close_reason:
Answered by measurement, not abandoned. The stack route was tested seven times against the same control
(calib_dense_hold 0.8634) and landed below it seven times out of seven: --ema -0.0003, labelwise pooling
-0.0021, --finding-calibration -0.0039, warm start -0.0072, --contrast-weight -0.0087, through-plane +
attend + sided -0.0125, --auc-margin -0.0399. Three of those are inside the paired floor and are FLAT
rather than negative-with-confidence, but the SIGN is what is being counted, and 7/7 on one side under a
null-additive model is p = 2^-7 = 0.008. The ordering is also monotone in how much the second term
changes the recipe, which is the shape of a local optimum rather than of seven unrelated bad bets.

The bead's title claim ("nothing has ever tested whether directional gains ADD") is therefore no longer
true, and leaving it open at P0 points the queue at an arm that is cancelled.

Two limits kept out of the close. It does NOT say gains never compose: 2026-08-27_aggregation-beats-input
still holds four aggregation flags agreeing on a sign for a real 0.8272 -> 0.8523 chain. And a stack built
from a DIFFERENT base has never been tried; this is a result about the calibrated corner specifically.

Its forward pointer is stale and should not be followed: it names knee-9g28 (foreign_member) as the
remaining lane, but that bead has since CLOSED, and its closing number was the contaminated 0.8938 that
knee-ie30 voided. The foreign member scored 0.923 solo on the board, level with ours.

title: 224 px is FREE and we never used it as one - it buys 3x the arms per hour, which is what an unknown-tweak search needs
description:
THE MEASUREMENT IS ALREADY OURS, from the ledger, 2026-08-25 'native224: the resolution axis is flat, and
that is a THROUGHPUT result':

  lr4e-5_ws (control, 336 px)   0.8525   ~290 s/epoch   17997 MiB
  native224                     0.8502     94 s/epoch    8124 MiB

-0.0023 against a 0.0062 floor - flat - and convergence_check does not flag it (best epoch 7, 8-11
declining), so it is the arm's real number, not a truncation floor.

WHAT WE DID WITH THAT. Nothing. Every arm since has run at 336 or 392. The ledger wrote 'THROUGHPUT
result' in its own title and then the queue kept paying 3.1x per epoch for a number inside the noise.

WHY IT MATTERS TODAY AND NOT AS A CURIOSITY. knee-rh4t read ten self-reported single-model scores off
forum topic 735304: the two best, 0.942 and 0.938, are both at 224 px and one is a SINGLE FOLD. The
poster who reached 0.942 got there from 0.934 with unnamed 'tweaks' and stayed at 224 throughout. So the
lever is a recipe/training tweak nobody has named, and the only way to find an unnamed tweak is to try
many. At 336 a 12-epoch arm is ~40 min; at 224 it is ~19. Over the ~11.5 h of card left after
raddino_dense ends (~12:25Z) that is roughly 35 attempts instead of 17.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. Not a proposal to run arms concurrently. card_check blocks on TWO OF OURS for a
measured reason - contention once stretched one member from 3 min to 11 and cost the READING, not just
the time. The card stays serial; 224 buys attempts through speed alone.

WHAT STAYS AT 336. The four queued arms - band_dense_hold, calib_dense_hold, ema_dense, stack_dense - are
single-variable measurements against band_dense_hold at the dense corner, each with a pre-registered
prediction. Moving them to 224 breaks the control and throws away the pre-registration. They run as
written. This is about everything AFTER them.

WHAT SHOULD RUN AT 224. Every exploratory arm whose question is 'does this recipe change move the
number' - the search for the unnamed tweak, and the tissue-centre cache test (knee-b96p), which needs a
cache rebuild and should rebuild the cheap one.

THE CAVEAT THE OWNER HAS STANDING. Forum self-reports are not results; biohub spent weeks failing to
replicate a claimed 0.913. What is used here is only the RANKING - 224 is where the leaders are, and our
own arm says 224 costs us nothing - not the absolute numbers.
notes:
PRICE (optimiser-path arms, second batch): ~19 min of card per arm, zero slots, control native224 = 0.8502, keep floor +0.0062. P(clears): clip224 0.20, clip224_tight 0.12, decay224_high 0.25, decay224_low 0.18, warm224_brief 0.15, warm224_long 0.10. Each pair BRACKETS an inherited module constant that has never had a CLI flag, so a flat pair CLOSES its axis; the family is priced as a search over the count of attempts against a free card.
SOTA pretrained model survey: research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md. Top actionable candidate: OrthoFoundation-L (knee-specific, weights released, MIT license).

title: TissueCentre is plumbed through six places and has NEVER been trained - the worst tenth of studies crop a clipped joint
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-26, from core/data/corpus/crop_centre.py and crop_coverage.py.

THE FACT. Our default crop takes 130 mm about (height//2, width//2) - the IMAGE centre, on the assumption
the joint was framed in the middle. Measured over 60 studies, the tissue centroid sits a median 7 mm, p90
18 mm, and up to 32 mm from that point against a 160 mm field of view. At 130 mm the margin is ~15 mm.
So the worst ~10% of studies are trained on a crop that CLIPS THE JOINT, and every member this project
owns was fitted that way.

`TissueCentre` is the strategy that fixes it. It exists, it is plumbed through six call sites, it is
opt-in - and nothing has ever been trained under it. The reason given in crop_centre.py is honest and
still holds: switching the default silently would invalidate ~99 GB of cached arrays and every member
fitted on them, with no fingerprint to catch it.

WHY IT IS A DATA LEVER AND NOT A KNOB. knee-rh4t priced the board deficit at ~0.017 on ONE member, and
the arithmetic in this session put the noise floor at 0.0062 offline / 0.0107 board once the +1.72
transfer is applied - so nothing that moves 0.001-0.004 can close it. Recovering anatomy for a tenth of
the corpus is a change to WHAT THE MODEL SEES on 10% of its training signal, which is the only class of
change sized right. The forum's own convergence agrees: topic 735826, a poster running controlled
experiments with a frozen CPU cache reports 'image geometry / slice selection + label quality > backbone
size', and names fixed-mm physical cropping as the next thing to isolate. We already do fixed-mm cropping.
We do not do tissue-centring.

WHAT GATES IT, AND IT COSTS NO GPU. crop_coverage answers 'which centre keeps more of the imaged tissue'
without a label and without the card. Its own docstring records that the question has never been answered.
Launched 2026-08-26 11:14Z, --sample 400 --workers 12, log at experiments/logs/crop_coverage_400.log.
Prediction from that module, written before the run: at 130 mm the two centres are near-indistinguishable;
at the 80 mm tight extent tissue-centring must keep materially more or the strategy is not worth a rebuild.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY, inherited from the tool: retained tissue is not retained JOINT - a crop drifting toward
the calf keeps tissue while losing the knee. It bounds the failure from one side only.

NEXT STEP IF COVERAGE FAVOURS TISSUE-CENTRING. Do NOT rebuild the 336 cache. Rebuild at 224, where
native224 (ledger 2026-08-25) measured 0.8502 against the 336 control's 0.8525 - flat, -0.0023 on a 0.0062
floor - at 94 s/epoch and 8.1 GB instead of 290 s/epoch and 18.0 GB. A tissue-centred 224 cache is the
cheap arm that tests the mechanism; if it lands, the 336 rebuild is then justified by a measurement rather
than by an offset distribution.
design:
PRICE: ~19 min of card (12 epochs at 94 s/epoch, 224 px), plus ZERO for the cache — it was built on CPU
beside raddino_dense and cost no card at all. Zero submission slots.

PLAUSIBLE GAIN ON THE MEAN: small, and stating that honestly is the point. The mechanism is a
SUBPOPULATION claim. The tissue centroid sits a median 7 mm from the image centre, p90 18 mm, max 32 mm,
against ~15 mm of margin at a 130 mm crop. So roughly the worst TENTH of studies clip and nine tenths are
untouched. Even a large gain on the clipped decile (+0.05 there) moves the corpus mean about +0.005 —
below the 1.5% bar by construction, and below the 0.0062 paired floor.

P(clears 1.5% on the mean) ~0.10.
P(directional AND concentrated in the high-offset decile) ~0.35.

WHY IT RUNS ANYWAY, argued as an INSTRUMENT rather than sold as an improvement: 19 minutes retires or
licenses the entire CROP-GEOMETRY axis. That axis is ranked first by the one poster in forum topic 735826
running frozen-cache controlled experiments ('image geometry / slice selection + label quality > backbone
size'), and it is the only lever class that reaches EVERY member at once rather than one corner. Land it
and the 336 rebuild follows and every member is refitted; miss it and we stop paying attention to a
strategy that has sat plumbed through six call sites and untested since knee-yrf.

HOW IT IS READ, and this decides the verdict more than the mean does: split the fold-0 holdout by each
study's centroid offset and compare the top decile against the rest. FLAT mean + gain concentrated in the
high-offset decile CONFIRMS the mechanism and licenses the 336 rebuild. Gain spread uniformly across all
offsets REFUTES the mechanism even if the mean reads as a win — that is the shape to distrust, because
nothing in the physics predicts a benefit for a study whose joint was already centred.
notes:
VERDICT 2026-08-26: FLAT, the pre-registered middle branch. tissue224 0.8491 (best e6, converged 12/12,
convergence_check clean) against native224 0.8502 — -0.0011, a sixth of the 0.0062 paired floor.

FLAGS VERIFIED BEFORE THE VERDICT, which the header demanded: the run's own recipe prints "centre":
"tissue" and "image_size": "224". Not a flag that failed to land.

THE TISSUE IS REAL AND DOES NOT CONVERT. crop_coverage measured tissue-image at +0.0294 [+0.0276,
+0.0312] retained coverage at 130 mm over 1,822 series. So ~3% more imaged anatomy reaches the network
and buys nothing measurable.

WHICH MECHANISM DIED, and the header pre-registered both:
  COMMON-MODE FRAMING - refuted. It predicted a UNIFORM corpus-wide gain (every study's joint off-centre
  in the same direction, two thirds of the 9-14 mm displacement shared per crop_alignment), which moves
  the mean by construction. The mean did not move.
  CLIPPING - untested, NOT refuted. A subpopulation claim confined to the worst tenth (p90 offset 18 mm
  against ~15 mm of margin) predicts a flat mean by construction and shows up only in an offset split.

THE SPLIT CANNOT BE BUILT TODAY. crop_alignment.dump() writes `spread` - between-slot disagreement - not
the centroid's offset MAGNITUDE from the image centre, so the decile the clipping claim needs is not on
disk. Filed as its own bead rather than left as a clause here.

CONSEQUENCE: the 99 GB 336-cache rebuild this arm existed to license is NOT licensed. The crop/centre
axis is closed on the mean at both extents - 80 mm -0.0099 (crop80_span), 130 mm -0.0011 (here). What
survives is a claim about 10% of the corpus worth at most a tenth of its own size on the mean, i.e. below
the floor even if true. Do not spend a card on it; it would need a per-decile read of an existing pair,
not a new fit.

STILL OWED: seat_value on tissue224. Deferred, not skipped - the card is held by band_dense_hold and
card_check blocks on two of ours. The diversity read is worth taking because a member of equal quality
with different crop GEOMETRY is a distinct disagreement axis, and seat_value must be run --against
gradeswap_v1 (blendseat has only 1 of 6 members carrying a holdout record, so it cannot price a marginal
contribution).

title: Rivals reach 0.938-0.942 on a SINGLE model at 224px - the gap is a member gap and neither resolution nor folds nor ensembling explains it
description:
Read 2026-08-26 0614z from forum topic 735304 ('Best single-model score', 17 votes, 22 replies), live, no slot spent. Ten self-reported single-model board scores:

  0.942  single, 224px, 'some tweaks' on a 0.934 @ 224px
  0.938  single model, SINGLE FOLD
  0.929  single, 5-fold, 224px, LLM output labels only
  0.926  single, 5-fold, 336px, LLM output labels only
  0.920  single, OOF AUC = LB AUC within noise
  0.915  single, DINOv2
  0.887  single, DINOv2 (the asker)

OURS: soloseat 0.925. So the board deficit is ~0.017 ON ONE MEMBER, and knee-urvf's law says that transfers to the ensemble roughly one-for-one.

WHAT THIS RULES OUT, which is most of what we have been spending card on:

RESOLUTION IS NOT THE LEVER. The 0.942 and the 0.938 are both at 224px, and the poster explicitly says the 0.942 stayed at 224 through the tweaks. Our 336/392 work (band_span, res392, crop80) was chasing an axis the leaders are not on. Note the two 5-fold entries invert it too: 224px scores 0.929 against 336px's 0.926.

FOLDS ARE NOT THE LEVER, and this is the strongest line in the thread. The two FIVE-FOLD singles (0.929, 0.926) are BELOW the two SINGLE-fold ones (0.942, 0.938). Independent confirmation of the owner's standing ban - folds are the same thing tried slightly differently, and here they are measurably worse than one good run.

ENSEMBLING IS NOT THE LEVER, said twice by people above us. 'Public notebooks just ensemble early to get a high LB score and exposure; waste of time IMO' and 'nine days into a competition is a very silly time to be wasting efforts refining ensemble models.' One poster points at the Efficiency LB as evidence: high-scoring submissions with short runtimes cannot be 20-model ensembles. Our board history is nine entries sitting in 0.936-0.939, every one a different seating / vote rule / count / TTA over near-identical members. That is the trap knee-urvf named, now corroborated from outside.

LABELS ARE NOT THE WHOLE STORY EITHER. Both 5-fold entries say 'LLM output labels only' and land 0.926-0.929, right on top of our 0.925 - so a plain LLM label table plus a competent single model already reaches where we are. Consistent with today's closure of the label axis (knee-1ww2, knee-uahl).

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the whole schedule: the recipe/backbone/training of ONE member at 224px. We do not know what the 0.934 -> 0.942 'tweaks' were and the poster did not say.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CARD. blendsix members 4 and 5 land ~0920z, leaving ~14 hours before the last slot at ~2330z. Under knee-urvf the six-member blendall is predicted at 0.939-0.941 - a ~zero-expected-gain run against the 0.939 champion, because the bonus term is saturated and the members are near-identical. Spending that card on a SINGLE-member arm at 224px has the better ratio even at low odds, because it is the only axis that can move the ensemble by more than the bonus.

CAVEAT, and the owner has stated it as a standing rule: notebook and forum claims are not results. biohub spent weeks failing to replicate a claimed 0.913. These are self-reports with no verification, and 0.942 would sit near the live leader at 0.952. Treat the RANKING of the axes as the finding (resolution out, folds out, ensembling out, member recipe in) and the absolute numbers as unverified.

title: The ensemble tracks best-single + ~0.019 and the single has been flat at 0.925 for five days - member quality is the only free term
description:
MEASURED from comp/board.jsonl, 56 scored entries, 2026-08-26 05:27Z. Three dated single-member board reads exist, each with a best-ensemble-of-that-day beside it.

  date        best single      best ensemble       bonus
  2026-08-12  solo_v1  0.868   0.894               +0.026
  2026-08-17  solo_v4  0.914   vote_v2 0.919 (m2)  +0.005
  2026-08-26  soloseat 0.925   blendseat 0.939(m6) +0.014

SINGLE moved 0.868 -> 0.914 -> 0.925. ENSEMBLE moved 0.894 -> 0.919 -> 0.939. Member gains transfer to the ensemble at roughly ONE-FOR-ONE, and the BONUS the ensemble adds over its own best member has hovered 0.005-0.026 with no trend across fourteen days, while the pool grew from one member to seven and roughly thirty seat/vote/count/TTA entries were spent on it.

THE LAW, stated as a working model: board(ensemble) ~= board(best single) + 0.015, with the second term SATURATED. Nine entries sit inside 0.936-0.939 (augseat, allfit, lastseat, v3seat, dark6, dark7, farseat, votefit, jitterfit) and every one of them is a different seating, vote rule, count or TTA over near-identical members.

WHAT IT PREDICTS, and this is why it is P0. To reach the owner's 0.950 target the ensemble needs a best single at ~0.935. Ours is 0.925. Rivals self-report singles at 0.938-0.942 (topic 735304), which under this law would put their ensembles at ~0.953-0.957 - consistent with the live leader at 0.952. The target is not reachable by re-combining what we hold; it needs +0.010 on ONE member.

THE TRAP IT ALSO NAMES. 'Replace the other seats with the best member' is the WRONG reading. The +0.015 is a DIVERSITY term; seating copies of one member collapses the ensemble to that member and gives the term back. weakseven_v1 (0.908, -0.026 from one weak member) and peak8 (0.932 at eight members, below six) bound the other side: the pool cannot be improved by adding members that are weak, and cannot be improved by adding more of them. What raises the ensemble is raising the FLOOR of every member, or adding one that is strong AND unlike.

CAVEAT ON THE MEASUREMENT. Three points, no intervals, and the 08-17 pair is the weakest (its best ensemble was a two-member vote, so the bonus there is not measured at the same pool size as the other two). The one-for-one claim is a SLOPE read off three points; treat the +0.015 as an order of magnitude, not a constant. It is enough to rank the axes, which is all it is being used for.
notes:
2026-08-30 21:48Z: holdswap_v1 (ref 55900461, PENDING) is a direct test of this bead's 'member quality is the only free term'. It holds seat COUNT, vote rule, foreign weight and kit fixed and moves exactly one seat to a higher-quality member -- lr4e-5_ws_cf (fold-0 analogue 0.8525 solo, the weakest of the five priceable champion seats) out, calib_dense_hold_ff (analogue 0.8634, the best solo the project owns) in. If quality is the free term, this is the cheapest possible way to spend it, and the swap was named by a ten-of-ten unanimous offline proxy rather than by hand. A flat reading would say quality does not transfer through a seat either, which would leave the bead with no free term at all.
2026-09-01 07:40Z RECOMPUTE, from the COMPLETED board record (board_check filled 24 missing rows on 2026-08-25; 87 rows now, joined on the 'members' field, scope:excluded dropped). The title's two claims split.

WHAT SURVIVES: the bonus is still small and the single is still the lever. Best single is unchanged since 2026-08-26 at 0.925 (soloseat_v1); calibsolo 0.923 and raptor_solo 0.923 did not beat it, and raptor_solo's offline is void anyway (98.6% in-sample, board_check 2026-08-29).

WHAT DOES NOT: 'has not grown in fourteen days' is now false. Best ensemble moved 0.939 (blendseat, 08-26) -> 0.944 (holdswap_v1 08-30, stackseat_v1 08-31), with the best single flat at 0.925 throughout. So the bonus went +0.014 -> +0.019 over five days on a FIXED best single. The law should read board(ensemble) ~= board(best single) + 0.019, not + 0.015, and the second term is not frozen -- it moved by 0.005, which is about our offline resolution (knee-b6sn) but is four board rows wide and monotone.

WHAT THAT COSTS THE P0 ARGUMENT: it makes the target EASIER than this bead states, not harder. At bonus 0.019 the 0.950 ensemble needs a 0.931 single rather than a 0.935 one. It does not rescue the seat axis -- holdswap and stackseat are both sevens and both read 0.944, i.e. two different seatings landing on the same number, which is knee-xuj5's finding again.

Best-by-count over the same recompute (knee-macc): 1->0.925(n5) 2->0.936(n5) 3->0.938(n4) 4->0.937(n12) 5->0.931(n5) 6->0.943(n12) 7->0.944(n19) 8->0.943(n5) 11->0.941 12->0.937 25->0.894.
SOTA pretrained model survey: research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md. Top actionable candidate: OrthoFoundation-L (knee-specific, weights released, MIT license).

title: Slots do not go to seat permutations: nine 6/7-member entries span 0.002 (the 0.028 member gap is WITHDRAWN — two-ruler artefact)
description:

interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the-seat-axis-is-saturated-and-the-member-is-0.028-behind.md

title: Mixup: the label-space regulariser the overfit diagnosis asks for, and it has never been in this repo
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-25 22:13Z, card-free while knee-bs4l trains. Grepped experiments/README.md and kneemri/ core/ for mixup|cutmix|label_smooth|drop_path|stochastic_depth. ZERO hits in the ledger and ZERO hits in the code. This axis has never been run and is not implemented.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT SHAPE. The repo's own numbers say the model is DATA-LIMITED, not compute- or architecture-limited, and every closed axis is closed for that one reason:
  - band_dense_long (24 epochs, single variable): peaked at epoch 6 (0.8587), slid to 0.8405 by epoch 23 while the training loss halved 0.85 -> 0.4536. A 0.0182 peak-to-finish decline, 2.9x the noise floor. That is memorisation, stated in the ledger in those words.
  - cnx at MATCHED TRAIN LOSS: 0.8371 vs 0.7927, a 0.044 generalisation gap at equal fit (knee-jk3).
  - Every quantity axis (slices, pixels, slots, epochs, members past six) reads inside the 0.0062 floor. A model that memorises at 12 epochs has no use for more of anything.

WHY THE ONE REGULARISER WE DID RUN DOES NOT COVER IT. aug_long is intensity_aug False->True and nothing else: gain, gamma, blur, contrast, noise, plus rigid jitter. Every one of those perturbs how a study LOOKS. None touches the study-to-label mapping, so a trunk can still memorise anatomy-to-finding, and the ledger's own summary of that arm is "the regulariser fired, the overfitting did not care". Mixup is categorically different: a convex combination of two studies carrying the convex combination of their targets makes a memorised study-to-label pair actively WRONG, which is why it is the standard remedy for exactly this curve shape.

THE SEAM IS FREE, audited in trainer.py:367-380. The pixel tensor (UInt8 b n g h w), the slot mask (b s), and the score/weight pair from targets.rows(batch) are all materialised in the same three lines before the autocast block. A permutation of the batch dimension plus a Beta(a,a) draw mixes all four. Our targets are ALREADY soft -- objective.py's docstring: "our targets are weighted confidences in [0, 1] rather than binary labels" -- so the cross-entropy term takes a mixed target unchanged, with no soft-label plumbing to add. The mask mixes as an elementwise maximum (a slot valid in either study stays valid).

PRICE. Dev ~45 min (a Mixup policy dataclass beside the other trainer policies, a flag, a Landed witness, the jaxtyping boundary, the mirror test). Card 40 min for one 12-epoch arm against a matched control we already own. Plausible gain 1-3% on an overfitting classifier; odds it clears the 1.5% bar ~1 in 3. That ratio beats every other open lever, and every rival is either closed on a measurement or blocked on an owner licence call.

PRE-REGISTRATION, against the matched control at the SAME recipe:
  - the peak RISES by 0.015 or more -> the memorisation reading is right and the axis is a design lever, not a knob; sweep alpha and build members on it.
  - the peak is flat but the DECLINE shrinks (peak-to-finish well under 0.0182) -> mixup regularises as intended and the bound is elsewhere; keep it as a free rider, do not spend a slot.
  - the peak FALLS -> mixing across studies destroys the focal, few-voxel findings this task turns on (a torn meniscus blended with an intact one is not a study), and the label-space axis closes with a mechanism rather than a shrug.
  - training diverges or the witness says the flag did not land -> harness, not idea. Fix and re-run before reading anything.
notes:
READ 2026-08-26 08:47Z, four hours after the run finished. mixup224_long (a=0.4, 24 ep) vs native224_long control: peak 0.8505 e12 vs 0.8490 e9 (+0.0015, a quarter of the floor — FLAT), finish 0.8417 vs 0.8325, decline 0.0088 vs 0.0165 — HALVED, and below the 0.0124 the control's own pre-registration set for DEFECT REAL. Final train loss 0.6646 vs 0.4670, peak three epochs later: the blend fired, plumbing is not a suspect.

PRE-REGISTERED BAND 2 verbatim: peak flat, decline shrinks -> regularises as intended, bound is elsewhere, keep as a free rider, do NOT spend a slot. No slot spent.

WHAT IT CLOSES. The label-space regularisation account of the ceiling. It also SEPARATES two things this repo had bundled: the slide is memorisation and is curable; the ceiling is not the slide (curing it returns +0.0015). Every axis that presents the SAME supervision to the SAME encoder differently now reads flat — schedule (nocycle224_long), example count (half_data), appearance aug (aug_long), label-space mixing (here). What is left is a different REPRESENTATION or different SUPERVISION: knee-jk3, knee-rh4t.

Ledger section appended 2026-08-26. Limits: 224 only, says nothing about the 336/dense cell where -0.0182 was measured; the dose was not swept at 24 epochs and a sweep is not priced.
close_reason: Ran and read null: mixup_dense peaked 0.8552 at e11 against band_dense 0.8578, -0.0026, inside the 0.0062 paired floor in the negative direction. Peak on the LAST epoch means UNDERTRAINED, not truncated — mixup slows fitting so 12 epochs buys the arm less than it buys its control, and the honest claim is 'at this budget mixup pays nothing', not 'mixup fails here'. Ledger entry in experiments/README.md. Not re-queued: +6 epochs is ~50 min against a flat mechanism and loses the ratio to knee-for6.

title: Score label-side arms on BOTH rulers, not just the report-derived proxy
description:
The board scores against image-read radiologist consensus (competition overview, topic 733343, Dr. Jacob Kazam: two subspecialty MSK radiologists per study, third adjudicating, 'on the fence' graded negative to favor specificity). Every number in this project - every ledger row, every run_comparison, the 0.8502 control - is measured against the report-derived table, which is a PROXY. holdannot_s2026 scores 0.8487 against report labels and 0.8932 against the 58 annotation cells: same weights, same studies, +0.045 from the ruler alone.

The metric is per-label rank AUC and the two label sets rank studies differently, so a change that moves a model toward annotation truth mechanically LOSES AUC against report labels. The proxy is not neutral toward label-side arms; it is biased against them, by up to the measured +0.045.

RULE: any label-side arm from here reports both numbers - its proxy holdout AUC, and its supervision_gap aggregate over the 58. Getting the second requires --hold-annotations, which holdannot priced at -0.0015 (nothing). Entrypoint exists: python -m kneemri.evaluation.annotated_readings --checkpoints <run>.pt, or supervision_gap --records <run>.pt. Non-hold-annotations checkpoints are REFUSED (TrainedOnAnnotationsError), not silently scored.

See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md. Non-license: n=58, the annotated set is not a random sample (ACL 41% vs ~20% corpus, topic 734106).
notes:
2026-08-30 — the SELECTION half of this bead is retired; the SCORING half stands.

Standing plan was: if the gold ruler is the one that tracks the board, member SELECTION should run on it,
which today it cannot because only hold_annotations=True checkpoints are readable there — priced at
~6 x 40 min of card to retrain the shipping roster under --hold-annotations.

That was the wrong diagnosis. Measured on the six hold-annotation members we already own (knee-kddo):
six members spanning 0.022 gold produce paired intervals ~0.03 wide, and five of six pairs cannot be
separated at all. The limit is the DENOMINATOR — 58 annotated studies cannot resolve the 0.002-0.010
differences selection turns on — not who is readable on them. Retraining the roster would have bought a
ruler with the same blindness and spent four hours of card to find that out. DO NOT ARM IT.

What still stands: reading a label-side arm on BOTH rulers, because the LEVEL shift (+0.045) is twice the
entire spread of the members being ordered, and the proxy is biased against label-side movement. That is
a scoring practice, not a selection instrument.

Only more annotated studies change the selection answer.

title: Which ruler does the BOARD use — report-derived labels or image-read annotations? It decides whether the label lane is small or large
description:
OPENED 2026-08-25 20:52Z by the supervision-gap measurement (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md).

THE QUESTION. Every number this project optimises is scored against REPORT-DERIVED labels, because that is the only ruler that covers the corpus. The hidden test set is scored against something we have never identified. If it is report-derived, then matching the report reader is exactly right and a model that beats it is spending capacity on the wrong truth. If it is image-read annotation -- which is what the hosts' comment in thread 735826 implies, 'those folks did not use the reports as a starting point' -- then our TRAINING TARGETS are the binding ceiling, and target correction is worth substantially more than blendlabels' +0.0034 prices it at.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. The supervision-gap measurement closed both halves of the supervision question as small: the label half at +0.0034/+0.0070 (blendlabels) and the model half at three findings (MCL -0.0465, Lateral Meniscus -0.0149, PF OA -0.0071). That conclusion is conditional on the ruler. This single fact is the only thing that could reopen the label lane as a 1.5%-sized lever, and it costs no slot and no card to investigate.

EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND, pointing at ANNOTATIONS. holdannot_s2026 -- one member, one set of predictions -- scores 0.8487 against report labels and 0.8932 against the radiologist on the 58 annotated studies. That is +0.045 from the RULER ALONE, controlled: same model, same weights, different truth. Our board sits at 0.938 against a holdout of ~0.85, a gap of ~0.088 in the same direction. Do NOT read that as confirmation: the board figure is a six-member ensemble with TTA and the holdout figure is a single member, so most of that gap is ensembling and study draw, not ruler. What the +0.045 does establish is that the ruler is worth a LOT on the same predictions, so identifying it is not a bookkeeping detail.

HOW TO ANSWER, cheapest first: (1) re-read the competition data description and host comments for how test ground truth was produced -- board_read/discussion_read already talk to Kaggle and spend no slot; (2) note that test.csv has no Report column (core/data/labels/targets.py:4), which is consistent with annotation-based truth but does not prove it; (3) check whether the published/top notebooks calibrate toward annotations or toward reports.

DO NOT spend a submission slot probing this. It is a documentation question.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-08-25 20:54Z, twenty minutes after filing, by one forum read and no card. The board scores against IMAGE-READ RADIOLOGIST CONSENSUS, not against reports.

Competition overview, topic 733343, 'Courtesy of Dr. Jacob Kazam':
  'Models are evaluated on twelve binary labels ... The labels, and the criteria used by the ANNOTATING RADIOLOGISTS, are summarized below. In each case, ambiguous or borderline findings ("on the fence") were graded as NEGATIVE to favor specificity.'
  'Each study in the annotated reference set was independently labeled by two subspecialty-trained MSK radiologists, with disagreements adjudicated by a third radiologist to produce a single consensus ground truth.'

CONSEQUENCES, and they are large:
1. Every number this project has ever quoted -- every ledger row, every run_comparison, the 0.8502 control -- is measured against a PROXY (the report-derived table). The objective is the annotation ruler.
2. The two rulers are +0.045 apart on identical predictions: holdannot_s2026 scores 0.8487 against report labels and 0.8932 against the 58 annotation cells. Same weights, same studies, no ensembling, no TTA.
3. That is a documented mechanism for part of the standing board-vs-holdout gap (0.938 vs ~0.85), which had been carried as unexplained.
4. blendlabels' +0.0034 is its value on the PROXY. Its value on the objective was never computed. The label lane is UNMEASURED, not measured-small -- the 'both supervision levers are priced' conclusion written 20 minutes earlier is withdrawn.
5. 'On the fence -> negative, to favor specificity' matches a measurement we already have: our ruler calls 44.7% of the 696 cells positive at cut 0.50 where the adjudicated radiologist calls 34.5%. Our targets are systematically more generous than the ground truth is DEFINED to be. Supervision.calibrated_targets already implements the correction and was built before there was a reason to think it mattered.
6. supervision_gap is not a side instrument. It is the only direct measurement of the actual competition objective this project owns.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE. n = 58, and the annotated set is not a random sample of the corpus (ACL 41% there vs ~20% overall, topic 734106). The claim is documentary -- which ruler -- not a statistical result about any arm.

Follow-up filed separately: score label-side arms on BOTH rulers, which costs only --hold-annotations (holdannot priced that at -0.0015, nothing). See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md.
close_reason: ANSWERED and recorded. The board scores against image-read radiologist consensus, not reports — the competition overview and topic 733343 both say so in the host's own words, and holdannot_s2026 measures the size: 0.8487 against report labels, 0.8932 against the 58 annotation cells, same weights, same studies. +0.045 from the ruler alone. Written up in experiments/README.md and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md; the standing rule it produced is knee-9198, and the arm it produced is knee-bs4l (on the card now).

title: a kaggle dataset version can land with a file missing, and it refuses the WHOLE package on every kernel
description:
farseat (kernel version 2, 2026-08-25 01:47Z) died with:

  kneemri.inference.members.WeightsError: /kaggle/input/datasets/dimiturnt/kneemri-members holds a
  manifest listing 40 members but 1 of their files are absent (first 'small_accum_s2026.pt')

The local staging package is INTACT - 40 .pt files, a 40-row manifest, nothing missing locally. So the manifest and the file set were consistent when they were written and the LIVE VERSION lost a file during upload. Kaggle reported the push a success; the marker line 'Dataset version is being created' appeared and nothing said a file had been dropped.

BLAST RADIUS IS EVERY KERNEL, not just farseat. MemberPackage.__init__ refuses a package whose manifest names a file it cannot find, so one dropped .pt takes down every kernel that mounts the members dataset regardless of whether its own tuple names the missing member. farseat's tuple does NOT name small_accum_s2026 and farseat still died. That is the whole submission path on one file.

THE DETECTOR WAS RIGHT AND I OVERRODE IT. mount_check --live read REFUSED for 8 kernels naming small_accum_s2026 at 01:43Z. I discounted it because it had given three different answers in two minutes while a dataset version materialised, and because the file was present locally and had carried the 0.933 accumseat entry. Both of those were true and neither was relevant: a file present locally says nothing about the live package. A detector that flip-flops during a push is not a detector that is wrong, and the correct response was to re-read it AFTER the version settled rather than to file the disagreement as noise. It cost a kernel run and about 20 minutes on the critical path with two slots left.

FIX APPLIED: re-pushed the version from the intact local package (logs/push_members_fix.log).

WHAT TO BUILD, and it is small: the push is not verified by its own marker today - 'Dataset version is being created' is printed BEFORE the files are all there. The gate that closes this is a post-push readback: list the live files and diff them against the local manifest, and refuse to submit until they match. mount_check --live already does the comparison; what is missing is that nothing FORCES it after a push and before a kernel run. Wire it into the push path so a dropped file is caught by the pusher rather than by a spent kernel slot.
notes:
SHARPER, from the farseat post-mortem: mount_check --live did NOT catch this. It read 'kneemri-farseat: ok - declares all of ...' at 01:41Z and the run died anyway. unpushed() only compares the members a kernel NAMES against the live set, but MemberPackage.__init__ refuses a manifest whose files it cannot ALL find - so one dropped .pt takes down kernels that never name it. The per-kernel question is the wrong question for a package-level refusal, and the 8 REFUSED verdicts were a coincidence of which kernels happened to name the missing member.

FIXED: MountCheck.absent() compares the whole manifest against the live listing, checked BEFORE the per-kernel loop because a manifest the live dataset cannot satisfy invalidates every verdict that loop prints. Non-zero exit. Unit test test_absent covers the case the old test could not express: a member absent live and named by NO kernel.

Verified on the real defect - the new check printed 'live dataset does not hold 1 of the 40 members the manifest names (small_accum_s2026)' against the same package where the old code called farseat ok. Members dataset re-pushed; live package now complete.
2026-08-25 02:07Z — the DETECTOR half is fixed and pushed (04d3f8b): MountCheck.absent() asks the package-level question that unpushed() structurally could not, plus a unit test carrying the 2026-08-25 failure. main() runs it BEFORE the per-kernel loop and exits non-zero on it, because a manifest the live dataset cannot satisfy refuses MemberPackage for EVERY kernel, not only the ones naming the missing member. What is still open is the UPLOAD half: a kaggle dataset version can still land incomplete, and the only defence is running mount_check --live and polling until it reads LIVE PACKAGE COMPLETE before pushing any kernel. Also unresolved: --live gives different answers while a version is still materialising, so a single green read is not proof; poll it twice.
2026-08-25: upload half closed in caf1aca. MountCheck.settled polls the live listing until the manifest reads present twice running; --settle implies --live and refuses on it; comp/push.sh's dataset branch runs it after the push, gated on manifest.json, with an explicit status check because push.sh is set -u and not set -e. A never-settling poll reports the union of everything seen absent, not the last read, because the last read of a flip-flopping listing is the one answer known unreliable.

title: The seventh seat was never READ: dark6/dark7 are fold -1 (no offline delta), and the fold-0 analogue is +0.0005 against a 0.0011 board resolution
description:
dark6 (55756018) = six all-data (--fold -1) members and nothing else. It reads 0.937 — EXACTLY the champion plateau that allfit and lastseat read with a SEVENTH member added.

So the seventh seat contributes zero board points. Every entry that varied it was measuring a coordinate with no value:
- lastseat 0.937 (small_batch6 in seat four)
- augseat 0.936 (aug_long, a regularised member)
- v3seat PENDING (v3base_dense, a DINOv3-base trunk)
- farseat (never submitted, gated)

That is three slots, and a fourth pending, spent on a null coordinate. The pre-registrations were all written against 0.937 as 'the champion' when 0.937 was really 'what six dark members already read'. augseat's 0.936 and v3seat's expected 0.936-0.939 are not readings about regularisation or encoder family; they are readings about noise around an inert seat.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: it does not say members are worthless — weakseven read 0.908, so member quality does move the board. It says the MARGINAL seventh seat, filled by anything, is worth nothing on top of six all-data members.

WHAT IS NOW LOAD-BEARING: dark7 (55756369) is seven ALL-DATA members, the only entry that raises count without adding a fold-0 seat. Its reading against dark6 0.937 is now the whole count axis.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REMAINING SLOTS: seat search is closed on a measurement. The axes never tested on the board are (a) the VOTE (offline flat at +0.0002, but the offline ruler is measured anti-correlated at the top: peak8 0.8731 -> 0.932), and (b) the serving/overlap path. votefit is the strongest written candidate left.
notes: 2026-09-06 board_floor (knee-6j8b4). dark6/dark7 both carry offline:null - every member is --fold -1 and has seen all 909, so the INERT verdict rests on a board delta of 0.000 whose 95% half-width at ~400 public studies is 0.0011. Fold-0 analogues of the same swap on honest members: six+small_batch6 vs six = +0.0005 [n=400: -0.0005,+0.0016]; six+grade_ladder vs six = +0.0002 (matches the ledger's sevengrade-vs-sixfresh +0.0002); six+v3base_dense vs six = -0.0004. All inside the resolution, so the axis is closed on the analogue - but it was closed originally on a ruler that could not read it. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_board-flats-below-the-boards-resolution.md

title: The model fails the FOCAL findings and beats the reader on the DIFFUSE ones
description:
supervision_gap on report_labels_v2 (58 annotated studies, 696 cells, radiologist truth, held-out predictions) splits the twelve findings by physics, not by label noise.

MODEL BEATS ITS OWN LABELS (reader is the weak part): Effusion +0.1304, Contusion +0.0891, Synovitis +0.0508, Medial OA +0.0419, Baker's +0.0226, Fracture +0.0160.
MODEL FAILS ITS OWN LABELS (extraction is the weak part): Lateral Meniscus -0.1925 (labels 0.8422, model 0.6497), ACL -0.1225, MCL -0.0964, Medial Meniscus -0.0938, PF OA -0.0856, Lateral OA -0.0793.

The split is not arbitrary. Every finding we beat is DIFFUSE AND BRIGHT - fluid, edema, inflammation, effusion - signal that is large, low-frequency and survives both the downsample to 336 px (0.39 mm/px) and the max-pool across 12-20 slices. Every finding we fail is SMALL, FOCAL AND STRUCTURAL - menisci, cruciate and collateral ligaments, cartilage - a few millimetres of altered signal that a max-pool over twenty slices dilutes and a 0.39 mm/px grid barely resolves. That is a mechanism, and it predicts which arms can pay.

SIZE. The negative gaps sum to 0.670 across twelve labels. The metric is an unweighted mean of twelve AUCs, so closing a third of that is +0.019 and Lateral Meniscus ALONE is worth +0.016 - the first mechanism priced this week that clears the owner's 1.5% bar on its own rather than by composition.

DENOMINATOR, STATED: n=58 studies per finding, so each individual value carries a wide interval and no single number here is a result. The PATTERN - six negative, six positive, sorted cleanly by whether the finding is focal or diffuse - is the finding.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE. 'Higher resolution' is already refuted IN AGGREGATE: 392 px at the control's own encoder rate read 0.8459, +0.0002 (knee-a8x), and res392's +0.0066 was the RATE not the pixels. But that null is an average over twelve labels and this finding says six move each way, which is exactly the shape an aggregate erases (CLAUDE.md: 'a metric averaging the effect away'). The open question is therefore NOT 'does resolution help' but 'does resolution help THE SIX FOCAL LABELS while costing the six diffuse ones'. lr4e-5_ws_s2026 (336 px) and res392_ws_s2026 (392 px) are a matched pair differing only in pixels, both cached, so the test is a paired per-label bootstrap at ZERO GPU. Running as logs/perlabel_res.log.

PRICE: the per-label read is free. If the focal labels move with resolution, the arm is a focal specialist - tighter field at higher in-plane resolution, slice pooling that does not max away a five-pixel lesion - and it is ensembled in for the labels it owns rather than for its aggregate. P(the split is real given the mechanism and the clean sort) ~ 0.6; P(an arm built on it clears 1.5%) ~ 0.25.
notes:
THIRD REFUTATION, 2026-08-25, FROM THE LEDGER AND NOT FROM A RUN — the surviving lever in note (2) is not
untested, it was run and per-label gated nine days ago, and it FAILED ON THE FOCAL HALF.

Note (2) ends: 'a tighter field at the same pixel count (more pixels ON the structure rather than more
pixels overall) is a different mechanism and is untested.' That is precisely `crop80_tissue`: 80 mm about
the tissue centre at 336 px = 0.238 mm/px, against the control's 130 mm at 336 px = 0.39 mm/px. Same pixel
count, tighter field, 1.6x more pixels on the structure. It ran 2026-08-16.

AND ITS GATE WAS THE PER-LABEL READ THIS BEAD ASKS FOR, pre-registered two-sided in `crop80_tissue.sh`
exactly as here (small structures up, diffuse down) with the mean explicitly forbidden as the read. The
gate returned: the diffuse half landed as predicted (Baker's -0.028, Synovitis -0.019, Effusion -0.015)
and THE FOCAL HALF — the half the whole argument rests on — did not move. Medial Meniscus -0.012, ACL and
MCL at the floor, only Fracture up (+0.019, and the worst-agreement label in the corpus). So the trade the
mechanism predicts is not a trade: we pay the diffuse side and are not paid on the focal side.

`centre_tissue` closes the alternative reading: at the control's 130 mm extent, moving the crop's centre
to the tissue is a null (-0.0048, inside the floor). So `crop80_tissue`'s pattern is attributable to the
RESOLUTION change and not to the centring, which is what makes it a clean test of this note's mechanism
rather than a confounded one.

THREE ROUTES NOW AGREE AND THEY DO NOT SHARE A RULER: 392 px at constant field, null per label on 909
report-holdout studies (note 2); 80 mm at constant pixels, negative on the focal half at matched epoch 7;
and the same member refused by joint selection on cached probabilities (best-N containing crop80 sits
below best-N without it, at every N). Sampling density is not the focal lever at any operating point this
project has measured.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is now only this: the model's ABSOLUTE weakness on the focal structural labels is
real and independently confirmed (MCL 0.7927 on the 909-study holdout, its own worst). The finding stands;
every GEOMETRIC route to it is closed. The remaining candidates are supervision (knee-ombx, external data,
owner-blocked) and representation (knee-jk3, the 0.044 gap at matched train loss) — not pixels, not field,
not centring, not pooling depth.

METHOD NOTE ON MYSELF: this cost no GPU and no slot. It is the CLAUDE.md rule 'READ THE LEDGER BEFORE
FILING' paying out — the note that called the mechanism untested was written the day after the ledger
recorded it failing.
close_reason: Analysis complete, no action left IN THIS BEAD. Three independent routes (392px at constant field, crop80_tissue at constant pixels, joint selection on cached probabilities) agree that sampling density is not the focal lever at any operating point measured. The FINDING survives and is confirmed absolutely (MCL 0.7927, its own worst on the 909-study holdout), but every route it licensed is closed and the two that remain live elsewhere: supervision in knee-ombx (owner-blocked on Redivis tables) and representation in knee-jk3. Closing so bd ready stops offering a settled question as P0 work.

title: seat_value went dark when the champion moved to the all-data pool - every arm now prints a traceback instead of its seat
description:
REPRODUCED 2026-08-24: python -m kneemri.kaggle.seat_value --candidates distill_pairs_s2026.pt

  ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty
  member_distance.py:86 in spread(), via seat_value.py:140 MemberDistance(held, rest).report()

MECHANISM, and it is a fact about the RESULT rather than about the code. Champion.recorded() now reads allfit (0.937), six of whose seven members were fitted with --fold -1. SeatValue.scoreable() drops every one of those - they have seen fold 0, so they carry no honest holdout record - leaving a roster of ONE (band_dense_long_s2026). MemberDistance.spread() then asks each seated member for its nearest neighbour among the others, and with one member that iterable is empty.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TRACEBACK. Seat value is how a member is BOUGHT here; solo score has repeatedly failed to predict it. run_train calls seat_value automatically at the end of every arm, so from the moment allfit became the champion, EVERY finishing arm prints this traceback in place of its seat - distill_pairs and margin_smoke both did today. The ruler that decides whether a member ships is dark, and it went dark silently, as a side effect of a board entry improving.

TWO PARTS TO FIX, and the second is a design decision not a patch:
  1. MemberDistance.spread() - a roster of one has no nearest neighbour. Say so in a line; do not crash.
  2. SeatValue - refuse with a STATED DENOMINATOR when fewer than two champion members are scoreable, naming the reason (fold -1 members have seen the holdout), and let a member be priced against a named board entry whose members ARE scoreable (--against <entry-id>), so the seat number always carries the pool it was measured in.

DO NOT paper over part 1 alone: a spread line that prints for a roster of one would report a seat priced against a single member as though it were priced against the champion.

title: Train the metric: AUC-margin loss (Deep AUC Maximization) instead of BCE
description:
THE MECHANISM. The competition metric is the unweighted mean of twelve per-label ROC AUCs. We train binary cross-entropy (kneemri/training/objective.py:182). BCE is a calibration objective; AUC is a ranking one, and AUC is invariant to every monotone recalibration BCE spends capacity on. So a measurable fraction of every gradient step goes into a degree of freedom the scoreboard cannot see.

PRIOR ART, not an idea of mine. Deep AUC Maximization with the AUC-margin surrogate took 1st place in the Stanford CheXpert competition (2020), which is the closest published task shape to ours: multi-label, class-imbalanced, medical imaging, scored on mean AUROC. Yuan et al., 'Large-scale Robust Deep AUC Maximization: A New Surrogate Loss and Empirical Studies on Medical Image Classification' (arXiv 2012.03173, ICCV 2021). Reference implementation: LibAUC (Optimization-AI/LibAUC), which ships a multi-label AUROC example on CheXpert with DenseNet121. Reported to beat both cross-entropy and focal loss on large-scale medical multi-label.

WHY IT FITS THIS REPO WITHOUT A REWRITE. objective.py already has the strategy hierarchy: Objective (BCE) -> RankedObjective (adds a pairwise hinge term) -> DistilledObjective (adds teacher imitation). AUC-M is a fourth sibling, not a fork. The loss carries per-label learnable scalars (a, b) plus a margin dual alpha, optimised min-max; LibAUC uses PESG for the outer step, and whether our one-cycle AdamW is close enough to work is the first thing to find out.

THE ONE REAL DESIGN QUESTION. Our targets are FIVE DISCRETE LEVELS (0.08/0.28/0.68/0.82/0.94, core/data/labels/targets.py:34), and AUC-M is defined on binary labels. But the METRIC itself binarises, so the loss should be taken against the same binarisation the scorer uses, with the graded levels retained only in whatever auxiliary term rides alongside. Getting this wrong silently trains a different objective than the one being scored.

WHY IT IS NOT A KNOB. It changes what the network is asked to do, not how hard it is asked. That is the class of change the owner asked for ('better loss handling' rather than sharpening a subscore), and CheXpert-scale reports put it at roughly 0.01-0.02 mean AUROC over BCE — at or through the 1.5% bar rather than under it.

COST. One 12-epoch arm, ~76 min of card, control band_dense = 0.8578 already in the ledger. Zero submission slots. Read PER LABEL: the mechanism predicts the largest gains on the most imbalanced labels, since that is where BCE's calibration effort is most wasted and where the AUC margin bites hardest. A uniform lift is a weaker reading and a uniform lift matched by the rare labels lagging would refute the stated mechanism.

DEPENDENCY NOTE. LibAUC can be vendored-by-reference under external/ per the repo rule, or the AUC-margin loss reimplemented directly in objective.py — it is about thirty lines and reimplementing avoids a dependency for one term.
notes:
PRICE: ~80 min of card (12 epochs at ~400 s), 0 submission slots, no cache to build. Control band_dense = 0.8578 already exists, so no matched-control arm is owed.

GAIN the mechanism could plausibly deliver: the metric is twelve rank statistics and every member fitted here descends cross-entropy, which reads values. The published version of this substitution (Yuan et al., arXiv 2012.03173) took 1st on CheXpert 2020 — mean per-label AUC on multi-label medical images, this metric with a different organ. If the value/rank mismatch is costing anything here it is an OBJECTIVE-level defect, so its size is not knob-sized: 1-2% absolute is the honest ceiling.

P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~ 0.20. Two reasons it is not higher. (1) The recipe ALREADY carries a ranking term at 1.0, so part of the rank-vs-value gap is already paid for — this arm is the difference between a ranking term added to cross-entropy and a pure rank surrogate replacing it, not the difference between rank and no-rank. (2) The rare-label batch hole is pre-registered: Fracture is positive in ~7% of studies against a batch of twelve, so its term is skipped in roughly half of all steps. Expected value is still good at 80 min because a null here is INFORMATIVE — it retires the whole 'the loss is not the metric' axis, which currently licenses several unrun ideas.

Arm written: experiments/arms/margin_seat.sh. arm_check --only margin_seat: 0 refused. Smoke next.

title: The offline ruler is same-distribution and blind to robustness - the 0.950 audit verdict was the wrong FORM
description:
THE OFFLINE RULER IS SAME-DISTRIBUTION AND THEREFORE STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO ROBUSTNESS. The owner named this on 2026-08-24 and he was right, and it invalidates the FORM of a verdict this project has issued many times.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. knee-y3pv's audit swept every identified mechanism, found each flat inside the 0.0062 holdout floor, and concluded the 0.950 goal had no route left. The chain was: every knob is flat on the fold-0 holdout, therefore data volume is the only axis, therefore no legal corpus, therefore the door is shut. The first step is where it breaks. A holdout drawn from the same distribution as the training side measures FIT. The hidden Kaggle test set is not our data. A mechanism that buys robustness to distribution shift and costs a little in-distribution fit reads exactly FLAT-OR-NEGATIVE on our ruler while being worth real board points. I measured fit and reported it as the whole space.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM, and the two are not the same statement: "no offline-MEASURABLE knob remains" is supported. "0.950 is unreachable" is not, and I collapsed them.

THE EVIDENCE WAS ALREADY IN THE LEDGER, and it points one way every time:
  calib_span -0.0020 offline, board up past 0.928.
  base_dense -0.0066 offline, outside the floor and 2.5x the card cost, board up a tick.
  through_dense flat in its own arm, board tick as the seventh seat.
  The ruler under-prices DIVERSITY by a measured factor of 2.4.
  And the 0.932 to 0.937 move itself was NOT bought by any offline gain - it was all-data seats plus seats bought on axis distance.
Three members whose offline number said no and whose board said yes is not scatter; it is a systematic sign error on one axis.

THE SECOND ARITHMETIC ERROR, which compounded it. I priced the remaining door against the knob space's measured ceiling of ~0.872, making +0.0068 offline look like 2.6x the remaining headroom, hence "shut". That is the headroom of the IDENTIFIED KNOB SPACE, not of the data axis. On the data slope the same target is 0.34 of a doubling, roughly +930 training studies - SMALLER than MRNet's 1,370. The door is LICENCE-BLOCKED, not unreachable, and those are different findings with different responses.

WHAT THIS CHANGES GOING FORWARD:
  A small negative offline delta on a mechanism whose PURPOSE is robustness is no longer sufficient to kill it. It is a reason to look at the board, which is the only ruler that sees the axis.
  The backlog of arms killed on deltas between -0.008 and 0 needs re-reading with that filter, since that band is where a robustness trade would land. aug_long is the first and is filed separately.
  Nothing here licenses ignoring offline numbers generally. It licenses distrusting them for ONE class of mechanism - those that trade in-distribution fit for invariance - and the class has to be named in advance, not after the board comes back.

NOT A REASON TO SPEND SLOTS FREELY. The board is a scarce ruler with its own repeat noise at this band, and this bead argues for re-reading a killed backlog, not for submitting from it at random.
notes:

  focal_pool adds a top-eighth-of-channel term to the pooled vector — a focal-lesion sensitivity term.

title: Rank-distillation from the fold-0 ensemble: one student, three exits (owner design 2026-08-24)
description:
OWNER'S DESIGN, and the unification is his. I had split this into three bets - distil-and-replace (efficiency), soft-targets-as-denser-supervision, and distilled-student-as-a-diverse-member. He collapsed them correctly: A and C are the SAME ARTEFACT with two exits chosen by the measurement rather than in advance, and B is not a separate training at all, it is an extra LOSS TERM in that one run. So: one student, one arm, three outcomes.

  EXIT A - student reaches teacher parity: ship it alone. 7 forward passes become 1, ~1h -> ~9min on a T4. That is the Efficiency Prize, which we currently lose by construction.
  EXIT C - student short of parity but structurally distant: seat it as a member. The ledger's own rule is 'buy a seat on the AXIS, not on the count and not on the solo score', and an encoder-family-distant member is more distant than anything ever seated (twin 0.930, recipe-distant 0.931, objective-distant 0.931, pixel-distant 0.932).
  EXIT B is the loss, and it runs either way.

THE LOSS FORM IS DECIDED BY THE METRIC, NOT BY THE DISTILLATION LITERATURE. Standard KD is KL on softened probabilities. That is wrong here and the repo already says why: ensemble.py:6, 'Calibration is worth nothing, so no thresholding, no temperature, no Platt scaling.' The metric is twelve rank-based AUCs, so a KL spends student capacity matching probability VALUES the metric discards. The term should be PAIRWISE ORDER against the teacher, and RankedObjective.pairs(above, below) already computes exactly that mass - it is handed labels today and would be handed teacher scores instead. Same tested code, different supervision.

WHY THIS IS NEW SUPERVISION AND NOT A RESTATEMENT OF THE LABELS - the mechanism that makes it worth card time. Under binary labels a pair carries order information ONLY if it is a positive against a negative; same-class pairs are unordered and teach nothing. Under teacher scores EVERY pair is ordered, including positive-vs-positive and negative-vs-negative. Effusion is positive in ~60% of studies so labels order ~48% of its pairs; Fracture is ~7% so labels order ~13% of its pairs; the teacher orders 100% of both. That is genuinely more supervision on the SAME corpus, with no external data and no licence answer - which matters because knee-y3pv's audit closed with data volume as the only axis above the bar and knee-ombx blocked on an owner licence call.

PRE-REGISTERED, and it is a PER-LABEL clause rather than a mean: the gain must CONCENTRATE on the labels with the most skewed positive rate, because that is where binary pairs are scarcest and where the teacher adds the most orderings. Fracture (~7%) should gain most, Effusion (~60%) least.
