This bead asked whether 864 images fits a T4 for the largest member. It is the wrong question twice over - a large member never sends 864, and the dry-run it prescribed cannot answer it (the visible test set has THREE studies, so a chunk never fills and the memory path is never exercised; it would pass and prove nothing).

WHAT THE WIDTH-SCALED BUDGET ACTUALLY GUARANTEES, computed rather than assumed:
    variant   dim   imgs/forward   weights   activations   total
    small     384      864          0.04 GB    1.15 GB     1.19 GB
    base      768      432          0.17 GB    1.15 GB     1.32 GB
    large    1024      324          0.61 GB    1.15 GB     1.76 GB
The activation term is IDENTICAL across variants by construction - that is what budget = IMAGE_BUDGET * BUDGET_WIDTH // dim buys - and every variant lands under 2 GB against the T4's 15.8. There is no tightness to worry about.

THE TERM THAT WOULD HAVE DOMINATED AND DOES NOT: a materialised 577x577 attention matrix. SDPA is on by default under transformers 5.15 (checked, _attn_implementation reports 'sdpa'), so it is never built. A naive estimate that included it would predict an OOM that will not happen - which is the shape of error worth naming, since it would have argued for shrinking a budget that is already correct.

So the guard is right, the headroom is an order of magnitude, and nothing needs measuring on the card.
close_reason: All three links fixed and the remaining question answered analytically: the width-scaled budget gives an identical activation peak across variants, every one lands under 2 GB against the T4's 15.8, and SDPA means the attention matrix that would dominate is never materialised. The dry-run this bead prescribed could not have answered it - three visible test studies never fill a chunk.

title: Overlap TTA and whole-stack are the SAME mechanism, which is why they do not compose
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 10:16Z by the corrected diversity curve, which reads each member the way it was fitted.

  member              trained holdout   curve with overlap TTA   TTA gain
  lr5x_d6 (windowed)      0.8323              0.8475              +0.0152
  max12   (windowed)      0.8310              0.8451              +0.0141
  large_deep (windowed)   0.8304              0.8450              +0.0146
  wsfold0_e6 (whole)      0.8457              0.8457               0.0000
  slices16   (whole)      0.8452              0.8452               0.0000

WHOLE-STACK GAINS NOTHING FROM WINDOW TTA, because it has no windows to average - and the windowed gain (+0.0146) is almost exactly whole-stack's training-time advantage (+0.0147). That is not a coincidence: averaging ten overlapping three-slice windows means the model DOES see every slice, aggregated in PREDICTION space (mean over windows) rather than in FEATURE space (max over slices). Same mechanism - see all the slices - reached two ways.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LEDGER: whole-stack's +0.0147 is measured against a control scored WITHOUT TTA. At inference, where the windowed members get their TTA, the advantage is gone: wsfold0_e6 scores 0.8457 and lr5x_d6 scores 0.8475. It is not that whole-stack is worthless - it is that we were comparing a recipe with its inference-time trick against one without.

THIS EXPLAINS THE LEADERBOARD. Our whole-stack members scored 0.882 while the older windowed five scored 0.888, and I had attributed that entirely to ensemble size and the whole_stack serving bug. Part of it is this: the windowed members were getting a +0.0146 inference-time lift that the whole-stack members structurally cannot get.

WHAT SURVIVES: res392 is 0.8523 with no TTA available to it, still ahead of every windowed member WITH TTA. Resolution is a genuinely separate axis and is unaffected by this.

THE ARM THIS IMPLIES: whole-stack needs a DIFFERENT test-time augmentation, on an axis it has not already exhausted - small rotations and shifts matching the training augmentation, or multi-scale crops. Slice coverage is spent; spatial jitter is not. If it lands near +0.014 it is the largest inference-side lever available and it costs no training.

title: Close the witness loop: verify_members must re-derive it through the inference path
description:
2026-08-12 07:50Z. HALF DONE - the witness is now RECORDED (578a785); nothing CHECKS it yet.

WHAT EXISTS. Every run from now on writes config['witness'] = {studies: [8 identifiers], predictions: [[12 floats] x 8]}, produced by trainer.predict at the best epoch - i.e. by the TRAINING path, reading the way training read. It is inside config, so package_members carries it into the manifest for free, and Member.witness reads it back. Empty for the twenty published members and every checkpoint on disk today.

WHAT IS MISSING, and it is the whole point: verify_members.py must load those studies FROM THE CACHE, run them through Ensemble.predict_member - the INFERENCE path - and refuse the member if the numbers move. Any consumer-side default that changes what the model reads shows up as a difference; that is precisely the class of defect the fingerprint cannot see, four of which shipped this session.

TOLERANCE: the two paths differ legitimately in one way - inference may average overlapping windows where trainer.predict reads one. For a whole_stack member they must now agree closely (both read the whole stack), so start there with a tight tolerance and treat a windowed member's witness as advisory until the window policy is pinned in the witness itself.

WHY IT IS WORTH FINISHING RATHER THAN LEAVING AS A RECORDED FIELD: a recorded field with no reader is exactly the bug this session found four times. Do not let the witness become the fifth.
notes:
2026-08-12 08:02Z — READER LANDED (comp/witness_check.py) and wired into prepare_submission.sh as step 2b, so it runs before every submission rather than on request.

It feeds the MIDDLE window - the whole stack for a whole_stack member, one group otherwise - which is exactly what Trainer.predict reads. Both paths then see the same pixels, so a difference is attributable to the READING (decode size, slot scheme and order, depth, pooling, whole-stack) rather than to test-time window averaging, which is a legitimate choice.

CURRENT STATE, honestly: 0 ok, 3 unverified, 0 refused. All three packaged members predate the witness, so there is nothing to re-derive; UNVERIFIED is reported separately from ok precisely so a check that cannot run does not read as a check that passed.

STILL OWED, and the reason this bead stays open: the REFUSE path has not been exercised against a real member. The next arm to finish under the new code (slice_attention) writes a witness, and the demonstration to run then is: check it passes, then flip whole_stack off in a copy of the manifest and confirm it is REFUSED. Until that is done the check is argued, not proven.
close_reason:
PROVEN, not argued. The refuse path is now exercised against a real member: sliceattn_s2026 with whole_stack flipped to False in a copied manifest is REFUSED at max|diff| 0.407 against a 0.00391 bound - 104x. Unflipped, four members pass (extended_ws 0.0156/0.0312, intensity392 0.00162/0.00391, schedule_8 0.00159/0.00391, sliceattn 0.00234/0.00391).

It earned its keep on first real use, finding three defects nothing else could see: torch.compile renaming every state-dict key (knee-5he), bf16 members served in fp16 (knee-5qt), and its own tolerance being tighter than bf16's epsilon (knee-6pi). Also gained --device so it runs without a free GPU.

title: [bug] Study.bag emitted six slots whatever the scheme said, so an extended cache would have been all zeros
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-12 07:33Z, third seam of the pipeline bughunt. Found BEFORE the 54 GB extended build was spent.

THE DEFECT. Study.bag routed with the pipeline's scheme (SlotScheme.slots) and then EMITTED using the module-level canonical SLOTS. The two halves of one method disagreed. With --scheme extended: route nine series, emit six bags.

THE FAILURE IT WOULD HAVE PRODUCED, which is the worst shape available: StudyCache allocates the images array at the scheme's width, so images[position] = bag raises a shape error for EVERY study. decode_one catches OSError/ValueError/RuntimeError/IndexError and reports the study ABSENT in every slot - by design, because a black image the mask calls acquired is a silent lie. So the build would log 4,407 'decode failed' lines, run to completion, write the mask with np.save at the end, and leave a 54 GB cache of zeros whose mask says nothing was acquired. wait_for_cache keys on that mask, so the queue would then have started a 90-minute training run against zeros.

It is the exact scenario the codebase already documents fearing in two places ('it would fit a mostly-zero array and return a plausible, wrong answer').

FIXED: bag() iterates self.pipeline.scheme.slots. Removing the last hardcoded use made the SLOTS import unused in study.py, which is the linter confirming there is now one source of truth. A test asserts a nine-slot scheme yields nine bags and nine mask entries.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, still open in knee-nwh: inference builds its pipeline with a DEFAULT SlotScheme, so an extended member would still be served six canonical slots at submission time even though the cache and training are now correct. Either thread the member's config['slots'] into SlotPipeline or refuse a non-canonical member at load.

RELATED, worth one line: decode_one and Submission.decode share ONE decode implementation (both call Study.from_directory(...).bag()). An earlier note in this session claiming 'two decode implementations' was wrong - what diverged was how the pipeline was CONFIGURED, not the code.

title: [bug] Inference hardcoded 336 px and the canonical six slots, ignoring what members recorded
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 07:18Z, second seam of the pipeline bughunt. Resolution FIXED; the slot half is still open.

THE PATTERN, now four instances deep: a field travels in the checkpoint, and inference reads a default instead. slices was fixed reactively after a member fitted on a deeper stack was scored on twelve. variant, slice_pooling and whole_stack each cost a separate incident. img and slots were never given the same treatment.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Submission.decode built Study.from_directory(dir, planes) with NO pipeline, so the decode ran at SlotReader()'s default 336 px regardless of member.img - and Study.bag iterates the module-level canonical SLOTS, so a nine-slot member gets six. pixel_group exists precisely to say which members can share one decode; verify_members prints how many groups there are and the inference path never asks.

WHY IT HAD NOT BITTEN YET: every member submitted so far is 336 px and six slots, so the default happened to be right. Both queued arms break that: resolution reads a 448 px cache at 392 (would have been served 336 upsampled to 392, where training downsampled from 448) and extended_slots is nine slots.

FIXED: Ensemble.decoded_size() returns the single distinct member resolution and RAISES on disagreement - resolution cannot be windowed down the way depth can, so two sizes are genuinely two decodes. Submission.decode now builds SlotPipeline(reader=SlotReader(image_size=...)) from it. Test asserts both halves.

STILL OPEN, and it blocks extended_slots from ever being submitted correctly: Study.bag iterates SLOTS from the module rather than the member's config['slots']. An extended member would load, run, and predict from six of its nine slots with the head's slot embedding misaligned. Either thread the scheme through SlotPipeline (it already holds a SlotScheme, so this is plumbing rather than design) or refuse a non-canonical member at load with a clear message. Do NOT leave it silent.

DO THIS BEFORE SUBMITTING ANY 448 OR EXTENDED MEMBER.
notes: 2026-08-12 07:43Z — CLOSED OUT. The slot half is fixed: Ensemble.decoded_scheme() rebuilds the scheme from the members' recorded slot names and Submission.decode passes it into SlotPipeline. Disagreement between members is refused (a different slot list is a different decode, not a subset), and a name this build does not define is refused rather than silently dropped. Tested for all three cases plus the canonical one. Extended members are now submittable as far as this path is concerned.

title: [bug] whole_stack was recorded in every checkpoint and read by nobody: inference windowed our best members
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 07:13Z in a pipeline bughunt. FIXED in the same session; the leaderboard cost is already paid and measured.

THE DEFECT. Ensemble.predict_member windowed EVERY member by member.group (3 slices), always. A whole-stack member is trained so a slot embedding is the elementwise MAXIMUM OVER THE FULL STACK; serving it three slices at a time gives maxima over a quarter of the stack and averages ten of those. Different function, same pixels.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, which is the part worth keeping:
  - The fingerprint pins image size and group, NOT stack depth or reading mode, so every member verified.
  - Holdout scoring (Trainer.predict) reads self.window, which whole_stack sets to the full stack - so the local number was measured consistently with training and looked fine.
  - The config key 'whole_stack' was written by MemberRecord from the day the flag existed, and Member had no accessor for it. Exactly the slice_pooling failure repeated: recorded faithfully, read by nobody.

THE EVIDENCE IT COST US: two whole-stack members at 0.8481 holdout scored 0.882 on the public board, while five channel-stacked windowed members at 0.8269 scored 0.888. The windowed members were served the way they were trained; ours were not. That inversion was filed as knee-lv2 and read as 'member quality does not transfer' - part of it was this bug.

THE FIX: Member.whole_stack (defaults False, so the twenty published members stay windowed - they were fitted that way), and predict_member takes ONE pass over the middle member.slices of the decoded chunk, mirroring Trainer.predict. Two tests protect it: one asserts the whole-stack path equals a single forward over the middle slices, one asserts a windowed member is NOT equal to that.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT UNDO: knee-9pl's member-count curve stands - 1 member 0.868, 2 members 0.882, 5 members 0.888 - because all three entries were served through the same defective path, so the COMPARISON between them is still like-for-like. What changes is that the absolute numbers for the whole-stack entries were depressed.

THE GENERAL LESSON, and the third instance now: a field that travels in a checkpoint needs a READER and a test, or it is decoration. Audit every remaining MemberConfig key for an accessor - 'rules', 'band', 'crop_mm' and 'slot_fallback' are read by pixel_group only, and slot_fallback has no implementation at all (knee-t92).

title: Ensemble SIZE beats member quality by 0.020 LB: one 0.8518 model scores 0.868, five 0.8269 models score 0.888
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12, four leaderboard entries built to isolate exactly this.

  members  holdout/member  public LB
    1        0.8518          0.868     kneemri-solo, our strongest single model ever
    2        0.8481          0.882     whole-stack fold0+fold1
    5        0.8269          0.888     the old channel-stacked windowed members
    3        0.8493          pending
   23        mixed           pending   fusion: ours + 20 published

THE RESULT: our BEST single model loses to five much weaker ones by 0.020. Per-member holdout quality of +0.025 (0.8518 vs 0.8269) is worth LESS than four extra members. Ensembling is the largest effect measured anywhere in this project - larger than whole-stack (+0.0147 holdout), larger than any knob.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: nothing here defends folds or seeds as a METHOD. They remain banned and the ban is well-founded - the noise floor is the holdout's own sampling error (knee-2rx), so re-running a recipe cannot produce a better measurement. What the curve says is that AVERAGING MANY PREDICTORS is worth ~0.02 on this metric, whatever produced them.

THE SYNTHESIS, and the plan it implies: get many members that differ by MECHANISM rather than by RNG. Every arm is fitted on the same fold-0 split, so every arm already produces an averageable member. We own about six: whole-stack, channel-stacked+rate, per-slice max windowed, 20-slice, DINOv2-large, and now 16-slice. diversity_curve measures every subset of these offline - no submission spent - and it is next in the GPU queue.

IF THE CURVE CONFIRMS: the shipping entry is a mechanism-diverse ensemble, and every future arm has a second purpose beyond its own verdict - it is also a member. That makes arms cheaper, not more expensive.

CAVEAT ON READING THE 5-MEMBER ROW: those five ARE fold members, so the 0.888 was produced by a banned method. It stands as EVIDENCE about ensemble size; it is not a recipe to repeat.
notes:
2026-08-12 10:31Z — THE CORRECTED CURVE, ON OUR OWN MEMBERS ONLY, no grafted weights:

  members  mean     best subset  marginal
    1      0.8452   0.8475        -
    2      0.8516   0.8552       +0.0064
    3      0.8539   0.8562       +0.0023
    4      0.8551   0.8567       +0.0012
    6      0.8563   0.8563       +0.0005

+0.0092 for the best 4-member subset over the best single member, saturating at four - the same shape the leaderboard showed (1 -> 2 big, 2 -> 3 nothing), reproduced from work we own. This is the number that says an all-ours ensemble is worth submitting.

CAVEAT: this ran on the SIX older members. It excludes res392 (0.8523, better than the best member in it) and slice_attention. The arm now includes both, which member_curve can only do since it learned to group checkpoints by cache - res392 reads the 448 px cache and the rest read 336. title: Per-label AUC is a fold-0 artefact: Fracture moves +0.119 between folds while the mean moves 0.005
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 06:04Z with the new kneemri.run_comparison, over three whole-stack runs of the SAME recipe on three folds.

  label      fold1 vs fold0   fold2 vs fold0
  Fracture       +0.1187          +0.0803
  ACL            -0.0368          -0.0745
  MCL            +0.0476          +0.0053
  MEAN           +0.0048          +0.0061

THE MEAN IS STABLE AND THE PARTS ARE NOT. Per-label AUC swings by 0.05-0.12 between folds under an identical recipe; the mean of twelve moves by 0.005. Averaging twelve noisy numbers is what makes the metric readable at all.

THIS BREAKS TWO THINGS I BUILT TODAY.

1. knee-1dw's premise. 'MCL 0.755 and Fracture 0.784 are our worst labels, worth +0.0173 if lifted' is a FOLD-0 statement. On fold 1 Fracture is 0.903 and on fold 2 it is 0.864 - it is not a weak label, it is weak on one holdout. MCL ranges 0.755-0.803. The bead was already re-priced once against CoPAS; this is the stronger refutation and it comes from our own data.

2. The falsification design of the resolution and extended-slots arms. Both were written to be judged by whether their gain CONCENTRATES in named labels (MCL/ACL/menisci, MCL/LCL). A concentrated gain of the size those mechanisms could plausibly deliver is SMALLER than the fold-to-fold noise in exactly those labels, so a single-fold per-label table cannot falsify either story. As written, the prediction is unfalsifiable rather than strict.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT FALSIFIABLE, none of which is a fold ensemble: score the SAME holdout for every arm (already true - all arms are fold 0), and compare per-label deltas only against the SAME-FOLD control, never across folds. That is what run_comparison does by construction. The remaining question is whether a per-label delta on one holdout is large enough to read at all, which needs the positive COUNT per label on that holdout - cheap to compute, not yet done.

DO NOT respond by running more folds. The point is that per-label numbers on one holdout are noisy, not that we need more holdouts; the arms are compared on a shared fold-0 holdout, which is the correct design.

title: Better members did not beat more members: 2 whole-stack (0.882) lost to 5 weaker (0.888)
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 05:55Z on the public leaderboard.

  5 members, holdout mean 0.8269 (channel-stacked, windowed)  -> LB 0.888
  2 members, holdout mean 0.8481 (whole-stack)                -> LB 0.882

The two whole-stack members are +0.021 better EACH on holdout and the ensemble scored 0.006 LOWER. I predicted an improvement; that prediction is refuted.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH. 0.006 is small and the public LB is a subset, so this may be LB noise rather than a real inversion. It is not evidence that whole-stack is worse - whole-stack is +0.0147 on a matched holdout comparison, measured twice.

WHAT IT DOES ESTABLISH: member QUALITY alone does not carry the leaderboard. Something about member COUNT, or about the DIVERSITY that count brings, is worth at least as much as 0.021 of per-member holdout - and our holdout gains are not transferring 1:1.

THE CURVE IS ALREADY IN FLIGHT, on nearly the same members, so this is answerable rather than speculative:
  1 member   kneemri-solo   (fold2, 0.8518)          submitted 05:55Z
  2 members  0.882                                    COMPLETE
  3 members  kneemri-trained v5                       submitted 05:55Z
  23 members kneemri-fusion (ours 3 + published 20)   RUNNING

READ IT AS A CURVE, not four results. If solo is far below 0.882 and 3 is above it, count dominates and the no-fold direction has a real cost that must be paid another way. If solo is close to 0.882, the count effect is small and the 0.882-vs-0.888 gap is noise.

IF COUNT MATTERS, the replacement is NOT folds or seeds. It is DIVERSITY ENSEMBLING over the arms we are already running: 336px vs 392px, 12 vs 16 slices, max vs attention pooling, six vs nine slots. Every arm produces a member fitted on the same fold-0 split, so they are directly averageable and each one was paid for by a question we wanted answered anyway. That is ensembling by mechanism rather than by re-running the same recipe with a different seed.

title: Extended slots: 1,139 discarded CORONAL series against our worst label, which is read coronally
description:
2026-08-11 21:25Z. Arm written: experiments/arms/extended_slots.sh, queued after the current GPU chain.

THE MECHANISM, and why it is not another knob. 2,421 of 24,371 series (9.9%) match no slot predicate, so nothing can route them; three sequences are 96% of that, and the largest is Coronal|fluid|nofs at 1,139 series. Every large effect measured here has come from giving the model more of the data it was already handed - whole-stack was +0.0147 on exactly that mechanism, while every knob inside the design returned about 0.005.

WHY IT IS AIMED. MCL is read CORONALLY and is our weakest label (0.755 vs Baker's 0.896) on an unweighted mean of twelve AUCs. A coronal sequence that never reaches the model cannot be read for a medial ligament. The arm therefore carries a falsifiable prediction: the gain CONCENTRATES in MCL and LCL and is small for the sagittal-read targets. A uniform lift would instead say the extra slots act as capacity, which is a weaker and different finding.

TWO PIECES OF PLUMBING WERE ALREADY RIGHT AND ONE WAS NOT. StudyCache.key already puts the scheme in the cache filename, so an extended build cannot clobber the six-slot cache every existing member was fitted on. lib.sh wait_for_cache did NOT - it keyed on mask_336px_12sl.npy, the canonical mask, which already exists, so an extended arm's gate would have passed instantly on a cache that was never built. Fixed in the same commit.

COST: a 9-slot cache is ~54 GB and must be built ALONE (the 448 build killed both itself and a trainer when it shared the machine). A step encodes 1.5x the images.

ACCEPTED COST: a nine-slot member has a wider slot embedding and cannot ensemble with the published six-slot members. That is cheap now that fold/seed ensembling is out and the target entry is a single model.
notes:
THE ARM RAN, 2026-08-12: extended_ws_s2026 = 0.8459 against the control's 0.8457. REFUTED as an improvement on the mean, and this bead has read as unstarted work ever since.

ITS FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION IS STILL UNANSWERED, and I got that wrong once today before correcting it. The arm predicted the gain CONCENTRATES in MCL and LCL. I recorded 'the per-label prediction failed' on the strength of MCL +0.0056 and Lateral Meniscus -0.0130 - but calibrated against each label's own sampling interval, NOT ONE of its twelve deltas clears (MCL's +0.0056 against +/-0.040). The prediction was never refuted, it was UNREAD, and calling it refuted spent a mechanism on noise.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, and it is now built: the paired interval (knee-3vh). Two arms scored on the SAME 881 studies share their sampling error, so the paired band is about eleven times tighter than the unpaired one used above - the difference between 'unread' and an answer. member_curve --paired reports it, and it needs one inference pass over members already on disk.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT DISPROVED BY A FLAT MEAN. 1,139 coronal series still never reach the model, MCL is still read coronally and still our weakest label. What is disproved is that adding them lifts the MEAN, which was never the interesting claim.
close_reason: Arm ran and is refuted on the mean (0.8459 vs 0.8457). Its per-label prediction is UNREAD rather than refuted - no delta clears its own interval - and settling it now belongs to knee-3vh, the paired floor, which is built and needs one inference pass. The member is retained for diversity. Leaving this open reads as unstarted work when the arm ran two days ago.

title: The metric is an unweighted mean, so our two worst labels are worth +0.0173 - above the bar
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 from the whole-stack fold-0 member (mean 0.8457), using the per-label table RunMetrics now records every epoch.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THIS THE BIGGEST LEVER ON THE BOARD: the competition metric is the UNWEIGHTED mean of twelve per-label ROC AUCs. A point of AUC on MCL is worth exactly as much as a point on Effusion. Our labels are not close to level:

  MCL              0.755   <- worst
  Fracture         0.784
  Lateral OA       0.822
  PF OA            0.824
  ...
  Medial Meniscus  0.893
  Baker's          0.896   <- best

Lifting a label to 0.873 - a level we demonstrably reach on five others - is worth (0.873 - x)/12 on the mean:
  MCL      +0.0098
  Fracture +0.0074
  bottom two together  +0.0173, which is ABOVE the 1.5% bar and larger than whole-stack (+0.0147).

TWO EXPLANATIONS TESTED AND BOTH REFUTED, which is what makes this actionable rather than a shrug:
  - NOT RARITY. Synovitis has 580 positives (13.2%), FEWER than MCL's 767 (17.4%), and scores 0.873 against MCL's 0.755.
  - NOT LABEL NOISE. Synovitis has the LOWEST mean reader confidence in the corpus (0.189) and still scores 0.873; MCL has high confidence (0.789) and scores worst. Baker's at confidence 0.508 is our BEST label at 0.896.
So neither how often a finding occurs nor how sure the report reader was predicts how well we do. MCL is HARD TO SEE. That is an imaging problem, and it contradicts this project's standing 'supervision-limited' thesis for at least this label.

WHERE THAT POINTS: the MCL is a thin structure at the MEDIAL MARGIN of the field, read coronally. A 130 mm crop at 336 px is 0.39 mm per pixel, and the occlusion test already showed centre-only and border-only scoring the same, i.e. no privileged reading of the joint centre. knee-dft (336 -> 448) carries a pre-registered prediction that any gain must CONCENTRATE in ACL/MCL/meniscus - it now has a named target with measured headroom, which makes it a sharper experiment than when it was filed.

FRACTURE IS PROBABLY A DIFFERENT PROBLEM: 7.1% prevalence and confidence 0.406 - both low. Marrow oedema needs fluid-sensitive fat-suppressed sequences, which we do route. Worth separating from MCL rather than treating 'the two worst labels' as one thing.

WHAT NOT TO DO, per the house rule: do not reweight the loss toward the weak labels. 'Keep the objective general - never fit it to a specific weakness; fix needs with balanced data, not loss-engineering.' If a balance fix is warranted it belongs in SAMPLING - oversampling studies carrying rare positives - not in per-label loss weights, and it should be justified by prevalence, which the numbers above say is NOT the problem here anyway.
notes: 2026-08-12 06:05Z — REFUTED by our own data; do not plan against the +0.0173. kneemri.run_comparison over three whole-stack runs of the same recipe shows Fracture at 0.784 on fold 0, 0.903 on fold 1 and 0.864 on fold 2, and MCL ranging 0.755-0.803. The 'two worst labels' were a property of the fold-0 holdout, not of the model. See knee-70w. The mean across twelve labels is stable to ~0.005 across the same folds, which is why the mean is the readable number and a single per-label AUC is not.
close_reason: REFUTED by knee-70w. The premise was that MCL 0.755 and Fracture 0.784 are stable weaknesses worth +0.0173. They are fold-0 sampling artefacts: Fracture moves +0.119 between folds while the mean moves 0.005, and the Hanley-McNeil SE for 62 Fracture positives is +/-0.061 at 95%. There is no per-label weakness here to target.

title: Attend across slices instead of maxing them: the published successor to what just worked
description:
PRIOR ART, found 2026-08-11 after whole-stack paid off. Medical Slice Transformer (Nature Scientific Reports 2025) encodes each slice with a 2D encoder - DINOv2, the same backbone we use - and then runs a SLICE TRANSFORMER with attention across slices, plus within-slice patch attention. A two-stage transformer with a [CLS] token over the slice sequence appears in the same literature, and Memory-Guided Transformer (Pattern Recognition 2025) adds group attention across anatomical planes, reporting best-in-class on MRNet.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT NEXT ARM RATHER THAN A NEW IDEA: we have just measured that seeing every slice per step is worth +0.0147, our largest change, using the crudest possible aggregation - an elementwise maximum. Max keeps, per feature dimension, whichever slice shouted loudest and discards which slice it was and everything the others said. Attention over the same axis keeps the axis.

THE CHANGE IS SMALL AND LOCAL. model.py slot_features already encodes each slice separately under slice_pooling='max' and ends with:
    pooled.reshape(batch, slots, group, -1).amax(dim=2)
The slice axis is right there. Replacing amax with a learned attention over dim=2 - a query per diagnosis, or a single shared query to start - is a contained edit behind a new slice_pooling value, so every existing member keeps loading.

SUPPORTING EVIDENCE FROM OUR OWN MEASUREMENTS:
  - the occlusion depth profile spans 0.7976..0.8332 across windows, so WHICH slice matters, and max deliberately throws that away.
  - SlotHead already does exactly this trick one level up (per-diagnosis query attention over slots, masked) and it works. This is the same mechanism applied to the axis below it.
  - the depth-by-label diagnostic exists to say whether labels want different depths; if they do, a per-diagnosis slice query is the correct shape rather than a shared one.

RISK, stated up front: it adds parameters to a model this project has repeatedly called supervision-limited, and 58 image-read labels is not much to fit an attention with. The anatomical prior - forcing correct slot attention - measured neutral, which is evidence that MORE attention machinery is not automatically better here. Start with a single shared query, not per-diagnosis.

RUN ORDER: after tonight's folds, and after knee-gtw (20 slices under whole-stack), which is cheaper and tests the same axis by adding evidence rather than parameters.

title: Slice count is UNREFUTED under whole-stack: the old test only ruled it out for windowed reading
description:
THE REFUTATION WE HAVE DOES NOT COVER THIS CASE, and the distinction is mechanical.

WHAT WAS REFUTED (knee-ezz, closed): 20 cached slices against 12, both read as ONE RANDOM 3-SLICE WINDOW per step. 0.8309 vs 0.8310 - nothing. It could not have worked: at a fixed group of 3 the window covers 3 slices however many are cached, so more slices only changes which window can be drawn, not what a step sees.

WHY WHOLE-STACK CHANGES THE QUESTION: whole-stack reads EVERY cached slice per slot per step, so the cached slice count IS the anatomy a step sees - 12 slices is 72 images per study, 20 is 120. No window, no group to thin. The mechanism that made the old arm null is absent.

SUPPORT: whole-stack itself is +0.0147 and its mechanism is exactly 'see more of the stack'; the occlusion depth profile spans 0.7976..0.8332; the 0.20-0.80 band holds ~18 slices on the median study and we keep 12; MRNet maxes over ALL slices, not a fixed 12. The 20-slice cache is already built (59.7 GB), so this costs no decode.

THE BLOCKER, measured rather than assumed: whole-stack at batch 12 with 12 slices puts 864 images through the encoder and holds 19.2 GB with gradient checkpointing on. Twenty slices is 1440 images, about 1.7x, so roughly 33 GB - MORE THAN THE 32 GB CARD. This arm cannot run as a drop-in.

THE THREE WAYS OUT, and none is free:
  1. Batch 8 instead of 12: ~960 images, fits in ~22 GB. But the ranking term scores pairs WITHIN a batch - 66 pairs at 12, 28 at 8 - so it changes the objective, and the arm would no longer be single-variable against tonight's folds.
  2. Cache 16 slices rather than 20: ~1150 images, ~26 GB. Fits, keeps the batch, and still recovers most of the band's median 18 slices. Costs one decode pass (~40 min, CPU).
  3. Accept the whole card and drop coexistence with the other project for the duration.

RECOMMENDED: (2). It keeps the batch and therefore the objective, it tests the same mechanism, and the decode is CPU work that can run while the GPU does something else. Sixteen is also closer to what the band actually holds than twenty.

RUN AFTER tonight's folds.
notes: 2026-08-12 06:46Z — REFUTED under whole-stack, by direct measurement rather than by the old windowed argument. Peak 0.8452 at epoch 6 against the control's 0.8457 = -0.0005, and the matched-epoch curve ran +0.001 to +0.002 throughout, all inside a 0.0053 floor. 16 slices cost 33% more compute per step (440-530 s vs ~350 s) for nothing. Depth coverage saturates at whole-stack 12; the mechanism that pays is reading the whole stack, not caching more of it.

title: Whole-stack peaks at epoch 9 of 24, so its epoch budget is wrong
description:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-11, and the shorter budget scored HIGHER rather than merely cheaper.

  whole-stack, 24 epochs: best 0.8413, peak at epoch 6
  whole-stack, 12 epochs: best 0.8457, peak at epoch 6

Same peak LOCATION, better peak VALUE, half the wall-clock. The peak epoch is a property of how much the model sees per step, not of the schedule length - 4x the imaging per step means convergence around epoch 6 either way.

WHY THE SHORTER RUN SCORES BETTER, which is the part that is not obvious: one-cycle is defined over total_steps. A 24-epoch budget stretches warmup and decay across epochs the model does not need, so at the epoch where it actually converges the learning rate is still far from annealed. Matching the budget to the convergence point makes the anneal land where the model is.

So an inflated epoch budget is not a harmless waste of GPU - it detunes the schedule. That reframes the 8 -> 24 epoch result from earlier today: that gain was measured on the WINDOWED recipe, which needs the longer budget because it sees a quarter as much per step. The budget belongs to the recipe, not to the project.

APPLIED: experiments/arms/whole_stack.sh and wholestack_folds.sh both run 12 epochs.
NOT YET TESTED: 8 epochs, which the peak-at-6 suggests might do as well again. Left alone tonight because folds 1-3 must stay matched to fold 0 for the ensemble to mean anything.

title: Resolution: 336 px for findings a few voxels wide, with a per-label prediction that makes it falsifiable
description:
MECHANISM THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY CLEAR 1.5%, now with PUBLISHED COUNTER-EVIDENCE recorded before the run.

THE ARM: 336 -> 448 px, everything else held. Cost is quadratic in bytes and step time; the cache is keyed by resolution so 336 px members stay reproducible. Needs --recompute-activations (gradient checkpointing) or it overflows 32 GB and thrashes.

THE ORIGINAL ARGUMENT: we read a 130 mm crop at 336 px, so a pixel is ~0.39 mm, while a meniscal tear or cruciate fibre discontinuity is millimetre-scale. Five of twelve targets are meniscus or ligament. Occlusion (knee-am4) shows centre-only 0.8021 against border-only 0.8006 and whole 0.8448, which is what a model leaning on coarse global context looks like.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE, found 2026-08-11 while reading prior art rather than after the result: MRNet (Stanford, PLOS Medicine 2018) detects ACL tears at AUC ~0.97 using AlexNet at 256 px - LOWER resolution than ours. If millimetre findings were unresolvable at 0.39 mm/pixel, that result should not exist. My 'we cannot resolve fine anatomy' argument is therefore weaker than I stated it.

WHAT SURVIVES THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE: MRNet's task is three coarse labels on one institution's curated dataset with radiologist labels. Ours is twelve labels across 16 sites and 12 languages with 98.7% LLM-derived labels. Harder supervision and more heterogeneity could plausibly raise the resolution requirement. But that is a story, and the counter-example is a measurement.

THE PREDICTION STANDS AND IS NOW SHARPER: the gain must CONCENTRATE in ACL, MCL, Medial and Lateral Meniscus and be near zero for Effusion and Baker's. Given MRNet, the most likely outcome is now NO concentrated gain - and that would be a clean refutation rather than a disappointment, because it redirects to what MRNet says actually carries the signal (see knee-jk3 and the whole-stack arm).

PRIORITY UNCHANGED at P0 but ORDER CHANGED: run whole-stack FIRST. It has published support and this arm now has published doubt.
notes:
2026-08-12 08:31Z — RESULT: 392 px peaks at 0.8523 against the 336 whole-stack control's 0.8457. +0.0066 on the mean, above the 0.0053 floor, single variable (same recipe, same fold, only the sampling grid moves). Best fold-0 number this project has produced, and it takes the running total against rank24_s2026 to +0.0251.

THE PER-LABEL PREDICTION IS NEITHER CONFIRMED NOR REFUTED, and that is a statement about the instrument rather than about resolution. The arm predicted a gain concentrated in MCL/ACL/menisci and near zero for Effusion and Baker's. Observed: MCL +0.0273 (fits) and Effusion +0.0025 (fits), but Baker's +0.0164 does not, and the two LARGEST movers are Fracture +0.0329 and Synovitis -0.0283 - the two noisiest labels in the corpus, carrying 62 and 116 holdout positives and 95% intervals of +/-0.061 and +/-0.045. Every per-label delta here sits inside its own error bar. Read the mean; the per-label table was never going to settle this (knee-70w).

CEILING REACHED. Patch-14 requires multiples of 14: 336 (576 tokens), 392 (784), 420 (900), 448 (1024). 392 holds 28.4 GB of 32 and 448 OOMs. The next rung needs a smaller batch, which moves the ranking term's within-batch pair count and stops this being one variable. So 392 is the shipping resolution unless the batch question is reopened deliberately.

title: Border-only scores 0.8006 of a 0.8448 model - the centre of the joint carries nothing privileged
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-11 by occlusion on base+ranking, 400 holdout studies (experiments/arms/attribution.sh):
  whole 0.8448 | centre-only 0.8021 | border-only 0.8006

The diagnostic's own docstring says border-only should be near chance. It is not. Keeping ONLY the outer region recovers 95% of the full score, and centre-only beats it by 0.0015 - inside noise. The centre of the joint carries nothing the periphery does not.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT YET PROVE. 'Border' here is the image minus the central 50%x50% square, which is 75% of the AREA and still contains a great deal of joint anatomy - the crop is 130 mm around the joint, so the central quarter-area is only the very middle. So the result is consistent with two very different worlds:
  (a) the signal is diffuse and redundant across the field - benign, and would predict that a model reading any large fraction of the knee does well;
  (b) the model is reading the periphery - coil, soft tissue, burned-in laterality marker or vendor text - which is a shortcut that would not survive a different scanner population.
The test as designed cannot separate them, and that is the defect worth fixing first.

WHY IT IS A P0 DESPITE BEING AMBIGUOUS: if (b) holds even partly, it caps generalisation to the hidden test set in a way no amount of encoder tuning addresses, and every gain measured this session was measured on a ruler that shares the artefact. It is also the only hypothesis on the board whose mechanism could plausibly be worth more than 1.5%.

THE SHARPER TESTS, cheapest first:
  1. A NARROW RING. Keep only the outer 10-15% of the field, which on a 130 mm crop is almost entirely outside the joint. If that alone still scores well above chance the answer is (b).
  2. LOOK AT THE PIXELS. Dump the border ring for a handful of studies and check for burned-in text or laterality markers - the DICOM tags will also say (BurnedInAnnotation, ImageComments).
  3. If (b): train with the ring blanked and see what the holdout does. A model that loses little is reading anatomy after all.

Cheap: no training, one occlusion pass each.
notes:
RESOLUTION 2026-08-13. All three of this bead's tests are now either done or shown to be unsound, and the answer is world (a).

  TEST 2, DONE, clean: BurnedInAnnotation and ImageComments are never populated across 60 studies. In the pixels over 400 studies the corners carry across-study std 52-57 against the interior's 53 - a FIXED marker would appear as sharp structure in the mean with LOW std, and the periphery instead varies per study, which is what anatomy does.
  TEST 1, UNSOUND AS DESIGNED: it assumes the outer 10-15% is 'almost entirely outside the joint'. Measured, that ring is 74-78% TISSUE and even the outer 5% is 69%. At a 130 mm crop around a knee about 100 mm wide there is NO reliably non-anatomical region, so the test cannot distinguish the two worlds - and running it would have produced a confident wrong answer.
  TEST 3, CONFOUNDED BY THE SAME FACT: 'train with the ring blanked' removes real anatomy, so a drop would not implicate a shortcut.

AND THE ARGUMENT THIS BEAD NEVER MADE: several of the twelve findings are ANATOMICALLY PERIPHERAL. A Baker's cyst is popliteal, at the image edge by construction; the collaterals sit at the medial and lateral margins; effusion collects in the suprapatellar pouch. 'Border-only recovers 95%' is exactly what the benign world predicts when a third of the label set lives at the border.

CLOSING RATHER THAN LEAVING A P0 OPEN ON A QUESTION THAT CANNOT BE ASKED AT THIS CROP. If a future member is ever fitted on a much wider field, the ring test becomes sound and this is worth reopening.
close_reason: World (a) - diffuse, redundant anatomical signal - is well supported, and (b) is not separable at a 130 mm crop: no region of the field is reliably non-anatomical (the outer 5% ring is still 69% tissue), so this bead's own decisive test cannot be run. No burned-in markers in headers or pixels, and a third of the twelve findings are anatomically peripheral by clinical definition.

title: Gate the reader work: what is the existing severity gradation actually worth?
description:
BEFORE investing in a better report reader that emits true ordinal severity, measure what the gradation we ALREADY have is worth. Cost-tiered: a cheap proxy gates the expensive commit.

THE ABLATION: report_labels_v2 carries three YES levels (0.68 / 0.82 / 0.94, 9,702 pairs). flatyes_v2.csv collapses all three to 0.82 - the middle level, so the average pull on a YES pair is unchanged - and changes NOTHING else. NO stays 0.08, UNK stays 0.28. The eval table is held fixed at the graded original so the ruler cannot move.

WHY THE RANKING TERM IS ON FOR THIS ARM: it is the only component that consumes the gradation (pair weight relu(s_i - s_j)); BCE mostly pulls both toward present and our local evaluation binarises at 0.5, collapsing the levels anyway. Running the ablation without ranking would test a channel nothing reads.

WHAT THE ANSWER BUYS:
  - If flattening COSTS materially: gradation is live signal, and a reader emitting true severity (grade 1/2/3, mild/moderate/severe) is worth building - the levels we have are a crude version of something that pays.
  - If flattening costs ~nothing: the three levels are assertion-strength the model cannot use, and a reader upgrade must supply genuinely NEW information (findings we do not extract at all) rather than finer grades. That would redirect the effort rather than cancel it.

EVIDENCE THAT MOTIVATED IT: a linear probe on the report embedding separates 0.94 from 0.68 at mean AUC 0.730 over 9,702 pairs (Effusion 0.845, ACL 0.813, Synovitis 0.576). So the levels are driven by report CONTENT, not by sampling noise. That says they are real; it does not say the IMAGE can see them, which is what this arm tests.
close_reason: GATE PASSED. Collapsing the three YES levels to one costs -0.0044 (0.8228 vs 0.8272) with ranking on and the eval table held graded. So the gradation we already have is signal the model can USE, not assertion-strength it ignores - which is the condition this issue set for investing in a reader that emits true ordinal severity. That work is knee-mxj, now unblocked by evidence rather than by assumption. Committed as experiments/arms/severity_flat.sh. Caveat kept: -0.0044 is under the 1.5% bar, so this licenses the effort, it does not promise the payoff.

title: Report-embedding supervision: we use 12 numbers where the report has hundreds of tokens
description:
THE BOTTLENECK, established today: the model is supervision-limited, not capacity-limited (large is +0.0021 over base and overfits by epoch 10). So the lever is more signal per study, and we are discarding most of what we have.

WHAT WE THROW AWAY: every study carries a full radiology report. We compress it to 12 graded numbers via an LLM label table and discard the rest - the anatomy named, the severity wording, the incidental findings, the negations, everything the twelve columns do not have a slot for. That is hundreds of tokens reduced to twelve.

THE METHOD (ConVIRT / GLoRIA / BioViL family, standard in medical imaging): embed each report with a multilingual text encoder ONCE, offline. Add an auxiliary head that predicts that embedding from the study representation, and train it jointly with the twelve-label loss. The image model is then supervised by the report's full content rather than by twelve extractions of it.

WHY IT IS LEGAL AND WHY IT FITS: test.csv has NO Report column, and this is exactly the setting the method assumes - text supervises at training time, inference is image-only. No external data, no licence question (knee-0s6 untouched).

WHY IT COULD BE WORTH PERCENT rather than a knob: it changes the AMOUNT of supervision, which is the constraint we just measured, rather than the capacity to absorb it, which we just measured as spent. It is also the one axis where our multilingual corpus is an ASSET instead of a liability - a multilingual encoder maps 'menisco medial roto' and 'medial meniscal tear' to nearby vectors, where our label reader has to parse both.

CHEAP FIRST TEST: multilingual sentence encoder -> per-report vector -> reduce to ~64 dims -> auxiliary cosine/MSE head at modest weight -> one small@24 arm against the 0.8272 ranking control. If the auxiliary loss trains at all and the number does not move, the idea is cheap to kill; if it moves, it scales to base and to the full-data fit.

RISK, stated: a multilingual encoder trained on general web text may embed radiology reports poorly, and 4,407 reports is a small target space. The failure mode is a useless auxiliary target that costs capacity - which is checkable by watching whether the auxiliary loss falls at all.
close_reason: REFUTED, and monotonically - which is what makes it a kill rather than a tuning miss. Report term at 0.3 = 0.8219, at 1.0 = 0.8209, control 0.8272. Both negative and MORE weight is MORE negative, so the weight is not the problem: forcing the slot embedding to predict a sentence-transformer embedding of the report actively costs the classifier. Mechanism: the report describes the whole study including everything the twelve labels already capture PLUS technique, history and incidental findings, so the auxiliary target pulls representation capacity toward text the metric never scores. The 12 numbers being fewer than the report's tokens was true and irrelevant. Encoder + report_embeddings.py + report_supervision.py stay in the tree, opt-in and default off.

title: Encoder learning rate: the axis the depth bracket could not see
description:
BACKBONE_LR = 8e-6 was a module constant with no CLI flag, so no run has ever varied it. The head:encoder ratio is 125:1.

WHY THIS INVALIDATES A RESULT I ALREADY REPORTED: the depth bracket (unfreeze 3 / 6 / 12) came out 0.8143 / 0.8205 / 0.8213. I read the 12-block arm as 'depth is a ceiling at 6'. But at 8e-6 the extra blocks barely move, so a null result cannot distinguish 'more trainable blocks do not help' from 'no block was going to move anyway'. The bracket measured adaptation capacity at a rate where adaptation does not happen.

Note the shallow arm still fell -0.0062, which says the rate is not so low that depth is irrelevant - only that the UPPER half of the bracket is uninformative.

MECHANISM FOR WHY THIS COULD BE WORTH PERCENT rather than a knob: DINOv2's features are natural-image features, and kneemri/trainer.py's own docstring says a frozen SSL encoder caps every downstream axis at once because nothing in natural images resembles a torn meniscus on a PD sequence. How far the encoder is allowed to move off those features is therefore the representation-capacity axis - and capacity is the only axis that has ever paid here.

ARMS (/tmp/chain15.sh), small + ranking @24, unfreeze 12, control rank24_s2026 = 0.8272:
  L: backbone 4e-5 (5x)
  M: backbone 1.6e-4 (20x)
Bracketed wide because the scale is unknown. Small rather than base because this is a signal test.

IF IT MOVES: re-run the depth bracket at the winning rate, since that result is currently uninterpretable, then take it to base. IF IT DOES NOT: the encoder is genuinely near its useful optimum under this supervision, and the next step up is domain-adaptive PRETRAINING on our own 24,371 series rather than a bigger fine-tuning rate.
close_reason: DUPLICATE, merged into knee-3om which holds the measurement: 8e-6 -> 0.8272, 4e-5 -> 0.8316 (+0.0044), 1.6e-4 -> ~0.739 collapsing. The 'IF IT MOVES' clause fired, and the re-run of the depth bracket at the winning rate is arm S/T, tracked in knee-3om. Nothing distinct left here.

title: Our ruler is a proxy: 58 annotated studies, so only the LB can arbitrate
description:
MEASURED: train.csv carries the twelve annotations for exactly 58 studies, all-or-nothing - 696 of 52,884 (study,label) cells, 1.32%. No partial annotations exist to scavenge.

So every local number in this project (0.8081 ... 0.8283) is agreement with LLM-READ REPORT LABELS, while the competition scores agreement with RADIOLOGIST ANNOTATIONS. We select epochs, members and recipes on a proxy.

NOT FIXABLE LOCALLY: the 58 are trained on at ANNOTATED_WEIGHT=3.0, so scoring them is scoring training data; held out, fold 0 gets ~12 of them with 2-7 positives per label, which is the Hanley-McNeil +/-0.17 regime knee-6xm already computed.

THE PROXY APPEARS TO COMPRESS ~2x. Two ledger rows carry both numbers: local 0.8162 -> LB 0.868, and local 0.8269 -> LB 0.888. +0.0107 local became +0.020 on the leaderboard. If that holds, the owner's 1.5% bar applied to the LB is about +0.008 locally - which would REINSTATE base (+0.0085) and put ranking (+0.0067) on the edge.

LIMITS, stated: two points, and the second row changed three things at once (augmentation fix + OneCycle + overlap TTA). Not a law. Enough to justify spending a submission to find out; not enough to re-score the ledger by.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SPENDING: 5 submissions/day, kernel pushes unlimited. The local number decides WHICH recipe to submit; only the LB decides whether it is better. Our best recipe (base + ranking, 0.8283) has never been on the LB - the 0.888 there is the old 5-fold ensemble.
notes:
SHARPENED 2026-08-16 18:30 UTC by `python -m kneemri.evaluation.board_transfer`, which is the board half of the question `ruler_transfer` says it cannot reach. Full write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-16_board_transfer.md. Machine-readable record: comp/board.jsonl.

  5 entries on the ensemble scope, 9 orderable pairs (excluded: 2 member_mean, 2 unknown)
  compression: median +4.67 board points per holdout point
  inversions: 2/9 pairs, but 0/5 of the pairs the holdout RESOLVES (a gap >= its own 0.0053 floor)

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD.

1. "The proxy appears to compress ~2x" understates it. The five resolved pairs convert at 1.2, 2.4, 4.7, 5.3 and 8.1. The bead's own arithmetic - "the 1.5% bar on the LB is about +0.008 locally" - becomes about +0.003 locally at the median ratio, which is BELOW the holdout's noise floor. The honest statement is that the ruler's resolution floor and the competition's result bar are about the SAME line: anything the holdout can resolve is worth a submission.

2. My own note of twelve minutes ago read the onedecode pair as the holdout UNDER-PRICING diversity. That is the compression, not a ranking failure. The holdout has not mis-ordered a single pair it can resolve. It ranks correctly and quietly.

LIMITS, stated: five entries, and four of the five resolved pairs share solo_v1 as one endpoint. The pairs are not matched - six days, and the kit changed underneath them. Only the two 17:45 entries are same-day, and their ratio is 2.37. Two further entries are excluded because the ledger never recorded which scope their number was on (knee-fvi0).
2026-08-20: a SECOND offline ruler now exists to compare against the LB, and on the seat experiment's four board points it beats the binary one. ordinal_signal (severity concordance over 334,942 cross-level pairs, no card, no labels file) orders the three seat challengers calib_span 0.759 > depth_regions_narrow 0.743 > band_span 0.736, which is the board order exactly (0.929/0.928/0.927). The binary ruler read alone orders them exactly backwards, and read in the seat gets the top right and inverts the middle. The by-construction confound is weakened by a direct instance: calibrated_targets carries the same flag and scores mid-pack at 0.739. THIS IS A LEAD, NOT A FINDING - three items is 1-in-6 by chance, and the three board entries differ by 0.001-0.002, which may be inside the hidden test's own resolution, in which case what was reproduced is its noise. Forward test pre-registered in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_the-ordinal-ruler-orders-the-seat-the-binary-one-inverted.md: the next single-member seat swap is chosen where the rulers disagree, by the ordinal one.
2026-08-20, THE PRE-REGISTERED ORDINAL FORWARD TEST IS NOT EXECUTABLE ON THIS POOL, and the reason is worth more than the test. The 2026-08-20 interpretation pre-registered: choose the next single-member seat swap where the binary and ordinal rulers DISAGREE, and choose by the ordinal one.

With the swap ruler built (knee-yu3e) both rulers can finally be read on the same quantity — the best seat against calibspan_v1 — and they AGREE at the top. attend_dense is first on the binary swap ruler (+0.0010) and first on ordinal (0.751/0.774 over 48 members). Below it the two do cross: focal_dense is 2nd-3rd ordinal (0.746) and 4th on swap (+0.0003), depth_regions_narrow is 2nd on swap (+0.0007) and 7th ordinal (0.743). But those crossings separate candidates by 0.003 ordinal and 0.0004 binary, and the four-occupant board points they would be tested against differ by 0.001-0.002. The test would be reading a disagreement smaller than either ruler resolves.

So the pre-registration stands UNRUN rather than refuted, and it is recorded here so it cannot be quietly dropped. It becomes executable when the pool contains two candidates the two rulers separate by a margin each of them can actually see — which is a reason to want a member from a genuinely different family, not another decode-family knob.

FORWARD TEST FIRED 2026-08-22 08:07 UTC — kneemri-gradeswap, kernel v1, slot 2 of 5 (3 remaining).

This bead recorded the pre-registration from 2026-08-20 as UNRUN rather than refuted, because no pair in
the pool was separated by a margin either ruler could resolve. The 23-member ordinal scan closed that:
grade_ladder reads 0.750 / 0.780 against depth_regions_narrow's 0.743 / 0.769 — +0.007 over labels and
+0.011 over pairs, against a seat experiment whose resolvable spread was 0.007 to 0.016. The margin is
finally inside the ruler.

The disagreement the pre-registration required is present and it is total. The binary seat-value ruler
puts grade_ladder's best seat elsewhere (lr4e-5_ws at +0.0004, or +0.0001 as a plain eighth) — both a
quarter of the 0.0015 BOARD_RESOLVABLE threshold, so it cannot resolve this question at all and points
away with what little it has. The residual-distance ruler actively predicts the entry LOSES: correcting
nearest-neighbour correlation for solo score (pearson 0.890, n = 23), grade_ladder is +0.0187, the most
redundant member of all 23 for its strength.

Read due ~15:45 UTC — the kernel projected 7.7 h over the hidden set, so this does not resolve today
early. Bands are the kernel docstring's, unchanged: above 0.932 confirms the ordinal ruler and licenses
re-ranking every seat by it; 0.932 is a tie; below 0.932 refutes the forward test on its first honest
trial and leaves residual-distance standing.

WHAT IT WILL NOT SETTLE. This is one trial, and one trial cannot separate "the ordinal ruler transfers"
from "grade_ladder is a good member". A pass licenses re-ranking; it does not prove the ruler. The
2026-08-20 ordering that started this was a 1-in-6 arrangement by its own interpretation's admission, and
a second pass would still be 1-in-36 rather than a proof. Whatever it reads, the next use of the ordinal
ruler is a re-test, not an assumption.
RESOLVED 2026-08-22 09:34 UTC: gradeswap scored 0.933, above the pre-registered 0.932 band. PASS. The ordinal ruler called the depth_regions_narrow -> grade_ladder displacement correctly; binary seat value was blind (+0.0001, a fifteenth of its own resolution); residual distance predicted an outright loss and was wrong. Re-ranking seats by ordinal concordance is licensed. Caveat stands as written: one trial cannot separate 'the ruler transfers' from 'grade_ladder is a good member' — the next use is a re-test, not an assumption. Second consequence: the +4.67 board-points-per-holdout-point compression recorded on this bead is now load-bearing, because a +0.0001 offline seat produced a +0.001 board tick. Any offline seat number compared against a board threshold without that multiplier is wrong; two documents were corrected for exactly that error today.
2026-08-24, THE ORDINAL FORWARD TEST IS EXECUTABLE AGAIN, and not for the reason this bead predicted. The 2026-08-20 note said the pre-registration becomes runnable 'when the pool contains two candidates the two rulers separate by a margin each of them can actually see - which is a reason to want a member from a genuinely different family'. That member now exists (vjepa_warm_s2026, V-JEPA2-large tubelet, the only non-2D encoder in the roster). Ran ordinal_signal over all 87 records on disk, card-free, ~10 s:

  aug_long_s2026      pairs 0.767  labels 0.738
  vjepa_warm_s2026    pairs 0.766  labels 0.743
  (top of the pool for scale: calib_span 0.791, small_accum 0.784, severity_weight 0.783)

So the DIFFERENT-FAMILY member did NOT open a gap on the ordinal ruler either - 0.001 on pairs, and the sign flips to +0.005 for vjepa_warm on the per-label variant. Both mid-pack. That retires the specific hope recorded on 2026-08-20, that family distance would be what finally separates the two rulers.

But it produces the disagreement anyway, in MAGNITUDE rather than in order. The BINARY ruler separates these two members by 0.0174 solo (aug_long 0.8511, vjepa_warm 0.8337) - nearly three times its own 0.0062 floor, a gap it is certain about. The ORDINAL ruler reads them level. And the board is about to test exactly this pair in exactly the same seat: kneemri-augseat (aug_long in seat 7) is scoring now, and comp/kernels/kneemri-farseat (vjepa_warm in the SAME seat, everything else byte-identical) is written and gated behind it.

PRE-REGISTRATION, before either number: if augseat and farseat land within 0.002 of each other, the ordinal ruler was right and the binary ruler's 0.0174 solo gap does not survive into a seat - which is a statement about SOLO SCORE being the wrong ruler for a seat, not about either member. If they separate by 0.005 or more IN THE BINARY RULER'S DIRECTION, the binary ruler is right about seats too and ordinal_signal stops being a candidate ruler for member selection. If they separate in the OPPOSITE direction the ordinal ruler beats it on a pair it called a tie, which is weaker evidence than it looks and should be read as scatter until a second pair repeats it.

COST: zero card. It is the second slot, and it only fires if augseat's own gate opens (>= 0.940) - so on the branch where farseat is not submitted, this test stays unrun and this note records why.

title: Slice coverage: we discard a third of the band we chose to read
description:
MEASURED, 642 series across 120 studies sampled from the real corpus: slices per series median 30 (p25 25, p75 33, p95 40, max 320). The 0.20-0.80 band we read therefore holds ~18 slices on the median study, and we cache 12 of them.

So we keep 67% of the band on the median study, and 89% of series have MORE than 12 slices inside it. A third of the evidence we already decided was worth reading is being dropped before the model sees anything.

WHY THIS AND NOT ANOTHER KNOB (the 1.5% bar): a meniscal tear is visible on 2-3 slices, and five of the twelve targets are meniscus/ligament. Dropping a third of the band is a real chance of never showing the model the slices the finding lives on - that is a mechanism that can plausibly move percent, unlike a loss tweak.

COST is on the cheap axis by the cache's own docstring: bytes grow LINEARLY with slices and with the SQUARE of resolution. 20 slices = 59.7 GB against 1.2 TB free, and the filename carries the slice count so the 12-slice cache is untouched and every existing member stays reproducible.

Building now (--slices 20 --workers 12). Arm to follow: base + ranking @24 on 20 slices vs the same recipe on 12 (0.8283).

WATCH: inference averages over MORE windows with 20 slices, so the efficiency kernel's runtime goes up. That is the accuracy entry's problem, not the efficiency entry's - they are separate submissions.
notes: REOPENED AS A CAVEAT, not as a reversal (2026-08-19). band_dense (0.10-0.90 at 20 slices) vs band_wide (same band, 16 slices) is the same density comparison this bead priced flat, and its MEAN behaves the same way — but the per-label composition does not. Against band_wide: Medial OA +0.0122 [+0.0004,+0.0239], PF OA +0.0194 [+0.0043,+0.0355], Synovitis +0.0135, against MCL -0.0111, ACL -0.0037, Contusion -0.0052, Fracture -0.0052. Trades of that size summing to nearly nothing on the mean. This bead's -0.0001 stands as a statement about the MEAN and must not be cited as 'density inside the band changes nothing' — it was, three times. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-19_density-inside-the-band-trades-centre-for-edge.md.
close_reason: REFUTED CLEANLY, and the excuse for the first failure was wrong too. Arm Q (12 slices, max pooling) 0.8310 vs arm R (20 slices, max pooling) 0.8309 = -0.0001. Max pooling makes a group's physical thickness independent of the slice count, so this is the deconfounded test the earlier -0.0016 could not be. The thickness story - 'more slices failed because each group spans less tissue' - predicted that 20 slices would WIN once thickness was held constant. It did not. More slices inside the band buy nothing; the third of the band we discard was not carrying the findings. The 20-slice cache stays on disk (59.7 GB) and every 12-slice member remains reproducible.

title: Ranking term: optimise the ordering the metric reads, not the calibration it discards
description:
CONFIRMED DIRECTIONALLY, NOT A RESULT. Seed 2026: 0.8272 vs 0.8205 (+0.0067). Seed 7: 0.8284 vs 0.8248 (+0.0036). On base: 0.8283 vs 0.8255 (+0.0028). Three arms, all positive.

RE-SCORED against the owner's bar (1-2% absolute, ~1.5% working, stated 2026-08-11): +0.005 is NOISE, not a finding. My earlier framing - 'the first change other than capacity to clear the noise floor' - judged it against the 0.0062 seed spread, which measures DETECTABILITY and not worth. Withdrawn.

KEPT IN THE RECIPE anyway, on cost rather than on effect: the term is free at inference, it is the exact quantity the metric scores (per-label pairwise order), and it is positive in 3/3 matched arms. It does NOT earn further seeds or a weight sweep.

Best recipe so far: base + ranking, 24 epochs = 0.8283, which is +0.0202 on the original small@8 baseline of 0.8081. The CUMULATIVE number clears the bar; no single step in it does.
close_reason: Implemented (objective.py RankedObjective), measured on 3 matched arms, all positive, all sub-bar. Kept in the recipe on cost (free at inference, exactly the quantity the metric scores) rather than on effect - and the bead itself says it earns no further seeds and no weight sweep. Nothing actionable remains.

title: Measure EMA: is the 0.0062 seed spread a variance problem we can damp?
description:
EMA is now wired (--ema). Queued as /tmp/chain6.sh behind chain5: two arms, small@24, one-cycle, weight-floor, report_labels_v2, fold 0, seeds 2026 and 7.

Controls already on the ruler: seed 2026 = 0.8205; seed 7 = chain3 arm 3, running now.

Two seeds and not one ON PURPOSE, which is not a violation of stage-gated rigor: the claim EMA makes IS about run-to-run variance, and a single seed cannot show a variance reduction at all. The mean moving is the secondary read; the spread narrowing is the hypothesis.
close_reason:
Measured, matched, two seeds: +0.0012 (s2026) and +0.0007 (s7). Same sign twice, mean +0.0010, far inside the 0.0062 noise floor - not a lever.

No convergence gain either, and the claim that there was one is withdrawn: time to within 0.001 of each arm's own best is EMA 12 vs control 13 epochs. The apparent 2x speedup came from comparing two noisy curves at one arbitrary epoch.

No variance claim possible at n=2 (control spread 0.0043, EMA 0.0038).

KEPT for the final full-data fit regardless, on an argument the fold-0 number cannot address: --fold -1 has no holdout and keeps its LAST epoch by construction, so the shipped artefact depends on where training stopped, and the curve wanders 0.004 between epochs 13 and 24. That is variance in the deliverable, not in a fold score.

title: A missing binary reads as a passing gate: 'cmd; echo EXIT $?' reports the echo
description:
PREMISE WAS WRONG, corrected 2026-08-11. The original claim - 'nox -s gates is weaker than pre-commit' - was false. gates calls lint, which runs hygiene.mirror; the two agree.

THE REAL CAUSE: nox is not on PATH in this Git-bash (only uv/uvx, at /c/Users/User/.local/bin), and it is not a project dependency either, so 'uv run nox' fails too. The working entry is 'uvx nox -s gates'.

WHY IT LOOKED GREEN: the command was 'nox -s gates > log 2>&1; echo "GATES EXIT $?"'. A compound statement's status is the LAST command's - the echo - which always succeeds, so the harness reported exit 0. The log held one line, 'nox: command not found', and I did not read it because the wrapper said 0. Reported the gates green twice on that basis.

SAME ROOT AS knee-74x, now twice in one session (pkill, nox): a command that does not exist fails in a way that reads as success inside a compound statement.

THE RULE: never infer success from a wrapper's exit code. Grep the LOG for the tool's own success marker ('Session gates was successful'), and prefer '&&' over ';' so a missing binary short-circuits.

Nothing was verified by those runs. The commits they blessed were separately checked by the pre-commit hook set, which does run and did block once - so the tree is fine; the reporting was not.
close_reason: Rule landed in CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md: uvx nox, verify by the tool's own success marker, '&&' not ';'. Nothing further to build; the postmortem is the deliverable.

title: Ship a single full-data fit, not a fold ensemble
description: REORDERED 2026-08-11: the full-data fit is a DELIVERABLE, not a finding. Running it before the EMA and ranking arms would spend ~40 GPU-min on a member we would re-fit if either wins. chain5 killed while still waiting; the fit runs last, with whatever recipe survives chain7.
notes:
LANDED 2026-08-16 08:10 UTC. final_ws_e12.pt — 12 epochs, --fold -1, all 4,407 studies (vs 3,498 for wsfold0_e6, +26% training data), same recipe otherwise: whole_stack, slice_pooling max, rank_weight 1.0, crop 130mm image-centred, train_size 392, 12 slices. Checkpoint verified: fingerprint present, holdout NaN (correct — it held nothing back), witness empty (correct — nothing to witness), epoch 11 kept, which is the last, as ranking-by-epoch-index intends for a final fit.

IT CANNOT BE SCORED LOCALLY, BY CONSTRUCTION. There is no holdout, so there is no honest local number for it and none should be invented — its only measurement is the board. That also means it cannot be compared against wsfold0_e6 on the ruler this project uses for every other arm; the case for it is the training-data delta and nothing else. Loss fell to 0.577 at epoch 11 and was still falling, so 12 epochs is not obviously the right budget either.

Note the epoch-index-in-the-auc-column defect (knee-97fa) was found ON this run's metrics file and is fixed at the reader.
OVERWRITTEN 2026-08-23 12:23 UTC. `experiments/arms/final_fit.sh` writes $PROCESSED/final_ws_e${EPOCHS}.pt with EPOCHS=12, which is the SAME filename this bead's 2026-08-16 checkpoint used, so the new fit replaced it on disk. Checked before writing this: no shipped kernel and no roster line named final_ws_e12 before today, so no board result lost a rebuildable path. What was lost is the 392 px / 12 slices / 130 mm-crop variant itself — an asset with no offline number by construction and no board reading either, so its loss is unmeasurable rather than free. DEFECT NAMED: the arm's output name is derived from EPOCHS alone and carries nothing about geometry, so any future re-fit at a different recipe silently collides again. `final_fit_six.sh` already avoids this with an explicit _ff suffix; `final_fit.sh` does not.
CLOSING 2026-08-23. The deliverable landed and SCORED: final_ws_e12 is seat 1 of kneemri-finalfit, submission 55715039, board 0.934 - the first board movement in five entries and the first to change what is IN the pool rather than which of it was seated. It is pinned in comp/champion.json and champion_check confirms the entry is still rebuildable.

The naming defect this bead named on 2026-08-23 12:23 is COVERED, not outstanding: experiments/lib.sh:422 refuses a run_train whose --out already holds a checkpoint unless ALLOW_OVERWRITE=1. The output name still carries no geometry, which is the deeper defect, but the guard converts a silent overwrite into a refusal that forces the choice - which is the behaviour wanted. Renaming was considered and REJECTED: champion.json and the roster both name final_ws_e12, and renaming it would break the rebuildable path of a scored 0.934 entry to fix a collision that is already blocked.

What this bead does NOT settle: 12 epochs is still not measured as the right budget for a --fold -1 fit (loss was still falling at epoch 11), and by construction it cannot be measured locally. See knee-krnd for the data-volume slope and the champion principle 'A MEMBER FITTED AT --fold -1 IS UNSCOREABLE FOREVER'.

title: Epoch budget also clears the noise floor: 8 -> 24 epochs is +0.0068 on small
description: CONFIRMED, final: 24-epoch small 0.8205 vs 8-epoch 0.8081 = +0.0124, twice the noise floor. Curve peaked around epoch 18-21 then flattened (0.8187-0.8189 at 22-23), so ~20-24 epochs is roughly the right budget for small at this data size. Larger than the encoder change (+0.0085), and a 24-epoch SMALL model beats an 8-epoch BASE one (0.8166). CONSEQUENCE: every arm in the ablation ledger was run at 8 epochs against a baseline that had not converged, so 'no measured effect' there means 'measured in the wrong regime'. The five leaderboard members are 8-epoch; retraining the same recipe at ~24 is worth about +0.012 before anything else changes.
close_reason: CONFIRMED and applied: 24 epochs is in every arm since. Ledger consequence recorded (the 8-epoch table was measured pre-convergence) and carried by knee-ghl. The question this bead asked is answered.

title: DINOv2-base clears the noise floor: +0.0085, needs seeds and more epochs
description: FINAL fold-0 ladder on report_labels_v2, all matched, floor 0.0062: small 8ep 0.8081, base 8ep 0.8166 (+0.0085), small 24ep 0.8205 (+0.0124), base 20ep 0.8255 (+0.0174). The two capacity levers ADD rather than substitute. Submission recipe: base, 20 epochs, batch 12. Five-fold retrain queued behind the label test; base submission path already dry-run verified on the host (variant resolves, mount matches, fingerprint passes). Leaderboard members are small-at-8-epochs, so this is the first change since the augmentation bug expected to move the public number.
close_reason: Answered: final matched ladder recorded, base+24ep is the recipe and has been the base of every arm since. The five-fold retrain it asked for has run. Any further capacity question is knee-7u5/knee-f0a, not this.

title: Per-slice encoding with max pooling, and a CNN backbone — the only untested difference of the right size
description:
EVERY KNOB IS EXHAUSTED AND THEY ARE ALL THE SAME SIZE. Measured on this architecture: schedule +0.0061, augmentation-applied +0.0110, TTA +0.0035, intensity augmentation +0.0019, weight floor +0.0019, better labels -0.0008, 32 slices -0.018. Apart from the three defects, nothing is worth more than 0.002.

THE REMAINING GAPS ARE AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE BIGGER: our per-member holdout 0.8269 against the .903 reference's reported OOF 0.8544, and 0.888 against the leader's 0.942. Nothing measured explains either.

THE .903 RECIPE DIFFERS STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY SETTINGS:
  backbone     single-channel ImageNet EfficientNet-B3   (ours: DINOv2-small ViT, 3-channel)
  study input  3 fluid-sensitive plane-diverse series    (ours: 6 plane x weighting slots)
  pooling      MAX over slice embeddings, then MEAN over series logits
               (ours: 3 consecutive slices stacked as CHANNELS, then per-diagnosis attention over slots)

THE POOLING DIFFERENCE IS THE ONE WITH A MECHANISM WE HAVE ALREADY FELT. Our channel stacking is what made 32 inference slices FAIL (-0.018): raising the slice count over a fixed band changes each group's physical thickness, so the model sees an input distribution it never trained on. Per-slice encoding has no such coupling — which is exactly why THEY can raise slices at inference and we cannot. The same coupling plausibly limits what a fixed 12-slice budget can see: a finding is either inside a sampled 3-slice group or invisible.

WHY IT IS NOW AFFORDABLE: `StudyModel` already takes its backbone as an injected `nn.Module` (structural, not a named protocol — written that way for exactly this), and timm 1.0.26 is in Kaggle's image, so an EfficientNet needs no wheel. What has to change is the bag layout and `_pool`.

SCOPE, and it is genuinely two experiments that should not be confused:
  1. AGGREGATION: keep DINOv2, encode each slice independently, max over slices. Isolates pooling.
  2. BACKBONE: keep the aggregation, swap the encoder. Isolates the encoder family.
Run 1 first — it is the one with a mechanism we have already observed, and it does not need a new model mount.

CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE FORGOTTEN: at ~0.002 per knob and an unmeasured noise floor, a single fold cannot resolve a small win here either. This is worth doing only because the hypothesised effect is 0.02-0.03, not 0.002 — if it lands in the noise, it is a refutation, not a tuning opportunity.
close_reason: REFUTED at the predicted size: per-slice max +0.0018 vs 0.0012 noise floor, for 3x encoder cost, on a matched pair (0.8099 vs 0.8081). The mechanism was also wrong - 32-slice inference costs the same -0.01 under BOTH poolings, so channel-stacking's thickness coupling was not why the wide read hurt. Backbone swap (experiment 2) not run: experiment 1 was the one with an observed mechanism and it did not survive.

title: We train on the second-worst public label table; a better one is free
description:
MEASURED ON THE 58 GOLD STUDIES (2026-08-11), mean per-finding AUC of each public reader against the expert annotations:

  pilkwang/rsna-knee-llm-labels      0.8705   <- WHAT WE TRAIN ON
  stevenleehans llm_labels_v2        0.8905
  stevenleehans llm_labels_v4_blend  0.8982   <- +0.028, free, already public
  lixin73 report_labels_gpt56sol     0.8431

Per finding the gaps are much larger than the mean suggests: Synovitis 0.695 (pilkwang) against 0.805, Contusion 0.756 against 0.862, Lateral Meniscus 0.844 against 0.886. Those are three of our four weakest labels on the holdout, and each costs a full 1/12 of the competition metric.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE NUMBER: the .903 notebook states plainly that 'the image model is downstream of label quality'. We have been tuning the model (schedule, augmentation, TTA) against labels that are 0.028 worse than the best freely available ones, so every one of those measurements was made against a handicapped target.

FUSION IS REFUTED FOR OUR READERS, which is worth recording because the .903 system's headline mechanism is fusion:
  mean of all four        0.8938
  rank-mean of all four   0.8966
  rank-mean of top three  0.8952
  best single (steven_v4) 0.8982   <- still the winner
Averaging drags the best table toward the weaker ones, and v4_blend is ALREADY a blend, so there is little independent signal left to add. Their fusion presumably worked because their private Qwen reader was independent of pilkwang's; ours are not.

DO NOT hand-pick a per-finding winner. The oracle that does scores 0.9016, but it is chosen on the same 57 studies it is scored on, and at these counts a per-finding AUC carries roughly +/-0.09. That is the same trap the annotation check sets (identical members scoring 0.7356 to 0.9164 on it).

ACTION: retrain on steven_v4_blend and re-measure. Every recipe result so far (schedule +0.0061, augmentation +0.011) should be re-confirmed against the better labels, because a gain measured against noisier targets can shrink or grow when the targets improve.
notes:
SWAP NEEDS NO CODE (2026-08-11). `Targets.load` already handles the better table unchanged:

  report_labels_v2 (ours)   7 distinct target values, 12 __conf columns, mean weight 0.692
  llm_labels_v4_blend       186 distinct target values, NO __conf columns, mean weight 1.026
