Options dump of the greedy-optimal seven shows five carry calibrated_targets=True and a sixth a derived table, so the crossing is already banked in the champion; margin_seat_s2026 is the only plain seat and therefore the only place the delta is unpaid. Consequence: the distill_pairs/raptor_distill refits approved in steer 7 item 2 buy a crossing five seats already have.
notes: DOWNGRADED 2026-09-06 07:20Z. The +0.017 gold-58 crossing is a LEVEL statement only, NOT an ordering one. Two independent catches: kimi (07:12Z letter) and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_the-gold-ruler-raises-everyone-and-orders-no-one.md, which already measured Spearman 0.14 between report-909 and gold-58 ranks over six holdannot members and showed the statistic is a DENOMINATOR artefact - the whole gold spread best-to-worst is 0.022, narrower than the half-width of every paired interval on that page. 58 studies cannot resolve the 0.002-0.010 differences selection turns on, and adding members does not cure a study count. So: +0.017 of level, ordering unpriced. Selection cannot move to the gold ruler and no retrain fixes it.

title: Price every remaining route against one denominator before it takes card time
description:
The gap to first place is +0.0117 offline and NO single route reaches it. Measured, not argued: seat_requirement closed selection over 206 members; the member axis has seven board flats; and column_lift caps the weak-column route at +0.0041 achievable (+0.0074 at a degenerate oracle). So first place has to come from two or three routes SUMMING, which is the project's own standing rule about sub-bar increments against the ORIGINAL baseline.

What is missing is a common denominator. Each candidate route must be priced in ENSEMBLE POINTS against the greedy-optimal seven at 0.8764, the same way column_lift prices the column route, BEFORE it takes card time.

1. LABEL DENOISING / confident learning on the consensus-graded panel - what does the offline score do if the noisiest label-study pairs are dropped from the ruler? Zero card, data already on disk. OPEN, and now the cheapest thing on this list.

2. TIE STRUCTURE / prediction granularity - CLOSED 2026-09-06, zero card. SharpenedRank(k) bends each member's ranks through a logistic before averaging; the flat rule is its k->0 limit so there is no null to fit. Monotone NEGATIVE at both pool sizes: over 109 members -0.0001 / -0.0002 / -0.0009 / -0.0038 at k = 2/4/8/16, and over the greedy seven -0.0001 / -0.0003 / -0.0010 / -0.0024. Mechanism: binarising a column pays only when the column is RIGHT - the oracle case in column_lift - and a 0.83 column loses the within-class ordering that is the only thing separating it from a coin. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_the-two-column-route-has-a-measured-ceiling.md, addendum.

3. VOTE RULE - STRICKEN, it was never open. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_every-no-card-axis-is-priced-and-flat.md lines 22-24 record it BOARD-measured twice: efficient_v4 0.919 -> vote_v2 0.919 flat, and dark6_v1 0.937 -> votefit_v1 0.938 flat. That same document also records that a P1 was already filed once claiming this axis had never been measured. This is the second time; the fix is the standing rule - read the ledger and the interpretations before filing. The only live residue is a correctness bug, not a score route: Vote.ranks still uses ordinal ranks where area_under_curve was fixed to midranks.

4. TEST-TIME / scanner-shift adaptation - card, unpriced. Note the scanner axis was already found to exist in the data and NOT in the member ordering (commit e3f69d19), which lowers the prior.

5. INPUT AXIS (field of view, laterality, medial-edge crop) - card, and now the only axis the frontier reading leaves open that has not been priced flat or capped.

DONE means: each route has a number in ensemble points and an interpretation, and the card queue is ordered by that number rather than by what was built most recently. Two of five are now closed for zero card, which is what this bead was for.

PRICE: zero card for route 1, which is why it goes first. P(clears 1.5% alone) ~ 0.05 for any one route; P(the remaining three account for the +0.0117) ~ 0.3, down from 0.4 because the two cheapest came back negative.

title: A member that leans toward MCL and Lateral OA — reweight or widen, never narrow
description:
pool_ceiling's per-column reading (interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_two-columns-carry-three-quarters-of-the-gap.md): MCL 0.8283 and Lateral OA 0.8369 against a pool mean of 0.8765, both deficits larger than their own bootstrap bands, together worth +0.0073 of the +0.0097 gap to first place. And no member leans that way: above a 0.80 quality floor the BEST-shaped of 188 members is still -0.0281 on those two columns against its own mean.

DESIGN IS CONSTRAINED BY A PRIOR FAILURE. focus_mcl used --focus-label MCL, regressed its own target label by -0.0576 paired, and collapsed to a 0.5332 twelve-column mean. Narrowing the objective destroyed the shared structure. So: keep all twelve labels.

TWO CANDIDATES, price both before either takes the card:
(a) REWEIGHT - twelve-label supervision with extra weight on MCL and Lateral OA. Cheap to smoke, but it is a knob.
(b) WIDEN THE FIELD OF VIEW - both columns are peripheral (MCL at the medial edge, Lateral OA compartment-specific) while every member reads a centre-weighted crop and a fixed slice budget chosen on the twelve-column mean. An input axis, which is the only axis the frontier reading left open.

Mechanism favours (b); cost favours (a). Read the ledger for existing crop/FOV arms before writing either.

PRICE: 1.25 h of card, zero slots. Control is margin_seat itself, same fold, already on disk, so no
matched control run is queued and the cost is one arm and nothing else.
P(clears 1.5% absolute on the solo twelve-column mean) ~ 0.02 - and a solo win is NOT what is bought.
P(MCL and Lateral OA rise measurably in the per-label read) ~ 0.35 - the keep/kill this arm exists for.
P(the member earns a seat over the greedy-optimal seven, +0.0117) ~ 0.15.
Expected value is the KEEP/KILL on the loss-reweighting half of the two routes the interpretation left
open: a null closes (a) and sends the next arm to (b), the input axis, with the cheap half already ruled
out rather than merely untried.
notes: RE-PRICED 2026-09-06 05:12Z by column_lift, measured not guessed. A synthetic member reading MCL and Lateral OA PERFECTLY, otherwise the seated blend itself, adds +0.0074 (degenerate, tied binary column) / +0.0041 (achievable ordering) against a required +0.0117. A +0.03 column lift - large for a loss-balance knob - is worth ~+0.0007 in the ensemble. P(seat over the greedy-optimal seven) drops 0.15 -> 0.02. The arm KEEPS its card slot: it is still the cheapest keep/kill on the loss-reweighting half and its control is on disk, but its value is now the keep/kill and nothing else. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_the-two-column-route-has-a-measured-ceiling.md

title: Are Fracture / MCL / Lateral OA real deficits or noisy columns?
description:
pool_ceiling's per-label reading (interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_three-columns-carry-the-whole-gap.md) puts the whole 0.0097 gap to first place in three findings: Fracture 0.8232, MCL 0.8283, Lateral OA 0.8369, against a pool mean of 0.8765. Lifting only those three to the mean is worth +0.0118, more than the gap.

BEFORE any card is spent on a member targeting them, measure whether the columns are DEFICITS or NOISE: positive count per column on the 909 shared studies, and the bootstrap interval of each column's stack score (LabelScores.paired_interval already bootstraps over studies; a one-arm interval is the same machinery). If Fracture's 0.8232 carries a +/-0.05 band on forty positives, the reading is about the ruler and not about the model.

PRICE: CPU-only, minutes, zero slots. It gates the sharpest target the project has had since the pool closed, so the ratio is as good as it gets.
close_reason: Measured. Fracture is NOT readable: 68 positives, band 0.1068, a 0.0533 shortfall against half a band - the column is about the ruler, exactly as this bead warned. MCL (171+, band 0.0702) and Lateral OA (233+, band 0.0583) are real deficits, and lifting only those two to the pool mean is worth +0.0073 against a +0.0097 gap. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_two-columns-carry-three-quarters-of-the-gap.md. Follow-up is a LEDGER read, not a run: do crop or slice-selection variants already score better on MCL and Lateral OA than on the mean.

title: Dark twins for the greedy-optimal seats: margin_seat_ff and finding_calib_dense_ff
description:
WHY. The champion (raptorweight_v1, board 0.944) is six FULL-FIT members. The best offline set this project owns is the greedy-optimal seven (seat_requirement.DEFAULT_BASE, offline 0.8764), and three of those seats have no full-fit twin, so any entry built from that set carries a DOSE confound against the champion: it would be fold-held members judged against full-fit ones. chainfour_ff removed that confound for the strongest of them on 2026-09-06. These two arms remove it for margin_seat and finding_calib_dense.

WHAT IS BEING CLAIMED, AND IT IS NOT A SEATING WIN. The member and seat axes are closed on the board (seven flats). This is not an attempt to buy score by adding a seat. It makes an ENTRY COMPOSITION shippable that has never been shippable: the best offline set, at the champion's dose. That comparison has never been run, because until chainfour_ff none of its members existed dark.

FLAGS. Each arm is its fold-0 original with --fold -1 and a distinct --out, nothing else. Both are DARK by construction: no holdout, no ledger row, no offline score. The board is their only ruler.

PRICE: ~2.5 h of card, on a card that is otherwise idle (mricore_corpus was already run on 2026-09-05 at 0.8390 and its re-arm refused on an existing checkpoint). Zero slots to build. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.02 — the dose constant is +0.007 board and the seat delta underneath it has read flat seven times, so the plausible ceiling is knob-sized. P(the composed dark entry beats 0.944) ~ 0.15. This is queued because the alternative is an IDLE card, not because the mechanism is large; if a mechanism-backed arm appears it takes the card ahead of these.

title: seat_requirement: the 8th seat adds +0.0002 against the optimal 7, first place needs 74x that
description: Measured 2026-09-06 over 181 priceable members vs the greedy-optimal 7-seat base. Best marginal gain +0.0002; target +0.0117. Inversion says solo 0.9781 (pool best 0.8635) or agreement 0.5668 (pool median 0.9073) - both unreachable, and the fit's rms residual 0.0003 exceeds the largest gain fitted, so the coefficients are not resolved and only the raw +0.0002 is quotable. Closes the single-member route. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_one-more-member-cannot-close-the-gap.md

title: The optimism constant was a two-fold reading quoted as a ten-fold one: +0.0201 -> +0.0019
description: priceable_blend's docstring quoted +0.0201 optimism from a single 455/454 split while the module's own DEFAULT_FOLDS is 10. At ten folds over the 206-member pool the optimism is +0.0019 (spread -0.0199..+0.0254, 91 studies per pricing fold). Under the old constant every searched blend was worthless by construction, since +0.0201 exceeds the +0.0121 seven seats buy over the best member. Fixed in the docstring 2026-09-06. Consequence: ensemble selection over the priceable pool comes OFF the closed list as an operation - but the greedy optimum over 206 members reads 0.8764 searched, 0.8745 corrected, which is honest12's 0.8751 within noise. The ceiling is a property of the pool, not of the selection method. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-06_the-ensemble-ceiling-is-not-a-selection-artefact.md

title: The accuracy lane IS priceable through a five-seat held proxy; tonight's three members price at +0.0027
description: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-06 01:46Z, before chainfour lands. comp/champion.json pins raptorweight_v1 (0.944), six FULL-FIT members - no offline ruler can read it, which is the mechanical reason all seven board flats on the member axis were decided blind. Five of the six seats have fold-held ancestors (calib_span, grade_ladder, merged_blend, lr4e-5_ws, through_dense); as a five-seat proxy they read offline 0.8700, which is 0.011 UNDER the champion's 0.944. So LEVELS are unusable and only DIFFERENCES are read - the quantity measured to transfer 1:1 twelve hours earlier (+0.002 offline read +0.003 on the board). MARGINAL CONTRIBUTIONS, nested by rule, no search: chaindense +0.0019, blendemalabel224 +0.0016, blendema224 +0.0010, all three together +0.0027 (sub-additive, 60 percent of the sum). PREDICTION: the three added to the champion move it about +0.003, to roughly 0.947. Under the 0.0062 floor, so this is an INSTRUMENT first - it tests whether marginal contributions measured on held twins transfer to full-fit originals, which if true converts a blind axis into a priced one permanently and is worth far more than the +0.003. KNOWN WEAKNESS, stated before use: the proxy cannot see error correlation between a new member and the FULL-FIT versions specifically, and full-fit dose is exactly the holdout studies. Sent to Kimi as question 2 at 01:46Z. Reading: logs/champion_proxy_seats_ledger.log
notes: RESOLVED 2026-09-06 02:40Z. chainfour peaked 0.8648 (best solo owned, +0.0014 over calib_dense_hold). On the five-seat held-twin proxy (base 0.8697) it adds +0.0020 alone against chaindense's +0.0019 - a 0.0001 difference, noise. The pair reads +0.0027 vs a 60%-of-sum prediction of +0.0023. But proxy+the proposed three = 0.8727 and proxy+those three+chainfour = 0.8727: +0.0000. TUPLE IS SATURATED, kneemri-proxyseat ships UNCHANGED at nine seats. A tenth seat that buys nothing offline still costs inference budget. Reading: logs/chainfour_ledger.log.

title: Offline nested-set DIFFERENCES transfer to the board at ~1:1 while levels over-read by 0.002-0.003
description: priceable_blend predicted +0.002 for the 3->10 seat step at the cheap corner, written and committed before cheapwide scored; the board moved +0.003. Levels over-read: offline 0.928/0.930 against board 0.925/0.928. n=1 on the difference, so DIRECTIONAL, not a constant. If it holds it prices seat decisions at zero slots, which is the only zero-cost ruler this project has for an axis that has produced seven board flats. Next free test: any future entry whose offline number is computed before submission - do not spend a slot to test this, ride an entry that is going anyway. Reading: logs/cheapcorner_seats_ledger.log

title: Cheap 224 decode corner caps at ~0.930 as a GROUP - seats do not lift it
description: Offline priceable_blend on nested cheap-corner sets: 3 seats 0.928, 10 seats 0.930, 12 seats 0.930. Adding the corner's two STRONGEST solos (0.8591, 0.8567) to a ten-seat group moved nothing. Splits cheapdecode_v1's 0.019 board deficit: ~0.002 is group/seat, ~0.017 is the corner. Predicts cheapwide (56043359) lands within 0.002 of 0.925 - written before it scored. Reading: logs/cheapcorner_seats_ledger.log. Consequence: an efficiency entry needing ~0.940 cannot be built from this corner by adding seats; it needs a better corner.

title: Does the chain sum on a BARE DENSE base? The 224 result and knee-orjq's 7/7 differ in two things at once
description: blendemalabel224 put three terms (blended labels, --ema, --slice-pooling labelwise) on the BARE 224 base native224 0.8502 and read 0.8591, +0.0089 = 1.4 floors: the chain sums. knee-orjq put second terms on the CALIBRATED DENSE base calib_dense_hold 0.8634 and read 7/7 negative, --ema -0.0003 and labelwise -0.0021 - the same two terms, opposite outcome. The two experiments differ in TWO things: the corner (224/12 vs 336/20) and the base's saturation (bare vs calibrated). Only one arm separates them: the same three terms on band_dense_hold 0.8573, which is dense geometry with a BARE recipe. If the chain sums there, saturation is the variable and composition stays a route on any unsaturated base. If it goes flat, the 224 gain was a cheap-corner artefact and composition closes on this project. Either way the arm's own score is a candidate member: predicted 0.8662 against a pool best of 0.8642.
notes: chainfour closed 02:37Z: 0.8648 at e7 of 12, MIDDLE branch, converged, rostered, ledger written. chainfour_ff (--fold -1 refit) queued 02:37Z pid 58256, ~75 min. Bead stays open until the full-fit twin lands.
close_reason: chainfour_ff_s2026.pt landed 04:02Z (ARM DONE written, 89.4 MB). Dark by construction; its ruler is the board. knee-oizh2 carries the two remaining dark twins.

title: No reader for the EFFICIENCY leaderboard — the one lane where we are losing to teams we outscore
description: board_read --live writes comp/leaderboard.json with leader/frontier/ours/gap/rank/field/tied, and every one of those is the ACCURACY board. There is no equivalent for the efficiency track, which is the lane where the standing is worst and the money is real: accuracy rank 41 at 0.944, efficiency rank 33 at 0.939, and 17 teams rank ABOVE us on efficiency while scoring BELOW us on accuracy. Podium pays 7k/6k/5k. The metric formula that produces that ordering is UNMEASURED by this project - we do not know how it trades accuracy against runtime, so we cannot tell whether a cheaper entry helps or hurts, and we have now spent a slot (cheapdecode_v1, board 0.925 at 3.7x cheaper decode) without being able to read what it did to the efficiency standing. WHAT IS NEEDED: find out whether the efficiency board is exposed by the Kaggle API at all (it may be a separate slug, a separate leaderboard endpoint, or published only as a page or a host notebook). If it is readable, add a reader beside board_read that records it with the same UTC-stamped discipline. If it is NOT readable by API, say so in writing and record where the rank 33 / 0.939 figure came from, because that number is currently quoted from memory with no instrument behind it - the same failure mode as the pinned gap that read 0.008 while the API said 0.015. WHY IT MATTERS: with the accuracy frontier closing at +0.00004/day (196 days to close +0.0086 at the current rate), the efficiency lane is the cheaper podium, and it is the only lane where we are demonstrably beaten by teams whose models are worse.
notes: CORRECTION, 23:45Z, and the bead was filed on a false premise - MY ERROR, found one grep later. kneemri/kaggle/efficiency_read.py ALREADY EXISTS and reads the efficiency board; interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_rank-not-gap.md is literally about the fact that the tool existed and nobody ran it. I repeated that exact failure: I probed the raw Kaggle API, saw only accuracy fields, and concluded there was no instrument instead of grepping the repo for one. THE ACTUAL READ, efficiency_read --live at 23:45Z: 3162 accuracy rows, 3132 efficiency rows, 3130 joined. Ours is accuracy rank 41 at 0.944 and efficiency rank 41 at 0.939 - NOT rank 33, so the remembered figure was wrong in the rank though right in the score, and our efficiency row is STALE because we submitted after the 21:47 snapshot. 25 teams rank above us on efficiency while scoring BELOW us, on runtime alone. THE LOAD-BEARING NUMBER: 122 teams within 0.002 of our 0.939 hold efficiency ranks 5 to 2738, median 2168. At fixed accuracy the rank spans essentially the whole field, so RUNTIME, not accuracy, is what orders this board - and being rank 41 inside that span means our runtime is already at the good end of it. Top 20 efficiency ranks score 0.927 to 0.952, median 0.940, which is the floor a cheap build must clear. cheapdecode_v1 at 0.925 is BELOW that floor, so the cheap-corner group is disqualified from the efficiency podium on accuracy, not on speed. THE LANE, RESTATED: hold ~0.940 accuracy and cut runtime. Not the reverse.

title: Does composition work at a DIFFERENT base? blendema224 re-asks knee-orjq at the cheap 224 corner
description: knee-orjq closed the stack route on 7/7 arms landing below control at the CALIBRATED DENSE corner, and its close names the limit explicitly: a stack built from a DIFFERENT base has never been tried. blendema224 is that arm. Base is 224px/12sl/0.2-0.8 - uncalibrated, not dense, and 3.2x cheaper per epoch. Terms: --labels blend_three_v1 (blendhold 0.8575 vs native224 0.8502, +0.0073) and --ema (ema224 0.8544 vs the same control, +0.0042), both measured AT this corner rather than transported in. One variable against blendhold. Additive prediction 0.8617. Full ladder in the arm header. ADDITIVE licenses stacking at the base where a chain of terms is affordable; SUBSTITUTES at a second structurally different base closes composition for the project rather than for one corner. ~20 min of card, zero slots.
notes: PRICE: blendemalabel224 (the re-pointed three-term arm) costs ~20 min of card and 0 submission slots, same corner and holdout as every 224 member. GAIN: the tested quantity is the SUM of three measured terms over the bare base native224 0.8502 - +0.0073 blended labels, +0.0042 ema, +0.0015 labelwise slice pooling = +0.0130, predicted 0.8632 - which clears the 0.0062 paired floor by about 2x, unlike the +0.0042 single link blendema224 tried to read. P(clears 1.5% as a member) ~0.02: no 224 member has come near the champion lane and this one is not expected to. P(returns a readable answer on whether a chain of small terms sums at this base) ~0.85, which is what it is bought for. knee-orjq closed composition at the calibrated dense corner and named a DIFFERENT base as the one thing it could not speak for. Negative (<=0.8570) makes two corners agree and removes composition as a route to 0.953; positive licenses adding a fourth and fifth term in ONE arm rather than one at a time. PRIOR READING: blendema224 0.8567, logs/blendema224_ledger.log - its band was unreadable because the term was smaller than the floor, which is the defect this arm fixes by changing the CONTROL, not the recipe.

title: Collapse the search-optimism bracket with K-fold priceable_blend --optimism
description: Two measurements of search bias exist and differ 7x because they measure different regimes: priceable_blend --optimism reads +0.0201 from a single 455/454 split over the 195-member pool, and kneemri/evaluation/selection_bias.py reads +0.0025 to +0.0031 at 7-12 seats over pools of 77-119 members with a board cross-check at +0.0027 (greedyseat_v1). The split-half moved BOTH knobs at once - half the studies and the widest pool - so +0.0201 is an upper bracket, not a value. Consequence: ceiling5 honest offline is bracketed 0.856 to 0.873 and the single-model step to the 0.953 target is +0.013 to +0.027 rather than the +0.027 quoted to Kimi at 21:28Z. FIX: run --optimism as K-fold over the full 909 studies so pool width stays at 195 while ruler noise is not doubled. Card-free. It collapses the bracket to a number and it is the number every literature candidate is being ranked against.

title: board_check --live read only the first page and invented seven phantom records
description: LiveBoard._kaggle asked for page_size=100 with no paging. The 107th submission pushed seven real rows off that page and the check reported each as recorded-and-not-on-the-board for days. Fixed here: page until a short page, ceiling PAGES=20. Filed so the class is on record - any live listing this project makes must page, and a record check that can invent a defect out of a short listing is worse than no check.

title: Searched offline scores must carry the selection-optimism correction
description: priceable_blend --optimism measures +0.0201 between selection half and held-out half over the 909 holdout studies, which is larger than the +0.0121 the whole seven-seat blend buys over its best single member. Every offline number this project quotes from a SEARCH is therefore about 0.020 high, and comparing one against a DESIGNED offline (distinct14) hands the searched side that much for free. board.jsonl already has a selection field for exactly this; distinct14 does not declare one. Work: make board_check refuse a searched row that quotes no corrected offline, and have priceable_blend.report print the correction beside its prediction rather than only in the docstring.

title: entry_offline resolved holdout records against the processed root, not the models root
description: EntryOffline was constructed with root.processed() while every HoldoutRecord lives under root.models(). The record check could therefore never succeed, so every entry that survived the in-sample test was falsely declined no-record. distinct14 and fitfour_v1 were declined that way while all 14 and all 4 of their members had .holdout.npz on disk. Fixed to root.models(); the two entries price at 0.8749 and 0.8711, both above 0.8695, and board_transfer top regime went from 2 to 4 resolved pairs, the 0.8678 band from 17 to 24. Every other kaggle tool that resolves checkpoints uses root.models(); champion_uncertainty even names the variable processed while assigning models(). Contrast is the tell.

title: trainer records no per-group learning rate, so a layer-decay arm cannot be read
description: band_deep_matched pre-registered its training loss as the instrument that decides whether the layer-decay compensation reached the optimiser. It floored 0.189 above band_dense (0.7667 vs 0.5780), worse than the 0.13 that disqualified the confounded band_dense_llrd it was built to fix, while every flag landed correctly in the recipe (unfreeze_last 12, layer_decay 0.7, backbone_lr 9.8e-05). Its header names the settling assertion - the top backbone group should read about 9.8e-5 - and that assertion cannot be made after the fact: encoder_rate_decay is in neither the metrics file nor the full log, and no parameter-group rate is recorded anywhere. Consequence: the arm scored 0.8487, which by score alone lands in the branch that CLOSES the depth axis and RETIRES the suspicion over every foreign-trunk negative (about 25 rows). That closure cannot be taken. Fix: record the realised per-group rates at optimiser construction into the recipe row, then re-read the existing checkpoint - no retrain needed if they show the compensation landed. See logs/band_deep_matched_ledger.log and knee-zt3l6.
notes: FIXED the witness, 2026-09-05. Trainer.backbone_rate captures the anchor off the built optimiser groups (BACKBONE_RATE, encoder_top_rate) and Landed compares it, so a --backbone-lr that does not reach Adaptation now blocks before the card is spent. backbone_lr moved out of NOT_A_SWITCH: it was written off as a rate no path applies partly, which was right about the path and wrong that a short path needs no witness. THE RETRO-READ IS IMPOSSIBLE: checkpoints save no optimiser state (keys are model holdout annot epoch epochs_done options targets slots config fingerprint fingerprint_config), so band_deep_matched cannot be re-read for the anchor it ran at. Settling it needs a re-run, now cheap at 224 px per band224. Depth axis stays open until then.

title: annotated_readings refusal misses fitted-constant leakage
description: withheld() checks only options[hold_annotations]. Every --calibrated-targets arm carries Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT, fitted on the same 696 gold cells; every --labels RECAL arm carries level_calibration level rates, fitted on the annotated rows (level_calibration.py:156) and applied corpus-wide. Neither READS those cells at train time, so the refusal passes and the tool prints none of them trained on these cells. That line was read as independence and a nine-member supervision ladder was written up as a five-knob confirmation before the provenance was checked. Fix: refuse or flag on supervision provenance, not just the hold flag, and make the census line state what it actually verified.

title: A parked duplicate arm shell wiped a finished run metrics file
description: band224 ran to at least epoch 10 (e8 0.8503, e9 0.8512, e10 0.8495 at 142 s/epoch) and then a SECOND band224 process, parked behind the first from a duplicate launch in an earlier session, started its own identical run at about 18:16Z. run_train truncates the metrics jsonl at start, so every epoch of the finished run was destroyed and the only surviving record of its numbers is a chat transcript. The checkpoint is being overwritten too. card_check reported OK throughout because only one of the two was ever ON the card at a time - the parked one is invisible to it by construction, which is exactly the hole card_check was built to close for the concurrent case. TWO FIXES ARE SEPARABLE: run_train must refuse to truncate a metrics file whose recipe matches its own and whose last epoch is at or past the asked-for budget (that run is DONE, and re-running it is a bug in every case since seeds are banned), and queue_check must count a PARKED arm shell as an owed arm rather than only counting watchers.

title: queue_check STRANDED list is stale
description: queue_check listed coatnet_hybrid.sh as STRANDED after the arm had already completed at Sep 5 03:45 with a 298 MB checkpoint on disk and ARM DONE in its full log. It nearly cost a duplicate card run and did chain into a banned repeat of mixup224_strong. STRANDED must check for the arm --out checkpoint on disk before reporting an arm as owed.

title: vendor_ruler top-N kept column has no null band
description: VendorRuler.line prints top-8 kept with no control. Philips keeps 2/8 while its rho sits inside its own null band, so the column contradicts the row it sits on. Any subset of a few hundred studies reshuffles seat membership by sampling alone. Either give the overlap its own null band (draw random subsets of the same size, count overlap, take the 5th percentile) or delete the column. Until then it must not be read.
notes: Still open and now written into the SEATS docstring and the interpretation, so the column cannot be read as a finding while it lacks a band.

title: Vendor ruler: read the result and decide whether the axis carries signal
description: kneemri.evaluation.vendor_ruler is built and running over the full record pool. It scores every member inside each vendor and field-strength stratum and reports Spearman rho against the pooled member ordering, beside a null band computed on 200 random subsets of the same size. The reading is the GAP: a vendor inside its own null band carries no ordering signal and the axis is silent; a vendor below its 5th percentile means member rank is a property of our scanner mix, which is a named mechanism for the seven board flats and licenses knee-hotxj and knee-vm3je. Absolute per-vendor AUC is NOT the reading - a stratum of a few hundred studies has an interval wider than the 0.0062 pooled floor.

title: Vendor-grouped ruler: does member RANK reorder across scanner vendors
description: Card-free instrument. Fitting persists the kept epoch per-study holdout probabilities beside every checkpoint as a HoldoutRecord keyed by study NAME (kneemri/runs/holdout_record.py:115); record_mix reaches 104 records over the shared 909 studies. Join the vendor and field-strength columns onto those records and compute per-vendor and per-field-strength AUC for the seated members. THE READING IS RANK, NOT LEVEL: a vendor subset is smaller than 909 so its own noise floor is wider than 0.0062 and absolute per-vendor AUCs will not be individually significant, but rank agreement across three vendor subsets of the SAME studies is paired and well conditioned. If greedy seat order is mix-dependent, ensemble selection has been fitted to our scanner mix, which is a named mechanism for the seven board flats. Cross-project support: cardiac-seg measured a 4-seed deep ensemble at +0.000 on a held-out vendor with BALD putting only 15-18% of the uncertainty epistemic. Depends on the reader fix.

title: Our corpus reader drops Manufacturer and MagneticFieldStrength: 0 of 4407 non-null
description: StudyMetadata declares field_strength_t and scanner, and the fastMRI/MRNet/Rijeka builders populate them. Study.from_directory(...).metadata() does not, so canonical_metadata.csv holds 0 non-null of 4407 in both columns while a direct pydicom read of one study returns Manufacturer=Philips Healthcare, ManufacturerModelName=Ingenia, MagneticFieldStrength=1.5. Census run by hand over all 4407 studies, 0 unreadable: Siemens ~1951, Philips ~1301, GE ~905, Toshiba/Canon 226; 1.5T 2543, 3T 1601, absent 238. Fix is in the reader, not a script beside it, and it must canonicalise the vendor string (SIEMENS/Siemens/Siemens Healthineers are one vendor; GE MEDICAL SYSTEMS collides on prefix with Philips Medical Systems). Blocks the vendor-grouped ruler. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-05_the-scanner-axis-exists-in-the-data-and-not-in-the-ruler.md

title: Kimi mail listener dead since 05:20Z - 19 letters queued unread
description:
DIAGNOSTIC, 2026-09-05T15:00Z. The peer inbox .agent-runtime/inbox/ holds 19 unconsumed letters. The most recent file in its read/ subdirectory is 20260905T0520Z-claude-shift-type-diagnostic.md, so the listener on that side last filed a letter at 05:20Z and has not run since. Every letter written from 11:47Z onward is queued and undelivered: q-pool, q-recipe, q-ceiling, q-meniscus, q-meniscus-amended, q-single, q-single-amended, q-single-final and eleven more.

WHY IT WAS NOT NOTICED. A dead listener looks exactly like a busy researcher. Letters land, the box fills, nothing errors, and the sending side has no signal at all - CLAUDE.md already warns that writing into the wrong box delivers nothing and looks perfectly healthy while doing it. This is the same failure with a different cause: right box, no reader. Roughly ten hours of question-writing produced no delivery, and three of those letters were careful withdrawals meant to STOP a search that was never started.

WHAT IS NOT LOST. Letters are files. When the listener restarts it will file the whole backlog in one pass, so the questions are queued rather than destroyed. Nothing needs rewriting.

FIX IS OWNER-SIDE, NOT OURS. The listener runs from the peer tree and this side must never edit it: python .agent-runtime/listen_for_mail.py, armed as a background task.

WHAT TO CHANGE HERE. Before writing a letter, compare the newest file in .agent-runtime/inbox/read/ against the newest letter in .agent-runtime/inbox/. If the box has grown and read/ has not, the peer is not listening and the letter is a queue entry rather than a question - which is still worth writing, but must not be planned around as though an answer were coming. Candidate for a check alongside queue_check, which already guards the equivalent hole for arm watchers.

title: Learned slice SELECTION at a fixed budget - the one upstream knob never turned
description:
knee-m69u asks for a new axis; the 2026-09-05 input-geometry re-audit (experiments/README.md, final section) closed multi-plane input, in-plane registration and the through-plane band, and left exactly two legs open. This is the live one.

CLAIM. Our aggregation stage is saturated from three directions: more slices -0.0001, more slots +0.0002, every combining rule within 0.0019. The ledger reads that as the limit sitting upstream, in what a single slice feature vector contains. Every arm this project has run samples slices UNIFORMLY across a fractional band. Which slices are taken, at a fixed budget, has never been varied.

WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY DONE BY MAX POOLING. Max pooling selects at READ time, over features the encoder computed from a uniformly chosen set. It cannot recover a slice that was never sampled. Selection here means changing which slices reach the encoder at all, which changes the gradient the encoder sees.

CHEAPEST FORM THAT WOULD SHOW SIGNAL. Two-pass. Run an existing trained whole-stack member over a dense slice grid, record per study which slices carried the argmax under max pooling, then train a fresh member at the SAME budget on those slices instead of the uniform ones. No new architecture, no new loss. The control already exists at every budget we use.

MEASURED HEADWIND to price against, not to ignore. The pooling-by-slice-count interaction says max wins short stacks and loses long ones, so a selection built from max argmax at a long stack is reading the operator that is worst there. The selector should be built at the budget it will serve.

PRICE. Not yet priced; do not arm until Q-SINGLE-B comes back from Kimi with an isolated published delta, or until the two-pass proxy is run card-free on existing checkpoints. Blocked on that, deliberately - the audit rule is plan before arm.

NOT the other surviving leg: a localiser crop is knee-tracked separately and carries crop80_span at -0.0099 against it.

title: Compensated layer-decay re-run: the depth axis the ledger says is owed
description: band_dense_llrd ran unfreeze-last 12 / layer-decay 0.7 at backbone-lr 4e-5 and read 0.8483 vs band_dense 0.8578, but parameter_groups anchors the ladder at the TOP opened block so the control's own six blocks were cut to 0.7^2.5 = 0.41 of their rate. The arm changed two things. band_deep_matched.sh compensates the anchor to 9.8e-5 = 4e-5/0.41 so blocks 6-11 hold the control's geometric-mean rate and only the grading moves. Matters beyond one arm: every foreign-trunk arm in the tree runs layer_decay 1.0, so if depth pays once the rate is held, radiodino/ortho/coatnet/mricore were all measured through the wrong recipe.
notes: PRICE: 2h05m of card (12 epochs x ~625s), zero slots. GAIN, stated in two parts because the arm is an instrument first. Direct: if depth pays once the rate is held, band_dense 0.8578 -> 0.8640+, which is +0.006 of holdout and about +0.006 of board at the 1:1 operating-point transfer — BELOW the 0.010 bar on its own, so this arm is not sold as an improvement. Instrumental, which is the real case: every foreign-trunk arm in the tree ran layer_decay 1.0 and unfreeze_last 6, so an ABOVE reading says radiodino_corpus 0.8214, ortho_dense 0.8452, coatnet_hybrid 0.8259 and mricore_corpus were all measured through a recipe that never let the trunk move, and re-running that family under a corrected schedule IS a >=0.010 lane (a foreign trunk reaching the 0.8521 seat bar). P(clears 0.8640) ~ 0.25; P(the reading is decisive either way) ~ 0.85, since the training loss discriminates 'compensation did not reach the optimiser' from 'depth does not pay'.
