title: Both local LLM readers are dead on the MATCHED denominator too, and the 121-vs-140 ranking was never a comparison
description:
reader_upgrade now prices the CORRECTION lane: the cells both readers assert, each scored against the same truth, paired bootstrap over studies. local_reader (Qwen3-8B): 463 shared, lexicon 0.795 vs candidate 0.812, gap +0.017 [-0.004, +0.039]. medgemma4b: 492 shared, 0.774 vs 0.774, gap +0.000 [-0.027, +0.025]. Neither clears zero, and neither clears the majority class on the blank pairs. The v2 lexicon's own rate on its 507 answered pairs is 0.771.

This RETIRES the naive reading of knee-wko44's gold-58 table (local_reader 121 wrong vs v2 140 wrong). That is not a comparison: local_reader answers 463 of the 507 cells v2 answers, so it is scored on a smaller and easier set. Same denominator failure as 19-percent-of-located read as 19-percent-of-all.

NOT a refutation of the labeler axis. The panel is 57 studies / ~500 shared cells and the paired half-width is ~0.022, so a real +0.02 correction is BELOW this ruler's resolution. Two questions with Kimi (letter 20260905T0908Z): (1) how many annotated studies does a +0.02 correction need at 80% power, paired over studies - if it is 300 then the GATE is the blocker and the next arm is annotation, not prompting; (2) Wollek's 0.939 row is a DISTILLED German BERT fine-tuned on rule-based plus manual labels, not a zero-shot LLM, so our cell has no published number - if distillation is where the +0.081 lives the arm is train-a-small-model-on-v2-plus-gold-58 and the endpoint sweep is off the path.
notes: 2026-09-05 09:30Z: the axis is bounded SMALL by two readings we already owned, and neither is the gold panel. blendlabels (ledger 325) trained on a three-reader blended table reads +0.0034 on the metric / +0.0070 on the six label-bottlenecked findings - the tie-breaking mechanism proven at +0.0216 on the gold-58 label ruler collapses to under the noise floor on the card ruler. And supervision_gap on holdannot has our model ALREADY beating its own labels by +0.0274, nine of twelve columns on the label side, so label noise is not the binding constraint there. The power question (how many annotated studies to resolve +0.02) is MOOT: the card ruler on 909 studies already answered. Pricing this axis off a 57-study panel when a trained member had priced it a week earlier is the error - CLAUDE.md says read the ledger BEFORE filing, and I filed first.

title: Per-column offline AUC partly tracks READER PRECISION, not model skill
description:
Measured 2026-09-05 over the 57 annotated studies / 684 cells (ReaderAgreement.cells, the only non-reader ground truth).

Per-column reader precision on YES calls vs band_dense_s2026 best-epoch per-label AUC:

  finding                gold+  TP  FP MISS   prec    AUC
  Contusion                 18  16  20    2  0.444  0.871
  MCL                        9   9   9    0  0.500  0.793
  Lateral OA                11   9   7    2  0.562  0.816
  Medial OA                 15  14   8    1  0.636  0.880
  Lateral Meniscus          23  20  10    3  0.667  0.846
  PF OA                     20  16   8    4  0.667  0.858
  Effusion                  34  34  16    0  0.680  0.860
  Fracture                  17  13   6    4  0.684  0.809
  Bakers                    12  11   5    1  0.688  0.907
  ACL                       23  23   9    0  0.719  0.874
  Medial Meniscus           26  25   7    1  0.781  0.905
  Synovitis                 27  13   3   14  0.812  0.876

  spearman precision vs AUC: rho=+0.529 p=0.077 (n=12)
  spearman recall    vs AUC: rho=+0.162 p=0.615

DIRECTIONAL, not a finding: n=12 columns, p=0.077, and Contusion is the counterexample (worst precision, mid AUC). Do not plan around the correlation itself.

THE SPECIFIC CELL THAT IS NOT DIRECTIONAL: MCL has 9 gold positives, 9 true positives and 9 FALSE positives. The reader DOUBLES the MCL positive rate - half of every MCL positive our members train on and are scored against is wrong. MCL is our worst offline column at 0.793, and knee-zsyp4 measured the boards implied MCL column at 0.980 (colmcl ref 56020054). The column where the board says the task is nearly solved is the column where our supervision is half wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS: our offline holdout is scored against the SAME lexicon table the members train on, so a column with noisy labels is deflated on BOTH sides. Member selection has been ranking on that ruler. This is a named mechanism for knee-zsyp4 (biased-ruler) and independent evidence for knee-wko44 (labeler axis).

NEXT: ask whether noisy-label AUC can be de-biased to clean-label AUC per column without new annotations (letter out to Kimi 2026-09-05). If it can, every ledger number gets a per-column correction and the reseat decisions get re-read.

title: Surgical fine-tuning: pick the block by SHIFT TYPE, the one recipe axis neither ortho_slow_trunk nor band_lpft touches
description:
Lee et al. ICLR 2023 (openreview APuPRxjHvZ) fine-tune a CONTIGUOUS BLOCK rather than the whole trunk, and the best block is decided by the KIND of shift: input-level (corruptions, low-level domain gap) wants EARLY layers, feature-level (subpopulation) wants MIDDLE, output-level (spurious correlation, label remapping) wants the head. WILDS Camelyon17, a histopathology SCANNER shift, is best at the earliest embedding layer; FMoW geo-shift is best at later attention blocks. Reported by Kimi in research/2026-09-05_ood-vit-finetune-schedules.md.

WHY IT IS A DISTINCT AXIS. Every unfreeze this project has run is a SUFFIX: --unfreeze-last N opens the trailing N blocks and nothing else, so early-layer-only has never been tested here. natural-image pretraining to greyscale MRI is the input-level case in Lee's taxonomy, which is the cell their own result says the trailing blocks are the WRONG choice for. That makes it a mechanism, not a knob.

WHAT IT NEEDS FIRST. train has no flag for an interior or prefix block range - --unfreeze-last only counts from the end. Cost is one small change to the trunk freezing code plus a flag, then one arm against band_dense = 0.8578 with the same everything else. Do NOT queue it before band_lpft reads: both arms move the same variable family (which parameters see gradient), and LP-FT is the cheaper and better-evidenced of the two.
design:
AUDIT 2026-09-05 05:38Z, kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py:233-320 read in full. The flag does not exist and the shape of the change is settled, so that when band_lpft reads this is one edit rather than a design sitting.

WHAT IS THERE. open_blocks(unfreeze_last) returns blocks[len(blocks) - min(unfreeze_last, len(blocks)):] - a strict SUFFIX, with the min and the count-from-the-front both deliberate (a [-0:] read the whole encoder under a head-only name, measured at 2,592 parameters either way). Three callers: opened() -> last_blocks() freezes the complement and returns the rest; backbone_groups() calls both, and under --layer-decay emits one group per opened block anchored at the TOP so the ledger rate stays the top block's rate.

THE CHANGE, and it is a widening rather than a second path. open_blocks takes a WINDOW, not a count: the suffix is the window [depth-N, depth). One value object beside the class - BlockWindow with a last(n) constructor and a range(lo, hi) one - and open_blocks becomes blocks[window.lo:window.hi]. last_blocks, opened and backbone_groups keep their signatures by holding a window instead of an int. That keeps ONE way to say which blocks are open, rather than an --unfreeze-range flag racing --unfreeze-last through an if.

TWO THINGS THAT MUST NOT BREAK, and both are equality checks rather than opinions:
- BlockWindow.last(n) must produce byte-identical parameter sets to today's open_blocks(n) for n = 0, 1, 6, 12 and for n > depth. Every number in the ledger was measured under that shape.
- backbone_groups' layer-decay ladder anchors at the TOP OPENED block. Under an interior window the top opened block is no longer the encoder's last, and the ladder must still anchor at the top of the WINDOW - otherwise an early-block arm silently runs its blocks at backbone_lr * decay^k for a k the ledger has never seen.

NOT WRITTEN YET, on purpose. Gates cannot run while an arm holds the card (uv rewrites the venv under it), and Q-SHIFT is out with Kimi asking whether the block can be PICKED by a published diagnostic or whether it is try-all-three. The edit is ~40 lines including the mirror tests; the question decides whether it buys one arm or three.
notes:
band_early (offset 6) CLOSED the position axis: 0.8418 vs control band_dense 0.8578, -0.0160, flag verified off the WEIGHTS (blocks 0-5 drift 0.025-0.030 vs stock dinov2-small, blocks 6-11 exactly 0.00000). Trailing blocks are load-bearing on DINOv2-small knee MRI; Lee's position effect does not transfer. Ledger row committed 203d03d1.
band_mid (offset 3) was TRUNCATED BY DECISION at 12:43Z 2026-09-05, epoch 2 of 12, ~33 min card. NOT a score - metrics.jsonl holds e1 only, convergence_check will class it TRUNCATED. It interpolates the SHAPE of an answer band_early already gave and cannot produce a member, so expected score gain ~0: instrument class. It was holding the card ahead of mricore_corpus, which was THIRD in the chain (band_mid -> band224 -> mricore) and the only mechanism priced >= 0.010 of holdout on its own. Chain watchers 63620 and 39336 killed with it; band224 is now unqueued and unrun.
RE-OPEN BY: running offset 3 in a gap once the trunk lane is decided. The pre-registered branch table in band_surgical.sh stands unedited.

title: The label detector is the ceiling, and confident learning is the measured floor - build a SimiFeat-style kNN detector over the cached features
description:
THE BUDGET AND ALPHA KNOBS ARE BOTH SPENT AND BOTH WERE KNOBS ON A CEILING. knee-jom26 priced the budget curve out in both directions: our confident-learning detector separates radiologist disagreements at AUC 0.7628, its precision at the operating point is 0.720, and its recall there is 0.129 - so it can reach 13 percent of the corpus's real label errors before precision collapses. Corrected-minus-corrupted peaks exactly at the cut errors_relabel already trains on. Nothing on this axis moves again until the DETECTOR moves.

THE LITERATURE SAYS CL IS NOT THE CEILING - IT IS THE FLOOR. Kimi's Q-DET reply, 2026-09-05:

  AQuA (Goswami et al., NeurIPS 2023, arXiv:2306.09467), a benchmark over 17 datasets, 4 noise types and
  4 noise rates evaluating AUM, Confident Learning, CINCER and SimiFeat, concludes verbatim: 'Overall, we
  found SimiFeat (SIM) to be the best cleaning method ... closely followed by CINCER (CIN) ... Confident
  learning (CON) consistently performed the worst among all the evaluated methods.'

  SEMD (Srikanth et al., arXiv:2312.02200) measures CL underperforming by -0.206 F1 on CIFAR-10 symmetric
  and -0.156 F1 on CIFAR-100 symmetric, and notes CL underperforms across all synthetic settings.

  SimiFeat (Zhu, Dong and Liu, ICML 2022, arXiv:2110.06283) is TRAINING-FREE: kNN over pretrained
  embeddings with test-time augmentation. On HUMAN-annotated noise it beats CL by about 20 percent F1 on
  CIFAR-10 and 10 percent on CIFAR-100 - human noise, which is the regime we are actually in.

WHY THIS ONE IS CHEAP HERE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT. SimiFeat needs embeddings and a neighbour search, not a training run. The processed root already holds full-corpus 336 px feature arrays for SIX trunks - ortholarge, v3large, large, radnet121, vjepa2l and small - each with its index json and mask. So the strongest published detector runs on arrays this project already paid for. ZERO CARD, ZERO SLOT. That is a far better ratio than any arm currently queued.

MEASURE IT THROUGH THE GATE THAT ALREADY EXISTS, so the number is comparable rather than merely new. kneemri.evaluation.label_errors already reports, against the 58-study radiologist panel: separation AUC over all 140 disagreements, precision and recall and lift at budgets 25/50/100/150/200 in gold-scaled units, and the same split for the 108 confident false positives and the 32 misses. The new detector must be scored by exactly that reporting path. Our CL numbers to beat:

  all disagreements (n=140)   separation AUC 0.7628   precision 0.720 at gold budget 25   recall 0.129
  confident false positives   separation AUC 0.7580   precision 0.640 at gold budget 25
  misses (n=32)               separation AUC 0.6903   precision 0.08-0.11 at every budget
  cleanlab's own mask         precision 0.484 all-disagreements, 0.258 on false positives (lift 1.63x)

NOTE WHERE THE HEADROOM ACTUALLY IS. Our detector is nearly blind to MISSES - 0.6903 separation and precision under 0.11 at every budget, against 0.7628 and 0.720 on the same panel for disagreements overall. The 32 misses are the cells where the lexicon said absent and the radiologist said present, and they are the half a report-derived label table should be worst at. A detector that only matches CL on false positives but reads misses at all would change the shape of the corrected corpus, not just its size.

WHAT A RESULT LOOKS LIKE. Separation AUC materially above 0.7628 on the same panel. Then re-run the net-benefit arithmetic from knee-jom26: a higher precision curve moves the corrected-minus-corrupted peak to a LARGER budget, which is the only thing that reopens the budget axis - and it does so with more corrected cells, not fewer. If the kNN detector ties CL, the label axis is closed on this corpus and should be written up as closed.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Not a member, not a submission, and it must not be sold as one. It is an instrument that decides whether an axis reopens.

SECOND CANDIDATE, CHEAPER STILL IF THE ARTEFACT EXISTS: AUM (Pleiss et al., NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2001.10528) ranks by area under the margin across epochs and needs only per-epoch per-sample logits. Checked - our metrics.jsonl stores per-epoch aggregates (loss, auc, ece, loss quantiles) and no per-sample margins, so AUM would need the runs re-instrumented and re-run. That makes it CARD, not free, and it goes behind SimiFeat.

DO NOT REACH FOR: Li et al. NeurIPS 2022 trains an LSTM meta-detector on synthetic noise; strongest reported transfer, but it is a build on top of a build and the training dynamics we would feed it do not exist either.

REFS: knee-jom26 (the budget closure and the net-benefit arithmetic), knee-v78o1 (reading_check), kimi letter 20260905T0615Z.

title: Knee-continued trunk at ViT-B scale - the one unbuilt cell in the DAPT table
description: In-domain continuation is MEASURED at +0.019 and it seats nothing only because the trunk it ships on is the wrong size. Three instruments, one sign: ortho_dense 0.8452 vs v3large_dense 0.8258 = +0.0194 at matched 303M trunk and byte-identical recipe (only --variant differs); the frozen probe re-read at per-trunk ridge penalties (the knee-x4yx defect - a shared penalty is unfair when trunk feature magnitudes differ ~17x) gives ortholarge 0.8249 vs v3large 0.8046 = +0.0203, agreeing with the fitted arm to 0.001; and ortho_stack reads +0.0140 on band_dense's recipe. The decomposition against base224 (DINOv2 ViT-B, 86M, 0.8509) is DAPT +0.0194, ViT-L lane -0.0251, net -0.0057 - inside the floor, which is why ortho_dense was declined. So the lane is blocked on TRUNK SIZE, not on corpus, and the two gains have never existed in the same weights because OrthoFoundation only ships ViT-L. THE ASK: a DINOv2/v3 ViT-B or ViT-S with knee or MSK continued pretraining already published. If one exists this is a checkpoint download and one 40-minute arm for a mechanism-backed +0.019 on our best trunk size - the largest priced-and-unspent lever in the pool. Out with Kimi as Q-BASE (letter 2026-09-05T0240Z). If no such trunk exists, the fallback is distilling ortholarge into ViT-B, which is a BUILD and must be priced separately before anything is queued. Does NOT re-open trunk size (members.declines line 195 forbids that): size is held fixed on both sides of the +0.0194 and the continuation corpus is the only free term.
notes:
MRI-CORE IS A TWO-STRIKE CANDIDATE AND IT IS NOT THE RIGHT INSTANTIATION OF THIS LEVER. Audited the ledger before spending the probe gate's card, and this repo has already measured both of MRI-CORE's defining properties, separately, on controlled arms.

STRIKE 1 - MEDICAL CORPUS AT ViT-B. radiodino_corpus (Snarcy/RadioDino-b16, ViT-B/16, DINO objective, RadImageNet 1.35M medical images) was run at v3base_dense's EXACT recipe, so the pretraining corpus moved with architecture and objective held fixed. It read 0.8214 against v3base_dense 0.8455, -0.0241, and its seat priced at -0.0008 on honest12. radiodino_s16 (ViT-S) is the capacity leg: base width buys +0.0106 over small on the identical corpus, so the corpus cost is NOT a capacity artefact - a medical-corpus trunk sits 2.4 to 2.9 points behind its natural twin at BOTH widths and the gap does not close by scaling. The ledger's own words: the medical corpus transfers WORSE than natural at fixed architecture and fixed objective.

STRIKE 2 - SAM INIT. MRI-CORE initialises from SAM's ViT-B and continues with DINOv2 for four epochs. This project already ran a SAM-family ViT-B trunk as medsam_dense: 0.8137 against the same recipe's controls band_dense 0.8578 and calib_dense_hold 0.8634, so -0.044 to -0.050, seven to eight times the noise floor. comp/members.declines names the reading: a segmentation-pretrained trunk transferred to a classification stack loses to both a natural-image trunk and a domain-pretrained one, and it is re-opened only by changing the TRANSFER (promptable encoder as region proposer), not by another plain-trunk arm. MRI-CORE as a plain trunk IS another plain-trunk arm.

Note what does NOT close this: radiodino_corpus did not reach its REFUTES branch (< 0.80), so the medical-image row is open and MRI-CORE is not retired. Both strikes are priors, not measurements of MRI-CORE. But two independent controlled arms pointing the same way is a bad prior for a lane whose whole appeal was a strong one, and 20 minutes of card buys a reading that two existing readings already predict.

WHAT THE LEVER ACTUALLY NEEDS. The +0.0194 DAPT gain was measured on OrthoFoundation - DINOv2 lineage, knee/MSK-specific continuation, ViT-L. MRI-CORE changes the LINEAGE (SAM not DINOv2), the CORPUS (hospital-wide MRI, knee one of 18 locations, not knee-specific) and the SCALE all at once, which is the three-variable mistake radnet_family already made here. The clean instantiation changes ONLY scale: distil a ViT-B student from FROZEN ortholarge on unlabelled knee slices, keeping lineage and corpus fixed, then run the same per-trunk-penalty frozen probe that measured the +0.0194.

Kimi's decision rule for that, and it is a real gate: if the student probe lands within ~0.005 of ortholarge 0.8249, the DAPT gain is a property of the WEIGHTS and survives a shrink, so the build is justified. If the gap is ~0.015 or more it is a property of CAPACITY, and this lane closes for good. TinyMIM (CVPR 2023) supports the shape: ViT-L to ViT-B is a small enough capacity gap that a direct distil is not gap-limited the way ViT-L to ViT-S is.

The comparison that decides the LEVER, as opposed to the mechanism, is student-ViT-B against v3base - a distilled-from-DAPT ViT-B has to beat a plain DINOv2 ViT-B, not merely approach its ViT-L teacher.

NEXT: price the distillation build. It needs an unlabelled-slice loader we already have, a DINOv2 ViT-B student init, and a feature-matching loss - no new supervision and no labels. Do NOT spend the MRI-CORE probe gate first; it is now the weaker of the two and its result is half-predicted.

title: Per-column board map priced at one slot per column - axis closed unless colhalf shows sparsity
description: Kimi's Q-RULER5 closure: case mix and definitional mismatch make identical predictions on all offline data, so neither is falsifiable without board cases or board labels. A reliable per-column map therefore costs one slot per column (12 slots, 2.4 days of every slot) against a 0.009 gap - not payable. colhalf is the sparsity test: concentrated deviation makes adaptive group ablation affordable, spread deviation closes the axis. MCL's 0.17 (0.980 board vs 0.8112 over the 103-member rostered pool) stands UNEXPLAINED - sampling ruled out at ~7 SE, label noise demoted by supervision_gap showing the lexicon is the better half on MCL.

title: Board headroom per column bounds every supervision lane
description: colmcl measured MCL board AUC at 0.980. Our holdout reads the same weights at 0.8104. The 0.17 gap is ruler, not model - so a relabel is paid only for the training-side injury, bounded above by the 0.020 AUC the column has left, i.e. 0.0017 of board. Kimi's literature price of +0.010 divided a holdout-scale recovery by twelve and is off by ~5x on its own best case. Mean constraint: eleven other columns average 0.9407, total board headroom 0.056, the 0.953 target is 16% of it. RULE: price every lane against board headroom per column, never against an offline AUC gap. colbaker at the 04:56Z mark decides whether MCL is representative.

title: Second column ablation - ablate a column our map calls STRONG
description: colmcl's own docstring named the refutation it cannot make: it cannot separate 'columns are weighted' from 'the board's MCL column is easier than our holdout's'. A second ablation on a column our offline map calls STRONG settles it. Baker's is the pool's best column at 0.9208. Copy comp/kernels/kneemri-colmcl, set ABLATED to Baker's, ship. Pre-register on the drop: near 0.944-0.904 again means every column is near-ceiling on the board and our map carries no information at all; a SMALL drop means the ordering is inverted broadly and our per-column supervision is anti-correlated with board truth; a drop matching (0.9208-0.5)/12 = 0.035 means the map transfers and MCL alone is anomalous. Costs one slot, no card. It is the cheapest instrument the project has and it gates every per-label plan.

title: colmcl is a joint test of labels-vs-model for one column, not just a weight read
description: With colnull confirming the plain mean, colmcl (ref 56020054) gives MCL's board AUC as (champion - colmcl) * 12 + 0.5. Our offline pool reads MCL at 0.8104, the worst of the twelve. If the board AUC comes back materially HIGHER than 0.8104, the gap is our supervision and not the model - which is exactly the direction the 2026-09-04 four-reader measurement points, where report_labels_v2 makes 108 false positives against 32 misses. If it comes back at or below 0.8104, the model is the limiter for that column and a training-side lift is the lane. Either answer aims the next arm. Record the arithmetic in comp/board.jsonl when it lands.

title: Post-hoc cross-column lift is closed on BOTH estimators, so the weak-column lane costs card
description: column_mixing with the sparse L1 label-graph rule, nested, on the seven-member fold-0 pool: mean -0.0085, worst -0.0653, best +0.0041. The ridge null was already recorded and bounded DENSE mixing only; the L1 rule existed because it is the estimator that can keep a real pair and zero the rest, and it was the open half. It is now closed. It also fails the specific question that made it worth re-running: it does NOT lift the weak columns. MCL +0.0001, Lateral OA +0.0041, and Fracture -0.0653 - Fracture has 68 positives and the fit destroys it. Consequence: the per-label axis priced by column_headroom (+0.0195 for the bottom three) has no free post-hoc road. Every remaining mechanism is training-side and costs card, so it must be ranked against whatever else holds the GPU. Note the metric leaves no within-column operation alive either (kneemri-monotone), so post-hoc is now empty as a class.

title: Pure fleet refit is dead at +0.002; the 0.006 was the calibration flag
description: uncalib (ref 56019970) read 0.937, exactly the pre-registered lower anchor. twinfive 0.935 to uncalib 0.937 is pure refit at five seats, +0.002. uncalib 0.937 to fiveship 0.941 is calibration, +0.004. The independent four-seat pair agrees and reads smaller: foldfour 0.936 to fitfour 0.937, +0.001. Both under the 0.0062 noise floor. Roughly thirty hours of card that the 0.953 chain budgeted at +0.006 buys +0.002. Refit WITH --calibrated-targets keeps the +0.006 because calibration is a flag on the same run. Consequence: never ship a refit without the flag, and never plan card time for a refit whose only justification is the refit.

title: local_reader_annotated.csv is the best labeler we own and its provenance is recorded nowhere
description: On the gold 58, scored with this repo's own reader_agreement, local_reader_annotated.csv reads 121 net wrong of 696 cells against report_labels_v2.csv's 140 - 83 false positives against the lexicon's 108, at matched recall (84.2% vs 84.6%) and +5.6 points of precision. It is the best of the four reader tables the project holds. Its mtime is 2026-08-29 16:40 and NOTHING records what produced it: not a doc in research/, not an interpretation, not a bead, not a committed entrypoint. api_labeler.py and llm_labeler are candidates, neither is confirmed. So the best supervision this project owns cannot be regenerated over the corpus, which is the only form in which it could ever be trained on. Asked as question 2 of letter 20260904T2346Z-claude-relabel-timing.md. Until it is answered the labeler axis (knee-wko44) can only be swept with Qwen3.8, which is a different reader with a different error shape (48 FP / 74 misses against 83 / 38).

title: Decompose each board pair's offline delta by difficulty band
description: transfer_strata gives a per-band slope (Q1 +0.44 rising to Q3 +0.81). That is a statement about which entries separate in which band, not yet a statement about where transfer lives. The refutation: for each already-scored board pair, split its offline delta into per-band deltas and ask which band's delta predicts the pair's BOARD delta. If a pair whose gain sits in Q5 does not out-transfer a pair whose gain sits in Q1, the per-band slopes are an artefact. Costs no slot and no card. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_transfer-is-blind-on-easy-cases.md
close_reason: Ran in the same wake it was filed. attribution() in kneemri/evaluation/transfer_strata.py splits each of the 348 resolved pairs at the median hard-share: gain made HARD transfers +0.74, gain made EASY +0.67. Seven hundredths, against a band table spanning +0.44 to +0.81 -- so most of the band spread is which entries separate where, not where the gain was made. The strong claim (easy gain worth half) is withdrawn in interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_the-ruler-is-not-blind.md rather than shipped. What stands: the ruler is NOT blind above 0.870, every band transfers, pair-level +0.7.

title: The refit constant is +0.001, not +0.006 -- the difference is --calibrated-targets
description: Two board pairs measure fold-0 twins -> full-fit at four seats: foldfour_v1 0.936 -> fitfour_v1 0.937 (+0.001) and twinfive_v1 0.935 -> fiveship_v1 0.941 (+0.006). Same seat count, same direction, five times the single-pair floor apart. The kernels say why and the board rows do not. fitfour seats four _ff members (--fold -1 --ema): refit and nothing else. fiveship seats ONE _ff and THREE _cf, and _cf is the _ff flags PLUS --calibrated-targets -- a supervision change, not a split change. So the clean refit term is +0.001 and the extra +0.005 is calibration or noise. CONSEQUENCE: roughly thirty hours of fleet-refit card is licensed by a constant that is now +0.001, i.e. not licensed. And the term that might carry the 0.006 is a TRAINING FLAG on runs we already know how to make. seat_bonus.py:58 already argues _cf is a supervision change from the other side. kneemri-uncalib isolates it in one slot: fiveship's exact seating with the three _cf seats replaced by their _ff twins, pre-registered on the delta against 0.941. Also corrects knee-6xmtl, which was filed on a false premise (merged_blend_cf is fold 0 per members.roster:387, so twinfive_v1's offline 0.8705 is honest).

title: fitfour_v1's board row names foldfour_v1's members, not the ones its kernel serves
description: comp/board.jsonl records fitfour_v1 with members_named = [calib_dense_hold_s2026, calib_span_s2026, through_dense_s2026, small_batch6_s2026] -- byte-identical to foldfour_v1's. Its kernel comp/kernels/kneemri-fitfour/kneemri-fitfour.py:129-132 serves calib_dense_hold_ff, calib_span_ff, through_dense_ff, small_batch6_ff. The row is the fold-0 half's member list pasted onto the full-fit half, which makes the pair read as two entries with identical members and different scores, and makes the refit measurement invisible to anything reading the record instead of the kernel. board_check never looks: it validates scope, selection, counts and all-data names, but never joins members_named against the kernel's chosen tuple. Two fixes: correct the row, and add a BoardCheck rule that parses the chosen tuple out of the row's kernel script and refuses a disagreement -- the same join board_check already does to recover a script for a refless row.

title: twinfive_v1 board row carries a contaminated offline, and the refit constant rests on it
description:
comp/board.jsonl records twinfive_v1 with offline 0.8705 and no exclusion. It cannot be honest: the entry's five seats are calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, merged_blend_cf, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026 -- and merged_blend_cf was fitted at --fold -1, so it has seen all 909 holdout studies. This is the raptor_solo defect (an in-sample number recorded as a fact) on a row that is load-bearing.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE CELL. twinfive_v1 was built as the fold-0 half of fiveship_v1, and fiveship_v1's five seats are calib_span_ff, grade_ladder_cf, merged_blend_cf, lr4e-5_ws_cf, through_dense_cf. So the pair's reported delta of +0.006 (0.935 -> 0.941) is the price of refitting FOUR seats measured against a control that was already one-fifth refit, not five. That +0.006 is one of only two measurements of the full-corpus refit term; the other, foldfour_v1/fitfour_v1, reads +0.001 at four seats. A six-fold spread, and now one of the two halves is dirty. The constant licenses roughly thirty hours of card spent refitting a fleet and is the final term of the arithmetic path to 0.953.

FIX: (a) mark twinfive_v1's offline as excluded with the reason, the way raptor_solo was handled; (b) kneemri-twinchamp is the clean fold-0 half -- the exact fold-0 twin of every one of fiveship_v1's five seats, honest offline 0.8700 measured with record_mix before the slot -- and completes the pair properly. (c) board_check should refuse an offline on any entry seating a member fitted at --fold -1, which is the general form of the defect and would have caught raptor_solo too.
notes: WRONG PREMISE, closed on the roster's own line. comp/members.roster:387 states merged_blend_cf is 'merged_blend_s2026's flags plus --calibrated-targets; fold 0, the arm's only offline read'. It is a FOLD-0 member, not full-fit, so twinfive_v1's offline 0.8705 is honest and needs no exclusion. fiveship_v1's row agrees from the other side ('four of the five are --fold -1' = the four DARK _cf/_ff seats, merged_blend_cf being the fifth and fold-0). The board_check rule this bead asked for (refuse an offline on an entry seating a --fold -1 member) ALREADY EXISTS as BoardCheck.unpriceable, keyed on ALL_DATA_SUFFIX/_ff plus final_ws_e12, and it correctly passed this row. Nothing to fix here. What the mistake did cost: I built comp/kernels/kneemri-twinchamp on the contamination story and it is a ONE-SEAT SWAP off twinfive_v1 (merged_blend_s2026 for merged_blend_cf) -- a banned seating operation, and one seat_bonus.py:52 already prices as unresolvable at the 0.0040 single-pair floor. Not submitted.

title: coatnet2 registry entry ran under IMAGENET normalization while timm publishes 0.5/0.5
description:
FIXED, and filed for the class rather than the instance. The COATNET_2 entry declared no normalization, so it took Encoder's default, IMAGENET (0.485/0.456/0.406, 0.229/0.224/0.225). timm publishes (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) for coatnet_rmlp_2_rw_384.sw_in12k_ft_in1k inside config.json's pretrained_cfg — the AugReg convention, HALF here. The arm ran 25 minutes of card on inputs centred a third of a standard deviation off in every channel.

WHAT IT WOULD HAVE COST. coatnet_hybrid is pre-registered with four branches and its FLAT branch closes the hierarchical row of the registry with three families measured. A mis-normalized trunk lands low, so the arm would very likely have read FLAT or REFUTES, and that reading would have been written into the ledger as a fact about a convolutional-prior-feeding-global-attention ARRANGEMENT when it was a fact about preprocessing. That is the faulty-PLUMBING row of the CLAUDE.md list exactly: a value recorded in a config while the consumer reads a constant.

WHAT CAUGHT IT. tests/integration/registry_to_checkpoints.py::test_every_encoder_states_its_own_constants, which refuses an entry that neither matches a published preprocessing document nor carries normalization_evidence prose. It did not run for two days because gates were red earlier in the chain (a god-file and a method mirror), so pytest was never reached. THAT is the real lesson: a blocking gate early in the session order hides every gate after it, and the arm was launched in that window.

THE CLASS. Encoder.normalization has a DEFAULT, and a default is what let this entry say nothing and be wrong. Every natural-image trunk here is ImageNet-normalized so the default was right eleven times, which is precisely how a twelfth silently inherits it. timm repositories are the exposed surface: they ship no preprocessor_config.json, so the published-document check cannot fire at all and only the evidence-prose rule stands between an entry and a default.

FIX SHIPPED: normalization=HALF plus normalization_evidence quoting the file, attempt 1's artefacts renamed _voidnorm (never deleted, never stitched — knee-gnzx), the arm relaunched 20:24Z, and the arm header now carries the void.

FOLLOW-ON WORTH DOING: make Encoder.normalization mandatory for any entry whose repository is a timm one, or drop the default entirely and make all twelve say ImageNet out loud. The second is more churn and strictly safer.

title: The rank loss was inert in sixteen arms - every batch-1 arm ran the plain recipe under a rank-loss name
description: experiments/recipe.sh sets RECIPE with --rank-weight 1.0. A pairwise term needs pairs, and --batch 1 forms none: --accumulate cannot repair it because it sums the gradients of micro-batch losses each computed alone. --pair-memory N is what supplies pairs across steps, and sixteen arms set --batch 1 without it: cnx_dense_448, cnx_distill_warm, cnx_mid_rate, cnx_own_recipe, cnx_top_rate, cnx_warm_anneal, radnet_family, raptor_feat_fit, raptor_feat_pre, swin_calib_dense, swin_distill_fit, swin_distill_pre, swin_open_half, swin_supervised, swin_toprate, swin_wholetop. That is the ENTIRE hierarchical-trunk family plus both raptor feature arms. Found because the trainer now REFUSES the combination outright and coatnet_hybrid died on it at smoke; fixed there with --pair-memory 15 = C(6,2) at --accumulate 6, by band_pairmem's own rule that 66 = C(12,2) matched --accumulate 12. WHAT THIS DOES NOT INVALIDATE: comparisons WITHIN the sixteen. They are mutually consistent - all sixteen ran the same plain recipe, so swin_supervised 0.8331 vs cnx_own_recipe 0.8186 vs swin_wholetop 0.8274 still order correctly against each other. WHAT IT DOES PUT IN DOUBT: the non-DINO deficit reading, which compares these sixteen against DINO arms run at batch 2 or higher where the term was at least partly live, and recipe.sh's own comment claiming --rank-weight is 'the only loss change positive in 3 of 3 matched arms' - name those three arms and check their batch size, because if any was batch 1 the claim is about nothing. Also check coatnet_hybrid's reading when it lands: it is the FIRST hierarchical arm with a live rank term, so it differs from swin_supervised in two variables, not one, and that is already stated in its header.

title: Arm a scoreable non-DINO conv member — the only heterogeneity seat this project could price
description:
Pool is near-homogeneous DINOv2/DINOv3 plus one foreign CoAtNet seat (raptor_v4_swa) that is 98.6% in-sample per foreign_overlap and therefore unpriceable offline. Kimi Q-EL: add exactly ONE non-DINO member, anything more is seating theatre. Q-EM answered: CoAtNet, gated on marginal contribution rather than on solo strength.

TRUNK CHOSEN AND PLUMBED 2026-09-04. coatnet_rmlp_2_rw_384.sw_in12k_ft_in1k, 72.9M, registered as variant coatnet2 through a new TimmMapWeights (timm answers forward_features and emits a map, so the CALL and the LAYOUT are both wrong; TimmTrunk fixes one, TrunkAsTokens.from_map the other). Measured through the registry entry: 16 TransformerBlock2d blocks across stages 2 and 3, so --unfreeze-last 6 opens 35.5M params INCLUDING both stage-3 blocks. That is the mechanism: Swin and ConvNeXtV2 both hold their longest block run below the widest stage, so every arm in those families froze the top, and swin_wholetop priced fixing that at -0.0057. CoAtNet reaches its own top by its own shape. 384 is the only legal read (448 raises a 784-vs-576 rel-pos mismatch, measured). 144 final tokens is not a handicap: the ledger 224 corner reads 256 tokens for native224 0.8502 against the 336 band 0.851, so this pipeline loses almost nothing per token dropped.

PRICE: ~2.2 h of card, on a card that is otherwise idle. P(clears the 0.0062 report floor as a priced seat into honest12) = 0.15. P(solo at or above swin_supervised 0.8331, the controlled comparison) = 0.35. Priced as an INSTRUMENT and a seat candidate, never as an improvement: seven board flats closed the seating axis and this does not re-open it. What it buys is the last untried arrangement on the trunk axis plus a reading on whether the frozen-top confound was ever the story. Arm: experiments/arms/coatnet_hybrid.sh. No Kaggle mount yet (Apache-2.0, upload deferred until a seat is earned).

title: focus_mcl_s2026 reads rank 0.0445 in seat_value against its roster line's 0.5332 solo
description: The whole-pool seat sweep (logs/pool_seat_sweep.log, 2026-09-04) classifies focus_mcl_s2026.pt DISTINCT at rank 0.0445, against a roster boundary of 0.8956 and against its own roster comment, which reads '0.5332 solo - and seated deliberately at that number'. 0.0445 is not merely weak, it is far below chance on a rank ruler, which is what an INVERTED prediction array looks like. The two numbers cannot both describe the same member, so one of them is wrong and it matters which: the member is on comp/members.roster, so it is shippable, and it was seated at eleven in at least one curve (experiments/README.md:5482). AUDIT FIRST, no fix proposed. Establish whether seat_value's rank column and the roster's solo number measure the same thing before touching anything - if they do, this is an inverted member sitting in the shippable pool; if they do not, the roster comment is quoting a ruler the sweep does not use and the sweep's own column needs a name that says so.
notes: RESOLVED, NOT A DEFECT, and the defect was my reading. seat_value prints 'focus_mcl_s2026.pt: nearest 0.0445  mean 0.0319  solo 0.5332' -- nearest/mean are rank DISTANCE columns, and the member's solo AUC is printed on the same line. Recomputed independently from the holdout npz: per-label AUC 0.671 0.735 0.674 0.355 0.674 0.424 0.400 0.313 0.434 0.626 0.642 0.450, mean 0.5332, which matches the roster line exactly. No inverted member exists. Its actual seat value against honest12 is -0.0002 [-0.0011, +0.0008], a straddle of zero. What IS real: the checkpoint is from epoch 2 and five of twelve labels sit below 0.5, so it is a coin-flip member seated for distance. See the follow-on bead on the output's column naming.

title: The champion's seats cannot be priced: 5 of raptorweight_v1's 6 members are fold -1
description:
seat_value refuses on our own champion:

  NO SEAT VALUE against raptorweight_v1: 1 of 6 members carry a holdout record, and pricing a marginal contribution needs at least 2
  unscoreable (fold -1, they have seen every holdout study): calib_span_ff, final_ws_cf, grade_ladder_cf, lr4e-5_ws_cf, through_dense_cf

raptorweight_v1 is the entry comp/champion.json pins at 0.944, and five of its six members were trained with --fold -1, so they have seen every holdout study. No marginal contribution can be computed for any seat in the entry that is currently defining the project's best result.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING. Every reading of the form 'this member is worth a seat' or 'the member axis is closed' is made against entries we CAN score. The champion is not one of them. So the seven board flats that closed the member axis were measured on scoreable entries, and the champion sits outside that evidence rather than inside it. We do not know which of its seats carry it.

It also means the fallback seat_value itself suggests -- --against honest12 (0.937, 12 members) -- prices seats in a DIFFERENT entry 0.007 below the champion, and any conclusion transferred from there to the champion is an assumption, not a measurement.

NOT PROPOSING A FIX YET. Retraining five members on a real fold is 10+ hours of card and would produce different checkpoints, not the champion's. The cheaper question is whether a held-out slice exists that none of the five saw, or whether the champion has to be re-derived from scoreable members before any seat claim about it is allowed. Audit first.

title: The trunk-family lever in the standing wake prompt is already closed by its own pre-registered gate
description:
Every wake carries a standing constraint naming the trunk-family arm (RadImageNet DenseNet first, supervised ImageNet VGG/ResNet second) as 'the only open lever that could plausibly deliver 1.5%'. The ledger refutes all three parts of that.

1. RadImageNet DenseNet-121 ALREADY RAN. 'radnet_family' peaked at 0.6716 and experiments/README.md line 6656 records it as closing the convolutional trunk lane EMPTY.
2. The BN-pinned follow-up ALREADY RAN. 'radnet_pinned' reads 0.7505 (+0.0789 over radnet_family, so the BatchNorm defect was real and is now priced) but still a full point below the incumbents.
3. The supervised-ImageNet VGG-16 / ResNet-50 arm is EXPLICITLY GATED OFF by radnet_pinned's own pre-registration: 'at < ~0.80 the supervised-ImageNet VGG-16 / ResNet-50 arm is NOT queued', on NVIDIA's IJCAI-ECAI 2022 result that a branch more than ~5 points off the incumbents measures as diverse and still ensembles worse. 0.7505 < 0.80, so the gate fired against it.
4. RadImageNet is NOT SHIPPABLE anyway. backbone.py line 406 records the mount withdrawn 2026-09-02: the weights are request-gated and the MIT reading off the Lab-Rasool re-host does not hold.

So queueing that arm would repeat a known result AND override a gate that was pre-registered precisely to stop it. Caught by auditing the ledger before re-arming the card chain, which is the rule that exists for this.

What it does license, card-free, is the per-case error correlation between radnet_pinned and the mean ViT incumbent -- the only measurement that could re-open the CNN axis. knee-cj40f.

ACTION: the standing wake prompt needs this lever struck and replaced with a lever that is actually open.
notes: 2026-09-05T19:52Z. The wake prompt names the TRUNK-FAMILY arm (RadImageNet DenseNet first, supervised ImageNet VGG/ResNet second) as the only open lever that could plausibly deliver 1.5 percent. It is CLOSED and was closed card-free the same day. radnet_pinned against honest12: both CNNs read DISTINCT on all three axes at once, rank 0.4394 and 0.6415 against a roster boundary of 0.8956, js 0.025-0.026 against 0.0150, maha 4.87-4.97 against 4.319, which makes radnet_family the most distinct member measured here. Seat value minus 0.0004 and minus 0.0009 added, minus 0.0001 as best swap, 0 of 2 clearing the plus 0.0040 line. Maximal distinctness, negative seat. Ledger: The CNN axis closed on its own named re-opener, card-free. The DenseNet half is separately unshippable anyway, weights request-gated at source, mirror deleted, mount_check refuses by design. The supervised ImageNet VGG-16 / ResNet-50 arm stays unqueued and the lane costs no further card on either argument. Substituted lever for the card: band_deep224, the depth re-run at 224 px against band224 0.8529, readable now that Landed witnesses encoder_top_rate.

title: arm_check does not refuse an arm that has ALREADY RUN — it cost a window and nearly 4h of card
description:
On 2026-09-04 a whole session armed, priced, pre-registered, smoked and QUEUED errors_dense on the belief that it had never run. It ran 2026-09-02 07:57 and completed twelve of twelve epochs: D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/experiments/errors_dense_s2026.full.log, checkpoint errors_dense_s2026.pt, metrics jsonl, and the log ends with 'ARM DONE errors_dense'. The watcher chain had it queued behind band_pairmem and would have re-run it for ~4h. It was caught only because a routine ls of the experiments directory happened to show the log, minutes before band_pairmem finished.

EVERY GATE WAS GREEN. arm_check --only errors_dense reported '1 checked, 0 refused, 0 uncached' and even ran a 60-study smoke. arm_check asks whether an arm CAN run; nothing asks whether it ALREADY DID. ledger_check does see unrecorded runs, but it runs AFTER arms finish and nothing chains it to arming. queue_check reports what a watcher owes, not whether the owed thing is already done.

WHY THE HUMAN CHECK FAILED TOO: CLAUDE.md says 'Folds and seeds are banned. Do not repeat experiments whose result is known' and 'READ THE LEDGER before filing a finding' — and errors_dense has NO ledger row, so reading the ledger actively CONFIRMED the wrong belief. The absence of a row was read as evidence the arm had not run, when it was evidence the arm was unrecorded. That is the same shape as the ledger_check finding it was built for.

THE FIX: arm_check refuses (or at minimum loudly warns) when an arm's --out checkpoint, its metrics jsonl, or a '<arm>.full.log' containing 'ARM DONE <arm>' already exists on disk. A deliberate re-run needs an --anyway '<why>' the way submit_check does, and that why belongs in the arm's header. The disk is the authority here, exactly as card_check asks the DEVICE rather than argv and mount_check --live asks Kaggle.

SECOND-ORDER COST: the belief was carried into a letter to Kimi (2026-09-04T1535Z) that CORRECTED their correct statement that pruning loses. That letter has to be retracted.

title: Prune by the RANKING at a small budget — cleanlab's own mask is the wrong selector for our defect (1.63x, not 4.05x)
description: errors_dense pruned all 5,360 flags (10.14% of read cells) and cost -0.0158 vs band_dense. The gate measured precision 0.640 at budget 25 (4.05x random) decaying to 2.15x by budget 200, so at a 10.14% budget the flagged set is dominated by hard-but-correct cells rather than mislabelled ones, and those carry the corpus highest gradients (the prune cost 3.4x what removing the same volume of random supervision costs). THE ARM: the same --label-errors path with the flag table truncated to the top-N by confident-joint rank, N ~500 (about 1 percent of read cells) where measured precision is still well above base rate. PRICE, and it is why this is P2: the upside is BOUNDED BY N. Removing ~500 genuinely-wrong cells out of 52,872 cannot plausibly move a mean AUC by the 0.0062 floor, let alone 1.5 percent. P(clears the floor) ~0.08. Costs ~4h card. Worth running only as an INSTRUMENT separating 'the treatment is wrong' from 'the budget is wrong', and only AFTER knee-f8hv5 (re-label) reads, because re-label subsumes it. Do not queue it ahead of f8hv5.
notes: PRICE, stated 2026-09-05 for arm rank966_hold. COST: 90 min card, twelve epochs at 336 px / 20 slices, plus ~4 min of CPU for the gold read. GAIN: 966 pruned cells are 1.8 percent of the 52,872 supervision cells; at the ranking selector precision of about 0.65 that is roughly 630 genuinely-wrong cells removed. Mechanism plausibly delivers 0.005-0.015 of gold AUC, so P(clears the 1.5 percent bar) is about 0.15. IT IS NOT SOLD AS AN IMPROVEMENT. It is an INSTRUMENT: errors_dense refuted PRUNE-at-the-confident-joint-mask-at-5360-cells, and that single point is currently carrying the whole label axis. This arm separates SELECTOR (ranking vs mask) from BUDGET (966 vs 5360) from TREATMENT (prune vs relabel, which relabel_hold tests) from RULER (gold vs the proxy that scored errors_dense). Under every branch it constrains what relabel_hold result is allowed to mean, which is the justification for the 90 minutes.

title: Re-label the flagged cells to the pool's held-out posterior, instead of pruning them (errors_dense's pair)
description:
THE PAIR TO knee-teh4, AND THE HEAD-TO-HEAD THE LITERATURE DOES NOT HAVE. A-QEB (Kimi, 2026-09-04, research/2026-09-04_qeb-label-noise-treatment-literature.md) searched for a published comparison of prune vs re-label vs down-weight under ONE detector in multi-label medical classification and returned an honest null: cleanlab (Northcutt JAIR 2021) is pruning-first and never compares the same detected set under re-labelling; BoMD (Chen, ICCV 2023) detects AND smoothly re-labels chest X-ray but is not an ablation; TLCM (Ghiassi, ACML 2023) is loss correction, not a treatment comparison. So the comparison is ours to make, and making it needs BOTH arms measured - which is why errors_dense (prune) still runs first rather than being skipped to the favourite.

WHY RE-LABEL IS THE FAVOURITE, with citations rather than taste. Meta Label Correction (Zheng, AAAI 2021) Figure 5: reweighting degrades significantly as noise rises while correction-based methods stay robust. Distilling Effective Supervision from Severe Label Noise (Zhang, CVPR 2020): meta re-labelling is very effective at high noise ratios and comparable at low ones. Nodet, Recovering by Relabelling (IAL 2021) gives the mechanism - a corrected sample contributes a full gradient, a down-weighted one contributes little. Our flag rate is 10.138% of read cells (5,360 of 52,872) with a gold-observed pooled error rate around 20.8%, which sits on the re-labelling side of that evidence. NOTE that no published CROSSOVER threshold exists; the '5-10%' rule Kimi looked for is folklore, not a cited result, and is not to be quoted as one.

AND WHY PRUNING MAY LOSE ON OUR SHAPE SPECIFICALLY. BoMD warns explicitly that sample selection under multi-label imbalance returns an extremely imbalanced clean set dominated by the no-findings class; TLCM reports corruption-matrix estimation failing on unbalanced label distributions. That is exactly errors_dense's pre-registered worst-case branch: a report-derived positive the models disbelieve may still be enriched for the finding, and Fracture, MCL and Synovitis carry 53% of holdout variance. Both arms therefore report PER-LABEL rows before any macro, those three first.

THE PLUMBING ALREADY EXISTS AND NEEDS NO TRAINING CODE. Supervision.unread (core/data/labels/targets.py:185) takes a (StudyInstanceUID, target, value) table that replaces a cell's SCORE and deliberately leaves its WEIGHT untouched, so the experiment stays one variable wide; Supervision.taught() reads it, drops rows for studies an arm's subset does not carry, and moves_the_ruler() already returns True for it. kneemri/evaluation/unread_teacher.py already writes such a table from PublishedRuler's twenty out-of-fold checkpoints. This arm is a new CELL SET for that machinery plus a table, not a new path.

THE ONE DESIGN DECISION, AND IT IS NOT INHERITED. unread_teacher is deliberately MEAN-PRESERVING inside each finding's UNK block: it adds ORDER without moving the marginal, because the UNK constant is the level the reader emits for silence and a prevalence shift is the one thing a twelve-head trunk transmits between heads. THAT PROPERTY MUST NOT BE COPIED HERE. Our flagged cells are confident FALSE POSITIVES - 108 against 32 misses on the gold 58 - so the whole content of the treatment is that their value should come DOWN. A mean-preserving override on this cell set would re-rank the cells while asserting the reader's marginal is right, which is the claim under test. The override is therefore genuinely value-lowering, and the prevalence shift it causes is a REAL second effect that has to be reported rather than designed away: state the per-finding positive-rate change the table causes before quoting any score.

READ IT ON THE PLAIN RULER. unread moves 5,360 VALUES, so a ruler read from the same file would rank against scores the member was just fitted toward. Pin --eval-labels, exactly as calib_span had to.

PRICE: ~4 h of card, 0 slots; the table costs minutes of I/O and no card, same as the flag table did. Runs only after errors_dense reads, because its value is the CONTRAST and a lone re-label arm answers a weaker question. P(clears the 0.0062 holdout floor over band_dense 0.8578, i.e. >= 0.8640) ~0.35, same as its pair - the literature moves the ORDER of the two treatments, not the size of the effect either can have here. Board transfer is UNKNOWN; no transfer number is to be invented for it.

Blocked on: knee-teh4 reading.
notes: CLOSED FLAT 2026-09-05. errors_relabel 0.8522 @ e6 vs band_dense 0.8578, MEAN -0.0056, inside its own pre-registered FLAT band (0.8578 > s >= 0.8516) by 0.0006. Twelve of twelve epochs, convergence_check clean, per-label spread -0.0250 to +0.0093 against half-widths up to +/-0.0310. Plumbing verified BEFORE the score: recipe carries unread_targets=relabel_rank1932_a06.csv and the table holds exactly 1932 rows. The null is quantitative rather than mysterious - 1932 cells is 3.65 percent of 52872 read cells, at precision 0.720 that is about 1391 corrected and 541 corrupted for a net +850 cells, and the gold panel's 140-of-684 rate puts about 10840 wrong cells in the corpus, so the arm fixed 7.8 percent of the defect. A treatment reaching under a tenth of the noise landing inside the noise floor is what the model predicts. Ledger row written, reading_check clean.

title: Pillar-0 was fine-tuned ON the competition train set — no offline read of it is honest on our studies
description: A-DV quotes the archive README: the checkpoint is 'a full fine-tune of the Pillar-0 BreastMRI foundation model on knee MRI from the RSNA 2026 Knee Abnormality Detection competition', with 'the 58 holdout studies were excluded from training'. A-DX says no split artefact exists, so the 909 read stays cancelled - but the 58 annotated studies price the MEMBER as well as the feed once our side is held-annotation members. holdannot 0.8932 / recal_holdannot 0.9037 against pillar0 0.7853: -0.1079, interval [-0.1476,-0.0700], clears. title: Pillar-0 feed is intact: -0.012 against published, so the 909-study holdout read is licensed

The per-label profile tracks their table label-for-label (Effusion highest 0.949 vs 0.965, MCL lowest 0.651 vs 0.630, ACL 0.756 vs 0.773, Bakers 0.846 vs 0.842), which independently confirms the PILLAR_LABELS head-permutation transcription at no extra forward. That is what foreign_gate exists to license: the shortfall is small enough that a 909-study read measures the MODEL, not our plumbing. Feed choice for that read is 336px_12sl -- it is the best of the three and the cheapest. Depth 12->20 is -0.004, i.e. nothing; do not spend card on the depth axis. NOTE the published 0.797 is below every lane ceiling this project owns, so this member is not seated on its own number -- it is the architecture-monoculture escape (one 3D trunk over a whole series, no per-slice step, no fusion operator), and the question is what it does to an ENSEMBLE, per knee-tl2ut.

What does NOT stand is the conclusion. title: Pillar-0 feed shortfall is the CROP, per-label profile says so
description: pillar0 through 336px_20sl reads macro 0.6532 against a published 0.7970 (-0.1438). The per-label profile confirms the head permutation is identity -- Effusion .965->.938, Baker's .842->.851, ACL .773->.754, PF OA .758->.801 all land within noise. The collapse is confined to peripheral-compartment findings: Lateral Meniscus .781->.367, Lateral OA .774->.487, Fracture .775->.483, Synovitis .821->.520, MCL .630->.506, Medial OA .941->.767. Their adapter reads the WHOLE uncropped series; ours is a 130mm crop of 12-20 slices resampled to depth 192. The ledger corroborates the mechanism independently: crop80_span at 80mm lost MCL -0.0265 and ACL -0.0263, the same peripheral signature on our own DINOv2 members. Instrument: an uncropped 40-slice 384px cache over the gold 58 only (--only-studies, 1.7GB), re-gated. If the macro recovers toward 0.797 the feed is proven and a corpus-wide build is licensed; if it does not, the shortfall is the model or the depth interpolation and the member is not worth card.
close_reason: WRONG, and wrong because the ruler was broken. Every reading it was built on came from a member whose head was fed UNNORMALISED trunk features (norm ~72 against head weights of absmax 0.39), so every per-series sigmoid saturated to exactly 0.0/1.0 and every AUC was computed over massive ties -- which is why three feeds differing in crop, depth AND resolution returned bit-identical numbers on four findings. Fixed by L2-normalising in PillarMember.embedding. Re-gated, the claim INVERTS: uncropped 384px_40sl is the WORST feed at 0.7685, the cropped 336px feeds read 0.7810 (20sl) and 0.7853 (12sl), and MCL -- the finding the crop hypothesis rested on -- FALLS 0.651 -> 0.562 when the crop is removed. The crop helps. Superseded by knee-tl2ut.

title: Pillar-0 as a foreign seat: the only maximally-distant checkpoint that is already fine-tuned on this task
description:
A-DU (2026-09-04) found fabotelli/pillar0-knee-finetune (Kaggle Model, atlas-336-2ep/1): a Pillar-0 BreastMRI 3D foundation model FINE-TUNED ON RSNA KNEE, gold-58 macro-AUC 0.797, Educational Community License 2.0 quoted from the artefact LICENSE. Decode: uint8 [D,256,256] -> z-score -> trilinear to [192,384,384] -> channel-replicate x3 -> visual encoder -> Linear(1152->12).

WHY THIS AND NOT THE REST OF THE CENSUS. Everything else A-DU listed is already worked or already priced: dreaddevelopment/raptor-knee-arms ships TODAY as fleettwo's eighth seat (raptor_ft_effv2l480), and comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:2664 prices cnv2b336/cnn336 out explicitly. The DINOv2/DINOv3 entries are siblings of our own monoculture. Pillar-0 is the only artefact on the list whose ARCHITECTURE, PRETRAINING MODALITY and STACK CONSUMPTION all differ from every seated member at once, and it needs NO CARD TIME because it is already fitted.

MECHANISM. The champion's own pin names the plateau: the pool is an architecture monoculture. The one non-DINOv2 seat this project ever added (raptor_v4_swa) moved the board 0.941 -> 0.943. A true-3D trunk is further from a 2D per-slice reader than a CoAtNet is.

WHAT A-DS DOES NOT SAY. A-DS closed the 3D family on published evidence that 2D >= 3D for CLASSIFICATION, and on the ABSENCE of any measured error correlation between a volumetric and a slice-pooled reader. Neither argument touches a free, already-fitted member seated for DIVERSITY, and this checkpoint is exactly the cheap instrument A-DS named as the way to re-open the family ('a measured error correlation between a cheap 3D member and our best 2D member').

PRICE: ~2 h of engineering for the decode, 0 h of card to fit, ~20 min of card to score. Gain if it seats like raptor_v4_swa did: +0.002 board. P(clears the 0.0062 holdout floor as a seat) ~ 0.3, P(any positive) ~ 0.55.

BLOCKER TO RESOLVE FIRST: like every raptor arm it is --fold -1 by construction, so it has no offline quality we can measure and its 0.797 may be in-sample. foreign_overlap is the tool. Q-DV asks Kimi for the licence text and the overlap.
notes:
PRICE CORRECTED 2026-09-04, downward, against this project's own precedent. My first pricing leaned on raptor_v4_swa (0.941 -> 0.943) and ignored the SECOND foreign seat: kneemri-fleettwo seated raptor_ft_effv2l480, chosen as the most isolated of thirteen raptor arms (nearest-neighbour agreement 0.8223), and comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:2664 records the axis as reading 'no further slot widening it'. So the distance-seat mechanism is 1 hit, 1 miss — and the miss was a member at 0.8716 solo. Pillar-0 is MORE distant and much WEAKER (0.797 macro). Distance alone did not pay at 0.8716; there is no reason it pays at 0.797. P(clears the floor as a FLAT seat) revised 0.3 -> 0.12.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. The artefact's per-label profile is inverted relative to ours: Effusion 0.965 and Medial OA 0.941 against a 0.797 macro, with MCL 0.630 and the ligament/meniscus column weakest ('Ligament/meniscus fine structure is where the domain gap concentrates', README). Our pool is strong where it is weak. A PER-LABEL seat -- weighting the foreign member only on the columns where it leads -- is not the flat-rank blend that effv2l480 was tested under, and Vote.ranks has never been given a per-label foreign weight. That is the version worth building.

CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE DROPPED: those column numbers are on 58 studies. A per-label AUC at n=58 has a CI wide enough to swallow the whole effect, so the 0.965 is a REASON TO MEASURE, never a number to plan on. The measurement is on OUR holdout, not theirs.

LICENCE AND OVERLAP, BOTH SETTLED (A-DV plus the artefact read directly): ECL-2.0 is Apache-2.0 with a narrowed patent grant, no NC clause, no competition restriction, consistent between the packaged LICENSE and upstream YalaLab/Pillar0-BreastMRI. Kaggle's 'Other' is a missing dropdown option, not a conflict. The split is declared in prose -- 'The 58 holdout studies were excluded from training' -- but there is NO machine-readable split in the checkpoint (keys are only model/head/ep). Same claim structure as raptor_v4_swa, whose 0.8938 was voided at 98.6% foreign_overlap. So the exclusion gets measured, not believed.

BUILD STATE. Checkpoint pulled to D:/models/foreign/pillar0 (333 MB, LICENSE + README + pillar_ft_a.final.pt). external/pillar-pretrain cloned at pinned commit ab06083 (gitignored per CLAUDE.md). Architecture resolved from tensor shapes and matches the repo's shipped Atlas config exactly -- dim 384, depth 8, num_scales 3, stages [2,2,8], embed_dim 1152 = 3 scales x 384 -- differing only in the modality: patch_embeds.breast_mr.conv_down.0.weight is (64,3,3,3,3), i.e. Conv3d(in_chans=3, 64, k=3), which is the README's channel-replicate x3. The class is miniclip.multimodal_atlas.MultiModalAtlas; the checkpoint's text tower is dead weight for us and is dropped.

title: band_pairmem: price the batch-1 pair-memory substitution on the small trunk, so every ViT-L row at 336/20 becomes readable
description: Every ViT-L number at the shipped operating point carries --batch 1 --accumulate 12 --pair-memory 66, because --batch 12 there prices 106144 MiB against a 32 GB card. The substitution's cost has never been measured at any trunk size, and it sits under ortho_stack, v3large_stack and every comparison drawn from them (knee-4joaj). band_pairmem.sh is band_dense's exact flag set plus the substitution, on the SMALL trunk where both sides can exist. notes: PRICE: band_dense's 12-epoch recipe at batch 1 rather than 12 on the 22M dinov2-small trunk. band_dense's own epoch cost is the reference; batch 1 with accumulate 12 holds the effective batch and the optimiser path, so the budget is one band_dense run, ~40-60 min. P(clears the 1.5% bar as an improvement) ~0.02 — its own pre-registration predicts a member NO BETTER than band_dense, so it scores ~0 as a gain. It is bought as an INSTRUMENT: it prices a confound that sits under four ledger rows (ortho_stack, v3large_stack, ortho_dense, v3large_dense as read against band_dense) and under every future ViT-L row at 336/20, because an un-handicapped ViT-L there prices 106144 MiB against a 32 GB card and can never be run. title: band_dense is the SMALL trunk, not v3large - ortho_stack and v3large_stack both name it as a matched control and it is not one
description: experiments/arms/ortho_stack.sh:157 and v3large_stack.sh both declare 'control band_dense = 0.8578 ... identical flags with the incumbent trunk', and experiments/README.md's ortho_stack table called band_dense's trunk 'v3large (incumbent)'. Read from the checkpoint config instead of the prose, band_dense_s2026 carries variant=small and pair_memory=0: band_dense.sh passes no --variant and options.py:186 defaults it to SMALL. So ortho_stack - band_dense = -0.0161 and v3large_stack - band_dense = -0.0301 each move the TRUNK SIZE and the pair mechanism together, and neither prices what its header says it prices. The only matched contrasts in the family are ortho_stack - v3large_stack = +0.0140 and ortho_dense - v3large_dense = +0.0194, both of which stand. Ledger corrected 2026-09-04; the two arm headers still carry the wrong line. Note the un-handicapped ViT-L row is not merely unrun but unrunnable at this geometry - ortho_stack.sh:38 prices --batch 12 at 106144 MiB against a 32 GB card - so the handicap cannot be removed, only measured, which is what band_pairmem does.

SWEEP DONE 2026-09-04. Two headers read band_dense as a control it is not.

1. vjepa_member.sh:38 said 'band_dense = 0.8578 (DINOv2-base, ...)'. band_dense is DINOv2-SMALL, ViT-S/14, 22M — established in the ledger's ortho_stack entry. The arm is a ViT-L, so the header understated the capacity gap it was reading across. FIXED.

2. ortho_stack.sh:33 called base224 -> band_dense 'the same unit step ... on the ViT-B (0.8509 -> 0.8578, +0.0069)'. base224 is DINOv2-BASE and band_dense is DINOv2-SMALL, so that +0.0069 crosses the trunk as well as the geometry and is not a clean unit price for the recipe move. FIXED.

NEGATIVE RESULT, and it is the useful half: 42 arms name band_dense = 0.8578 as a control and the other 40 are clean. Of the arms running a different-capacity trunk against it, base_dense.sh:49 states 'byte-identical recipe on dinov2-small' explicitly (correct), cnx_dense/cnx_dense_448/cnx_own_recipe are cross-FAMILY by thesis and say so, and cnx_own_recipe.sh:55 names both band_dense and base_dense side by side. title: Knee continuation pays ~+0.015-0.020 twice, but only at ViT-L where SIZE costs more than continuation buys: run it at ViT-B
description:
THE 2x2 IS ALMOST COMPLETE, and read as a grid it says something neither arm said alone.

  recipe \ trunk    ViT-B (v3base)   ViT-L (v3large)   ViT-L knee-continued (ortholarge)
  dense 224/12       -                0.8258            0.8452   (+0.0194 continuation)
  stack (band_dense) 0.8578           RUNNING           0.8417   (v3large_stack ep7 0.8269, 1.9h left)

TWO INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS OF THE CONTINUATION, same sign and size: the dense pair reads +0.0194, and
the frozen probe re-read at each trunk's own ridge penalty (knee-x4yx) reads +0.0203. That is not in
question.

WHAT IS IN QUESTION IS THE SIZE. Both ViT-Ls sit BELOW the ViT-B on the shipped recipe -- ortho_stack
0.8417 against band_dense 0.8578, and v3large_stack is tracking below ortho_stack at the same epoch. If
it peaks where it is heading, the grid says: continuation is worth ~+0.015 at ViT-L, and ViT-L is worth
about -0.016 against ViT-B on this data at this recipe. The two nearly cancel, which is exactly why
ortho_stack read as a null against band_dense and why reading that single number as 'the trunk lane is
closed' would have been wrong.

THE CELL NOBODY HAS RUN is knee continuation at BASE size -- the trunk size that actually wins here. If
the +0.015-0.020 is a property of the continuation rather than of the checkpoint, band_dense + a knee
continuation lands near 0.873 against the 0.8578 incumbent. The target needs +0.0175 offline on the best
member (holdfive_v1 anchor, +0.97 board points per holdout point at the shipping band). This is the only

IT ALSO DODGES knee-nxthh. OrthoFoundation-L is fastMRI-derived and its shipping licence is unadjudicated,
so every ortho number is currently an instrument. A continuation WE run on data we hold has no such

BLOCKED ON: (a) v3large_stack converging -- it prices the size term, and without it the grid has a hole;
(b) what corpus the continuation runs on, and whether that corpus is shippable (fastMRI is closed for
shipping under our own DSA reading; MRNet, our own unlabelled RSNA slices and SKM-TEA are not);
(c) a wall-clock price for an SSL continuation run, which nothing in the ledger has ever paid.

DO NOT ARM until (a) lands and (c) is written down. The failure mode this bead exists to prevent is

title: kneemri-orthorehearse is REFUSED by mount_check — it names ortho_dense_s2026 and the all_ours package does not carry it
description:
mount_check --live on 2026-09-04: 90 ok, 5 skipped, 1 REFUSED. The refusal is kneemri-orthorehearse, which asks for ['ortho_dense_s2026'] against a D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/all_ours package holding 118 members, none of them any ortho_* checkpoint.

This is the knee-nbk3 shape one step earlier. KernelRun DROPS a member whose encoder it cannot mount and keeps going, so had this kernel been submitted it would have produced a COMPLETE run, a real submission.csv, a score, and a board row under a name for an entry that was never assembled — which is exactly how farseat_v1 shipped six of seven named members and had its flat read as closing the cross-family ensemble-diversity axis for five days.

It did not ship, because mount_check refuses one step ahead of the slot. That is the check working, and the finding is that the defect existed at all.

TWO POSSIBLE FIXES and they are not equivalent: either the all_ours package is stale and ortho_dense_s2026 belongs in it (in which case every OTHER kernel naming an ortho member is in the same state and the census is the work), or orthorehearse names a member that was never packaged and the kernel's chosen tuple is wrong. Determine which BEFORE repackaging — repacking to satisfy one kernel is the fix that hides the census.

No slot is blocked by this today; the 09:37Z mark is kneemri-holdsolo, which is among the 90 ok.

title: MedSAM read-out point: neck (256d) or raw ViT tokens (768d)
description: sam_trunk returns SamModel.vision_encoder, whose forward ends in the 256-channel neck built for the mask decoder. Three published results argue the neck is the wrong read-out for classification: SAMantics (arXiv:2411.15288) linear-probes SAM's neck output at 11.1 percent ImageNet top-1 against DINOv2's 77.4; FODA-PG (arXiv:2409.03947) drops the MedSAM neck explicitly to read patch embeddings for a medical task; the neck is a 3x compression with no decoder here to serve. Against that, MedSAM's paper says the fine-tune updated ALL image-encoder parameters and publishes no layer-wise breakdown, so a neck-concentrated adaptation would make raw tokens discard what makes the checkpoint medical. kneemri.models.sam_drift measures that directly against facebook/sam-vit-base, card-free. Decide the read-out on its ratio before any medsam arm is queued. See research/2026-09-04_sam-neck-vs-raw-tokens-for-classification.md

title: Nine members' input caches are gone from disk, the roster head among them, and nothing recorded it
description: roster_check on 2026-09-04 reports nine scoreable members whose input cache .npy is no longer on disk: res392_ws_s2026 and intensity392_ws_s2026 (images_448px_12sl.npy), extended_ws_s2026, band140_s2026, band_full_s2026, band_wide_s2026, crop80_span_s2026, crop80_tissue_s2026, adjacent224_s2026. The checkpoints survive. The caches do not, so none of those members can be re-scored, re-derived or WITNESSED offline. res392_ws_s2026 is the best single member this project has produced (0.8523) and the head of comp/members.roster; intensity392_ws_s2026 and crop80_tissue_s2026 are also rostered, and crop80_tissue is the only physically different crop in the pool. THE MECHANISM IS DISK PRESSURE, not a bug in any tool. D:/data is at 96 percent, 181G free of 3.7T. The caches are the largest deletable objects there and something reclaimed them. Nothing wrote it down, which is the actual defect: an asset was destroyed and the only record is a check that has to be re-run to notice. WHY IT IS P1 RATHER THAN HOUSEKEEPING. witness_check is a pre-submission gate and it needs the offline cache. A rostered member that cannot be witnessed cannot be shipped safely, so the roster now names members the shipping path cannot clear, and the failure surfaces at the slot rather than before it. That is the same shape as the mount_check and run_check families: green everywhere a human looks, wrong at the moment it costs a slot. It also closes off re-reading the resolution axis without rebuilding a cache the ledger prices at about 99GB, against 181G free. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. Serving on Kaggle decodes from the competition data inside the kernel and does not read our cache, so this is not evidence that any shipped entry is broken. The claim is narrower: those nine cannot be verified offline any more. WORK: 1. roster_check should FAIL on a rostered member whose cache is gone, not merely print it, since that is a shipping defect and not a note. 2. Decide per member whether to rebuild the cache or move it to declines with this as the reason. 3. Record current free space and a floor under it, so the next reclaim names what it is destroying.

  extended_ws_s2026      0.0156  of 0.0312

title: radnet_family 0.6716 is a fine-tuning failure with a 0.8197 frozen witness, and it closed a lane
description:
THE ANOMALY. radnet121 frozen probe scores 0.8197. The same trunk fine-tuned (radnet_family_s2026) peaks 0.6716 at epoch 6 of 12 and ends 0.6586. Fine-tuning cost 0.148 against its own frozen features. Every other trunk on this registry GAINS from fitting. A 12-epoch run that ends below its own linear probe is a broken fit, not a family verdict - and 0.6716 is the number written into comp/members.declines that closed the trunk-ARCHITECTURE-family lane, which the loop policy still lists as CLOSED.

IT IS NOT THE SILENCED RANKING TERM. knee-tj88y prices that term at ~+0.010 asymptotic. 0.6716 against a family floor of 0.83 is fifteen times that. Different defect.

IT IS NOT BATCH-1 BATCHNORM EITHER - checked and refuted. model.slice_features flattens b*s*g into the encoder batch, so at --whole-stack --slices 20 every BatchNorm sees ~20 samples per forward, not 1. Recorded so nobody re-derives it.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED. RadImageNet DenseNet-121 is the ONLY BatchNorm trunk this project has ever fitted; every incumbent (DINOv2/v3, ConvNeXtV2, V-JEPA2, Swin, ViT) is LayerNorm, which is batch-size and statistics invariant. There is NO BatchNorm handling anywhere in kneemri/training/ or kneemri/models/: no track_running_stats, no norm-layer eval(), no momentum override. The only .eval() on the training path is trainer.py:639, the validation switch.

SO THE ARM'S OWN NORMALIZATION ARGUMENT IS FALSE AS WRITTEN. radnet_family.sh reasons that norm0 sits inside the frozen prefix at --unfreeze-last 6 'so its running statistics cannot adapt to a wrong input scale', and picks the input scale by which candidate lands nearest the unit distribution those statistics encode. Freezing sets requires_grad=False; BatchNorm running_mean/running_var are BUFFERS and keep updating in train mode regardless. The premise the input-scale measurement rests on is contradicted by the code. That does not by itself explain -0.148, and it may even argue the wrong scale would have been absorbed - but the selection procedure was decided on a property the trunk does not have.

REMAINING CANDIDATES, unranked: learning rate inherited from a recipe tuned for 86-88M ViTs applied to a 7M DenseNet (the classic frozen-beats-fitted signature); running-stat drift across a frozen prefix whose weights cannot follow; the unfreeze depth meaning something different in a densely-connected trunk than in a block-stacked one.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT LICENCE. It re-opens the DECISION to close the lane, not the member. Frozen is 0.8197, the seat bar is 0.8459 and the best solo on disk is 0.8642; a repaired fit that gains the usual 0.02-0.04 over frozen lands near 0.85, so this is very likely correctness debt rather than a rescued member - the same shape as knee-tj88y. Do NOT spend the card on it ahead of a lever that could plausibly reach a better member. What it costs is the honesty of the CLOSED list: the medical-supervised pretraining cell is recorded as measured-and-empty when it was never measured.
notes: STRENGTHENED 2026-09-04 by the frozen-probe seat table (ledger, same date). radnet121@focal-max is not merely a good frozen witness in isolation - priced against the champion twelve it is the BEST of all ten cached trunks (+0.0016 seat, band [+0.0009,+0.0023]), ahead of ortholarge, vjepa2-large and both dinov2-large readouts. So the trunk whose FITTED member reads 0.6716 carries the most seat-relevant frozen signal we have measured. That is a fine-tuning failure with an independent witness at the ENSEMBLE level, not just the solo one, and it makes radnet_pinned (queued behind v3large_stack) a mechanism arm rather than a retry.

title: the full-fit +0.006 is not a constant: 0.953 chain needs rewriting
description:
Kimi's Q-CZ reply (outside view, Hestness 2017 power-law scaling; Mohr 2024 learning curves; Cawley-Talbot 2010 selection optimism; Breiman 1996 / Caruana 2004 on ensemble variance): the full-fit board term is the vertical gap between two points on a CONCAVE learning curve, not a portable constant. It should shrink with (i) pool quality, (ii) ensemble size - averaging has already absorbed part of the variance that more data reduces - and (iii) recipe convergence. Some of the measured +0.006 is also not data at all: _ff checkpoints differ in stopping/annealing from _s2026, and the seats were selected on the same holdout they are refit against. Planning number at an honest 0.945: +0.002 to +0.004.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE 0.953 PATH. It was: fleet moves honest ensemble 0.8751 -> 0.885, x0.97 transfer = +0.010 -> 0.947, then full-fit +0.006 -> 0.953. At +0.002-0.004 that lands 0.949-0.951 and MISSES. The fleet must carry ~0.888-0.890 honest offline rather than 0.885, or another lever must be found.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TONIGHT'S PAIR (foldfour/fitfour, 4 seats). Four seats and a weaker pool is exactly where the concave model says the term is LARGEST, so the pair's delta is an UPPER BOUND on the term at the champion's seven seats. Asymmetric instrument: only a null or small delta is decisive (it kills the chain's last step); a large delta is uninformative about the champion band and must NOT be read as licensing +0.006 there.

The measurement that would settle it directly is refitting honest12's or greedyseat_v1's seats at --fold -1 and comparing that board delta to twinfive/fiveship's - it prices the term at the 0.937 quality level where it is actually needed. Blocked on the card until ortho_stack + v3large_stack clear (~07:20Z).
close_reason: Measured +0.001 at the upper-bound seating; the last step of the 0.953 chain is dead. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_the-refit-step-is-dead-at-its-own-upper-bound.md

PLAUSIBLE GAIN +0.019 offline -> ~0.877 vs best solo 0.8642 (+0.013); board transfer +0.97-1.25 => +0.013-0.016 board against a 0.008 gap.
