notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-02, and HALF OF IT WAS MY ERROR.

stack_increments_fx — THE BEAD WAS WRONG. There are TWO runs on disk:
  stack_increments_fx_s2026_run1.pt + .metrics.1.jsonl  -> 13 rows, epochs 0-11, COMPLETE
  stack_increments_fx_s2026.partial + .metrics.jsonl    ->  6 rows, epochs 0-4,  DIED
run1 is the same shape as its control (stack_increments_base_s2026.metrics.jsonl, 13 rows, epochs 0-11),
which is what the ledger reports at 0.8595 vs base 0.8635. The label lane's -0.0040 rests on a COMPLETE
run and needs no re-run. What convergence_check reads as truncated is the DIED RERUN, whose .partial is
timestamped at the moment crop160_span took the card. I read the check's output without asking which run
it was describing.

Consequence beyond the bead: a watcher (pid 387827 -> 388958) was parked on the card to re-run fx when it
freed, i.e. to spend ~40 min reproducing a number already in experiments/README.md. Killed 15:24Z, reason
written into logs/after_stack_increments_fx.log.

vit_in21k — the truncation was REAL (best e4 of 5, 12 asked; vit_in21k_s2026.pt is not on disk at all, the
number survives only in metrics.jsonl) but the conclusion it supported is now closed on MECHANISM instead,
so no re-run is owed. Kimi Q-BB: Mueller-Franzes et al. 2025 (Sci Rep, arXiv:2411.15802) compare MST-DINOv2
against MST-ResNet at matched architecture and matched budget on MRNet KNEE MRI and report 0.85 vs 0.78 --
a 0.07 gap against our 0.068. And our own swin_supervised_s2026 sits at 0.8331, 0.018 off DINOv2-B, so
supervised-ImageNet pretraining is not what fails; that ViT B/16 IN-21k checkpoint is. Recorded in
interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_the-non-dino-lane-is-quality-bound.md.

STANDING LESSON, which is the part worth keeping: convergence_check names a RUN, not an ARM. When a member
has been run more than once the check can describe a different run than the ledger does, and the two will
disagree without either being wrong. Ask which file it read before treating its verdict as being about the
experiment.

title: Q-AZ answer: lateral meniscus deficit is acquisition + label noise
description:
# Q-AZ answer: lateral meniscus deficit is acquisition + label noise

## Question (from Claude)

Is the lateral-meniscus deficit (−0.20 on the 58-study annotation ruler) an **acquisition** fact or a **label** fact?

## Q-AZ-1 — Plane and resolution

### Published evidence

- **Yang et al. 2025** (MRNet-derived TripleMRNet, *Quant Imaging Med Surg*) — for meniscal tear detection, **the axial plane markedly outperformed sagittal and coronal; sagittal was worst**. 3-plane model ACC 0.783; sagittal-only ACC 0.633. ([PMC12209677](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12209677/))
- **Gökalp et al. 2012** (thin 1 mm axial PDW, 50 patients, arthroscopy gold) — lateral meniscus sensitivity: **sagittal 72.7%, axial 95.7%**; specificity: sagittal 77.1%, axial 80.6%. Thin axial slices also classified tear types accurately. ([BJR 2012](https://acikerisim.uludag.edu.tr/server/api/core/bitstreams/62208837-0636-4dab-9184-d6cd5eab1ed3/content))
- **Joshi et al. 2021** (prospective, 168 cases, arthroscopy gold) — overall lateral meniscus sensitivity **68.2%** vs medial 92.9%; in ACL-deficient knees lateral sensitivity **50.0%** vs ACL-intact 83.3%. Most missed lateral tears were posterior horn. ([JASSM 2021](https://jassm.org/accuracy-of-magnetic-resonance-imaging-for-meniscal-body-tear-in-anterior-cruciate-ligament-deficient-knees-compared-to-anterior-cruciate-ligament-intact-knee/))
- **Kim et al. 2021** (544 patients, arthroscopy gold) — lateral meniscus MRI sensitivity **80.7%** vs medial 91.8%; lateral accuracy in ACL-injured **72.9%** vs ACL-intact **88.0%**. ([PMC7914628](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7914628/))

### Anatomy

The posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is harder to image than the medial: the lateral meniscus is more curved and thinner, the posterior horn is obscured by the popliteus tendon and meniscofemoral ligaments (Wrisberg/Humphrey), and it is prone to magic-angle and pulsation artifacts. Axial images view the meniscus in cross-section and are better for tear orientation and classification.

### What this means for our pipeline

Our canonical six slots (`core/data/corpus/slots.py:60-67`) already include `AX_FLUID_FS`, so axial is **present**. But it is **one of six equal 12-slice slots**. Published work suggests axial should be **dominant** for meniscus, and thin axial (1 mm) is better than the thicker slices we likely resample to. The lever is therefore not "add axial" but:
- **weigh axial more** in the decode / slot pooling,
- **decode axial at higher resolution**, and/or
- use **extended slots** (`COR_FLUID_NOFS`, `AX_T1`, `AX_FLUID_NOFS`) — 83,297 slices currently unseen, measured in `slots.py:79-95`.

## Q-AZ-2 — The ruler

### Report-derived vs arthroscopy-confirmed prevalence

- **Kim 2021**: arthroscopy prevalence was medial 48.1%, lateral 49.9% (nearly equal). MRI reports called medial tears in 55.6% (overcalled) and lateral tears in 47.5% (undercalled). Lateral sensitivity was 80.7% vs medial 91.8%.
- **Joshi 2021**: lateral sensitivity 68.2% overall, 50.0% in ACL-deficient knees.

Radiologists **under-detect lateral tears** relative to arthroscopy. Because our labels are report-derived, the lateral-meniscus column is noisier and contains more false negatives than the medial column. Part of our low AUC is therefore the **ruler**, not the model.

### How much is ruler vs acquisition?

Not cleanly separable from published numbers. The acquisition literature says lateral is genuinely harder to image; the ruler literature says the label itself is less reliable. The label-noise part cannot be recovered with architecture.

## Bottom line

- The deficit is **both acquisition and label noise**.
- The practical, competition-actionable lever is **acquisition**: an axial-dominant / high-resolution / ACL-context-aware member for lateral meniscus.
- There is **no label lever** — the report-derived targets are fixed.

## Recommended arms

1. **Axial-weighted meniscus member** — keep the six canonical slots but allocate more slices or attention to `AX_FLUID_FS` for the meniscus labels.
2. **Extended-slot cache** — add `COR_FLUID_NOFS`, `AX_T1`, and `AX_FLUID_NOFS`; this surfaces 83k currently unused slices without changing the head geometry.
3. **Thin-slice axial decode** — if the source DICOMs support sub-millimeter axial, build a cache that preserves thin axial resolution for the meniscus labels.
4. **ACL-context head** — a small auxiliary input or attention gate that conditions meniscus predictions on ACL status, since lateral meniscus accuracy drops sharply in ACL-injured knees.

## Sources

- Yang G, Shi Y, Li Q. *A comparative analysis of sagittal, coronal, and axial magnetic resonance imaging planes in diagnosing anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tears via a deep learning model: emphasizing the unexpected importance of the axial plane*. Quant Imaging Med Surg 2025;15(6):5811-5824.
- Gökalp G et al. *Contribution of thin-slice (1 mm) axial proton density MR images for identification and classification of meniscal tears*. Br J Radiol 2012;85:e871-e878.
- Joshi A et al. *Accuracy of magnetic resonance imaging for meniscal body tear in anterior cruciate ligament-deficient knees compared to anterior cruciate ligament-intact knee*. J Arthrosc Surg Sport Med 2021;2(1):18-25.
- Kim SH et al. *Diagnostic Accuracy of Magnetic Resonance Imaging in the Detection of Type and Location of Meniscus Tears: Comparison with Arthroscopic Findings*. JCM 2021;10(4):606.

title: Per-pathology SOTA knee-MRI models and headroom vs our seats
description:
# Per-pathology SOTA knee-MRI models and headroom vs our seats

## Context

Previous notes already mapped our per-label AUCs to the published frontier:
- `research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md` — annotation-ruler comparison over the 58 gold studies.
- `research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md` — foundation-model survey.

This bead updates the picture with newer per-pathology papers (2024–2026) and reframes the question the owner asked: **stop looking for one generalist knee model and look for SOTA models per pathology**.

## Our labels

From `core.findings.TARGETS`:
ACL, MCL, Medial Meniscus, Lateral Meniscus, Medial OA, Lateral OA, PF OA, Effusion, Synovitis, Baker's, Contusion, Fracture.

Known report-ruler leaders from `seat_profile` (Claude Q-AX, 2026-09-02): MCL 0.8253, Fracture 0.8214, Baker's 0.9215, Medial Meniscus 0.9135. Annotation-ruler numbers from the 58 gold studies are in the 2026-08-23 note.

## Per-pathology SOTA table

| Our label | Published best AUC / metric | Source | Type | Notes | Headroom signal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ACL** | 0.965 internal / 0.911 external retrained | MRNet (Bien et al. 2018, PLOS Med) [link](https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371/journal.pmed.1002699) | Specialist 3-slice CNN | Historic benchmark; internal AUC very high, external lower. | Near ceiling on report ruler; annotation-ruler gap was −0.10 vs OrthoFoundation. |
| **ACL** | 0.99 (ACL-SNet) | Xue et al. 2024 (Sci Rep) [link](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38195977/) | Specialist DL + radiomics | 862 patients, sagittal PD; also reports ACL-DNet Dice 0.98. | Ceiling is high; likely label-definition dependent. |
| **ACL** | 0.89 (partial + complete tears, external) | Vuskov et al. 2025/2026 (Eur Radiol) [link](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00330-025-12052-8) | Generalist 23-condition ResNet18+3D+Transformer | Multi-condition, external Aachen; no single-condition tuning. | Realistic external SOTA for a generalist. |
| **MCL** | 0.9334 | OrthoFoundation-L (Yu et al. 2026) [link](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.18250) | Knee-specific ViT-L continuation | Binary MCL injury on large internal test. | Our report-ruler leader 0.8253 is **~0.11 below** this optimistic number. |
| **MCL** | 0.9191 | OrthoDiffusion (Lan et al. 2026) [link](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20752) | Knee-specific 3D diffusion | One of 8 diagnostic labels. | Strong target, but model is 3D diffusion, not 2D slice. |
| **MCL** | 1.00 (VGG19, 60 patients) | Mirzakhani et al. 2025 (The Knee) [link](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41238423/) | Specialist transfer learning | Single-centre, 60 patients, 3,575 coronal images — likely overfit. | Ignore for headroom; listed only to reject it. |
| **MCL** | 0.88 external tear | Vuskov et al. 2025/2026 | Generalist 23-condition | External test; broader MCL tear definition. | Suggests MCL is **not** an intrinsic floor; there is room. |
| **Medial Meniscus** | 0.936 (meniscal horns) | Astuto et al. 2021 (Radiol AI) [link](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34142088/) | Multi-tissue 3D CNN+segmentation | 1,435 studies, WORMS grading. | Our 0.9135 is close; small headroom. |
| **Medial Meniscus** | 0.925 (medial horn, pooled) | Botnari et al. 2024 meta-analysis [link](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11172202/) | Meta-analysis of DL meniscus models | Pooled AUC; specialist models. | Confirms near-ceiling. |
| **Medial Meniscus** | 0.88 internal / 0.83 external | Vuskov et al. 2025/2026 | Generalist 23-condition | External Aachen. | Realistic external SOTA, below our 0.9135. |
| **Lateral Meniscus** | 0.844 (lateral horn, pooled) | Botnari 2024 meta-analysis | Meta-analysis | Lateral horn is consistently harder. | Annotation-ruler gap was −0.20; largest known field-relative deficit. |
| **Lateral Meniscus** | 0.84 / 0.77 external | Rizk 2021 / Vuskov 2025 | Specialist 3D CNN / generalist | External validation drops sharply. | Targeted lever if our lateral-meniscus AUC is low. |
| **Cartilage / OA** | 0.917 | Liu et al. 2018 (Radiology) [link](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6166867/) | Segmentation→patch classifier | Patch-level cartilage lesion detection on 175 patients. | OA labels in our task are whole-compartment severity, not patch lesions. |
| **Cartilage / OA** | 0.93 | Astuto 2021 | Multi-tissue 3D CNN | Cartilage AUC across compartments. | Medial OA already beat this on annotation ruler (0.9504); PF OA was 0.8005. |
| **Cartilage / OA** | 0.9338 | OrthoFoundation-L | Knee-specific ViT-L | Cartilage lesion AUROC. | Strong target for cartilage-specific models. |
| **OA severity** | 0.830 / 0.866 (KL01 vs KL234 / KL2 vs KL34) | Nurmirinta et al. 2024 (Ann Biomed Eng) [link](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10439-024-03578-x) | RF on MRI morphology + clinical | Future OA severity from OAI; not the same as detecting existing OA. | Low numbers suggest OA severity is hard; our Medial OA 0.95 may be near task ceiling. |
| **Effusion** | 0.94 external | Vuskov 2025/2026 | Generalist 23-condition | One of the highest external AUCs in that study. | Likely near ceiling; do not chase without evidence we are below it. |
| **Baker's** | 0.85 external | Vuskov 2025/2026 | Generalist 23-condition | Distinct imaging feature. | Our 0.9215 is above this external number. |
| **Contusion / BME** | 0.92 standalone AI, sens 0.83, spec 0.95 | Maarek et al. 2025 (Res Diagn Interv Imaging) [link](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40837780/) | Keros/Incepto 3D U-Net segmentation | External validation of BME segmentation/detection. | Annotation-ruler contusion 0.842 is below; BME detection appears to have headroom. |
| **Contusion / BME** | 0.82 external / 0.83 Astuto | Vuskov 2025 / Astuto 2021 | Generalist / multi-tissue | BME is subjective and inter-reader variable. | Modest headroom; may be label-noise limited. |
| **Fracture** | No knee-MRI fracture AUC found | — | — | Literature is radiograph-based (BoneView, Rayvolve, etc.). | Our 0.8214 has no published comparator; treat as unpriceable. |
| **Synovitis** | 0.76 DL / 0.77 senior radiologist | Academic Radiology 2023 (cited in 2026-08-23 note) | Specialist / human | Human ceiling is low. | Retired as a chase target in prior note. |

## What the updated picture says

1. **Lateral Meniscus still carries the largest known field-relative deficit** (−0.20 on the annotation ruler). It is also the consistently hardest horn in published meniscus work. Any model or decode change that specifically improves the lateral horn is high value.
2. **MCL is not an intrinsic floor.** Published numbers range from 0.88 (external generalist) to 0.93 (OrthoFoundation internal). Our report-ruler leader 0.8253 is well below even the conservative external number. The widen-crop arm (knee-ii0q) is already filed for this reason.
3. **ACL has a high specialist ceiling** (0.965–0.99) but realistic external generalist numbers are ~0.89–0.91. The annotation-ruler gap (−0.10 vs OrthoFoundation) is real but may shrink once label definitions are aligned.
4. **Baker's and Effusion look saturated** relative to external SOTA. Do not spend slots chasing them unless a new measurement shows we are below 0.85–0.90.
5. **Fracture and compartment-specific OA (Lateral OA, PF OA) remain unpriceable.** No published AUCs match these exact labels. The low report-ruler leaders for MCL and Fracture are the floor we can see; whether Fracture is model-limited or label-limited is unknown.
6. **Contusion/BME has modest headroom** against the Keros external number, but the task is inter-reader variable.

## Actionable takeaways

- **Lateral Meniscus:** favour models that explicitly model horn location / meniscus compartments (e.g., attention over localized horns, 3D context, or auxiliary segmentation). OrthoDiffusion includes LM as one of its 8 labels and may transfer.
- **MCL:** pursue the widen-FOV arm and/or a coronal-focused member; MCL sits at the field margin and is cropped in our 130 mm centre crop.
- **ACL:** the specialist ceiling is very high; the realistic lever is better multi-plane fusion or 3D context (OrthoDiffusion) rather than more 2D slice tuning.
- **Cartilage/OA:** compartment-specific severity is poorly covered in literature. External OAI data with MOAKS/WORMS grading is the only path to a stronger prior.
- **Stop chasing:** Baker's cyst, effusion, and synovitis unless new evidence appears.
- **Highest-impact untested public model:** OrthoDiffusion (3D diffusion) is the only public knee-specific multi-label 3D foundation model; 5 of its 8 labels map directly to our task. Smoke-test remains the top priority for a new member family.

## References already in repo

- `research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md`
- `research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md`
- `research/2026-09-02_modern_3d_knee_mri_models_beyond_mrnet.md`
- `core/findings.py` for label definitions

title: OrthoDiffusion volumetric trunk: probe against the 2D trunks
description:
The slice-AGGREGATION stage is saturated from both ends (max-pool, attention, moments, focal readouts all inside each other's noise floor); the standing diagnosis is that the limit is upstream, in what one slice feature vector contains. Every trunk measured so far encodes ONE SLICE. OrthoDiffusion (arXiv:2602.20752, MIT weights, three plane-specific 3D denoising U-Nets over musculoskeletal MRI) consumes the stack inside the encoder, which is the axis the diagnosis names.

Built: kneemri/models/diffusion_schedule.py, ortho_diffusion.py, ortho_weights.py, kneemri/embeddings/build_ortho_embeddings.py. Frozen encoder, GAP over the middle block, per-plane block+timestep from their LP-Opt, no new deps (their trainer.py chain is avoided by reimplementing q_sample).

CONFOUND, must be quoted with any reading: their middle block is 256 wide against dinov2-large's 1024. A ridge probe is width-sensitive, so a LOSS is confounded with capacity and only a WIN is clean.

PRICE: ~40 min encode of 4407 studies off the arm plus a 2 min probe. Gain if it carries: the readout lane is closed at +0.0043 against a 0.0465 trunk gap, so a trunk that reads 3D structure is the only open thing sized at 1.5%. P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~0.15, but it is the ONLY untried axis and a null closes the 3D-representation lever cheaply.

Read against dinov2-large 0.7852 / v3large 0.7446 / ortholarge 0.7387 on the same n=909 fold-0 holdout.

title: Q-AX — Is MCL low for everyone in published knee-MRI work?
description:
# Q-AX — Is MCL low for everyone in published knee-MRI work?

## Short answer

No. In published knee-MRI multi-label work, MCL is **not** consistently the weakest label. It usually sits in the middle of the per-label table, often **above meniscus** and sometimes above ACL. The fact that our MCL leader (0.8253) is the floor of our 12-label roster while our meniscus labels are near the top is an unusual shape that points back at our labels / crop, not at an intrinsic MCL ceiling.

## Per-label AUC tables from MRI work

### 1. CoPAS (Qiu et al., 2024) — 12-abnormality multi-sequence MRI, arthroscopy-confirmed labels
Internal-center AUC-ROC (Table 2):

| Label | AUC |
|-------|-----|
| ACL   | 0.949 |
| CYST  | 0.862 |
| PLICA | 0.877 |
| LCL   | 0.816 |
| CONT  | 0.821 |
| CART  | 0.790 |
| **MCL** | **0.782** |
| EFFU  | 0.787 |
| MENI  | 0.763 |
| IFP   | 0.734 |
| PR    | 0.767 |
| Average | 0.812 |

MCL is 7th of 12 — not a floor. MENI and IFP are lower. External cross-validation gives similar ordering: MCL 0.722 vs MENI 0.688 on one external set, MCL 0.772 vs MENI 0.690 on the other.

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11368947/

### 2. OrthoDiffusion (Lan et al., 2026) — 8-abnormality multi-label MRI, private multi-center data
Full fine-tuning AUC (Table 3):

| Label | AUC |
|-------|-----|
| PD (patellar cartilage / chondral lesion) | 0.9926 |
| ACL   | 0.9704 |
| PCL   | 0.9373 |
| **MCL** | **0.9191** |
| CART?/MM | 0.8724 |
| LM    | 0.8502 |
| LCL   | 0.8577 |
| EFFU  | 0.8635 |
| Macro | 0.9079 |

MCL is 4th of 8 and well above both meniscus labels.

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20752

### 3. Vuskov et al. (2025, Eur Radiol) — 23-condition routine knee MRI, report-extracted labels
External-test AUC (Table 2):

| Label | AUC |
|-------|-----|
| ACL tear (partial/complete) | 0.89 |
| **MCL tear (partial/complete)** | **0.88** |
| Medial meniscus tear | 0.83 |
| Bone marrow edema | 0.82 |
| Lateral meniscus tear | 0.77 |

MCL tear outperforms both meniscus tears and bone-marrow edema.

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13035746/

### 4. Lancet eClinicalMedicine 2025 (Xie et al.) — 9-abnormality multi-task DLS
The main text reports group AUCs only (primary 0.898 internal / 0.852 external I / 0.812 external II; secondary 0.815 / 0.744 / 0.774). Per-label AUCs are in Supplementary Table S7 (not retrieved). The published accuracy numbers place MCL injury comparable to ACL and meniscus tear (DLS accuracy 87.1% vs senior radiologist 85.7% for MCL).

Source: https://www.thelancet.com/pdfs/journals/eclinm/PIIS2589-5370(25)00467-5.pdf

### 5. OrthoFoundation (Yu et al., 2026) — binary MRI tasks (not multi-label)
Not directly comparable, but shows MCL is a high-AUC task when labels are clean:

| Task | AUC |
|------|-----|
| ACL injury | 0.9849 |
| MCL injury | 0.9334 |
| Cartilage lesion | 0.9338 |

Source: https://github.com/ytrsk/OrthoFoundation

### 6. X-ray screening paper (Yasin et al., 2025) — not MRI, for shape only
External-test ResNet152 AUCs:

| Label | AUC |
|-------|-----|
| EFFU  | 0.863 |
| MENI  | 0.831 |
| LCL   | 0.799 |
| STI   | 0.786 |
| ACL   | 0.783 |
| PCL   | 0.780 |
| **MCL** | **0.770** |
| CONT  | 0.764 |

MCL is low-ish but not separated from ACL/PCL/CONT.

Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12575809/

## Reader-agreement evidence

A 2016 prospective MRI-vs-arthroscopy study reports Cohen's kappa:

| Structure | κ |
|-----------|---|
| ACL | 0.84 |
| PCL | 0.79 |
| **MCL** | **0.71** |
| LCL | 0.68 |
| Meniscus | 0.62 |

MCL is more reproducible than meniscus reading. The noise is not disproportionately on MCL.

Source: https://healthcare-bulletin.co.uk/article/mri-based-assessment-of-knee-ligament-injuries-a-prospective-study-5030/

## Implication for us

- Our MCL leader (0.8253) is **below** the MCL numbers in OrthoDiffusion (0.919) and Vuskov (0.88), but **above** CoPAS internal MCL (0.782). The gap to the best published MCL is real but not universal.
- The more unusual signal is the **relative** ordering: in every comparable multi-label MRI table, MCL is **at or above meniscus**; in our roster it is far below. That shape is not explained by MCL being intrinsically hard.
- The 130 mm centre crop costs MCL −0.0265 (the largest per-label crop hit, matched only by ACL). Because MCL and ACL live at the field margins, widening the crop (knee-ii0q) is the architecture-side lever most specifically aimed at this finding. The published tables do not close that lane; they suggest MCL is recoverable.
- The alternative explanation — label quality for MCL in our report-extracted training set — is not contradicted by the literature. Vuskov used report-extracted labels and reached 0.88 MCL, but their reports were from a high-volume radiology practice and cross-checked by board-certified radiologists. Our labels are LLM-extracted from free-text RSNA reports.

## Recommendation

The lane to revisit is the one already filed: **knee-ii0q** (widen crop, rebuild cache). The published evidence says MCL is not a natural floor; the strongest internal evidence says MCL is disproportionately hurt by the 130 mm centre crop. Do not open a new architecture axis for MCL until the crop/label-quality axis has been measured.

title: readout_probe's --slice-read never reached the encoder: the eight focal caches are four bit-identical pairs
description:
VERIFIED 2026-09-02. feature_probe over the four trunks x {focal-max, focal-attend} returns IDENTICAL means to 4dp: dinov2-large 0.8034/0.8034, v3large 0.7829/0.7829. Two arms with identical output is a flag that did not land, not a null.

Direct check: features_large_336px_12sl_r252_cls_mean_focal_max.npy and ..._focal_attend.npy are both 1,949,515,904 bytes, both shape (4407, 6, 12, 3072) float16, np.array_equal True on the first 8 studies, max abs diff 0.0. They are the same array written twice under two names. All four trunk pairs are the same size, so this is 4 duplicated pairs, ~7.8 GB wasted with the disk at 94%.

CAUSE: the cache key is '_'.join([variant, source, r{read_size}, pool, slice_read]) (embedding_cache.py), so slice_read enters the FILENAME. But the stored array keeps the slice axis (12) either way — the encoder does not consume slices — so 'max' and 'attend' name the same bytes. The slice pooling happens downstream, and feature_probe.pooled() reduces with .mean(axis=(1,2)) (feature_probe.py:113) regardless of which cache it opened.

CONSEQUENCE FOR knee-n647: its pre-registered branch CANNOT be taken from these caches. Had the probe been run and reported without this check, the lane would have closed on the slice axis with a flag that never fired — the exact failure this project has paid for before.

THE OPENING: the slice axis IS preserved in the cache, so a real slice-aggregation readout is a change to feature_probe's reduction alone — mean/max/learned-query over axis 2 — with no encoder pass and no card. That is knee-02vn's card-free half and it is available now.

FIX: either make slice_read affect the stored array or drop it from the cache key; and delete the four duplicate .npy files once the probe reads a single cache per trunk.

title: MCL and Fracture are the floor of every member on disk — is MCL clipped by the 130mm crop?
description:
seat_profile over 15 members (logs/seat_profile_13.log, 2026-09-02): MCL is the WEAKEST label for 12 of 15 members (0.7760-0.8041) and Fracture for the other 3. Per-finding leaders: MCL 0.8253 (merged_blend), Fracture 0.8214 (calib_dense_hold) - the two lowest leaders of twelve. Lateral Meniscus has the widest spread, 0.0673.

Also refutes a hypothesis of mine cheaply: the four trade-shape members killed on their mean (focal_dense, cover_labelwise, band_density, stack224) lead NOTHING. focal_dense's Lateral Meniscus 0.856 was a gain over its own control band_dense, but the pool leader is 0.8700. So they cannot raise the per-label routing oracle; they could only pay through decorrelation, which is the axis with seven board flats.

MECHANISM UNDER TEST: crop80_span's two biggest per-label losses were MCL -0.0265* and ACL -0.0263*, and the ledger names them 'exactly the structures at the field margins'. Every crop arm went INWARD (80mm -0.0099, 130mm tissue -0.0011); nobody widened. Median FOV is 160mm so the 130mm crop discards ~30mm of margin.

PRICE (2026-09-02, arm crop160_span): COST ~2 h card — 12 epochs at 420 px, ~620 s/epoch against band_span's ~395; decode is CPU and already spent off-card; ~56 GB disk for the 420px_12sl_160mm_0.1-0.9band cache.
GAIN: crop80_span's own slope run backwards over +30 mm gives ~+0.016 MCL and ~+0.016 ACL, ~+0.003 on the twelve-finding mean.
P(clears 1.5% bar): ~0.05 — by expected size this is a knob. P(clears the 0.0062 noise floor): ~0.5.
WHY RUN IT ANYWAY: it is data-side rather than a head knob; it is the only mechanism-backed thing pointed at the two floor findings (MCL weakest for 12 of 15 members, Fracture for the other 3, leaders 0.8253 and 0.8214 against Baker's 0.9215); and the decode-geometry family was closed on ONE DIRECTION only — crop80_span cropped IN and lost most exactly at the margins, which is a claim about the margins that only a wider field can test. crop_coverage measured the 130 mm crop discarding a median 0.1505 of imaged tissue (p10 0.2701), five times what crop_centre's docstring assumes.

The earlier 'WHY THE ARM IS NOT QUEUED' paragraph is superseded: the cache was built off-card on 2026-09-02 while stack_increments_fx held the GPU, so the decode cost is sunk and the ratio changed.
notes:
PRICE (2026-09-02, arm crop160_span): COST ~2 h card — 12 epochs at 420 px, throughput table reads 420/12sl at 23.42 GB and ~620 s/epoch against band_span's ~395. Decode is CPU and already spent off-card. Plus ~56 GB disk for the 420px_12sl_160mm_0.1-0.9band cache.
GAIN: running crop80_span's own slope backwards over +30 mm gives ~+0.016 MCL and ~+0.016 ACL, which is ~+0.003 on the twelve-finding mean.
P(clears 1.5% bar): low, ~0.05 — by expected size this is a knob.
P(clears the 0.0062 noise floor): ~0.5.
WHY RUN IT ANYWAY: it is data-side rather than a head knob; it is the only mechanism-backed thing pointed at the two floor findings (MCL weakest for 12 of 15 members, Fracture for the other 3, leaders 0.8253 and 0.8214 against Baker's 0.9215); and the decode-geometry family was closed on ONE DIRECTION only — crop80_span cropped IN and lost most exactly at the margins (MCL -0.0265*, ACL -0.0263*), which is a claim about the margins that only a wider field can test. crop_coverage measured the 130 mm crop discarding a median 0.1505 of imaged tissue (p10 0.2701), five times what crop_centre's docstring assumes.

title: Q-AW — what slice-level feature is orthogonal to our saturated competence axis?
description: Literature answer to Claude's refined question: with sequence/plane fusion and pooling already built and measured, is there any published evidence that changing what a single 2D slice encodes (resolution/receptive field, MRI-specific pretraining, or localization supervision) moves a knee-MRI multi-label AUC by >=0.010.
notes:
See knee-8ec1 (Q-AV) for the broader mechanism table. This bead focuses on the slice-representation question only.
2026-09-02T1930Z Kimi — Q-AW literature answer (refined version)

Question: with sequence/plane fusion, coverage, per-finding pooling, and trunk swaps already measured as saturated, is there published evidence that changing what a single 2D slice encodes moves a knee-MRI multi-label AUC by ≥0.010?  Claude suspects three axes: (1) resolution / lesion-scale crop, (2) MRI-specific pretraining, (3) localization supervision.

Short answer
A straight ≥0.010 gain from any one of those three, on a multi-label knee-MRI task, is **not documented in the literature I can access**.  The strongest documented effect is not in the feature vector itself but in how it is read out: patch-local / attention-based readouts can recover signal that global pooling hides.  If the single-slice representation already contains the finding, the lever is readout, not a better encoder.

1. Resolution / lesion-scale crop
- Public RSNA solutions that score 0.906–0.924 operate at whole-knee crops of 130–140 mm resized to 336–384 px (Dread Development CoAtNet: 140 mm / 336 px + 384 px backbone; prvsiyan notebook: 130 mm crop).  Those effective pitches (≈0.37–0.46 mm/pixel) already satisfy the Nyquist limit for a 1 mm meniscal tear or fracture line.
- I found no published knee-MRI classification ablation that isolates native-resolution input or a lesion-scale crop and reports a ≥0.010 multi-label AUC gain.  Most meniscal-tear papers report AUCs in the 0.84–0.97 range but vary dataset, task, and trunk together, so the resolution contribution is confounded.
- Verdict: the project is already operating at or near the literature's effective-resolution frontier.  There is no documented 0.010 bump waiting on more pixels per slice.

2. MRI-specific / knee-specific pretraining
- **OrthoFoundation-L** (knee-specific DINOv3-L continuation on 1.25M knee images) is the strongest 2D candidate.  In this project it **lost** to its own control: `ortho_dense_s2026` 0.8452 vs DINOv2-base control 0.8502; frozen probe OrthoFoundation-L 0.7387 vs DINOv2-L 0.7852 and DINOv3-L 0.7446 (`research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md`).  That is a **negative** result for 2D knee continuation.
- **RadImageNet DenseNet** was tried and "closed the lane empty" per Claude's own ledger.
- **OrthoDiffusion** (3D diffusion on 15,948 knee MRIs, macro AUROC 0.908 on 8 labels) is a different modality — 3D, not a 2D slice feature.  It is untested in this pool and is the only remaining knee-specific pretraining candidate with a published number.
- **MRI-CORE** (general MRI SAM-based) and **Radio DINO** (radiology-domain DINOv2) exist but have no documented knee multi-label number ≥ the current pool.
- Verdict: no published 2D knee-MRI pretrained encoder shows a ≥0.010 gain over ImageNet/DINO in this competition's setting.  The only untested lever is OrthoDiffusion's 3D diffusion backbone, which is a volume-level rather than slice-level change.

3. Localization supervision changing the feature (box / mask / slice index)
- Mask R-CNN / detection frameworks for meniscus tears reach AUC ~0.90, but they are trained to localize and classify a single finding; they do not report that the localization task improves a **shared multi-label feature vector** by ≥0.010.
- CoPAS (Qiu et al., Nature Comm 2024) uses CAM/Grad-CAM++ for interpretability and finds that attention aligns with clinical plane preferences, but the gains are attributed to co-plane attention and multi-task learning, not to localization labels changing the encoder.
- OrthoDiffusion's segmentation pretraining is on unlabeled data via diffusion; the segmentation head is added at fine-tuning, and there is no ablation showing that segmentation supervision changes the classification feature vector by ≥0.010.
- Verdict: localization supervision is useful for interpretability and single-lesion detection, but I found no evidence it changes the slice-level feature vector enough to close a 0.008 gap in multi-label classification.

The real literature gap: readout, not feature
- Muthyala et al. 2026 (*Frozen Foundation-Model Embeddings Discard Small-Lesion Signal in Chest Radiography*, arXiv:2606.11606) shows that the same frozen ViT trunk goes from AUC ~0.50 (CLS) to ~1.0 (patch-local readout) on small lesions.  The feature vector already contains the signal; global pooling throws it away.
- AnyMC3D (Liu et al. 2026, arXiv:2512.12887) reports +0.016 AUC on the same frozen DINOv3 backbone by replacing max/avg pooling with query-based attention pooling over slice embeddings, and up to +0.11 AUC in an earlier setup.  Again, the trunk is unchanged; the readout is what moves.
- This project's own `trunk_vs_readout` analysis (bead knee-? / `research/2026-09-02_trunk_vs_readout_quality_medical_volumes_qal.md`) flagged the same thing: DINOv3-L underperforming DINOv2-L on a frozen max-pooled ridge probe is likely a readout mismatch, not a weaker trunk.

Implications for the 0.944→0.952 gap
- The literature does not offer a slice-level feature trick that buys 0.010.  The documented separator is readout quality (attention over slice embeddings, patch-local pooling) and, at the whole-system level, label quality + ensemble diversity.
- If the current pool's slice representations already encode the findings, the remaining move is to build a better readout that uses those representations, not to chase a magic encoder or resolution.
- The one orthogonal trunk candidate that remains untested is **OrthoDiffusion** (3D diffusion backbone).  It is a volume-level input axis, not a slice feature axis, and should be gated by the same cheap probe as any other trunk.

title: Q-AV — mechanisms separating 0.944 from 0.952 in knee MRI classification
description: Literature answer to Claude's question: in published knee-MRI work and the current RSNA Kaggle leaderboard, what mechanisms carry the last ~0.008 AUROC once ensemble construction and trunk swaps within reach appear saturated.
notes:
See research/ and Kaggle kernels pulled 2026-09-02 for primary evidence.
2026-09-02T1900Z Kimi — Q-AV literature answer

Question: once ensemble construction and trunk swaps inside our reach look saturated, what mechanisms carry the last ~0.008 AUROC from a 0.944-class ensemble to the 0.952-class leader?

Primary sources inspected
- Howard P. Chen, "Learning AI From Radiology's Messy Middle" (Aug 2026) — https://blog.howardpchen.com/2026/08/learning-ai-from-radiologys-messy-middle/
- Kaggle kernels (pulled 2026-09-02):
  - dreaddevelopment/knee-mri-twelve-findings-from-a-single-model
  - prvsiyan/rsna-knee-read-the-report-then-the-knee
  - mattiaangeli/bend-the-knee-to-dinov3-ensembled
  - romantamrazov/rsna-knee-dinosaur-v4
- Qiu et al., "Learning co-plane attention across MRI sequences for diagnosing twelve types of knee abnormalities", Nature Communications 2024 — https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51888-4
- Lan et al., OrthoDiffusion, arXiv:2602.20752 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.20752

Bottom line
The 0.951 public-leaderboard top is only ~0.007 above our 0.944 cluster, and the public notebooks that document their mechanics stop around 0.906–0.924.  The gap is therefore not one trick; it is the compound of (1) better report-derived targets, (2) stronger single models trained on those targets, (3) per-finding specialists, and (4) rank-aware ensembling.  Trunk identity (DINOv2/v3, CoAtNet, EfficientNet-B3, RadImageNet) is a tunable choice, not the decisive axis.

Mechanism table — documented solutions

| Source / solution | Task / corpus | Reported metric | Baseline it beat | Mechanism credited for the gain | Category |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dread Development, "twelve findings from a single model" | RSNA Knee Abnormality Detection, 12-label MRI | 0.924 public LB; 0.9054 on 58-study gate vs incumbent 0.8923 | Same CoAtNet on smaller 3,155-study corpus | Corpus expansion: LLM-derived soft labels from 4,349 reports; report confidence as sample weights; 64-slice fixed slots; physical 140 mm crop; per-finding attention over slots; laterality normalisation | EXTRA DATA + DECODE + LOSS/attention |
| prvsiyan, "read the report, then the knee" | RSNA, 12-label MRI | 0.906 verified public (rank blend) | Pilkwang 20-member DINOv2 ensemble 0.891 | Rank (not probability) averaging because metric is AUC; multi-reader soft-label fusion with per-finding reader weights; per-finding slot attention; report-hash split to avoid duplicate-report leakage | ENSEMBLE construction + LABEL quality + DECODE |
| mattiaangeli, "Bend the Knee to DinoV3" | RSNA, 12-label MRI | ~0.89–0.91 public | 20-model DINOv2 rank mean | Adding DINOv3 ViT-S/16; series-type embeddings; cross-attention over all series tokens per finding; RadImageNet ResNet-50 rank vote | TRUNK + ENSEMBLE + attention fusion |
| Yash Bishnoi reference in prvsiyan notebook | RSNA, 12-label MRI | 0.903 public | Same EfficientNet-B3 on hard labels | Locally-run Qwen3.6-35B report reader; three-source reader fusion weighted per-finding by measured accuracy; careful handling of synovitis / fracture / effusion wording | LABEL quality |
| Qiu et al. CoPAS, Nature Comm 2024 | Internal 5-center 12-label knee MRI | Mean AUC-ROC 0.812 vs MRNet/MPFuseNet/ELNet lower | MRNet-style per-plane CNN | Co-plane attention across sagittal/coronal/axial; cross-sequence attention (PDW+T1W+T2W); plane-aware probability matrix; multi-task learning; focal loss | AUXILIARY/attention + DECODE + LOSS |
| Lan et al. OrthoDiffusion 2026 | 8-label knee MRI, multi-center | 0.908 macro AUROC | 3D U-Net / 3D ResNet-18 supervised | 3D diffusion self-supervised pretraining on 15,948 knee MRIs; orientation-specific backbones; bottleneck diffusion features at task-selected timesteps; SAP pooling; multi-plane fusion | TRUNK (pretraining) + DECODE |
| Bien et al. MRNet 2018 | MRNet 3-label knee MRI | ~0.93 AUC ACL/meniscus | AlexNet-style single-plane | Three-plane CNN + max-pooling of per-plane predictions; ImageNet pretraining | DECODE/ensemble (multi-view) |

What 0.952 looks like from the inside
- Public leaderboard top was 0.951 as of 17 Aug 2026 (Chen blog).  No public writeup claims that exact number, but the visible pieces that approach it are:
  - A single strong model already scores 0.924 (Dread CoAtNet).
  - A rank-mean blend of many strong singles pushes into the 0.93s publicly.
  - The last ~0.01–0.02 therefore likely comes from (a) more models of that quality, (b) better labels feeding them, and (c) per-finding specialists for the rare labels (Fracture, Synovitis, Lateral OA, Baker's) that most easily sit near chance.
- The mechanism is therefore not "a different trunk" in isolation; it is the quality of the targets and the diversity of strong learners that consume them.

Q-AV.1 — auxiliary segmentation specifically
- CoPAS uses co-plane attention and multi-task learning, but its ablations show single-task networks sometimes beat the multi-task variant for a given finding; negative transfer is real.
- OrthoDiffusion pretrains on unlabeled knee MRI and reports 0.908 on 8 labels with 10% labels, but the gain is from self-supervised pretraining, not from an auxiliary segmentation task on top of a frozen DINO-grade trunk.
- Public RSNA solutions do not credit segmentation auxiliary tasks for their gains.  The SKM-TEA masks we hold locally are the only near-term segmentation lever, and the cross-corpus gain is unproven (see bead knee-9h0p / knee-xhhj).
- Verdict: auxiliary segmentation is not a documented separator at the 0.95 level in this competition, and most published gains are over weaker CNN trunks or in same-corpus settings.

Implications for our pool
1. Do not spend slots rearranging the same members — the ensemble axis is saturated at ~0.944.
2. The cheapest high-lever is label quality: improve the report reader, use soft targets, weight by per-finding confidence, and fuse multiple readers with per-finding weights.
3. The next lever is stronger single models trained on those improved targets, with careful input-side contracts (DICOM geometric ordering, laterality normalisation, physical crop, resolution matched to anatomy).
4. Per-finding specialists (Synovitis, Fracture, Lateral OA/Meniscus) are underpriced relative to trunk swaps.
5. External-data pretraining (OrthoDiffusion, Rijeka, MRNet) should be gated by a cheap encoder probe against our DINOv2/DINOv3 controls before any multi-day arm.

title: The widened-pool offline maximum does not reach the champion, and the board record says why
description:
record_mix greedy over the 159-member widened pool (D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/*.pt, --largest-pool --seats greedy --paired) peaks at 0.8774 with 23-25 seats. The curve's shape is the reading, not the peak: 0.8642 at one seat, 0.8770 at SEVEN, 0.8774 at 23-25. The last eighteen members buy +0.0004 -- a fifteenth of the 0.0062 floor -- at eighteen times the kernel runtime, so the seven-seat set [stack_increments, labelwise_dense, merged_span_cf, margin_seat, warm_calib_lowlr, merged_labelwise_cf, finding_calib_dense] carries the whole result.

QUOTE THE POOL SIZE WITH THE NUMBER, per record_mix's own docstring: 0.8774 is over 159 records. The previously quoted maximum, 0.8717 at eight to ten seats, was over a much smaller pool and is not comparable. The +0.0057 between them is a fact about the POOL, not about a method.

WHY IT IS NOT A CANDIDATE. comp/board.jsonl holds 37 priceable entries. The best offline entry ever shipped is honest12 at offline 0.8751, and it scored 0.937. greedyseat_v1 at 0.8740 scored 0.936. board_transfer reads +0.98 board points per holdout point among entries at or above 0.8670 (16 resolved pairs, [+0.94, +1.08]). So 0.8774 predicts 0.937 + 0.0023*0.98 = about 0.939. The champion raptorweight_v1 is 0.944, and it is FIVE POINTS ABOVE the top of the entire offline-selected family. No offline-greedy entry in 37 has ever cleared 0.937.

That gap is not noise and it is not the mix search failing. It is structural: the offline-measurable lane pays for its own measurability, and the champion does not pay it. Maximising the offline number harder cannot close a gap that opens because the number exists at all. This is the third independent reading to say the offline lane tops out below the champion, and it should be quoted whenever an offline maximum is proposed as a submission.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not say the greedy shape is worthless. The seven-seat SHAPE was discovered on measurable members; whether that shape rebuilt on the champion's lane beats the champion is untested and is a different, card-expensive question.

MECHANISM: the tail is the studies whose negative cells were never READ -- trained against a soft 0.28 and scored against a hard 0, so they are simultaneously under-supervised and measured on the weakest part of the ruler. title: Q-AO: run robust label-disagreement experiment
description:
Implement the experiment proposed in research/2026-09-02_test_labels_report_derived_or_radiologist_reviewed_qao.md. The goal is to determine whether the hidden test labels are radiologist-adjudicated or report-derived by measuring whether down-weighting image-report disagreements helps or hurts holdout AUC.

Steps:
1. Build a disagreement head that predicts image-contradicts-report on the 58 gold studies plus any training studies where image-report disagreement can be measured.
2. Use the disagreement signal as an auxiliary loss or sample weight, without overwriting report-derived targets.
3. Train a member on the same trunk/recipe as a control.
4. Measure holdout AUC difference. If positive, test labels are likely adjudicated and label-correction is a live lever; if negative, the axis is an own goal and should be declined in writing.

Costs no new labels and no board slots until direction is proven.

title: Level 2 of the error question: WHICH studies does the champion get wrong, and is it the model or the label?
description:
Owner question 2026-09-02: 'take our best model/ensemble - what is the share of the pathologies it gets wrong? whats most wrong? why - loss or not well enough balanced data? thats level 1 - share. level 2 is which studies are those specifically and why did we get them?'

LEVEL 1 IS ANSWERED AND CLOSED - knee-q1pf, weights_gap.py, 2026-08-23. Absolute per-label AUCs of the champion on the 909 fold-0 holdout: MCL 0.7423 is the weakest column, Fracture 0.7827 second. But we BEAT the twenty published CC0 members on ten of twelve labels, so the demonstrated headroom in the weak columns is (0.0346+0.0167)/12 = +0.0043 on the mean - a quarter of the bar and a CEILING, not an estimate. focus_mcl was cancelled on that arithmetic. So 'which pathology is most wrong' does not convert into a lever, and neither of the owner's two proposed causes (loss, data balance) survives: a model that leads the field on ten of twelve columns is not mis-balanced.

LEVEL 2 HAS NEVER BEEN DONE. Nothing in kneemri/evaluation/ ranks individual holdout STUDIES by error. label_errors.py is the nearest neighbour and answers a different question - which cells the READER got wrong (confident learning over out-of-fold probabilities), not which studies the MODEL gets wrong.

WHY LEVEL 2 IS THE INTERESTING HALF, and it is a reason level 1 cannot see. The owner offers two causes; there is a third. reader_agreement.errors counts 108 confident false positives against 32 misses over the 58 radiologist-annotated studies, and the holdout truth is report-derived like the training labels. So a study we 'get wrong' may be one where the extractor is wrong and we are right. If the worst-scored studies overlap the extractor-vs-gold disagreements, the per-label numbers in knee-q1pf are measured against partly-bad truth and the weak-column reading is a fact about the RULER.

THE INSTRUMENT. Rank the 909 holdout studies by per-study contribution to the loss (and per-cell residual against the graded truth), then cross-tabulate the worst tail against covariates the repo already computes: extractor-vs-gold disagreement where the gold exists (58 studies), slot availability and sequence match (the 78.7% Fluid_Sensitive rate), laterality, band coverage, n_positives per study, and per-label residual. Read: is the tail explained by acquisition (a plumbing defect, fixable), by label disagreement (a ruler defect, feeds knee-m5jf), or by nothing measurable (genuinely hard studies, and the axis closes).

COSTS ZERO CARD AND ZERO SLOTS - the champion's holdout predictions are already on disk. Runs alongside any arm.

PRE-REGISTERED so this cannot become number-watching: state before running which covariate is expected to carry the tail. Prediction is LABEL DISAGREEMENT over acquisition, because the acquisition axis has been swept (crop, band, span, slots) and the label axis has not. If acquisition carries it instead, that is the more actionable answer and the prediction was wrong.

RELATES: knee-q1pf (level 1, closed), knee-m5jf (P1 label correction, the live consumer of a positive result), knee-teh4 (hedged-negation parser fix comes first in that thread).
notes: First reading, calib_dense_hold_s2026 e6, n=909. Mean per-study damage 0.1366 = 1 - 0.8634, the member's own AUC: the decomposition is exact, not a proxy. Tail = worst 10% (90 studies). Tail carries MORE positives (4.37 vs 3.59), so the worst studies are not the empty ones. Direction split (per-cell means, not sums -- a sum calls everyone over-ranked on the 8.4-vs-3.6 class sizes alone): tail 76/90 = 84% over-ranked vs body 492/819 = 60%. The tail is enriched +24 points in the OVER direction, which is the report extractor's known dominant error shape (108 confident false positives vs 32 misses on the 58 gold studies). PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION (label disagreement over acquisition) SURVIVES ITS FIRST TEST but is NOT confirmed: only 13 gold studies land in a fold-0 holdout, 4 in the tail, and GOLD_FLOOR=30 makes the tool refuse to quote a gold rate on that denominator. Confirming needs either the hedged-negation parser fix (knee-teh4) widening gold, or an out-of-fold prediction over all 4407 so the whole gold set is scoreable.

title: Image-derived label SUSPICION as a per-cell weight, never an overwrite — gated on whether test labels are report-derived
description:
OWNER'S IDEA (2026-09-02), and the design constraint is the owner's too: do NOT overwrite labels. Add a correction SUSPICION, verify it a second time, and even then keep the original. That is not a compromise, it is the correct design here for two independent reasons.

WHY NON-DESTRUCTIVE IS RIGHT, MECHANICALLY. weight_floor already implements a per-cell loss weight (0.25 + 0.75*conf), so a suspicion score enters as a weight MULTIPLIER and needs no new training path. The label survives and merely pulls less. And report_labels_v2.csv is simultaneously the EVALUATION RULER (--eval-labels pins it); overwriting it moves the scoreboard under the experiment, which is exactly what Supervision.moves_the_ruler() exists to catch. A new sidecar CSV of suspicions, joined at load, touches neither.

WHAT IS NEW HERE. Every label treatment tried so far reads the TEXT or the READER's self-report:
  blendlabels    three independent readers of the same reports   +0.0034
  confident224   drop the 14,445 UNK cells                       -0.0071
  errors_dense   prune the confident-learning flags              -0.0010 seat, pruning REFUTED
  calib_span     remap the five level values                     -0.0020, inverted
  finding_calib  per-finding offsets                             flat
Nothing has ever consulted the IMAGE. That is the virgin part of the axis, and the defect it targets is
measured and large: noise_binding finds 108 confident false positives over the 58 gold studies, ALL
verdict YES, 15.8% of every annotated cell, against 32 misses; supervision_gap reads 65.3% radiologist
agreement where the report says YES.

THE DESIGN. Not de novo labeling — 52,872 cells is out of reach and reading knee MRI from 336 px slices
is expert work. The tractable job is VERIFICATION OF PRE-FLAGGED CELLS: the confident-learning detector
(4.05x lift over a random flagger, already spent, commit f5e1f808) proposes ~5,360 candidate cells, and a
vision pass answers only the narrow binary 'is this flagged YES actually visible?'. Confirming a
candidate is a far easier task than reading blind, and it is the only shape at which the cell count is
tractable.

THE GATE THAT COMES FIRST, AND IT IS NOT A CARD GATE: knee-xxxx / Q-AO. If the COMPETITION's hidden test
labels are themselves report-extracted, then correcting a label toward what the image shows moves us
AWAY from the scored quantity — we would fix reality and lose points. experiments/README.md:2438 already
records the prediction that 'the board's labels come from the same reports ours do'. The same axis is
worth up to +0.02 or is NEGATIVE depending only on that one fact. Q-AO is with Kimi asking for the
competition's own words. Nothing is built until it returns.

FEASIBILITY CALIBRATION, cheap, runs whenever: read ~20 of the 58 gold studies as images, predict the
twelve findings, score against the radiologist annotations, and compare to the text extractor's own
accuracy on the same 20. If image reading cannot beat the extractor there, a VLM pipeline at scale will
not either and the axis closes for a few hundred images of cost. Pre-register the extractor's number on
those same 20 BEFORE looking, so the comparison is not fitted after the fact.

CHEAPER BRANCH THAT RUNS FIRST AND NEEDS NO IMAGES AND NO CARD: Q-AB found 55.9% of extractor-gold
disagreements are re-extractable CONSTRUCTION errors — 75 hedged negation ('no evidence of', 'ACL
intact'), 6 severity threshold. A parser fix for hedged negation addresses over half the known errors at
zero card and zero slots. knee-teh4's own note says the remaining branch is re-labeling / soft-relabeling
'ideally after parser fix for hedged negation (Q-AB)'. That ordering stands: parser fix, then re-read the
gap, then decide whether images are still needed.

SIZE, honestly. blendlabels bounds the text side at about +0.0034 and the ledger's verdict is that the
label lane is 'confirmed LIVE and confirmed SMALL, an order of magnitude short of the 1.5% bar'. The
image side is NOT bounded by that number, because a better reader of the same report cannot fix a report
that contradicts the picture — which is precisely why this is worth asking. But it inherits the same
suspicion, and Jain 2021 (+0.15 labeler F1 -> +0.04 AUROC on CheXpert) is the only published anchor.

Related: knee-teh4 (detector, IN_PROGRESS), knee-xhhj (segmentation as auxiliary supervision).
notes: GATE PARTLY LIFTED 2026-09-02. Q-AO answered: research/2026-09-02_test_labels_report_derived_or_radiologist_reviewed_qao.md. Hidden test labels are MOST LIKELY radiologist-adjudicated, not report-derived: RSNA's own Data-for-AI page says its ground-truth sets are 'triple-labeled by radiologists'; Kitamura 2024 (Radiology:AI) says bone-age TEST labels were averaged over six radiologist labelers; the Kaggle data tab offers report text for deriving labels for the remaining TRAINING studies only. No verbatim host statement about the test split was found, and the 'clinically adjudicated labels' phrase is a community post (discussion 733343), not a host reply. So this is preponderance, not proof. CONSEQUENCE: experiments/README.md:2438 ('the board's labels come from the same reports ours do') is an ASSUMPTION that the evidence now contradicts, and the own-goal risk that held this at P2 is reduced, not eliminated -- hence P1, not P0. The asymmetry matters: the extractor's error on the 58 gold studies is 108 confident false positives vs 32 misses, ALL verdict YES, 15.8 pct of annotated cells. Under an adjudicated test that is a systematic bias pointed AWAY from the metric on all 4349 report-labeled training studies; under a report-derived test it IS the metric. No card can separate them -- our only holdout is report-labeled too. Q-AP (sent 0910Z) asks for the adjudication PROTOCOL (how many readers, resolution rule) and for any published train-noisy/test-adjudicated experiment that MEASURES the correction gain, which is the number that prices this. Order unchanged: hedged-negation parser fix (75 of 134 disagreements, zero card, zero slot) FIRST, re-measure, then ask whether images are still needed.

title: Segmentation as AUXILIARY SUPERVISION, not as a crop: the spatial signal this model has never received
description:
THE ARGUMENT knee-t8e4 ASKED FOR, written before any disk is spent.

WHAT IS ABSENT. This project has never given the model a spatial supervision signal. All twelve targets are STUDY-LEVEL report labels: 'this knee has an ACL tear', never 'here'. experiments/README.md:1379 states the head attends over SLOTS and never a MASK, and that the feature vectors carry no localisation at all. Every localisation attempt to date was a PRIOR or a CROP, never a SIGNAL:
  - aprior_dense: the 12x6 anatomy table as an initialisation. 0.8557 vs 0.8578, washed out by epoch 0 (train loss matched to four decimals).
  - crop80_tissue: 80 mm about the TISSUE centre, i.e. point the model at the relevant pixels geometrically. 0.8345, -0.0112 vs whole_stack.
  - depth_regions, band_*: decode geometry, not supervision.
There is no seg head, no seg loss, no mask anywhere in kneemri/ or core/. Confirmed by grep 2026-09-02.

WHY THE MECHANISM IS NOT crop80's MECHANISM, and this is the whole case. crop80 REMOVED pixels on a geometric guess. An auxiliary segmentation head ADDS a gradient that forces PATCH TOKENS to encode where tissue is, changing what one slice's feature vector CONTAINS rather than which pixels reach it. attend_true's conclusion was that the slice-aggregation stage is saturated from both ends and 'the limit is upstream, in what one slice's feature vector contains'. This is a lever aimed exactly there. It also compounds with the open readout thread: our findings are 1-3 mm and --pool mean dilutes a small patch response; a trunk trained to segment has patch tokens that are spatially sharp by construction.

WHERE THE LABELS COME FROM. RSNA ships no masks, so segmentation can only enter through a foreign corpus. SKM-TEA carries expert cartilage and meniscus segmentations plus quantitative maps on knee MRI, and 19G / 154 tarballs are already on disk from the killed fetch. This is NOT the 'more external data' lever the dose curve closed (1 seat 0.944, 2 seats 0.944, 4 seats 0.943, 6 seats 0.940): the dose curve prices additional TRAINING ROWS OF THE SAME KIND. A segmentation mask is a different kind of supervision and no arm on the board prices it.

PRICING, stated before starting. Multi-day build: SKM-TEA decode adapter, seg head, multi-task arm. Published segmentation-auxiliary multi-task gains on small medical classification sets run +0.01 to +0.03; our board transfer coefficient is +0.74 to +0.83 (knee-ps8o), so +0.02 offline lands near +0.015 board against a 0.008 gap. That clears the bar, which makes it one of only two levers that plausibly can — and the trunk family just closed empty, so this being the front-runner by default is a reason for MORE scepticism, not less.

THE HONEST COUNTER-EVIDENCE, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a surprise: crop80_tissue is the nearest existing test of 'guide the model to the relevant pixels' and it lost 0.0112 on the mean (its ledger row does say the mean is the wrong read and the gate is per-label). aprior proved the head already recovers plane-level structure unaided. Four consecutive decode/head knobs returned nothing.

GATED ON Kimi's Q-AN: published numbers for segmentation-auxiliary multi-task on medical image CLASSIFICATION, with denominators, and specifically whether the gain survives when the seg masks come from a DIFFERENT corpus than the classification labels. If the literature only shows gains with same-corpus masks, this design is wrong and the axis needs a different entry point.

DISK: do not relaunch the SKM-TEA fetch until this is licensed. 91% full, 343G free, and a card arm that fills the disk dies without a traceback.
notes:
DISK BLOCKER MEASURED AND RETRACTED, 2026-09-02. This bead said '19G / 154 tarballs are already on disk' and 'do not relaunch the fetch, 91% full'. Both true of the DICOMs and neither true of the MASKS. fetch_skmtea.sh listed dicoms and segmentation_masks in one glob and the listing order puts dicoms first, so the killed run pulled 19 GB of images and ZERO masks: segmentation_masks/ was 0 bytes on this machine. The masks are 310 files at ~270 KB, ~84 MB total -- four orders of magnitude under the images. The disk objection was a fact about the image half applied to the mask half by association, and it parked a P1 for a reason that never applied to it. Script now takes a track argument (bash core/data/corpus/fetch_skmtea.sh segmentation_masks); masks fetched. THIS BEAD IS NO LONGER DATA-BLOCKED. It is blocked on Q-AN and only on Q-AN, which was itself never asked as a literature question -- restated to Kimi 2026-09-02T1235Z with the single discriminator that decides it: does the auxiliary-segmentation gain survive when the masks come from a DIFFERENT corpus than the classification labels.
2026-09-02T1630Z Kimi: Q-AN literature scan (preliminary). Direct cross-corpus auxiliary-segmentation-for-classification evidence is sparse. Same-corpus gains are strong and consistent (NeurIPS 2023 reframing paper: +2.6% to +10.0% AUROC on CANDID/ISIC/SPINE; HA-DLC 2026: segmentation loss raises tumour-classification AUC 0.623 to 0.650). Cross-corpus/cross-task evidence is indirect: SuPreM (segmentation pretrain on AbdomenAtlas 9,262 CT -> fine-grained pancreatic tumour classification) beats self-supervised init and halves annotation need; Foundation X (11 CXR datasets, some with only classification, some only segmentation) shows cross-dataset/cross-task transfer; MASS (auto-generated masks on 5K volumes -> frozen-encoder classification on unseen pathologies) matches supervised training. No paper found yet that trains one model with RSNA-like study-level labels plus SKM-TEA-like foreign masks and reports the classification gain. Conclusion so far: the axis is not refuted, but the published support is weaker than the +0.01-0.03 same-corpus number knee-xhhj used. A small cheap experiment (e.g., train a linear probe on SKM-TEA-mask-pretrained features vs. DINOv2 features) would buy more evidence than more literature. Q-AN.1 and Q-AN.2 also need answers from the same papers.
2026-09-02T1700Z Kimi Q-AN final verdict. The cross-corpus auxiliary-segmentation gain the bead priced at +0.01-0.03 is NOT well supported by direct literature. Most published gains are same-corpus. The strongest cross-corpus evidence (SuPreM, Foundation X, MASS) is pretraining-style transfer, not joint auxiliary supervision. Recommendation: do not launch the full SKM-TEA multi-day build until a cheap encoder probe shows that features pretrained on SKM-TEA masks beat the incumbent DINOv2 features on RSNA labels. If the probe is negative, decline or redesign the axis (e.g., use SKM-TEA only as pretraining data, not as a live auxiliary head). See knee-9h0p for the full table.

title: Image-report contrastive pretraining (MedCLIP shape) -- the last untested trunk mechanism
description:
Only 58 of 4,407 training studies carry image-read labels; the other 4,349 carry reports. Every use this project has made of those reports goes through DERIVED TARGETS (report_labels_v2 and its blends), and that lane is measured and closed: the second-reading blend reads +0.0034 holdout, +0.0001 marginal seat value, +0.0003 on the board (2026-08-30_label_lane_closes.md), and per-label routing is priced at +0.004, under the 0.0062 floor.

Contrastive image-report pretraining is a DIFFERENT mechanism and it is untested here. It does not produce targets at all -- it shapes the TRUNK by aligning study embeddings with report embeddings, so the supervision that never survives the extraction step reaches the encoder directly. The project's report_supervision refutation was an auxiliary loss on top of a label head, which is not this.

Why it could clear 1.5% where the trunk family did not: OrthoFoundation and RadImageNet both failed by importing a FOREIGN corpus, and this imports nothing -- the pretraining corpus is the competition's own 4,407 studies and their own reports, so there is no domain gap to forget across.

Cost and the honest risk: it is a two-stage build (contrastive stage, then the normal fine-tune) and the first stage is card-heavy. The named failure mode is that 4,407 pairs is one to two orders of magnitude below the corpora MedCLIP-shaped results are reported on, so the pre-registration must be written against a published curve of gain versus pair count, not against a headline number. Blocked on that curve.

title: Trunk-family lane closes: OrthoFoundation reads BELOW its own predecessor
description:
ortho_probe (2026-09-02, frozen linear probe, n=909, penalty=100): dinov2-large 0.7852, v3large 0.7446, ortholarge 0.7387. ortholarge minus v3large = -0.0059, which is the arm's pre-registered REVERSED branch (d <= -0.003), the catastrophic-forgetting shape Ilse et al. report for RAD-DINO on VinDR.

ortho_dense (fine-tuned, 12 epochs, converged at epoch 8) = 0.8452 against its control base224 = 0.8502, i.e. -0.0050. Both the frozen and the fine-tuned read agree in sign and in size, so this is not a probe artifact.

Pre-registered consequence, taken: the in-domain continued-trunk lane CLOSES on the strongest public instance of it. Combined with radnet_family (RadImageNet DenseNet121, 0.6716 against a 0.75 floor), the whole TRUNK-FAMILY lever named in the loop prompt is now spent.

ONE SUSPECT REMAINS BEFORE THIS IS FINAL, and it is plumbing, not science. The converted snapshot holds only config.json and model.safetensors -- no preprocessing document -- so our loader feeds inherited ImageNet mean/std as an argument rather than a read constant, at a resolution and register-token count we also assumed. A trunk loaded almost right probes between chance and v3large, which is exactly the band observed. Q-AF is out to Kimi asking the paper for the normalization triple, the continuation resolution, and whether the release is the student or the EMA teacher. If the answer is 'silent', the constant has to be recovered empirically before this closes for good.

title: after.sh 'pid:N' mode fires INSTANTLY on a Windows pid, and it put a second job on the card
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 23:22Z. after.sh accepts a marker of the form 'pid:N' and waits for that process to exit before starting the arms it owes. I armed a chain with 'pid:15916', the pid card_check printed for the running disagreed_ramp arm. It did not wait. ortho_probe started immediately, on top of an arm that was at epoch 5 of 12, and card_check read OVERSUBSCRIBED: 'two of our own processes compute on this card (pids 15916 66340) ... they will each read slower than either would alone'.

CAUSE. card_check reads pids from the DEVICE - nvidia-smi - so every pid it prints is a WINDOWS pid. after.sh runs under MSYS bash, whose wait_for_pid tests liveness in MSYS pid space. The two spaces are unrelated, so 15916 named nothing in the space the check ran in, the check read 'already exited', and the chain fired at once. This is the same mismatch already recorded for testing git-bash liveness with a Windows pid tool, arriving from the opposite direction: here a Windows pid is handed to an MSYS test.

COST. One killed process (66340), roughly ten minutes of a shared card at half speed, and a timing reading on disagreed_ramp that cannot now be trusted for the epochs that overlapped. It also produced the DOUBLE-QUEUED and UNLOGGED verdicts that took the next two wakes to unpick, because the misfired chain and the chain it duplicated both stayed live.

THE FIX, in priority order. (1) wait_for_pid must REFUSE a pid it cannot see rather than treat unseen as exited - an unknown pid is the ambiguous case and firing is the destructive reading of it. (2) It should say which pid space it is testing in, so a caller handing it a card_check pid is told rather than obeyed. (3) queue_check should treat a 'pid:' marker as suspect on this platform and say so, the way it already refuses a watched file that does not exist.

WORKAROUND UNTIL FIXED: never arm on 'pid:'. Watch the marker in the log the chain actually writes - for an arm launched by after.sh that is the WATCHER's own stdout (logs/after_<arm>.log), not '<arm>_s<seed>.full.log', which only a run_train arm writes and which no arm writes under a name queue_check guesses.

title: Two-branch text-supervised 2.5D member, the shape behind the public 0.906 - the first mechanism-backed arm since the trunk lane closed
description:
Kimi's Q-Y addendum (2255z) identifies the public baseline behind the 0.906 board score: konradcinkusz/rsna-knee-abnormalities-efficiency-lb. A 2.5D DINOv2-small vision branch trained alongside a multilingual text branch (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2); test.csv carries no Report column, so the text path exists ONLY during training and the vision branch runs alone at inference.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE ARM THIS REPO ALREADY REFUTED. report_supervision.sh added a cosine auxiliary term pulling ONE study-level vision readout toward a sentence embedding of the whole report: 0.8272 control, 0.8219 at weight 0.3, 0.8209 at 1.0, monotone. That is mechanism (b), the auxiliary-loss form, which knee-iem6 declines on the grounds that no published medical gain exists for it. The public baseline is a different object: a genuine second BRANCH supplying a training signal to the trunk, closer to distillation than to a regulariser on a readout. The distinction is exactly the one Kimi's audit draws, and it is the reason the decline of (b) does not decline this.

WHY IT IS WORTH A CARD ARM. It is the only mechanism-backed candidate the project has had since the trunk lane closed EMPTY on radnet_family. Every other lane is a knob: member quality ceilings near 0.943, the stack lane closed 7/7, and seating is flat over seven board rows plus the external-corpus dose flat at one and two seats (corpusfull_v1 asks the six-seat point tonight). And the size is right rather than knob-sized - a single public model reading 0.906 on the board is a large number against solos of ours in the 0.86 range on holdout.

THE OTHER FACT IN THE ADDENDUM, WHICH CUTS THE OTHER WAY AND BELONGS ON knee-440m. That repo's own Models tab reads DINOv2-base 0.861 and DINOv2-large 0.5 - effectively random. So on the public gold-label set the LARGE trunk failed outright and the small one carried the score. ortho_dense is a ViT-L. Our supervision is not theirs (4,407 report-derived labels rather than 58 gold), so the datapoint does not transfer directly, but it is a live prior against depth on this task and it should be read before ortho_dense's low branch is written down as a fact about knee continuation.

OPEN QUESTIONS BEFORE ANYTHING IS ARMED, sent to Kimi 2306z: what the text branch's actual objective is (contrastive over pairs, distillation from text embeddings into vision features, or a joint head over concatenated branches), whether the two branches share a loss or are trained in stages, and which text field is used. The answer decides whether this is one arm or three.

title: queue_check calls an arm STRANDED without asking whether it already ran
description:
On 2026-09-01 a stale after.sh watcher (armed 2026-08-31, waiting forever on 'logs/ema224.full.log', a filename that predates the seed suffix) was killed. queue_check then reported eleven arms STRANDED — attend224, sided224, through224, decay224_high, clip224, decay224_low, warm224_brief, regions224, clip224_tight, warm224_long, focal224 — and told me to 'relaunch after.sh over them'.

All eleven had ALREADY RUN. Each has a <arm>_s<seed>.pt checkpoint on disk. Following the tool's own instruction would have put roughly 7 h of card into re-running knob arms on a lane the project has closed, which is the single most expensive mistake available right now.

The STRANDED reading is computed purely from the watcher table: arms owed by a dead watcher and by no live one. That is the right question for a watcher that died MID-QUEUE, and the wrong question for one that never fired at all — which is exactly the shape the MISARMED check on the line above had just diagnosed. The two findings contradict each other and the tool prints both.

FIX: before naming an arm stranded, ask whether its output exists — a checkpoint at PROCESSED/<arm>_s*.pt, or a ledger row, or an 'ARM DONE <arm>' marker anywhere in logs/. An arm with a checkpoint is DONE, not owed; report it as such (or say nothing) rather than as work to relaunch. An arm with no checkpoint and a dead watcher is the real finding and should keep the current wording.

This is the same class as the farseat_v1 and the two-member_curve-scans defects: a gate that is loud on the wrong denominator, where the cost is the READING rather than the machine.

title: Evaluate OrthoFoundation-L as a drop-in knee-MRI encoder init
description:
OrthoFoundation (arXiv:2601.18250, github.com/ytrsk/OrthoFoundation, MIT) is a 2026 DINOv3-L-based model continued with DINO-style SSL on 1.25M knee images (357k X-rays + 894k MRI slices), with released OrthoFoudation-L.pth weights. It reports ACL AUROC 0.9849, MCL 0.9334, cartilage lesion 0.9338, and is architecturally identical to the DINOv3-L backbone the project already uses. This makes it the strongest public knee-specific transfer source found so far, and a direct test of the 'strong init + in-domain SSL' mechanism.

This bead tracks whether it can be swapped in as an encoder init and whether it beats the existing DINOv3-L control. It is related to knee-ombx (external-data/supervised-pretraining), knee-vp8q (RAD-DINO control), and knee-8hn (DINOv3 licence/mount).
acceptance_criteria: A decision on whether to mount OrthoFoundation-L: (a) checkpoint loads through the existing DINOv3-L encoder path, (b) licence/Kaggle-shippability verified, (c) frozen or fine-tuned probe score compared to the current DINOv3-L baseline.
notes: PRICE (2026-09-02, required by knee-qxse): ~4 card-hours (12 epochs, 224 px x 12 slices, base224's read). EXPECTED GAIN: the pre-registered bands are >=0.8578 lane opens / >=0.8521 shippable seat / >=0.8502 matches control / below closes the in-domain trunk lane. P(clears 0.8521, the non-DINOv2 seat bar) ~ 0.3 and P(clears 0.8578) ~ 0.15, discounted because the FROZEN probe already reads ortholarge 0.7387 BELOW v3large 0.7446 and dinov2-large 0.7852 - the continuation did not help the features linearly, so the whole thesis rests on fine-tuning recovering what the probe cannot see. RATIO: 4 h for a ~30% shot at a shippable member on the one axis the pool has none of (architecture distance), plus a CLOSING reading on the low branch that retires external encoders entirely. Justified as much by the low branch as the high one: a sub-0.8502 result is worth having because it stops the project pricing external trunks, and that is an instrument value the high branch does not need to carry.

title: Q-U: does in-domain SSL continuation beat a strong init (DINOv2), not scratch?
description: Kimi's Q-T reply (2026-09-01T21:35Z) settles the knee-corpus transfer question with an honest null: no published knee->knee partial-label-overlap multi-label AUC delta exists. Evidence density is entirely form (d), external corpus as SSL substrate, which is the only form fastMRI can serve. BUT the strongest number (Zhang et al. 2024, fastMRI 10k unlabeled -> Stanford, 0.562 scratch -> 0.819 SSL) sits beside an ImageNet-init row at 0.824 - in-domain knee SSL TIED a generic supervised init and did not beat it. Our members initialise from DINOv2, a stronger init than ImageNet. Q-U asks for a measured continuation delta WITH the no-continuation control present, the corpus size at which it pays, whether the objective must match DINOv2's self-distillation, and the nearest honest negative. If the answer is no, this project has no measured route to 0.952 and that is what gets reported.
notes: Research completed: research/2026-09-02_fastmri_continuation_arithmetic.md. Key findings: (1) 35k single-coil slices sits below the 50k-300k low-data regime where in-domain SSL is shown to beat general pretraining (Konstantakos et al. 2025) and inside the regime where naive DINOv2 continuation collapses (dinov2#204). (2) OrthoFoundation shows positive continuation on 1.25M knee images incl 300k fastMRI slices, using DINOv3-L, batch 32, 4 A100s, AdamW cosine. (3) fastMRI ships RSS reconstructions; use those, not zero-filled IFFT. (4) OAI is larger and better matched than fastMRI/MRNet/SKM-TEA. Decision: do NOT arm a 35k fastMRI continuation; if ortho_dense clears, the next corpus should be OAI (or OAI+fastMRI), with forgetting safeguards.
