title: Curriculum is a SCHEDULE, not a reweight — and the disagreement-schedule cell is empty
description:
Measured on our own corpus, 12 epochs each, same recipe:

  disagreed_full     static difficulty tilt      0.8471
  disagreed_uniform  matched control (bootstrap) 0.8507
  certainty_ramp     difficulty SCHEDULE         0.8584

A static tilt toward hard studies COSTS 0.0036. Ramping difficulty over training PAYS 0.0077, above
the 0.0062 holdout floor. That is the same shape Zhou et al. ISBI 2023 report on elbow-fracture X-ray
(+0.0245 binary AUC from a VoG-ordered curriculum, no human difficulty annotation), and it is the only
supervision-axis intervention with both a published AUC delta and a reproduction here.

The 2x2 has one empty cell. Difficulty has two available signals: label certainty (report confidence)
and ensemble disagreement (train_disagreement). Certainty x schedule pays. Disagreement x static costs.
Disagreement x schedule is untested, and it is the cell where the two signals disagree about WHICH
studies are hard: certainty is what the labeller felt, disagreement is what the models cannot resolve.

Both mechanisms already exist in the tree: Disagreed(spread, alpha) in kneemri/training/sampling.py
and trainer.ramp_certainty(). The arm is an alpha ramp over the disagreement weights rather than a
fixed alpha, so no new sampler is needed.

PRICE: ~1.5 h card at 12 epochs. P(clears control + floor, i.e. >= 0.8569) ~ 0.3 given the certainty
ramp cleared its own by 0.0077 and the published curriculum effect is 3x our floor. P(flat but
decorrelated, a seat on a supervision-space axis) ~ 0.4. The static arm is the control already on
disk, so no control arm runs.
notes: PRICE: ~1.5 h card, 12 epochs, no control arm (both controls on disk). P(clears disagreed_uniform + floor, >=0.8569) ~0.3: the certainty schedule cleared its own control by 0.0077 and the published curriculum effect (Zhou et al. +0.0245) is 4x our floor, but the static arm on this same signal LOST 0.0036, so the schedule has to recover that before it pays anything. P(flat-but-rescued, 0.8471-0.8569, seat candidate on error correlation) ~0.45. P(dead, <=0.8471, closes the difficulty row with a negative) ~0.25. Every branch fills a cell; the arm is a finding either way. Arm: experiments/arms/disagreed_ramp.sh

title: Explore true 3D CNN path for knee MRI (MRNet-style) vs tubelet transformers
description:
Owner flagged the MRNet project (https://stanfordmlgroup.github.io/projects/mrnet/) as a possible 3D exploration branch. The repo already ingests MRNet (1,248 ACL studies merged into merged3) and has a tubelet trunk via V-JEPA2-L, but has not tried a dedicated 3D convolutional architecture like MRNet's per-view 3D CNN + global max-pool + logistic regression ensemble.

Questions to answer:
1. What is MRNet's actual architecture and reported AUC on ACL/meniscus/abnormal?
2. Does the repo have everything needed to train an MRNet-style 3D CNN on our slices (canonical decode, labels, folds)?
3. How does a 3D CNN differ from the V-JEPA2 tubelet in terms of inductive bias, memory, and likely AUC?
4. What would a minimal arm cost (card-hours, mount feasibility)?
5. Is there a published 3D CNN result on knee MRI that beats the project's DINOv2-based 0.85x members?

Acceptance: a go/no-go decision with a cost estimate, or a concrete arm spec if go.
notes:
Initial literature pass 2026-09-01:
- MRNet (Bien et al. 2018, PLOS Med) architecture: AlexNet backbone, per-series 3D CNN treated as a volume, global max pool, logistic regression over 3 series.
- MRNet internal validation AUC: abnormal 0.937, ACL 0.965, meniscus 0.847 (1,370 exams).
- External Rijeka ACL: 0.824 zero-shot, 0.911 when trained on external data.
- Repo already has MRNet corpus (1,248 ACL studies in merged3) and a tubelet trunk (V-JEPA2-L, 0.8343 holdout), but no dedicated 3D conv CNN like MRNet.
- The user's instinct is valid: MRNet-style 3D CNN is a distinct branch from both 2D slice transformers and tubelet transformers.
- Next step: decide whether to implement an MRNet-style arm or a modern 3D CNN (3D ResNet/I3D/nnUNet encoder) on our canonical cache.

title: Slot dropout: withhold a PRESENT slot during training
description: First supervision-axis regulariser here. Fill rates: AX_FLUID_FS 100%, SAG_FLUID_FS 98%, COR_FLUID_FS 93%, SAG_FLUID_NOFS 55%, COR_T1 60%, SAG_T1 57% - nearly half of all studies reach inference with slots the model has only ever seen filled. SlotScheme.presence already MASKS an absent slot rather than zero-filling, so the gap is not misrepresentation, it is that absence was never in the training distribution. Precedent at its real strength: Grovik 2021 npj Digital Medicine held AUC exactly FLAT (0.989 vs 0.989) while Dice rose 0.021 and FP/patient fell 7.0->3.6; Chrysochoou 2026 npj Precision Oncology beat zero-fill and synthesis on every missing-sequence cell. Both are segmentation and the one paper measuring AUC measured no gain, so this is armed as a diversity/supervision lever, NOT a solo-score lever. Code wired through augmentation/trainer/options/run_setup/flag_vocabulary/landed; owes unit tests and an arm with pre-registered branches.
notes: PRICE: ~1.5 h of card at 12 epochs (band_dense's recipe, dropout is a mask multiply and adds no memory). P(clears the 0.0062 floor as a SOLO) ~0.15 - the only precedent that measures AUC (Grovik 2021) measured it exactly flat, 0.989 vs 0.989, so a solo gain is not what the mechanism predicts. P(the flat-and-decorrelated branch, i.e. error correlation against champion members below every incumbent pair) ~0.4. EXPECTED VALUE IS IN THE SECOND BRANCH, and it is why the arm is worth 1.5 h: every closed axis here (seating, combiner, pooling, count, serving, decode) is a DECODE-space axis, competence_axis reads 81.7-82% of what separates 105 members as one scalar, and a member taught to survive a withheld acquisition is the first candidate for leaving that axis. Ratio: 1.5 h against a ~40% chance of the first new seat MECHANISM since seating closed, versus ~15% of a directional solo number. Priced as an INSTRUMENT on the supervision axis, not as a score improvement.
close_reason:
Slot dropout WORKS and is the best single member the project owns: 0.8592, converged (convergence_check: 1 converged, peak e9 of a 12-epoch budget, not truncated).

Against the members it has to beat: band_dense 0.8578 (+0.0014), certainty_ramp 0.8584 (+0.0008), base224 0.8502 (+0.0090). Both of the first two are inside the 0.0062 holdout noise floor, so the honest reading is DIRECTIONAL at the top of the pool rather than a new ceiling - but it is directional in the right direction, free, and mechanism-sound: withholding a PRESENT slot during training forces the head to read evidence from the slots that remain instead of leaning on the one that happens to carry the finding, which is the same argument that makes dropout work anywhere and is not a reweight of the loss.

It joins the roster at 0.8592. What it does NOT do is open a lane: the member-quality lane ceilings near 0.943 as an ensemble against a leader at 0.952, and seven board flats close reweight/add/swap/count. A better member is worth having and is not worth a slot.

title: RadImageNet DenseNet-121: a domain-supervised CNN trunk needs a non-AutoModel load path
description:
Every encoder in the registry loads through AutoModel.from_pretrained, so a trunk shipped as a bare state_dict has no load path. RadImageNet DenseNet-121 is the best-precedented candidate for the trunk-family axis (Nilay et al. report +0.031 from a cross-family ensemble containing it), and it is the empty cell on our pretraining grid: every trunk we own is either self-supervised (DINOv2/v3, ConvNeXtV2-FCMAE, V-JEPA2, RAD-DINO) or supervised on natural images (Swin IN-22k). None is supervised on medical images.

Measured 2026-09-01: the Lab-Rasool/RadImageNet HF mirror ships DenseNet121.pt as an OrderedDict of 725 keys prefixed backbone.0., which strip to a strict load into torchvision densenet121().features - 0 missing, 0 extra, 0 shape mismatch, 7.04M params, and (1,1024,14,14) out of a 448px read. Stride 32, dim 1024: the same output contract ConvNeXt-base and Swin-base already satisfy, so TrunkAsTokens.from_map applies unchanged. The Google-Drive plumbing Kimi priced at multiple hours is not needed.

Open: the input normalization RadImageNet trained under is unverified (asked as Q-L2), and the licence for a Kaggle mirror is unresolved (Q-L1) - a local arm needs neither, a submission needs both.
notes: VRAM measured 2026-09-01: at matched flags vram_need prices convnextv2-base (cnxbase) at 14443 MiB and radnet121 at 40880 MiB -- above the whole 32 GB card. arm_smoke refused the arm as written: 'NO ROOM radnet_family: card had no room: needs 40880 MiB, 30991 MiB free'. Dense connectivity concatenates every earlier feature map inside a block, so cost tracks resolution and depth, not the 7.04M parameter count. Ladder at 448 px: sl20 40880, sl14 29265, sl12 25393, sl10 21521, sl8 17649. At 336 px sl20: 23094. RESOLVED by dropping --train-size 448 -> 336 (and --vram-gb 16 -> 24) rather than cutting slices: 336 is the cache's own resolution (336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band) and cnx_own_recipe UPSAMPLES it to 448, so the deviation costs an upsampling factor, not information, where 20->12 slices would have cost eight real slices of the stack. Stated in the arm header as a deviation: a difference vs cnx_own_recipe is now pretraining AND upsampling.

title: ConvNeXt: honour cnx_own_recipe's PARTIAL branch — augmentation strength, not another rate rung
description: cnx_own_recipe scored 0.8186, landing in its own pre-registered PARTIAL band (0.80-0.83). That branch reads: 'the deficit is real but not all recipe, and the next knob is augmentation strength (never moved on this family) rather than another resolution step.' The branch binds. Do NOT run a 1.2e-3 rate rung on the strength of the ladder observation alone (see the sibling issue) — discarding a fired pre-registration is the defect that produced cnx_dense's retracted verdict. Arm = cnx_own_recipe.sh with augmentation strength raised, every other flag held. Bar context: the non-DINOv2 seat bar is 0.8521 and this family tops at 0.8186, so this is an instrument about whether our CNN numbers are under-read, not a member bet.
notes: Augmentation branch VOID (2026-09-01). The branch assumed the recipe's augmentation was off; it is not. kneemri/data/augmentation.py:60-68 declares the geometric transforms, experiments/recipe.sh:23 passes the flag that enables them, and kneemri/training/options.py:74 defaults it on. Any reading that treats the shipped members as un-augmented is wrong, and the branch that would have added augmentation is measuring a thing already present. What survives: the QUESTION of augmentation STRENGTH is untouched -- the defaults were never derived here -- but that is a knob, priced accordingly, not the branch this bead pre-registered.

MRNet (Stanford 2018) is decoded on disk: images_336px_12sl_mrnet.npy, 5.08 GB, 1250 exams, three slots (SAG_FLUID_FS / AX_FLUID_FS / COR_T1 against Rijeka's one), index and mask built 2026-08-29. It is in NO merged cache and has never trained anything, because labels/mrnet_acl.csv was never written: the pixels came from a Redivis export that ships arrays alone, and mrnet_labels.TableLabels exists precisely for that case but was never fed a directory.

RESOLVED HALF: the tables are public. techtech69/mrnet-knee-mri-stanford-aimi carries train-acl.csv, train-abnormal.csv, train-meniscus.csv and the three valid-*.csv, ~8 KB each. All six downloaded to raw/mrnet/ on 2026-09-01. TableLabels globs *<split>*acl*.csv, which matches them as named.

BLOCKER: MRNetCorpus reads its archive through zipfile.ZipFile and raw/mrnet/ holds EXTRACTED axial/coronal/sagittal directories with no zip, so build_mrnet cannot run the join. The decode does not need to be redone — only the table does, and it is derivable from index_336px_12sl_mrnet.json (a 1250-entry list of mrnet-NNNN) plus the CSVs plus the level mapping.

WHY IT IS WORTH A P1. The corpus axis is one of the two things the board record still calls open (the other is the trunk). Rijeka's 736 exams bought merged_blend +0.0063 over its control, and the per-label split says the gain is ENCODER TRANSFER rather than supervision: Lateral Meniscus +0.0196 on a finding Rijeka never labels. MRNet is 1250 exams from a THIRD site, 1.7x Rijeka, and would take the merged corpus from 5143 to 6393.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: only ACL is supervised here (mrnet_corpus's own docstring argues meniscus and abnormal must not be mapped onto columns they do not mean), so the abnormal/meniscus CSVs are downloaded but unwired. And the dose is not assumed linear - Rijeka's own was measured sub-linear.

THE SECOND HALF OF THIS BEAD is the survey nobody has done: WHICH other public knee-MRI corpora exist, under what licence, at what size, and with what findings labelled. Two are on disk by accident of what somebody happened to find. That is not a survey.

title: The best-board-score-by-member-count curve was fitted on an incomplete record: +0.024 is really +0.019, and 2-3 seats buy most of it
description:
RECOMPUTED 2026-09-01 over all 87 rows of comp/board.jsonl (scope: excluded dropped), against the table in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the-seat-axis-is-saturated-and-the-member-is-0.028-behind.md, which was built from 53 rows before board_check completed the record.

members: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 11 12 25
n:       5 5 4 12 5 12 19 5 1 1 1
best:    0.925 0.936 0.938 0.937 0.931 0.943 0.944 0.943 0.941 0.937 0.894

The document records 1 -> 0.914, 2 -> 0.921, 3 -> 0.913, 6 -> 0.938, 7 -> 0.937. Three of those five moved by more than the board quantum. Consequences:
  * 'ensembling buys +0.024 and then turns over' is really +0.019 from one seat to the best entry we own (0.925 -> 0.944).
  * A TWO-member entry reads 0.936 and a THREE-member 0.938. Everything from four seats up sits inside 0.937-0.944. So most of the ensembling gain on the completed record is bought by the second and third seat, not by getting to six.
  * The turnover at eight is gone: 8 -> 0.943, one tick under the best seven.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. Count and member quality are CONFOUNDED across these rows - the high-reading small entries are late ones built from better members, and no matched count sweep exists. This is not 'count is worth less than we thought' measured; it is the count table no longer supporting the claim it was quoted for.

WHAT SURVIVES. 'Slots do not go to seat permutations' (knee-xuj5) is independently measured and untouched: nine 6/7-member entries span 0.002, and every single-seat operation at the top since - holdswap_v1, vjepaseat_v1, spanseat_v1 - read flat.

CLASS OF DEFECT, and this is the reusable part: every board-wide table computed before 2026-08-25 was fitted on 34-58 of the submissions. board_transfer's +1.82 had the same cause (knee-8pp8). Any board aggregate quoted from a document older than that date must be recomputed before it is used.
notes: 2026-09-01 07:42Z: DO NOT spend a slot re-reading the count curve. I proposed a three-seat instrument (champion's first three seats, everything else held) to break the count/quality confound this bead names, then found the ladder is ALREADY on the board and was built deliberately at recent member quality: soloseat_v1 0.925 (1, 08-26), onepair_v1 0.936 (2, 08-28), trioseat_v1 0.938 (3, 08-29), fourseat_v1 0.937 (4, 08-29). Those four are consecutive days at the same pool, which is the closest thing to a matched count sweep this project owns -- the confound is smaller than this bead states for counts 1-4. It is counts 6-8 that stay confounded (0.943/0.944/0.943 spread over 08-20..08-31 with the pool changing underneath). A new count entry would be repeating an experiment whose result we hold.

title: The label lane was closed on the one ruler knee-9198 says is biased against label-side arms
description: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_label_lane_closes.md closes the label lane on blendlabels_s2026 reading +0.0003 peak and +0.0003 flat under label_combine.py's split-half estimator, plus seat_value +0.0001 and per-label routing +0.0009 (same order as knee-m69u's +0.0002 weighting ORACLE). Its result table is PROXY ONLY; the gold 58 appear in the framing lines and in no measurement. knee-9198, updated the SAME DAY, states the rule that any label-side arm from here reports BOTH numbers - proxy holdout AUC and supervision_gap over the 58 - precisely because a change moving a model toward annotation truth mechanically LOSES AUC against report labels, by up to the measured +0.045 (holdannot_s2026: 0.8487 proxy vs 0.8932 gold, same weights, same studies). So the lane was closed on the ruler that is structurally biased against what it was measuring. THE HONEST COUNTER, which is why this is P1 and not P0: 2026-08-30_the-gold-ruler-raises-everyone-and-orders-no-one.md plus knee-kddo show six members spanning 0.022 on gold give paired intervals ~0.03 wide, five of six pairs inseparable - so reading blendlabels on the 58 would very likely come back INCONCLUSIVE. That is the point. 'Closed' and 'cannot be resolved by any ruler we own' are different states and the record currently writes the second as the first. Cheapest fix costs no card: run supervision_gap over the 58 for blendlabels against its control, report the interval, and rewrite the closure to say which of the two states it is in.

title: context_width returned the head's INPUT width, so no feature-distillation arm had ever run
description: Readout.context is SlotHead.hidden wide (256); context_width() returned self.head_width = dim * POOL_PARTS[pool] = 2048, which is what the head is FED. run_setup built nn.Linear(2048, 1024) and feature_distillation fed it 256: 'mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (1x256 and 2048x1024)'. It died before epoch 0, so the arm read as queued-and-fine rather than dead, and knee-8009(b) had never run once. Fix is in the working tree (return self.head.hidden), blocked from committing by the model.py god-module finding. CLASS OF DEFECT: a crash before the first epoch line leaves no missing epoch to notice.

title: Rijeka knee MRI (736 labelled volumes) is on disk and unblocks supervised knee pretraining without MRNet
description:
knee-ombx wants supervised pretraining of the encoder on knee pathology, and has been blocked on obtaining MRNet. It does not need to be. D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kneemri_rijeka/kneemridataset.zip has been on disk unextracted the whole time: 736 volumes plus a metadata.csv carrying examId, seriesNo, aclDiagnosis (0 healthy / 1 partial / 2 complete ACL tear), kneeLR (laterality), and a per-volume ROI box (roiX/Y/Z, roiHeight/Width/Depth). 3.1 GB, 737 members, one CSV and 736 .pck files.

This is the supervised knee-pathology signal the MRNet plan wanted, and it is already local. The MRNet archive the owner downloaded (now at D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/mrnet, 7.3 GB, 1250 studies x axial/coronal/sagittal) is IMAGES ONLY - it is a flattened repack with none of the six train-/valid- label CSVs, so it cannot supervise anything until those are fetched separately.

Why it matters now: five consecutive board entries have read flat on every operation over the champion pool (reweight, add, swap, count, kind, fit), and what the record leaves open is what a member IS. A trunk pretrained on knee pathology labels rather than on natural images is exactly that axis, and it is the axis raptor_feat_fit is currently probing from the foreign-checkpoint side.

Three supervision signals, in descending order of expected value:
- aclDiagnosis as a 3-class ordinal head. Directly the knee-ombx mechanism.
- kneeLR as laterality supervision. The project already audits laterality (processed/laterality_audit.csv) and has crop/centre arms that assume it.
- the ROI box as localisation supervision, which the crop_mm / crop80_span family currently approximates with a fixed millimetre box.

KNOWN COST BEFORE ANY CARD TIME: .pck is a pickle container, not npy or DICOM, so it needs a decoder before a cache can be written. Do not hand-build the truncated cache - arm_check --smoke writes a 60-study _first60 array in under a minute and that is what proves the decode. Hand-decoding crop80_span's cache on 2026-08-19 cost a session and the tool already had the step.

FIRST THING TO CHECK, before anything is trained: whether the Rijeka corpus overlaps the RSNA competition corpus. foreign_overlap put raptor at 98.6 percent in-sample here, which is what voided raptor_solo's 0.8938 and cost a whole reading. A pretraining corpus that overlaps the holdout would do the same thing one level deeper and would be much harder to see.

PRICE: decoder plus cache maybe 1-2 h of wall time and no card; the pretraining run itself prices like swin_supervised's 12 epochs. knee-ombx put the odds of the mechanism at roughly 1 in 3 and called it the best ratio on the board; that pricing was for MRNet's 1250 studies with three label heads, so 736 studies with one strong head plus two auxiliary ones is a smaller dose and the odds should be read down accordingly, not carried over unchanged.
notes:
Found 2026-08-31 while relocating the MRNet download into the modality-first taxonomy (D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/<dataset>). The zip had never been opened. Listed without extracting via zipfile.namelist plus a read of metadata.csv.
Local inventory update: MRNet, Rijeka, fastMRI, SKM-TEA, KMAR-50K are on disk at D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/. fastMRI knee has 16k bbox annotations over 974 scans. See research/2026-09-02_external_knee_mri_data_access_audit.md section 9.
Scheme B dataloader design: research/2026-09-02_scheme_b_dataloader_design_local_corpora.md. fastMRI branch is highest-confidence first experiment.

title: peak8 did not refute the offline ruler: board_transfer says 0/269 resolved pairs inverted
description:
THE CLAIM ON RECORD IS WRONG, and it is steering the project. comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:2892 is titled
"the offline ruler fails" and comp/board.jsonl's peak8 row says "the offline argmax is NOT a board
argmax: selecting members by the fold-0 holdout picks a set that scores worse the more carefully it
is optimised". Two consequences were written from that: member_curve's greedy "may no longer be used
to JUSTIFY a slot", and seat_value's argmax "is a holdout artefact rather than a ranking".

WHAT THE TOOL SAYS. `python -m kneemri.evaluation.board_transfer`, run 2026-08-31 with BOTH peak8 rows
in the file: 33 ensemble entries, 421 orderable pairs, "inversions: 11/421 pairs the board ordered the
other way, 0/269 of the pairs the holdout resolved at all (a gap >= 0.0053)". Every one of the eleven is
printed UNRESOLVED, peak8's own two included:
  peak8 over gradeswap_v1: holdout +0.0037 (UNRESOLVED, under the floor), board -0.001
  peak8 over accumseat_v1: holdout +0.0036 (UNRESOLVED, under the floor), board -0.001
That is the same 0/N the 2026-08-29 refit reported at 0/127 and 0/233. peak8 did not break it; it
extended it to 269.

THE PREMISE IS ALSO FACTUALLY WRONG. "the best offline number this project owns (0.8731)" was true on
2026-08-24 and is not true now. Sorted from comp/board.jsonl:
  honest12       0.8751 -> board 0.937
  greedyseat_v1  0.8740 -> board 0.936
  peak8          0.8731 -> board 0.932
peak8 is THIRD offline and THIRD on the board. Against the two entries it is compared with, the holdout
gets the SIGN right both times and merely cannot resolve the gap:
  peak8 vs greedyseat_v1: holdout -0.0009 (UNRESOLVED, floor 0.0053), board -0.004
  peak8 vs honest12:      holdout -0.0020 (UNRESOLVED), board -0.005
  peak8 vs greedy7_v1:    holdout +0.0019 (UNRESOLVED), board -0.001  <- the only sign flip, one board tick
So "the harder a set is optimised the worse it scores" rests entirely on pairs the ruler itself declines
to order. There is no measured inversion to explain.

WHAT THE RULER ACTUALLY DOES, over 30 deduped ensemble rows carrying both numbers:
  ALL          n=30  Spearman +0.961  pairwise 390/421 = 0.926
  board>=0.925 n=21  Spearman +0.906  pairwise 173/197 = 0.878
  board>=0.930 n=13  Spearman +0.819  pairwise  57/68  = 0.838
The top-band degradation is what a 0.0062 offline floor against a 0.007-wide board band predicts, not
evidence of selection overfit.

A BIAS CORRECTION WAS TESTED AND DOES NOT HELP. member_curve.honest (member_curve.py:163-198) already
measures greedy selection bias, replicated in four logs (logs/greedy_all.log:191-207,
logs/honest_packaged.log:92-108, logs/honest_pool_20260829.log:189-202): +0.0025 to +0.0031 at 7-12
seats over 77-119 members. Subtracting it from the raw search-selected rows moved retro-prediction
DOWN, not up (ALL Spearman 0.961 -> 0.947; board>=0.930 0.819 -> 0.647), because the early four-seat
entries were searched over 10-22 members and a large-pool constant does not apply to them. The correction
is right for the row it was measured on (knee-jsgb: raw 0.8768 predicted 0.939 vs actual 0.936; corrected
0.8740 predicted 0.936, err +0.0001) and must not be applied as a blanket.

THE REAL DEFECT IS PLUMBING, NOT THE RULER. knee-jsgb closed 2026-08-30 with a standing instruction:
"Any future entry selected by search must be entered in board.jsonl bias-corrected, never raw." peak8
shipped 2026-08-31, one day later, greedy-selected, and its row carries the RAW 0.8731 with an
offline_scope that discusses fold-0 scoreability and never mentions selection bias. Corrected to ~0.8704
it predicts 0.934 against an actual 0.932 (raw predicts 0.936). The row disobeys a rule the project had
already written down, and board_check does not enforce it.

WHAT TO DO
 1. Correct the peak8 row's offline_scope to name the selection bias, as greedyseat_v1's does.
 2. Rewrite comp/SUBMISSIONS.md:2892's section: peak8 is a THIRD fold-0 anchor extending board_transfer
    to 0/269, which is a good result for the slot, not a refutation.
 3. Reinstate member_curve's greedy for slot justification WITH the correction, and re-open seat_value's
    argmax. Both were retired on this reading.
 4. Add the assertion to board_check: a row whose entry was search-selected must carry a bias-corrected
    offline, the same way a row's offline must be read on studies the entry did not train on.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. Nothing about the ~0.008 blind-vs-fold-0 structural gap, which is untouched and
still explains why an all-fold-0 entry cannot reach 0.944. And nothing licenses firing on a sub-0.0053
offline preference: the ruler does not resolve those, which is exactly what it correctly reports.

title: switch_coverage counts a SCRIPT as an ARM: the 'sixty-one keys all varied' closure is a survey wearing a measurement's clothes
description:
normcount224's ledger entry (README:5005-5021, 2026-08-27) claims the flag surface is 'CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT rather than by survey'. That claim rests on switch_coverage.armed() (kneemri/experiments/switch_coverage.py:79-81), which scrapes --flag TOKENS out of experiments/**/*.sh text. It cannot distinguish an arm that RAN from a script that merely exists.

Confirmed hole: --head-lr is counted covered because arms/headlr_dense.sh:57 mentions it. That arm has never run — its name appears 0 times in the 6555-line ledger. switch_coverage.py:50-57 itself already lists head_lr among five switches 'landed-checked, stamped, and never once RUN', so the module contradicts its own coverage number.

WHY IT MATTERS: the closure was used to stop looking for recipe levers. If the true covered set is smaller than 61, the 'no unexplored flag remains' reading is wrong by an unknown margin, and every downstream 'the recipe axis is closed' statement inherits it.

FIX: armed() must join against the LEDGER (a run with a recorded holdout), not against script text. Report three states, not two: never scripted / scripted-never-run / run. Re-derive the coverage number and correct the README entry with the real one.

Found during the knee-s9cr 224 px audit, 2026-08-31.

title: The twin-transfer route to a per-finding vote is dead three ways, and vote.py does not say so
description:
Someone reading kneemri/inference/vote.py sees LabelQualityRank, sees it has never shipped, greps board.jsonl, finds zero per-finding entries, and proposes fitting it on the champion seats' fold-0 TWINS to get around the --fold -1 contamination. That route was proposed and killed on 2026-08-31 without spending a card or a slot. It will be proposed again, because nothing at the point of discovery says otherwise.

WHY IT IS DEAD.

(1) THE AXIS IS CLOSED, MEASURED, FOUR TIMES. knee-xsfc closed on the pre-registered clause 'if the honest per-label read does not beat flat, the vote axis closes for good and no further rule is written'. LabelQualityRank honest vs flat: +0.0002 (42 members/909), +0.0001 (77 members/909), +0.0011 (109 members), +0.0000 (four-seat shipping shape), +0.0001 (six-seat one-decode shipping shape). Every one under the +0.0015 seat_value floor.

(2) THE OVERFIT GAP PRICES THE SHRINKAGE CURVE WITHOUT RUNNING IT. The obvious objection is that 72 fitted parameters need shrinkage toward flat and the reading should be reported as a function of it. It does not need running. A shrinkage curve interpolates between flat and the unshrunk fit, so the FIT-ON-SELF number is the upper envelope of the entire curve -- and it is +0.0004 to +0.0007. The rule barely beats flat EVEN WHEN GRADING ITS OWN HOMEWORK. So every point of the shrinkage curve is bounded in [+0.0000, +0.0007] by construction. There is nothing in the per-label quality table to find, which coheres with competence_axis: member quality is 81.7% of pool spread, so members differ in overall strength, not in WHICH labels they are good at.

(3) THE TWIN TRANSFER ADDS A STEP THAT MOVES THE EXACT QUANTITY BEING FITTED. Per final_fit_six.sh, every _ff seat is its _s2026 twin plus '--fold -1 --ema', and every _cf seat is its _ff plus '--calibrated-targets'. So four of the champion's six seats (grade_ladder_cf, lr4e-5_ws_cf, through_dense_cf, final_ws_cf) differ from their proposed fold-0 twins by TWO trained variables besides the fold. And --calibrated-targets is the most per-label-heterogeneous lever in the ledger: on calib_span its MEAN was flat (-0.0020) while Effusion read -0.0212*, PF OA +0.0170* and Baker's -0.0167*, three labels clearing their own paired half-widths. It rearranges which labels a member is good at while leaving the mean alone. That is precisely and only the quantity LabelQualityRank fits. A per-label weight table fitted on the twin is fitted on the wrong per-label profile, on the one axis being transferred. So the transfer version is strictly WORSE than the +0.0007 fit-on-self bound, not better.

(4) THE INFORMATION CAP. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_the_pool_is_redundant_not_the_task.md: 0.0565 bits of epistemic disagreement in a 0.6807-bit pool (8.3% reducible across the roster, 12.7% on honest12). A vote rule can only redistribute weight within the disagreement; it cannot create any. The measured 0.0000-0.0015 spread across all five rules is what that cap looks like from the other side.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY FIX (the point of this bead):

- kneemri/inference/vote.py: LabelQualityRank's docstring still reads as an OPEN invitation -- 'It exists to be read on a SPLIT HALF by vote_ceiling ... because the gap between those two is the measurement'. It HAS been read, four times. Give it the same MEASURED-AND-CLOSED paragraph MedianLogit carries, with the numbers and the overfit-gap argument, so the class states its own verdict at the point of discovery. QualityWeightedRank's docstring has the same staleness ('has to be read on a split half' -- it was).
- Add the twin-transfer route by name, so the specific way around the contamination is refused in advance rather than re-derived.

SECOND DEFECT, INDEPENDENT, found on the way: comp/members.roster calls calib_span_hold_s2026 'the champion's own calib_span_ff twin'. It is not. Per the arms, calib_span_hold = calib_span + '--hold-annotations'; calib_span_ff = calib_span + '--fold -1 --ema'. The correct fold-0 twin of calib_span_ff is calib_span_s2026, which is ALSO on the roster. This matters beyond pedantry: the ledger measures the calibration lever's sign as INVERTED across exactly that hold/non-hold boundary (band_span_hold 0.8493 -> calib_span_hold 0.8565 = +0.0072, against band_span 0.8565 -> calib_span 0.8545 = -0.0020, a 0.0092 swing). So the mislabelled twin is not merely a different member, it is one sitting on the far side of a measured sign inversion of the seat's own defining flag. Fix the roster comment.

THIRD, minor: comp/kernels/kneemri-pixgroup says QualityWeightedRank is 'structurally unfittable here'. True of the champion's members, but it reads as an open problem awaiting a route rather than a closed axis. One cross-reference to knee-xsfc would have stopped this.

title: Asymmetric label smoothing with SHARPENING of confident cells (Rep-GLS) — the published lever we do not have, and our data says it points the wrong way
description:
EXTERNAL RESULT (research/2026-08-31_report_label_noise_and_uncertainty_heads.md). Rep-GLS (arXiv 2508.02495) is our labelling scheme, published: an LLM parses each radiology report into per-finding uncertainty keywords, a small network maps keywords to a smoothing rate r in (-1,1), and the per-class loss is (1-r)*L_CE + r*L_uniform. On MIMIC-CXR-JPG, 14 diseases:

  BCE baseline                          79.63
  end-to-end, no expert RGN pretraining 80.27
  softening only (r >= 0)               81.56
  full, sharpening enabled (r < 0)      84.14

Softening uncertain cells buys +1.93. SHARPENING confident cells buys a further +2.58 — the larger half of the total gain.

WHAT WE HAVE. Only the softening half. Supervision.applied maps reader certainty to measured agreement 0.08/0.28/0.68/0.82/0.94, so even a maximally confident report is softened relative to a hard 1.0; weight_floor gives 0.25 + 0.75*conf and only ever DOWN-weights. No term anywhere pushes a confident cell past plain BCE. On their ablation that is the bigger lever and we have none of it.

WHY IT IS NOT A FREE ADOPT. Their sharpening assumes a confident report statement is TRUE — their expert rate table gives 'positive' r = -0.2 explicitly. Our supervision_gap says the radiologist agrees only 65.3% where the report says YES, and noise_binding finds 108 confident false positives, 15.8% of annotated cells, all verdict YES. Sharpening drives the model harder onto exactly those cells. The published lever points the wrong way on our corpus, and it points wrong precisely where it is largest.

BLOCKED ON the extractor-vs-reader audit of the 108 (sibling P0). That audit decides this bead:
* If the 108 are mostly EXTRACTION failures, then confident report statements ARE mostly true once the extractor is fixed, and sharpening becomes adoptable — but only AFTER the extractor fix, and it should be re-derived against the corrected labels rather than the current ones.
* If the 108 are genuine reader disagreement, this bead CLOSES UNBUILT and the closure is a real finding: it says our corpus differs from MIMIC-CXR in a way that makes the field's larger label lever unavailable to us, and that is worth writing into the interpretation.

DESIGN NOTE IF IT IS EVER BUILT. Their two-stage form (expert-supervised rate network, then training) beat end-to-end by 3.87, so a hand-derived rate table is the right shape and matches how MEASURED_AGREEMENT was built. Do not reach for the end-to-end version first. Note also that r is per-FINDING per-STUDY in their scheme, which is the 'per-STUDY confidence rather than a per-FINDING constant' door that finding_calib_dense's post-mortem explicitly left open.

title: Exit-127 arm death recurs with --no-sync and .venv-arm both in force; no watchdog noticed 45 min of idle card
description:
base_clean run 1 died mid-epoch-3 at 2026-08-31T14:34Z: exit 127, no traceback, no OOM, throughput flat 486 img/s to the last recorded step, peak 27.49 GB against a 32 GB card. Identical signature to the 2026-08-13 event documented at experiments/lib.sh:588, whose cause was uv re-syncing the environment under the running interpreter. Both fixes that event bought were active here — UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv-arm (lib.sh:29) and 'uv run --no-sync' (lib.sh:591) — and .venv-arm/Scripts/python.exe has today's date nowhere near it. So the cause is open.

Two separable defects.

(1) CAUSE UNKNOWN. Candidates not yet excluded: the ARM_SRC snapshot tree being removed or rewritten mid-run; a Windows-side kill; a driver/runtime fault that exits without a Python-level traceback. Next occurrence should capture: snapshot dir mtime and existence at death, Windows event log around the timestamp, and whether nvidia-smi logged an Xid.

(2) NOBODY NOTICED. The card sat free for ~45 minutes and only a hand-run card_check found it. queue_check guards watcher liveness for QUEUED chains; nothing guards a single running arm against silent death. A watchdog that compares the arm log's mtime against the recorded seconds-per-epoch and shouts past ~1.5x is cheap and would have bought back most of that 45 minutes. This is the higher-value half: the cause may stay unknown, and the idle card must not.

(3) Minor, same incident: lib.sh's ARM FAILED line printed a path that does not exist — it said base_clean.full.log while _arm_log had written base_clean_s2026.full.log (ARM_LOG_NAME is applied when writing but not when reporting the failure). Cost one wasted tool call chasing a missing file.

title: attribution.py's occlusion maps are the LESS faithful readout — captum scores them worse than attention on 12 of 12 findings
description:
Measured 2026-08-31 under knee-wgaa (commit 860a99a2), by captum's captum.metrics.infidelity and sensitivity_max, on attend_true_s2026, 24 studies, centred window. Comparing the SLOT ATTENTION readout against the occlusion attribution kneemri/evaluation/attribution.py produces:

    infidelity        attention 0.037-0.125   occlusion 0.052-0.188
    sensitivity_max   attention 0.70-0.90     occlusion 0.88-2.41

Attention is more faithful on 12 of 12 findings on BOTH metrics.

WHY THE SENSITIVITY NUMBER IS THE SERIOUS ONE. sensitivity_max above 1.0 means the explanation changes MORE than the signal does under small perturbations of the features — the diagnostic is noisier than the thing it is explaining. Occlusion reaches 2.41. An explanation that unstable is not a weak signal, it is a signal about the perturbation procedure.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE MODULE. Nothing had ever checked this. The occlusion maps were trusted because they existed and because they were the only attribution the project had. This is the same failure shape as the fabricated board constant and as raptor_solo's contaminated 0.8938: a plausible artefact in the right range, with no instrument pointed at it.

OWED:
 1. Sweep past readings that rested on an occlusion map and mark which conclusions they carried. Any that are load-bearing get re-read against the attention readout.
 2. Then either FIX attribution.py — the likely cause is the occlusion window/baseline choice, and a baseline that is itself off-manifold is the classic source of exactly this instability — or DEMOTE it with a docstring note saying which readout to prefer and why, so the next reader does not re-trust it.
 3. Do not delete it. The negative is about the current parameters, not proof the approach cannot work; record the mechanism that failed so a later use is re-tested rather than assumed dead.

CREDIT WHERE DUE: this is the payoff of using a mature library rather than a hand-rolled check. A hand-written faithfulness score would have had nothing auditing IT, and would most likely have been tuned until the existing maps looked fine.

title: Steal systole's frozen-TestSet + generalisation-matrix design for the OOD read (knee-l8ax)
description:
knee-l8ax needs a scorer that runs OUR member on a FOREIGN corpus — a direction no existing module covers (foreign_member, foreign_gate, foreign_ruler, foreign_overlap, board_transfer, ruler_transfer ALL run the opposite way, foreign checkpoint on our corpus). So it is new code, and the shape it should take already exists next door.

SOURCE. D:/personal_projects/cardiac-seg — core/data/ingest/testsets.py and cardioseg/evaluation/matrix.py. Three ideas, in descending value:

1. AUTOMATIC OOD-vs-LEAK FLAG PER CELL. Every score in the matrix is labelled by reconstructing what the model saw from the model's OWN saved config, with seen = train u val. This is the defect we bled on: raptor_solo's 0.8938 stood as evidence until somebody thought to run foreign_overlap and found 896 of 909 studies in-sample. That one cell was carrying the whole 'compression goes negative at the top' reading plus eleven of fifteen apparent ruler inversions. Systole makes forgetting the check impossible; we make it a thing you remember. Highest-value idea in the file.

2. A TEST SET IS A CODED PREDICATE + A SHA256 LOCK over its resolved subject ids, not a manifest string and not a glob. If the store grows or an id changes, the lock mismatches and it is a HARD ERROR, never a silently different denominator. Directly applicable to our foreign caches (Rijeka, MRNet), which are built per-geometry and are exactly the kind of thing that drifts under you.

3. THE MATRIX IS ANY MODEL x ANY FROZEN CORPUS, pure inference, each model loaded with ITS OWN preprocessing. That last clause matters here: foreign_member already measured that the same published checkpoint reads 0.9167 through their decode and 0.8819 through our best cache, a -0.0348 shortfall that is entirely the feed. A matrix that does not carry per-model preprocessing would attribute that gap to the model.

SO: build knee-l8ax's scorer as a MATRIX WITH A LEAK FLAG, not a one-off Rijeka script. Same wall-clock, and it then answers every later foreign-corpus question without new code.

Constraints already recorded on knee-l8ax: the Rijeka cache images_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka.npy matches swin_supervised/swin_distill_fit geometry EXACTLY; Rijeka labels ACL only; MRNet only exists at 336px/12sl; knee-yu9k records build_rijeka was uncallable; verify the Rijeka index actually carries labels before promising the read.

title: [bug] The offline-to-board line 'board = 1.37 x offline - 0.2598' is fabricated; the real slope at our operating point is ~0.95
description:
ORIGIN. This constant was produced in-session on 2026-08-31 and quoted repeatedly as if it were a fitted repo constant, including to the owner while pricing base_clean. A repo-wide grep for '1.37' and '0.2598' returns hits ONLY inside .venv/ (kagglesdk version string, matplotlib test fixtures). It is in no module, no doc, no bead. It survived several context compactions because it kept being restated in prose, which is the only place it ever existed.

WHY IT IS WRONG IN KIND, not just in value. kneemri/evaluation/board_transfer.py opens with the heading 'PAIRS, NOT A REGRESSION' and argues the case explicitly: offline is LLM-read report labels on our holdout, board is radiologist annotations on the hidden set, and the two were never meant to agree on LEVEL -- only on ORDER. It reports a median of pairwise ratios for exactly that reason. Fitting a line is the thing that module was written to refuse.

WHAT THE DATA SAYS. comp/board.jsonl holds 83 rows; 36 carry both a numeric offline and a board score, 32 of them ensembles.
  * OLS over all 32 ensemble rows: slope 1.945
  * OLS over the top 16 (offline >= 0.867), which is where we operate: slope 0.953
  * board_transfer's own pairwise median, top regime: +0.99 [+0.77, +1.18]
1.37 matches none of these. The whole-record and top-regime slopes differ by 2x because the relation is CURVED, which is the second reason a single line is the wrong shape.

THE COMPOUNDING ERROR. Max offline ever observed is 0.8751 -> board 0.937. The champion at 0.944 has NO numeric offline; 38 board rows lack one. So 'board 0.944 implies offline 0.879' inverted a nonexistent line onto a point outside the dataset, and the projection to 0.8836 sits beyond every offline reading ever taken. Extrapolation past the end of the data, presented as arithmetic.

CONSEQUENCE FOR PRICING, since this changed a live decision. base_clean was sold to the owner as +0.0062 solo -> +0.0085 board -> top-3, at P~0.35. At the real slope (~0.95, no amplification) and with a new member entering as one seat of six or seven rather than moving the ensemble one-for-one, the ensemble gain is ~+0.001-0.003 and the board gain the same, against a board quantum of 0.001. P(beats the champion) is ~0.10. The arm keeps its INSTRUMENT value (it removes the four-flag confound that base_dense, v3base_dense and raddino_normfix are all quoted on) and has no credible score value.

RELATED, AND THE OWNER RAISED IT: 'ensemble = best-single + 0.0143' (knee-urvf) has the same defect in waiting. It is fitted over a regime where every member sits within ~0.01 of the others. Equal-weight averaging gives a new member weight 1/N, so a member far ahead of the pool is DILUTED, not amplified, and the sum-law inverts. No member in the fit was ever far ahead, so the fit cannot see its own ceiling. Do not price a step-change member with it.

FIX: quote board_transfer's regime-local pairwise ratio with its interval, never a slope-intercept line, and never invert one to manufacture an offline number for an entry that has none.

title: Does the distilled trunk generalise better OFF-distribution? The one axis swin_distill_fit was never scored on
description:
OWNER'S QUESTION 2026-08-31: could a distilled pretrained model beat a supervised one on a NEW dataset, via better generalisation? Real mechanism -- soft teacher targets carry inter-class structure a hard label discards, and distillation is a stronger regulariser than label fitting; flatter minima and better shift behaviour are the standard reported consequence (born-again nets, self-distillation, OOD-robustness distillation).

WHAT THE EXISTING ARM DID NOT MEASURE. swin_distill_fit read -0.0077 against swin_supervised on fold-0 of OUR corpus: same reader, same decode, same population. That is in-distribution FIT. It is silent on generalisation. The interpretation written today (2026-08-31_distilling_logits_is_not_pretraining.md) names 'stage one undertrained' as its caveat and does NOT name this one, which is the larger of the two.

THIS IS knee-avzz FROM THE OTHER SIDE -- 'the offline ruler is same-distribution and blind to robustness'. Same complaint, reached from the audit rather than from an arm.

THE READ IS ALREADY AFFORDABLE, no training and no submission slot. Both checkpoints are on disk, and images_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka is built at EXACTLY the geometry both were trained at (336 px, 20 slices, band 0.1-0.9). Different hospital, scanner and population.

CONSTRAINT, stated so it is not discovered later: Rijeka labels ACL only, so this prices ONE finding, not the mean. The comparison must be stated on ACL or not at all. MRNet would add meniscus but is only built at 12sl and needs a rebuild to join the 20sl geometry.

BRANCHES, before the run:
* distilled trunk loses LESS on Rijeka than supervised does -> the write-up's scope is wrong, knee-8009 (a) reopens as a ROBUSTNESS lever rather than closing as a fit lever, and the same OOD read is owed to every arm closed on the same-distribution ruler.
* both lose the same -> the logit-target reading survives contact with the axis it was never tested on, which is worth more than the original result.
* distilled loses MORE -> the logit trunk is worse on both axes and (a) closes harder.

OWNER'S OWN CAVEAT, recorded: the hidden test is likely similar to our data, so this may not transfer to the competition. Counter-datum, not proof: board_transfer fits board = 1.37 x offline - 0.2598, and a slope of 1.37 means offline deltas AMPLIFY rather than transfer one-for-one. Prevalence and metric scaling can produce that too, so 'similar' is likely and 'identical' is not established.

PRICE: minutes of card (inference only), 0 slots.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-31T14:19Z, BEFORE planning the run. The price is not what the bead assumed.

NO TOOL RUNS THIS DIRECTION. Every foreign-corpus module in kneemri/evaluation/ serves a FOREIGN checkpoint through OUR corpus, which is the reverse of what this bead needs:
  * foreign_member.py -- serves a published checkpoint through ITS OWN decode, records it as one of our members.
  * foreign_gate.py -- the plumbing oracle scoring what foreign_member serves. Split from it by import-linter.
  * foreign_ruler.py -- joins a foreign checkpoint's PUBLISHED per-finding AUCs to our 58 radiologist-annotated studies. No inference at all.
  * foreign_overlap.py -- whether an entry trained on the studies it is being scored on.
  * board_transfer.py / ruler_transfer.py -- offline-to-board fits, not corpus transfer.

So OUR member on a FOREIGN corpus has no entrypoint. This needs a small scorer: load one of our checkpoints, run it over the Rijeka cache at its native geometry, score the labels Rijeka actually carries. That is code, not a CLI invocation, and it is the reason this bead cannot simply be 'run it when the card frees'.

WHAT IS STILL CHEAP. The cache is right: images_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka is built at EXACTLY the geometry swin_supervised and swin_distill_fit were fitted at, so no rebuild and no re-decode. Both checkpoints are on disk. The run itself is inference over one foreign corpus -- minutes of card, 0 slots. Only the scorer is new.

TWO THINGS TO VERIFY BEFORE WRITING IT:
  * whether index_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_rijeka.json carries the labels, or whether they must be joined from the raw Rijeka annotations.
  * knee-yu9k records that build_rijeka was UNCALLABLE (--spacing collided with CacheFlags --spacing). The cache on disk predates or dodges that, but whatever wrote it should be confirmed rather than assumed, because a cache built by a broken builder is the harness-suspect branch of this very arm.

SEQUENCING. Blocked twice over: the card is saturated by base_clean until ~16:50Z, and knee-wgaa already holds the one coding-subagent slot. This goes next after that, ahead of any new training arm.

title: base_clean: dinov2-base at the stackfit recipe with the three confounds removed
description:
base_dense read -0.0118 against stackfit and is quoted as 'the bigger trunk is worse'. run_comparison's own diff shows FOUR flags changed, not one: batch 12->6, ema True->False, calibrated_targets True->False, variant small->base. Three of the four are known-positive levers, all lost in the arm read as a verdict on width. v3base_dense (-0.0176) carries the identical confound. Gradient accumulation (knee-55k8) has since landed, so --batch 6 --accumulate 2 restores the control's effective batch of 12 at half the activations. This arm is stackfit's line flag-for-flag with --variant base as the only change.

PRICE: ~4.5 h of card, 0 slots.
P(clears +0.0062) ~ 0.35.

Branches are pre-registered in experiments/arms/base_clean.sh. The FLAT branch is the informative one: a tie says width itself is worth nothing at this operating point and closes scale as a quality lever, sending the search to knee-nj4l axes 2 (per-finding routing) and 3 (slice budget). A tie still goes to member_axes + seat_value first — a 768-wide member that ties on the mean is the different-in-KIND candidate pool_census says is missing.
notes: READ (D44, 2026-09-07): base_clean_s2026 ran 2026-08-31, 3.1 h, converged (peak e7 of 11). Ledger 0.8570 vs calib_dense_hold 0.8634 = -0.0064; 896 L75mid 0.8886 vs 0.8948 = -0.0062; swap vs calib_span -0.0005; corr to block 0.918. Pre-reg branch < +0.003 = TRUNK AXIS CLOSED at this recipe. Ledger row and # reading: line added 2026-09-07 (the arm had neither for seven days).

title: The run harness is bash and the checks are Python - the bash half is where the silent failures are
description:
13 non-arm shells: experiments/{after,queue,await_free_card,displacement,lib,lib_staleness_check,recipe,stub_lib}.sh, comp/{poll_scores,prepare_submission,push,submit_when_ready}.sh, inbox/watch.sh. They are a run harness written in bash, on Windows, while every CHECK is already Python in kneemri.experiments (arm_check, queue_check, card_check, ledger_check, trajectory_check, convergence_check).

The split is not cosmetic and there is a measured cost. On 2026-08-31 at ~10:18 UTC after.sh read swin_distill_fit's smoke as BROKEN (a false alarm - the arm builds its own --encoder-weights input on its first line), printed '0 refused', and then was gone from the process table with the card free and stage two never started. ~15 minutes of card time lost, and it would have been hours if nobody looked. The bug was in the bash half; the Python half (card_check) is what caught it. See the sibling bead on the smoke defect.

This is also the owner's standing directive applied to this tree: everything a part of a pipeline, roughly ten pipelines, no confused single files.

TARGET SHAPE: bash keeps exactly one job - one invocation per experiment, which is what it is good for and what makes an arm readable as a pre-registration. Orchestration (gating on a marker, waiting for a card, chaining arms, launching a watcher) moves into the Python package beside the checks that already inspect it, where a dead chain is an exception rather than a missing process.

title: after.sh's smoke gate cannot smoke an arm that BUILDS its own input, and the chain died on it
description:
swin_distill_fit.sh exports its own encoder file (kneemri.training.fitted_encoder) as its first line, then passes it to run_train via --encoder-weights. ArmSmoke read the arm's invocation, resolved --encoder-weights to a path that does not exist YET, and reported 'BROKEN swin_distill_fit: FileNotFoundError'. It did not refuse (0 refused), but the chain nevertheless ended there: after.sh was gone from the process table at 10:19 UTC on 2026-08-31, the card was free, and swin_distill_fit had never started. Stage one had completed cleanly (ARM DONE swin_distill_pre, holdout 0.8177 at epoch 3), so ~15 minutes of card time was lost between the stages and would have been hours if nobody looked.

Two separate defects, and they should not be fixed as one:

(1) THE SMOKE IS WRONG ABOUT THIS ARM. An arm whose input is produced by an earlier line of the SAME arm is unsmokeable by construction under the current reading, which only sees run_train's flags. Every future two-stage arm has this shape, and distillation-as-pretraining is the pattern the project just committed to. Either the smoke runs the arm's prelude (correct, and it costs seconds here), or it recognises a --encoder-weights path an earlier line writes and declines to judge it, saying so.

(2) A BROKEN SMOKE THAT DOES NOT REFUSE SHOULD NOT BE ABLE TO END THE CHAIN. 0 refused means proceed; the chain proceeded to nothing. Whatever consumed the BROKEN line stopped after.sh without a refusal and without an error of its own, which is the worst of the three outcomes because the log reads as a clean check.

Relaunched swin_distill_fit by hand at 10:19 UTC; the export ran fine as the arm's first line, which is the proof that the smoke's FileNotFoundError was about ordering and not about the arm.

title: Training-stage instrument hook points: start, middle, end
description: The owner's framing: instruments are multipliers on the information content of every arm, and an instrument that must be REMEMBERED is skipped on exactly the arm whose mean looks decided. So the train pipeline gets declared hook points and the instruments hang off them rather than off a human. START: harness assertions (the flag LANDED, the data census, the control declared - arm_check and arm_read --assert already exist). MIDDLE: trajectory_check, which already exists and already truncates. END: convergence_check, arm_read per label, roster_check. The work is the SEAM, not new detectors: most of these are written and none of them are scheduled. Depends on the taxonomy child because a hook point is a stage boundary and the stages are not named yet.

title: DECIDE: the ~10 named pipelines, their stages, and what a stage owns
description: Turn the audit's map into a named taxonomy: roughly ten pipelines, each a sequence of declared stages, each module belonging to exactly one. The candidate list from the epic (ingest/corpus-build, label-table build, train, per-arm read, member/roster curation, ensemble fit, package/kit, submit, board record, architecture+gates) is a starting point to be ARGUED against the audit, not adopted. The decision must state what a stage OWNS - at minimum: which instruments run at its boundary, and what it is allowed to import - because a taxonomy that only names folders is a rename. Record it as a decision doc so the next reorganisation is measured against a written intent.

title: AUDIT: every module in core/ and kneemri/ mapped to a candidate pipeline stage
description: The blocking child; nothing in this epic moves until it is written. Read the modules themselves, not greps about them: for each module in core/ and kneemri/, record (a) does it have a main(), (b) who imports it, (c) which candidate pipeline stage would own it, (d) if none would, say why it exists. Output is a committed document under docs/architecture/, not a bead comment. It must name the ORPHANS explicitly - a module with a main() that nothing schedules and nothing imports is the defect the epic is about - and it must name the modules that would belong to TWO stages, because those are where the taxonomy is wrong rather than the code. kneemri/evaluation/ alone is 48 modules; the audit is the expensive half of this epic and the reorganisation is the cheap half.

title: EPIC: ~10 named pipelines own every module — no more loose single files
description:
OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-31: 'that also means architecture, folder structure, reorganization, putting them at start / end / mid of training logging, mlflow and other and so on. no more confused single files - everything must be a part of a pipeline. and we dont need more than 10 pipelines (of course thats an approximation)'.

THE STATE THAT PROVOKED IT. kneemri/evaluation/ alone holds 48 modules, each a CLI with a main(). They are individually well-argued and collectively unowned: nothing says when member_divergence runs, nothing runs run_comparison after an arm finishes, and the near-miss on stack224 (a flat mean nearly closing the slice-coverage axis, rescued only by a hand-rolled per-label query) is what an unowned instrument costs. arm_read was written the same day to make ONE of those reads mechanical; the directive is that this should not have needed a bespoke module - the read belongs to a pipeline stage.

THE SHAPE. A pipeline is a NAMED sequence with declared stages, and every module belongs to exactly one. Roughly ten, an approximation not a target. The candidate decomposition, to be argued in the audit child, not assumed here: ingest/corpus-build, label-table build, train, per-arm read, member/roster curation, ensemble fit, package/kit, submit, board record, architecture+gates. Instruments hang off stage boundaries - a diagnostic that runs at the START of training (harness assertions, data census), the MIDDLE (trajectory_check, which already exists and already truncates), and the END (arm_read per label, convergence_check, roster_check).

WHY IT IS P1 AND NOT HYGIENE. The owner's own framing for the instruments applies here: they are multipliers on the information content of every arm, and arm budget is the scarce resource. An instrument that must be REMEMBERED is an instrument that is skipped on exactly the arm whose mean looks decided. Ownership by a pipeline stage is what makes running it the default rather than the exception.

CHILDREN: the module-to-pipeline audit, the training-stage hook points, the experiment-tracking decision (mlflow or an argued alternative), and the reorganisation itself. NOTHING MOVES until the audit is written: a folder reshuffle done before the map is drawn rebuilds the confusion at a new path.

title: arm_read: the per-label reading of an arm against its declared control, made mechanical
description:
Built 2026-08-31. kneemri/experiments/arm_read.py joins ArmHeader.controls (which has parsed '# control  <name> = <score>' for weeks) to RunComparison (which has printed per-label deltas with 95% intervals for weeks). The two had never been joined, so every per-label read was hand-rolled from a metrics query and therefore run only when someone thought of it. stack224 is the cost: mean delta -0.0026 reads flat and would have closed the slice-coverage axis; per label it was a two-label collapse (-0.0263 Lateral Meniscus, -0.0180 Fracture) inside a nine-label rise, i.e. an aggregator failure. The arm that followed exists because someone remembered to look.

--assert with no --arm sweeps the corpus: on first run, 86 of 162 arms declare no control. That includes stack224, native224 and calib_dense_hold - the arms other arms are read AGAINST. Backfilling the line on the arms that are still quoted as controls is the follow-up.

title: cover_labelwise: full coverage failed under max pooling on exactly the labels it named - retest with per-label slice attention
description:
PRICE: ~50 minutes of card (12 epochs, 36 slices at 224 px; stack224 measured 257 s an epoch, labelwise attention adds a little). P(clears native224's 0.8502 on the mean) = 25%; P(recovers Lateral Meniscus and Fracture above control) = 40%.

WHAT HAPPENED. stack224 (knee-qphd) read the whole 36-slice stack for the first time and finished at 0.8476 against native224's 0.8502, -0.0026 on the mean. Its pre-registration said a flat mean with the thin findings UP was the finding. They went down hardest:

  Lateral Meniscus 0.8028 vs 0.8291  -0.0263
  Fracture         0.7929 vs 0.8109  -0.0180
  Synovitis        0.8740 vs 0.8638  +0.0101
  ACL              0.8809 vs 0.8768  +0.0041

Every thick finding rose or held; the two thin ones the mechanism named collapsed. That is not noise scatter, and it is not the coverage idea failing on its own terms - it is the shape of an AGGREGATOR failure.

THE MECHANISM. stack224 pools slices with --slice-pooling max. A maximum over 36 candidates has a strictly higher noise ceiling than a maximum over 20: the expected maximum of a set of noisy per-slice scores grows with the size of the set even when nothing in the volume changed. A finding present on two slices is exactly the case a spurious maximum drowns, and a finding present on twenty is not. So coverage and max pooling are in direct conflict, and the more slices are covered the worse the thin findings get. The measured per-label pattern is what that predicts, label for label.

THE TEST. Same arm, one flag moved: --slice-pooling labelwise (LabelwiseAttention), which gives each of the twelve findings its own attention map over the slices rather than one shared extremum. It is the mechanism-matched aggregator for a finding that lives on two slices out of thirty-six, and it is already proven at 20 slices (labelwise_dense_s2026, 0.8613). Everything else is stack224's invocation untouched, so the read is matched against BOTH stack224 (aggregator moved, coverage held) and native224 (the standing 224 control).

BRANCHES, before the number. Thin findings above native224's control and mean at or above 0.8502: the aggregator was the whole defect, coverage is real, and stack_cover_ff (knee-ujd3) un-gates with labelwise substituted for max. Thin findings recover but the mean does not: coverage is a per-finding lever, not a member lever - record it and do not ship it. Thin findings still down: coverage itself is refuted independent of the aggregator, knee-qphd closes, and knee-ujd3 closes with it.

Also drops --recompute-activations, as knee-ujd3 argues: stack224 peaked 21.9 GB of 32.6 WITH it, and the flag's 19% tax was calibrated for a 4.5x larger footprint. An OOM is itself the finding.
notes: READ 2026-08-31. cover_labelwise best holdout 0.8495, converged (12/12, best e8). Branch 3 fired: both thin findings still below native224's control (Fracture -0.0198 no recovery, Lateral Meniscus -0.0150 vs stack224's -0.0263 = about half back, inside the +/-0.0372 half-width), mean 0.8495 < 0.8502. Coverage refuted as a member lever independent of the aggregator. Seat value vs honest12: -0.0001 [-0.0006,+0.0004], 0 of 1 clears +0.0015. member_axes calls it DISTINCT (rank 0.8587 / js 0.0173 / maha 4.627 against boundaries 0.8956 / 0.0150 / 4.436) - DISTINCT is necessary for a seat, never sufficient, and both rulers declining agrees rather than adjudicating knee-iyad's gate. Only starred move: MCL +0.0247 against BOTH controls, Medial Meniscus +0.0125 against native224. Written up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_coverage_is_not_an_aggregator_bug.md
close_reason: Answered. The aggregator hypothesis is real as a mechanism and sub-resolution as a lever; coverage closes with knee-qphd. Full reading in the notes and in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_coverage_is_not_an_aggregator_bug.md

title: stack_cover_ff: full slice coverage carried into the best recipe, fit blind
description:
PRICE: ~45 minutes of card (12 epochs, 36 slices at 224 px; stack224 measures 257 s an epoch with --recompute-activations, ~215 s without). P(clears +0.0047 on a single member) = 10%, and GATED - see the gate below.

Route arithmetic, fitted this session on the 36 scored board entries that carry an honest offline number: board = 1.37 x offline - 0.2598. Board 0.946 therefore asks for an ensemble offline of 0.8815, against the best ever assembled (honest12, 0.8751) - a gap of +0.0064, one paired floor (STRONG_OF_BEST = 0.0062) wide. The ensemble tracks best-single + ~0.015, so that is +0.0047 on ONE member against the pool's best clean fold-0 run (merged_span_cf 0.8618 over 97 runs sharing its ruler). Nothing smaller is worth a seat: BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015 at the entry and a seat is diluted about 1/9 inside the champion.

Route B (blind refit, removing a seat's fit penalty) has exactly one move left and stackseat makes it: five of six champion seats are already --fold -1 --ema. After that entry scores, every further slot is paid out of member quality.

This arm is the first candidate for that: 36-slice full coverage (the cell no member has occupied, knee-qphd) carried into the blend-three corpus plus raptor-teacher distillation (the two levers worth ~+0.014 that make the pool's best members). Coverage changes which pixels are seen; the corpus and teacher change what is asked for. Independent inputs, one run.

THE GATE. stack224 is the fold-0 sibling that prices coverage on its own, and at epoch 10 it reads 0.8476 against its control native224's 0.8502 - flat to slightly negative ON THE MEAN. The mechanism never claimed the mean: it names the thin findings that live on few slices (Lateral Meniscus, Fracture). So this arm runs ONLY if stack224's final per-label read shows those two up. Flat mean with the thin findings up is the finding; flat mean with them flat kills the coverage lever and this arm with it, and the card goes to the KIND axis (knee-ombx) instead.

Fit is --fold -1 --ema by design: the destination is the champion. No holdout number exists by construction.

Also drops --recompute-activations (19% measured tax, calibrated for a 4.5x larger activation footprint). That half is unconditional and near-free: the first epoch's peak-memory line answers it either way. stack224 peaked 21.9 GB of 32.6 WITH the flag; predicted ~29 GB without, and an OOM is itself the finding that the threshold sits between 20 and 36 slices at 224.
notes:
PRICE. 12 epochs at 36 slices / 224 px. stack224 measures 257 s an epoch WITH --recompute-activations; without it, 19% less, so ~215 s -> ~45 minutes of card.

GAIN. It must clear +0.0047 on a single member for the ensemble to reach the offline 0.8815 that the board fit says 0.946 needs. Nothing smaller is worth the seat: BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015 at the entry and a seat is diluted about 1/9 inside the champion.

P(clears +0.0047) = 10%, and it is GATED, not open. stack224 is the fold-0 sibling that prices the coverage lever on its own, and at epoch 10 it reads 0.8476 against its control native224's 0.8502 - coverage is flat to slightly negative ON THE MEAN. The mechanism never claimed the mean: it names the thin findings that live on few slices (Lateral Meniscus, Fracture). So this arm runs ONLY if stack224's final per-label read shows those two up. Flat mean with the thin findings up is the finding; flat mean with them flat kills the coverage lever and this arm with it, and the card goes to the KIND axis (knee-ombx) instead.

The throughput half is unconditional and near-free: whether --recompute-activations can be dropped at 36 slices / 224 px is answered by the first epoch's peak-memory line either way.
close_reason: Closed by cover_labelwise (knee-tlya), 2026-08-31, on knee-tlya's own pre-registered branch 3. Full 36-slice coverage read under labelwise pooling scores 0.8495 vs native224's 0.8502: both thin findings still below control, mean still below control. The AGGREGATOR mechanism did hold on one of the two labels it named (Lateral Meniscus -0.0263 -> -0.0150) but inside a +/-0.0372 half-width, and Fracture did not move (-0.0180 -> -0.0198). So coverage is refuted as a member lever independent of the aggregator; the aggregator argument survives as a mechanism worth under a third of one label. knee-ujd3 closes with it (it was gated on coverage surviving) and its throughput half is separately answered: --recompute-activations is load-bearing at 36 slices / 224 px (OOM without it) and dead weight at 20, so the 19% is bought. Does NOT close labelwise pooling itself, which reads 0.8613 at 20 slices. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_coverage_is_not_an_aggregator_bug.md

title: Drop --recompute-activations on 224-px arms: a 19% tax for a memory problem that no longer exists
description:
`experiments/recipe.sh:31` sets THROUGHPUT=--recompute-activations and every arm inherits it. Its own docstring (kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py:285-300) records the cost as MEASURED: 798 img/s against 946, a 19% tax, taken 2026-08-12 at batch 6.

That measurement was taken on the 336-px geometry: 12 studies x 6 slots x 12 slices = 864 images at 577 tokens each. That footprint pinned all 32 GB and genuinely paged over PCIe, so the tax bought the run.

A 224-px arm is a different problem. stack224 runs 36 slices x 6 slots x batch 12 = 432 images at 256 tokens - about 4.5x less activation - and measures 24.3 GB reserved of 32.6, with 8 GB of headroom the whole run. It is paying a 19% throughput tax to solve a memory problem it does not have.

Do: on the next 224-px arm, drop $THROUGHPUT from the invocation and record peak reserved memory plus s/epoch against stack224's 257 s. If it fits (predicted ~29 GB, still under), 224 exploration gets ~19% cheaper for free and the standing exploration resolution (knee-s9cr) gets faster. If it OOMs, the tax is justified at 36 slices and the finding is that the threshold sits between 20 and 36 slices at 224 - which is itself worth the one arm.

Do NOT touch recipe.sh's default: the 336 arms still need it.
notes: ANSWERED BY ONE LAUNCH, 2026-08-31. cover_labelwise launched without $THROUGHPUT at 08:02Z died with torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 488.00 MiB ... 25.50 GiB allowed; 25.09 GiB is allocated, at 224 px / 36 slices — against the 21.9 GB stack224 peaked at WITH the flag at 20 slices. So the flag is dead weight at 20 slices and load-bearing at 36 at the SAME 224 px: the threshold is slice COUNT, not image size, and it sits between 20 and 36. The 19% (798 vs 946 img/s) is bought, not wasted, on any whole-stack arm. Do not drop it on a coverage arm. Cost: three minutes.

title: Read the WHOLE stack once: 36 slices at 224 px, the one decode cell no member has ever occupied
description:
THE PUBLIC FRONTIER READS 64 SLICES PER STUDY. The DINOsaur/raptor kernel (research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md, and the notebook pulled 2026-08-31) fills its five slots with 18+14+12+8+12 = 64 slices. Every member this project owns reads 12 or 20 (95 arms at 20, 43 at 12, 1 at 16, and NOTHING above 20 in 137 arm scripts). A sagittal knee series holds 30-40 slices, so at 12-20 we are reading a third to a half of the volume and the sampler picks which half.

WHY THE SLICE-COUNT LEDGER DOES NOT ALREADY ANSWER THIS. It measures 12 -> 20 only: +0.0080 (band_span_hold -> band_dense_hold), +0.0013 (band_span -> band_dense), -0.0001 under max pooling (knee-ezz), -0.0028 on the merged corpus. Mixed and knob-sized. But 12 -> 20 is a change of WHICH SUBSET, not of coverage; 36 of a 30-40 slice stack is the first read that cannot miss a slice. Those are different mechanisms and only the second one can answer 'is a thin finding falling between our samples'.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN RUN, AND WHY IT IS FREE NOW. VRAM is a function of slice count and nothing else (experiments/README.md:253): at 336 px, 20 slices reserve 26.92 GB of a 32 GB card, so 36 was never affordable. At 224 px native224 reserved 8124 MiB at 12 slices, so 36 lands near 24.4 GB and fits. knee-s9cr's owner directive makes 224 the standing exploration resolution, and native224 (0.8502 vs the 336 control's 0.8525, -0.0023, inside the floor) says the resolution costs nothing. band224.sh was written at 20 slices and never ran, so the 224 slice axis is entirely untested.

THE ARM. stack224: native224's invocation with --slices 36 and the band opened to 0.05-0.95. Two flags, ONE concept - read the whole stack - and they cannot be separated, because 36 slices inside a 0.2-0.8 band would resample the middle 60% at triple density rather than cover the volume. Everything else held: 224 px, max slice pooling, whole-stack, backbone-lr 4e-5, 12 epochs, fold 0, canonical scheme, report_labels_v2 ruler.

CONTROL. native224_s2026 = 0.8502, same fold-0 holdout, same ruler, same everything but the two flags.

READ IT PER LABEL, NOT ONLY ON THE MEAN. The mechanism names WHICH labels it should move: the frontier's own corpus jump reported its biggest gains on Lateral Meniscus +0.071, Fracture +0.057, Lateral OA +0.048 - the thin findings that live on few slices. A mean-AUC delta averages a two-label effect away across twelve. If the mean is flat but Meniscus and Fracture move together and the rest do not, that is the finding, and it points at per-finding slice budgeting rather than at a global count.

PRICE: ~55 min of card (94 s/epoch at 12 slices scales to ~285 s at 36; 12 epochs), zero slots, at 224 px where the queue is cheap. Plausible gain if the mechanism is real: +0.005 to +0.015 on the mean, concentrated in 2-3 labels. P(clears the 0.0062 paired holdout floor) ~ 30% - the nearest measurement (12->20 under max pooling, -0.0001) predicts a null, and this arm's claim is that the null was about subset choice and not about coverage.

BRANCHES, PRE-REGISTERED.
  * delta >= +0.0062 on the mean. Coverage is a lever, the whole 12/20 corpus was reading a third of the volume, and the next arm is 36 slices at 336 px on a smaller batch.
  * mean inside the floor but Lateral Meniscus and Fracture both up 0.02+. The effect is real and per-label; the lane becomes per-finding slice budgeting (slot_head already reads findings on particular planes), not a global count.
  * flat everywhere. Coverage is not the limit, the sampler was already picking the informative slices, and this closes the slice axis for good - knee-nj4l's axis (3) dies with it.
  * delta <= -0.0062. More slices dilute a max pool (experiments/README.md:5054 argues this for the mean pool). Then the finding is that the aggregator, not the sampler, is what cannot spend more slices.

HARNESS CHECK. The printed recipe must show image_size 224, slices 36, band [0.05, 0.95], slice_pooling max, whole_stack True, fold 0, and the log must load 4,406 studies holding out 909.
close_reason: Closed by cover_labelwise (knee-tlya), 2026-08-31, on knee-tlya's own pre-registered branch 3. Full 36-slice coverage read under labelwise pooling scores 0.8495 vs native224's 0.8502: both thin findings still below control, mean still below control. The AGGREGATOR mechanism did hold on one of the two labels it named (Lateral Meniscus -0.0263 -> -0.0150) but inside a +/-0.0372 half-width, and Fracture did not move (-0.0180 -> -0.0198). So coverage is refuted as a member lever independent of the aggregator; the aggregator argument survives as a mechanism worth under a third of one label. knee-ujd3 closes with it (it was gated on coverage surviving) and its throughput half is separately answered: --recompute-activations is load-bearing at 36 slices / 224 px (OOM without it) and dead weight at 20, so the 19% is bought. Does NOT close labelwise pooling itself, which reads 0.8613 at 20 slices. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_coverage_is_not_an_aggregator_bug.md

title: stack_increments_ff: the pool's best solo, refit blind so it can enter the champion
description:
PRICE: 73 min of card (12 epochs x 363s), zero slots. The member is the highest-scoring solo the project owns; refitting it --fold -1 --ema removes the ~0.008 blind-vs-fold-0 penalty that has made it unshippable into an entry whose five other seats are blind. Target seat is merged_blend_cf, the champion's lone fold-0 seat and the one paying that penalty today.

P(clears +0.0015 on the board as a swap) ~ 25-30%. It is the only lane knee-urvf leaves open (member quality), and unlike the seating lane it has no flat board reading against it: every inert reading to date is an operation on the ARRANGEMENT of seats, not on the quality of the member filling one.

WHY NOT SEATING. Measured and inert: raptorseat 0.943, vjepaseat 0.943, fleettwo 0.942 (adding a distant seat), raptorweight +0.001 (reweight), holdswap_v1 0.944 (swap, dead flat). Offline, three candidates priced +0.0002/+0.0005/+0.0000 on 2026-08-31.

NO HOLDOUT NUMBER EXISTS by construction. Nothing may enter the ledger as its score; the board is the only instrument. Arm file experiments/arms/stack_increments_ff.sh carries the harness check.

title: The most decorrelated member the project owns has never been in a board entry - blind-refit it for the champion lane
description:
swin_supervised_s2026 scores 0.8331 solo with a nearest-neighbour agreement of 0.8346, against a seated spread of 0.8772-0.9225. It is by a wide margin the most decorrelated member here, and it is the only non-DINO trunk that ever came close to seat-worthy. It was declined at -0.0012 seat value against greedyseat_v1.

WHY THAT DECLINE DOES NOT SETTLE IT. Every seat_value reading is taken on greedyseat_v1, a fold-0 roster scoring 0.936. The entry we actually ship is raptorweight_v1 at 0.944, five of whose six members are --fold -1 blind fits that RecordMix excludes by construction. So the ruler cannot price the champion at all, and -0.0012 is a statement about a different ensemble. Three separate candidates priced at +0.0002, +0.0005 and +0.0000 on that same ruler on 2026-08-31, which is what a saturated ruler looks like, not necessarily a saturated pool.

knee-nj4l is the standing P0 this answers: the champion is an architecture MONOCULTURE and that is the mechanical cause of the 0.937-0.941 plateau. swin_supervised is the only decorrelated non-DINO trunk available to break it, and it has never appeared in any board entry.

THE ARM.
