reads it RAW, so the annotations are not compared with themselves.

(1) PER-FINDING, our table against the radiologist rows:

finding             n+   auc   bestthr  agr@best  agr@0.5
ACL                 24  0.987    0.94     0.966    0.845
MCL                  9  0.976    0.82     0.948    0.828
Medial Meniscus     26  0.944    0.82     0.914    0.845
Lateral Meniscus    23  0.842    0.82     0.810    0.759
Medial OA           15  0.909    0.82     0.862    0.828
Lateral OA          11  0.789    0.68     0.845    0.828
PF OA               21  0.886    0.82     0.862    0.793
Effusion            35  0.815    0.50     0.724    0.724
Synovitis           27  0.687    0.68     0.707    0.690
Baker's             12  0.932    0.68     0.897    0.879
Contusion           19  0.753    0.94     0.724    0.621
Fracture            18  0.870    0.82     0.845    0.828
MEAN                    0.866             0.842    0.789

THE ORDERING IS GOOD AND THE VALUE IS NOT. Mean rank AUC 0.866 (ACL 0.987) while binarised agreement at
the 0.5 the project uses everywhere is 0.789. Ten of twelve findings want a threshold ABOVE 0.5, eight of
them 0.82 - our reader over-calls positives on every finding except Synovitis, which it under-calls
(14 misses, 4 false positives). Contusion is the worst cell: 20 false positives against 39 negatives.

(2) THE POOLED CALIBRATION CURVE, which is the actual proposed fix and needs no per-finding fit:

  reader level   cells   P(gold positive)
      0.08        196         0.041
      0.28        177         0.136
      0.50         12         0.417
      0.68         98         0.378
      0.82        141         0.688
      0.94         72         0.958

Monotone apart from the twelve-cell 0.50 bucket, and badly miscalibrated in the MIDDLE. The 0.68 bucket is
the finding: 98 cells, 62% of them actually NEGATIVE, trained today as a 0.68 positive. The target is wrong
by about 0.30 on 14% of all cells, always in the direction that invents positives. 0.08 and 0.28 each
over-state by roughly a factor of two. The two ends (0.94 -> 0.958, 0.08 -> 0.041) are nearly right, which
is why nothing downstream has noticed: the reader is confident exactly where it is correct.

MECHANISM, and it is the forum's, confirmed on our own data: the reader's number is confidence in applying
a heuristic to WORDS, and the gold is a radiologist reading an IMAGE. The two agree at the extremes, where
the words are unambiguous, and come apart in the middle, where 'small effusion' is a coin the report already
flipped. So the fix is not a better reader - it is a monotone re-map of the LEVELS onto the empirical rate,
six parameters fitted on 696 cells.

THE RULER PROBLEM, stated before any arm is armed. Our offline holdout truth IS the report-derived table.
A supervision change that moves toward the image-read process can therefore LOWER the offline number while
raising the board - the offline ruler does not have this axis. The only rulers that do are the 58 gold rows
(foreign_gate --gold-auc, n=58, weak but pointed at the right process) and a submission. Pre-register that
asymmetry: an arm here is read on gold AUC first and on holdout second, and a holdout regression inside the
floor is NOT a refutation.

title: convergence_check --run took a run NAME and reported UNSCORED for the file it never found
description:
--run is a Path. Passing a run NAME resolves against the working directory, RunMetrics reads nothing,
best() returns None and _judge files it as UNSCORED. So 'convergence_check --run swin_supervised_s2026'
printed '1 runs: 1 unscored' for a run that is CONVERGED with a best epoch of 6 at 0.8331, and it exited
zero doing it.

That is the exact failure RunMetrics.__init__'s own comment names about the doubled suffix: 'an error
that describes a real state and hides a typo'. Here it is worse than cosmetic, because this check exists
to stop a number being quoted from a run that cannot support it — so a reading taken of NO FILE is the
one answer it may never return quietly. It cost a wrong ledger note: swin_supervised was written down as
needing a score it already had.

FIXED: --run now asserts RunMetrics.exists() and raises SystemExit naming the resolved path and the fact
that it takes a path rather than a name. The unit test passes a bare name and asserts the raise.

title: swin_wholetop: re-run the supervised trunk with its top actually unfrozen
description:
swin_supervised read 0.8331 and earned no seat (-0.0012 against greedyseat_v1). knee-94ec then showed
the run was handicapped: block discovery found only stage 2, so --unfreeze-last 6 opened
layers.2.blocks.12-17 and layers.3 — the final two blocks, 1024 wide, the top of the network — never
trained. This arm is that recipe, byte-identical, on the fixed discovery. Single variable: which six
blocks train.

WHY IT IS PRICED WORTH ~3 H. Swin's nearest-neighbour correlation to a seated member is 0.8346 against a
seated mean of 0.8772-0.9225 — the most decorrelated member the project owns. Diversity that large could
not pay for a 0.020 solo deficit; this arm attacks the deficit, and what was frozen is the part a
fine-tune moves most. It is also the cheapest live path to the stated goal of a non-DINO member with a
seat: the alternative is an unfitted family at a full recipe search.

Odds, stated before the run: perhaps 40% that opening the top is worth a floor or more, and conditional
on that perhaps half that the seat turns positive. Expected value is a seat on a member nothing else in
the pool resembles.

PRE-REGISTERED against 0.8331, floor 0.0062:
  LANDS   >= 0.8560 — mirror to Kaggle, mount, build an entry, spend a slot.
  SEAT    0.8393-0.8559 — price the seat; mount at +0.002 offline or better.
  COSTS   0.8269-0.8392 — within a floor either way; the handicap did not account for the deficit, and
          this trunk at this recipe is not competitive. Do NOT re-run the ConvNeXt pair on the same hope.
  REFUTES < 0.8269 — opening the top made it worse; 1e-4 is too high for stage 3's wider blocks and the
          follow-up is a rate arm, not another family.
notes: Curve through e7 (14:32 UTC): 0.7444 0.7816 0.8109 0.8164 0.8168 0.8189 0.8274 0.8228. Peak so far 0.8274 at e6, sitting in the arm's own COSTS band (0.8269-0.8392). Deficit against swin_supervised: e6 -0.0057, e7 -0.0033 — the monotone-widening claim the knee-tild tie-break rested on is BROKEN at e7, so that ruling is re-read against the full curve and not held on the partial one. Four epochs remain and the one_cycle anneal is untaken: from e3=0.8164 the corpus gains are median +0.0209 (0.8373), p90 +0.0380 (0.8544), max +0.0529 (0.8693), so SEAT (0.8393-0.8559) is still reachable and no branch may be called before the peak exists.
close_reason: Ran and answered, negative. swin_wholetop reached 0.8274 on the fixed block discovery against swin_supervised's 0.8331 with its top FROZEN - unfreezing layers.3 made it worse, and 0.8274 is 0.0186 under the 0.8459 seat bar. The knee-94ec handicap was real and was not what held the trunk back. Reading in experiments/README.md around the knee-wqfz seat rule; checkpoint, metrics and holdout record all on disk. Consequence: the supervised/conv trunk lane is closed FAIRLY, not by a harness defect, and VGG/ResNet would be a fourth instance of a mechanism that has now failed three times.

title: Per-label routing buys nothing over global seat choice — the ceiling is the pool, not the combiner
description:
Card-free, no slot. record_mix --largest-pool --seats honest --vote logit --routing over the whole processed root.

Denominator, read off the log line and not off the paths passed in: 113 of 202 records became members
over 909 shared studies, voting LogitAverage. Identical to the pool the seat-count curve was measured on
the same day, so the two numbers are directly comparable.

THE THREE MECHANISMS, all split-half honest, all on that one pool:

    flat rank-average over all 113                       0.8666   (the routing curve's own last row)
    per-label routing, peak at top-10 members per label  0.8760
    global honest greedy seats, peak at 19 seats         0.8763

SELECTION IS WORTH +0.0094 OVER THE FLAT AVERAGE, which is above the 0.0062 floor and is the one real
thing here. ROUTING SUPPLIES NO PART OF IT. Its peak sits 0.0003 under the global greedy's — 0.05 of a
floor — and the two rules are structurally different: one picks a single subset for every label, the
other is free to pick a different subset per label and had every chance to exploit a specialist.

The routing curve's own shape says the same thing twice. It rises 0.8657 -> 0.8760 over ten members and
then decays monotonically for a hundred more, back to the flat average at 113. If any member were a
per-label SPECIALIST, the top-1-per-label column would be where it showed, and top-1 (0.8657) is the
WORST point on the whole curve — below even the flat average. Nothing in this pool is good at one label
and bad at the others; members differ in general competence, and per-label freedom only buys noise.

WHAT THIS CLOSES AND WHAT IT OPENS. It closes the combiner as an axis: with the seat-COUNT curve already
flat to 0.4 of a floor across 1-24 seats (knee-m69u) and now the seat-CHOICE rule flat across two
mechanisms that share no structure, 0.876 is where this pool tops out however you pick among it. That is
not a property of the rule, it is a property of the members — 113 checkpoints that are overwhelmingly
DINOv2-small at 336 px, which comp/champion.json already names as the plateau.

So the only lever left on the offline number is a member that is not from that monoculture, which is
exactly what swin_supervised and vit_in21k are for. Two independent combiner nulls in two days is the
strongest argument yet for spending card time on trunks rather than on ensembling.

DO NOT SPEND A SUBMISSION ON THIS. It is a null, and the shipped champion already votes logit over a
globally-chosen seat set, which is the better of the two mechanisms measured here.

title: vitb16_in21k: the objective axis isolated at ZERO architectural distance, against v3base
description:
WHY THIS ARM. `swin_supervised` is the project's first supervised-pretrained trunk, and it varies TWO
things at once against every incumbent: the objective (IN-22k labels, not self-distillation) AND the
architecture (shifted-window attention, not global attention over a flat grid). Whatever it reads, it
cannot say which half carried it. `google/vit-base-patch16-224-in21k` can: it is an EXACT architectural
twin of the `v3base` entry already in the registry -- ViT-B/16, twelve blocks, 768 wide, the same global
attention over the same patch grid at the same stride -- and differs from it in the pretraining objective
ALONE (AugReg supervised IN-21k against DINOv3 self-distillation on LVD-1689M). At 336 px and patch 16
the token count is identical too, 441 either way, so even the compute is matched.

WHERE IT SITS ON THE knee-y59c CURVE. That measurement anti-correlates solo strength with
distance-from-DINOv2 across seven trunks, and the two far-end deaths are `mae_matched` (0.6735) and
`focus_mcl` (0.5332). An architectural twin sits at ~0 on that axis, so the curve predicts a real number.
If a supervised ViT dies here anyway, the curve was never about architecture.

THE CONTROL IS ON DISK. `v3base_dense` ran this exact recipe on the architectural twin: 0.8455 solo at
best epoch 6, seat value -0.0005 against the five-member champion. `base_dense` (DINOv2-base, same recipe)
is the other twin at 0.8512.

NOT IMAGENET NORMALIZATION. AugReg states 0.5/0.5 -- a property of that pretraining CODEBASE rather than
of its corpus, so it cannot be guessed from the data the way RAD-DINO's greyscale constants can. Declared
in the registry as `HALF` and held to the checkpoint's own preprocessor config by
`tests/integration/registry_to_checkpoints`.

PRICE: ~2.5-2.9 h on the card (v3base_dense's wall-clock at an identical token count), plus ~0 analysis
time -- the control already exists, so this buys its comparison for free rather than paying for a matched
arm. Plausible gain: a member in the dense band is worth a seat at +0.002 to +0.005 on the board via the
usual seat-to-board compression, and the BEATS-THE-TWIN branch would be worth far more than that, since
it reopens every trunk decision this project made by reading a self-supervised checkpoint's number.
P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.05 on the solo score alone. THE ARM IS NOT SOLD ON THAT NUMBER: it is bought as an
INSTRUMENT, and a cheap one, because it is the only run that can DISAMBIGUATE `swin_supervised` -- which
confounds objective with architecture and whose reading is otherwise uninterpretable whichever way it
lands. P(the objective axis is settled either way) ~ 0.8, and that is what the 2.7 h is spent on.

PRE-REGISTERED, four outcomes. Floor 0.0062, so the twin's band is 0.8393-0.8517.
- BEATS THE TWIN  >= 0.8517 -- supervised transfers BETTER at fixed architecture; the objective is a
    lever on COMPETENCE, and every trunk decision made off an SSL checkpoint's number reopens.
- MATCHES        0.8393-0.8516 -- the objective does not move competence, so the seat value is the whole
    question. A matched solo with a POSITIVE seat says the objective moves the trunk's OPINION and not
    its competence -- the diversity knee-m69u asks for, and the first mechanism that could supply it
    without costing strength by construction.
- COSTS          0.8000-0.8392 -- transfers worse at fixed architecture. Price the seat anyway:
    `base_dense` lost its control outside the floor and won the board.
- REFUTES        < 0.8000 at zero architectural distance -- closes the objective axis outright instead of
    leaving it confounded in `swin_supervised`, and makes the y59c curve a statement about pretraining
    DATA SCALE rather than about architecture.

ARM: `experiments/arms/vit_in21k.sh`, `v3base_dense.sh`'s invocation with `--variant vitin21k`
substituted. NOT to be armed while `swin_supervised` holds the card -- `card_check` is the gate.

MOUNT: Apache-2.0 and ungated, so mirroring is permitted outright, same dataset-upload shape as
`dimiturnt/swin-base-384`. Deferred until a member earns the seat, per the registry's standing rule.
notes:
PLUMBING PROBE CLOSED, CARD-FREE, NO DEFECT ON THE TRAINING SIDE.

The earlier reading — parameter_groups returning a backbone group of ZERO parameters at 4e-5 — was my
probe's argument, not a fact about ViT. `unfreeze_last=0` means freeze every block, and `opened()`
answers it literally. The control settles it: `v3base` (the architectural twin, and the trunk every
ledger number was measured on) returns the SAME (0, 4e-05) at unfreeze_last=0.

    v3base    unfreeze 0  [(11, 0.001), (0,  4e-05)]     vitin21k  unfreeze 0  [(11, 0.001), (0,  4e-05)]
    v3base    unfreeze 4  [(11, 0.001), (68, 4e-05)]     vitin21k  unfreeze 4  [(11, 0.001), (64, 4e-05)]

At four blocks open both build a real group, and the 68-vs-64 difference is itself the expected one:
DINOv3 carries a layerscale parameter per block that an AugReg ViT does not, so the twin has one extra
tensor per opened block. Block DISCOVERY works on ViT — `applied()` reports opened_blocks 12 and
recompute_activations True, so `$THROUGHPUT` lands too.

The arm passes no --unfreeze-last, so it runs at `Adaptation().unfreeze_last` = 6
(flag_vocabulary.py:432), which is the same code path as the 4 measured here, one block deeper.

So the arm's remaining risk is the SCIENCE, not the harness: forward pass verified end-to-end on CPU
after the GridFit fix, block discovery verified, gradient plumbing verified, throughput flag verified.

title: depth_regions_span_s2026's checkpoint and its holdout record were written by DIFFERENT RUNS
description:
SWEPT 2026-08-30 08:05Z, no card, no slot. One defect in 93 roster members, and the sweep that found it also REFUTES a much larger worry I raised on the way to it.

THE DEFECT. depth_regions_span_s2026.pt reports epoch=9 / epochs_done=10 and is BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5 d14324e52e) to depth_regions_span_s2026_run1.pt. Its holdout record depth_regions_span_s2026.holdout.npz reports epoch=8, source=trained, and scores 0.8487 — which is what comp/members.roster:546 carries for the member. But the run those predictions came from is the SECOND run: .metrics.jsonl holds nine epochs 0-8 with a best of 0.8487 at e8, while run one's twelve-epoch metrics survive as .metrics.1.jsonl and _run1.metrics.jsonl (7928 B against the current file's 6234 B). The re-run's own weights never committed — they are still in depth_regions_span_s2026.partial at epoch 8.

So the file that would SHIP is run one's epoch-9 checkpoint and the number that PRICES it is run two's epoch-8 predictions. Those are not the same model, and the roster's 0.8487 is a number no shippable weight file has been shown to produce.

WHAT BOUNDS IT. Nothing has shipped on it: comp/champion.json pins raptorweight_v1 (board 0.944, six members) and depth_regions_span appears in no board entry and no champion. The exposure is the POOL — record_mix globs records, 0.8487 is above the 0.8460 merit level the declines file uses, so a seat search can pick it up and an entry built from that search would carry the mismatch onto the board.

WHAT THE SWEEP REFUTED, and it is the more useful half. 48 of 93 roster members have a holdout record whose mtime is more than fifteen minutes from the checkpoint's, and 92 of 93 leave a .partial behind — so neither is a signature of anything. Seven big positive gaps (res392_ws +6.9 days, sliceattn, lora_r8_v3small_224, deep24, intensity392_ws, extended_ws, calibrated_targets) all read source=re-derived: understood, stamped, benign. The negative gaps of 15-100 minutes prompted the real worry — that .pt is the LAST epoch while the record is the BEST — which would have meant every long run shipped weights far past its peak (band_dense_long best e6 0.8587, last e23 0.8405). It is FALSE: on band_dense_long, aug_long, v3base_dense, base_dense, band_dense and stackfit the checkpoint's own stored epoch equals the record's epoch equals the metrics' best epoch, six for six. The trainer saves on improvement; the mtime lag is residue, not the weights.

THE REAL SIGNATURE is a _run1.pt or a .metrics.1.jsonl sibling, and only four roster members have one: merged_dense_cf and aprior_dense_s2026 are both clean (ckpt.epoch == record.epoch == metrics best), final_ws_e12 is a --fold -1 member with no record at all by construction, and depth_regions_span_s2026 is the defect.

THE FIX, and it is cheap. Re-derive the record from the checkpoint that is actually on disk — the same path that stamped the fifteen re-derived records in the pool — and let the member carry whatever run one's epoch-9 weights actually score. If that number lands below 0.8460 the member moves to comp/members.declines with this as the reason. Do NOT simply relabel the existing record: its predictions came from weights that exist only inside a .partial.

WHY IT IS NOT P0. Bounded to the pool, one member, and roster_check does not currently look at this axis — which is the follow-up worth considering once the number is known: a check that a record's epoch is reachable in the checkpoint beside it costs one torch.load per member and would have caught this the day it happened.
notes:
DETECTOR DECISION (2026-08-30): do NOT add the roster_check assertion this bead proposed. The class is
already closed AT THE SOURCE. `RunMetrics.begin` (run_metrics.py:140-172) rotates a previous run's epochs
AND its artefacts aside before a re-run writes anything -- `live.replace(aside)`, a MOVE -- so after that
change a re-run to the same --out cannot leave the earlier run's .pt beside the later run's .holdout.npz.
Its docstring names this very member as the incident it was written for.

depth_regions_span_s2026's byte-identical .pt/_run1.pt pair is therefore a HAND-MADE copy from 2026-08-19,
made before the rotation existed, and not a defect the code can still produce. A detector here would guard
a fixed bug and cost a gate, a test and a mirror file to do it.

WHAT REMAINS IS THE ARTEFACT, not the mechanism: re-derive this member's holdout record from the .pt
actually on disk (needs the GPU; queued behind the Swin arm). That is the whole fix, and closing this bead
should follow the re-derive, not a new check.

title: Swin-base-384-in22k: the first supervised-pretrained trunk, and the adapter seam that took
description:
THE AXIS THIS PROJECT HAS NEVER VARIED. Nine encoders are on the registry and every single one of them
was pretrained WITHOUT LABELS: DINOv2 and DINOv3 by distillation, ConvNeXtV2 by masked autoencoding,
V-JEPA2 by latent prediction, RAD-DINO by distillation on chest films. "A different trunk" has therefore
always meant a different way of having no labels. Swin-base-384-in22k is 21,841 human-assigned classes of
supervised pretraining — an objective that rewards exactly the discriminative structure the head is then
asked to find, and the one pretraining axis with zero runs against it (knee-zfgn measured the run ratio at
189:1 toward DINOv2; this is worse, it is 9:0).

THE ARCHITECTURE IS ALSO NEW, and deliberately not at the far end. Shifted-window attention is neither
global attention over a flat grid nor pure local convolution: attention inside a 12x12 window, windows
displaced every other block so information crosses their seams. knee-y59c measured distance-from-DINOv2
anti-correlating with solo strength across seven trunks -- mae_matched at 0.43 nearest scored 0.6735 solo,
focus_mcl at 0.04 scored 0.5332. Swin sits in the MIDDLE of that axis on purpose.

WHAT WAS BUILT TO MAKE IT POSSIBLE. `Encoder.load` decided its output wrapper with `if self.family !=
CONVNEXT`, correct exactly until a second non-conforming family arrived. Swin is that second one and it
does not want the same adapter: it emits a sequence already (n, t, d) and is missing a PREFIX TOKEN, where
ConvNeXt emits a map and is missing both. The branch is replaced by an `adapter` strategy field on the
entry, and `SequenceAsTokens` joins `MapAsTokens` over a shared `pooled_prefix`. Verified live on CPU
before any card time: (1, 145, 1024) at 384 px, 86.9M parameters, 24 blocks.

384 IS THE ONLY LEGAL READ and require_tiling cannot enforce it. The window size is baked into the
pretrained relative-position tables at 12. 384 at stride 32 gives a 12x12 grid that the window tiles
exactly; 352 tiles the STRIDE and not the WINDOW, and transformers will pad and interpolate rather than
refuse -- a plausible answer on a geometry the tables never saw. The arm pins --train-size 384.

PRICE: ~90 min of card (12 epochs at 384 px on an 87M hierarchical trunk, priced off cnx_own_recipe's 448
px run). Control is the whole-stack dense family at 0.855-0.863; the honest comparison for a first arm on
a new trunk is cnx_own_recipe's 0.8186, which is what our recipe transferred to the last time it left the
DINOv2 family.
P(clears the 0.0062 floor as a solo member): LOW, ~15%. A first arm on a new trunk has never cleared it
here. That is not what this run is for and it must not be sold as such. It is priced as an INSTRUMENT
plus a SEAT candidate: the mixing side is spent (2026-08-30 interpretation), the pool is 82% one number,
and the only unexplored source of a genuinely different opinion is a trunk pretrained under a different
OBJECTIVE. A seat worth +0.002 offline on a retrained entry transfers one-for-one to the board
(board_transfer +0.98 at the top of the record), which is inside the top-10 gap of 0.008.

PRE-REGISTERED, read on the 909-study fold-0 holdout.
  LANDS -- solo at or above 0.8560. Within 0.008 of the dense DINOv2 members, from a supervised trunk on
    its first arm. Mirror the weights to a Kaggle dataset (Apache-2.0, no licence question of the kind
    DINOv3 needed), add the mount, build an entry, spend a slot on it.
  SEAT-ONLY -- solo 0.8300 to 0.8559. Not competitive alone but plausibly decorrelated. Price it as a seat
    with record_mix against a FULLY SCOREABLE entry (honest12 / greedyseat_v1), never against
    raptorweight_v1, five of whose six members are fold -1. Mount it only if the seat delta is at or above
    +0.002.
  STARVED -- solo 0.8000 to 0.8299. The band cnx_own_recipe landed in. The reading is then about the
    RECIPE, not the trunk: a schedule fitted to a 22M SSL ViT does not transfer to an 87M supervised
    hierarchical one. The follow-up is one arm at --backbone-lr 4e-4 (what cnx needed, worth +0.026 over
    cnx_dense's 4e-5), not another architecture.
  REFUTES -- solo below 0.8000. Supervised IN-22k pretraining does not transfer to knee MRI. That closes
    the pretraining-objective axis, which is a real finding and the cheapest possible way to learn it.

THE BACKBONE RATE IS THE ONE GUESS AND IT IS STATED AS ONE. 4e-5 is DINOv2's best (lr1e-4_ws 0.8490,
lr2e-4_ws 0.7391 -- higher rates hurt an SSL ViT). 4e-4 is what the one non-DINOv2 trunk needed. 1e-4 is
the geometric middle and it is chosen because the two arguments point opposite ways: a supervised trunk's
features are already task-adjacent, which argues for LESS adaptation, and the cnx evidence argues for
more. STARVED's branch is what settles it if this rate is wrong.
notes:
THE SHIPPING PATH, PRE-REGISTERED 2026-08-30 09:05Z, BEFORE THE SCORE LANDS.
The goal is a submission on a non-raptor non-DINO trunk. Worked the arithmetic out now so the entry is
not designed around whatever number swin happens to return.

WHERE THE MEMBER CAN SIT. comp/champion.json's raptorweight_v1 has six --fold -1 seats, so that pool has
no offline number by construction and a candidate cannot be seat-scored against it at all. The door the
pin itself names is `seat_value --against <board entry>`, and there is now exactly one good target:
  greedyseat_v1 - board 0.936, 2026-08-30, ref 55877491, SEVEN seats all --fold 0 with holdout records,
  offline 0.8740 bias-corrected (raw greedy 0.8768, greedy bias +0.0028 measured over 111 records).
It is the freshest fold-0 anchor and the only one whose offline/board pair was confirmed on both rulers:
its own row records the two prior anchors at 0.8712 -> 0.933 and 0.8751 -> 0.937, a slope of 1.026 board
points per holdout point, and the bias-corrected prediction missed the board by +0.0001.

WHAT THAT SLOPE SAYS ABOUT A SWIN ENTRY, and it is the part worth having in writing:
  to beat raptorweight_v1's 0.944 from a 0.936 anchor needs +0.008 board = +0.0078 OFFLINE seat value.
  Measured seat values in this project run +0.0001 to +0.0005. A seat scan of 63 candidates once spanned
  a third of its own resolution. +0.0078 is fifteen times the largest seat value ever recorded here.
So a Swin entry on the fold-0 lane CANNOT take the champion, and any plan that quietly hopes it will is
arithmetic-free. Half the 0.008 is the all-data dose anyway (-0.004/-0.005 measured), which no fold-0
entry can pay back.

THEREFORE THE SUBMISSION IS AN INSTRUMENT AND MUST BE SOLD AS ONE. What it buys: the first board reading
of a SUPERVISED-pretrained, architecturally distinct trunk in any seat this project has shipped - the
whole pool is one lens (knee-m69u, and the monoculture principle in champion.json). Every axis the ledger
has closed was closed inside that monoculture. A member from outside it is the only thing that can say
whether the plateau is a property of ensembling or a property of the lens, and the fold-0 anchor is the
only place the reading can be taken cleanly.
  P(the Swin entry beats 0.944) ~ 0.02. P(it prices the trunk axis either way) ~ 0.8.
That is the same shape as the arm itself, which was armed as an instrument, and it is consistent.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: a --fold -1 refit of the trunk (another ~3 h card) puts it on the champion's own
lane where the all-data dose is already paid. Do NOT queue that off a SEAT-ONLY solo - it is only worth
the card if the seat value against greedyseat_v1 comes back at the top of its range.

title: record_mix --largest-pool over the processed root silently seats foreign contaminated records
description:
2026-08-30 04:02Z. A glob of every *.holdout.npz in the processed root (142 files) passed to `record_mix --largest-pool --vote logit --seats honest` returned 127 members and an honest peak of **0.8994 at six seats** — against the 0.8754/13-seat reading the ledger carries over 104 records. A +0.024 offline jump, four times the 0.0062 floor, off nothing but 23 extra members.

It is contamination. The four top solos in that pool are the FOREIGN raptor checkpoints:

    raptor_v4_swa 0.8938 · raptor_v4 0.8915 · raptor_v9 0.8769 · raptor_effv2l480 0.8703

against the best honest solo we own, calib_dense_hold_s2026 at 0.8634. raptor_v4_swa's 0.8938 is the exact cell board_check voided on 2026-08-29: knee-ie30 measured 896 of our 909 fold-0 holdout studies inside raptor's published labels_llm_soft.csv, 98.6% in-sample. Three seats already read 0.8977, so the whole curve is built on members that have seen the ruler.

Nothing in the tool objects. `--largest-pool`'s drop rule is 'shares a split AND a label table', which a foreign record satisfies — it is decoded onto OUR studies under OUR table, which is precisely what makes it mixable and precisely what makes it contaminated. foreign_overlap cannot see this: it takes a foreign LABEL TABLE, not a record, so it guards where a foreign model is PRICED and not where one is SEATED.

Workaround in use: filter the glob to the 77 records whose checkpoint is named in comp/members.roster (logs/roster_records.txt). That is correct by construction — the roster is where provenance is recorded, raptor_distill_s2026 is on it because we trained it, and the four raptor_v* are not on it because they are theirs. It is also hand-maintained, so it is a convention and not a guard.

Fix direction: record provenance IN the holdout record (or a sidecar) at write time, and have record_mix refuse a foreign record unless asked for one explicitly. 'The default is guilt' is already foreign_overlap's stated rule; the mixer does not implement it.

Do not quote 0.8994 or the six-seat count anywhere. The honest rerun over the roster-only pool is logs/pool_roster_0830.log.
notes:
2026-08-30 07:35Z, FIXED. The audit above was wrong on its own blocker, and that is what unblocked it.

Option (b) — provenance in the record — is not future work: it already exists. HoldoutRecord.write has
always written a `source` field, foreign_member stamps FOREIGN at line 190, and the default is TRAINED.
So the "142 existing records are unstamped, a default refusal would refuse the whole pool" reading is
false. A survey of the processed root: 144 records, 123 trained / 15 re-derived / 6 foreign, ZERO
unstamped. The six foreign are exactly the contaminating set (raptor_v4, raptor_v4_swa, raptor_v9,
raptor_effv2l480, raptor_cnv2b336, raptor_coat384). Guilt by default costs nothing and needs no backfill.

Neither candidate home was needed. record_mix never had to ask the roster who is ours — the record says
so itself — so MemberRoster does not move and the submission path is untouched. The import-linter
contract is not approached: HoldoutReading.source lives in kneemri.runs, which evaluation may import.

The fix: RecordMix(records, *, foreign=False). readings() drops a record stamped FOREIGN and names it
through the new foreign_dropped(), symmetric with dropped(). CLI gains --foreign. Two callers pass
foreign=True because they reproduce a SHIPPED fact rather than search: entry_offline.scored (dropping a
member an entry sent to the board would price a different ensemble under its name; contamination there
is declined()'s job, which already voids the row) and decode_entry.over (the search is ABOUT distinct
decodes, and a foreign member is where a distinct one comes from — it may never price a seat). The four
search callers — competence_axis, side_blindness, vote_ceiling, seat_value — keep the refusal.

Verified against the real records in both glob shapes. Over *.pt the foreign records were already dropped
by the no-checkpoint rule (they have no .pt beside them). Over *.holdout.npz — the shape that produced
0.8994 — path.exists() is trivially true for the record itself, so the dead-run rule does NOT fire and
this guard is the only thing standing there. It fires: raptor_v4_swa and raptor_v4 refused and named,
seated only under foreign=True.

The workaround is retired: the roster-name filter (logs/roster_records.txt) is no longer needed, because
the pool now refuses foreign records without consulting a hand-maintained file. Still do not quote 0.8994.

title: RememberedContrast: the fix contrast_dense pre-registered as its own suspect exists in this repo and was never pointed at it
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-30 03:33Z, no card, no slot. Answers knee-m69u's standing demand ('name a NEW axis or stop arming') with a lane that is not new but is UNRUN, and whose blocker is a dispatch chain rather than a measurement.

THE ARGUMENT, IN THE REPO'S OWN WORDS.

contrast_dense (knee-ek5s) ran 2026-08-27 and read -0.0087 against calib_dense_hold's 0.8634, eleven of twelve labels down. The ledger does NOT record that as a refutation, and it named why BEFORE the run: 'a batch of twelve sees a 7%-prevalence finding about once - the positives a supervised contrastive term needs are mostly absent from the batch it is computed on. That is a HARNESS suspect (faulty TRAINING), not the idea, and it fired exactly where predicted.' The reading on file is 'supervised contrastive at batch 12 costs 0.009 and buys nothing', not 'shaping the representation does not work'.

The ledger then names the precondition and marks it untried: 'RememberedRanking - a remembered pool of past readouts - is the named precondition and remains untried.' ContrastiveObjective's docstring says it twice more: 'RememberedRanking already proves the fix in this repo if the term shows signal at all.' MarginObjective carries the identical sentence for the identical reason.

THE FIX IS BUILT AND PROVEN HERE ALREADY. kneemri/training/remembered_ranking.py holds RememberedRanking, wired at run_setup.py:193 behind --pair-memory, over kneemri/training/pair_memory.py. Its own docstring closes the loop: the remembered side is 'a fixed target, exactly as in a contrastive memory queue'. It was built for the ranking term against the same batch-12 pathology, and it works.

WHY IT HAS NEVER RUN ON THE CONTRASTIVE TERM, and this is the whole finding: run_setup.objective is a single if-chain, and 'if options.contrast_weight' (line 187) returns ContrastiveObjective BEFORE 'if options.pair_memory' (line 192) is ever reached. The two flags cannot compose. This is NOT a silent hole - _check_contrast_alone raises, and its docstring is explicit that the reason is structural and not semantic: 'Not because the terms disagree - a representation term and a pairwise ordering term compose fine [...] but because the DISPATCH here is a single chain returning one class.' So the one experiment the ledger names as the precondition for the representation lane is blocked by the shape of a dispatch, and nobody has noticed because each half is individually correct.

WHAT TO BUILD. A RememberedContrast(ContrastiveObjective) holding a memory of past per-finding CONTEXT vectors (Readout.context, dimension D) rather than logits, so an anchor's positives and negatives are drawn from the pool and not from eleven batch neighbours. NOTE THE ONE REAL DESIGN QUESTION: PairMemory stores what the ranking term compares (logits/scores, twelve numbers a study); a context memory stores D-dimensional vectors twelve times a study, so the memory cost is real and has to be priced before the capacity is chosen. Whether PairMemory generalises or a sibling ContextMemory is the honest structure is an implementation call, not settled here.

PRICE, STATED BEFORE ANY CARD IS SPENT. Build ~1-2 h, no card. The arm costs what contrast_dense cost: 420 s an epoch x 12 = 84 min at dense/336, or roughly a third of that at 224 (knee-s9cr). Against the control already on disk at 0.8634, so no matched baseline arm is owed.

EXPECTED GAIN, HONESTLY. This does NOT plausibly deliver 1.5% and must not be sold as if it did. It is an INSTRUMENT in the sense CLAUDE.md licenses: it retires a suspicion the ledger has carried in writing since 2026-08-27, and it licenses or closes the whole REPRESENTATION axis - the one lane knee-m69u's axis table does not list as closed, because it has never been run under conditions where its supervision was non-degenerate. Two outcomes and both are worth the card:
  - term stops costing 0.0087 -> the representation lane is live and re-opens knee-ek5s's strong form (masks, knee-2sbk)
  - term still costs -> 'shaping the representation does not work HERE' becomes sayable for the first time, and the lane closes honestly instead of on a known-broken harness

AND THE DOWNSIDE IS ALREADY BOUNDED, which is unusual. contrast_dense LOST 0.0087 solo and STILL earned a seat - greedy forward selection under record_mix --largest-pool --vote logit over 104 records / 909 shared studies seats contrast_dense_s2026.pt FIFTH at 0.8749. The contrastive term changed WHAT THE MEMBER DISAGREES ABOUT, which is the owner's standing diversity thesis measured on our own pool rather than asserted. So a flat solo result here still produces a seat candidate, and a better-supervised version of a member that already seats fifth is the cheapest diversity we can manufacture.

PRE-REGISTERED READING, so this is not scored after the fact:
  - solo within +/-0.0062 of 0.8634 = FLAT: supervision was not the binding constraint; representation lane closes on price
  - solo above +0.0062: the batch-size artefact is confirmed and the axis re-opens
  - solo below -0.0062 again: the term is harmful independent of batch size; lane closes on mechanism
  - IN ALL THREE CASES also price the seat with seat_value, because the -0.0087 version already earned one

VERIFY THE FLAG LANDED before reading any number - this bead exists because a mechanism was blocked by plumbing nobody checked. Assert the run's stored recipe carries BOTH the contrast weight and the memory capacity, and that settings() reports the pool the memory really holds (RememberedRanking.settings already asks the memory itself rather than echoing the flag - copy that).

Depends on nothing. Blocks nothing. Closes when the arm runs and its pre-registered branch is recorded.
notes: PRICE: 40 min of card for one 12-epoch fit at the dense recipe (contrast_dense's own measured 420 s/epoch says 84 min is the honest upper bound — price an arm off its control's measured epoch time, not off a prediction). Zero submission slots. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0.02: this is member quality, and calibsix's measured ~23% board pass-through ceilings any such gain near 0.943, so the run is NOT sold as an improvement. It is armed as an INSTRUMENT under knee-qxse: what 40-84 min buys is which of three pre-registered readings is true — flat inside +/-0.0062 of 0.8634 closes the representation lane ON PRICE and sends topology to the strong form (masks, knee-2sbk); above contrast_dense's 0.8547 by more than 0.0062 CONFIRMS the batch-size artefact and re-opens the axis with a mechanism; below it closes the lane on MECHANISM, which is the stronger closure. P(one of the three lands cleanly) ~ 0.8, and the axis is retired or re-opened either way instead of staying open on a suspicion. Seat priced with seat_value in all three cases: contrast_dense lost 0.0087 solo and still seats fifth. WIRED 2026-08-30: RememberedContrast + PairMemory embedding + run_setup._contrastive dispatch; --pair-memory no longer refused beside --contrast-weight. Arm experiments/arms/contrast_pool.sh.
close_reason:
Built, armed, read, and it refuted the suspect it was built to test. RememberedContrast composes PairMemory with the supervised-contrastive term (the dispatch chain in run_setup.objective was the only thing that had ever blocked the pair, and _check_contrast_alone's refusal of --pair-memory beside --contrast-weight is lifted with the reason recorded). Equality oracle in the unit tests: an empty memory reproduces ContrastiveObjective exactly, so the arm is one variable against its control.

RESULT: contrast_pool_s2026 0.8515 at e5, converged. -0.0032 against contrast_dense_s2026 (0.8547, inside the 0.0062 floor) and -0.0119 against calib_dense_hold_s2026 (0.8634, outside it). Seat value 0.0000 - the honest greedy over the roster peaks at 0.8763/20 seats with or without it, identical to four decimals. Declined in comp/members.declines with the argument, not just the number.

THE MECHANISM FIRED, which is what makes this a refutation and not a null: training loss 5.859 vs the control's 3.605 at e0 and ~2.2 higher throughout, which is what widening a log-sum-exp denominator from 12 keys to 96 does. So the batch-size explanation contrast_dense offered for its own -0.0087 - 'a batch of twelve sees a 7%-prevalence finding roughly once' - is refuted on measurement. Eight times the contrastive population, no movement.

None of the three pre-registered readings applied; the fourth did. Supervised contrastive at this operating point closes on MECHANISM rather than on price. It does NOT close representation shaping generally - one formulation (SupCon over the readout, T=0.1, w=1.0), one attachment point. A re-open needs a different term, not this one at another weight.

Ledger: experiments/README.md 2026-08-30. Code shipped in 4839b5d.

title: A 3D encoder is the one named axis the ledger left untouched — price it before arming
description:
THE ARGUMENT, TAKEN FROM THE LEDGER RATHER THAN INVENTED. The `depth_true` row closes the aggregation
stage from three directions: more slices -0.0001, more slots +0.0002, and every combining rule within
0.0019 of every other (max 0.8457, order-aware gate 0.8461, mean 0.8473, permutation-blind gate 0.8476).
Its own conclusion is that the limit is UPSTREAM, in what one slice's feature vector contains. It then
names what it did NOT rule out, verbatim: "through-plane mixing at the FEATURE level is what died; a 3D
encoder that sees the volume before any per-slice feature exists is a different mechanism and untouched."

Nothing in beads and no row in experiments/README.md has touched it. Every member in the pool is a 2D
encoder run per-slice with a pooling stage bolted on.

WHY IT CLEARS knee-m69u'S BAR. m69u's standing position is that the card idling is correct until a NEW
axis is named, because every mapped axis is closed or knob-sized. This is a mechanism change, not a knob:
it alters what a feature vector can contain, which is precisely the quantity the aggregation work
identified as binding.

WHY IT IS WORTH IT EVEN IF THE MEMBER IS WEAKER. A 3D encoder is maximally decorrelated from twelve
slice-wise members. The owner's standing instruction: "even if a single model doesnt outperform our
previous models, its still worth testing if an ensemble with it have better performance - after all, its
about diversity, not averaging 7 numbers that are the same number." A 0.83 member that disagrees is worth
more here than a 0.86 member that does not.

WHAT MUST BE PRICED BEFORE ANY CARD TIME. Do not arm this on the strength of the argument above.
  1. Is there a pretrained 3D encoder available OFFLINE on this machine or fetchable, and is its licence
     compatible with the competition? Training a 3D encoder from scratch on 4406 studies is a different
     and much worse bet than fine-tuning one.
  2. Wall-clock for one arm, measured not guessed — a 3D encoder over ~20 slices is not the same cost as
     a 2D one over 20 slices.
  3. The cheap gate FIRST: the frozen-feature proxy called both signs correctly on the pooling axis at
     ~2 min against ~45 (see the depth_true row). Find out whether an equivalent proxy exists here before
     spending a full arm.

Ratio to state out loud when the answers are in: hours the arm costs, the gain the mechanism could
plausibly deliver, and the odds it clears 1.5%. Top-10 needs +0.0042 offline and no mapped axis pays it;
this is the only named candidate of that size besides a different corpus (knee-ombx, blocked on the owner).
notes:
WITHDRAWN THE SAME HOUR IT WAS FILED — the ledger had already armed this axis twice and I filed on an
incomplete grep. I searched experiments/README.md for "3d encoder|3D CNN|volume before|videomae|swin.*3d|
i3d" and none of those is the name it was run under. It is V-JEPA.

BOTH LEGS OF THE BEAD ARE FALSE, and each was measured:

1. "Untouched." False. `vjepa_probe` (2026-08-22) read V-JEPA 2 ViT-L frozen over the whole 12-slice
   stack: 0.7620 against a DINOv2-large control at 0.7669, a tie inside the 0.0062 floor with the
   capacity confound removed by construction. `vjepa_warm` (2026-08-22) then fitted it as a member at
   --whole-stack --slices 20 --train-size 256, which is exactly "sees the volume before any per-slice
   feature exists": solo holdout 0.8337 against roster members at 0.8525-0.8578.

2. "Maximally decorrelated from twelve slice-wise members, so worth a seat even if weaker." False, and
   this is the part that was actually measured rather than assumed. Residual distance to nearest
   neighbour 0.8210 (mean 0.8100), while the roster's MOST DISTANT seated member is 0.8801. The
   volumetric trunk is CLOSER to the pool than the pool's own outlier. Seat value +0.0002, 0 of 1
   clearing +0.0015.

So the diversity argument I built the bead on is the one the evidence contradicts most directly. A
different pretraining objective over a different input geometry produced a member that disagrees LESS
than the 2D members disagree with each other, which is a more interesting fact than the score is.

What the depth_true row meant by "untouched" was written before, or without reference to, these two rows.
It is not an open axis; it is a closed one under another name.

No card time to be spent here. Re-opening requires answering the residual-distance number, not re-quoting
the mechanism.

title: Does the gold ruler REORDER members, or only raise the level? Six hold-annotation members, no card cost
description:
knee-9198's last note names this and gates it: 'if the gold ruler is the one that tracks the board, member SELECTION should run on it ... Do not queue it before knee-bs4l reads; that pair is the cheapest evidence on whether the second ruler changes an ORDERING or only a level.' knee-bs4l HAS read (calibration +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotation, same sign), so the gate is lifted.

WHY THIS IS NOT A KNOB. Every selection this project makes -- the greedy seat search, the 28-seat pool ceiling of 0.8753 offline, the transfer line, and the verdict in 2026-08-30_the-board-priced-an-offline-constant.md that '+0.0042 has no payer' -- is computed on the report-derived PROXY. knee-9198 measures the proxy and the objective +0.045 apart on identical weights, and argues the proxy is structurally BIASED against label-side movement because the metric is per-label rank AUC and the two label sets rank studies differently. If the gold ruler reorders these six, the shortfall is partly a FAULTY TEST rather than a missing mechanism, and the whole selection stack is being run on the wrong ruler.

THE READ COSTS NOTHING. It needs no submission slot and no training. It is 58 studies x 6 members of inference, because six --hold-annotations members already exist and only those may legally be read there (annotated_readings REFUSES the rest with TrainedOnAnnotationsError rather than scoring them).

PROXY ORDERING, all six, fold-0 honest, one label table, one sweep (logs/pool112.log, 2026-08-30):
  calib_dense_hold 0.8634 | blendhold 0.8576 | band_dense_hold 0.8573
  calib_span_hold  0.8564 | holdannot 0.8506 | band_span_hold  0.8493

PRE-REGISTRATION, written before the gold numbers are read:
 - ORDERING PRESERVED (Spearman near 1) -> the gold ruler is a LEVEL shift, selection is safe on the proxy, and the +0.0042 shortfall stays a missing-mechanism problem. This is the outcome that keeps the current plan.
 - ORDERING CHANGES at the top -> member selection is running on the wrong ruler. That does not by itself buy a point, but it re-opens the selection axis, which every audit has closed, and it prices re-training the shipping roster under --hold-annotations (~6 x 40 min of card, knee-9198) as a real option rather than a speculative one.

THE LIMIT, and it is severe: n=58, ~696 cells, and per-label standard error 0.04-0.09 (label_power). Six members spanning 0.014 of proxy will not separate pairwise on 58 studies. So the readable claim is the ORDERING PATTERN (does the proxy's best stay best), not any pairwise delta, and a reorder is a reason to measure further, never a result on its own.

SECOND LIMIT, already documented in annotated_readings' own docstring: a --calibrated-targets member's targets carry Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT, a constant FITTED on these same 696 cells, and --hold-annotations drops the cells without refitting it. So calib_* members have a structural edge on this ruler. level_agreement.stability prices it -- 4 of 5 levels under 2 sigma on disjoint halves -- but it is not zero, and calib_dense_hold being the proxy leader makes it exactly the member the caveat lands on.

Log: logs/goldrank.log
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-08-30: it raises the level and orders NOTHING. Closing.

The body above carries a PRE-FIX table read through the crossing defect (knee-bk99) — five of six rows
were under the wrong member's name. Ignore it. The corrected numbers, verified by equality against six
single-member reads:

  member                 proxy  rank    gold  rank
  calib_span_hold       0.8564     4  0.9152     1
  calib_dense_hold      0.8634     1  0.9117     2
  band_span_hold        0.8493     6  0.9023     3
  band_dense_hold       0.8573     3  0.8956     4
  blendhold             0.8576     2  0.8952     5
  holdannot             0.8506     5  0.8932     6

Spearman 0.14 — read bare, the pre-registered "ORDERING CHANGES" outcome. It does not survive its own
interval. annotated_readings now prints paired deltas against a baseline named on the command line
(--against), and against the proxy's top member five of six pairs sit inside the band:

  band_dense   -0.0161 [-0.0355, +0.0019]
  band_span    -0.0094 [-0.0277, +0.0053]
  calib_span   +0.0035 [-0.0121, +0.0187]
  blendhold    -0.0165 [-0.0362, +0.0029]
  holdannot    -0.0185 [-0.0398, -0.0019]  clears, and in the SAME direction the proxy already had

The entire gold spread best-to-worst is 0.022, narrower than the half-width of every interval on the
page. The apparent reorder is one pair moving +0.0035 inside a band twelve times its width. Spearman 0.14
is what ranking six indistinguishable members produces by construction — the statistic was measuring the
denominator, not the ruler.

Write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-30_the-gold-ruler-raises-everyone-and-orders-no-one.md

title: member_curve scores full-fit members in-sample and admits them to the greedy
description:
`member_curve` scores every checkpoint handed to it on the fold-0 holdout, including members fitted at
`--fold -1`. A full-fit member has TRAINED on those studies, so its number is in-sample and inflated.

MEASURED, 2026-08-30: `logs/curve_pool.log` printed `base_dense_ff.pt alone: 0.9035` while every
honestly-scored member in the same sweep read 0.83-0.86. That is not a good member; it is a leaked one.
The `_ff` / `_cf` families are all affected: base_dense_ff, calib_dense_hold_ff, calib_span_ff,
final_ws_cf, grade_ladder_cf, grade_ladder_ff, lr4e-5_ws_cf, lr4e-5_ws_ff, small_batch6_ff,
through_dense_cf, through_dense_ff.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE WRONG NUMBER: the greedy seats in score order, so leaked members are seated
FIRST. Any seat ordering or honest-seat count derived from a member_curve sweep over a mixed pool is
meaningless, and it fails SILENTLY — the log looks like every other sweep.

THE SISTER TOOL ALREADY HANDLES THIS. `kneemri/evaluation/record_mix.py` skips them, logging
`no holdout record, skipped` (record_mix.py:139 and :409), which is why `logs/greedy_named.log` reads
`111 of 200 records became members`. The asymmetry is the defect: two tools answering the same question,
one of which refuses leaked members and one of which averages them in.

FIX: `member_curve` should apply the same skip — a member with no holdout record cannot be scored on the
holdout. Its `seat_value` path already skips them; the `alone:` scoring loop does not. Make the skip
happen once, at pool construction, so both paths inherit it.

TEST THAT PINS IT: a pool containing one fold-0 member and one `--fold -1` member yields a curve over
the fold-0 member only, and names the skipped one.

title: greedyseat: fire a PROCEDURALLY selected fold-0 seven to buy back the offline ruler
description:
WHY, and it is not the score. comp/champion.json:53 records that two pins in a row bought board position by spending the ability to measure offline: six of the champion's seven seats are --fold -1, so the pinned entry has NO offline number by construction and board.jsonl records offline null. board_transfer confirms the damage from the other side - 29 of 31 ensemble entries are one-sided, and above 0.8691 the compression constant rests on FIVE resolved pairs. Every roster decision is now made against the board alone at five slots a day.

WHAT. The seven seats the greedy named over 111 members (logs/greedy_named.log): calib_dense_hold_s2026, merged_span_cf, labelwise_dense_s2026, blendhold_s2026, finding_calib_dense_s2026, margin_seat_s2026, warm_calib_dense_s2026. Offline 0.8768. All seven are already on comp/members.roster, so it is packageable with no new training. All seven are fold-0 and carry holdout records, so the entry IS seat-scoreable - which the champion is not.

TWO THINGS IN ONE SLOT. (1) The instrument: an anchored fold-0 point at the TOP of the offline range converts future seat decisions from a slot each into free offline reads. (2) A mechanism never tested: every entry this project has shipped was HAND-PICKED. Procedural greedy selection has never been put on the board.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS, from two fold-0 anchors in board.jsonl mapped at the top-band compression +0.89 to +0.97 board points per holdout point: 7-member anchor 0.8712 -> 0.933 gives +0.0056 * 0.89..0.97 = 0.938; top anchor 0.8751 -> 0.937 gives 0.9385. Both agree.
  >= 0.943 - procedural selection matches or beats hand-picking AND the fold-0 penalty is smaller than believed. Two results at once; re-read the all-data boundary.
  0.936-0.942 - AS PREDICTED. The ruler is bought, the anchor lands, no score claim. This is the expected outcome and it is a success for the stated purpose.
  0.930-0.935 - the anchor still lands and is still worth having, but the fold-0 all-data dose is larger at the top than the -0.004/-0.005 previously measured, which is itself a recorded finding.
  < 0.930 - procedural selection is WORSE than hand-picking by more than the fold-0 dose can explain; suspect the greedy overfits its own in-sample selection over 111 members before blaming the seats.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE. The greedy run is IN-SAMPLE over 111 members and seats 10 and 11 go to the pool's two worst members inside a plateau where +0.0024 buys twenty-five seats. A good board number here does not make the greedy order a ranking. And it does not touch the champion pin: raptorseat_v1 at 0.943 stays.

COST: one slot, zero card time, no training. Does NOT spend the slot held for the owner's explicit go.
notes:
LANDED. 55877491 scored 0.936 -- the bottom edge of the pre-registered 0.936-0.942 AS PREDICTED band.

THE INSTRUMENT WORKED, AND IT DID MORE THAN ANCHOR. Through the two prior fold-0 anchors
(0.8712 -> 0.933, 0.8751 -> 0.937; slope 1.026 board points per holdout point):

  raw greedy in-sample 0.8768 -> predicts 0.9387, rounds 0.939, actual 0.936, err -0.0027
  bias-corrected       0.8740 -> predicts 0.9359, rounds 0.936, actual 0.936, err +0.0001

The +0.0028 greedy selection bias was measured purely offline on 111 records. The board prices the same
correction at +0.0027 without being shown it. That is a cross-ruler confirmation of an offline constant,
and it is the real return on this slot.

IT ALSO KILLS AN APPARENT RULER INVERSION. Raw, this entry reads offline UP 0.0017 against the previous
anchor while the board went DOWN 0.001 -- the third point breaking the ordering, the same shape recorded
before. It is not an inversion: it is the greedy bias, and the correction restores the ordering exactly.
Any future entry selected by search must be entered in board.jsonl bias-corrected, never raw.

PROCEDURAL SELECTION DOES NOT BEAT HAND-PICKING. 0.936 vs raptorweight_v1's 0.944. The fold-0 all-data
dose covers ~half (-0.004/-0.005), leaving ~0.003-0.004 for the selection term itself -- above the
0.0015 board resolution by two ticks, so present but small. STATED LIMIT: no hand-picked fold-0 seven
exists, so this crosses the fold boundary and the dose is an estimate, not a matched control.

Row written to comp/board.jsonl with offline 0.8740 (corrected) and offline_scope naming the correction.
Documented in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md. board_check --live and champion_check both green; the champion pin
stays raptorweight_v1 at 0.944, as the pre-registration said it would.

title: Foreign seat WEIGHT is unmeasured: 1/7 is a convention, the mechanism says ~1/3
description:
FILED 2026-08-29 21:15Z. No bead has ever named this dial.

WHAT IS UNMEASURED. Every foreign-seat entry holds RaptorSeat.weight = 1/7. raptor_seat.py states its own
reason: "One member entering a six-member roster takes one seat of seven, which is the weight every seating
entry in this project's history has used." That is a convention about SEAT COUNT, and the premise is wrong
about what is being blended.

THE MECHANISM. The blend is two SYSTEMS, not seven members. Ours is a six-member logit-average at 0.941
board. Theirs is ONE model at 0.923 board (raptor_solo 55829913) - level with our best single by
measurement. A 0.941 system and a 0.923 system averaged at 6:1 gives the independent side a seventh of the
vote when its quality justifies nearer a third. Equal quality would say even; ours is stronger and is
itself an ensemble, so ~1/3 is the honest correction.

WHY IT SURVIVES TODAY'S CLOSURES. fleettwo_v1 closed the COUNT dimension of foreign seating (0.942, flat).
fourseat/trioseat closed our own seat count. Neither touched the weight. It is the one dial of the
foreign-seating axis with no reading at all.

IT IS ALSO AN INSTRUMENT FOR knee-uco3. That P0 reads dark6's 0.937 as the seventh seat being INERT. An
inert seat cannot care about its weight: flat here CONFIRMS knee-uco3, any move REFUTES it.

WHY ONE SLOT AND NOT A SWEEP. Board-only, because every raptor arm is --fold -1 and no offline pairing
exists - raptor_seat.py's own objection. So spend ONE at the largest step the mechanism supports:
0.143 -> 0.333, a 2.3x move. Slope shows in one slot; flat closes the axis in one instead of four.

KERNEL: comp/kernels/kneemri-raptorweight, built 2026-08-29 21:14Z. One float differs from
raptorseat_v1 - same six, same order, same overlap=False, same LogitAverage, same kit, same checkpoint.

PRE-REGISTERED (vs champion 0.943, BOARD_RESOLVABLE 0.0015):
  >=0.946        real lever AND top ten. Re-pin champion.json; next slot sweeps to 1/2.
  0.9435-0.9455  real gain. Keep 1/3; price 1/2 only on an idle slot.
  0.9405-0.943   FLAT. Foreign seating closed in both dimensions. knee-uco3 gains support.
  <=0.940        dilutes at real weight. 1/7 was at or near a maximum; stop widening the foreign side.

LIMIT IT CANNOT PASS: cannot separate "the weight is flat" from "THIS foreign member is flat". Same
--fold -1 limit fleettwo_v1 carries for the count dimension.
notes:
RESULT: raptorweight_v1 read 0.944 (ref 55875622, scored 2026-08-30). New best row; pin moved in comp/champion.json.

THE BAND LABEL AND THE ARITHMETIC DISAGREE AND THE ARITHMETIC WINS. 0.944 landed in the pre-registered 0.9435-0.9455 branch, whose text reads 'a real gain over the champion, above the resolution floor'. It is not. 0.944 - 0.943 = +0.001, UNDER this arm's own BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015, and 0.9435 was never an attainable score because the board quantises to 0.001. The band was mis-drawn: it put a clears-the-floor label on a value below the floor. Every future pre-registration on this board must snap its edges to attainable 0.001 steps and check each edge against the floor before the number arrives.

WHAT IS TRUE: this is the best board row the project owns and the pin follows it. WHAT IS NOT: the weight is not shown to be a lever. A 2.3x change in the foreign share moved one unresolvable tick, which reads closer to the FLAT branch than the gain branch. With fleettwo_v1's flat count reading, NEITHER dimension of the foreign-seating axis has produced a resolvable move, and knee-uco3's inert-seat reading gains its second support.

DO NOT sweep the weight to 1/2. That instruction was conditional on clearing the floor and the floor was not cleared.

title: Nothing writes comp/members.roster when a run finishes — 5 of 16 best seats were missing
description:
Found 2026-08-29 21:05Z while building the 16-seat entry. Five of its sixteen seats were not in comp/members.roster: merged_span_cf (greedy seat 2, solo 0.8618), labelwise_dense_s2026 (seat 3, solo 0.8613 — THIRD-BEST SOLO THE PROJECT OWNS, and the only member pooling slices labelwise), warm_calib_dense_s2026 (seat 7, a warm restart from a fitted encoder — the lane champion.json calls '0 of 131 arms have ever used'), focus_mcl_s2026 (seat 11), contrast_dense_s2026 (seat 13).

The roster is the package's ONLY definition: a member absent from it cannot be shipped no matter what any other file says. So this was five of the sixteen best available seats silently unshippable, including the third-best checkpoint in the project.

MECHANISM: a run finishing writes a checkpoint, a holdout record and (usually) a ledger section. NOTHING writes the roster. It is a hand-edited file, so every member in it is there because somebody remembered.

FIX, mechanically checkable: a check asserting the roster is the scoreable pool minus an EXPLICITLY DOCUMENTED decline. Every .pt under the processed root with a holdout record is either (a) named in members.roster, or (b) named in a declines list with a reason. Anything in neither is a finding. That would have caught all five, and it costs one pass over a directory.

NOTE the trap it must avoid: 12 checkpoints are smoke runs or scored under an older label table (record_mix --largest-pool drops them by name). Those belong in the declines list, not the roster.

Related: knee-utxq (the 16-seat entry this was found building), and the process lesson recorded in experiments/README.md — recover provenance from metrics.jsonl BEFORE declining an undocumented checkpoint, since the recipe is always there.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-30 00:05Z, and the defect was three times the size the bead recorded. kneemri.kaggle.roster_check (committed, unit-tested, 9 tests) asserts every checkpoint under the processed root that has a HoldoutRecord is named in comp/members.roster OR in the new comp/members.declines WITH A REASON; a bare name in the declines file is itself a finding, because a name alone records that somebody decided and not what. It also reports a member that is in BOTH files and a roster line matching nothing on disk.

FIRST RUN: 123 scoreable of 200 checkpoints, 47 packaged, 0 declined, 76 UNDOCUMENTED. Not five - seventy-six. And the worst of them is not labelwise_dense_s2026: stackfit_s2026 scores 0.8631 solo under LogitAverage on the 909-study fold-0 holdout, which makes it the SECOND-BEST solo checkpoint the project owns (behind calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634 and ahead of merged_span_cf 0.8618), and it was unshippable. raptor_distill_s2026 0.8613 and distill_pairs_s2026 0.8594 were too.

THE SPLIT, and the rule is not a score cut. Thirty members joined the roster: every undocumented member clearing 0.8460 solo, which is extended_ws_s2026 - the weakest member this roster has ever added on MERIT. The roster does package weaker checkpoints (lora_r8_v3small 0.8215, crop80_tissue 0.8345, focus_mcl 0.5332), but each of those is a named INSTRUMENT, which is a reason and not a number; so the way back onto the roster from a decline is to name the instrument the member would be. Forty-six were declined in writing: thirty-four below that merit level, eleven smoke/probe runs that never became members on the current label table, and confident224_s2026 - a REAL arm that falls out of the same-ruler pool and returns on a rescore (knee-8hau), written down as such so it is not mistaken for a twelfth smoke run.

AFTER: 123 scoreable, 77 packaged, 46 declined, 0 undocumented, exit 0. Wired into CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as the thirteenth check, to be run after any run finishes and before building an entry out of the pool.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not push the package - the roster is the DEFINITION, and thirty new lines mean a dataset push before any of them can be mounted. That is a separate, deliberate step (package_members), and knee-0dtv was about the definition.

title: Ship the 16-seat entry: same 5 decodes as 28, +0.0045 offline, prices at ~+0.005 board
description:
From the matched seat curves (2026-08-29 20:50Z, experiments/README.md). The honest curve — greedy refit on half the studies, scored on the other half, so no selection bias — peaks at 0.8753 with 28 members. The shipped champion's five-twin shadow reads 0.8701. That is +0.0052 offline, the first delta since fourseat_v1 that is near the 0.0053 floor rather than a tenth of it, and it comes from SEAT COUNT rather than from member quality (closed, knee-07b0) or rank-space diversity (refuted, same section).

Unknown and blocking: what those 28 members cost in DECODES. The roster's 56 seats ride 27 on one decode, 19 on a second, ten singletons; if the honest 28 scatter across ten decodes it is unshippable inside the kernel's runtime, and the efficiency track (rank 16, 0.925) gets worse not better.

Next step, both free and no slot:
  1. Pull the 28 names from logs/seats_honest.log (the honest curve names its picks in order).
  2. python -m kneemri.kaggle.roster_reads --candidates <the 28> — prices them in decodes.
  3. If the read cost is one or two decodes, this is the best-argued candidate for the one spendable slot. If it is ten, ask decode_entry for the best 28-seat set CONSTRAINED to few decodes and re-read the honest number under that constraint.

Note the denominator trap decode_entry already fell into once: its search sees the SCOREABLE pool only, so a set it proposes cannot include any --fold -1 member. The honest curve has the same blind spot, which is a floor on what a shipped roster does, not a ceiling.
notes:
CLOSED WITHOUT A SLOT, 2026-08-29 21:12Z — REFUTED BY AN ENTRY THAT ALREADY SHIPPED.

comp/board.jsonl holds honest12 (ref 55817896, 2026-08-27): the SAME instrument, `record_mix --seats
honest --vote logit`, seated at its own peak of TWELVE. Offline 0.8751, board 0.937. Champion 0.943.
Its holdout said +0.0050 and the board paid -0.006: a sign flip, not a compression.

The 16-seat set here is honest12 plus six more seats from the same greedy — ten of honest12's twelve
recipes are in it. So its transfer coefficient is not unmeasured; it is measured once and negative.
Both pre-registered branches (0.945-0.950 / 0.940-0.943) omitted the only branch with evidence, ~0.937.

MY ERROR: priced this off champion.json's saturation prose (6-11 seats, ~0.941) and never opened
board.jsonl, which carries a twelve-seat entry off this exact curve with a score and a written verdict.
CLAUDE.md's rule — read the ledger and the record before filing — would have caught it in one grep.

WHAT SURVIVES: the six members surfaced by the hunt, all now rostered and documented, and knee-0dtv.
The seating dies, the members do not. honest12's own verdict sends the next slot to a better SINGLE
member (knee-wbwq, warm restarts) — and warm_calib_dense_s2026 (0.8562) is now on disk and rostered.

title: The kaggle CLI is uninstalled again — sync ALL five extras before the next slot
description:
python -m kneemri.kaggle.board_read --live died 2026-08-29 19:45Z on ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'kaggle' (board_read.py:108). Same failure as the one already recorded in memory: uv sync --extra X UNINSTALLS every extra not named on that invocation, and the extras here are five - dev, submit, foreign, reader, devtools. Any sync that names fewer removes the rest silently, and 'submit' is the one that carries the Kaggle CLI.

CONSEQUENCE RIGHT NOW: board_read cannot run, so comp/leaderboard.json cannot be refreshed, and champion_check refuses a read over two days old. No slot can be spent and no board gap can be quoted until this is fixed.

NOT FIXED IMMEDIATELY ON PURPOSE. focus_mcl owns the card until ~20:25Z and a sync may try to rewrite torch DLLs the running process holds open. Do it after the arm exits:

    GIT_SHIM_LOG_ONLY=1 uv sync --extra dev --extra submit --extra foreign --extra reader --extra devtools

(the shim flag because a devtools_ref build needs git reset --hard in uv's own cache), then re-run board_read --live and confirm comp/leaderboard.json's taken timestamp moved.

THE PERMANENT FIX is not another reminder - this has now cost the CLI twice. Either fold the five names into a nox session (uvx nox -s sync) so the list lives in one place, or make board_read fail with the exact sync command in its message instead of a raw ModuleNotFoundError.

title: Backfill offline holdout reads for the 35 ensemble entries that have a board number and none
description:
comp/board.jsonl now holds 74 of 74 live submissions, but 35 of the 60 ensemble-scope rows carry a board number and offline: null - including the pinned champion raptorseat_v1, calibsix_v1, votefit_v1, soloseat_v1, calibsolo, onepair_v1, trioseat_v1, fleettwo_v1 and fourseat_v1. Every one of those is a pair board_transfer cannot form, which is why the regime that actually prices today's decisions is fitted on THREE resolved pairs (top cell +0.99 [+0.77, +1.18]).

This costs no card and no slot: each entry is a set of members already on disk, served through the same vote the kernel used, scored on the fold-0 holdout. The blocker is that some entries are all --fold -1 members, whose holdout sits inside their training set - those must stay null rather than be filled with an in-sample number, which is exactly the defect knee-* on raptor_solo just cost us. So the deliverable is: fill the ones that CAN be honestly filled, and record scope/reason for the ones that cannot.

Why it matters: the compression constant and the ensemble-bonus law are both quoted as planning premises, and both are currently fitted mostly on entries from before 2026-08-20.
notes:
2026-08-29 21:40Z DONE, and the deliverable was the bound rather than the numbers. kneemri.kaggle.entry_offline surveys every null offline cell and either fills it or records offline_scope naming why not. 34 rows with named members and a null: 10 filled (ratepair_v1, solotop_v1, rateviews_v1, topviews_v1, sixstrong_v1, sixfresh_v1, sevengrade_v1, sixfresh_v2, sevenplane_v1, accumseat_v1; board 0.921-0.933; scored under RankAverage because all ten shipped before kneemri-vote served LogitAverage), 24 declined - 20 in-sample (_ff / final_ws_e12), 2 foreign-in-sample (raptor_v4_swa, per foreign_overlap), 2 no-record (_cf merges wrote no holdout file).

board_transfer re-fit: whole record +1.55 -> +1.25; top regime (>=0.8668) +0.99 [+0.77,+1.18] on THREE pairs -> +0.97 [+0.94,+1.11] on FIFTEEN; a second cell now resolves at >=0.8691 (+0.89 [+0.70,+1.19], 5 pairs); inversions 0/127 -> 0/233 resolved.

The constant did not move (0.02, inside its own interval). The interval halved and the pair count went 3 -> 15. So this bought CONFIDENCE in a premise already being quoted, not a new premise. Compression above board 0.937 stays unmeasured and the file now says so per row.

title: Foreign checkpoints trained on 896 of our 909 holdout studies; the +0.030 member gap is contamination and is retired
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-29T17:44Z. No card, no slot. One set intersection against two files already on disk.

THE ANOMALY. Two readings of one checkpoint, raptor_v4_swa, disagree by ~0.05 and both were already in the repo. knee-9g28 (closed 2026-08-27) scored it at 0.8938 on our 909-study fold-0 holdout against our best member 0.8634 — +0.0304 at 0.0% fallback. knee-rh4t (2026-08-28) records the same checkpoint scoring 0.923 solo on the board, exactly level with our own best single. board_transfer fits +1.72 to +1.82x, so +0.0304 offline predicts ~+0.05 on the board. It delivered 0.000, and the two numbers were never put beside each other.

THE MEASUREMENT. Their published label table D:/data/external/raptor/labels/labels_llm_soft.csv against our own ReportFolds assignment:
  corpus 4407 | fold0 holdout 909 | their labels 4349
  holdout in their label file: 896 / 909
  gold in their label file:      0 / 58
  holdout that is gold:         13
The arithmetic closes exactly (909 = 896 + 13). Their row set is the corpus MINUS the 58 gold and nothing else, and our holdout is 98.6% inside it. That is the signature of train-on-everything-hold-out-the-oracle, corroborated from their side by the fact that the metric their checkpoints self-report is gold_auc on those same 58.

THE THREE RULERS. gold 58, both held out: 0.9167 vs 0.9152, NULL. Our fold-0 909, theirs 98.6% in-sample: +0.0304. Board hidden test, both held out: 0.923 vs 0.923, NULL. Two clean rulers agree at zero; the single contaminated one carries the whole gap.

WHAT IT KILLS. The member gap as a quantity. Its four supports are now: a forum self-report of 0.938-0.942 (single, unreproduced, already flagged on knee-rh4t), the +0.030 offline lead (contaminated), the board (null), the gold 58 (null). On every ruler where both models are honest, the best published member of this field and ours are level. Six open P0s rest on member quality being the free term and that premise now has no measurement behind it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT KILL. The foreign member as a SEAT. Its seat values were priced on the same contaminated ruler, so raptor solo 0.8928 and champion-six-plus-raptor 0.8910 are unreadable in BOTH directions. The pricing is void, not the seat. Re-pricing needs a ruler it did not train on: the gold 58 (too small to seat on) or the board (a slot). Also untouched: the 224px throughput argument (knee-s9cr) rests on our own ledger, and every purely-internal comparison is unaffected — this is contamination in one foreign checkpoint family, not in our fold.

THE CORRECTION OWED, AND IT IS FILED. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-feed-was-the-whole-shortfall.md has a section 'A ruler that disagrees with itself' that spots this exact contradiction and pins it on OUR selection over 105 arms, concluding the member gap is NOT retired. The selection effect is real and secondary; it cannot explain the board null. Correction appended to that page; full reading in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-29_the-foreign-member-trained-on-our-holdout.md.

THE GUARD. python -m kneemri.evaluation.foreign_overlap --foreign <table> [--fold N] [--assert-clean], committed with four unit tests. Default is GUILT: a competitor's model has seen our holdout unless their own artefacts prove otherwise, since our fold assignment is a hash of report text that no external party has any reason to respect. Costs no card and no slot, and runs BEFORE the number is read rather than two days after it has driven six P0s.

WHERE IT POINTS. knee-fuhq. Two independently built models — different architecture, decode, corpus and label reader — landing on the same 0.923 on a hidden test is what a shared supervision ceiling looks like, and it is the only reading left standing.

title: The offline ruler resolves ~0.004; below that a submission is a coin flip
description:
Fit board on offline over the 22 scored ensemble entries in comp/board.jsonl whose offline column is our ruler on our members (raptor_solo excluded, foreign member on a different ruler):

  slope 2.099   95% CI [1.197, 3.012]   r 0.855   residual sd 0.0078
  forced slope 1.00 -> residual sd 0.0101
  forced slope 1.82 -> residual sd 0.0078

THE CONSTANT SURVIVES. board_transfer ~ +1.82 sits inside the interval and fits as well as the free slope, so nothing recorded needs changing.

THE INTERVAL AND THE RESIDUAL ARE THE FINDING. [1.20, 3.01] is not a multiplier to believe a product from. Residual sd 0.0078 is what predicting a board score from an offline score is actually worth, and it is comparable to the ENTIRE gap to first place (0.009 at the 14:00Z live read).

TWO CONSEQUENCES, both about slot spending:
1. An offline difference under ~0.004 predicts nothing about the board — the two rosters' predicted board scores overlap almost completely. This is the quantitative reason sixteen board entries sit inside 0.005 of each other despite each being chosen as an improvement: the ruler that chose them cannot resolve them.
2. It prices the honest seat plateau. Eight seats to twenty-four is +0.0005 offline, an eighth of the resolution floor. Submitting to find out which is better spends a slot on a coin flip.

So a slot buys knowledge only for a change big enough to clear ~0.004 offline. Nothing in the current pool is. This is the case FOR the raddino arm and AGAINST another reseating, in the instrument's own units, and it is why the spendable slot stayed holstered today.

A METHOD NOTE THAT COST ME A WRONG FILING. Reading the gap board-minus-offline down the TOP EIGHTEEN entries it looks like a flat OFFSET of +0.061 with no slope at all, which would contradict +1.82 outright. Those eighteen span an offline range of 0.017; range restriction flattens a slope toward zero, and eyeballing the top of a score-sorted list IS range restriction. Fit the whole set or do not fit.

ALSO SETTLED HERE (see the same interpretation): the _cf leak does NOT reach the shipped champion. honest12 carries two fold-1 members and its board-minus-offline gap is +0.0619 against a pack mean of ~+0.0613 — about +0.0006 of inflation, a third of the scatter. Two leaked members of twelve are real and unmeasurable. That does NOT clear the honest seat curve, where the leak is two of EIGHT and greedy selected them on their leaked scores; it caps how large that inflation can be.

Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-29_seats-per-decode.md
notes:
2026-08-29 15:11Z — the _cf half of this issue's description is RETRACTED; the transfer measurement is not.

The description says the _cf leak 'does NOT reach the shipped champion' and reads honest12's +0.0006
residual as an upper bound on its size. There is no leak to bound — _cf is scheme=merged, fold 0 of 5,
split_seed 2026, same split as every other member (knee-anx7). The +0.0006 is what a roster with no leaked
member looks like. An effect that is merely small when the hypothesis predicts small is not confirmation.

EVERYTHING ELSE STANDS and none of it depended on the leak: slope 2.099, CI [1.197, 3.012], r 0.855,
residual sd 0.0078, +1.82 fitting as well as the free slope, and the range-restriction trap that nearly
had me file the constant as refuted. The two consequences for slot spending are unchanged — an offline
difference under ~0.004 predicts nothing about the board, and the eight-to-twenty-four plateau (+0.0005)
is a coin flip to submit.

title: card_check exists and I skipped it, because label_combine's docstring says 'costs no card' and that is conditional on a warm cache
description:
