title: Rank the 105 members on the three deficit findings alone, then price the top as a seat
description:
competence_axis (2026-08-27) found that ACL, MCL and Lateral Meniscus carry near-zero loading on the pool's one shared axis (+0.014, +0.053, +0.028) while their own across-member spreads are ORDINARY (0.0141, 0.0165, 0.0183 - above Contusion's 0.0097). Members differ on the three findings the supervision gap resolved as our deficit, and that difference is orthogonal to every design axis we have swept. It is idiosyncratic, which is precisely the variation a flat rank-average destroys.

THE STEP. Take the double-centred competence matrix competence_axis already builds, average each member's residual over {ACL, MCL, Lateral Meniscus}, rank, and hand the top of that ranking to seat_value against the champion roster. Costs no card and no slot: every array exists.

WHY IT IS WORTH A P1. It is the first evidence this project has that a TARGETED seat choice has something to select on. Every seat search so far ranked on the mean, which is the direction the pool is already saturated in (member quality is 81.7% of the spread). A selection rule aimed at a bounded, resolved weakness is a different die, not a better roll of the same one.

THE DISCOUNT, stated up front. 2026-08-27_every-no-card-axis-is-priced-and-flat.md prices every seat permutation between -0.004 and +0.001, and this is still a seat permutation. Also the deficit-strong member may be an _s2026 fold-0 member while the champion seats _cf/_ff, and crossing fit regimes gives back the +0.004 the regime is worth - so a cross-regime winner is a CARD question (build the twin), not a slot question.

Reading: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-pool-is-82-percent-one-number.md, knee-54yp, knee-yx0n
notes:
DONE, and the answer is a CEILING rather than a seat. 2026-08-27 19:40Z.

RANKED. kneemri/evaluation/competence_axis.py now answers --on <findings>, ranking members by double-centred residual competence on a subset named IN ADVANCE. On {ACL, MCL, Lateral Meniscus}: mae_matched +0.0242, encoder_adapt +0.0189, encoder_adapt_gentle +0.0178, encoder_layer_9 +0.0171, band_density +0.0166, lr2e-4_ws +0.0158.

THE PRICING HALF CANNOT BE RUN, and would not be worth running. Two independent blocks:
(1) REGIME, and it is total rather than partial. 103 of the 105 members are _s2026 fold-0; only merged_blend_cf and merged_dense_cf carry a holdout record, because a --fold -1 member holds nothing out by construction. Five of the champion's six seats are not in the matrix at all, so the champion cannot be scored offline and seat_value has no baseline to price against. The description guessed this as a risk ('may be an _s2026 member'); it is not a risk, it is the pool.
(2) CEILING, and this is the one that closes it. knee-q1pf (weights_gap, 2026-08-23) prices the ENTIRE per-label weak-column programme at +0.0043 on the mean, and measured us BEATING the twenty published members on ACL by +0.0292 and on Lateral Meniscus by +0.0712 - the largest margin on that table. Two of the three findings this bead selects on are the two we lead the field on hardest. Only MCL is a competitive deficit (-0.0346) and buying it outright is +0.0029, under the 0.0062 arm-vs-arm floor. focus_mcl was already cancelled on this same arithmetic in August.

The supervision gap is ABSOLUTE (our pixels vs our reports); weights_gap is RELATIVE (our pixels vs theirs). Both true. Absolute headroom is not a competitive lever when the whole field shares it - that sentence is the finding, and it retires the targeted-seat idea rather than the deficit measurement.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is worth more than the seat was. Four of the top five are ENCODER arms (three explicit adaptation arms plus an MAE-pretrained one); the first geometry arm is fifth. Encoder arms are a minority of the 105 and nothing in the ranking favours them, so the clustering is signal. That converges with knee-wbwq from a completely different direction (arm-script archaeology: fitted_encoder exists, 0 of 131 arms use it, merge_adapters doubles adaptation capacity) and with knee-q1pf's own does-not-rule-out list, which names 'a genuinely different encoder'. warm_calib_dense_s2026, the one warm-started member on disk, ranks 10th here at +0.0116. Member quality is not capped by a per-label ceiling.

Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-pool-is-82-percent-one-number.md

title: Supervision-gap aggregate spans zero: only ACL, MCL, Lateral Meniscus and Effusion are resolved
description:
The 0.027 model-below-teacher gap that has been steering the queue was bounded this session with the paired band SupervisionGap.separation now prints: +0.0266 [-0.0082, +0.0610] over 58 studies. It INCLUDES ZERO, so neither the label-bottleneck branch (the forum's reading) nor the modelling-headroom branch (ours) is licensed on the aggregate any more.

What survives is the split. Four of twelve per-finding bands exclude zero and they are the four largest gaps: ACL -0.1225, MCL -0.0964, Lateral Meniscus -0.1925 on the deficit side, Effusion +0.1304 on the label side. Twelve bands read together are twelve chances, so this is a shape not four findings - but it lands on both sides and it converges with the blendlabels arm, whose pre-registered six/six partition from this same split landed +0.0070 on the six against +0.0034 on all twelve.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE CARD. The three resolved deficit findings are all thin ligamentous/fibrocartilaginous structures whose report labels are excellent (0.9865 / 0.9762 / 0.8422) and whose pixels the model cannot read (0.8640 / 0.8798 / 0.6497). No label work reaches them. This is the first capacity argument this project holds that rests on a bounded number rather than a mean. The honest next step is the CHEAPEST instrument that separates resolution from capacity on those three specifically - not a bigger backbone armed on the strength of this reading.

See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-supervision-gap-is-four-findings-not-an-average.md.
notes:
INSTRUMENT RUN THE SAME HOUR, and it closes the pixel branch. The pair lr4e-5_ws_s2026 (336 px) vs res392_ws_s2026 (392/448) already exists on disk, identical on every other flag. On the three resolved deficit findings: ACL +0.0109, MCL -0.0088, Lateral Meniscus -0.0001, MEAN -0.0002. Mixed signs, nothing marked against its own paired band (half-widths to +/-0.0353), and run_comparison flags the structure-scale summary INVERTED (focal -0.0027 vs regional +0.0032). The ledger had called this axis flat twice at two rates, but both readings were MEANS; this is the first read on the split, and it agrees.

CONSEQUENCE: the deficit is not in-plane sampling. knee-jk3's '336 px for findings a few voxels across' is now read down on the exact findings it claimed, not just on the mean. The capacity argument points at THROUGH-PLANE coverage and architecture instead - consistent with band_dense (20 slices, +0.0053) being the only geometry change that ever moved this family. Do not arm an in-plane resolution rung.

title: Cross the two treatments that actually paid: calibrated targets ON a blend-supervised twin
description:
The board's own lesson, read across 58 submissions on 2026-08-27: the only two changes worth more than one tick are TREATMENTS APPLIED TO EVERY SEAT AT ONCE, never seat permutations.

  votefit 0.938 -> calibsix 0.941   --calibrated-targets on all six      +0.003
  fit regime                        --fold -1 on every seat              +0.004 (ema_dense separates EMA at +0.0010)

Every seat permutation tried since is worth between -0.004 and +0.001.

Blend supervision is the ONLY other treatment of the all-seats shape - it changes the label SOURCE (external expert reads, Rijeka) where calibration re-scales the label VALUES. Different mechanisms on different parts of the pipeline is the standard precondition for two effects to add rather than overlap. The cross has never been built: no calibrated blend twin exists.

Honest discount, pre-registered: the blend DOSE curve is flat from one seat to three (votefit 0.938 -> blendseat 0.939 -> blendthree 0.939), so blend's own axis may be saturated and the cross may inherit that. What licenses arming it anyway is that dose was measured as seat REPLACEMENT while calibration was measured as an all-seat TREATMENT, and the board says only the second shape pays. The cross has not been measured in the shape that works.

Card question, not a slot question - needs a blend-supervised twin trained with --calibrated-targets. First thing to arm when the card returns from the peer project. Smoke it with arm_check --only <arm> --smoke <throwaway dir> --smoke-studies 60 before queueing.

Evidence: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_every-no-card-axis-is-priced-and-flat.md

title: The 0.0062 floor has two incompatible provenances, and it is the wrong ruler for roster-vs-roster
description:
TWO PROVENANCES. comp/kernels/kneemri-calibsix calls it 'the 0.0062 three-seed floor' (a training-variance number: retrain the same recipe under three seeds, read the spread). core/bootstrap.py's STUDY_RESAMPLES docstring says the count 'is frozen until something re-reads' because changing it 'would move the 0.0062 paired floor' — i.e. bootstrap-derived over studies. Those are different measurements of different quantities and only one can be the origin. Same failure mode as board_transfer's slope and the compression constant: a number quoted from prose until nobody can say what it measured.

WRONG RULER. Whatever its origin, 0.0062 bounds an ARM-vs-ARM comparison — two separately trained models. Two ROSTERS built from the SAME fixed member predictions involve no training variance at all: the arrays are frozen and the only uncertainty is which studies were scored. Two rosters sharing five of six members are near-perfectly correlated per study, so their paired mean-difference interval is strictly, and probably far, narrower. Applying the arm-to-arm floor to a roster delta is conservative in the direction that makes every roster comparison unreadable — 'faulty TEST: a ruler that cannot see the axis'.

I made exactly this error today: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_seat-count-is-flat-both-rulers.md argues the 6->24 seat span of 0.0030 is 'inside the floor'. The CONCLUSION survives on independent board evidence (honest12 0.937 vs calibsix 0.941; 6 and 11 seats both 0.941), but the offline argument for it used the wrong ruler, and the interpretation's closing claim — that the offline curve 'cannot rank two rosters of the same size' — may be false.

MISSING INSTRUMENT. LabelScores has paired_interval (per-label difference, paired) and mean_interval (one arm's mean, UNPAIRED). It has no paired interval on the MEAN DIFFERENCE, which is the competition metric and the quantity every roster decision turns on. Build LabelScores.paired_mean_interval(first, second, targets) over StudyBootstrap.interval, and report it in record_mix for roster-vs-roster.

CAVEAT that must ship with it: a tight paired interval is honest for ONE PRE-SPECIFIED pair. Read on the winner of a roster search it is selection-optimistic — the trap label_combine's docstring names — so a searched roster still needs the split-half honest() treatment.
notes:
CORRECTION, same day. The bead as filed implied every roster decision used 0.0062. It did not. MemberCurve.swap — the method the roster policy actually permits — already uses BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015, fitted empirically on six entries pairing an offline joint-holdout score with a board score (knee-825t), plus BOARD_COST_MULTIPLE for negatives. That is a better-argued ruler than the borrowed floor and it was there first.

CORROBORATION, and it is the useful part. A paired study bootstrap on the competition metric at real scale (909 studies, 12 labels, 1000 resamples) reads a 95% band of 0.00134 for two near-identical arms — the shape of two rosters differing by one member — against 0.01663 for two independent arms. So the bootstrap route and the offline-vs-board route land at essentially the same resolution, ~0.0013 vs 0.0015, from completely different evidence. paired_mean_interval is therefore the PER-COMPARISON, principled version of the plateau BOARD_RESOLVABLE records as a single global constant, and each corroborates the other.

WHERE 0.0062 WAS ACTUALLY MISAPPLIED, narrowed to two places: (1) MemberCurve.marginal, which prints bare deltas with no band at all, leaving the reader to reach for the floor they know; (2) my own interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_seat-count-is-flat-both-rulers.md, which called the 6->24 seat span of 0.0030 'inside the floor'. Under the project's own 0.0015 that span is nominally resolvable — while the board ran the same roster as honest12 and returned 0.937 against calibsix's 0.941, the opposite sign. That tension is the open question, not the flatness: BOARD_RESOLVABLE was itself fitted on member SWAPS at FIXED count, so quoting it against a seat-COUNT delta repeats the board_transfer axis error one level up.

The two-provenance problem for 0.0062 (three-seed in the calibsix kernel, bootstrap-derived in core/bootstrap.py) is untouched by this and still stands.

title: board_transfer slope must not be applied to a seat-count delta
description:
The fitted slope of +2.14 board points per holdout point was fitted on member QUALITY changes — a better member measured solo, then seated. It is not a general exchange rate between the offline ruler and the board.

On 2026-08-27 it was nearly used to price a seat-count delta: the honest curve reads 12 seats +0.0030 over 6, which at +2.14 predicts +0.0064 board, i.e. 0.941 -> 0.947 for zero training. Both halves of that are wrong. The 0.0030 span is inside the 0.0062 paired holdout floor, and the board had ALREADY run the experiment: honest12 is that exact twelve-member roster and scored 0.937 against calibsix's 0.941. The sign flipped, not just the magnitude.

Same class as the compression constant being quoted from prose twice (board_check). Action: board_transfer's docstring/report must state the axis it was fitted on and refuse — or at minimum warn — when asked to price a delta that is not a member-quality change. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_seat-count-is-flat-both-rulers.md.

title: Harness checks keyed by parameter name must resolve on a known-good checkpoint first
description:
labelwise_dense pre-registered 'slices.pool.gate.3.weight' to assert its per-diagnosis attention gate had trained. That key does not exist; the real one is 'slices.gate.3.weight'. The dump came back an EMPTY key list, which is indistinguishable from the dead-gate failure the check was written to catch — on a run whose gate was in fact healthy (absmax 0.171, std 0.059, whole stack trained off its zero init).

A mechanism-fired check that names a key must first be shown to resolve on a checkpoint known to have the mechanism. Otherwise the check reports its own typo as the result, and it does so in the direction that kills a working idea. Same class as the CLAUDE.md 'faulty PLUMBING' bullet: assert the flag LANDED.

Fix: a small helper that raises on an unresolved key pattern instead of returning an empty list, used by every arm header that greps a state dict.

title: A new member costs a 7 GB package push before it can take a seat — the last-slot plan has to start it early
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-27T17:57Z, while de-risking the 23:30Z slot with five hours of margin rather than five minutes.

kneemri-calibsix mounts dimiturnt/kneemri-members, which is the all_ours directory: 58 files, 7.0 GB. A member is small — calib_dense_hold_s2026.pt is 86 MB, and a labelwise member would be the same — but the Kaggle dataset CLI versions a DIRECTORY, not a delta, so putting one 86 MB member in front of a kernel re-uploads all 7 GB.

THE SECOND-MOUNT SHORTCUT IS REFUSED, and not for lack of imagination. Adding a small kneemri-member-<name> dataset to dataset_sources would upload 86 MB instead of 7 GB, but MemberPackage.shipped_root (kneemri/inference/members.py:474) exists specifically to keep ONE directory carrying that dataset id: a second home aged silently on 2026-08-18 and made mount_check refuse a valid kernel. Manifest, fingerprints and the tie rule are all package-scoped. Inventing a two-package mount hours before a submission is the kind of unforced change that loses the slot, not the kind that wins it.

SO THE PLAN IS TIMING, NOT ARCHITECTURE. Any last-slot play that needs a member not already in all_ours must start its push as soon as the member lands, not when the slot is fired. Note that all_ours is ALREADY behind the members on disk — blend_through.pt was written 2026-08-26 and is not in the package, which is why mount_check refuses kneemri-blendall for blend_through and blend_base.

AND THE CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE IS REAL, so it must be priced against the swap rather than skipped. A last slot spent on a new COMBINATION over members already packaged costs zero upload and zero risk of a half-pushed dataset. It is only worth less if the new member's seat value beats what re-weighting the existing 58 can buy. Decide that with numbers when the member has a holdout record — do not default to the swap because the member is new.

UNMEASURED, and it gates the timing: nothing here records how long a 7 GB push actually takes. The first one that runs should be timed and the number written into this issue.

title: labelwise pooling at 20 slices: the cell where per-diagnosis attention has depth to spend
description:
`labelwise224` read +0.0015 at 12 slices / 224 px and the ledger closed the axis with 'a58 image-read labels cannot supervise twelve separate attention channelsa'. That denominator is wrong: the 58 are the EVAL set, and training supervision is the report table over ~4,349 studies x 12 findings. The axis was also tested at 12 slices, where a per-diagnosis query has almost no depth to distribute over.

Today's foreign_gate curve is new evidence that did not exist when that verdict was written. Raptor's coatnet_v4_full carries a per-finding attention pool and reads 0.8700 / 0.8727 / 0.8773 through our 12 / 16 / 20 slice caches: +0.0027 then +0.0046, steepening at the depth we stopped at. Our own slice sweep read -0.0001 for 20 over 12 (knee-ezz) but ran under MAX pooling, which commits all twelve findings to one window. Each axis was closed in the absence of the other; the interaction cell is empty.

It is emptier than it looks. `attend_dense` appears to have tested pooling at this corner (-0.0009) but knee-7gyw found the aggregator in no parameter group, gate exactly 0.000e+00 after a full epoch, so it compared the arithmetic mean against the max. The ledger's own words: 'the pooling-operator cell REOPENS'. Working attention of any kind has never been read at 336 px x 20 slices.

ARM: experiments/arms/labelwise_dense.sh. Byte-identical to calib_dense_hold except --slice-pooling max -> labelwise. Control 0.8634 is already on the ledger, so nothing is spent re-establishing it.
notes:
SIDE-BLINDNESS BASELINE, measured 2026-08-27T17:21Z, so labelwise_dense can be read on MECHANISM and
not only on the mean. `side_blindness --records calib_dense_hold calib_span_hold band_dense_hold
band_span_hold` (909 studies, 4 members combined, no card -- pure arithmetic over records on disk):

  Medial Meniscus / Lateral Meniscus   n=57 lateral-only vs 313 medial-only
    Lateral Meniscus  0.7483 [0.6598, 0.8248]  resolves the side
    Medial Meniscus   0.8534 [0.8110, 0.8900]  resolves the side
    PF OA             0.4960 [0.4137, 0.5786]  control clean
  Medial OA / Lateral OA               n=65 lateral-only vs 165 medial-only
    Lateral OA        0.5464 [0.4619, 0.6295]  INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM SIDE-BLIND
    Medial OA         0.7326 [0.6646, 0.7974]  resolves the side
    PF OA             0.4938 [0.4103, 0.5731]  control clean

Both neutral controls straddle 0.50, so the burden confound is not firing and the pair columns are
readable. The defect is ONE column of ONE pair, not the compartment axis at large: the meniscus pair
resolves both sides comfortably. Lateral OA is the docstring's minority-class signature exactly --
side IS in the representation (partner reads 0.7326) but was learnt on the majority compartment at
2.5:1. On n=65 the interval cannot separate "blind" from "unresolved", so the point estimate is not
quotable on its own.

WHY THIS SITS ON THIS BEAD. `side_dense` (knee-6u12) refuted getting the side out of the LOSS: the
contrast rose 0.062 on demand and all twelve labels fell -0.0641. Its surviving prescription, written
into the ledger at the time, is that the term "survives as a small-weight regulariser on a head that
SEES position (pooling or field of view for the OA compartments)". `labelwise` is the first head this
project has built that can hold position PER DIAGNOSIS -- Medial OA and Lateral OA get separate depth
queries -- so it is the precondition that prescription was waiting on. Both this arm and its control
are trained WITHOUT a side term, which is the one condition under which `side_blindness` is a clean
instrument (it cannot audit a side-term run; the term dirties the neutral control).

READ IT AS A DIAGNOSTIC, NEVER AS A PROXY. `2026-08-23_side_resolution_is_not_score.md` established
that this contrast and the competition metric are orthogonal orderings over the same logits, and that
buying the second cost the first outright. So a labelwise arm that moves Lateral OA here has NOT
thereby earned a seat, and a labelwise arm that leaves it flat is not thereby refuted. What the
reading buys is the mechanism question the mean cannot answer: whether a per-diagnosis query puts
compartment position into the representation at all.

title: queue_check counts the Bash-tool nohup wrapper shell as a second watcher and reports DOUBLE-QUEUED
description:
FALSE POSITIVE, 2026-08-27. queue_check reported DOUBLE-QUEUED: experiments/arms/contrast_dense.sh. The process table held two matches: pid 919283, the real watcher (bash experiments/after.sh ...), and pid 919281, the nohup wrapper shell the Bash tool launches, whose argv QUOTES THE ENTIRE COMMAND. A substring match over argv therefore counts one chain twice. Only one after_*.log names the arm.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC MISCOUNT. The documented response to DOUBLE-QUEUED is to kill all but one chain. Following it here would have killed the only live watcher and left the card idle after fuse_regions finished - which is the EXACT hole queue_check exists to close, opened by queue_check itself.

FIX, either of: (a) match argv[0..1] == (bash, experiments/after.sh) rather than a substring anywhere in the command line; or (b) drop any matching process that is the PARENT of another match, since a wrapper always is. (b) is cheaper and also covers whatever the next harness wraps things in.

VERIFY WITH: launch a watcher through the Bash tool nohup path, then run queue_check --directory experiments/logs; it must report OK with one live process, not DOUBLE-QUEUED.

title: queue_check counts the nohup wrapper shell as a second watcher, so one armed chain reads DOUBLE-QUEUED
description:
queue_check reports 'DOUBLE-QUEUED: experiments/arms/contrast_dense.sh - more than one live after.sh will start each of these' when exactly ONE watcher owes it.

The process table at 2026-08-27T15:36Z:
  919283  bash experiments/after.sh ARM DONE fuse_regions <log> experiments/arms/contrast_dense.sh   <- the watcher
  919281  /usr/bin/bash -c ... eval 'cd ... && nohup bash experiments/after.sh "ARM DONE fuse_regions" <log> experiments/arms/contrast_dense.sh > experiments/logs/after_contrast_dense.log 2>&1 & disown; ...'

919281 is the Bash-tool wrapper that LAUNCHED 919283. Its argv quotes the whole command, so a substring match on 'after.sh' + the arm path matches it too, and the arm is counted twice. Only one log names contrast_dense.sh, and only one real watcher exists.

The false positive is the expensive direction: the documented response to DOUBLE-QUEUED is 'kill all but one chain', and following it here would kill the ONLY watcher and leave the card idle after fuse_regions finishes - the exact hole queue_check was built to close, opened by queue_check.

FIX: match the watcher by argv[0..1] == ('bash', 'experiments/after.sh') rather than by substring anywhere in the command line, or drop any process that is a PARENT of another matched process.

title: --calibrated-targets reads +0.013/+0.016 on the annotated ruler, but that ruler shares its constants -- the board rows are the non-circular support
description:
Six cached annotated_predictions sets, macro AUC on the 58 radiologist-annotated studies, all six holding those studies out:

  calib_span_hold       0.9152   <- calib
  calib_dense_hold      0.9117   <- calib
  finding_calib_dense   0.9098   <- calib
  band_span_hold        0.9023
  band_dense_hold       0.8956
  holdannot             0.8932

The two PAIRED single-flag comparisons: span pair +0.0129 (band_span_hold -> calib_span_hold), dense pair +0.0161 (band_dense_hold -> calib_dense_hold). Same recipe, same studies, one flag.

WHY THE LEDGER READ IT NEGATIVE. calib_span scored -0.0020 on the offline holdout and the family was closed on that. The offline holdout scores against REPORT labels, which carry the very miscalibration the offsets correct -- finding_calibration.py's own docstring states this before anything measured it: 'the offline ruler is biased AGAINST any table that stops agreeing with the reader.' So the -0.0020 is not a measurement of the lever, it is a measurement of how far the lever moved away from the reader.

THREE INDEPENDENT AGREEMENTS, one mechanism:
  1. annotated ruler: +0.0129 / +0.0161 macro (this bead)
  2. board, six seats:  resseat 0.938 -> calibsix 0.941  (+0.003)
  3. board, 11-12 seats: honest12 0.937 -> calibmix 0.941 (+0.004)
Two board entries at 0.941 from different member sets is a replication, not a lucky draw.

HONEST SIZE: +0.013/+0.016 is 1.1-1.3 sigma against the n=58 macro SE of ~0.012 taken UNPAIRED; the pairing cuts that but is not quantified here. Directional on this ruler alone; a finding only because three rulers agree in sign.

CONSEQUENCE: the calib_dense follow-up killed under knee-ep74 ('a calibration that is negative on the span corner cannot be positive on the denser one') rests on the biased ruler and REOPENS. The dense corner posts the LARGER paired gain (+0.0161 vs +0.0129), which is the opposite of what that closure assumed.

Also: the offline holdout being blind to this lever is a general hazard, not one about calib. Any label-side change that moves the target away from the report is scored by a ruler made of the report. Every such lever in the ledger needs re-reading on annotated_readings before its sign is trusted.
notes:
CORRECTION, same session, before this was quoted. This bead as filed overclaimed novelty and got its framing backwards. Read experiments/README.md 4266-4300 and kneemri/evaluation/annotated_readings.py's docstring.

1. NOT NEW: the span corner's +0.0129 annotated is knee-bs4l, already in the ledger. The 2026-08-26 dense-hold entry already states '--calibrated-targets is the only measured-positive term this project currently holds'. The lever was revived a day before I 'found' it. My 'the ledger read it negative / we threw it away' sentence describes the OLD calib_span arm and ignores its revival.

2. NOT INDEPENDENT: annotated_readings.py's own docstring says a calibrated arm's annotated read is scored on the ruler its constants were fitted against -- Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT (and FINDING_OFFSETS) are hardcoded constants fitted on these same 696 cells, and --hold-annotations drops the cells from the training table without refitting them. So +0.0129/+0.0161 is a CONSISTENCY CHECK between two rulers that share an origin, never a confirmation. level_agreement.stability puts four of five levels under 2 sigma, which is why the number is quotable at all, but it does not make it independent.

3. knee-ep74 does NOT reopen on my argument. I claimed the dense corner was killed unrun on a biased ruler; it was in fact RUN (calib_dense_hold, 0.8634 @ e6, +0.0061 offline vs band_dense_hold) and is this project's best offline single member. Nothing to reopen.

WHAT SURVIVES AS ACTUALLY NEW, and it is smaller than the bead's title:
 a. The dense corner's ANNOTATED number, +0.0161 (band_dense_hold 0.8956 -> calib_dense_hold 0.9117). The ledger holds the dense corner on the offline proxy only. Third corner-ruler cell, same sign as the other two, subject to caveat 2.
 b. finding_calib_dense reads 0.9098, BELOW pooled calib_dense_hold's 0.9117, on the annotated ruler. The PER-FINDING offsets do not beat the POOLED constants where both are read against the radiologists. Bears on knee-p9oc; also subject to caveat 2, and -0.0019 is far inside n=58 noise, so it is at best 'no evidence per-finding helps', not 'per-finding hurts'.
 c. All six *_hold members ranked on one annotated ruler, which had not been tabulated.

The board evidence (calibsix/calibmix both 0.941, two seat counts, two member sets) is the only NON-circular support for calib and it stands unchanged -- it is what the user asked about and it does not depend on any of the above. Retitle when acted on.

title: Raptor's published label table cannot be scored on the 58, because its author removed them
description:
dreaddevelopment/rsna-knee-labels (labels_llm_soft.csv, 4349 studies x 12, published 2026-08-14, pulled to D:/data/external/raptor/labels/) is a SECOND INDEPENDENT LLM read of the same 4407 reports we read. It is the only foreign reader whose author states its provenance and whose model weights are also published.

IT CANNOT BE PLACED ON OUR RULER. 4349 = 4407 - 58. The 58 radiologist-annotated studies are exactly the ones the author held out, so `kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap --labels <their csv>` returns labels 0.5000 for all twelve findings - an empty join, not a score. Our own table reads 0.8658 on that ruler and the best public foreign table reads 0.8927; theirs reads NOTHING. Any claim that their labels are better or worse than ours is unmeasurable with the instruments this repo has.

WHAT IS MEASURABLE, AND THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS. rubric_gap over both tables, same eight rules, same reports: ours 502 contradicted cells over the rules the annotations BACK, theirs 34 - a 93% reduction, and 1600 vs 157 over all eight. That looks like a better reader and IS NOT SHOWN TO BE ONE. The control: their macro positive rate is 0.187 against our 0.303, lower on 11 of 12 columns. A reader that says negative more often contradicts a negative-class rule less often for free. rubric_gap cannot separate a better threshold from a more negative one, and this is the confound to state whenever that tool is pointed at a foreign table.

BASE RATE AGAINST THE 58 AS REFEREE (the annotated positive rate per column, the one truth available). Mean absolute error of the corpus positive rate against it: OURS 0.109, THEIRS 0.158. Ours is closer on 7 of 12. The readable gaps - the referee's own SE at n=58 is ~0.06, so only large ones count - are Effusion (ours off by 0.001, theirs by 0.347), ACL (0.139 vs 0.284), Lateral Meniscus (0.146 vs 0.262) and Contusion (0.038 vs 0.176) in OUR favour; Synovitis (0.336 vs 0.221) and Medial OA (0.108 vs 0.013) in theirs. Both tables sit far below the annotated rate on Fracture (0.068 and 0.037 vs 0.310), which is the known report-vs-image gap, not a reader defect.

THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING. Inter-reader correlation per column is 0.72-0.90 on eleven findings and 0.389 ON SYNOVITIS. Two independent LLM readers of the SAME reports barely agree there. Corroboration from two directions: their own model's worst label is Synovitis at 0.7575 (read from the checkpoint's own aucs dict), and forum topic 737566 is titled 'Why everyone Synovitis AUC is stuck around 0.6-0.7'. Synovitis being label-limited has been suspected here; this is the first evidence that is INDEPENDENT of our reader.

DO NOT spend a card arm on adopting or blending this table. table_blend already measured that blending readers on this ruler moves +0.0015 [-0.0069, +0.0121] - unresolved - and that averaging our coarser table into a stronger reader DILUTES it. A fourth reader that cannot be scored on the ruler adds an unauditable input to a blend the ruler already cannot resolve.

title: Offline greedy seat selection is refuted as an instrument (honest12 sign flip)
description:
honest12 scored 0.937 on the board from a +0.0050 offline holdout gain (0.8751 at twelve seats vs the champion five-twin shadow 0.8701). That is a SIGN FLIP, not a compression: every other board/offline mismatch this project has measured shrank a gain (board_transfer slope +0.74; knee-nas5's 2.4x went the other way). A selector whose gains arrive on the board with the opposite sign is broken, not weak.

Mechanism: the greedy fits on 454 studies (half of 909 shared holdout), which cannot resolve a seat worth less than the 0.0062 three-seed paired floor. So it seats mae_matched_s2026 (0.6735 solo) at the honest curve's own dip at nine seats and reads it as a gain.

CONSEQUENCE - do not spend another slot on an offline-greedy seating, in either direction. Six board entries now span 0.937-0.941 across six seatings and the ordering is INVERSE to offline holdout gain: honest12 0.937 (12), resseat 0.938 (6), blendseat 0.939 (7), blendthree 0.939 (7), pixgroup 0.940 (8), calibsix 0.941 (6), calibmix 0.941 (11).

WHAT THIS DOES NOT KILL: the members. calib_dense_hold_s2026 (0.8634, the best solo member we own) has never been read alone on the board, and seven of honest12's twelve are individually unpriced. A bad seating of good members says nothing about the members. Nor does it kill offline holdout as a ruler for a SINGLE member - only for ranking seatings.

Recorded: comp/board.jsonl, comp/SUBMISSIONS.md.
notes:
2026-08-29 15:12Z — the sign flip has a quantitative explanation, and it changes the CONSEQUENCE. Not a broken selector; a selector read below its resolution.

knee-b6sn fits board on offline over the 22 scored ensemble entries: slope 2.099, CI [1.197, 3.012],
r 0.855, and RESIDUAL SD 0.0078. That last number is what predicting a board score from an offline score
is worth, and it is what this issue was missing.

APPLY IT TO THIS ISSUE'S OWN EVIDENCE. honest12's gain was +0.0050 offline — 0.64 of one residual sd. The
six entries whose ordering is 'INVERSE to offline holdout gain' span 0.937-0.941 on the board, a range of
0.004, against an offline spread of about 0.005 whose predicted board spread is ~0.009. Six points inside
half a residual sd, ordered at random, is not an instrument returning the wrong sign. It is an instrument
returning noise, which has a 50 % chance of looking like the wrong sign and did.

THE DIAGNOSIS MATTERS BECAUSE THE CONSEQUENCE DIFFERS.
  'broken'           -> never seat by offline greedy again, in any direction.
  'below resolution' -> offline greedy is uninformative below ~0.004 and unrefuted above it.
Nothing in that six-entry set was ever more than ~0.005 apart, so the set cannot distinguish the two
readings — and this issue chose the stronger one. The mechanism written here (a 454-study fit cannot
resolve a seat worth less than the 0.0062 paired floor) is the SAME statement as 'below resolution' and
already pointed at it.

CORROBORATION FROM TODAY, on a ruler this issue did not have. record_mix --seats honest over ~110 records
gives held-out 0.8743 at eight seats and 0.8748 at twenty-one: +0.0005 across thirteen seats, an eighth of
the holdout floor and a sixteenth of the transfer resolution. The seat axis genuinely has nothing left to
resolve past eight, so any selector ranking those seatings must return noise. That is knee-va22's
saturation, priced.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: reopening the practical advice. 'Do not spend another slot on an offline-greedy
seating' stands unchanged, because every seating difference now on the table is below 0.004. The change is
that it stands on the SIZE of the differences rather than on the selector being broken — so a seating that
someday differs by 0.005+ offline is not barred by this issue.

Suggest retitling to 'refuted below ~0.004' rather than 'refuted as an instrument' when this is next
touched; leaving the title for the owner's call rather than rewriting the record unilaterally.

title: ReadingPrompt gave the reader the class docstring instead of its five grade definitions
description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-27, but the CONSEQUENCE is open.

ReadingPrompt.system() rendered 'grade.__doc__' for each ReportGrade member. A bare string under an enum
member does NOT become that member's __doc__ - it falls back to the CLASS docstring. So every reader run
this project has ever made was handed the ReportGrade class docstring FIVE TIMES, about a thousand tokens
of repeated prose, exactly where the definitions of absent/unclear/possible/present/severe belonged. The
model was told the five WORDS and nothing about what they mean.

Silent by construction: the reader answers in the right vocabulary either way, so no parse fails and no
metric names it. It surfaced only because writing the rubric into the prompt meant PRINTING the rendered
prompt for the first time.

FIXED: definitions moved to a WORDING dict beside the enum (same shape as LEVEL two lines below), and
test_system asserts each definition appears AND that the class docstring does not. Corrected prompt is
775 tokens against the broken one's 1037 - twelve published criteria added and still a quarter shorter.

WHAT IS OPEN: every existing reading was produced by this prompt. The 'possible' rung carrying 6461 cells
at 0.68 was assigned by a model never told what 'possible' means. blendlabels' +0.0034 reader ceiling and
every per-label supervision gap read off it were measured with an instrument never given its own units.
Not a reason to redo anything on its own - the corpus re-read in knee-ufz5 fixes it as a side effect, and
that is where the measurement lands. This bead exists so the re-read's result is not read as a pure
rubric effect when it is a rubric effect PLUS a grade-vocabulary effect, confounded and unseparable.

Does NOT reopen the ladder's CALIBRATION: what a rung is WORTH was fitted against image annotations and
is independent of how a cell earns the rung (level_agreement, calib_span).
notes: Blocks nothing; the measurement lands inside knee-ufz5's re-read, which it confounds.

title: Re-read the corpus under the host's published annotation rubric (topic 733343)
description:
The Overview thread publishes the complete image-review criteria for all twelve labels, and ReadingPrompt.system() carries none of them. It instructs the reader to transcribe what the report SAID; the target is a two-radiologist image review under stated criteria, with a third adjudicating. tear_rubric measures the meniscus arm of that gap at 163 contradicted cells (1.85% of the corpus's meniscus cells, a floor over the 40.1% English subset it can read).

The criteria, as published:
- Global: ambiguous or borderline findings (on the fence) were graded NEGATIVE to favour specificity.
- ACL: >50% of fibres, or discontinuity. Mild signal change, degeneration or thickening WITHOUT discontinuity is negative.
- MCL: high-grade ACUTE only. Low-grade sprains and chronic/remote stress change are negative.
- Meniscus: signal definitely contacting the articular surface on 2+ images, or a morphologic abnormality. Intrasubstance degeneration is negative.
- OA (medial/lateral/patellofemoral): a moderate or large area, 1cm or more, of >50%-thickness cartilage loss.
- Effusion: moderate or large only.
- Baker's cyst: moderate or large only.
- Contusion: marrow-edema-like signal from impact WITHOUT a discrete fracture line.
- Fracture: an acute cortical break.

The change is three to six sentences in ReadingPrompt.system() plus one LLM pass over 4406 reports. No submission slot. It reaches every language because the READER does, not a regex — which is why the cheap English-only post-hoc fix on the 163 cells was rejected in the interpretation: it converts uniform label noise into language-dependent noise.

The gate, pre-registered: the re-read is scored by whether tear_rubric's 163 contradicted cells MOVE. A re-read that leaves them where they are has failed loudly rather than silently. Second gate: kneemri.evaluation.annotated_readings against the 58, which must not regress.

NOT the ladder. The confidence-ladder question (0.68 for 'possible' sitting above the midpoint on 6461 cells) is CLOSED, twice over: level_agreement measures 0.68's pooled constant at 0.378 on our own annotated cells (below midpoint, chi2 p=0.100 consistent with pooling, 0.9 sigma settled on disjoint halves), and calib_span already spent an arm remapping every level to its measured agreement and came back -0.0020 with its per-label prediction inverted. This bead changes which RUNG a report earns, not what a rung is worth.

Sizing, honestly: two of twelve columns for the meniscus arm, so a per-column gain divides by six on the mean; calibsix's measured board pass-through is 23%. Directional under the 1.5% bar on the meniscus arm alone. The reason to run it is that it is a data fix a HOST statement licenses, it composes with everything banked, and it touches all twelve findings rather than two. Gated on the card clearing warm_calib_dense / fuse_regions / contrast_dense.
notes:
THE RULER NOW REFUSES ITS OWN UNTRUSTWORTHY ARMS. Extended from 3 rules / 4 columns to 8 rules / 9
columns (Effusion, Baker's and the three OA compartments join, size vocabulary imported from
severity_boundary so the threshold keeps one home). But the count is now gated on the annotations:
RubricGap.backed asks whether the radiologists agree this rule's subthreshold class is negative, and the
bar is ZERO counterexamples, because the rule's claim is a rate of 0 rather than a rate under a half.

  BACKED   Medial/Lateral Meniscus 165 (0 of 3)   ACL 98 (0 of 1)   Baker's 239 (0 of 1)   = 502
  REFUSED  MCL 185 (3 of 7)  Effusion 524 (6 of 12)  Medial OA 123 (1 of 2)
           Lateral OA 112 (2 of 5)  PF OA 154 (1 of 4)                                     = 1098

SCORE THE RE-READ ON THE 502, NEVER THE 1600. Scoring it on the refused cells would reward the reader for
agreeing with a ruler the radiologists do not. Meniscus's 165 is the only arm with a two-sided pass (its
accepted bucket also agrees 23 of 27); ACL and Baker's are one-cell passes and weak.

The SIZE family fails as a family: pooled, 10 of 23 annotated subthreshold cells under a size rule are
annotated POSITIVE, and topic 735826 has two competitors reporting the same effusion sentence annotated
both ways. On those five columns the report may not carry the information the label was made from, which
is a ceiling on the reader lane rather than a defect in it.

MCL's subthreshold count is 187, not the 213 this note carried before the edema fix.

CONFOUND, UNCHANGED: the re-read moves two things at once - the host's thresholds AND, for the first time,
a definition of the reader's own five grade words (knee-a664). Its result is both effects together.

title: Host states the label RUBRIC: definite tear only, report wording does not determine contusion/OA — our reader was never told
description:
Discussion topic 733491, host reply read 2026-08-27 (posted with the thread's 11:39Z update):

  'For meniscal tears, the target is a definite tear; intrasubstance degenerative signals that do not
   reach the articular surface are negative. ... marrow edema, cartilage findings, and terminology in
   the narrative or impression do not by themselves determine the contusion, osteoarthritis, or other
   challenge labels. Those labels reflect the standardized image-review criteria. ... A report may
   therefore use language that appears inconsistent with the corresponding image-based label because
   the original report and the image-based labels were generated through different processes.'

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT IN OUR DATA AND NOT A CURIOSITY. Every target this project trains on is derived
from the REPORT. `ReportReading`'s system prompt says 'say what THE REPORT SAID about it. Do not
diagnose, do not infer' — which is the correct instruction for transcription and the WRONG one for this
competition, because the ground truth is not what the report said. It is an image review under a stated
rubric, run by two readers with a third adjudicating. The host has now named three places the two
diverge systematically:
  (1) meniscus: degenerative intrasubstance signal not reaching the surface is NEGATIVE, and our reader
      grades it present/possible. `interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot_tables.md`
      row 33 already caught this by hand ('Lateral meniscus degeneration without definite tear' read as
      YES 1) and names four more studies with the same shape (059, 062, 088, 090) — filed then as a
      reader error, now confirmed as a rubric error.
  (2) contusion: marrow-edema wording does not make it positive. Same table, rows 6/29/50.
  (3) OA: cartilage wording does not make it positive. Same table, row 17.

These are the three finding families where `supervision_gap` measures our worst columns, so the
population at risk and the weak columns are the same set.

FIRST STEP IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A RE-READ. Size the population: over the corpus, how many studies carry
degeneration-without-definite-tear wording in a meniscus sentence, and what does our target table say
about them. The host's rule supplies the correct answer for those cells without needing an annotation,
so this needs no ground truth and no card. State the denominator over the WHOLE corpus, not over the
English subset that parses (`severity_boundary` carries that discipline; 59.9% of reports are not
English).

DEPENDS ON NOTHING. Costs no slot and no card.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-27, and the measurement INVERTS this bead's own lead. Tool: `core/data/labels/rubric_boundary.py`
(`uv run --no-sync python -m core.data.labels.rubric_boundary`). No ground truth, no card, no slot.

Table measured: `merged_blend_v1.csv` — the table the champion's seats were FITTED on. The eval ruler
(`report_labels_v2`) is deliberately not the default: a contradiction in the ruler moves what a holdout number
MEANS, a contradiction in the training table moves what the model LEARNED. This asks the second question.

Denominators, both stated: 1768 English reports of 4407 (40.1%). The non-English 59.9% is UNMEASURED — every
share below is a share of the English subset, never of the corpus.

  meniscus       — CONTRADICTED:   4 cells —  3.3% of its excluded bucket,  0.11% of the family's 3536 English cells
  contusion      — CONTRADICTED:  39 cells — 18.2% of its excluded bucket,  2.21% of the family's 1768 English cells
  osteoarthritis — CONTRADICTED: 615 cells — 86.9% of its excluded bucket, 11.60% of the family's 5304 English cells

THE LEAD WAS WRONG. This bead led with meniscus, on the strength of the host naming it first and of the pilot
table's row 33. Meniscus is nearly clean: four cells. The mass is OSTEOARTHRITIS — 615 cells where the report's
only OA-family sentence is chondral/cartilage/chondromalacia wording, which the host says does not by itself
determine the label, and our table calls positive anyway. Fourteen of fourteen sampled rows were the named case
on inspection.

THE COUNT IS A FLOOR, for a reason worth naming. The host's own phrasing of the meniscus case — 'degeneration
WITHOUT a definite tear' — carries a negation word, so it bins as DENIAL rather than as excluded wording and
never reaches the contradiction line. Those cells are still printed (a positive in the denial row is a reader
error under any reading), but they are not counted here. A BOTH bucket (excluded and qualifying wording in one
sentence, e.g. 'degenerative tear reaching the surface') is genuinely positive under the rule and is likewise
excluded from the count.

ONE FALSE READING WAS CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE THIS NUMBER. Printing the SENTENCES rather than the counts
surfaced 'Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained' sitting in the excluded bucket — a
knee report says negative without a negation word. Adding intact|preserved|well-maintained|normal to the denial
guard moved the OA excluded bucket 1095 -> 708 while the contradictions moved only 638 -> 615, so the fix removed
true negatives and the headline is robust to it.

SIZING, HONESTLY. The ledger's measured label lane is small: `blendlabels` +0.0034 on the mean and +0.0070 on the
six label-bottlenecked findings, both at or under the 0.0062 arm floor. A rubric correction touching ~12% of the
cells on three OA columns is a materially larger perturbation of the training table than any blend recomposition
was — `table_blend` already bracketed every reweighting of the readers we have at +0.0015 [-0.0069, +0.0121] —
but it is still an unpriced perturbation, and pricing it costs a card arm.

A SECOND, LARGER DEFECT SURFACED AND IS NOT THIS BEAD'S: the OA 'no sentence names this column' bucket holds 714
positives of 2604 cells (27.4%) — our table calls OA positive on compartments the report never mentions. That is
compartment ATTRIBUTION, not the host's rubric, and it is filed separately.

title: An arm snapshots the WORKING TREE at launch, so an uncommitted half-edit kills a queued arm hours later
description:
fuse_regions died at 12:44Z, eight seconds in, with 'TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable Readout object' at trainer.py:392 — inside experiments/fuse_regions.src, the snapshot lib.sh takes at launch.

The tree was NOT broken. It was MID-EDIT: model.py already returned the new Readout dataclass and trainer.py had not yet been rewritten to read it when fuse_attend finished and the chained fuse_regions started. The snapshot froze that torn instant. Every gate would have passed minutes later, and did.

The cost was a card window, not a file: fuse_regions had been chained behind fuse_attend precisely so no wall-clock was lost, and instead the card sat idle from 12:44Z.

The rule this wants: while ANY arm is queued or chained, edits to shared training code land as a COMMIT or not at all — a queued arm reads the tree at ITS start time, not at the time you last thought about it. Options worth pricing: (a) lib.sh snapshots from 'git stash create'/HEAD rather than the dirty tree, which makes the snapshot reproducible as well as safe; (b) a launch-time refusal when 'git status --porcelain' touches kneemri/training or kneemri/models; (c) nothing but this note, on the argument that arms are usually launched from a clean tree.

title: Warm starts: fitted_encoder exists, 0 of 131 arms use it, and the merge doubles adaptation capacity
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-27. `kneemri/training/fitted_encoder.py` converts a fitted member into the file `--encoder-weights` reads. It was built for exactly this and then never used: 0 of 131 arm scripts pass --encoder-weights/--warm/--resume/--init-from, and `train` exposes no other warm-start flag. Every member on disk was fitted cold from the stock trunk.

THE SCALE OF THE WASTE. 98 members carry 36 distinct recipe skeletons (epochs/px/slices/lr/whole-stack/pooling/crop/scheme). The modal skeleton (12ep 336px 20sl lr4e-5 whole-stack max cls_mean) accounts for 31 of them; the top four skeletons account for 56 of 98. So a third of the roster is one decode path re-run with a different loss, label table or calibration - precisely the change the house rule says to warm-start rather than refit. Each of those paid a full cold fit.

TWO CLAIMS, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT. (1) TIME: a loss/head tweak on an unchanged decode path should not re-learn the trunk. (2) QUALITY: `merge_adapters` folds a LoRA parent's correction INTO the base weights, so `--lora-rank` then builds a FRESH rank-r adaptation on an already-adapted trunk - doubled adaptation capacity at no serve-time cost. NOTE (2026-08-30): claim (2) applies ONLY to a LoRA parent. A full-fine-tune parent (lora_rank 0) has nothing to merge and nothing is doubled; for those the mechanism reduces to a second anneal from a better starting point. The bead was conflating the two.

THE COST IT DOES NOT PAY FOR. A warm-started member is correlated with its parent. Decode-path diversity is the one axis measured to transfer at ~2.4x the average board slope (knee-nas5), so warm starts buy member QUALITY and card-hours, never seat diversity. They should replace repeat arms and never replace new-mechanism arms.

=== RESULT, ARM A, run 2026-08-27 and first READ 2026-08-30 ===

`warm_calib_dense` warm-started calib_dense_hold_s2026 (0.8634, best solo we own) at the parent's own 4e-5 and scored 0.8562 - LOST 0.0072. The two trajectories say opposite things and both matter:

  cold 4e-5  .7515 .8007 .8280 .8438 .8544 .8554 [.8634] .8620 .8607 .8596 .8603 .8598
  warm 4e-5  .8503 .8469 .8555 .8510 .8549 .8526 [.8562] .8529 .8540 .8518 .8515 .8513

TIME CLAIM VALIDATED, harder than its docstring asked. The warm run's FIRST epoch reads 0.8503, a score the cold run needs four epochs to reach. One warm epoch is worth about five cold ones on this recipe. Settled; needs no further arm.

QUALITY CLAIM REFUTED AT THIS RATE, AND THE PRE-REGISTERED SUSPECT FIRED. Epoch 1 DROPS (0.8503 -> 0.8469) and the run then oscillates 0.847-0.856 for eleven epochs without reaching the parent's peak. warm_calib_dense.sh named this in advance: one_cycle does NOT resume the optimiser, it restarts and ramps to peak near epoch 2, so an annealed trunk is hit with a RISING rate on epoch 1 - "that outcome sends the next arm to a lower --backbone-lr, not to the graveyard." The prediction and the observation are the same epoch.

A CHECKPOINT IS THE PEAK, NOT THE LAST EPOCH, which is what makes warm starting worth more than time. cnx_own_recipe_s2026.pt stores epoch 6 / 0.8186 while its last epoch read 0.8130 after declining five straight epochs. A warm start resumes from a state the parent RUN threw away. General property of every member on disk.

FittedEncoder WORKS ON A CONVOLUTIONAL TRUNK. Written for LoRA ViT members; converting cnx_own_recipe_s2026 wrote 378 tensors, variant cnxbase, and PretrainedEncoder.into neither refused the variant nor tripped the key check. The smoke then ran. The warm-start path is not ViT-specific.

UNBLOCKED. knee-l93q is closed and CAP_HEADROOM = 1.15 sits at device_budget.py:392, so the OOM that stopped this on 2026-08-27 is gone.

=== THE TWO ARMS THIS OPENS, PRICED ===

ARM B  warm_calib_lowlr.sh - the pre-registered follow-up, ViT, single variable against arm A.
  PRICE: ~40 min card, 0 slots. Control is on disk (warm 0.8562); cold parent 0.8634. Only --backbone-lr moves, 4e-5 -> 1e-5.
  P(clears the warm control 0.8562 by >0.0010, i.e. the ramp WAS the cause) ~ 0.45.
  P(clears the cold parent 0.8634, i.e. best single this project owns) ~ 0.15.

ARM C  cnx_warm_anneal.sh - the same ramp question on a NON-DINO trunk. Smoked ok 2026-08-30.
  PRICE: ~20 min card, 0 slots. Parent cnx_own_recipe_s2026, peak epoch 6, holdout 0.8186. 6 epochs at 1e-4 (a quarter of the parent's 4e-4, the same ratio arm B uses).
  P(clears +0.010 over 0.8186) ~ 0.30. P(seats, i.e. clears roster merit 0.8460) ~ 0.03.
  Priced as an INSTRUMENT rather than a member: it asks whether a converged non-DINO trunk has anything left after a second anneal, which is knee-nj4l's open question, and it is the cheapest read of it we own.
notes: warm_calib_lowlr_s2026 (2026-08-30) SPENDS branch A. --backbone-lr 4e-5 -> 1e-5, one flag, same encoder, same twelve epochs. 0.8577 @ e4 vs the warm control's 0.8562 and the cold parent's 0.8634. A 4x rate reduction moved the outcome +0.0015, a quarter of the 0.0062 arm-vs-arm floor, so the one_cycle ramp is NOT what costs the warm start its 0.0057 -- a lever that is the cause does not survive being quartered unchanged. The epoch curve says what it is instead: 0.8540 at epoch 0 before any training, monotone decline through eight of the twelve while training loss falls 0.82 -> 0.45. The warm encoder already holds what twelve cold epochs build; fine-tuning on top of it only fits the train set, at either rate. Warm starting is therefore a TIME mechanism with no quality term -- real and usable (one warm epoch ~ twelve cold ones to within 0.009), but it never makes a better member. Branch B is now the ONLY live cell of the rank-0 x warm x schedule grid: a LoRA parent (dinov3_base_lora_s2026 or lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026) warm-started WITH a fresh --lora-rank, which is the only configuration where fitted_encoder.py:88-97 MERGES rather than falling every tensor through. Branch C (warm_calib_dense_short) was gated on A or B; A did not clear, so it is gated on B alone. Ledger entry: experiments/README.md, 'warm_calib_lowlr'.

title: model.py:322 silently ignores --slice-regions when --slice-pooling attend is set
description:
`kneemri/models/model.py:322`:

    return self.slices(stacked) if self.slices is not None else self.over_depth(stacked)

`over_depth` is the `--slice-regions` path and `self.slices` is the `--slice-pooling attend` path, so the two are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE and attend wins. A run given both records a region count in its recipe that it never used — no error, no log line, and the ledger then carries a fact about an arm that did not run.

CONSEQUENCE ALREADY PAID: any arm that named both is mis-attributed in the ledger. `fuse_attend` and `fuse_regions` were split into two arms specifically because of this — they would have been one arm if the flags composed.

FIX: either compose them (regions within attention) or refuse the combination at argument-parse time. Refusing is the smaller change and closes the silent-misrecord hole; composing is the one that might buy something, since the aggregation axis is where the fourteen-arm split found all the positive deltas (knee-7d53).
close_reason: the flag now has to land: Landed asks DEPTH_REGIONS and the model answers with the count it will actually split on, so --slice-regions with attend or channel pooling refuses at pre-flight instead of recording a region count no forward pass used

title: Aggregation beats input: fourteen arms split by WHAT they changed, and the four positives have never been stacked
description:
Read on 2026-08-27 with kneemri.evaluation.run_comparison --split, control lr4e-5_ws_s2026, on the six model-bottlenecked findings (ACL, Lateral Meniscus, Lateral OA, MCL, Medial Meniscus, PF OA).

EVERY ARM THAT ADDS INPUT LOSES: slices16 -0.0206, slotmean -0.0159, focal_pool -0.0159, crop80_span -0.0098, intensity392 -0.0076, attend_true -0.0068, depth_regions_span -0.0052, res392 -0.0022, sliceattn -0.0117, pair_memory -0.0494.

EVERY ARM THAT CHANGES AGGREGATION GAINS: sided_pool +0.0076, attend_dense +0.0059, depth_regions +0.0016, through_dense +0.0005.

MECHANISM. A thin focal structure occupies two or three slices of twenty, so any pooling that averages over depth divides its evidence by the slice count. Adding slices makes it WORSE, which is why slices16 is the single worst arm of the fourteen and why res392 INVERTS (regional +0.0032, focal -0.0027 -- it helped exactly the findings a tighter view should have cost). Adding pixels does not touch the dilution at all. Only a pooling that can concentrate on the slices where the structure lives recovers it.

WHAT THIS KILLS: the 512px / focal-crop lane. Three resolution arms and two crop arms, all negative on the term they were built for. Resolution is not the mechanism behind the supervision gap on focal findings (knee-cwpk).

WHAT THIS OPENS: the four positives act at three different points -- through_plane before the encoder sees a slice, attend across the slice axis, sided across the slots -- and have never been run together. experiments/arms/fuse_attend.sh and fuse_regions.sh are that stack.

DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY: model.py:322 returns the attend path and never reaches over_depth, so --slice-regions passed beside --slice-pooling attend is SILENTLY IGNORED. No error, no log line. That is why the stack forks into two arms instead of one.
notes: PRICE: ~19 min of card per arm, zero slots. Control native224 = 0.8502 (e7, converged). Keep floor +0.0062. P(clears): sided224 0.15, attend224 0.20, regions224 0.10, through224 0.15, focal224 0.08. Priced as a SEARCH over five cheap attempts on the ONE family that ever gained (sided_pool +0.0076, attend_dense +0.0059, both at dense, never at 224), not as five independent bets; regions224 and focal224 are instruments that close a grid-dependence question rather than bets on a number.
