title: Topology, not intensity: nothing here models a tear as a DISCONTINUITY
description:
Owner's idea 2026-08-27: learn what the DIFFERENCE between healthy and pathological looks like per label — 'torn meniscus is probably physically separated as a link'.

AUDIT SAYS THE APPEARANCE HALF IS MEASURED OUT. Every locality lever this repo has is an INTENSITY STATISTIC over patch tokens or slices, and all of them are flat-to-negative:
  --pool cls_mean_focal (per-channel top EIGHTH of the patch grid, whose docstring names 'meniscus, ACL, MCL occupy a fraction of the field') -> focal_dense +0.0007 / +0.0003 / -0.0002, flat
  depth_regions 0.8549 / depth_regions_narrow 0.8554 / depth_regions_span 0.8505, all BELOW band_dense 0.8578
  aprior_dense (--anatomical-prior, SlotHead.prior from the 12x6 plane-by-finding table)
  focus_mcl / focus_latmen (--focus-label)
  attribution.py occlusion: slot importance, border-vs-centre, depth profile — diagnostic only
  slotmean 0.8406 vs attention -0.0051, so slot-level ATTENTION is earning; spatial pooling is not.

WHY THEY WERE ALWAYS GOING TO BE FLAT, AND WHY THE IDEA IS NOT REFUTED BY THEM. Mean, max, top-eighth and region-mean all answer 'how bright, where'. The owner's claim answers 'is it CONNECTED'. A healthy meniscus is a continuous dark triangle; a torn one has a bright linear cleft crossing it. A tear and a bright artefact share an intensity signature and differ in TOPOLOGY. No pooling operator over patch tokens can express connectedness at any percentile. So the flat focal result kills that USE of the intuition, not the intuition.

NEVER TRIED, ZERO ARMS: (1) no segmentation anywhere in this repo — nothing delineates meniscus/ACL/cartilage, no masks of any kind; (2) no healthy-vs-pathological contrastive objective — every loss is BCE on study-level labels; (3) no shape/continuity/topology feature.

THE BLOCKER IS THE SAME DOOR AS EVERYTHING ELSE. The strong form needs structure masks and this competition ships none. The public knee-MRI corpus that carries tissue segmentations is SKM-TEA, which sits inside the external-data question blocked on the Host ruling (knee-2sbk). Second time in one window that a lane sized for the gap terminates at that door.

CHEAP FORM, NO MASKS, DO THIS FIRST: supervised-contrastive loss alongside BCE, per finding — force the embedding to separate torn from intact rather than only to predict a probability. A loss change, ~1 arm. Prior: this is the class of change (architecture/objective) the house says outsizes knobs, but it is still MEMBER QUALITY, so calibsix's 23% board pass-through ceilings it near 0.943. Price it as an instrument for the topology question, not as a board bet.

DEPENDS: knee-2sbk (external data ruling) for the strong form.
notes: RAN 2026-08-27. contrast-weight 1.0 vs calib_dense_hold 0.8634 (single variable, recipe-diffed). Best 0.8547 @ e5 of 12, converged. -0.0087, outside the 0.0062 paired floor. 11 of 12 labels down (worst Effusion -0.0208), only PF OA +0.0104; the meniscus labels the idea targeted read -0.0127 / -0.0057. Uniform mild damage = auxiliary term taxing the shared trunk, same shape as side_dense at a tenth the size. The arm's own pre-registered weakness fired: batch 12 sees a 7%-prevalence finding about once, so the supervised-contrastive positives are mostly absent. Reading is 'supervised contrastive at batch 12 costs 0.009 and buys nothing', NOT 'representation shaping is refuted'. RememberedRanking (a remembered pool of past readouts) is the named precondition, untried. No dose sweep: it would sweep the wrong variable. Cost 420 s/epoch (~84 min) vs a predicted ~200 s/~40 min — price an arm off its control's measured epoch time. Ledger entry written.

title: UNK weight 0.2875 is a magic number and double-counts uncertainty (CheXpert U-Ignore precedent)
description:
confident224 measured a second point on the supervision-spread line: UNK cells at weight 0.0 score 0.8431, at 0.2875 score 0.8502 (native224). Both points say LESS spread between UNK and YES is better. floor>0.25 is untested and is the direction the slope points.

Census of report_labels_v2.csv (52,872 cells, zero NaN): value 0.08/conf 0.85 -> weight 0.8875 (22,298 cells) - value 0.28/conf 0.05 -> 0.2875 (14,445) - value 0.68/0.82/0.94/conf 0.95 -> 0.9625 (16,129). weight = CONFIDENCE_FLOOR + (1-CONFIDENCE_FLOOR)*conf, targets.py:330.

BLOCKED ON CODE: --weight-floor is store_true (flag_vocabulary.py:199), floor is 0.25 or 0.0 (options.py:257, landed.py:269), and it rescales EVERY cell not just UNK. A value sweep needs a float flag, and the bool must survive because 100+ recorded recipe stamps and arm_check compare against it.

DELIBERATELY NOT DOING IT YET, and the reason is the point of this bead: this is a MEMBER-QUALITY lever, and calibsix measured 23% pass-through from member gains to board (six seats improved on one axis, pre-registered ~0.944, read 0.941), which ceilings the whole lane near 0.943 against a leader at 0.952. ~25 min of code for a knob that cannot reach +0.011 board is the wrong ratio while slots are live. Run it in a card gap AFTER the diversity-structure lane is exhausted, or if the lane target changes.
notes:
RE-PRICED P3 -> P1 2026-08-27 09:25Z. Not a knob sweep — a derivation replacing two inherited constants.

WHERE 0.2875 COMES FROM. weight = CONFIDENCE_FLOOR + (1-CONFIDENCE_FLOOR)*__conf (targets.py:330). CONFIDENCE_FLOOR=0.25 is copied from a public Kaggle baseline — its own docstring at targets.py:291 says it 'reproduces the public baseline's 0.25 + 0.75*conf'. __conf=0.05 is the reader LLM's SELF-REPORTED confidence, never validated against anything. Neither factor was fit to our data. Census verified over all 52,872 cells of report_labels_v2.csv, zero NaN: value 0.08 / conf 0.85 -> weight 0.8875 (22,298 cells) - value 0.28 / conf 0.05 -> 0.2875 (14,445) - values 0.68,0.82,0.94 / conf 0.95 -> 0.9625 (16,129).

THE WEIGHTS ARE ANTI-CORRELATED WITH LABEL INFORMATION. Against MEASURED_AGREEMENT (targets.py:115-119), level -> measured positive rate (n) -> information 1-H(p) -> current weight:
  0.08 -> 0.041 (n=196) -> 0.753 -> 0.8875
  0.28 -> 0.136 (n=177) -> 0.426 -> 0.2875   <-- LOWEST weight, ~10x the information of the 0.68 level
  0.68 -> 0.378 (n=98)  -> 0.043 -> 0.9625   <-- HIGHEST weight, and 37.8% positive is near a coin flip
  0.82 -> 0.688 (n=141) -> 0.105 -> 0.9625
  0.94 -> 0.958 (n=72)  -> 0.749 -> 0.9625
The 'mild' cells carry almost no information and the top weight. That is a second, independent defect this bead surfaced: the 0.68 weight should come DOWN as well as the 0.28 weight going UP.

AND THE DOUBT IS COUNTED TWICE. The UNK cell already carries its uncertainty in the VALUE (0.28, mapped by --calibrated-targets to the measured 0.136). Discounting it AGAIN in the WEIGHT double-counts. Standard practice is one or the other: soft targets (uncertainty in the value, weight 1.0) OR loss reweighting (hard value, weight carries reliability) OR noise-transition correction (Patrini forward/backward — which MEASURED_AGREEMENT already IS, half-used, since reliability() deliberately declines to apply it at the 0.28 level).

PRECEDENT — CHEXPERT (Irvin et al., AAAI 2019), the same problem: uncertain findings extracted from radiology reports. They benchmark U-Ignore / U-Zeros / U-Ones / U-SelfTrained / U-MultiClass. STATED CAREFULLY, because a first draft of this note overstated it: their final per-pathology baseline selects U-Ones (Atelectasis, Edema), U-MultiClass (Cardiomegaly, Pleural Effusion), U-SelfTrained (Consolidation) — U-Ignore is chosen for NONE of the five. Where compared directly, U-Zeros and U-Ones both beat U-Ignore on Consolidation; on Edema U-Ignore is almost as good as U-Ones. So the citable claim is DROPPING UNCERTAIN LABELS IS NEVER THE WINNER, AND THE WINNER DIFFERS PER FINDING — not 'dropping is always worst'. confident224 IS U-Ignore and landed -0.0071, consistent. https://stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/chexpert/

PRESCRIPTION, derived rather than swept: keep the calibrated value, raise the UNK weight toward the NO cells' 0.8875, lower the 0.68 weight, and make the policy PER-LABEL because CheXpert's own result is that the winner differs by finding. Our three extreme-UNK labels are Synovitis 84.2%, Fracture 56.4%, Baker's 45.9%.

BLOCKED ON CODE: --weight-floor is store_true (flag_vocabulary.py:199), floor is 0.25 or 0.0 (options.py:257, landed.py:269), and it rescales EVERY cell rather than one level. Needs a per-level float table. The bool must survive because 100+ recorded recipe stamps and arm_check compare against it.

LANE CAVEAT: this is member-quality, and calibsix measured 23% pass-through to the board (six seats improved on one axis, pre-registered ~0.944, read 0.941), ceilinging that lane near 0.943 against a leader at 0.952. It is P1 on MECHANISM CORRECTNESS — the weights are demonstrably backwards — not on expected board points. Do not spend a slot on it alone.

title: confident224: gate knee-pju4's reader project on whether label CONTENT binds us at all, at a corner that fits a SHARED card
description:
knee-pju4 proposes a local open-weights reader over the 14,445 UNK (study,finding) pairs. That costs a
model download, deps this machine lacks (vllm / accelerate / gptqmodel all absent), the whole card for
inference, and a retrain of every seat -- call it a day -- on the UNTESTED premise that label CONTENT
moves our score at all.

`experiments/arms/confident_span.sh` is that premise's own test and has never run. It clears every UNK
VALUE rather than filling it (`Targets.load` then skips the target and gives weight 0.0), so it trains
on strictly LESS supervision and asks the same question from the cheap side. But it is written at the
336 px / 12-slice corner and reserves 17997 MiB, and celltrack holds this card by arrangement leaving
17147 free -- it misses by 850 MiB.

THIS ARM IS THAT ARM AT 224 px. `native224.sh` verbatim -- 12 slices, band 0.2-0.8, --image-size 224,
12 epochs, backbone-lr 4e-5, max pooling, whole-stack, fold 0 -- with `--labels confident.csv` in place
of the standard table. Single variable. `vram_need` reads 8124 MiB, so it runs beside a co-tenant
holding up to 24 GB, and 224 px is ~94 s/epoch: ~19 minutes, not 60.

CONTROL IS ALREADY ON THE LEDGER: `native224` = 0.8502 (best epoch 7, convergence_check clean). No
matched baseline needed, so this costs ONE run.

PRE-REGISTERED, against the 0.0062 three-seed paired floor:
  >= 0.8564  label content moves the score. knee-pju4's reader project is LIVE and worth the day; the
             expensive multilingual read becomes the thing to build.
  0.8440-0.8564  within the floor. Removing 27.3% of the supervision changes nothing measurable, so the
             targets are not what binds us -- and the reader project is dead before it costs a day.
             This is the branch that saves the most.
  <= 0.8440  the UNK cells carry real signal at their 0.2875 weight (--weight-floor is in $RECIPE:
             floor 0.25 + 0.75*conf). Then the honest move is the OPPOSITE one -- trust silence MORE --
             and `--calibrated-targets` (0.28 -> 0.136 via MEASURED_AGREEMENT) is the already-built
             lever to push further rather than remove.

PRICE: 19 minutes of card (12 epochs at ~94 s), zero submission slots, and it runs BESIDE celltrack's
15 GB rather than waiting for the card to empty -- so its cost against the queue is ZERO, because the
arm it displaces (`finding_calib_dense`, 28934 MiB) cannot run at all while the co-tenant is there.

P(clears 1.5%) ~ 0, and deliberately so: this arm trains on strictly LESS supervision, so the >= 0.8564
branch would be a surprise. It is an INSTRUMENT, not a candidate, and is justified as one:
  P(clears 0.0062 upward, label content is live)  ~0.15  -> licenses knee-pju4's day of reader work
  P(within the floor)                             ~0.65  -> RETIRES that day on a 19-minute measurement
  P(clears 0.0062 downward, silence has signal)   ~0.20  -> inverts the prescription toward
                                                            --calibrated-targets rather than a reader
The expected value is the middle branch: 19 minutes that retire a P0 day at 65% is the best ratio on the
board today, and no other queued arm fits the card as it currently stands.

CAVEAT STATED BEFORE THE NUMBER. This is the 224/12-slice corner, weaker than the champion's dense one.
A null bounds the effect HERE; a positive would want confirming at 336 before any seat is retrained.
224 is not an unrepresentative corner though -- knee-rh4t reads the two best self-reported single-model
rivals (0.942 and 0.938) as both at 224 px.
notes:
RESULT 2026-08-27 09:08Z. confident224 = 0.8431, best epoch 6 of 12 run / 12 asked, five declining epochs after (0.8389 / 0.8422 / 0.8428 / 0.8416 / 0.8412). convergence_check clean — the run is in its 81 converged, not among the 7 truncated. Control native224 = 0.8502. Delta -0.0071 against the 0.0062 three-seed paired floor: 1.15 floors, DOWNWARD.

Harness verified before reading: printed recipe says image_size 224, labels confident.csv, weight_floor True, calibrated_targets False, slices 12, band 0.2-0.8, whole_stack True, slice_pooling max, epochs 12, backbone_lr 4e-05. 7.42 GB reserved against the 8124 MiB vram_need predicted. Every flag landed.

PRE-REGISTERED BRANCH 3 FIRES, AND BY 0.0009. The written condition was '<= 0.8440 — the UNK cells carry real signal at their 0.2875 weight, and silence IS weak evidence of absence exactly as CONFIDENCE_FLOOR's docstring argues'. 0.8431 clears it by 0.0009, so the branch fires MARGINALLY, not decisively — one arm, one seed, 1.15 floors. Report as directional.

WHAT IT SAYS. Clearing 27.3% of (study,finding) pairs to weight 0.0 COSTS score. The UNK cells are not noise being tolerated; they are weak evidence already being used, at the 0.2875 the weight floor gives them. CONFIDENCE_FLOOR's docstring argued this before the measurement and the measurement agrees with it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. This is the 224/12-slice corner, weaker than the champion's dense one, and the caveat was written into the arm header before the number landed: a null would have bounded the effect HERE only. A NEGATIVE is stronger evidence than a null would have been — removing supervision hurt at the cheap corner, and there is no mechanism by which it would stop hurting at the dense one — but it is still one arm at one corner.

CONSEQUENCE FOR knee-pju4, which this arm was built to gate: the reader project's premise is INVERTED, not confirmed. It was priced as replacing garbage cells with real reads. The cells are not garbage. See knee-pju4 for the disposition.

title: Per-finding label calibration: arm on the dense-hold corner, pre-registered
description:
core/data/labels/finding_calibration.py fits one empirical-Bayes-shrunk logit offset per finding on top of the pooled MEASURED_AGREEMENT map. tau=0.294 (sd 0.543 logits) survives the moment subtraction, so the twelve findings do not share one scale. Shipped as FINDING_OFFSETS in core/data/labels/targets.py behind --finding-calibration (REQUIRES --calibrated-targets; UncalibratedFindingShiftError otherwise).

WHY: noise_binding (2026-08-27) shows every --hold-annotations member tracks the reader's 108 confident false positives at +0.54 to +0.70, and that --calibrated-targets cuts that by ~0.15 at two independent corners. The pooled map flattens a 37-point per-finding spread (Contusion 44.4% vs Synovitis 81.2% agreement on positive calls) and the two fail in OPPOSITE directions, so one pooled number cannot carry both.

PRICE: ~40 min of card, no submission slot. Expected offline +0.002-0.004 - DIRECTIONAL, under the house bar. Justified as an INSTRUMENT: it licenses or kills a whole family (per-finding loss weighting, per-finding thresholds, per-finding heads), and a label-table change is the 126-147% pass-through class because it retrains every seat.

PRE-REGISTERED against calib_dense_hold 0.8634 (paired three-seed floor 0.0062):
  >= 0.8696  the lever is real, open the per-finding family
  0.8572-0.8696  FLAT on this ruler - but see the caveat, do not kill on this alone
  <= 0.8572  it hurts; the pooled map is right and the family closes

HARNESS CAVEAT, stated before the run: the offline holdout is scored against the REPORT labels, which carry the very defect these offsets correct. The offline ruler is biased AGAINST this table, so its number is a FLOOR. The primary rulers are kneemri.evaluation.annotated_readings (the radiologist read) and kneemri.evaluation.noise_binding (does the binding to the lexicon drop below --calibrated-targets alone?).

SELF-CRITIQUE, priced in: a per-finding MONOTONE map leaves each head's own ranking unchanged, so in the well-specified limit per-head AUC is untouched. Whatever this buys comes through the SHARED TRUNK and cross-head gradient balance - the same indirect route the pooled calibration must already be working through. That caps the expected size at second-order relative to the pooled +0.0061.

title: convergence_check is blind to any run not in the ledger, and epochs_done reads like a truncation when it is not
description:
Today the four 2x2 hold checkpoints (band_span_hold, calib_span_hold, band_dense_hold, calib_dense_hold) each stamp epoch=6..9, epochs_done=7..10, epochs=12, patience=0. Read straight off the checkpoint that is the exact TRUNCATED signature the check defines: died short of the budget it asked for, no stopper armed, so the score is a FLOOR. I was one step from recording all four scores as floors and hedging the additivity finding on it.

They are not truncated. The .metrics.jsonl files carry e0..e11 for all four - every run completed its full 12 epochs and peaked mid-run on the one_cycle tail. So epochs_done does NOT mean epochs completed, and nothing in the checkpoint says what it does mean.

TWO HOLES, both live:

1. convergence_check --run <name> answers '1 runs: 1 unscored' for every one of these, because it reads the LEDGER and these runs were never scored into it. The check that exists to stop a floor being quoted as a fact is silent on exactly the runs most likely to be quoted from a checkpoint - the ones no arm recorded.

2. The truncation verdict is derived from epochs_done when .metrics.jsonl is the ground truth and is sitting next to the checkpoint. A run's own per-epoch curve says whether it finished; a counter of ambiguous meaning should not outrank it.

FIX: convergence_check should fall back to the metrics file when a run is absent from the ledger, and should prefer the metrics line count over epochs_done wherever both exist. Either rename epochs_done to what it actually counts or drop it from the stamp.

COST OF NOT FIXING: the same misread in the other direction - a genuinely truncated run whose epochs_done happens to read full - would quote a floor as a converged score, which is the failure this check was built for.

title: calibsix: the champion seating with --calibrated-targets on EVERY seat - pre-registered before the number
description:
The champion's six seats, each retrained with the one term this project has measured POSITIVE twice (--calibrated-targets: +0.0061 at the dense-hold corner, +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotated at calib_span). Roster: final_ws_cf, calib_span_ff, grade_ladder_cf, merged_blend_cf, lr4e-5_ws_cf, through_dense_cf. Serving is votefit's: overlap=False, LogitAverage, kit unchanged.

WHY THIS IS NOT A SEAT PERMUTATION (knee-xuj5). Nine 6/7-member entries span 0.002 because every one of them moved WHICH member sat where. This moves no seat. It changes what each of the six IS, on the same axis, in the same direction, all at once - the only entry that does. knee-urvf and knee-rh4t both say member quality is the only free term left; this is the first submission that spends it on all six seats rather than one.

WHY IT MIGHT NOT COMPOUND. The 23% pass-through measured on 2026-08-26 was for ADDING one member to a roster of seven, not for IMPROVING all six. Those are different quantities and nothing here has measured the second. If quality passes through at 23% even when every seat moves, this reads flat and the member lane is closed for good.

PRICING, with knee-ps8o's correction applied. board_transfer's whole-range fit is +1.72 but the local slope where we sit is 0.74-0.88, so a +0.006 offline roster gain converts to roughly +0.005 board, NOT +0.010. Against blendseat 0.939 that predicts ~0.944. This entry cannot reach 0.950 on its own arithmetic and is not being sold as if it could.

PRE-REGISTERED against blendseat 0.939 (best board):
  >=0.945  calibration compounds ACROSS seats at better than the 23% pass-through; the member lane reopens at full rate and every remaining slot goes to applying measured-positive terms to whole rosters rather than to single seats.
  0.941-0.944  the predicted band. A real new best, the lane pays at roughly the local slope, and stackfit (knee-orjq) becomes the additivity test worth card time.
  0.936-0.940  FLAT. Improving all six members by the only term we hold buys nothing the board can see - that closes the member-quality lane (knee-urvf) and sends the remaining slots to labels, corpus or serving.
  <=0.935  the calibrated members share an error the vote used to average out; per-member logit scales want auditing before any further roster-wide change.
notes: RESULT 2026-08-27 06:26Z: calibsix = 0.941. NEW BEST (+0.002 over blendseat/blendthree 0.939) and the FIRST of twelve entries to leave the 0.936-0.939 plateau. Against the four pre-registered branches: it landed BELOW the ~0.944 prediction, so the branch that fires is 'directional, mechanism-consistent, not a finding' - +0.002 is under the 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor and under the 0.0062 three-seed floor. THE MEASURED QUANTITY: the 23% seat pass-through was measured for ADDING one member; this is the first measurement of improving ALL SIX on one axis at once, and it does not compound. CONSEQUENCE: the member-quality lane ceilings near 0.943 against a leader at 0.952, so 0.950 is not reachable down this lane. Recorded in comp/board.jsonl (calibsix_v1), comp/SUBMISSIONS.md, and comp/champion.json (pin moved, champion_check green).

title: build_cache accepts --scheme rijeka/merged and writes OUR corpus under a foreign name
description:
build_cache.py decodes the RSNA study list and takes --scheme only as a NAME for the output file. Passing --scheme merged produced (4407, 6, 20, 336, 336) -> images_336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_merged.npy: the canonical corpus wearing the merged corpus's filename. --scheme rijeka does the same, (4407, 1, 20, ...) under images_..._rijeka.npy, and would have overwritten the real 736-study rijeka cache had the geometry matched.

build_rijeka.py already refuses any scheme but its own, with a docstring naming the 71.6 GB this class of error costs. build_cache.py has no such guard on the other side: it should refuse the schemes that belong to a FOREIGN study list (rijeka, mrnet, merged), since it can only ever decode ours. Caught only because the printed shape read 4407 where the merged corpus is 5143 - two decodes were launched and killed before either finished.

FIX: build_cache.py errors on scheme in {RIJEKA_SCHEME, MRNET_SCHEME, MERGED_SCHEME}, with the same wording build_rijeka uses. The corpus a builder can decode is a property of the builder, not of a flag.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-27. core/data/corpus/slots.py gains FOREIGN_SCHEMES = (rijeka, mrnet, merged) — the schemes naming a corpus this repo's own decoder cannot produce, each owned by its own builder — and build_cache refuses all three before it touches the filesystem, pointing at core.data.corpus.build_<scheme>. Same shape as build_rijeka's existing scheme guard, which is what the defect should have been caught by.

TEST, and it found a SECOND live defect on its first run. tests/unit/core/data/corpus/build_cache.py drives every builder's main() with --help under monkeypatched argv: parser construction is reached, no filesystem work is. build_mrnet was uncallable for exactly the same reason build_rijeka was — its own float --spacing collided with the one CacheFlags.add_to adds, so argparse raised while CONSTRUCTING the parser. Renamed to --pixel-spacing, same as build_rijeka. Two of four corpus builders had been dead CLIs and nothing in the tree said so, because no test had ever built these parsers.

The refusal itself is pinned per-scheme (exit 2), so a fourth foreign corpus added to FOREIGN_SCHEMES inherits the guard and its test.

title: merged_dense_cf: the dense stack geometry on the merged corpus, our best-scoring axis
description:
Our top two holdout members are merged_blend_s2026 (0.8589) and merged_blend_cf (0.8597) -- the RSNA corpus merged with Rijeka expert image reads, three-reader blended labels, calibrated targets. That axis has only ever run at the 12-slice 0.2-0.8 geometry it was first written with. Every decode knob is closed on the report-labelled corpus, but the dense geometry (20 slices, 0.1-0.9) is the operating point five seated members were fitted at, and its span half measured +0.0039 alone in band_span. The claim under test is that the corpus lever and the geometry lever COMPOSE, because they act on different parts of the chain (what the network sees vs what it is told).

PRICE: a ~70 GB cache build (336px_20sl_0.1-0.9band_merged; the 12sl merged build is 41.8 GB) at about 2 h of decode, then about 2 h of training -- so ~4 h of a card that is otherwise idle, and the cache unlocks the dense geometry for every future merged-corpus arm rather than only this one. Expected gain +0.004 offline, which is what band_span measured alone. P(clears 1.5%) ~0.05. P(clears the 0.0062 noise floor) ~0.3. It is bought as a CHAIN LINK, not as a finding: merged corpus +0.0087, calibrated targets +0.0010, this ~+0.004, all against native224 0.8502.

Control merged_blend_cf 0.8597. Pre-registration is in experiments/arms/merged_dense_cf.sh.
close_reason: RAN, and the solo is the least of it. merged_dense_cf peaks 0.8569 at e8: -0.0009 vs band_dense, -0.0028 vs merged_blend_cf, both sub-floor, so no member and no corpus gain at the dense corner. THE COMPOSITION CLAIM IS REFUTED AND IT CLEARS THE FLOOR: the same 12sl-0.2-0.8 -> 20sl-0.1-0.9 move buys +0.0053 on our corpus (rate_wholestack 0.8525 -> band_dense 0.8578) and -0.0028 on the merged one (merged_blend_cf 0.8597 -> merged_dense_cf 0.8569). 0.0081 apart, 1.3x the 0.0062 paired floor, sign inverted. The geometry gain is a fact about the corpus it was measured on. Harness cleared: distinct merged dense cache key, builder refuses foreign corpus names since knee-48br, recipe stamp carries slices 20 / band 0.1-0.9, converged e8 of 12, and this is the relaunch not the nvlddmkm-killed first attempt. Caveat kept: one seed a cell, 1.3 floors not 3. Seat value +0.0007 (best seat +0.0008), 0 of 1 clearing +0.0015 -- no seat, no slot. CONSEQUENCE: this is the only composition measurement the project holds and it reads SUBSTITUTION, which lowers the prior on knee-orjq's stack route; written into experiments/README.md BEFORE stackfit's number lands so it cannot be fitted to it.

title: Contiguity, not band width: our 9 slices are linspace-spread, a rival measures +0.018 for center-adjacent
description:
FORUM EVIDENCE (topic 737597, read 2026-08-26 23:00Z, theirs and self-reported). A competitor at 0.7815 OOF / 0.870 public, EfficientNet-B0, 4 slots, 288 px, 140 mm crop, 5-fold: 'Slice geometry mattered more than resolution: center-9 ADJACENT beat 9 equal-spaced across 24 by +0.018 on fold 0.' Their negative list is a clean sweep of the training-regime axis at the same time (EMA +0.003, mixup +0.002, 60-epoch cosine +0.001, asymmetric loss -0.139) and their per-finding deficit is OURS: Baker's 0.855 / Effusion 0.843 / Fracture 0.832 against Lateral Meniscus 0.740 / PF OA 0.748 / Lateral OA 0.751 / MCL 0.758 - large-discrete-positional works, thin-small-graded does not.

WHAT WE ACTUALLY DO. core/data/corpus/slot_reader.py:252 - band_indices() takes np.linspace(low, high, slices) over the central band and de-duplicates. Every slice we feed is EQUAL-SPACED across the band. Not one arm in the ledger has varied the SPACING RULE; every one varied the band WIDTH (0.20-0.80 = 0.8525, 0.10-0.90 = 0.8565, 0.00-1.00 = 0.8427).

WHY THAT IS NOT THE SAME AXIS, AND WHY OUR BAND RESULT DOES NOT ALREADY REFUTE IT. Wider band beat narrower here, which reads as evidence FOR spread - but band width is EXTENT and adjacency is CONTIGUITY, and they carry different mechanisms. Extent buys coverage of where a finding might sit. Contiguity buys the 3D continuity a focal finding is DEFINED by: a meniscal tear is 1-3 mm of signal that has to touch an articular surface on two CONSECUTIVE slices, and equal-spacing across a wide band guarantees no two of our nine slices are consecutive in mm. Under linspace the model can never see that continuity at all, on any band width. So the two results are compatible and the axis is untested.

SIZE. +0.018 is 3x the 0.0062 three-seed floor and above the 1.5% bar - the first lever in a week whose CLAIMED size is not a knob. It is also the surviving arm of the deficit question this project has been circling from three directions (focal deficit, supervision gap, our-model-past-its-teacher), and it is a DATA change rather than a loss or a head change.

COST, AND THE ONE THING TO CHECK FIRST. This is a CACHE-shape change: slot_reader's own docstring says changing band_indices invalidates 99 GB of decoded arrays and every member fitted on them, with no fingerprint to catch it. BEFORE pricing a rebuild, check whether the cache stores more slices than a run consumes (slice_count arms ran at 12 and 20) - if it does, a contiguous CENTER-9 can be subselected from an existing 12- or 20-slice cache at zero rebuild cost, which turns a 99 GB job into one 40-minute arm.

PRE-REGISTER BEFORE RUNNING: >=+0.010 contiguity is a real lever and the cache is rebuilt on its account; +0.006 to +0.010 directional, keep as a diversity member and re-test; within +/-0.006 the axis closes and the rival's +0.018 is their 5-fold OOF ruler rather than a transferable mechanism; <=-0.006 spread is load-bearing here and our wide-band result is the reason.

Their number is self-reported and unverifiable. Read it as a claim that names a mechanism, and let our own arm settle the size.
notes:
MEASURED AND REFUTED 2026-08-27: adjacent224_s2026 0.8462 vs native224_s2026 0.8502, MEAN -0.0040, converged. The one marked delta was Medial Meniscus -0.0136*, precisely the finding contiguity was written for, with Regional -0.0073 against focal -0.0018 - the mechanism fired and it cost. Full row: experiments/README.md, 2026-08-27 section.

RE-OPEN CONDITION RETIRED 2026-09-05, WITHOUT AN ARM. The close note licensed one re-test at a denser stack where span is not the thing being spent. That condition is not reachable. Spacing docstring asserted that under SPREAD no two sampled slices are ever adjacent AT ANY WIDTH; that clause is FALSE and it is false exactly at our operating point. Series depth over a 12-study sample (68 series): min 16, p25 26, median 32, p75 38. At slices=20 the band offers ~25 indices on a median study and we take 20 of them, so consecutive pairs out of a possible 19 run spread-vs-adjacent as 12v12 at depth 16 (IDENTICAL index sets), 18v19 at p25, 14v19 at median, 8v19 at p75 - while adjacent pays full span cost at every depth (24 to 19 indices at median, 30 to 19 at p75). Contrast is large only on DEEP series, which are exactly where adjacency discards the most span, so a big contrast and a cheap span are anti-correlated by construction. A denser stack is where SPREAD CONVERGES TO ADJACENT, not where adjacency gets a fair test. DO NOT re-run this axis. The rivals +0.018 stands unchallenged for THEIR point (9 slices across 24 is the regime where the old clause is true); it does not transfer. Ledger: experiments/README.md 2026-09-05 contiguity section. Docstring now carries the table instead of the claim.

title: The deadline is 2026-10-22: ~280 slots remain, and the ratchet reaches 0.950 without a step change
description:
Read from the Kaggle API 2026-08-26 22:45Z: deadline 2026-10-22 23:59, 2469 teams, our rank 46. 56 days remain, ~5 slots a day, so roughly 280 submissions - not five. The deadline appeared in no doc, bead, kernel or interpretation before today; every plan was made against the recurring prompt's four-hour horizon.

Our running-best climbs +0.0016/day over 9 days (+0.0010 over the last 3). 0.950 needs +0.011, i.e. 7-11 days, inside the window with 45 days to spare. Of 57 scored submissions 18 set a new best (31.6%), but every one of the last eleven was +0.003 or smaller - individually knobs, together +0.014 since 08-18. The project is running a working RATCHET, not failing to find a lever.

Consequences to hold to:
1. Slots are not the scarce resource; card hours and ideas are. 'Spread the slots' is a DAILY rule and correct as one - it must not be read as a global scarcity that argues against firing an informative arm.
2. Do not abandon the ratchet for a step change. Pursue a step change in PARALLEL - that is what closes on first place rather than on 0.950.
3. Seating is the ratchet's cheapest fuel and nearly spent: nine six-member entries span 0.014 total, and the last two gains came from a vote rule (votefit) and better label supervision (blendseat), not a seat swap.

See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_the-horizon-is-56-days-not-4-hours.md. Related: knee-wvfr (leader series - the one unevidenced assumption).

title: The reader over-calls 108 cells and hides 24 - a replacement must be built for PRECISION, not coverage
description:
Displaces the sizing argument in knee-pju4 (see its notes, measured 2026-08-26 22:33Z).

THE MEASUREMENT. core.data.labels.reader_agreement --> silence/silence_report, over 684 annotated cells / 57 studies:
  177 silent cells (25.9%, matching the corpus 27.3%)
  radiologist positive rate 13.6% among SILENT cells, 41.6% among spoken ones
  perfect silence-filler ceiling: 24 cells. Over-calling: 108 cells.

So the reader's dominant defect is saying YES where the radiologist says no - 108 of 684 cells, 15.8% of everything annotated, and errors() reports every one of them as a confident YES rather than an abstention. Per-finding net over-calling: Contusion +18, Effusion +16, ACL +9, MCL +9, Medial OA +7, Lateral Meniscus +7. Synovitis is the sole inversion at -11.

WHY THE CONFIDENCE COLUMN CANNOT HELP. __conf takes one value per verdict level (std 0.0 over all 52,872 cells), so it is a deterministic function of the verdict and cannot downweight a confident error. This is the same defect knee-b8g9 names from the forum side: LLM self-reported confidence measures certainty in APPLYING A HEURISTIC TO TEXT, not diagnostic uncertainty.

WHAT TO BUILD, in order of size:
1. A precision-tuned second pass over the cells the lexicon calls YES (311 of 684 annotated; corpus-wide the YES cells, not the blank ones). The acceptance test is reader_agreement's own per-language and per-finding agreement table, run before and after - it exists and it refuses tables it cannot read.
2. A targeted Synovitis pass. 84.2% UNK corpus-wide, 41 silent of 58 annotated, 14 hidden positives - the only finding where silence is the larger failure, and the finding whose labels predict the radiologist worst (0.6870, supervision_gap).
3. Only then the general blank-filling of knee-pju4, which is now priced at <=3.5% of cells.

CONSTRAINT WORTH STATING: our member already scores 0.8932 against the radiologist while its teacher scores 0.8658 (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_our-model-is-past-its-teacher.md). The model is ALREADY discounting the teacher's over-calls to some degree. A better table has to beat what the model has learned to ignore, which is a higher bar than beating the table.

DENOMINATOR: 684 cells / 57 studies / 1.3% of the corpus. 108 and 24 are small integers with no intervals - read the RATIO, not the rates.

title: The efficiency board says the leaders are not ensembles - price seating against member quality accordingly
description:
Topic 736678, read 2026-08-26 22:20Z, written up in research/2026-08-26_rival_single_models_and_the_label_bottleneck.md.

Two competitor statements that together make the reading: (a) only ~32% of the public LB top 50 also appear in the efficiency LB top 50, and (b) the top TWO public LB submissions do appear on the efficiency board. The broad plateau is slow; the very top is fast. A third poster is efficiency-LB #1 with no ensemble at all, and a fourth sits at Efficiency 22 / Public 78 with 0.926 on a ~20-minute single-model 5-fold pipeline.

Read together: ensembling is what the 0.936-0.940 plateau is MADE of, and the leaders are above it without one. We reached 0.939 through six members. Eleven of our entries now sit in 0.936-0.939 across count, member identity, fold status, regularisation, encoder family, architecture family, vote rule, serving views, corpus and supervision.

What this is NOT: a licence to drop the ensemble. 0.939 is our best result and decode-path diversity is the only axis with a measured board transfer (knee-nas5, 2.4x). It is a PRICE: another seating variation is a knob on a plateau the field says tops out near 0.94; a better member is the axis the leaders are on.

Note the disagreement worth keeping rather than merging: the forum says the lever is a better MODEL; our own gold-label reading (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_our-model-is-past-its-teacher.md) says our model is already 0.027 ABOVE its teacher and the lever is better LABELS. Both point away from seating. knee-pju4 (P0, the local relabeller) is the one that satisfies both readings, since better labels are how a better member gets built here.

No slot and no card needed to act on this - it is a ranking of the open levers, not an experiment.

title: LLM confidence measures heuristic-application certainty, not diagnostic uncertainty
description:
A competitor states the defect our calibrated-target arms inherit (topic 735826): asking an LLM for its confidence in a finding returns its confidence in APPLYING THE HEURISTIC TO THE TEXT, not the uncertainty in the diagnosis. It will be very confident that 'small effusion' means Effusion=0, because the rule is clear and the words are clear — while the process that produced the word 'small' rather than 'moderate' was itself noisy and is where the real uncertainty lives.

Evidence it is not merely an argument: filter reports whose effusion sentence carries a small-size qualifier (small/minimal/trace) and the group contains BOTH Effusion=0 and Effusion=1; two reports with the same English template and the same sentence carry opposite labels, and at least one 'moderate effusion' report is labelled 0.

Consequence for us: every calibrated/soft-target arm treats reader disagreement as if it were model uncertainty, with the confidence pointing the wrong way exactly where the labels are least reliable. Cross-check against core/data/labels/severity_boundary.py and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_effusion-threshold-ruler.md, which found the boundary independently. A soft target derived from AGREEMENT BETWEEN READERS is the mechanism-correct replacement; a soft target derived from LLM self-reported confidence is not.

title: Score the label extractor and the image model against the same 58 gold studies
description:
Topic 735826 volunteers a diagnostic we have the parts for and have never run in this direction: score the LABEL EXTRACTOR against the 58 provided gold labels, then score the IMAGE MODEL against the same 58. If the image model does not beat its own teacher there is modelling headroom; if it beats the teacher by a large margin the labels are the ceiling. Either answer redirects the next block of card time, and it costs no submission slot and no training.

kneemri/evaluation/annotated_readings.py already scores readings against the annotated subset. What is missing is the PAIRED comparison on one denominator: teacher-vs-gold and member-vs-gold over the identical 58 studies, reported side by side. State n=58 explicitly — it is small enough that most differences will not resolve, and a rate computed over a subset that an English regex could parse is not a rate over the corpus (that error has been made three times here).

Context: research/2026-08-26_rival_single_models_and_the_label_bottleneck.md. Rivals self-report SINGLE models at 0.926-0.942 while our six-member ensemble scores 0.939, so the gap is member quality, and the field's consensus bottleneck is label quality.

title: Uniform-lift census over 85 matched pairs: no second candidate exists
description:
The "stack three independent uniform lifts" plan for +0.0133 offline is NOT executable: the disk
record contains exactly one uniform-lift candidate, and its evidence is confounded.

METHOD. 175 .pt records, 155 carry a recipe. Matched pairs = differ in exactly one recipe key,
ignoring non-semantic keys (out/labels/paths/eval_labels/vram_gb/compile_encoder/
recompute_activations/accumulate/batch/cache_studies) and the banned axis (seed/split_seed).
Ignoring those took the count from 56 pairs / 27 switches to 85 pairs / 22 switches. Each pair
scored by RunMetrics.best(); a switch is a uniform lift only if the sign holds across DISTINCT
seats and the magnitude clears the 0.0062 three-seed noise floor.

RESULT, every switch with >= 2 scored pairs:

  calibrated_targets  +0.0072 (band_span_hold -> calib_span_hold)
                      +0.0061 (band_dense_hold -> calib_dense_hold)
                      -0.0020 (band_span      -> calib_span)
      NOT uniform. Both positives carry --hold-annotations; the one seat without it reads
      NEGATIVE. This independently reproduces the confound calibsix.sh already names at its
      lines 75-82 and deliberately declines to resolve. No new information, but it is now
      measured from the record rather than argued from three quoted pairs.

  intensity_aug off   +0.0077 (aug_long -> band_dense_long, 336px/20sl/24ep)
                      +0.0064 (intensity392_ws -> res392_ws, 448px/12sl/12ep)
      Uniform in sign, both above the noise floor, two genuinely distant seats. And worth
      ZERO: only 2 records in the whole corpus ever set intensity_aug=True, and both ARE this
      experiment. Every production seat already trains with it off. A closed negative, not an
      available lever.

  bf16 off            +0.0024 +0.0017 +0.0016 +0.0013 (4/4 positive)
      All four share one base seat (throughput_*), all four below the noise floor, and the
      owner has standing direction for bf16 training / fp16 serving. Not a lever.

  unfreeze_last 6->4  0/5 positive (-0.0062 .. -0.0073); 6->12 -0.0148. Settled at 6.
  slice_regions       0/4 positive. regions=4 loses to None/1 uniformly. Closed negative.
  slices 20->12/16    0/3 positive. Settled at 20.
  hold_annotations    2 pairs, both small and opposite-signed. Unresolved on its own.
  variant             7 pairs, 3 positive, mixed. v3base loses to both base and small.
  mixup               7 pairs, 2 positive, all |d| < 0.0070. Scatter.
  epochs, backbone_lr, encoder_weights  dominated by one huge pair each (a 1-epoch throughput
      probe, a 2e-4 divergence, a null-adapter). Not comparisons of settings.

CONSEQUENCE. There is no second uniform-lift flag on disk to stack. Every remaining candidate
would need a fresh matched pair ON CARD to price, which is the resource we do not have. The
+0.0133 offline that 0.950 now costs (see knee-ps8o: transfer is +0.83, not +1.72) has no
in-repo lever sized for it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR calibsix (knee-1c00). Priced honestly: 7.1 h for a pooled solo +0.0038 whose
only unconfounded pair reads -0.0020, times ~0.83 transfer = ~+0.003 board, against a 0.0062
noise floor. Odds of clearing the 1.5% bar: ~0. The arm that the RECORD supports is
--calibrated-targets WITH --hold-annotations (+0.0072 / +0.0061); calibsix declines that as
reassembly, which is a defensible choice about seat identity but leaves it running the one
configuration the data reads negative on. Not changing a 7.1 h arm unilaterally - flagged for
the owner.

Probe script was throwaway (job tmp). Not building uniform_lift.py: the record it would read
has now been read, and it says no.

title: MRNet is probably BARRED: host ruled against KneeCoT on the required-agreement mechanism
description:
Kaggle discussion topic 734109, host reply (read 2026-08-26 17:10Z via kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read --live --topic 734109):

  'After deliberation, we decided to not allow the use of KneeCoT dataset due to the required data
   agreement with dataset institution. In our interpretation of the rules, this can make the playing
   field uneven for participants who can complete the formal agreement to seek approval compared those
   that cannot. ... If the situation changes, for instance if the data use policy changes on HF, or if
   the data organizers communicate their intent differently, we may change our stance.'

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN ANY ARM. External data of a different KIND is the only lever this repo has
identified whose mechanism could plausibly deliver the +0.0133 offline that 0.950 now costs (see
knee-ps8o: the transfer coefficient is +0.74-0.83 in our regime, not +1.72). Every other open lever is
a knob worth <= +0.003 board. MRNet was that lever.

THE ARGUMENT THAT LOOKED SETTLED, AND IS NOT. Topic 733652 carries a participant who pulled the actual
rule text: 2.6(a) is a DISJUNCTION - External Data must be 'either publicly available and equally
accessible ... at no cost to the other Participants, or satisfies the Reasonableness criteria as
outlined in Section 2.6.b', and 2.6.b says 'the use of external data and models is acceptable unless
specifically prohibited by the Host'. On that plain reading MRNet/fastMRI+/OAI/SKM-TEA all clear, since
all are free and not geo-restricted. The 734109 ruling is the host SPECIFICALLY PROHIBITING on exactly
the axis 2.6.b reserves to them, and their stated reason is the AGREEMENT, not the cost and not the geo.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MIGHT STILL SAVE IT, stated honestly rather than hopefully. KneeCoT requires a
'formal ethical-use agreement with the affiliated hospital' and the host's own words are 'complete the
formal agreement TO SEEK APPROVAL'. MRNet is a click-through Research Use Agreement at
stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/mrnet/ - name/email/institution, immediate download link, no
approval step, no counter-signature, no institutional review. Whether the host's objection is to
'an agreement exists' or to 'approval can be withheld' decides MRNet, and nothing in the ruling settles
which.

WHAT TO DO, AND WHAT NOT TO DO.
  DO NOT accept the RUA or download the archive on the strength of the 2.6.b argument. The build path
    (build_mrnet --archive <path> --scheme mrnet, then build_merged --extra-scheme mrnet) stays unbuilt.
  DO NOT spend engineering on the MRNet ingest until a host answer exists. It is a multi-hour path whose
    permission is now actively in doubt.
  DO ask the host, in topic 733652 where the disjunction was raised, the narrow question: does a
    click-through RUA with no approval step fall under the 734109 reasoning, or only agreements where
    approval can be refused? Name MRNet, fastMRI+, OAI and SKM-TEA together - the host preferred a
    category answer over a per-dataset one in 733652 and said so.
  POSTING IS OUTWARD-FACING and needs owner sign-off; draft only.

BLOCKS: knee-w84q and every other queued arm is unaffected, but the 0.950 plan is now without a
plausibly-sized lever until this resolves. Say that plainly rather than substituting knobs for it.
notes:
DRAFT FORUM POST for topic 733652 — OWNER MUST POST IT; posting is outward-facing and I do not do that
unasked. Copy-paste as-is or edit. It deliberately asks a CATEGORY question, because the host said in
733652 they preferred that, and it cites their own 734109 ruling so they can answer inside their own
reasoning rather than re-deriving it.

---
Thanks for the KneeCoT ruling in #734109 — that answers the gated-HF case clearly. Could I ask for the
boundary, since the reasoning there seems to cover a much wider category than the one dataset?

The stated basis was "the required data agreement with dataset institution", because participants who
can "complete the formal agreement to seek approval" would be advantaged over those who cannot. That
reasoning turns on an approval step that can be refused. The other public knee-MRI corpora do not have
one:

- MRNet (Stanford) — a click-through research-use agreement: name, email, institution, and the download
  link is returned immediately. No counter-signature, no institutional review, nobody to refuse.
- fastMRI / fastMRI+ (NYU), the Osteoarthritis Initiative, and SKM-TEA — the same shape: free,
  not geo-restricted, registration and an agreement checkbox, no approval gate.

So the narrow question: does #734109's reasoning bar any dataset behind an agreement at all, or only
those where approval can be withheld? A category answer covering MRNet / fastMRI+ / OAI / SKM-TEA
together would settle #733652, #735497, #735121 and #734109 at once.

The reason it matters now rather than later: pretraining on an external corpus is a multi-hour
commitment and the deadline is 22 October, so teams are choosing whether to start on an unresolved
reading. If the answer is no, that is genuinely more useful said early than said in a winners' review.
---

WHY THIS IS WORTH A POST RATHER THAN A GUESS. The plain 2.6(a)-disjunction reading says yes; the 734109
ruling says the host reads 2.6.b restrictively on exactly this axis. Those cannot both govern MRNet.
Building the ingest on the optimistic reading risks the work; abandoning it on the pessimistic reading
discards the only lever sized for the goal (knee-ps8o prices 0.950 at +0.0133 offline; every in-repo
lever is <= +0.003 board). A forum question costs nothing and resolves the branch.

title: Forum sweep 2026-08-26: single models reach 0.942, and our model does not beat its teacher
description:
Zero-slot research sweep of the competition forum plus three of our own instruments, run while the card was busy with blendhold.

WHAT STANDS.

1. SINGLE-MODEL FRONTIER. Topic 735304 carries several independent single-model claims: 0.942 at 224px ('single model 0.934 @ 224px, update: 0.942 with some tweaks'), 0.938 single-model single-fold, 0.934, plus a cluster at 0.915-0.929. Our board single is 0.925 and our SIX-MEMBER ensemble is 0.939 -- so a claimed single model beats our whole ensemble. Unverified claims, per the owner's standing warning about notebook claims, but the efficiency-leaderboard argument underneath is structural rather than honesty-dependent: high-scoring entries have short runtimes, so they are not 20-model ensembles. This corroborates our own seat pricing (23% pass-through of a new member into a saturated pool) from the opposite direction: MEMBER QUALITY is the bottleneck and the combiner never was.

2. WE DO NOT BEAT OUR TEACHER. kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap on report_labels_v2 over 58 annotated studies / 696 cells: labels 0.8658, model 0.8392. A forum reply proposes exactly this diagnostic ('if your image model is not beating the label extractor teacher, there is likely modeling headroom'). By that rule the binding constraint for US is MODELING, not labels -- which is the opposite of the forum's own majority answer (most replies vote label quality). Per-finding the split is clean by structure type: the model beats the reader on the diffuse findings (Effusion +0.130, Contusion +0.089, Synovitis +0.051, Medial OA +0.042, Baker's +0.023, Fracture +0.016) and loses on the thin focal ones (Lateral Meniscus -0.193, ACL -0.123, MCL -0.096, Medial Meniscus -0.094, PF OA -0.086, Lateral OA -0.079). CAVEAT ON THE DENOMINATOR: the per-finding numbers rest on 58 studies where our own severity_boundary work prices the per-label standard error at 0.04-0.09, so the RANKING is weak evidence and only the aggregate and the coarse diffuse-vs-focal split should be quoted.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE QUEUE. calibsix and margin_calib are both label/target-side flags, aimed at the term this measurement says is not binding. It does NOT refute them -- their case is direct measurement (+0.0038 pooled solo, +0.0056 and +0.0084 ensembled on two nested pools), not a theory about which term binds -- but it lowers the prior on any FURTHER label-reader work, and it argues the next NEW arm should be model-side.

WHAT DIED, and all of it died on evidence already on disk at zero card cost.

3. BAND GEOMETRY, re-read on the right ruler. The band axis was closed on the 12-label macro, where a fix recovering all of Lateral Meniscus's headroom would show as +0.016 -- inside the 0.0062 floor, the 'metric averaging the effect away' failure. run_comparison prices band members per-label AND by structure scale, so the question was already answerable: Lateral Meniscus moves -0.0058 / +0.0007 / -0.0035 / +0.0036 across band_span, band_wide, band_full, band140 against half-widths of +/-0.03. band_full restores the ENTIRE band and Lateral Meniscus still reads -0.0035, so 'the 0.2-0.8 band deletes the lateral compartment' is refuted from the one direction that could refute it. Band axis stays closed, now on a ruler that could have seen the effect.

4. SIDE-BLINDNESS, rediscovered and already retired. side_blindness reads Lateral OA at 0.5184 [0.4364, 0.6014] -- indistinguishable from side-blind -- while Medial OA resolves at 0.7328 and both menisci resolve, with PF OA clean as a control. Both positional members are equally blind (through_dense 0.5092, depth_regions 0.5261), so no mechanism we own touches it. But interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-23_side_resolution_is_not_score.md settled this on 2026-08-22: side_dense moved the Lateral OA contrast +0.062 and the holdout mean -0.0641, with the term verified landed three ways. An AUC orders study-against-study within a label; the side term orders label-against-label within a study; the orderings are orthogonal and buying one costs the other. That doc explicitly retires the contrast as a selection instrument. My rediscovery adds nothing and cost twenty minutes that reading the interpretation first would have saved -- the second time in one session the ledger has caught a finding I was about to file.

5. TWO KNEES IN ONE DICOM (topic 735639, posted today). 7 studies of 4,407 = 0.16%. Not a lever. The laterality question underneath it is already handled: core/data/corpus/laterality.py normalises to a left-knee convention using a geometric rule covering 100% of the corpus where the DICOM tag covers 49.3%, it is consumed through study.py, and augmentation.py forbids horizontal flips precisely to protect it.

title: Residual ambiguity predicts seat value at r=+0.5 to +0.7 where distance predicts nothing
description:
A merit column that survives its own validation, and the first one here that does.

MEASURED 2026-08-26 16:26Z, zero card, zero slots. Fifteen members priced as seats against gradeswap_v1
(0.933, 7 members, fully scoreable) — experiments/logs/seat_fifteen.log. Correlated against the two
competing merit columns over the SAME TWELVE members, dropping cnx_dense (solo 0.7927) and raddino_dense
(0.8141) so that neither column is credited for spotting a member that is simply broken:

  residual ambiguity   r = +0.81
  distance (nearest)   r = -0.15

Residual ambiguity is the knee-qij2 quantity: pair-ambiguity above what the member's own solo quality
predicts, from a fit with slope -0.179 and r-squared 0.875 across fifteen members. Distance collapses the
moment the broken members leave, which is knee-bxp2 confirmed and GENERALISED — its apparent predictive
power was the weakness confound all along, across families and not merely within one.

The rankings agree end to end. Seat value, best swap, against residual:
  merged_blend        +0.0014   resid +1.63   ALREADY SEATED
  blendlabels         +0.0011   resid +1.70   NOT SEATED IN blendseat OR gradeswap
  crop80_span         +0.0004   resid +1.58   not seated
  calibrated_targets  +0.0003   resid +1.11
  vjepa_warm          +0.0001   resid +1.02
  band_span           +0.0001   resid -0.10
  depth_regions       +0.0001   resid -1.38
  band_wide           +0.0000   resid -0.41
  band140             -0.0000   resid -0.81
  severity_weight     -0.0004   resid -2.47
  v3base_dense        -0.0005   resid -0.57
  band_full           -0.0006   resid -0.67
  raddino_dense       -0.0012
  cnx_dense           -0.0025

THREE CONSEQUENCES:
1. blendlabels is the highest-value UNSEATED member we hold and it is free to add.
2. Both top-two are LABEL-TABLE members. That is independent confirmation of calibsix's bet (knee-1c00)
   from a ruler built to answer a different question.
3. The three most DISTANT candidates are the three worst seats. Buy-the-distant-member is closed with a
   named mechanism rather than a shrug.

LIMITS, BEFORE THEY ARE ASKED. n=12. Every one of the fourteen seat values sits inside +/-0.0015, the bar
under which this ruler has never been shown to pick a board tick, so the correlation runs over quantities
the ruler cannot resolve ONE AT A TIME — it is a statement about ordering, not about any single seat.
And there is PLAUSIBLE CIRCULARITY: the residual was fitted on pairs with band_dense, and band_dense sits
in the roster the seats are priced against. Different pool and different combine rule, so partial rather
than total, but real. A second anchor costs nothing and settles it, and that is the next step here.
notes: CORRECTION, second anchor completed 2026-08-26T16:36Z. The three stragglers landed (severity_weight, v3base_dense, vjepa_warm) and they move the number DOWN. Residual-ambiguity vs seat value on anchor band_span, three nestings: n=8 (pre-stragglers) slope -0.156, r=+0.82 | n=11 all comparable, slope -0.198, r=+0.66 | n=10 strict (solo >= 0.84), slope -0.091, r=+0.52. vjepa_warm is the cause: solo 0.8337, residual +14.9, seat +1 -- a big residual with no seat. It sits between the broken members (cnx_dense 0.7927, raddino_dense 0.8141) and the comparable band (0.84-0.86), so it survives the cut while behaving like a leverage point, the same pathology that dropped r to +0.35 when the broken pair was restored. severity_weight disagrees mildly (residual +2.7, seat -4); v3base_dense agrees (-5.6 vs -5). CLAIM AS CORRECTED: the merit column is positive under every nesting and merged_blend + blendlabels rank top-two in all three, so the ORDERING replicates and is what licenses calibsix. The STRENGTH does not: quote '+0.5 to +0.7, sensitive to where weak members are cut off', never '+0.82'. SECOND FINDING, against my own earlier note: on the strict band the ambiguity-on-solo slope is only -0.091 versus anchor-1's -0.179, so 'ambiguity is mostly member weakness' (experiments/README.md, commit ef80bc1) is itself carried by the weak members. Among members that work, solo quality explains much less of ambiguity than that section states. It does not overturn knee-qij2 -- no axis group separated there either, and that conclusion was drawn over the full set -- but the slope quoted there needs this caveat attached.

title: Which AXIS of member difference buys ambiguity? (pre-registered, zero card)
description:
MOTIVATION. calibsix's measurement (knee-1c00) found --calibrated-targets buys +0.0018 of AMBIGUITY, not
just quality — calibrated members disagree with each other more than their uncalibrated twins do. That is
the first diversity this ledger has obtained from a lever that was never asked for diversity. Every lever
that WAS asked (dissent_seat's negative-correlation loss, -0.0008; the architecture axis, closed three
measurements deep) returned a twin or nothing.

THE QUESTION. Is that a property of calibration, or of the LABEL TABLE AXIS? If members that differ in
what they were TAUGHT are systematically more ambiguous than members that differ in how they DECODE or in
what BACKBONE they use, then roster selection has been asking the wrong question. We have been picking by
distance (knee-bxp2: anticorrelated with seat value within a family) and by quality (23% pass-through into
a saturated pool). Neither is an axis. This would be one.

THE MEASUREMENT, free, no card, over records already on disk. Anchor band_dense (settled geometry, plain
labels). For each of ~20 members pair it with the anchor and compute

    ambiguity = pair_ensemble - mean(solo_anchor, solo_member)

grouped by which axis the member differs from the anchor on:
  LABEL       calibrated_targets blendlabels merged_blend severity_weight report03 report10
  GEOMETRY    band_span band_wide band_full band140 max12 max20 depth_regions crop80_span
  ARCHITECTURE cnx_dense dinov3_v3small v3base_dense base_dense raddino_dense vjepa_warm

PRE-REGISTRATION, written before the numbers are read:
  LABEL mean ambiguity exceeds GEOMETRY mean by >= 0.0015, with the group intervals not overlapping
      -> THE AXIS IS REAL. Roster selection should spend seats on label-table variety, and calibsix is a
         special case of a general rule rather than one lucky flag. Next arm is a roster built one member
         per TABLE at a fixed geometry.
  LABEL exceeds GEOMETRY by 0 to 0.0015, or intervals overlap
      -> DIRECTIONAL ONLY. Keep it free, do not plan around it, do not spend a slot on it. This is the
         likeliest outcome: the ambiguity deltas being compared are ~0.002 against a 0.0062 floor.
  ARCHITECTURE is the largest group
      -> THE ARCHITECTURE AXIS WAS CLOSED ON THE WRONG RULER. It was closed on seat value and board score,
         both quality rulers. That would not reopen it as a route (raddino_dense -0.0371, vjepa_warm solo
         0.8337 — the members are too weak to seat regardless), but it would say the CLOSURE ARGUMENT was
         about member quality and not about diversity, which is a different sentence than the ledger
         currently carries.
  no group separates
      -> ambiguity is a property of the member pair and not of any axis, and calibration's +0.0018 is one
         pair's scatter. That would weaken calibsix's mechanism story to a coincidence, though not the
         arm itself, whose prediction is already priced at pass-through 1.0 with ambiguity discarded.

WHAT IT CANNOT SAY. Every pair here shares one anchor, so these are not independent observations — they
are 20 readings of band_dense's neighbourhood, and a group difference could be a fact about the anchor.
The honest follow-up if a group separates is a second anchor on a different geometry, which is also free.
Solo deltas in the source measurement were all inside the 0.0062 floor, and these ambiguity numbers are
smaller still.

PRICE: zero card, zero submission slots, ~4 minutes of wall-clock in a gap where the card is busy with
ema_dense. It cannot fail expensively.
P(clears the >= 0.0015 separation bar) ~ 0.3 — the quantities are a third of the noise floor, and the
only reason to expect separation at all is one measured pair plus a mechanism argument.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-08-26 16:2xZ. Outcome: NO GROUP SEPARATES, and the confound is the finding.

15 usable members (report03, report10, max12, max20, dinov3_v3small carry no holdout record and were
dropped — their 'pair' reads 0.8578, the anchor alone).

RAW ambiguity = pair - mean(solo_anchor, solo_member), anchor band_dense 0.8578:
  ARCHITECTURE  +0.0121  (cnx_dense .01765, raddino .01525, vjepa .01205, v3base .00835, base .00730)
  LABEL         +0.0079  (calibrated_targets .00935, blendlabels .00915, merged_blend .00815, severity .00510)
  GEOMETRY      +0.0071  (crop80_span .01030, band_full .00875, band_span .00685, band_wide .00675,
                          band140 .00630, depth_regions .00585)

Read raw, that is pre-registered outcome 3 (architecture largest). IT IS A CONFOUND, NOT AN AXIS.
Ambiguity regressed on the member's own solo over all 15: slope -0.179 ambiguity per unit solo,
**r-squared 0.875**. Eighty-eight percent of the ambiguity variance is HOW WEAK THE SECOND MEMBER IS. The
architecture group IS the weak group — cnx_dense 0.7927, raddino 0.8141, vjepa 0.8337 are the three
worst members in the whole set and they hold the three largest ambiguities.

RESIDUALS after removing the quality trend:
  LABEL        +0.00049   (blendlabels +0.0017, merged_blend +0.0016, calibrated +0.0011, severity -0.0025)
  ARCHITECTURE -0.00004
  GEOMETRY     -0.00030
LABEL over GEOMETRY is +0.00079, HALF the pre-registered 0.0015 bar, with one of four label members
strongly the wrong way. Pre-registration says DIRECTIONAL ONLY: keep it free, do not plan around it, do
not spend a slot on it. The axis is not real at this resolution.

WHAT IS REAL, AND IT IS THE GENERAL RESULT: ambiguity is not a currency that can be shopped for. It is
mostly a restatement of the candidate's weakness, which is why every 'pick the distant member' rule this
project has tried (knee-bxp2's distance column, dissent_seat's decorrelation loss) has failed on the
board — they were all buying error and calling it diversity.

IT STRENGTHENS calibsix (knee-1c00) RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. Calibrated members are BETTER solo (+0.0038),
so this fit predicts their ambiguity should FALL by 0.179 x 0.0038 = -0.00067. It ROSE +0.00184. The
calibration ambiguity gain runs AGAINST the confound, so quality-adjusted it is +0.0025, not +0.0018 —
the one lever measured here that buys disagreement without buying error. Caveat: the slope is fitted on
band_dense pairs and the trio is a different pool, so cross-applying it is approximate.

LIMIT, as pre-registered: all 20 pairs share one anchor. These are 15 readings of band_dense's
neighbourhood, not of the corpus. A second anchor is free and is the honest follow-up if this is ever
leaned on.

title: calibsix — lift five champion seats with --calibrated-targets (the uniform-lift arm)
description:
Seat pricing 2026-08-26 measured two DIFFERENT pass-through numbers, both real:

  marginal new member into a saturated pool   23%   (calib_dense_hold +0.0056 solo -> +0.0013 seat)
  uniform lift of every member                92%   (measured, three matched pairs, zero card)

The uniform-lift A/B:
  calibrated trio   (calib_dense_hold + calib_span_hold + calib_span)   0.8685
  uncalibrated twins(band_dense_hold  + band_span_hold  + band_span )   0.8629
                                                             delta     +0.0056
  mean solo delta of the same flag at the same corners                 +0.0061

No contradiction: ensemble error = mean member error - ambiguity. A uniform lift moves the first term
and leaves ambiguity alone; a single better-but-redundant member moves both and they cancel.

THE ARM: experiments/arms/calibsix.sh — the champion's five uncalibrated seats (final_ws_e12,
grade_ladder_ff, through_dense_ff, lr4e-5_ws_ff, merged_blend) each refitted with exactly one added
flag, --calibrated-targets. calib_span_ff is the sixth seat and already carries it. Each recipe copied
VERBATIM from its own arm per final_fit_six.sh's rule (a reassembly is a configuration nobody ran, and
--fold -1 leaves no holdout to catch it). Distinct _cf suffix so no seated fold-0 original is
overwritten.

--calibrated-targets and --grade-ladder compose: checked, not assumed. grade_ladder is an OBJECTIVE
policy (thresholds subtracted inside the loss); calibrated_targets is a TARGETS policy
(core/data/labels/targets.py). Different pipeline stages.

PREDICTION: 5 seats x 0.92 x +0.0061 = +0.0047 offline; x board_transfer +1.72 = +0.0081 board;
champion blendseat 0.939 -> 0.947. Not 0.950 alone. margin_calib's seat (knee-myl0) is the arm that
would carry the rest.

READOUT IS BOARD-ONLY for four of five (--fold -1 has seen every holdout study). merged_blend_cf stays
fold-0 like its original and is the ONLY offline read: score it against merged_blend_s2026 0.8587 via
convergence_check first. If that one seat reads NEGATIVE, do not ship — it is the only evidence that
the flag transfers to corners outside the two it was measured at.

RISKS, named before the card: (1) the flag was measured at two corners only; seats four and five sit at
0.2-0.8/12 slices and seat five trains on the merged corpus, so transfer there is assumed. (2)
blendthree swapped three seats for better-SUPERVISED twins and read 0.939 dead flat — nearest
precedent, returned nothing; defence is size not kind (+0.0034 at three seats vs +0.0061 at five). If
calibsix also reads flat, the uniform-lift route is refuted at the operating point and the ensemble
axis closes for good. (3) it needs a submission slot to read at all.

PRICE: ~7.1 h of otherwise-idle overnight card (five 12-epoch 336px fits, ~425 s/epoch over 4406
studies), ZERO submission slots to produce, one slot to read. Runs after margin_calib.
P(clears +0.004 offline / a board tick over 0.939) ~ 0.45 — the mechanism is measured rather than
argued, but blendthree is a flat precedent at the same operating point.

SLOT DISCIPLINE: slot 5 of 2026-08-26 is HELD by owner directive (knee-pubw). This ships no earlier
than 2026-08-27 and the owner is ASKED before it is spent.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-26 16:0xZ, before the card was spent. The 92% pass-through in this bead's
description is wrong and so is its +0.0061 mean. '+0.0061' is the DENSE pair alone, generalised to
three pairs by nobody but me — the denominator failure CLAUDE.md names. experiments/README.md:318
already recorded calib_span at -0.0020 vs band_span, which that mean silently absorbed.

All six re-scored solo over the same 909 shared studies:
  dense, hold     0.8634 / 0.8573   +0.0061
  span,  hold     0.8565 / 0.8493   +0.0072
  span,  no hold  0.8545 / 0.8565   -0.0020
                          MEAN      +0.0038

Ensembled, two nested pools:

  --calibrated-targets              buys QUALITY (+0.0061 at this exact corner, replicated in sign at calib_span)

interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_architecture_diversity_is_closed_and_the_empty_cell_is_strong_and_distant.md

the mechanism has fired; the risk is that calibrated targets and an AUC margin are the SAME lever wearing
two names -- both reshape which studies the loss cares about -- and the distance collapses to
calib_dense_hold's 0.9273. That failure mode is the informative one and is why the read below is the
nearest-neighbour column, not the solo.

  seat >= +0.0018 and nearest <= 0.90   the cell is occupied. Both terms compose; the next arms are more
                                        members built this way, and member-quality arms stop.
  seat >= +0.0015, nearest 0.90-0.93    it seats, but on quality not distance. Directional, keep it free,

  seat <  +0.0015, nearest >= 0.92      SAME LEVER. Calibration and the margin are one axis; that CLOSES

  solo <  0.8525                        suspect the harness before the mechanism: both terms measured
                                        positive alone at this corner, so a fall below the weaker one is a

  margin_seat        0.8525  (the margin term alone, no hold)
  calib_dense_hold   0.8634  (the calibration term alone, with hold)
  band_dense_hold    0.8573  (neither term, with hold -- the free reusable control)

  less the -0.0005 hold price margin_seat does not carry = 0.8581.

Seat -0.0013 [-0.0021, -0.0005] against gradeswap_v1 — negative with a band excluding zero. Distance nearest 0.8298, the most distant candidate ever priced here.

THE ARITHMETIC, stated before the arm:
  calib   +0.0061  (calib_dense_hold 0.8634 vs band_dense_hold 0.8573; replicated at a
                    second corner by knee-bs4l, +0.0072 proxy / +0.0129 annotated)
  EMA     +0.003   (competitor single-variable ablation, research/2026-08-26_the-ablation-

our own measured terms plus the two of theirs that our own harness already reproduces in sign
and size (mixup +0.0015 vs +0.002).

targets say, EMA changes which weights are kept, mixup changes what the inputs are.

under the floor, so a null is the modal single-seed outcome and the reading is DIRECTIONAL.
Its value is the SUM against band_dense, not the increment against its own control.

  observed  = 0.8631  ->  -0.0013 vs predicted, -0.0003 vs the control.

WHAT IT DID SETTLE. The negative branches are far from the null and are refuted:
