title: The four internal-derangement structures are model-bottlenecked; resolution and slot coverage both eliminated
description:
supervision_gap on 58 gold studies: aggregate model 0.8392 BELOW its teacher labels 0.8658, so by the field's own rule (735826) we have MODELLING headroom, not a label ceiling. Split is structured: ACL, MCL, medial and lateral meniscus are 4 of 4 on the deficit side, carrying four of the five highest report-label AUCs. Six deficit findings sum to -0.049 macro.

Two explanations tested and refuted the same day, both by run_comparison's built-in structure-scale grouping:
- in-plane resolution (336 vs 224, native224 pair): focal -0.0035, explicit REFUTED verdict
- slot coverage (extended vs canonical, +1139 coronal series incl. a standard meniscus sequence): focal -0.0029, and three of the four internal-derangement findings go NEGATIVE

Aggregation was already closed from both ends (knee-ezz slice count -0.0001; three pooling operators span 0.0019), and encoder scale is null twice (base224 +0.0007, competitor 735154 +0.0011).

CAVEAT THAT BOUNDS EVERYTHING: these are the PUBLISHED members' out-of-fold predictions. Ours are fitted with the annotated studies upweighted and would be scoring training data. So this prices the public baseline's deficit and ASSUMES ours shares its shape. n=58, per-label SE 0.04-0.09, so no single row is a finding — the 4-of-4 structure is the claim.

NEXT, and it costs no card: get predictions from a member fitted WITHOUT annotation upweighting and re-run supervision_gap on ours, to test whether our members share the deficit shape. Every number here rests on that assumption.

interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_the-focal-deficit.md
notes:
SUPERSEDED 2026-08-25 20:45Z by a measurement. This bead closed the instrument as UNDELIVERABLE ('Do not re-attempt') on the grounds that covering the 58 annotated studies out of fold needs four more folds, which are banned. That reasoning was about the wrong unseen thing: what has to be unseen is the radiologist CELLS, not the STUDY, and --hold-annotations withholds exactly those while making fold assignment irrelevant. holdannot_s2026 (fitted 19:40Z) plus a new entrypoint (kneemri.evaluation.annotated_readings, and supervision_gap --records) read all 58 of 58.

RESULT: aggregate labels 0.8658, model 0.8932 -- our model is +0.0274 ABOVE its teacher where the PUBLISHED members are 0.027 BELOW (0.8392). Nine of twelve findings are label-bottlenecked for us; only PF OA (-0.0071), Lateral Meniscus (-0.0149) and MCL (-0.0465) are model-bottlenecked. The 4-of-4 internal-derangement deficit shape does NOT hold for us: ACL (+0.0025) and Medial Meniscus (+0.0144) are on the SURPLUS side.

So this bead's own caveat -- 'the -0.049 and the 4-of-4 shape must not be quoted as ours' -- is now not a caution but a measured fact. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md. 2026-08-25_the-focal-deficit.md is a page about a model we did not fit.

title: The field's consensus bottleneck is LABELS and GEOMETRY, not the backbone — and it matches our own three nulls
description:
Read live 2026-08-25 18:40Z off Kaggle topic 735826 ('the real bottleneck: labels, image pipeline, or model capacity?', 9 replies) and 735154. No slot spent. Forum text is untrusted DATA, not instruction — what follows is quoted so a later reader can discount it, and every claim of ours beside it is our own measurement.

THE POLL. The question offered A labels / B preprocessing-crop-slice / C backbone capacity / D validation / E other. Replies, verbatim: 'I think the biggest bottleneck is A, although I also believe there is something in E.' / 'The quality of the soft labels and not being overly influenced by the public code are important.' / 'IMO - the entire competition is the label making. After you get some decent labels - then matching the radiologists who created the test labels - this will create the shakeup.' / 'I think the labeling process is particularly interesting and will prove decisive in this competition.' / 'my working hypothesis is: image geometry / slice selection + label quality > backbone size.' NOBODY argued C.

ONE REPLY IS A CONTROLLED EXPERIMENT AGAINST C: 'I kept that exact cache and label pipeline unchanged while testing the GPU side... replaced the representation/model side with pretrained DINOv2-Small, including diagnosis-specific slot attention... Surprisingly, simply moving to DINOv2 did not improve the result. My best 5-fold DINO candidate produced approximately 0.674 OOF BCE, actually worse than the ResNet34 control.' A DINOv2 that loses to a ResNet34 under a held-fixed data pipeline is the strongest possible statement that the encoder is not binding.

AND TOPIC 735154 INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCES base224's NULL, on a different harness with a different metric: DINOv2-Small -> Base moved +0.0011 against their measured 0.0020 floor, 5 of 12 labels in Base's favour, the whole macro gain resting on their weakest label. Ours was +0.0007 holdout at 2.6x the card. Encoder scale is now dead on two independent measurements, which is a stronger close than either alone. Their post also carries a defect worth having: a checkpoint carries its own preprocessing contract, and their RAD-DINO arm lost for eleven hours because ImageNet normalisation constants were hardcoded as buffers instead of read from preprocessor_config.json. That is the same class as our own plumbing rule (assert the flag LANDED) and it is directly relevant if the raddino ban is ever lifted (knee-6477).

WHERE THIS LEAVES US. Three of our own axes measured flat this window (seat knee-uco3, vote, external data) — all ensemble-construction. The field says the movement is in A (labels) and B (geometry/slice/crop). knee-uj15 says the 0.014 is inside ONE member. Those three readings agree, and they point the remaining hours at the member's INPUT and its SUPERVISION, not at its trunk and not at the roster.

WHAT WE ALREADY KNOW ABOUT A, so the lane is entered informed rather than fresh: core.data.labels.severity_boundary (2026-08-25) reads the 58 gold annotations against the competition's own stated moderate-or-above threshold and finds 7 of 28 readable English annotations contradict it — six small effusions annotated 1, one moderate annotated 0. The size word is not even monotone in the gold class (small 50% positive, moderate-or-larger 67%, unqualified mention 86%). That RETIRES 'parse the reports better for Effusion' — a better extractor recovers wording, and the wording is what disagrees with the truth. Two competitors report the same defect from the other direction in 735826. So the label lane is NOT 'improve the reader'; it is 'the map from adjective to annotation', which is an IMAGE question wearing a text question's clothes.

NEXT, unarmed and unpriced until the card frees (biohub holds it): blendlabels is the only supervision axis not yet shown flat and it is ~20 min. Everything on the B axis (crop geometry, physical slice ordering, stack-end removal) is untouched by us and is what the one competitor who named a mechanism says paid them +0.0059 across 10 of 12 labels — 'that is what a real effect looks like'.
notes:
CORRECTION, 18:47Z, same hour as filing. The description's closing line said the B (geometry) lane is untouched by us. That is FALSE and I wrote it from a forum post without opening our own tree — the exact inversion of audit-before-planning.

All four steps that competitor lists as their NEXT experiment shipped here on 2026-08-11: fixed-mm physical crop (slot.crop_mm, 130 mm, core/data/corpus/study.py:58), physical slice ordering by k = p.n-hat from ImagePositionPatient/ImageOrientationPatient (slot_geometry.py), stack-end removal (Band 0.1-0.9, it is in the cache FILENAME), and slice grouping audits (crop_coverage, crop_alignment, crop_laterality). The 130 mm constant was validated on our own corpus rather than borrowed: FOV median 160 mm, 1st percentile 130 mm, only 0.43% of series narrower than the crop.

WHAT THAT CHANGES. Their +0.0059 across 10 of 12 labels is a gain TOWARD where we already stand, not a lever above us. It prices the distance between a public-notebook pipeline and ours, and it means the 0.942 single model is beating our 0.938 seven-member ensemble FROM A GEOMETRY FLOOR WE ALREADY SHARE. So B is not the opening. The weight goes back on A, and on whatever 'some tweaks' covers in a recipe we cannot see.

ONE LIVE THREAD SURVIVES THE AUDIT: laterality is absent on 50.7% of series and not at random — Siemens 84.3% tagged, Philips 38.3%, GE/Toshiba/Canon 0.0%. That is the detection half of knee-bduq, it is already half-built in crop_laterality.py, and mirror-to-canonical is an augmentation that costs neither card nor corpus.

title: Distance is anticorrelated with seat value WITHIN a family - it is a twin detector, never a merit column
description:
Measured 2026-08-25 18:35Z, pricing the whole 224 family against gradeswap_v1 (0.933, 7/7 scoreable) in one call.

  candidate                     seat value   nearest
  dinov3_v3small_224_s2026        -0.0017     0.7936
  lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026       -0.0010     0.8159
  base224_s2026                   +0.0007     0.8679
  native224_s2026                 +0.0002     0.8946

Monotone, and in the WRONG direction for anyone reading distance as merit: across four candidates the
more distant the member, the more it COSTS the mix. Four points, one family, so it is a lean rather
than a law - but the mechanism is not subtle and it is the one that generalises.

WHY: distance is confounded with quality. A weak member is distant BECAUSE its predictions are noisy,
and noise is maximally uncorrelated with everything. A rank-distance column cannot tell orthogonal
SIGNAL from orthogonal NOISE, and those two have opposite value. The seated members' own spread says
the same thing from the other side: every seat sits at 0.88-0.92 to its nearest, i.e. the board's best
roster is built from members that are neither twins nor strangers.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is a correction to what I had already written into the slot plan (knee-5clp).
I had argued slot 1 as a DISTANCE bet - base224's 0.8679 being below every seated member's nearest.
That argument is void. Distance's real job is the one seat_value's own doc gives it: a TWIN DETECTOR,
which is how the 2026-08-22 split was called (band_span priced +0.0002 and cost a tick because it was a
near-twin of a seated member, and a rank average cannot charge for contributing one ordering twice).
It vetoes a candidate that is too CLOSE. It does not endorse one that is far.

So the usable rule is a BAND, not a maximum: a candidate wants positive seat value AND a nearest inside
roughly 0.86-0.92. base224 is the only member of the 224 family that satisfies both, which is why it
stays the slot-1 candidate - on being best on both columns at once, not on being far.

This also retires an idea worth naming before it comes back: shipping dinov3_v3small_224 for its 0.7936
would have been the single most distant member we have ever measured and the worst seat value in the
family.

title: Full-fit premium: +0.003 across five conversions, 0.000 at the marginal seat — and the 7th seat is inert
description:
Filed first as a shipping rule ('refit any new member at --fold -1 before it ships'). The ledger already refutes the marginal-seat half of it, and I filed before reading it. Corrected reading:

WHAT IS TRUE. finalfit_v1 0.934 -> allfit_v1 0.937 is the same seven members with FIVE swapped fold-0 -> _ff. +0.003. Mechanism checks out: fold-0 trains on 80% of the corpus, _ff on 100% (1.25x), and half_data measured the data slope at ~0.020 per 2x, which log-scales to ~0.006 per member, diluted over seven and applied to five.

WHAT IS FALSE, AND MEASURED FALSE. The marginal member's conversion buys NOTHING:

  lastseat_v1  0.937   6 dark + small_batch6_s2026   (fold-0)
  dark7_v1     0.937   6 dark + small_batch6_ff      (SAME member, --fold -1)

One flag moved, board identical. small_batch6_ff.sh pre-registered exactly this ('FLAT -> the dose curve is saturated at six, which retires the whole full-fit axis') and the board returned FLAT. So the axis is CLOSED, by its own pre-registration, and a 70-minute _ff refit of a new member is not worth a minute of card.

THE BIGGER THING THIS SURFACED, which is the one that should shape the 00:00 plan. The seventh seat is INERT no matter what fills it:

  dark6_v1    0.937   the six dark members
  dark7_v1    0.937   + small_batch6_ff      (the best member this project owns, 0.8598)
  lastseat_v1 0.937   + small_batch6_s2026
  farseat_v1  0.937   + vjepa_warm_s2026     (the most distant member available)
  augseat_v1  0.936   + aug_long_s2026
  allfit_v1   0.937   + band_dense_long_s2026

Six rosters, five different seventh members spanning best-quality to most-distant, one tick of spread. ADDING a member to the dark six does not move this board. Only votefit_v1 (0.938) sits above them, and it moved the FUSION, not the roster.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE 00:00 SLOTS. Do not spend a slot adding base224/band224/blendlabels as a seventh seat — that move is measured inert six times. A new member is worth a slot only as a SWAP into the six, or alongside a fusion change. And price the swap against gradeswap_v1 (knee-q40e), never against votefit, which prices nothing.
notes:
2026-08-26 07:05Z — THE PRICE OF THE FULL-FIT PREMIUM HAS GONE UP, without the premium changing.

What the conversion bought: +0.003 board across five conversions, 0.000 at the marginal seat. Below the
0.0062 paired noise floor either way — directional at best.

What it cost, stated now that it binds: the champion roster is SIX full-fit members plus final_ws_e12,
and blendsix's own arm log names five of them unscoreable — 'calib_span_ff, final_ws_e12,
grade_ladder_ff, lr4e-5_ws_ff, through_dense_ff'. The ledger's denominator note (README:2800) was
written when ONE member was unscoreable and six were not. That has inverted. seat_value, member_distance
and every other offline instrument now read approximately NOTHING about the shipped entry.

WHY THAT IS EXPENSIVE TODAY AND WAS NOT IN AUGUST. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_what-0950-actually-costs.md
shows the plan forks on one unmeasured quantity: the ensemble bonus is +0.011..+0.014 on the two clean
pairings and +0.005..+0.026 on the loose ones. At the low end the ensemble axis is spent and only member
quality matters; at the high end a 0.924 single reaches 0.950 with no member improvement at all. Those
are two different projects and we cannot tell them apart OFFLINE — because the roster is full-fit. So a
+0.003 premium is now being paid for with the only instrument that could settle a fork worth a full slot.

NOT A CALL TO REVERT. It is an argument that any NEW member should keep a fold-0 counterpart, so the
diversity axis stays measurable while the shipped seat stays full-fit. Cheapest place to apply it is
knee-fh31 (RAD-DINO), which already reads on fold 0 by design.

title: Price new members against gradeswap_v1 (0.933, 7/7 scoreable) — the board's whole top is unpriceable
description:
seat_value refuses against the pinned champion votefit_v1: 0 of its 6 members carry a holdout record, because all six are '_ff' (fitted at --fold -1, having seen every holdout study). A survey of every ensemble row in comp/board.jsonl shows the refusal is structural, not incidental:

  8/8 scoreable  0.932  peak8_v1
  7/7 scoreable  0.933  gradeswap_v1, accumseat_v1, greedy7_v1     <- the highest FULLY priceable entries
  7/7 scoreable  0.932  sevenplane_v1
  7/7 scoreable  0.931  sevengrade_v1
  6/7 scoreable  0.934  finalfit_v1      (missing final_ws_e12 only)
  1/7 scoreable  0.937  allfit_v1, lastseat_v1, farseat_v1

Use --against gradeswap_v1 for any candidate (base224, band224, blendlabels): 7/7, top of the priceable range, and its members are the same fold-0 family every new arm is trained in, so the mix arithmetic is like-for-like.

The refusal now NAMES these itself — PriceableEntries.suggestion in kneemri/kaggle/seat_value.py appends the top three fully-scoreable entries to the 'price against a scoreable entry instead' line, which was a placeholder the caller could not fill without doing this survey by hand.

Do NOT read the 0.933-vs-0.938 difference as a quality gap between rosters. It is the full-fit premium (+0.003 matched, knee-97ib) plus the vote-fusion tick (+0.001, dark6 -> votefit).

CORRECTION: this bead first named sevengrade_v1 (0.931) as the top priceable entry. That came from reading my own survey through 'tail -30', which cut its head off — the six entries above it were in the output and not on the screen. The tool now prints the answer so no reading of a truncated pipe stands between the question and it.

title: Slot plan for the 00:00 UTC window (5 slots, spread)
description:
Today's five are spent (grep -c '"date": "2026-08-25"' comp/board.jsonl = 5). Plan for the next reset, revised 2026-08-25T17:10Z after the forum read and the board audit.

WHAT IS RETIRED. 'Board one member alone' is gone: solo_v4 already scored 0.914 with one whole-stack member (2026-08-17), solotop_v1 0.925 with four. The solo->ensemble lift is a measured +0.024, not an open question.

THE HONEST FRAME. quarter_data's concave data slope leaves no lever on the board priced above 1.5%, our solo sits at the field's stated single-model level (0.91-0.92), and a seat swap buys about +0.001 board. votefit is 0.938; the leader is 0.952. THE ORDER.

title: dinov2-base at 224: the encoder axis re-asked with the batch handicap removed
description: base_dense read 0.8512 vs band_dense 0.8578 (-0.0066) and was recorded as an ENCODER reading, but it carried a forced --batch 6 (336px x 20 slices needs 56.3 GB) and small's unrescaled rate. native224 shows the pixel axis is flat at this geometry (0.8502 vs 0.8525) at 0.44 the patches, so base fits the control's own batch of 12 for the first time. One variable against native224: --variant base. Pre-registered bands in experiments/arms/base224.sh. Smoke with --studies 60 --epochs 1 before queueing to price the epoch.
notes:
RESULT 2026-08-25 18:27Z, 12/12 epochs, ARM DONE (not truncated; best epoch 9).

QUALITY NULL. base224_s2026 = 0.8509 holdout. Control native224 = 0.8502. +0.0007, an order of
magnitude under the 0.015 noise floor and under the 0.0015 the board resolves. The arm existed to
re-ask encoder scale with the batch handicap removed - earlier dinov2-base runs at higher resolution
were starved on batch. Handicap removed (batch 12, 14.0 GB allocated of a 17 GB gate), the axis still

The flag landed: config variant=base, and the 277s first epoch against small's ~150s confirms the
bigger trunk actually ran. This is a reading about the axis, not about a mis-set arm.

DIVERSITY IS THE FINDING. Priced --against gradeswap_v1 (0.933, 7/7 scoreable): +0.0007 as an add,
+0.0008 as a swap for lr4e-5_ws, both under +0.0015. But its nearest-neighbour correlation to that

It is the most distant member we have ever measured against this roster.

The two columns therefore disagree, which is the pair seat_value was built to surface: on 2026-08-22
lr4e-5_ws priced -0.0003 here and took 0.931 while band_span priced +0.0002 and cost a tick, and
distance was the column that ordered them the way the board did. n=1, so this is a lean, not a law.

Closes the encoder-scale half of knee-w84q. The sampling half (band224) is untouched.

title: Our label table is not worse — it is COARSER; tie mass explains the whole supervision gap
description:
Measured on kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap against the 58 radiologist-annotated studies.

  ours report_labels_v2         0.8658   5 distinct levels, tie-pair mass 0.385
  stevenleehans llm_v4_blend    0.8927  85 distinct levels, tie-pair mass 0.173
  steven QUANTISED to our 5     0.8445  <-- the control that reframes everything
  flight0234 v4hybrid           0.8991  (same distribution as steven v4_blend + __conf cols; NOT an independent reader)
  lixin73 gpt56sol              0.8352

At EQUAL resolution our reader BEATS theirs by +0.021. The 0.027 gap read earlier as supervision
quality is a scale-resolution artifact: AUC punishes ties, and our five MEASURED_AGREEMENT levels
create 38.5% tie mass against their 17.3%.

Breaking the ties recovers nearly all of it, and the weight does not matter:
  ours + w*(steven-0.5), w in {0.02,0.05,0.10}   0.8874   (0.25 -> 0.8872)
  mean(ours, steven)                             0.8885
  mean(ours, steven, lixin)                      0.8912
w-invariance is the mechanism proof: AUC is rank-based, so any small w yields the same ordering.
The +0.0216 is purely TIE-BREAKING, not reweighting.

HONEST LIMIT: blend_three 0.8912 does NOT beat steven alone 0.8927. The variance-reduction argument
predicts blend > best single and it does not hold here. On 58 studies / ~696 cells that difference is
inside its own sampling interval, which has not been computed. Do not quote any of these as separated.

THREE TABLES SCORE 1.0000 AND THAT IS LEAKAGE, NOT QUALITY: yunusgmsoy report_labels_v5,
gxpixel train_labels_final (ships gold_58.csv and an is_gold column), rayanbabur train_targets_soft
(ships gold_benchmark_58.csv). Anyone ranking public tables against the gold set is fooled by them.

WHAT THIS LICENSES. Not 'download a better table' — that lever is smaller than it looked. The claim is
that a 5-level BCE target carries less ordering information into the gradient than an 85-level one,
which is a TRAINING argument the gold ruler cannot settle. The arm that settles it trains the canonical
recipe on the blended table and is scored with --eval-labels pinned to report_labels_v2, because our
holdout is scored against v2 itself and an unpinned ruler measures disagreement, not quality.
PRICE: ~1 h at 336px/12sl. P(clears 1.5%) = 0.20. Justified by the forum naming label-making as the
bottleneck (735826), not by the gold delta, which is inside its interval.
notes: 2026-08-25 20:46Z — the label lane is now measured to be OURS, not just live-and-small. supervision_gap over all 58 annotated studies, using holdannot_s2026 (a member whose loss never saw a radiologist cell), reads aggregate labels 0.8658 vs model 0.8932. Nine of twelve findings are label-bottlenecked for us. blendlabels' six pre-registered findings all sit inside those nine, and three MORE are reachable by the same lever: Medial Meniscus (+0.0144), Lateral OA (+0.0039), ACL (+0.0025). The size does not change (+0.0034 on the metric, +0.0070 on the six) — the surface does. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_our-model-beats-its-own-labels.md.

title: The frontier is a SINGLE MODEL, not an ensemble — our seven seats are not where the 0.014 lives
description:
Discussion 735304, read live 2026-08-25. Independent competitors, unprompted:

  * 'I am at 0.938 with a single model, single fold.'
  * 'Single model 0.934 @ 224px. Update: 0.942 with some tweaks, still @ 224px.'
  * 'I am on a single model. OOF AUC = LB AUC within noise, 0.92.'

title: Read at DINOv2's native 224px: the resolution axis was never tested on OUR recipe
description:
Every cache this project holds is 336px or 448px. The only 224px arms were DINOv3-family ones (ledger:335, 'read size is not the axis: 0.0023 from 441 patches to 196') and that family is refuted with its own recipe, so it says nothing about the canonical DINOv2 dense recipe.

MECHANISM: DINOv2 is patch-14 pretrained at 224 (16x16=256 patches). At 336 the position embeddings are INTERPOLATED to 24x24=576 — off-distribution for the encoder, on every member we own.

EXTERNAL EVIDENCE, and it is WEAK — say so. Discussion 735304 (read 2026-08-25): one competitor reports 'single model 0.934 @ 224px ... 0.942 with some tweaks'. But the only SAME-AUTHOR comparison in the thread is '0.926 @ 336px' against '0.929 @ 224px' — +0.003, inside anyone's floor. The strong 224 numbers come from a different competitor with unknown other differences. Treat the forum as motivation for an untested axis, never as a measured delta.

COST: cache build is CPU-only (free wall-clock beside a running arm); the arm itself is ~2.25x fewer patches than 336, so ~130s/epoch against 292s, ~26 min for 12 epochs. P(clears 1.5%) ~0.15. Justified on ratio, not on confidence.

PRE-REGISTERED: control is the canonical dense arm at 336. >=+0.015 = the interpolation was costing us on every member and the whole stack should be re-read; +0.006 to +0.015 = directional, keep as a DISTANT member (a 224 read is architecturally unlike six 336 reads); within +/-0.006 = the axis is flat and closes; <=-0.015 = 336 is earning its patches.
notes:
PRICE: 0.5 h card (12 epochs at ~130 s, cheaper than 336 because 2.25x fewer patches) + 0.4 h CPU cache build that ran beside a fitting arm and cost no card time. P(clears 1.5%) = 0.15. Expected value is carried by the DISTANT-member branch as much as by the gain branch: a 224 read is architecturally unlike the six 336 members and MemberDistance can price that even if the mean is flat.
RESULT 2026-08-25: native224 0.8502 vs control lr4e-5_ws 0.8525. -0.0023, inside the 0.0062 floor; convergence_check does not flag it (best e7 of 12, e8-11 declining). Flat on score, 2.25x cheaper: 94 s/epoch vs ~290, 8124 MiB vs 17997. Read as a THROUGHPUT result -- a 12-epoch arm costs 19 min instead of 60, and every matched comparison from here can run at 224 against 0.8502 as its control. Does not generalise past this geometry (12 slices, 0.20-0.80 band); band_dense was excluded as control to avoid confounding geometry with resolution.

title: fastMRI+ as a fourth corpus: severity-graded knee labels, and the first foreign corpus that supervises more than one of our twelve
description:
FOUND WHILE PRICING THE EXTERNAL-DATA PROGRAMME, and it is a better corpus than MRNet on the axis that matters. quarter_data fitted the data slope with a third point and it is CONCAVE — each doubling buys ~0.48 of the last, the next one prices at ~+0.009 and MRNet ALONE at ~+0.004. So no single corpus clears the bar and the ledger says so. What the ledger also says, and nobody has acted on, is that ALL remaining doublings sum to ~+0.017, which DOES clear it. External data is a PROGRAMME of several corpora, not one download, and this is the third of them.

WHAT IT IS. fastMRI+ (Zhao et al., Scientific Data 9:152, 2022; arXiv 2109.03812) adds 16,154 subspecialist bounding-box annotations plus 13 study-level labels across 22 pathology categories to the NYU fastMRI knee corpus. Sagittal proton-density with fat saturation — ONE plane, so one slot, the Rijeka shape rather than the MRNet shape.

THE LABEL VOCABULARY, read from the annotation CSV itself rather than from the paper's prose (header: file,slice,study_level,x,y,width,height,label):

  Cartilage - Partial Thickness loss/defect     ~340
  Cartilage - Full Thickness loss/defect        ~80
  Bone- Subchondral edema                       ~120
  Meniscus Tear                                 ~520
  Displaced Meniscal Tissue                     ~60
  Joint Effusion                                ~140
  Ligament - ACL Low Grade sprain               ~100
  Ligament - ACL High Grade Sprain              ~80
  Ligament - MCL Low-Mod Grade Sprain           ~100
  Ligament - PCL Low-Mod grade sprain           ~30
  LCL Complex - Low-Mod Grade Sprain            ~40
  Periarticular cysts                           ~110
  Bone-Fracture/Contusion/dislocation           ~110
  Muscle Strain                                 ~30
  Bone - Lesion                                 ~25

WHY THIS BEATS MRNET DESPITE FILLING ONE SLOT INSTEAD OF THREE.

  1. IT CARRIES SEVERITY. 'ACL Low Grade sprain' and 'ACL High Grade Sprain' are distinct labels. MRNet's ACL is BINARY, which is precisely why mrnet_corpus.MRNET_LEVEL had to take 0.82 (the middle confident-yes level) instead of 0.94 — a label that lumps partial with complete cannot honestly claim the unhedged-severe level. fastMRI+ can: low grade onto ~0.28, high grade onto ~0.94, off Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT the same way. That is the first foreign corpus whose supervision has the same SHAPE as our reader's output rather than a collapsed version of it.

  2. IT SUPERVISES MORE THAN ONE COLUMN. MRNet and Rijeka both supervise ACL and nothing else, so eleven of twelve heads take zero gradient from them (Targets.pair weights the absent columns at 0.0). fastMRI+ maps cleanly onto at least THREE: ACL (two grades), MCL, Effusion. Under the data-volume mechanism that is three heads getting more studies rather than one.

HONEST MAPPING PROBLEMS, stated before any code so they are not discovered as bugs:

  * 'Meniscus Tear' does NOT split medial from lateral, and our table carries both. Same call as MRNet's meniscus: DROP it rather than write one label into two columns, which would teach a medial tear as lateral-positive.
  * The cartilage labels do not name a COMPARTMENT, so they cannot land in Medial OA / Lateral OA / PF OA. Drop.
  * 'Bone-Fracture/Contusion/dislocation' is one label over two of our columns (Fracture, Contusion). Drop, or map to whichever the box location resolves — the boxes are per-slice with coordinates, so this one is recoverable with work rather than structurally lost.
  * 'Periarticular cysts' is NEAR Baker's cyst but not identical (a Baker's is one specific popliteal location). Do not map it without checking box locations.
  * PCL, LCL, muscle strain, bone lesion, subchondral edema have no column of ours. Absence is the mechanism.

THE DENOMINATOR TRAP, which is the defect most likely to sink this. These are annotations of PRESENT findings. A study with no ACL box is either ACL-NEGATIVE or simply not annotated for it, and writing 'absent = negative' without establishing which would manufacture thousands of confident-absence cells at 0.08. The corpus ships a separate list of studies read as having no findings; the ingest must join against THAT and refuse to emit a negative cell for any study not on it. This is the same class of error as reading 19% of located cells as 19% of all cells.

ONE MORE GOTCHA, from the repo's own conversion notes: fastMRI was converted to DICOM for annotation and 'pixel arrays were flipped (up/down)' in the process. A silent vertical flip against every member's fitted geometry is exactly the kind of plumbing defect that reads as 'foreign data does not transfer'. Assert the orientation, do not assume it.

LICENSING: the ANNOTATIONS are MIT (github.com/microsoft/fastmri-plus). The IMAGES need the NYU fastMRI data sharing agreement at fastmri.org/dataset/ — owner-gated, same shape as MRNet's RUA. Per the owner's ruling on 2026-08-25 a licence is a SHIPPING gate and not a MEASURING gate, so the ingest can be built and measured before the shipping question is asked.

SEQUENCING. Do NOT start this before the merged_corpus arm reads. That arm is ours+Rijeka and it is the first evidence about whether ANY foreign corpus transfers here. A flat reading there does not kill this one (Rijeka fills one slot of six, which confounds 'foreign' with 'degenerate input' — the ambiguity mrnet_corpus was built to break) but it does change the order.

DEPENDS ON: knee-0p87 — MergedCache joins exactly TWO corpora, and this would be the fourth source.
notes:
RAISED TO P1 2026-08-31 by the backlog triage (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-31_the-backlog-triage-nobody-ran.md). It is one of only TWO live lanes in a 289-bead backlog; six of the ten most promising-sounding open beads turned out to be refuted in their own notes and were closed on that pass. fastMRI+ is not behind the licence door knee-ombx and knee-2sbk are blocked on, it carries SEVERITY where MRNet's ACL is binary, and it supervises three of our columns where MRNet and Rijeka supervise one. Sits at P1 above knee-ombx for those three reasons.
fastMRI+ fits into two unified schemes: (1) Scheme B — use MIT-licensed annotations as partial-label supervision for ACL (graded), MCL, effusion; meniscus dropped because no med/lat split; contusion recovered only via box location. (2) Scheme A — use images unlabeled for SSL continuation. Do not run a fastMRI-only continuation; it sits below the literature threshold for gain.
Local inventory update: MRNet, Rijeka, fastMRI, SKM-TEA, KMAR-50K are on disk at D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/. fastMRI knee has 16k bbox annotations over 974 scans. See research/2026-09-02_external_knee_mri_data_access_audit.md section 9.
Scheme B dataloader design: research/2026-09-02_scheme_b_dataloader_design_local_corpora.md. fastMRI branch is highest-confidence first experiment.

title: Ingest MRNet (Stanford) as a third corpus: three planes into three canonical slots
description: Rijeka fills ONE slot of six; MRNet ships sagittal/coronal/axial per exam and fills THREE, so a foreign exam stops being a degenerate input. 1,250 available exams (1,130 train + 120 valid; the 120-exam test split is withheld). Supervises ACL ONLY: MRNet's meniscus label does not distinguish medial from lateral while our table carries both columns, so writing one label into both would teach a medial tear as lateral-positive - the same error rijeka_corpus.labels() refuses when it declines to write 0.5 into eleven columns nobody read. Its 'abnormal' label has no column of ours. Mirrors core/data/corpus/rijeka_corpus.py + build_rijeka.py; needs MRNET_SCHEME in slots.py with the same 'any other scheme writes onto our own corpus' guard. Blocked on the owner accepting the Stanford RUA at stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/mrnet/ and dropping the zip under D:/data/raw/ - licence gates SHIPPING, not measuring.
notes: Loader built and green without the card. Three new files: core/data/corpus/mrnet_corpus.py (MRNetExam + MRNetCorpus), core/data/corpus/build_mrnet.py (CLI, carries the scheme guard), tests/unit/core/data/corpus/mrnet_corpus.py (9 tests). slots.py gains MRNET_SCHEME + MRNET_SLOTS = (SLOTS[0], SLOTS[2], SLOTS[4]) — sagittal/axial/coronal per Bien et al. 2018, modal not guaranteed. Only ACL is supervised: meniscus does not split medial from lateral and abnormal has no column. Levels 0.08 / 0.82 off Supervision.MEASURED_AGREEMENT, weight 0.95 (report-derived, like ours; NOT Rijeka's 1.0 expert image read). MRNET_SPACING 0.625 = 160mm FOV / 256px, derived and weaker than Rijeka's — no in-corpus physical length to check it against, and load-bearing (208px vs 260px of 256 decides whether the 130mm crop happens at all). Improves on the Rijeka template on one axis: volumes() round-trips through cache.enrolled, so a --cache-studies smoke writes a file that says what it holds; Rijeka still has that hole. REMAINING, both owner-side: accept the RUA at stanfordmlgroup.github.io/competitions/mrnet/ and drop the ~5.7GB zip under D:/data/raw/, then 'uv run python -m core.data.corpus.build_mrnet --archive <path> --scheme mrnet' (--cache-studies 60 first). And MergedCache joins exactly TWO corpora, so ours+Rijeka+MRNet needs two passes through an intermediate scheme that does not exist yet.

title: Merged cache: our corpus + kneeMRI in ONE array, so external data reaches the trainer by the route the ledger has NOT closed
description:
The kneeMRI ingestion (knee-allv) is DONE — images_336px_12sl_rijeka.npy, 736 studies, built 2026-08-25 14:58Z. The consumer is what is missing, and the obvious consumer is the wrong one.

THE ROUTE THAT LOOKS FREE IS THE CLOSED ONE. `kneemri.training.pretrain` takes CacheFlags, so `--scheme rijeka` runs today with no new code, and it emits an encoder the supervised recipe loads through `--encoder-weights`. That is the SSL-as-init family exactly: encoder_adapt 0.6902, encoder_adapt_gentle 0.6875, encoder_adapt_lower 0.7309, encoder_adapt_thawed 0.7162, mae_matched 0.6735 — five collapses, 0.09-0.15 below a control that starts from stock, with plumbing/data/variant/test all cleared as suspects by adapt_null. mae_matched refuted the masked objective over 402,600 of OUR OWN slices; 8,832 foreign ones through the same import path is the sixth collapse, not a result. Zero new code is not zero expected score.

WHAT kneeMRI ACTUALLY CARRIES IS A LABEL. 736 double-blind expert ACL reads from another site, another scanner, another population. Supervised external data is a different axis from unsupervised adapt-and-import, and nothing on the ledger speaks to it.

THE BLOCKER IS THAT train.py READS ONE CACHE. `cache.load()` is a single call returning one (corpus, identifiers) pair, so the two corpora cannot both reach one run today. That is the whole gap, and it is a data-preparation job, not a training one — no card.

THE MERGE IS EXACTLY WHAT THE MASK IS FOR. Both caches are 336px/12sl uint8 under the same reader geometry (the rijeka build used CacheFlags defaults precisely so this would hold). kneeMRI acquired ONE sequence and it is SLOTS[0] — sagittal PD-FS on a 1.5T Avanto — our first slot's predicate exactly, which tests/unit/core/data/corpus/slots.py::test_built already asserts. So:

    images  (1325+736, 4, 12, 336, 336)   ours copied wholesale; rijeka into slot 0
    mask    (1325+736, 4)                 ours as-is; rijeka [1, 0, 0, 0]
    index   ours + rijeka identifiers
    labels  train.csv rows + rijeka_acl.csv rows

and the three mechanisms already audited in rijeka_corpus.py's docstring carry the rest: ReportFolds.assign hashes an identifier absent from train.csv, Targets.pair gives an absent column weight 0.0 / score 0.5 so eleven heads take no gradient from these rows, and the head's softmax renormalises over the mask. ~40 GB on disk, CPU only, no card, no slot.

PRICE IT HONESTLY BEFORE RUNNING IT. +55% studies on ONE of twelve labels. If the gain were confined to ACL it is worth roughly a twelfth of its size on the averaged metric and would not clear the 1.5% bar; the case for it is that a trunk which has seen a second site generalises on the HIDDEN test set, which is not our corpus — the owner's standing point. That is the mechanism to state in the pre-registration, and it is the reason to run it rather than the ACL subscore.

DO NOT let this become the sixth SSL arm by another name. The arm is a normal supervised run over the merged cache against a matched control on ours alone.
notes:
SEAT PRICED 2026-08-25 18:36Z — the reading the RESULT note could not compute, now that gradeswap_v1
(0.933, 7/7 scoreable) is available as a pricing base. The refusal in that note was correct and is now
answered rather than overturned.

  merged_corpus_s2026   seat +0.0002 (add) / +0.0003 (swap for lr4e-5_ws)   nearest 0.9009

AND IT REFUTES THE ARGUMENT THE ARM WAS TAKEN ON. The instrument's whole case was that a trunk which
has fitted a second site yields a member with a diversity axis no seated member has — the one lever
acting on distribution shift toward a hidden test set, which no offline number can price. The distance
column CAN price part of it, and it says the member is not distinct: 0.9009 sits in the middle of the
seated spread (0.8801 to 0.9248), closer to the roster than base224's 0.8679 and than every 224-family
candidate. 736 foreign studies, +17% of the corpus, labelling one of twelve findings, changed this
model's ORDERING of our holdout studies barely at all.

So the axis closes on two independent columns rather than one. The score was flat (+0.0020, inside the
0.0062 floor) and the ordering is flat too. That is a stronger close than the RESULT note could claim,
and it is worth the distinction: a flat score with a distinct ordering would have left the hidden-test
argument fully alive, because the seat is what that argument cashes out as. A flat score with an
ordering indistinguishable from the incumbents does not.

WHAT IT STILL DOES NOT SAY. The corpus supervises ONE of twelve labels, and the pre-registration priced
that at a twelfth of any ACL gain. This is a reading about THIS use of external data — 736 studies, one
label, merged supervised — not about external data as an axis. MRNet is 1,370 exams x 3 series x 3
labels and remains the stronger corpus (knee-ombx, knee-dnhd); the cache writer and merge path built
here are exactly what it drops into. Do not let this note be quoted as 'external data does not work'.

The instrument did its job: it retired the only DATA axis that was open, at 1.3 h of card, and the
retirement is now double-sourced.

title: kneeMRI (Rijeka) ingestion: cache writer + labels table, so an external-data pretraining arm can launch the moment the card frees
description:
knee-ombx is the P0 saying external data is the biggest axis never tried in 107 runs, BLOCKED on a
licence decision. As of 2026-08-25 that blocker is downgraded (knee-ombx notes: the 2.6(a) disjunction,
2.6(b) and the 2.8 carve-out, confirmed against the standard Kaggle rules template). This bead is the
part that costs no card and no slot: the INGESTION.

WHY kneeMRI AND NOT MRNet FIRST - a practical fact, not a preference. MRNet needs a human to accept
Stanford's Research Use Agreement in a browser; no agent here can. kneeMRI is mirrored on Kaggle
(sohaibanwaar1203/kneemridataset) and pulls with the API we already hold, no slot spent. knee-ombx's
ordering is UNCHANGED - MRNet is the stronger corpus (3 labels x 3 series vs one ordinal label). This is
about what is obtainable today, and the writer is shaped so MRNet drops into the same path later.

DOWNLOADED AND INSPECTED 2026-08-25 14:36Z -> D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kneemri_rijeka/
kneemridataset.zip, 3.31 GB, 737 entries.

  THE MIRROR IS A SUBSET AND THE DENOMINATOR IS 736, NOT 917. metadata.csv carries all 917 published
  rows, but only vol01..vol08 ship - vol09 and vol10 are absent, so 736 volumes are on disk (80.3%).
  Every .pck joins a metadata row; there are no orphans. The dropped 181 are NOT label-biased:

      aclDiagnosis        0 healthy      1 partial      2 ruptured
      all 917             690 (75.2%)   172 (18.8%)    55 (6.0%)
      present 736         547 (74.3%)   144 (19.6%)    45 (6.1%)
      missing 181         143 (79.0%)    28 (15.5%)    10 (5.5%)

  So the corpus is usable as-is and any figure quoted from it is over 736, never 917. 45 complete
  ruptures is a thin positive class - acceptable for encoder PRETRAINING, and it is not the target task.

FORMAT, measured rather than assumed:
  metadata.csv  examId,seriesNo,aclDiagnosis,kneeLR,roiX,roiY,roiZ,roiHeight,roiWidth,roiDepth,
                volumeFilename
  volumes       pickled numpy arrays, `pickle.loads` -> ndarray (depth, 320, 320) uint16, 12-bit range
                (one sampled volume: shape (32,320,320), min 0, max 1529). Depth varies 21-45.
  So a windowing step to uint8 is required; our cache is uint8. A per-volume percentile window is the
  obvious derivation - fix it from the data, do not pick a constant.

WHAT THE AUDIT FOUND, better news than expected: THE TRAINER NEEDS NO CHANGE.
- core/data/corpus/folds.py:36 - `reports.get(identifier, identifier)` falls back to hashing the
  identifier itself, so a foreign corpus absent from train.csv still gets a stable fold assignment
  rather than failing.
- core/data/labels/targets.py:236-251 - a target column ABSENT from the labels CSV gets weight 0.0 and
  score 0.5. A table carrying only `ACL` supervises ACL and contributes exactly nothing on the other
  eleven, with no flag and no code path added.
- kneemri/training/train.py:65-71 - `Targets.pair` reindexes train.csv onto our identifiers; unknown
  ones become NaN, and `supervision.annotations` is off by default, so nothing reads them.

So the work is two artifacts plus one registry entry:
 1. A `StudyCache`-shaped cache: images_<key>.npy [studies, slots, slices, size, size] uint8,
    mask_<key>.npy [studies, slots] float32, index_<key>.json. Written directly rather than through
    `StudyCache.build`, whose `decode_one` calls `Study.from_directory` on DICOMs.
 2. A labels CSV in report_labels_v2.csv's shape: `StudyInstanceUID, ACL, ACL__conf` only.
 3. A slot scheme registered in core/data/corpus/slots.py SCHEMES.

THE SCHEME ENTRY IS A SAFETY REQUIREMENT, NOT A CONVENIENCE. `StudyCache.key` is
`{size}px_{slices}sl{reading.suffix()}{routing.suffix()}{truncation}` and `Routing.suffix()` is EMPTY
for the canonical scheme. A kneeMRI cache at 336 px / 12 slices under the canonical scheme would write
to `images_336px_12sl.npy` - the path the 71.6 GB corpus every member on disk was fitted on occupies -
and destroy it, differing only in its first axis. That is the exact disaster `StudyCache.key`'s own
docstring records narrowly avoiding three times (slot count, physical crop, slice band). A distinct
scheme name makes the collision unrepresentable.

TARGET MAPPING, derived rather than picked. core/data/labels/targets.py holds four reader levels with
measured precisions: 0.08 (0.041), 0.28 (0.136), 0.68 (0.378), 0.82 (0.688). kneeMRI's classes are
double-blind EXPERT reads of the ligament itself, not findings mined from report text, so they are more
trustworthy than any of our levels rather than less. healthy -> 0.08, partial -> 0.68, ruptured -> 0.82
at high confidence. The ORDERING is what carries the mechanism; the exact values matter little for
encoder pretraining.

UNRESOLVED BEFORE THE SCHEME ENTRY IS WRITTEN: sources disagree on the sequence. The Kaggle mirror says
proton-density weighted with fat suppression; several downstream papers say T1-weighted sagittal. It
decides which of our slots this corpus is analogous to and how the domain match is argued. Resolve from
the 2017 paper (Comput Methods Programs Biomed 140, 151-164). The ROI columns also go unused for now -
they are an ACL bounding box and a possible crop-centre signal, which is a separate question.

NOT IN SCOPE: the arm itself, which needs the card - and the card is biohub's, open-ended, until they
write back. This bead ends with a cache on disk and a smoke proving it maps.
notes:
2026-08-25 — INGESTION WRITTEN, gates pending. core/data/corpus/rijeka_corpus.py + build_rijeka.py, mirror tests beside them.

SEQUENCE RESOLVED. Stajduhar et al. 2017 acquired the whole corpus on one Siemens Avanto 1.5T, sagittal, proton-density-weighted with fat suppression. That is SLOTS[0] = SAG_FLUID_FS's predicate exactly — our most-used first slot, so the best possible domain match, and a Rijeka exam occupies the same slot-axis position it would occupy in ours. Hence RIJEKA_SLOTS = (SLOTS[0],), one slot.

SPACING DERIVED AND CHECKED. metadata.csv records none. 160 mm FOV (our own measured median, slots.DETAIL_MM) / 320 px = 0.5 mm/px. Checked against the one physical length the metadata DOES carry: the ACL boxes median 90 x 91 px = 45 x 45 mm at this spacing, right for boxes 'enveloping the wider cruciate ligament area' around a 30-35 mm ligament. 0.4 would make them 36 mm, 0.6 would make them 54.

TARGET MAPPING CORRECTED — this note supersedes the 0.08/0.68/0.82 written when the bead was filed, which came from a four-level reading of targets.py. There are FIVE levels and each is worth its MEASURED agreement rate (targets.py:36-43). healthy -> 0.08 (4.1%), partial -> 0.82 (68.8%), ruptured -> 0.94 (95.8%). These are double-blind expert IMAGE reads, not text-mined findings, so they belong at the confident end; no level below 0.68 fits a confirmed injury.

DENOMINATOR IS 736, NOT 917. The Kaggle mirror ships vol01..vol08 and omits vol09/vol10. Not label-biased: present 74.3/19.6/6.1% against published 75.2/18.8/6.0%.

TRAINER NEEDS NO CHANGE — three mechanisms already admit a foreign corpus: ReportFolds.assign hashes the identifier when absent from train.csv; Targets.pair gives an ABSENT column weight 0.0 (so eleven heads take no gradient, which is why the labels table carries ACL alone and NOT 0.5 fillers); train.py never reads the NaN rows unless annotations are on.

CLOBBER MADE UNREPRESENTABLE TWICE: RIJEKA_SCHEME suffixes the cache key (_rijeka), and build_rijeka refuses any other --scheme. Under canonical a 336px/12sl build would write images_336px_12sl.npy over the 71.6 GB every member on disk was fitted on, differing only in axis 0.

NEXT: run the ingestion (no card, no slot):
  python -m core.data.corpus.build_rijeka --archive D:/data/volumetric/mri/raw/kneemri_rijeka/kneemridataset.zip --scheme rijeka --slices 12 --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9
Then the pretraining arm, which DOES need the card and so waits on biohub.
BUILT 2026-08-25 14:58Z, CPU only, ~60s (the card is biohub's until their GPU train ends; they confirmed at 14:26Z they will ping when it is device-empty).

  images_336px_12sl_rijeka.npy   (736, 1, 12, 336, 336) uint8, 997 MB
  index_336px_12sl_rijeka.json   736 identifiers, '<examId>-<seriesNo>'
  mask_336px_12sl_rijeka.npy     (736, 1) all ones — the corpus acquired the one sequence it has
  labels/rijeka_acl.csv          736 rows, StudyInstanceUID/ACL/ACL__conf, levels 547/144/45

GEOMETRY IS THE CANONICAL ONE, NOT THE 0.1-0.9 BAND THE PLAN NOTE NAMED. Built with CacheFlags
defaults — the historic crop, centre and band every member on disk was fitted under — because the whole
mechanism this module exists for is that the two corpora reach the encoder in ONE geometry and ONE
intensity space. A pretraining corpus sampled under a band our members were never fitted on would make
the transfer measure the band difference as well as the dataset difference. Only --scheme is non-default,
and that is the safety flag.

The 547/144/45 in the labels table is the 736-row split exactly (74.3/19.6/6.1%), so the join held all
the way through the build. Our own 35.8 GB images_336px_12sl.npy is untouched — still its Aug 10 mtime.

NEXT: the pretraining arm. Nothing else about ingestion is outstanding.

title: smoke and arm write the SAME log, so a failed smoke's traceback is destroyed by the run it gates
description: experiments/arms/v3lora_dense.sh smoke passes --out v3lora_smoke.pt but run_train still names the arm 'v3lora_dense', so both modes write $PROCESSED/experiments/v3lora_dense.full.log. On 2026-08-25 the smoke exited 1 and the arm that followed overwrote the log before the traceback could be read — the smoke gate produced a FAILURE with no DIAGNOSIS, which is the one thing it exists to produce. The smoke's whole argument is 'two minutes of smoke against 2.5h of arm'; that trade only pays if the two minutes leave evidence behind. Fix in lib.sh run_train: derive the log name from the OUT checkpoint stem rather than the arm name, so v3lora_smoke.pt lands in v3lora_smoke.full.log and can never be clobbered. Applies to every arm with a smoke mode, not just this one.
notes: FIXED 2026-08-25 in experiments/lib.sh: run_train sets ARM_LOG_NAME from the --out checkpoint stem, and the four reads of the arm's log go through _arm_log, which prefers that stem and falls back to the arm name for a run with no --out. The smoke and the arm it gates now write different files because their checkpoints already had to differ -- run_train REFUSES an arm whose --out exists, so two runs sharing a name cannot share a checkpoint path either. Verified: ARM_LOG_NAME=merged_corpus_s2026 resolves to .../merged_corpus_s2026.full.log and the unset case to .../fallback.full.log.

title: A checkpoint carries its own preprocessing contract, and rad-dino's is not ImageNet
description: model.py registers IMAGENET_MEAN/IMAGENET_STD as buffers for EVERY encoder. Audited all seven registry encoders against their own preprocessor_config.json (primary source, HF raw + local cache): dinov2 small/base/large, dinov3 vits16/vits16plus/vitb16 and convnextv2-base-22k-224 all declare the ImageNet constants, so six of seven are correct by coincidence -- which is why this never surfaced. microsoft/rad-dino declares image_mean 0.5307 and image_std 0.2583 (greyscale, native 518 px), and we feed it ImageNet. At x=0.5307 the trunk should see 0.0 and sees (0.5307-0.485)/0.229 = 0.200, a 0.20-std offset, with a scale error of 0.2583/0.229 = 1.128 (12.8 percent). raddino_dense scored 0.8137 solo against base_dense_s2026 0.8512 at the same recipe and was read as evidence about medical-domain pretraining; that reading is confounded, and it is a SECOND confound on top of the run being TRUNCATED at epoch 6 of 12. Our mounted snapshot at rad-dino/ carries no preprocessor_config.json at all, so the constants are not even present to read -- which is why the fix belongs on Encoder in the registry (the house pattern params_m already uses) rather than as a checkpoint read. The buffers are persistent so they ride in the state dict: every member already on disk keeps the constants it was fitted with, and only a new fit changes. V-JEPA2 is UNVERIFIED -- no local snapshot and the HF repo answers no readable preprocessor_config.json -- so its constants must be checked before any vjepa arm is armed. Found in kaggle forum topic 735154, verified independently against the primary source.
notes: FIXED 2026-08-25. Encoder.normalization (kneemri/models/backbone.py) now carries the pair per encoder, IMAGENET is the default, RAD_DINO declares 0.5307/0.2583. Consumers moved: StudyModel.__init__ + from_config (registry-resolved from the config's variant, so both inference paths rebuild correctly), run_setup, SpectralMae, pretrain. Buffers stay PERSISTENT, so every packaged member keeps the constants it was fitted under and only a new fit moves. Tests: Normalization.declared/triple/assert_declared, one over the whole registry, and a model-side test that from_config resolves RAD_DINO's pair while an unnamed variant stays ImageNet. raddino_dense's ledger entry now records the second confound. V-JEPA2 left unverified and split into its own bead.

title: The 58-study ruler contradicts its own reports at the severity boundary, and every label-column number rests on it
description:
Read 2026-08-25 from competition discussion topic 735826 via kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read (no submission slot). Two independent competitors report the same defect in the 58 provided annotations, with a check anyone can run:

  - Filter reports whose effusion sentence carries a small-size qualifier ('small', 'minimal', 'trace', or the equivalent in the other languages). That group holds BOTH Effusion=0 and Effusion=1. In one sample two reports used the SAME English template and the SAME sentence and got OPPOSITE labels.
  - Then find a report stating a MODERATE effusion. At least one of those is annotated Effusion=0 - so it is not a 'small=negative, moderate=positive' threshold either, which is what the competition's own introduction lays out as the heuristic.
  - A second poster makes the same point structurally: 'the image label clearly flouts the rules of diagnosis laid out in the introduction ... close to the decision boundary the report label and the image label will often disagree; radiologists will just disagree.'

WHY THIS IS OURS AND NOT THEIRS. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_labels-or-pixels.md prices every finding as two AUCs against those 58 annotations - labels 0.8639 vs model 0.8391 aggregate, Effusion 0.8137 -> 0.9453. Both columns are scored against a ruler this claim says is internally inconsistent AT THE BOUNDARY, which is exactly where a report-derived label lands. The claim does not overturn the split (the ordering is over twelve labels and the two largest gaps are far from the noise), but it bounds the LABEL column specifically: a better reader (knee-dbw, knee-bot) cannot recover agreement the annotation itself does not obey.

THE CHECK, CPU-ONLY, NO SLOT, NO CARD:
  1. Over the 58 annotated studies, bucket each report's effusion sentence by severity qualifier (small/minimal/trace vs moderate/large vs none).
  2. Cross-tab against the radiologist Effusion annotation. STATE THE DENOMINATOR - n=58 total, and the count in each bucket, not a rate inside the bucket that happened to parse.
  3. If a qualifier bucket holds both classes, the ruler is subjective at the boundary and the effusion label column has a ceiling below 1.0 that no reader improvement crosses.
  4. Repeat for the other graded findings the intro gives a threshold for; knee-bot already records that we train on 0.68 where the radiologist agrees 38%, which is the same shape measured from the other side.

WHAT IT WOULD CHANGE. If the bucket is mixed: stop spending on the reader for effusion, and treat the graded findings' targets as a distribution rather than a threshold. If it is clean and only OUR extraction is mixed, the defect is ours and knee-dbw pays after all. Either outcome retires a suspicion for the cost of one pandas cross-tab.

CAVEAT ON THE SOURCE: this is a competitor's report of their own sample, not our measurement. It is cheap enough that arguing about it costs more than running it.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 on our own data — the claim holds, harder than the forum reported.

python -m core.data.labels.severity_boundary (CPU, no slot, no card):
  28 English annotated studies of 58 annotated
    small / minimal / trace           12 studies   annotated positive   6
    both, e.g. small to moderate       1 studies   annotated positive   1
    moderate or larger                 3 studies   annotated positive   2
    mentioned, no size word            7 studies   annotated positive   6
    effusion denied                    5 studies   annotated positive   0

The negative side of the stated threshold is a coin flip (6 of 12). The positive side is 2 of 3. Seven
studies are named by the tool with their UIDs. Denominator is 28 English of 58 annotated, NOT 58.

HARNESS SUSPICION PAID: the first run named EIGHT. 'No significant knee effusion', annotated 0, had been
bucketed moderate-or-larger because 'significant' is a LARGE word inside a DENIAL. That row is agreement,
filed as a contradiction by the tool. A DENIED regex now removes denied sentences, and the resulting
'effusion denied' bucket is a free control: 5 studies, 0 positive — the agreement a working ruler shows on
easy cases. Sensitivity: dropping 'mild' from SMALL_WORDS moves 4 studies and leaves the small bucket at
5 positive of 8. Still mixed. Not a vocabulary artefact.

CONSEQUENCE: part of every reader error measured against these 58 is not error, and no better reader
recovers it. Effusion is where supervision_gap shows the biggest label-to-model gap (0.8137 vs 0.9453);
a slice of that gap is annotation noise at the boundary, not headroom. Also prices down LLM-confidence
weighting: confidence over a report measures confidence in applying a crisp rule to a clear word, not in
the finding — 'small' is easy to read while the process that wrote 'small' rather than 'moderate' is the
noisy part.

Written up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-25_effusion-threshold-ruler.md

title: Frontier reaches our ENSEMBLE score with ONE model at 224px - the gap is member quality, not ensembling
description:
Read 2026-08-25 from the competition discussion via the Kaggle API (kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read; no submission slot). Topic 735304 'Best single-model score', 10 messages, 17 votes.

SELF-REPORTED SINGLE-MODEL SCORES ON THE BOARD:
- 0.942 @ 224px ('Single model 0.934 @ 224px. Update: 0.942 with some tweaks, still @ 224px')
- 0.938 single model, single fold
- 0.926 single model 5-fold @ 336px, LLM-output labels only
- 0.92 with OOF AUC = LB AUC within noise
- 0.915 DINOv2-based

OURS, from comp/board.jsonl: best SINGLE member solo_v4 = 0.914. Best ensemble votefit_v1 = 0.938 over six members. So our ensembling machinery buys +0.024 and is real - but the frontier's ONE model equals or beats our SIX, and does it at 224px against our 392px members, so it is not a compute story.

READ: the 0.014 board gap lives in MEMBER QUALITY, not in ensemble construction. Our ensemble work has been buying back a deficit rather than extending a lead. That is above the 1.5 pct bar as a claim about WHERE to spend, and it is the first evidence this session that localises the gap at all.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT REFUTE: the recorded measurement that diversity beat member quality within OUR pool (interpretations/kneemri, bead knee-eeo). Both hold at once - given members clustered at ~0.91, diversity is the best available lever; the frontier instead has a member that does not need it. Do not re-run that ablation on this.

EVIDENCE QUALITY: unverified self-reports, no way to confirm 0.942. But five independent posts cluster 0.915-0.942 and one anchors OOF=LB within noise, so the cluster is consistent rather than one boast. Treat the LEVEL as soft and the ORDERING (their single >= our six) as the finding.

CHECKABLE FOLLOW-UP named in the same thread: the public Efficiency LB (kaggle.com/code/ryanholbrook/rsna-knee-abnormalities-efficiency-lb) shows runtimes, and a poster argues high scorers there have short runtimes, i.e. are not 20-model ensembles. That is free, independent, non-self-reported evidence for the same claim - read it before acting.
notes:
2026-08-25, from discussion topic 736678 (kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read --topic 736678): the Efficiency LB is the NON-SELF-REPORTED corroboration this bead asked for, and it holds.

  - As of Aug 22 only ~32% of the public-LB top 50 also appear in the Efficiency-LB top 50. A high score bought with a long runtime is a score bought with ensembling.
  - The poster is Efficiency LB 22nd and Public LB 78th at 0.926 with 'preprocessing plus a single model trained with 5-fold', total runtime ~20 minutes.
  - A second poster is currently Efficiency LB #1 with NO ensemble.
  - A third notes the top two public-LB submissions also sit on the Efficiency LB, so the very top is not runtime-heavy either.

That is a public board rather than a forum claim, and it says the same thing the self-reports did: a single model reaches ~0.926-0.942 while our six-member ensemble reads 0.938. The ensembling we do is real (+0.024 within our pool) and it is buying back a member-quality deficit, not extending a lead. Efficiency also bears on knee-5bv.
2026-08-25, kneemri.kaggle.efficiency_read (new tool, live read, no slot): the Efficiency-LB corroboration this bead asked for is now MEASURED rather than quoted, and it is stronger than the forum version - but it is bimodal, which the forum version was not.

The poster's overlap claim verifies: public top-50 and efficiency top-50 share 17 teams (34.0%), against their '~32% as of Aug 22'. Top-10 overlap is 20%, top-100 is 32%.

WHAT THE BOARD SHOWS THAT THE FORUM DID NOT. Joining the public top-20 to their efficiency rank, the same accuracy is reached by two completely different builds:
  public 4  Scott Willis   0.947  efficiency rank    1   (0.947 - same entry)
  public 5  Matteo Vitali  0.946  efficiency rank    8   (0.946 - same entry)
  public 14 Tucker Arrants 0.944  efficiency rank    5   (0.944 - same entry)
  public 8  CloseAI        0.946  efficiency rank 1678
  public 20 Pizza Boy      0.943  efficiency rank 1856
  public 16 Ignat          0.943  efficiency rank 1350
So ~0.943-0.947 is reachable BOTH at efficiency rank 1 and at efficiency rank 1856. Two routes to the same number, differing by orders of magnitude in runtime.

THE DATUM THAT MATTERS, and it is a board fact rather than a self-report: the efficiency-#1 team scores 0.947 on the PUBLIC board with the SAME entry. A cheap build reaches 0.947. This bead's finding was 'their ONE model equals our SIX' from unverified posts clustering 0.915-0.942; the board now says a fast build reaches 0.947, which is 0.009 ABOVE our six-member 0.938 and above every self-report in the thread. The ordering this bead called the finding is confirmed by non-self-reported evidence, and the LEVEL it called soft is, if anything, understated.

THE EXCEPTION WORTH NAMING: the actual public leader, Brandon Low at 0.952, sits at efficiency rank 41 with a SEPARATE 0.922 entry. So the very top is not on the cheap route - the forum's 'the top two public entries are on both boards' does not hold for #1 as of this read. The cheap route's demonstrated ceiling is 0.947, not 0.952.

WHAT THIS SETS UP, and it is a SUM rather than a choice: our ensembling buys a measured +0.024 within our own pool and a cheap frontier member reaches 0.947 solo. Those compose. The target is a replicated member at frontier quality FEEDING our existing ensemble machinery, not a choice between replicating theirs and building ours. GPU-blocked at the time of writing.

EVIDENCE CAVEAT: the efficiency board is a snapshot with newest submission 2026-08-23 22:30 while the public board is live - see knee-5bv, where that lag was found to have inflated a different measurement by 14 points. It does not touch the rows above, whose two scores agree, but any efficiency figure quoted from this read is as of Aug 23.
2026-09-01 07:41Z: the headline is no longer literally true. Our best ensemble reads 0.944 (holdswap_v1 2026-08-30, stackseat_v1 2026-08-31) against the frontier's best CLAIMED single of 0.942 at 224 px. The frontier single now reaches our SIX (0.943, champviews_v1) rather than our best entry. The member gap this bead exists to close is otherwise unchanged: our own best single is still 0.925 and has not moved since 2026-08-26. Recompute source: completed comp/board.jsonl, 87 rows, joined on 'members'. See knee-macc.

title: board_check should join unnamed rows on NAME and refuse an empty members_named
description:
Three board rows were recovered by hand on 2026-08-25 (chosen_v2, onedecode_v2, weakseven_v1) after two earlier passes left them unnamed, and each was missed by a mechanism a check can hold.

1. NAME JOIN. The earlier recovery offered a row a script only through the row's own `kernel` field, so a row with `kernel: null` was never handed one. Joining on the entry id instead (chosen_v2 -> comp/kernels/kneemri-chosen) finds a surviving script for THIRTEEN of the fourteen rows the file called unrecoverable. The note said 'no script survives'; that was true of fusion25_v2 alone.

2. ABSENT, NEVER EMPTY. weakseven_v1 carried `members_named: []`. A consumer asking `'members_named' in row` reads that as recovered, one asking for truthiness reads it as missing. It had a kernel AND a literal tuple and was still skipped.

3. THE REAL BLOCKER IS SELECTION STYLE, not a missing script. The eleven that stay unnamed call KernelRun(members=N) - strongest(N) over recorded holdouts - which a parse cannot replay against a package that has since changed. Worth recording per row so nobody re-audits them.

Proposed: board_check grows an assertion that no row has an empty members_named, and that any row lacking members_named either has no matching kernel directory or selects by rank. Recovery must read the AS-SUBMITTED commit, not HEAD: kneemri-chosen was edited 2026-08-17 after chosen_v2 shipped (tuple unchanged, but checked rather than assumed - the sixfresh caveat is this exact hazard).

title: champion.json pins allfit 0.937 while votefit_v1 holds the board at 0.938
description: The pin lags the board by one entry, which is the exact failure its own principle #39 names verbatim ('A PIN THAT LAGS THE BOARD SILENTLY MISPRICES EVERY CANDIDATE UNDER IT ... champion_check asserts the pinned entry can be REBUILT; it cannot know the entry is still the best one'). seat_value reads the roster from the pin precisely so no arm header holds a stale copy. title: board.jsonl: the five best entries carry no members_named, so from_board raises on the top of the board
description: 31 of 48 rows in comp/board.jsonl have no 'members_named' (and mostly no 'kit'). Champion.from_board reads row['members_named'] and row['kit'] directly, so it raises a bare KeyError -- not its own 'no board entry named X' message -- on every one of them. The remaining 26 rows are knee-ykny.

title: DeviceBudget prices a frozen block at zero: unfreeze4 under-capped by 35.7%
description:
MEASURED over 74 recorded runs by `python -m kneemri.experiments.budget_residuals` (commit 1f79eca), which prices every run whose epoch rows carry the corrected reserved peak.

THE DEFECT. `DeviceBudget.needed()` multiplies the WHOLE slice cost by `trainable_blocks / FITTED_TRAINABLE`, i.e. it prices a FROZEN block at exactly zero memory. A frozen block still runs its forward and still holds the activations the blocks above it read; only its gradients and optimiser state go away. So the model is wrong in BOTH directions, and both are measured:

  unfreeze4_s2026        measured 14.79, derived 10.90  (+35.7%)  CAP UNDER DEMAND — allowed 11.79
  encoder_adapt_thawed   (killed earlier this axis, in the OVER direction)

A cap under a measured demand is the one failure this model calls fatal: it prevents nothing and guarantees the OutOfMemoryError.

THE FORM THE DATA SUPPORTS. Per-slice-per-batch unit cost, backed out of three recorded points at u = trainable blocks:
  u=4  -> 1.2142
  u=6  -> 1.3350   (the fitted point, GB_PER_SLICE)
  u=12 -> 1.7730
A two-parameter line a + b*u fitted on u=4 and u=6 gives a=0.9726, b=0.0604, and predicts u=12 at 1.697 against 1.773 measured — 4.5% off, on a HELD-OUT point that also differs in batch and slice count. The current pure ratio predicts 2.67 at u=12, 51% over. The intercept a is the frozen forward: 0.97/1.335 = 73% of a fully-open block's cost is the forward pass, which is the right order for bf16 activations against fp32 grads+Adam.

WHY THIS IS THE SHAPE, NOT A FUDGE. It is the same failure as knee-kwdh, knee-ylp0 and knee-bj90 one term further along: a term fitted at one configuration and handed to another. The difference is that this time there are three measured points on the axis and a held-out check, rather than one point and an invented constant.

FIX: `GB_PER_SLICE * (slices + 1) * step` where step's trainable factor becomes (FROZEN_SHARE + (1 - FROZEN_SHARE) * trainable / depth)-shaped, derived from the two fitted points rather than assumed. Re-run `budget_residuals` after: the three CAP UNDER DEMAND rows are the acceptance test, and it graduates into nox when `--assert` passes clean.
close_reason: Fixed in 3b4d2e6. The trainable-blocks term is now affine (TRAINABLE_FLOOR 0.9726 + TRAINABLE_PER_BLOCK 0.0604 per open block, normalised at 6) instead of a pure ratio. Fitted on the four-open and six-open ledger points, twelve-open held back: both held-out twelve-open runs (encoder_adapt_thawed -32.8% -> +4.3%, band_dense_llrd -32.7% -> +4.5%) land inside 4.5%. unfreeze4_s2026 goes +35.7% -> -0.0% but it is a fit point, so that is construction not evidence. budget_residuals: 3 runs capped below measured demand -> 2. Only those three rows move; every arm at the default unfreeze_last derives what it derived before, because the line's value at six IS GB_PER_SLICE.

title: models/model.py is 731 lines against a 750 god-file gate, and StudyModel holds two responsibilities
description:
`kneemri/models/model.py` is the largest file in the tree at 731 lines. `[tool.structure]` file_max is 750 and ENFORCED, so the next feature that touches this file blocks the gate — the same way arm_check.py did at 789 on 2026-08-23, which is what forced the ArmHeader extraction mid-change rather than on purpose.

The split is already visible in the method list. StudyModel does two things:

FORWARD (the architecture): per_slice, check_whole_stack, forward, slot_features, over_depth, slice_features, supervised, fingerprint, _tokens, _pool.

ENCODER SURGERY (the optimisation plumbing, roughly lines 397-708): load_trained, _blocks, low_rank, applied, _opened_blocks, _base_parameters, parameter_groups, _readout_parameters, _open_blocks, _opened, _last_blocks, compile_encoder, recompute_activations. That is ~310 lines about LoRA wrapping, block freezing, parameter groups, torch.compile and activation recompute — none of which the forward pass reads.

DESIGN: lift the second group into `kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py` as an `EncoderSurgery` holding the backbone (and whatever readout parameters it needs). StudyModel keeps THIN DELEGATING methods for the six names consumers actually call — low_rank, parameter_groups, compile_encoder, recompute_activations, load_trained, applied — because a caller reaching `model.surgery.low_rank(...)` is exactly the chained-call-into-a-stranger the demeter gate exists to refuse. Delegation costs ~25 lines back and nets ~250 out.

CONSUMERS (audited, all through StudyModel and so unchanged by this): run_setup.py:332-337, serve_bench.py:206, holdout_predictions.py:63, members.py:638, landed.py:146.

CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: model.py drops well under 750, the surgery module gets its own mirror tests, and a smoke recipe (`arm_check --smoke`-sized, 60 studies 1 epoch) trains and reports the same `applied()` dict — landed.py reads that dict to assert a flag actually fired, so it is the one output that proves the surgery still runs rather than merely imports.

title: TrainingOptions is a 666-line god-config with 55 flags and six disjoint responsibilities
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25. kneemri/training/options.py: 666 lines, 55 add_argument calls, LCOM4 = 6 - the
highest in the tree by a factor of 1.5 (next is CropAlignment at 4). The cohesion detector names the six
components itself, so the seams do not need to be invented:

  {band, crop, reading} · {routing} · {cache} · {supervision} · {sampled} · {thinned}

Six groups sharing one class means every consumer of one flag imports all fifty-five, and every new arm
flag lands in the same file regardless of what it configures. It is also the reason the arm scripts pass
long undifferentiated flag strings that arm_check then has to re-parse to price.

PROPOSAL: keep TrainingOptions as the composition root, move each component to its own frozen dataclass
beside its consumer (per the repo rule that a supplementary type lives beside its producer, not in a
types bucket). The parser stays one parser - what splits is the STATE, not the CLI surface.

CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: every arm script in experiments/arms/ must produce a byte-identical
invocation before and after, and arm_check --switches must report the same switch set. That is the
equality check; without it this is a rewrite with a chance of silently dropping a flag, and a dropped
flag is a run that reads as a fact about an architecture.
notes:
AUDITED AND PARTLY REFUSED 2026-08-25 (e2e7f7f).

The proposal in this bead - nest each cohesion component into its own dataclass - is REFUSED, and the
refusal is the finding. `TrainingOptions.parse` is `cls(**vars(parser().parse_args()))`, so argparse's
dest names and this dataclass's field names are one set. FIVE separate guards walk that set FLAT, each
against a defect that already happened:

  switch_coverage.py:80,84   - proves no flag is left unarmed by every arm
  landed.py:315,322          - proves no write-off names a flag TrainingOptions no longer has
  tests/integration/argv_to_checkpoint.py:495 - proves every declared field is READ by a run
  tests/unit/kneemri/training/options.py:103  - asserts dests == field names, exactly
  tests/unit/kneemri/runs/member_record.py:144 - a new field lands in exactly one of three places

Nesting makes all five recurse. That is MORE code guarding the same defects, which is the opposite of
what this bead wanted. And the split it asks for already exists in the shape this repo chose: crop,
band, reading, routing and supervision are each scalar fields plus a grouping property.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, and is now fixed: `sampled` and `thinned`. Two numpy methods on a config
object, called from exactly one place, taking and returning exactly the tuple `ReportFolds.holdout`
produces. They are the next two steps of the SPLIT, not a statement about a recipe. Moved to
`core/data/corpus/folds.py` as `FitPositions`, together with the two disclaimers train.py spelled out
inline (`caveats`). options.py no longer imports numpy at all.

WHY LCOM4 WENT 6 -> 5 AND NOT 6 -> 4: the new `positions` property is itself a component, exactly as
crop/band/routing are. LCOM4 on this class is MEASURING THE ACCEPTED PATTERN, not a defect - it cannot
drop below about 5 while scalar-fields-plus-grouping-property stands, and driving it lower means
nesting. Do not chase that number here.

The equality constraint this bead asked for was met: the field set is byte-identical at 63 either side,
so every arm invocation and every switch the coverage walk reports are unchanged.

REMAINING, IF ANYTHING: the file is ~625 lines of which the large majority is argparse help text - i.e.
documentation, and the most valuable thing in it. Each field's default is spelled in two homes (the
dataclass and the flag), but that drift is already caught totally by options.py test_defaults, which
asserts whole-object equality. Generating the parser from the fields would remove ~55 duplicated
defaults at the cost of a reflection machine and would have to re-home the help text anyway. Not worth
it. Closing.

title: 68 CLI entrypoints hand-roll the same six-line preamble; ~300 lines of it are pure duplication
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 over kneemri/ + core/ (163 modules, 36.9k lines):

  ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)   55 modules
  logging.basicConfig(...)              60 modules
  --paths default paths.yaml            45 modules
  DataRoot.from_config(arguments.paths) 45 modules
  if __name__ == '__main__': main()     61 modules
  'for line in X.report(...): logger.info(line)'  24 modules
  add_argument calls, total             308

Three read in full (core/data/corpus/band_coverage.py, kneemri/evaluation/label_stability.py,
kneemri/evaluation/paired_floor.py) open with the SAME five statements in the same order before any
module-specific line appears. That is not a coincidence of style: it is the repo's only CLI contract,
written out 45-60 times instead of once, and it is why main() is the complexity hotspot in the tree
(arm_check.main CC 21, report_prices 14, slot_ties.main 13, mount_check.main 12).

There is NO shared CLI helper today. kneemri/commands.py is an index GENERATOR (it parses modules for a
top-level main and rewrites kneemri/README.md); it does not run anything.

PROPOSAL: core/cli.py holding the contract once - the parser seeded from __doc__, --paths declared once,
logging configured once, DataRoot resolved once, and a report(lines) sink for the 24 modules that print a
line iterator. A module then declares only its own arguments and its body.

THE RISK, stated up front so the work is judged on it: a CLI framework trades explicit lines for
indirection, and a bad one makes every entrypoint harder to read than the six lines it replaced. The bar
is that a module using it must be SHORTER and no less obvious, and that argparse stays visible rather
than being wrapped in a decorator DSL. If the first three ports do not read better, the finding stands
and the framework does not.

Do NOT port all 68 in one commit. Port three (one per package), measure the delta, then decide.
notes:
36 entrypoints ported to core.cli.Command in 519a396 (91 lines net, argparse leaves 30 modules) and 18 report loops collapsed to command.report in aa12a10. Every ported entrypoint smoked with --help and answers with --paths in its options. Three modules built their logger inside main() below where the preamble needs it; the definition moved up. STILL HAND-ROLLED, deliberately, each for a different reason worth its own read: arm_check (no --paths in the preamble block), label_probe and protocol_prior (statements between parse_args and basicConfig), run_comparison, holdout_backfill, teacher_readings (no canonical ArgumentParser line). Six left of 42.
41 of 42 ported (c7f5ca0). Only arm_check left, and DELIBERATELY: its parser has no --paths (an arm's paths travel inside TrainingOptions) and Command always adds one, so porting it would add a dead flag. That one belongs to knee-eydz.

title: Rigid test-time views on the shipping roster — the last unmeasured serving axis
