PRE-REGISTERED, against the 0.937 champion with one seat swapped and everything else held - same vote, same overlap, same kit, same count:
  >= 0.939  the regularisation axis buys a seat the ruler cannot see. That licenses re-reading every arm killed on a small negative offline delta, which is a large backlog.
  0.935-0.939  inside the board's own repeat noise at this band. Reads as neutral; the member is not the lever but the ruler's blindness is not refuted either.
  <= 0.933  the swap costs. The offline number was right about this member, and the blindness argument does not extend to the regularisation axis specifically.
Whichever way it lands, it is a REPEAT MEASUREMENT at the 0.937 band, which this project has exactly one of.
notes:
2026-08-24T12:26Z — SHIPPED as kneemri-augseat v1, submission watcher armed (logs/submit_augseat.log). Zero card; distill_pairs is on the card meanwhile.

The pre-registration in the kernel docstring TIGHTENS the one written here, because lastseat ran first and supplied the control this bead never had. lastseat held everything and exchanged the same fold-0 seat for a SAME-TYPE member of HIGHER solo quality (small_batch6_s2026, +0.0011) and read 0.937 — the champion's own number to the tick. So a same-type exchange at seven members moves nothing even when solo quality rises. Any movement from augseat is therefore attributable to the KIND of distance and to nothing else: not seat scatter, not solo score.

Consequence for this bead's own bands: the 0.935-0.939 'neutral' band now splits. A tie no longer leaves the blindness argument merely un-refuted — a member 0.0076 WORSE offline holding the board flat is itself evidence the ruler over-prices in-distribution fit. What a tie would kill is the SEAT argument, not the RULER argument. Recorded in the kernel docstring's 0.936-0.939 band.
augseat (55743145) scored 0.936 board, recorded in comp/board.jsonl as augseat_v1 and in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md. Seven members, kit e7b65a0 (sha read from the kernel log), one fold-0 seat = aug_long_s2026 in place of lastseat's small_batch6_s2026. Lands in the pre-registered 0.936-0.939 band: type does not carry at seven. Third entry in a row at 0.936-0.937 across a single-seat exchange.

title: The GPU lock is machine-scoped but only one project speaks it, and that cost an arm today
description:
2026-08-24 09:22Z I started ema_dense; it held $HOME/.gpu.lock and its free-VRAM gate correctly read ~30 GB free against the 28934 MiB the recipe reserves. At 09:24Z the sibling project started a ~4.8 GB job that did not take that lock. Total went to 31.8 GB of 32.6 and the arm reported 94 img/s against its own peak of 1221 - PCIe paging, 13x, which turns 72 minutes into fifteen hours. Killed at 09:31Z; nvidia-smi went 31.8 -> 7.2 GB, which is how the 24.7/4.8/2.3 split was measured.

TWO SEPARATE HOLES, and only one of them is fixable inside this tree.

1. THE LOCK IS SPOKEN BY ONE SIDE. It was moved to $HOME on 2026-08-21 precisely so both projects could resolve it identically without reading each other's config, after the same collision in the other direction (their eval at 11.4 GB, our arm at 1923 MiB free, parked an hour on a lock they could not see). The move was correct and incomplete: nobody told them the path. Letter sent (biohub inbox, 2026-08-24) with the four-line contract - atomic mkdir, pid inside, clear-if-dead, release-only-if-still-mine. This half is now blocked on them, not on us.

2. BOTH MECHANISMS ONLY READ THE CARD AT START TIME. wait_for_free_card queries memory.free once before launching and never again; hold_card serialises STARTS. A foreign job arriving ninety seconds in is invisible to both by construction. The heartbeat DETECTS the resulting collapse - it is what printed the 94-vs-1221 line - but detection fires after the card is already being wasted, and today it fired into a log nobody was watching for another seven minutes.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is an action on the heartbeat's own detection. It has the number that proves paging (throughput against the run's own peak) and it currently only prints. Options, cheapest first: (a) have the heartbeat write a line into logs/ that a watcher can Monitor on, so a human or session learns in seconds rather than minutes; (b) have it re-read memory.free on collapse and NAME whether a foreign process appeared, which turns 'STALLED' into 'STALLED, and 4.8 GB arrived after you started'; (c) have it abort the run, which is wrong by default - a transient stall is not a foreign job, and killing a fit ten epochs in wastes the card time the abort was meant to save.

(b) is the one to build: it costs one nvidia-smi query on an already-exceptional path, it makes the log self-diagnosing, and it does not take any decision away from the operator.

MY OWN ERROR IS PART OF THE RECORD. At 09:12Z I wrote to biohub that the card was theirs and to plan against a free card. At 09:22Z I removed logs/YIELD_CARD and started the arm. The lock cannot fix a person breaking their own arrangement ten minutes after making it.
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-24 by b29cdda. The fix is NOT the lock: the sibling adopted the protocol as logs/CARD_CLAIM rather than as $HOME/.gpu.lock, so the machine has two mechanisms each covering one direction. Reading theirs costs nothing where a lock nobody else takes protects nobody, so experiments/lib.sh now globs ../*/logs/CARD_CLAIM (wait_out_peer_claim) and writes ours in their format (claim_card). Bounded by the peer's OWN expected_finish, not a timeout of ours, and a stale claim is ignored LOUDLY - a killed peer's file does not vanish, which is the cross-project version of the dead-holder failure the mkdir lock already learned. Four branches verified: park, expired, unparseable, released. Detection side landed too (CardMemory): a STALLED line now names whether VRAM vanished after this run started, which is the seven minutes of hand attribution the 09:22Z collision cost.

title: The door-closing arithmetic rests on a slope never measured in the region we now occupy
description:
comp/SUBMISSIONS.md line ~1960 closes the plan with arithmetic: 0.937 -> 0.950 is +0.013 board = +0.0068 offline at +1.92, against a measured offline ceiling of ~0.872 (+0.0026 over the champion), so the requirement is ~2.6x the entire remaining headroom of the audited space, and seat swaps, ensemble width, decode knobs and vote rules are 'arithmetically short by 3x'.

That conclusion is only as good as the constant, and the constant has a defect the backfill did NOT fix. board_transfer's own output names it: the four best entries (allfit, finalfit, sevenplane, accumseat) are ONE-SIDED and enter no pair, three of them because --fold -1 erased their offline number. So +1.92 is fitted entirely on entries at or below board 0.933, and every use of it above 0.933 is an EXTRAPOLATION - including the one that closes the door.

The direction of the risk is not symmetric. If the board-per-offline ratio STEEPENS near the top (plausible: the metric is a mean of twelve AUCs, and the labels that are still cheap to move are the ones every member already gets right, so late offline gains concentrate in the hard labels the board also weights), then the offline headroom needed for +0.013 is smaller than +0.0068 and the audited space is not arithmetically dead. If it FLATTENS, the door is shut harder than stated. We cannot tell, because the pairs that would tell us are exactly the ones --fold -1 destroyed.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT. A pair of entries above 0.933 that BOTH carry an offline number - i.e. a fold-0-only pool scoring near the champion. weakseven (0.908, offline 0.8562) is the nearest thing and it is 0.029 below. The 0.933 chain (gradeswap 0.8694, greedy7 0.8712) is the top of the measured range, so one more fold-0 entry meaningfully above 0.933 would extend the fit into the region that matters. That is a SLOT, not card: the fold-0 members already exist and are packaged.

CONSEQUENCE IF IGNORED. Every 'this family is arithmetically short' verdict written since 2026-08-24 inherits an untested extrapolation, and those verdicts are currently what stops us running cheap arms.
notes:
THE FIX IS BLOCKED BY THE SAME DAMAGE, and saying so is part of the finding. A fold-0-only pool meaningfully above 0.933 is what would extend the fit, but 0.933 IS the fold-0 ceiling as measured: gradeswap/accumseat/greedy7 all read it, member_curve's greedy accumulation saturated four steps running, and the seven-member vote is flat to wholesale exchange. There is no rearrangement of existing fold-0 members that clears it, so the slot cannot be spent on this today.

The only way the fold-0 ceiling moves is a BETTER FOLD-0 MEMBER, which needs card. ema_dense (knee-56w5) is exactly that shape and is on the card now: if it lands in its top band (>=0.8640 against band_dense's 0.8578) it is both an EMA verdict AND the first fold-0 member above the seated band since the ceiling was declared, which would let a fold-0 entry be built that extends the slope fit into the region the door-closing arithmetic extrapolates through. Two questions, one 72-minute run. Do not re-plan this bead before that arm reads.

title: Instrument: is allfit's +0.004 the DATA or the EMA that rode along with it?
description:
PRICE: ~72 min of card (band_dense's recipe, 12 epochs at ~361 s). P(clears 1.5%) = 0.02 — this is NOT sold as an improvement and must not be read as one.

WHAT IT BUYS. kneemri-allfit read 0.937 on 2026-08-24, +0.004 over the 0.933 chain, and it is the only board movement this project has produced. It was written up as the ALL-DATA axis. But every _ff member is its _s2026 twin's flags plus --fold -1 AND --ema, and the twins carry no EMA. Two variables moved together on the entry that moved the board. The interpretation named the confound at the time and read the number as a data result anyway, because --fold -1 members have no offline number of any kind and the alternative was untestable on that pool.

THE TRICK. EMA is not a data flag, so it can be measured at fold 0 where the 909-study holdout still works, against band_dense 0.8578 already on disk. The confounded pair cannot be separated where it occurred; the confounding VARIABLE can be measured where the confound does not exist. No control arm is queued — quick over matched.

BANDS, pre-registered in experiments/arms/ema_dense.sh before the run, floor 0.0062:
  >= 0.8640 — EMA is real, allfit's data reading is DEBITED, and EMA becomes a FREE lever on all seven seats.
  +0.0015 to +0.0062 — directional, unresolvable; allfit's reading stands but carries a named co-variable; no further card.
  -0.0015 to +0.0015 — FLAT; EMA cannot be what the board paid for, allfit's data reading is CLEAN, knee-tfj3's closure stands.
  <= -0.0015 — NEGATIVE, and the most interesting: allfit scored 0.937 while PAYING for EMA, so the data axis is LARGER than +0.004 and the seventh-seat decision was made against an understated curve. Re-opens the seventh seat.

HARNESS SUSPECT NAMED IN ADVANCE: --ema defaults False, so a flag that never reaches the trainer yields a run byte-identical to the control. If the answer is flat, assert ema:true in the checkpoint config and assert the weights DIFFER from band_dense's before believing the null.
notes:
QUEUE REORDER 2026-08-26 10:18Z: ema_dense is no longer the next arm. knee-ep74 (calib_dense) reopened
above it on ratio.

  calib_dense  ~40-50 min, control FREE (band_dense 0.8578 on the ledger), single variable, measured
               mechanism (+0.0072 held / -0.0020 unheld on the span corner), predicts >0.860
  ema_dense    ~72 min, needs no new control either, but the term was just re-priced from OUTSIDE:
               a competitor's single-variable fold-0 ablation reads EMA at +0.003 against this arm's
               own pre-registered +0.0062 bar (research/2026-08-26_the-ablation-table-a-competitor-
               published.md)

NOT A DEMOTION OF THIS BEAD'S OTHER HALF. ema_dense is also the INSTRUMENT that splits allfit's +0.004
into DATA vs the EMA that rode along with it (_ff members are their _s2026 twin's flags PLUS --fold -1
PLUS --ema). No outside number can answer that -- it is about OUR confound -- so that value is
untouched and this arm still runs. It runs SECOND.
close_reason: FLAT: ema_dense 0.8588 vs band_dense 0.8578 = +0.0010, inside the pre-registered -0.0015..+0.0015 band. So allfit's +0.004 is a DATA result and knee-tfj3's closure stands. Harness suspect cleared not assumed: checkpoint config stamps ema:True and the score differs from the control, so the flag reached the trainer. Outside single-variable ablation reads the same flag at +0.003; two independent measurements, same sign, both sub-floor. BONUS FINDING, recorded in experiments/README.md: ema_dense's nearest seated neighbour is 0.9306, the tightest twin any candidate has posted -- an EMA member averages the SAME trajectory as its non-EMA twin, so it is disqualified as a diversity lever by construction, whatever its solo number does.

title: Gate: every result heading in SUBMISSIONS.md must have a matching id in board.jsonl
description: comp/board.jsonl went unwritten from 2026-08-20 to 2026-08-24 while comp/SUBMISSIONS.md stayed current, so seven entries (sevenplane, gradeswap, accumseat, greedy7, finalfit, weakseven, allfit) lived in prose only. board_transfer prices every experiment from board.jsonl, so the slope was silently fitted on a four-day-old field, and the 2026-08-24 hand refit that filled the gap mis-paired gradeswap's offline with finalfit's board and produced +2.14 where the backfilled tool reads +1.92. Third stale-claim-in-a-live-document this week and none of the three was caught by a gate. Build the check: parse the '## ' / '### Result:' headings of SUBMISSIONS.md for entry names, parse board.jsonl for ids, assert every scored entry named in prose has a row. Should also assert no row carries an offline number for a pool containing a --fold -1 member, which is the entity error that produced the bad anchor.
notes:
Built as kneemri/kaggle/board_check.py, but joined on the KAGGLE SUBMISSION REF rather than by parsing SUBMISSIONS.md headings. Heading parsing cannot work: kernel names repeat (sixfresh shipped twice), prose spells them freely, and a heading score is not unique (seven entries read 0.937). The ref is Kaggle's own identifier and the listing costs no slot.

What it found: the record held 34 of 58 submissions. Fifteen scored all-ours entries were absent, including basedense_v1 (the entry comp/champion.json pins) and votefit_v1 at 0.938 (the best score this project owns). board_transfer's compression constant read +1.82 on the incomplete set and +1.72 on the complete one, over 21 ensemble entries with 0 inversions in 108 resolved pairs. Kernels ship quoting +1.82, +1.92 and +2.14, all fitted short.

Record backfilled 34 -> 58 rows. Every submission now has a row; the ten this file will not price carry scope: excluded plus a why, which is what turns the check from a heuristic about which absences were meant into an exact set comparison. A submission whose description stated only a delta records offline: null - a delta is not a level.

The bead's second ask is in: unpriceable() refuses any offline number over a pool naming a --fold -1 seat, by NAME (_ff suffix plus final_ws_e12), because the disk rule needs a data root and this must run in CI.

First live run found five prose gaps besides - fusion25_v2, dark6_v1, dark7_v1, v3seat_v1, votefit_v1 priced here and named nowhere in SUBMISSIONS.md; the ledger stopped at peak8. Both halves repaired. Now reads 58 recorded, 58 live, no refusals. Committed fb76367.

title: Five _ff members inside the live allfit entry carry no serving witness
description:
witness_check --device cpu --members calib_span_ff grade_ladder_ff base_dense_ff lr4e-5_ws_ff through_dense_ff reads 0 ok, 5 unverified, 0 refused. All five report 'no witness (trained before the check existed, or a published member)'.

These five are seats in kneemri-allfit, which is on the board scoring now. Six of that entry's seven seats therefore have nothing for the fingerprint check to compare against, so a member that serves differently in the kernel than it did in training would not be caught, and the pre-registered bands in the kernel docstring would be read against a contaminated number.

Suspected cause, NOT yet confirmed: the witness is recorded at holdout-evaluation time, and a --fold -1 member holds out nothing and never evaluates a holdout, so the recording step is never reached. If that is right it is structural, not an oversight, and every future all-data member inherits it. The fix would be to record the witness from a fixed handful of TRAINING studies replayed through the training path, which is what the witness actually needs (a replay fingerprint), not a holdout.

Confirm the mechanism before fixing: find where witness is written and check whether a --fold -1 run reaches it.
notes:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-24 07:53Z, and FIXED for future members.

Mechanism, exactly as suspected: kneemri/training/fitting.py Fitting.ranked returns predicted=None when
'not fold.scored', and Fold.scored is 'len(self.holdout) > 0'. Fitting.keep then had
'witness = None if predicted is None else ...'. A --fold -1 run holds nothing back, so the witness was
taken from a holdout that does not exist. Structural, not an oversight — every all-data member ever
fitted has an empty witness, including the five in the live allfit entry.

The unit test ASSERTED the defect: test_an_unscored_run_reports_no_number_and_keeps_the_last_epoch
carried 'assert kept.witness is None, "there is no held-out study to witness"'. That sentence is the
whole error in miniature — nothing in a replay fingerprint needs the studies to be unseen. Line removed.

FIX: new Fitting.witnessed(fold, predicted). With a holdout it behaves as before; without one it takes
the first WITNESS_STUDIES TRAINING positions and replays them through trainer.predict. Those studies are
memorised, so the numbers say nothing about generalisation and were never asked to — what they pin is
the READING (img, slots, decode resolution, window, precision), and every defect this check has caught
was a consumer-side default disagreeing with a recorded value. RNG-neutral: Trainer.batches takes
shuffle=False on this path and never draws from the generator, so a member fitted through it is
bit-identical to one fitted before.

Also fixed comp/witness_check.py's message, which said 'trained before the check existed, or a published
member' — a wrong cause that reads as a known one, and it retired the question for a whole board entry.

REMAINING, not done here: the five _ff members already shipped cannot gain a witness without retraining.
A post-hoc backfill looks possible in principle — load the checkpoint and replay trainer.predict over
eight studies using the config recorded IN the checkpoint, then compare against the serving path. Same
comparison, done later. Worth building only if the allfit board read is close to a pre-registration band
boundary, since its value is protecting that interpretation before a 7.3h card commitment.

title: An arm ran ~5h of card past its own written stop condition, and nothing checked
description:
final_fit_six.sh's header states its own gate: 'Run this ONLY if kneemri-finalfit reads 0.936 or above on the board. At 0.934-0.935 keep the one member and stop; at 0.933 or below this arm is retired unrun.'

kneemri-finalfit read 0.934 (submission 55715039, 2026-08-23). The gate says: keep the one member and STOP. The arm was launched anyway and ran four members to completion plus a fifth to epoch 10 of 12 — roughly 5 h of card — before anyone re-read the header. It was stopped on 2026-08-24 at 06:19Z only because a PEER PROJECT asked for the card, not because the gate was checked.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not the arm being wrong: the header is exactly right, was written before the board reading, and priced the decision honestly at '93 min of card decides these ~7 h'. The cost-tiered design worked. The defect is that its verdict had no consumer.

WHY IT SURVIVED. Every existing check guards a SHIPMENT or a PROCESS: arm_check reads flags, card_check asks the device, queue_check counts watchers, ledger_check reconciles status, kit/mount/champion_check guard the kernel. Nine checks, and not one of them asks 'does this arm's own precondition still hold against the latest board reading?' The gate lived in a bash comment, which is the one place nothing executes.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING: the cost was mis-stated twice while the arm ran, both times by using the wrong epoch count. Member 6 (band_dense_long_ff) is a 24-epoch seat, ~7.3 h at the observed ~1100 s/epoch, and was described to the peer project as 3.7 h and before that as finishing by 07:30Z. The script's own header even names the 24-epoch seat as the first to drop under contention. So the arm carried its stop condition AND its contention rule AND its true cost in prose, and all three were re-derived worse from memory.

THE FIX WORTH BUILDING, and it should be mechanical because prose already failed: arms declare their gate as DATA rather than a comment — a line the launcher can evaluate, naming the board entry and the threshold ('gate: kneemri-finalfit >= 0.936'). arm_check then refuses to arm an arm whose gate is unmet or unread, the way kit_check refuses a stale kit. comp/SUBMISSIONS.md already holds the board readings the gate would be evaluated against, so the data side exists; what is missing is the declaration and the check.

CHEAPER INTERIM, if the above is not worth the build: arm_check greps an arm for a header line matching 'ONLY if|retired unrun|gate:' and, when it finds one, refuses to arm silently — it prints the sentence and requires an explicit acknowledgement flag. That does not evaluate anything, but it puts the sentence in front of the person at the moment the slot is spent rather than in a file nobody opens after launch.

RELATED: the yield mechanism added at 72d4cc8 (logs/YIELD_CARD, checked per run_train call) is what made stopping cheap once the problem was seen. It does not prevent this — it only makes the recovery not require killing a shell by pid.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-25. A gate is now DATA: '# gate: <entry> >= <threshold>' in an arm header, parsed by kneemri/experiments/arm_gate.py (ArmGate), evaluated against comp/board.jsonl, which already held every scored entry. arm_check gained an UNMET-GATE verdict — always-named on every sweep, and REFUSING on the run that arms an arm (--only), so an unmet gate costs a queue slot rather than five hours of card. An UNREAD gate refuses for the same reason a low one does: an arm gated on a submission nobody pushed is the arm most likely to be launched on a hunch, and a missing board file is a check passing because its evidence is absent.

SECOND, LARGER HOLE FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, and it made the first fix a no-op until closed: every header rule resolved a header as experiments/arms/<name>.sh, but an arm is keyed by the name it PRINTS. final_fit_six.sh prints six member names and none is its filename — so the gate, the '# bead:' line and the '# control' line were all unread on exactly the arms that spend the most card. Proven live: 'arm_check --only final_fit_six' raised 'no arm printed an invocation named final_fit_six'. Fixed by recording which shell printed each name as the shells run, and falling back to it when no arms/<name>.sh exists.

That extraction is now kneemri/experiments/arm_header.py (ArmHeader: text/record/beads/controls/deliberate/gated), which also split arm_check.py back under the 750-line god-file threshold it crossed (789 -> 709).

VERIFIED LIVE: 'arm_check --only base_dense_ff' exits 1 with 'UNMET-GATE base_dense_ff: gated on kneemri-finalfit >= 0.936; the board reads 0.934' — the exact arm, the exact reading, that spent the five hours.

title: A submission slot expires worthless - spend it on the instrument when no candidate is ready
description:
On 2026-08-23 two of five slots expired unspent. The stated reason was 'nothing measured justified them', which is the wrong test and champion.json already says so: 'a submission is a verification that the pipeline runs end to end, not a measurement of a method, and it must be priced that way.' A slot gated on candidate quality is a slot gated on a bar that does not apply to it.

The cost is concrete and was sitting in the queue: knee-825t is blocked on a THIRD board point outside the current offline range, and that point needs NO training - a deliberately weakened roster (drop the top two members) reads ~0.860 offline against the existing chain's 0.8648-0.8691, extending the calibration x-axis by roughly 3x. Two days of that were available and both expired.

RULE: at the last check before 00:00Z rollover, any unspent slot goes to the best INSTRUMENT entry available, in this priority: (1) a real candidate if one exists, (2) a knee-825t calibration point off the current offline range, (3) an end-to-end verification of a serving path not yet exercised on the board. Never let one expire on the grounds that nothing is good enough - nothing being good enough is what makes the instrument entry the right spend.
notes:
SLOT PLAN for the 00:00Z reset, decided 2026-08-24 21:56Z rather than improvised at the reset.

All four queued kernels pass mount_check (count8, dark6, votefit, farswap). A fifth kernel, farseat, is
REFUSED - it names vjepa_warm_s2026, a member that does not exist. Tonight's convergence measurement
retires the reason it was built: vjepa_member died at 10 of 12, and a kill at 10 costs a median of +0.0000
across 54 finished runs, so the V-JEPA warm re-run buys a clean exit code and not a score. Do not build
farseat's member to unblock farseat.

The ordering follows the goal-pricing interpretation, which forbids spending slots on another seat swap.
Ranked by whether the entry can TEACH something rather than by expected board points:

1. votefit  - rank-vote combination instead of averaging. The only queued kernel that changes the
              COMBINATION MECHANISM, so it is the one whose result is not already a draw from the
              0.930-0.937 distribution. Fire first, soon after 00:00Z.
2. farswap  - swaps in the far encoder (DINOv3 vits16). Diversity axis, which is the axis the owner
              named explicitly: it is about diversity, not averaging seven numbers that are the same
              number. Fire second, well separated.
3. count8   - eight members. Member count is measured and every entry lands inside 0.930-0.937; this is
              one more draw from a sampled distribution. Instrument value only.
4. dark6    - six dark (--fold -1) members. The all-data dose axis is recorded as real, sub-linear and
              SPENT (+0.003 over five extra seats). Lowest information of the four.
5. HOLD     - decided from the first results, per the standing directive to spread and keep the last one
              back. If votefit or farswap moves, the fifth repeats that axis; if neither does, the fifth
              is an instrument slot under this bead's own rule rather than a fifth seat draw.

Spread them: a slot that expires unspent is worth nothing, but four fired inside an hour measure one
board state four times.

title: Does cross-slot misregistration actually cost AUC, and only on the focal findings?
description:
crop_alignment measured the INPUT: 5.7 mm median cross-slot spread, ~15 px at 0.387 mm/px, against a 1-2 mm meniscal tear. It says nothing about the OUTPUT. Both fixes it licenses (tissue-centred crop, slot-to-slot registration) cost a 99 GB cache rebuild plus hours of refit, so a cheap instrument has to gate them.

kneemri/evaluation/alignment_damage.py joins the per-study spread against the holdout mix and asks whether studies whose slots disagree score worse, SEPARATELY for the seven FOCAL and five REGIONAL findings. The partition is core.data.corpus.anatomy.Extent, which is assigned from structure and whose docstring forbids fitting it to results — so it is pre-existing, not fitted to this question.

THE CONFOUND, and why the raw gap is not the read: a study with a scattered tissue centroid is plausibly just a worse study, and a worse study scores lower on everything. That moves both classes together. Misregistration moves only the focal half. The DIFFERENTIAL (focal gap minus regional gap) is the part difficulty cannot produce.

PRICE: ~76 min CPU for the spread pass (running, 909 holdout studies, 12 workers so the trainer keeps its loader margin) plus seconds for the join. Zero GPU. It cannot raise a score; it can only kill a rebuild.
notes:
PRE-REGISTERED, on the differential and its 95% bootstrap interval.

SIZING THE BANDS. A perfect registration fix would lift the poorly-agreeing half toward the well-agreeing one, on focal findings only. That is differential x (7/12 labels) x (1/2 the studies) = differential x 0.29 on the mean AUC. So the 1.5% bar needs a differential near 0.051, and even a 0.01 move needs 0.034.

  >= 0.050, interval excluding 0  the registration fix could plausibly clear the bar. Start it: it is the
                                 only mechanism measured here that reaches 1.5%.
  0.020 - 0.050                  real but sub-bar on its own. Do NOT start a 99 GB rebuild for it alone;
                                 hold it as a rider on any rebuild something else pays for.
  <= 0.020, or interval spanning 0  the registration fix is NOT licensed by this evidence.

WHAT A NULL WOULD NOT RULE OUT, stated before the number so it cannot be composed afterwards:
  - the COMMON-MODE offset, which is ~2/3 of the raw displacement and is INVISIBLE to this design by
    construction — every study shares it, so it cannot separate studies. Killing registration here leaves
    the CENTRING fix exactly where knee-yrf left it, priced on retention.
  - the proxy. An Otsu mass centroid is not a joint centre and is dragged by coil, fat and the far limb.
    That noise attenuates any true gap toward zero, so a null here is a weak null, not a strong one.
  - a finer fix than a rigid shift. This tests whether DISAGREEMENT predicts error, not whether alignment
    would help a model that was trained aligned from the start.
MEASURED 2026-08-23. 909 holdout studies, champion's six scoreable members, split at 5.85 mm. focal mean gap -0.0068, regional -0.0171, DIFFERENTIAL +0.0103, 95% [-0.0305, +0.0421]. Lands in the pre-registered '<= 0.020 or interval spans zero' band: the registration fix is NOT licensed, and is dropped rather than held as a rider (the bar needed ~0.051). Unpredicted: both raw gaps are NEGATIVE, so the poorly-agreeing half scored BETTER on both classes -- the Otsu spread is not a proxy for acquisition quality, which is the assumption underwriting the whole crop_alignment reading. NOT ruled out: the common-mode offset (invisible to this design by construction; tissue-centred cropping stays priced on retention where knee-yrf left it), the proxy's attenuation toward zero, and a model TRAINED aligned from the start. Written up in experiments/README.md.

title: Do a study's slots agree where the knee is? crop_alignment was written and never run
description:
crop_alignment.py exists, is complete, and has NO ledger row, NO interpretation and NO bead. Written 2026-08-14ish and left.

THE GAP IT FILLS. interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-21_what_survives_the_closures.md dismisses CoPAS's +0.056 ROI-crop component with 'we already crop to 130 mm'. That answers crop PRESENCE. The mechanism CoPAS (Nat Commun 15:7637) actually credits is 'cropping along ROI can align the spatial position across sequences' — and a 130 mm box about the IMAGE CENTRE aligns nothing. knee-yrf measured the within-slot offsets (|dy| median 6.9 mm, p90 18.0, 10/60 studies >20 mm against 15 mm of margin) and was closed on RETENTION, a within-series quantity that cannot speak to cross-slot agreement.

WHY IT MATTERS. Every slot-aggregation arm this project has run landed inside the noise floor. If the box places the knee at a different offset in each slot, those arms were fusing views that do not correspond and the aggregator was never at fault.

PRICE: ~20 min CPU, 20 workers, ZERO GPU (card is on final_fit_six for 6.4h). An INSTRUMENT, not an improvement — it cannot raise a score. Justified as an instrument because it either closes an axis or licenses one with a published +0.056 behind it.
P(clears the bar) n/a — it is not an improvement arm. P(it changes what runs next) ~0.5.

PRE-REGISTERED, on the per-study SPREAD of offset MAGNITUDE across routed slots:
  spread p50 >= 10 mm — slots genuinely disagree. The alignment mechanism is live here, the flat
    slot-aggregation arms get a named cause, and a derived-joint-centre crop becomes a DATA lever
    rather than the correctness fix knee-yrf declined to pay for.
  spread p50 4-10 mm — partial. Read the PER-PLANE signed components, where the axes are consistent,
    before any verdict; a sagittal-vs-axial magnitude comparison is the only honest cross-plane one.
  spread p50 <= 4 mm — slots already agree. Alignment is UNAVAILABLE here at any price. Closes the
    axis and forces a different explanation for the six flat slot-aggregation arms.

LIMIT, from the module's own docstring: an Otsu mass centroid is not a joint centre — it is dragged by coil, fat and the far limb, and knee-yrf measured that tissue-centring's WORST series is worse than image-centring's at 80 mm. This bounds the question from one side only: a small spread is conclusive, a large spread is suggestive.
notes: MEASURED 2026-08-23. Middle band: within-study cross-slot spread p50 5.7 mm, p90 10.7, max 18.8. Per-slot |offset| p50 9-14 mm, so ~2/3 is COMMON MODE (study shifted whole, slots together) and does not break correspondence. Clean within-plane read: three sagittal slots at +10.7/+2.9/+3.4 mm anterior-posterior, so SAG_FLUID_FS is ~7.8 mm off the other two on a consistent axis. Residual 5.7 mm = ~15 px at 0.387 mm/px = 3-6x a 1-2 mm meniscal tear; predicts fine-structure labels suffer, and MCL 0.7893 / Lateral OA 0.8246 / Lateral Meniscus 0.8504 are our weakest against Effusion 0.8655 / Baker's 0.9086. Splits into TWO separable fixes: common-mode -> crop centring (knee-yrf, now with a second reason); residual -> slot-to-slot registration (the actual CoPAS mechanism). Does NOT license CoPAS's +0.056 — that was against an unaligned full-FOV baseline. Ledger row in experiments/README.md.

title: seat_value cannot price any candidate: champion roster holds an unscoreable fold -1 member
description:
kneemri/kaggle/seat_value.py:114 calls Pool.split(roster), which raises 'roster members with no holdout record: final_ws_e12.pt'. The raise is CORRECT — member_curve.py:135 argues it: a roster silently scored as 6 of 7 makes every delta below it read against the wrong base. The hole is structural: the shipped champion (finalfit, board 0.934) contains final_ws_e12, trained with --fold -1 and therefore unscoreable FOREVER. So seat_value can price no candidate at all against the entry that actually scored, and it fails only at the moment of use, as a traceback in an arm's post-run step.

Do NOT fix by softening the raise. Fix by pricing against the SCOREABLE SUBSET and stating that denominator in the output — 'priced against 6 of 7 champion members; final_ws_e12 unscoreable (fold -1)'. A labelled proxy roster is honest; a silent one is the failure the raise exists to stop.

Found 2026-08-23 when sided_pool's post-run seat step crashed. Training was unaffected.
notes: FIXED 2026-08-23. SeatValue.scoreable() partitions the pinned roster into members that carry a holdout record and ones that never can, using HoldoutRecord.exists() rather than a hand-built filename (its TWINS rule already handles the .metrics case a naive stem would get wrong). report() prices against the scoreable subset and LEADS with the denominator. Verified on the real champion, not just synthetic: 'priced against 6 of 7 champion members; final_ws_e12 unscoreable (fold -1)' / 'roster of 6: 0.8693'. The raise in RecordMix.split is untouched -- the fix is a labelled proxy, not a softened guard.

title: Member-pool globbing has no finished-run guard, and a dead member is the one greedy reaches for
description:
record_mix-style member lists are built by globbing *.holdout.npz. That file is written from EPOCH ZERO of any run, so the glob silently seats dead and in-flight members. On 2026-08-23 a focus_latmen checkpoint that died at epoch 1 sat at rank 10 of the greedy curve and inflated the peak from 0.8717 to 0.8721 — the whole apparent gain of five new members. A partially-trained member is near-random, near-random is DECORRELATED, and a greedy selector reaches for exactly that. It is the failure mode the tool is least able to warn about because it looks like the result you are hoping for.

The finished marker is the .pt checkpoint's EXISTENCE. Note .partial survives a successful run (band_dense has both) so absence-of-.partial is NOT the test.

This is the class of hole the repo's *_check convention exists to close and there is no check for it. Wanted: the pool builder refuses an npz with no .pt beside it, and a pool_check that reports what it dropped and why.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-25 (kneemri session, off-card lane).

THE HOLE IS ONE LINE: record_mix.py:90 refuses only when BOTH the checkpoint and its holdout record are missing (`if not path.exists() and not record.exists()`). A run that died leaves .partial + .holdout.npz and NO .pt, so it passes that test and is seated off its record alone.

Confirmed against the write sites, not assumed: fitting.py:149 writes .partial on every improving epoch and fitting.py:142 writes .holdout.npz with it; train.py:137 writes the .pt ONLY after Fitting.run returns. So .pt existence is exactly 'the run reached its own end', which is what the bead proposed.

BLAST RADIUS MEASURED on the processed root: 9 of 91 .holdout.npz files have no .pt beside them — aprior_dense_s2026_run1, focus_latmen_s2026, margin_smoke, raddino_dense_s2026, raddino_dense_s2026_run1, smoke_vjepa, vjepa_member_s2026, vjepa_member_s2026_run1, vjepa_member_s2026_run2. ~10% of the pool. Two of them are the crash readings already filed as knee-6477 and knee-2a82, so this guard closes those from the other side.

Dropping the rotated _run1/_run2 records is correct too, not collateral: their checkpoint was overwritten rather than rotated, so no weights exist for them either. A member with no .pt cannot ship, so it has no business scoring a seat.

displacement.sh is NOT the caller that seated the dead member: it globs "$D"/*_s2026.pt, which already excludes them. The exposure is any hand-passed or npz-derived --records list.

PLAN: RecordMix refuses a record whose .pt is absent, names it and why; pool_check reports what it dropped.
FIXED in RecordMix.readings: a record with no .pt beside it is dropped and NAMED (new RecordMix.dropped), because the trainer writes .holdout.npz每 improving epoch and the .pt only after Fitting returns — so record-without-checkpoint == a run that died, weights gone, can never be packaged. main now prints 'N of M records became members' plus the dropped names, so the denominator is on the page. Test fixtures were writing a record with NO checkpoint (record_mix + seat_value _member) — they now write the .pt too, which is the honest fixture. LIVE: over adapt_null_s2026 + vjepa_member_s2026 + raddino_dense_s2026 it reports 1 of 3, naming both dead ones. NOT CHANGED: ordinal_signal --directory globs *.holdout.npz and will still rank dead runs, but it is a read-only concordance diagnostic that prints its own denominator, not a pool that seats shippable members. No separate pool_check module: the guard fires inside the only pool builder and names the drop, so a second entrypoint would be a second place to keep in sync.

title: sided token pooling: the head has never been able to see WHERE a response sat
description:
THE MECHANISM IS A TYPE SIGNATURE, not a suspicion. All three token poolings in TOKEN_POOLINGS collapse
the patch axis — TokenPooling.reduce is typed "n t d" -> "n f" in every one, and ClassAndPatchMeanAndTail
discards even the indices topk returns. The head cannot express WHERE in the field a response sat. Five
of twelve targets are defined by exactly that: both menisci, both tibiofemoral compartments, the MCL.

MEASURED TODAY, two independent pools over the 909-study fold-0 holdout, same three labels at the bottom
of both (champion-6 mix 0.8693 / pool-of-70 mix 0.8616):
  MCL         0.8039 / 0.7893   n=171
  Lateral OA  0.8267 / 0.8246   n=233
  next worst  0.8654 / 0.8500
Every medial/lateral PAIR splits the same direction on our own fitted members as on the published ruler
(Medial-Lateral Meniscus +0.0425, Medial-Lateral OA +0.0585). Fracture is NOT a target despite reading
0.8216: n=68 gives SE ~0.04, so it is not separable from 0.90.

WHY THE HEAD AND NOT THE DATA. knee-yrg has refuted all four data-side explanations of the lateral gap —
laterality flip, slice band, prevalence, and the in-plane crop (which clips MEDIAL harder, [-0.0130,
-0.0095], pointing the wrong way). side_dense then asked the LOSS for the contrast and regressed -0.0641
with all twelve labels falling, but its compartment contrast ROSE 0.062 on demand: the encoder HOLDS the
side and the pooled head is where it is lost. Its own row deferred the remaining idea to "a head that
SEES position". This is that head.

WHY A COLUMN SPLIT IS AN ANATOMICAL SPLIT. Laterality mirrors every study onto one canonical side inside
the cache pipeline (core/data/corpus/study.py:26,52), at 100% coverage because the geometric rule reaches
the half the DICOM tag does not. In that frame medial is always the same side of the array. No new input,
no cache rebuild, no label.

THE DESIGN. ClassAndSidedMean, parts=3: class token + left-half mean + right-half mean, split on the
midline column, an odd column count dropping its centre from both halves because that column IS the
midline. It SUPERSEDES cls_mean rather than competing with it — the halves partition the grid, so their
mean is the patch mean the default emits; the head can form that sum AND the difference. One extra part,
nothing removed. That makes a flat result informative in a way the other pooling arms' were not: it says
the head could have ignored the split and did.

PRICE: 72 min of card, one arm, no cache build. P(clears 1.5% on the mean) ~ 0.10 — a long shot on the
headline, and that is the honest number. It runs FIRST anyway because the board reading differs: MCL and
Lateral OA sit 2.6 and 2.0 SE below the pool median, lifting only those two to 0.87 is +0.0091 on the
mean, and the measured board transfer of +4.67 multiplies that several times past the 0.006 gap to 0.940.

PRE-REGISTERED vs band_dense = 0.8578 on the same 909 studies:
  >= 0.8628      the split carries; go to a finer grid than two halves.
  0.8548-0.8627  inside the 0.0062 floor. NOT a refutation — read the PER-LABEL columns for MCL /
                 Lateral OA / Lateral Meniscus first; the mean can absorb a real move on 3 of 12.
  <= 0.8547      suspect the head WIDTH first (three parts changes the first linear layer's fan-in),
                 then assert Laterality fired on this cache, before blaming the idea.

WHAT A NULL WOULD NOT RULE OUT: a finer spatial split (quadrants, or compartment columns rather than
halves); the same pooling on a head that also sees depth regions; and the small-weight side regulariser
side_dense left standing, which was deferred to exactly this kind of head.

title: full-data refit of the champion's members: every shipped member throws away 20% of the corpus
description:
EVERY member in the 0.934 entry except final_ws_e12 was fitted at --fold 0, i.e. on 3,497 of 4,406
studies. The 909 held out are training data we pay for and do not use. `folds.py` already supports
--fold -1 ("trains on everything") and the champion already contains exactly one such member.

PRICE: 6 members x ~72 min = ~7.2 h of card, serial (one GPU, shared with biohub by arrangement).
P(clears 1.5% on the board) ~ 0.25. Expected offline gain per member ~+0.0029, read off the CONCAVE
data slope quarter_data fitted (each doubling buys ~0.48 of the last; 3,497 -> 4,406 is 0.33 of a
doubling). That +0.0029 is the largest number left anywhere on this board — every other axis is priced
below it, and the ensemble axis was re-confirmed exhausted today (greedy peak 0.8721 at 11-13 over 70
records, +0.0004 over yesterday's 70-record peak despite five new members from three new axes).

WHY IT IS NOT JUST ANOTHER SUB-BAR KNOB. Three reasons it is worth 7 h when a knob is not:
- It composes across members rather than replacing one. Six members each fitted on 26% more data is a
  different POOL, not a rearrangement of the current one, and the pool is what today's greedy says is
  the binding variable.
- The direction already has one board point behind it: the current champion is the first entry ever to
  contain a full-data member, and it is the best entry this project has.
- The house rule licenses it explicitly — increments below the bar still compose, and a chain of them
  that sums past it IS a result.

WHAT IT COSTS THAT IS NOT CARD TIME, and this is the real decision: a --fold -1 member is UNSCOREABLE
FOREVER (champion.json's last principle). It has seen every holdout study, so it can never be
seat-scored, curve-scored or distance-scored, and no pool containing it may report an offline mean.
Refitting six members this way makes the ENTIRE roster blind — every future roster decision is then made
against whatever the board last said, at 5 slots a day. That is why this is filed rather than started:
it trades the offline ruler for a one-way data gain.

MITIGATION that keeps the ruler: refit the SIX at --fold -1 for shipping, and keep the existing fold-0
records for every offline comparison. The pool used for SELECTION stays scoreable; only the SHIPPED
weights change. Selection is then made on fold-0 twins and executed with full-data members, which
assumes the seat ordering is invariant to the extra 26% of data — an assumption, stated, not measured.

PRE-REGISTERED: the entry either ticks (board >= 0.936, consistent with the slope times the 4.67
transfer at its low end) or it does not (<= 0.935, meaning the offline data slope does not transfer and
the fold -1 step is worth its ~+0.001 alone). Below 0.933 says the full-data members are WORSE in the
seat, which would refute the one board point this direction currently rests on.

title: annotation-holdout: a member that never trains on the 58 image-read annotations, so supervision_gap can be pointed at OUR architecture
description:
INSTRUMENT, not a score move. eleven axes have now read flat inside the 0.0062 floor (knee-jk3); knee-7d1 names the RULER as the top remaining suspect, and a label ceiling is exactly what eleven flat axes look like.

The measurement already exists: kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap, run 2026-08-14 on the published members' out-of-fold predictions (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-14_labels-or-pixels.md). aggregate labels 0.8639 vs model 0.8391; six labels sit BELOW the line with a mean gap ~0.11 -> ~0.055 over twelve labels if closed. That is the only quantity in this repo that matches the frontier gap (0.018) it needs to explain, with room over.

BLOCKER it fixes: the module needs predictions that never trained on the annotations. core/data/labels/targets.py:239-243 overrides those 58 studies' scores with the annotations and weights them at ANNOTATED_WEIGHT=3.0 in EVERY member we fit. 696 cells x 3 ~= 0.66% of total training weight, paid for with the only radiologist-truth ruler in the project.

DESIGN (machinery already in the repo): add Supervision.annotations: bool = True; guard the override with it; extend moves_the_ruler() to include 'not self.annotations'. Targets.pair then re-reads the ruler under plain Supervision (annotations=True), so the arm TRAINS without them and is SCORED on the unchanged ruler -- every ledger comparison stays valid. Record the switch in Targets.supervised() so the pre-flight landed check proves the flag fired, and wire it through options.py:171-175 and landed.py:235-243.

PRICE: ~1.6-3.2 h of card (6-12 epochs at ~950 s) for zero direct score. What it BUYS is a clean supervision_gap read on the CURRENT architecture, which either confirms the ~0.055 below-the-line gap and names which labels carry it (licensing a data move -- re-extraction -- rather than a twelfth knob), or shows it has closed and sends eleven flat axes to a different explanation. Card is busy with raddino_dense until ~21:45 UTC; this is keyboard work queued behind it.

PRE-REGISTERED READ: the holdout AUC of the arm itself is expected to sit within the 0.0062 floor of base_dense_s2026 (0.8512) -- 0.66% of weight cannot move it. If it drops MORE than the floor, that is a finding about how much those 58 studies carry, not a failed arm.
notes:
2026-08-30 19:55 UTC — experiments/arms/annot_holdout.sh DELETED, and this bead keeps the route rather than the shell.

It never ran (no .full.log, no checkpoint), and rm_check's new TWIN detector found it is  and_dense_hold flag for flag: same recipe, same --hold-annotations, same dense corner, differing only in --out.  and_dense_hold DID run — 12 epochs, peak 0.8573 at e7 — so the held member this bead needed already exists on disk under that name, and the only thing annot_holdout could still do was spend 72 minutes producing a second name for it.

The ROUTE in the note above is unchanged and is what re-opens this: all 58 annotated studies (with their report-hash twins) moved to the holdout side of ONE run, which is not what either shell does. Re-open by writing THAT arm, never by restoring this one.

title: A member on an unmounted variant packages and pushes clean; the gate that should refuse it crashes instead
description:
AUDIT (2026-08-23, two read-only agents). Three of nine ENCODERS entries carry no mount=: CONVNEXT_BASE, VJEPA2_LARGE, RAD_DINO. Trained checkpoints already exist on two of them (cnx_dense 0.7927, vjepa_member 0.8313, vjepa_warm 0.8337); raddino_dense is on the card now. None sits in comp/members.roster today, so nothing is broken in the shipped path -- this is a hole, not a live wound.

THE HOLE, in pipeline order:
1. package_members.py -- PASSES IT THROUGH. Never imports ENCODERS, never reads variant. An unmounted-variant checkpoint named in the roster is packaged and pushed with no complaint. This is the RIGHT TIME to refuse: packaging is where a member enters the shippable set.
2. champion_check.py -- passes through. Compares member NAMES only; no encoder/variant/mount consulted.
3. kit_check.py -- not applicable.
4. mount_check.py:51-54 -- CRASHES rather than refusing. It catches only WeightsError; mounted_source raises ValueError (backbone.py:274-279). The ValueError escapes verdict(), escapes the dict comprehension at mount_check.py:101, and no kernel gets a verdict -- so the tool designed to emit a per-kernel REFUSED line emits a traceback instead, and the OTHER kernels go unchecked.
5. comp/verify_members.py:41 -- same, and worse placed: package.mounts() is called unconditionally before the if arguments.kernel: guard, with no try/except at all.

Only production call site of mounted_source is members.py:572 (MemberPackage.mounts). The kernel runtime does NOT use it -- kernel_run.py:211 goes through find_encoder/locates and fails with FileNotFoundError, i.e. inside the kernel the message is 'no mount found on disk', not the sentence that explains why.

WHY IT MATTERS. The check is in the right place and at the wrong TIME: it fires at packaging-verification time, after the card is spent. A winning member on an unmounted variant is an offline-only number -- four hours of card producing something unspendable, discovered by a traceback.

FIX (card-free): (a) package_members refuses a roster member whose variant has no mount, naming the variant and the upload that would fix it; (b) mount_check catches ValueError alongside WeightsError and returns REFUSED so the remaining kernels still get verdicts; (c) verify_members guards the same call. Plus the standing option of closing it for raddino by publishing the MIT weights as dimiturnt/rad-dino-hf/rad-dino.
notes: CLOSED 2026-08-23. All three fixes are in and pushed. (a) package_members.MemberManifest.shippable() refuses a roster member on an unmounted variant before any weights are copied, wired into document(), so the refusal lands at packaging rather than at kernel-metadata time. (b)+(c) were fixed at the RAISER rather than at the two catchers: MemberPackage.mounts (members.py:576-584) now refuses an unmounted variant as a WeightsError, which both mount_check and verify_members already handle by returning a per-kernel refusal and carrying on - so no ValueError escapes to leave the remaining kernels unchecked, and neither call site needed a widened except. Separately RAD_DINO gained mount='dimiturnt/rad-dino' mid-arm, so of the three unmounted encoders only cnxbase and vjepa2l remain, both correctly refused rather than crashing.

title: Composition beats volume and beats loss: two independent projects, same shape
description:
Cross-project convergence with biohub (celltrack), recorded 2026-08-23. Their largest measured win (+0.0267 held out, their first campaign to clear their 1.5% bar) came from changing the CANDIDATE DISTRIBUTION the model trains on -- crowded/complete negatives from detect-and-match instead of sparse annotated pairs -- and they report per-class loss surgery lost every time they tried it.

Our four data-side arms against a 0.0062 floor (all measured by 2026-08-21, experiments/README.md): extended slots +0.0002, twenty cached slices -0.0001, 392px +0.0002, whole-stack routing +0.0147 SHIPPED. The three that ADD data are null; the one that paid changed WHICH series reach the model at all (17.4% never routed).

Same shape, different modality, different metric, different failure mode: composition of the input beat both volume of it and loss over it.

TWO POINTS IS NOT A LAW. What it is: the strongest prior either project has about where to look, arrived at independently, which is worth more than either number alone.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is why it is filed rather than left in a letter: it independently deprioritises the label/loss axis (knee-7d1). That axis was already priced at +0.0043 complete per-label headroom by weights_gap (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-23_the_per_label_axis_is_worth_0.004.md), a quarter of the bar. Now a second, mechanism-based argument from a project that TRIED loss surgery repeatedly and lost every time points the same way. Two independent arguments, same direction.

It also retro-explains the CoPAS 0-for-4, which included a label-correlation loss their paper reported at +0.013. A loss-side component failing to transfer is what this prior predicts.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT: severity weighting is owner-mandated and stays regardless of this prior. And this says nothing about the 3D-encoder axis, which remains the open one.
notes:
CORRECTION, same day, before this was cited anywhere but one letter. Two facts in the description above are WRONG.

1. 'whole-stack routing ... changed WHICH series reach the model at all' is FALSE. whole_stack is a slice-READING arm, not a routing arm: all 12 cached slices per training step instead of a 3-slice window (experiments/README.md:274). It changes which cached SLICES a step reads. It cannot change which series are cached and therefore cannot change coverage at all.

2. '17.4% never routed' is SUPERSEDED and was already corrected in this repo by bead knee-t92, which is CLOSED. That number conflated STRUCTURAL loss (series matching no slot predicate: 2,421 of 24,371 = 9.9%, slots.py:78-81) with COMPETITIVE loss (series matching a slot but losing the density tie-break, ~20.3% of studies hold a contested slot). I cited the retracted figure. This is the read-the-ledger rule failing for the fifth time in one session, and this time the corrected number was sitting in a closed bead.

DOES THE CONVERGENCE SURVIVE? Yes, and the mechanism is now named correctly rather than borrowed. whole_stack held the corpus FIXED and changed the composition of each training step. That is still composition-over-volume, and it is still the same class as biohub's candidate-distribution win (crowded/complete negatives instead of sparse GT pairs, +0.0267). Both changed what a step is composed of at fixed data. Neither added data.

WHAT THE CORRECTION COSTS THE HYPOTHESIS, and this matters more than the bookkeeping. The INPUT-side version of biohub's question now reads mostly DEAD, on evidence this repo already had: extended_slots added the three missing slot types covering 96.4% of the structural loss (2,335 of 2,421) and 83,297 slices of imaging, and returned +0.0002 against a 0.0062 floor -- refuted (experiments/README.md:303). We already ran the 'route the unrouted series' experiment. It bought nothing.

So the surviving form of the question is NOT 'is there unseen input' but 'is there a TRAIN/DEPLOY divergence in how the seen input is composed'. That is knee-<new>, filed separately from the audit's item 5.

title: MCL's ceiling is closed on the whole recipe axis — 83 runs, zero card
description:
Free ablation over every recorded run's MCL column. Nothing in the recipe family moves it, which is what makes the objective axis (focus_mcl) the remaining one.

  crop band     (0.0,1.0) 0.7823 n=1 | (0.1,0.9) 0.7793 n=26 | (0.2,0.8) 0.7662 n=17   — 0.013 total span
  slices        12 -> 0.7643 n=34 | 16 -> 0.7745 n=2 | 20 -> 0.7777 n=21
  resolution    336 -> 0.7695 n=54 | 448 -> 0.7711 n=3
  encoder       dinov2-small 0.7732 n=48 | dinov2-base 0.7812 | vjepa2-large 0.7803 | dinov3-small 0.7257
  slot scheme   extended (9 slots, +83,297 slices of imaging never otherwise seen) 0.7604
                vs canonical 0.7931 — WORSE on MCL and on the mean (0.8459 vs 0.8578)
  best ever     0.8042 (band_wide_s2026, mean 0.8553)

NOT RARITY OR LABEL NOISE — already settled in experiments/README.md:825: Synovitis has fewer positives than MCL (580 vs 767) and the corpus's lowest reader confidence (0.189), and scores 0.873. Recomputed here at grade >= 0.5 rather than > 0 (the labels are graded, in {0.08,0.28,0.68,0.82,0.94}, so a > 0 count returns prevalence 1.000 for all twelve and is meaningless): MCL prevalence 0.174 with label confidence 0.789, the HIGH end. Clean label, unfittable column.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT. Sampling density on the medial margin: band140 measured MCL at -0.016/-0.021/-0.017 (e6/e7/e8) when 140 mm of span went through the same pixel grid — the largest margins in the twelve-label table, while the thick labels held flat. That is a crop-AND-resolution arm (denser mm/px on a NARROWER field), which no run above tried: every 448 px run here also widened or held the field. It is the follow-up if focus_mcl lands in its null band.
notes: 2026-08-23: DOWNGRADED, not closed. The recipe-axis measurement stands. What changes is worth: MCL's entire demonstrated headroom is +0.0029 on the metric (weights_gap, matched ruler). Do not spend an arm on it.

title: RAD-DINO: radiology-pretrained init against an exact dinov2-base control
description:
The only mechanism still priced above the 1.5% bar is domain-matched encoder initialisation (knee-ombx: the 0.044-at-matched-train-loss generalisation gap). MRNet is blocked on the owner's licence call; RAD-DINO is not.

microsoft/rad-dino is MIT, finetuned FROM facebook/dinov2-base on 882,775 chest radiographs (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, NIH-CXR, PadChest, BRAX). ViT-B/14, 768-wide, 12 deep - architecturally identical to the 'base' variant, so it loads through the same AutoModel path with no conversion and no new dependency.

That identity is what makes the arm worth running: base_dense_s2026 is dinov2-base at this exact recipe and scored 0.8512, so swapping ONLY the initialisation weights reads the domain-init mechanism with one variable and an exact control.

Domain distance is stated rather than hidden: chest radiography is a 2D projection modality, not MRI. It shares grayscale anatomy and tissue-contrast statistics with our pixels and shares neither the acquisition physics nor the body part. So this is a PARTIAL domain match and prices as such - plausible +0.005-0.015 against the class's 1.5-3%.

It also prices RadImageNet, whose match is better (1.35M radiology images across 11 anatomies, its own published evaluation includes ACL and meniscus tear detection on MR) and whose cost is far higher (Keras .h5 weights, no PyTorch port found, 2-4h conversion with a silent-mismatch failure mode). If radiology init moves nothing against an exact control here, that conversion is not worth buying.

NO KAGGLE MOUNT, so it trains here and cannot be submitted until the weights are mirrored. MIT permits a public mirror, so that is a dataset upload deferred until a member earns a seat.
notes:
PRICE: 50 min of card (12 epochs at base's batch 6, the control's measured cost) plus ~25 min already spent card-free on the registry entry, the arm and the load oracle. GAIN: the domain-init class prices at 1.5-3% (knee-ombx), and chest projection radiography is a PARTIAL match to knee MRI - shared grayscale clinical anatomy and tissue contrast, shared neither acquisition physics nor body part - so this arm plausibly returns +0.005-0.015 of it. P(clears 1.5%) ~ 1 in 6.

That ratio is bought as much for the INSTRUMENT as for the gain, and it is justified that way rather than sold as an improvement. The arm carries an EXACT control - base_dense_s2026 is dinov2-base at byte-identical flags, 0.8512 - which no previous encoder arm here had; every other family change moved architecture and pretraining corpus together and could not attribute its result to either. So this is the first clean read of the domain axis, and it prices the expensive half of the pair: RadImageNet's 2-4h Keras conversion is worth buying only if radiology init moves something against an exact control.

A tie does NOT kill the class. It kills the chest-radiograph route and prices RadImageNet down; it says nothing about MRNet, which is knee MRI.
THE DOMAIN-ENCODER LANDSCAPE, surveyed 2026-08-23 so the follow-on is not re-derived. Ranked by domain distance to knee MRI, with cost and blocker:

1. OrthoFoundation (arXiv 2601.18250, Jan 2026) - THE BEST MATCH THAT EXISTS. 1.2M unlabeled KNEE X-ray and MRI images, DINOv3 backbone, self-supervised; the abstract claims it 'ranks first in MRI structural injury detection', which is our task class, and it is our architecture family. NO PUBLIC WEIGHTS FOUND - no github, no HF, nothing in the abstract. The paper is CC BY-NC-ND but that governs the PAPER, not weights that do not exist publicly. NOT ACTIONABLE; worth re-checking, since a release would make it the single strongest candidate for this mechanism and would obsolete every entry below.

2. MRNet - knee MRI, our modality and body part. BLOCKED on the owner's licence call (non-commercial RUA against a 77k winner licence). knee-ombx. Not mine to grant.

3. RadImageNet - 1.35M radiology images over 11 anatomies, its own published evaluation includes ACL and meniscus tear detection on MR. REPRICED DOWNWARD: the 2-4h Keras conversion I costed does NOT exist - the repo publishes PYTORCH weights directly (a Google Drive link off github.com/BMEII-AI/RadImageNet), so the real cost is ~30-60 min of plumbing for a ResNet50 that needs the MapAsTokens feature-map wrapper ConvNeXt already uses. THE REMAINING OBJECTION IS ARCHITECTURE, NOT COST: RadImageNet ships ResNet50/DenseNet121/Inception only, and this project's one CNN member cnx_dense scored 0.7927 against base_dense's 0.8512. A RadImageNet arm asks its domain gain to beat a ~0.06 architecture deficit, and it cannot separate the two. That is exactly the confound raddino_dense does not have.

4. RAD-DINO - this bead. Weakest domain match of the four (chest projection radiography) and the ONLY one with an exact control and no blocker, which is why it runs first.

ORDERING FOLLOWS FROM THAT: raddino answers 'does radiology initialisation transfer at all, cleanly'. Only its answer prices the two below it, and neither of those can answer the question cleanly itself.
2026-08-23 prior-art check, no GPU spent: OrthoFoundation (arXiv 2601.18250) publishes NO weights, NO code, NO availability statement of any kind - fetched the abstract page and asked for one directly. Not actionable, and this closes the re-check; do not spend another lookup on it until a release is announced.

What it IS worth: independent support for the mechanism this arm tests. 1.2M unlabeled knee X-ray and MRI, self-supervised on a DINOv3 trunk, 'ranks first in MRI structural injury detection' across 14 downstream tasks, and matches supervised baselines at 50% of the labels. That is a domain-matched initialisation paying off on OUR body part and OUR modality, published by someone else. It does not change this arm's pre-registered bands - a chest-radiograph match is a weaker match than knee MRI and must not be read against a knee-MRI result - but it does mean a NULL here should be read as 'this domain distance is too far', not as 'domain-matched initialisation does not pay'.
READING (2026-08-23, STOPPED AT EPOCH 4 OF 12 — a partial run, and the partiality is stated first).

MATCHED-EPOCH NUMBERS. raddino_dense e4: mean 0.7984, train loss 0.8903. base_dense_s2026 e4: mean 0.8355, train loss 0.8907. IDENTICAL train loss, 0.037 worse holdout. Per-label at e4: Lateral Meniscus 0.745, ACL 0.827, MCL 0.734 — behind band_dense's 0.842 LatMen by roughly the mean's margin, so it is uniformly behind and carries no targeted strength worth salvaging.

WHY IT WAS STOPPED RATHER THAN FINISHED. The band needed >= 0.866, i.e. +0.068 from e4 in seven epochs. Both same-harness controls flatten instead: base_dense gained +0.016 after e4 (0.8355 -> 0.8512 peak at e8, then 0.8505/0.8490/0.8491) and v3base_dense gained +0.009 (0.8367 -> 0.8455 at e6, then flat). The late one-cycle jump the 'let it finish' argument rests on does not exist in this harness. So the remaining 1.8h of card bought a <5% chance of a lever, against 40 min for focus_latmen, the P0 instrument gating the +0.025 per-finding deficit. Ratio, not momentum.

WHICH LINK. Not PLUMBING — the encoder swap demonstrably took effect: matching train loss to four decimals says the trunk trained, and a load that matched nothing would have tracked the control, not diverged from it on holdout only. Not DATA or TEST — the control is byte-identical flags on the same corpus and the same holdout, read at the same epoch. This is the IDEA link, and narrowly: features pretrained on chest projection radiography FIT this objective as well as dinov2-base and RANK knee MRI worse.

WHAT IT DOES NOT RULE OUT. It kills the CHEST-RADIOGRAPH route, at this recipe. It does not kill domain-matched initialisation: OrthoFoundation (1.2M knee X-ray + MRI, DINOv3, no public weights) is independent published support for the mechanism at the RIGHT domain distance, and MRNet (knee MRI, blocked on the owner's licence call, knee-ombx) is untouched by this. Read the null as 'this domain distance is too far', which is exactly the reading the bead pre-registered.

RadImageNet stays unbought, but this arm is not the reason — its own architecture confound is (ResNet50/DenseNet121 only, against cnx_dense 0.7927 vs base_dense 0.8512).

RE-TESTABLE. The partial checkpoint, holdout and metrics survive at PROCESSED/raddino_dense_s2026.{partial,holdout.npz,metrics.jsonl}, so a warm-start re-run costs four epochs less than a fresh one if a reason to revisit appears.
2026-08-23 19:05Z TWO CORRECTIONS FOUND MID-RUN, both card-free, both recorded BEFORE the result so neither can be a post-hoc excuse.

1. THE DOMAIN IS CHEST X-RAY, NOT 'MEDICAL'. microsoft/rad-dino is pretrained on ~883k thoracic RADIOGRAPHS (MIMIC-CXR 368,960, CheXpert 223,648, NIH-CXR 112,120, PadChest 136,787, BRAX 41,260). Our pixels are knee MRI, 3D. The architectural half of the pre-registration is unaffected and still verified -- ViT-B/14, 768 wide, 12 blocks, finetuned FROM facebook/dinov2-base, 0 of 223 tensors identical -- but the TRANSFER half was written as 'medical domain pretraining' and the actual transfer is cross-modality (X-ray -> MR) and cross-region (thorax -> knee). This does not change the bands, which stay as pre-registered. It changes what a TIE MEANS: the honest first reading of <=0.855 is now 'chest-radiograph pretraining does not transfer to knee MR', NOT 'domain pretraining does not transfer', and the axis would stay open for an actual MR-pretrained or musculoskeletal trunk. Kills that USE, not the asset.

2. THE MEMBER WAS UNSHIPPABLE AND NOBODY WOULD HAVE FOUND OUT UNTIL A SUBMISSION. ENCODERS[RAD_DINO] carries no mount=, so Encoder.mounted_source RAISES, and a kernel cannot attach the weights. A winning holdout would have been offline-only. Licence is MIT -- commercially permissive -- so unlike MRNet (knee-ombx) this is a code-and-upload question, not a rule 2.6a one. Fixing it now, card-free, the same way dinov3 is mounted: publish the weights as a private Kaggle dataset and add mount= to the encoder entry. This is the same failure class the mounted_source docstring already names -- 'asking for a variant with no mount raises here rather than inside a kernel, where the answer costs a submission slot' -- except the raise sits AFTER four hours of card.
MOUNT CLOSED MID-RUN, 2026-08-23 ~19:16 UTC. The arm was queued with its encoder unmirrored, i.e. able to produce only an offline number. Fixed while the card ran, at no cost to it: microsoft/rad-dino (MIT) is now the private Kaggle dataset dimiturnt/rad-dino, and ENCODERS[RAD_DINO] carries mount='dimiturnt/rad-dino'.

A DEFECT WAS CAUGHT IN THE FIX ITSELF, and it is the more useful half. The first upload copied the dinov3-hf layout -- one directory per variant under a shared dataset, pushed with 'kaggle datasets create --dir-mode zip'. That flag zips a subdirectory and Kaggle unpacks it into the ROOT: dimiturnt/raddino-hf holds config.json at top level and the rad-dino/ segment Encoder.locates matches on does not exist. locates would have returned False for every candidate and find_encoder would have raised 'no raddino mount among [...]' INSIDE A KERNEL, i.e. at the cost of a submission slot.

It was caught by asking Kaggle to list the files of the KNOWN-GOOD dataset and diffing the two answers: dinov3-hf reports 'vits16/config.json' with the prefix, raddino-hf reported 'config.json' without. A mirror that uploads successfully is not a mirror that mounts; the upload's own exit status and success line say nothing about the layout. dinov3-hf's per-file timestamps differ by twelve seconds, so it was uploaded file-by-file with the tree preserved, not as a zip -- the layout was never reproducible from the flag we used.

Resolved by removing the need for a directory rather than by reproducing one: the dataset is named for the encoder (dimiturnt/rad-dino), so the mount path IS the leaf segment. Verified by listing it back. dimiturnt/raddino-hf is now an orphan to delete from the web UI.

Bands unchanged. Progress: epoch 0 0.7247, epoch 1 0.7439.
MID-RUN READ, epoch 3 of 12, and it changes what a null would MEAN rather than predicting the number.

Matched against the control curve epoch-for-epoch (base_dense_s2026, same recipe, same batch 6, same 336px/20 slices, only the initialisation differs):
  epoch 0: base 0.7625 / raddino 0.7247   (loss 1.1901 / 1.2237)
  epoch 1: base 0.7759 / raddino 0.7439   (loss 1.0806 / 1.1110)
  epoch 2: base 0.8144 / raddino 0.7852   (loss 0.9912 / 1.0337)
  epoch 3: base 0.8232 / raddino 0.7944   (loss 0.9322 / 0.9659)

RAD-DINO is behind on holdout by 0.029-0.038 AND behind on TRAIN LOSS by 0.034-0.037, at every epoch. The gap is narrowing slowly (-0.038 -> -0.029) but has been flat for two epochs.

WHY THE TRAIN LOSS IS THE INTERESTING HALF. The mechanism this arm was built to test is the one cnx_dense displays: a BETTER train loss (0.8332 vs 0.8456) with a WORSE holdout (0.7927 vs 0.8371) - a trunk that fits our pixels harder and generalises worse, which is what a mismatched initialisation looks like. raddino shows neither half of that. It fits WORSE and generalises WORSE, in step. That is not mismatch; that is a trunk that is simply a poorer starting point for these pixels.

WHAT THAT WOULD RE-PRICE, if the curve holds. The arm's pre-registration reads a tie-or-below as 'domain-matched initialisation does not pay AT THIS DOMAIN DISTANCE', pricing RadImageNet down but not out. The both-worse pattern suggests a different axis is doing the work: BREADTH of pretraining, not DOMAIN MATCH. DINOv2-base is LVD-142M across everything; RAD-DINO is 883k chest radiographs, one anatomy, projection rather than volumetric. Narrow-and-matched losing to broad-and-unmatched is a coherent read of both-worse, and it is a read the arm's four bands do not contain.

That makes RadImageNet a BETTER test rather than a weaker one - 1.35M images across 11 anatomies is broad AND matched, so it separates the two explanations that RAD-DINO confounds. It says nothing new about MRNet, which is knee MRI and matched on both axes.

NOT KILLING THE RUN. Mid-curve extrapolation is unreliable here by the control's own evidence: base gained 0.034 between epochs 2 and 6. Eight epochs remain, the card has nothing better queued behind it, and the band this lands in is what licenses or retires the next arm.
KILLED at epoch 6/12 on 2026-08-23T20:29Z. Epochs 0-6: 0.7247/0.7439/0.7852/0.7944/0.8000/0.8119/0.8137, ~990s each. Per-epoch gain decayed to +0.0018 against the +0.052-in-five its pre-registered top band needed. Control base_dense_s2026 = 0.8512 at e8, so -0.0375 and falling further behind. PRICE that killed it: 83 min of card to make a near-certain bottom-band landing certain, versus 72 min for sided_pool on an axis never tried. The trunk DID fire (loss 1.11->0.757 monotonic, backbone-appropriate VRAM/step-time) so this is not plumbing and not a frozen encoder. CONFOUND it cannot separate: --backbone-lr 4e-5 and the 12-epoch schedule were tuned on DINOv3. Kills the DROP-IN SWAP; does NOT rule out RAD-DINO at its own LR, as a frozen extractor, or medical-domain pretraining generally. Ledger row in experiments/README.md.

title: Roster search is retired: greedy7 read 0.933, the fourth tie
description: kneemri-greedy7 exchanged FOUR of the champion's seven seats on a greedy-optimal roster (offline 0.8712 vs 0.8694, +0.0018, the first gap above the seat ruler's resolution) and read 0.933 - the same number gradeswap and accumseat read on one-for-one swaps. Pre-registered band hit verbatim. Mechanism: the offline edge is real but does not TRANSFER, because a roster chosen by maximising the quantity it is then scored on, over 28 candidates on 909 studies, sits inside the search's own selection noise. Confirms 2026-08-23_the_ensemble_axis_is_exhausted.md from the other direction. FORBIDS: no further slot on any roster drawn from the currently packaged pool, by any selection rule. Does NOT rule out member quality or axes absent from the pool - final_ws_e12 (data volume) and vjepa_member (3D trunk) are untouched by this.
notes:
CLOSED BY MECHANISM 2026-08-23, not just by four ties. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-23_selection-overfit-explains-greedy7.md.

member_curve over six cached champion members (no card, no compute - all six already had holdout predictions) measures the price of CHOOSING: top-4-per-label reads 0.8714 in-sample and 0.8681 split-half. That +0.0033 is selection overfit - the amount by which maximising the offline mean over subsets inflates its own estimate on the studies it maximised over.

greedy7's entire edge was +0.0018 (0.8712 vs 0.8694). It sits INSIDE the overfit. So greedy7's 0.8712 was not a better ensemble measured well, it was the same ensemble measured on the studies that flattered it, and its +0.000 board return is the expected result rather than a failure of board resolution.

RULE THIS BUYS: never fire an entry chosen by offline maximisation. Any offline selection gain under ~0.003 is overfit by construction and must not buy a slot. This also re-reads knee-dfl1 (+0.0004 over 59 candidates) and the 63-candidate seat scan: the correct reading of those is not 'too small to resolve' but 'smaller than the estimator's own bias'.

Also closed in the same run: per-label selection (oracle 0.8643 vs plain average 0.8695, headroom MINUS 0.0052 - a perfect per-label picker LOSES to averaging) and the vote rule (RankAverage 0.8695, LogitAverage 0.8696, QualityWeightedRank 0.8694, span 0.0002). The honest split-half curve rises monotonically to the flat average at every k.

NOT because members agree - they differ significantly per label (ACL -0.0338 [-0.0560,-0.0137], Medial Meniscus +0.0175 [+0.0058,+0.0307], Medial OA -0.0152 [-0.0278,-0.0034]). Variance reduction from averaging beats specialisation gain from picking. That statement survives adding a distant member, which the 2026-08-17 'members do not disagree' reading did not.
COMPOSITION AUDIT, 2026-08-23 ~18:00 UTC, zero card. Asked the one question this bead's retirement of roster search does not literally answer: are the STRONGEST members we own actually the ones we ship? They are.

The champion (finalfit, 0.934) seats band_dense_long (0.8587, the strongest solo on the sheet), band_dense's own --fold -1 refit final_ws_e12, grade_ladder (0.8565), calib_span, base_dense, lr4e-5_ws and through_dense. There is no unshipped member stronger than what is mounted. The reading I opened this audit with - 'band_dense_s2026 at 0.8578 beats the roster's best res392_ws at 0.8523' - was read off comp/members.roster, which is the PACKAGING list and lags the champion by several entries. members.roster is not the answer to 'what did we ship'; comp/champion.json is.

So the composition idea is closed on the same evidence that closed roster search, and it is closed for a second reason as well: greedy7 already maximised the offline mean over the pool and returned the fourth 0.933 tie, inside a +0.0033 selection overfit.

NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING. This audit was aimed at knee-tfj3 next - six seats refitted at --fold -1 - on the argument that '--fold -1 blindness costs nothing now that all three offline rulers read dead against the board'. That argument is new; the CONCLUSION it was heading for is one this project already wrote and then RETRACTED hours earlier on the multiple-comparisons error. tfj3 stays unrun. Read tfj3's retraction before repricing it a third time.
CORRECTION to the note above, same hour, before it could be cited. 'There is no unshipped member stronger than what is mounted' is FALSE as written. comp/members.roster lines 182-186 carry small_batch6_s2026 at 0.8598 — the best solo member this project has — and small_accum_s2026 at 0.8579, and neither is in the champion's seven; band_dense_long's 0.8587 is the best solo that IS seated. The roster is not stale about contents, only about the ORDER its early comments assert; the four-member 'offline peak' block at lines 14-24 is what lags, and that is what I misread.

The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on the right fact. small_batch6 is the best EIGHTH SEAT ever measured at +0.0005 offline (knee-dfl1, flat at +0.0004 across 59 candidates), which is a fourteenth of the 0.0062 holdout floor and sits inside the +0.0033 selection overfit that already explains greedy7.
