FIX: arms run against a dedicated environment (.venv-arm, built with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, gitignored) so the shared .venv is no longer shared with a live run. lib.sh must set UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT in run_train -- BLOCKED until the current arm lands, because lib.sh is the file that arm's shell is executing and editing it mid-run is the depth_regions_span failure recorded at lib.sh:219-221. Until then: DO NOT PUSH WHILE AN ARM RUNS.
design:
ONE EDIT POINT, because all four uv sites in lib.sh (46, 329, 388, 464) already pass --no-sync and differ only in what they run. Export the environment once near the top of lib.sh, beside REPO/PROCESSED, and every uv call in every arm inherits it:

    # ARMS DO NOT SHARE AN ENVIRONMENT WITH THE GATES. uv syncs .venv to EXACTLY the extras it is
    # given, so 'uv run --extra dev' and 'uv run --extra devtools' rewrite it in opposite directions
    # -- in place, with no lock. A pre-commit or pre-push hook doing that under a live trainer
    # deletes the files its interpreter is running from: exit 127, no traceback, no error line.
    # Measured twice (2026-08-13 mid epoch 4, 2026-08-20 mid step 182). --no-sync below stops THIS
    # process from syncing and cannot stop another one, which is why the fix is a separate directory
    # rather than another flag.
    export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT="$REPO/.venv-arm"
    [ -d "$UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT" ] || uv sync --extra dev --extra devtools

WHY NOT --no-sync ON THE HOOKS INSTEAD: .pre-commit-config.yaml is template-owned (sdlc-scaffold), and
--no-sync there would make a gate silently run against a stale environment, trading a loud failure for
a quiet one.

WHY NOT A LOCK: hold_card already serialises the CARD, and a second lock over the ENVIRONMENT would
make every gate wait out a forty-minute arm. Two directories cost ~2 GB and no waiting.

VERIFICATION, and it must be a positive check rather than 'no crash': with an arm running, run
'uvx nox -s gates' (which alternates extras, the exact trigger) and confirm the arm reaches its next
epoch line. Second check: '.venv-arm/Scripts/python.exe -c "import torch"' still imports after the
gates finish -- the environment the arm holds was not touched.

BLOCKED ON: the current severity_weight run. lib.sh is sourced by that arm's shell and is re-entered
after the trainer returns (to write LIB/_mark, seat value, the best-holdout check). Editing it mid-run
is the depth_regions_span failure at lib.sh:219-221.

ALREADY DONE: .venv-arm built (uv sync with UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT, 2026-08-20) and gitignored with the
reasoning. Proven usable in both directions today -- the full AST gate batch and supervision_gap both
ran green against it while the arm held .venv.
notes: knee-z99y is the same race seen from the other side: it recorded gate flakiness, this bead records arm death. One .venv, no lock, two writers.

title: Severity should set the loss WEIGHT, not just the target value: mild YES is right 37.8% of the time and trained at the same 0.95 as severe
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-20, zero GPU, from report_labels_v2.csv and targets.MEASURED_AGREEMENT.

THE DEFECT, in one table. The reader emits five levels. The value carries severity. The weight does not:

  value  meaning    weight(__conf)   cells    radiologist says POSITIVE
  0.08   NO             0.85         22,298      4.1%
  0.28   UNK            0.05         14,445     13.6%
  0.68   mild YES       0.95          6,461     37.8%
  0.82   moderate YES   0.95          6,427     68.8%
  0.94   severe YES     0.95          3,241     95.8%

The three YES levels are severity grades 1/2/3 (the verdict/severity bijection, audited 2026-08-20) and
they all carry conf 0.95, verified over all 52,872 populated cells (min == max == 0.95 at each level).
A mild-grade YES is correct 37.8% of the time and is trained at the SAME confidence as a severe YES that
is correct 95.8%. A 2.5x reliability gap that the loss cannot see.

SIZE OF THE DEFECT, with its denominator stated. 6,461 mild cells x (1 - 0.378) = ~4,020 cells that are
confidently wrong-signed at weight 0.95. Over the 52,872 populated cells that is 7.6% of the corpus —
about twice the 100-report contest pilot's 4.0% contested rate, and unlike the pilot's it is spread
across ALL TWELVE labels rather than concentrated in Fracture and Contusion.

WHY THIS IS NOT calib_span, WHICH LOST 0.0020, and this is the load-bearing distinction.
calib_span (--calibrated-targets, Supervision.applied) rewrites the VALUE to the measured rate:
0.68 -> 0.378. That is BELOW 0.5, so 6,461 mild cells FLIP SIGN — a mild tear becomes a negative target
under BCE. That is a destructive change and is the most likely reason it inverted every clause.
This arm rewrites the WEIGHT and leaves the value alone. The mild tear stays a positive target; it is
merely trusted less. The ordinal ladder 0.68 < 0.82 < 0.94 is preserved intact, so the pairwise ranking
term — the only loss change positive in 3 of 3 matched arms — keeps every pair it currently forms.
So the ledger's one refutation on this axis does NOT transfer: it refuted a value edit, not a weight edit.

THE DESIGN, derived rather than picked (no magic numbers). Weight = P(label is correct | level), which
MEASURED_AGREEMENT already holds:
  NO   0.08 -> correct 95.9%   (weight up slightly from 0.85)
  UNK  0.28 -> 13.6% positive, ambiguous by construction — leave at 0.05
  mild 0.68 -> 0.378
  mod  0.82 -> 0.688
  sev  0.94 -> 0.958
Every number comes from the 58 image reads, fitted there and scored on the fold-0 report holdout, which
is how Supervision already keeps the ruler independent. Gate on WEIGHT_FLOOR interaction: --weight-floor
is in the shipped RECIPE and clamps low weights, so the arm must state what floor it runs under or the
0.378 it is testing never reaches the loss. VERIFY THE FLAG LANDED IN THE CHECKPOINT CONFIG.

DENOMINATOR CAVEAT, stated because it bounds the whole design. MEASURED_AGREEMENT is computed over 684
annotated cells, 311 of them positive calls, so the three YES levels carry roughly 124 / 124 / 62 cells.
The severe rate 95.8% sits on ~62 cells. The per-level ordering is solid (monotone across a 0.58 span,
and the corpus-weighted mean 61.8% reconciles with the independently reported 65% positive agreement),
but no single rate should be treated as precise to better than a few points.

CONTROL: band_dense = 0.8578 at epoch 8, the settled operating point (4e-5 backbone, 20 slices, band
0.10-0.90, whole-stack, 336 px, batch 12, 12 epochs one-cycle). Single variable: the weight column only.

PRE-REGISTERED, written before the run:
  PREDICTION — peak clears 0.8578 by more than 0.0062, and the gain is NOT concentrated in the six
    label-bottlenecked findings (knee-dtk), because a weight change touches all twelve.
  REFUTATION — peak at or below 0.8578. Then reliability weighting is not what the head is missing, the
    flat 0.95 was not costing anything, and the severity axis is closed on the LOSS side as well as the
    value side (calib_span). Say so and stop reaching for supervision.
  THIRD OUTCOME — mean flat but the mild-heavy labels move. Medial Meniscus is 53.3% YES and Effusion
    60.5%; if their per-label numbers move while the mean does not, the mechanism is real and something
    else is absorbing it.

RISK TO THE SHIPPED RESULT: NONE. This is a fold-0 matched arm. It writes a new checkpoint, touches no
member in comp/champion.json, and champion_check still guards that the 0.925 entry rebuilds. The only
cost is GPU time, and the card is currently held for biohub.

NOT QUEUED. Needs the card and an explicit go-ahead.
notes:
2026-08-20 10:32Z — BUILT, SMOKED AND RUNNING. The card freed and the user said so; launched directly
(no sentinel — nothing was running). Commit 2fcfdcf. Log: logs/severity_weight.log.

DENOMINATOR CORRECTION — the "~124 / 124 / 62 cells" above was MY PROPORTIONAL ESTIMATE, not a
measurement, and it was wrong. The real per-level n and CIs are in the Calibration docstring
(kneemri/labels/targets.py:62-67) and were there the whole time:

    level   measured   95% CI            n
     0.68    0.378     [0.282, 0.474]    98
     0.82    0.688     [0.611, 0.764]   141
     0.94    0.958     [0.912, 1.004]    72

This makes the design STRONGER, not weaker: the three intervals DO NOT OVERLAP. 0.474 < 0.611 and
0.764 < 0.912. The ordering is not "solid but imprecise" as the caveat above hedges — it is resolved.
The severe rate sits on 72 cells rather than the 62 I guessed, and moderate on 141 rather than 124.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BUILT, and it differs from the design above in one place:
  Supervision.severity (a bool) + Supervision.trusted() + Supervision.reliability(), consumed at
  targets.py:224 BEFORE applied(), because a calibration rewrites 0.68 to 0.378 in place and a grade
  looked up afterwards would match nothing and fall back to __conf silently. The two switches compose
  only in that order.
  Supervision.moves_the_ruler() now gates the second read in Targets.pair — it was `if calibrated`,
  which would have graded the HOLDOUT under this arm and moved the AUC by construction.
  --severity-weight on TrainingOptions, stamped through Request.wanted() into the checkpoint config,
  so "verify the flag landed" is a config read rather than an inference.

MEASURED ON THE REAL TABLE (52,872 populated cells, post-annotation-override so counts differ slightly
from the raw-table counts in the description above):
  scores byte-identical between arm and control — this is not a calibration
  0.08 NO       n=22,102   0.8875 -> 0.9693
  0.28 UNK      n=14,268   0.2875 -> 0.2875 (untouched, it asserts nothing)
  0.68 mild     n= 6,363   0.9625 -> 0.5335
  0.82 moderate n= 6,286   0.9625 -> 0.7660
  0.94 severe   n= 3,169   0.9625 -> 0.9685

TWO THINGS MOVE, WHICH THE DESIGN ABOVE DID NOT SAY. The NO bucket is the largest at 22,102 cells and
it rises +0.082, uniformly across all twelve labels. So the arm grades the positives AND strengthens
the denials, and a bare mean cannot say which paid. The pre-registered clause was rewritten in the arm
to separate them: the denial uplift can only produce a UNIFORM lift, so a uniform lift now REFUTES.
The grade effect can only appear on labels a report actually grades — meniscus, cartilage/OA, ligament
sprain-to-tear. A lift concentrated in MCL also refutes (the pilot found 0 rulebook errors there and
resolution.sh argues it is bounded by what we can SEE).

Gates: uvx nox -s gates successful; 879 unit tests pass. Four total-partition gates fired on the new
switch and each was answered rather than suppressed — switch_coverage (needs the arm script to exist),
Request/test_not_a_switch, member_record.NOT_IN_CONFIG, run_comparison.SUPERVISION_AXES.
CLOSED 2026-08-21 on the pre-registered REFUTATION clause. The arm ran to completion on 2026-08-20
and its full reading is in experiments/README.md:1238. Peak 0.8530 at epoch 8 against control
band_dense 0.8578 at the same epoch: -0.0048, inside the 0.0062 floor and the wrong sign.

The clause that fired, quoted from the description above: 'REFUTATION -- peak at or below 0.8578.'
It was. The finer pre-registered ruler agrees and is the part that carries the read: the arm predicted a
gain CONCENTRATED in the five graded rows, and four of those five went NEGATIVE (Medial Meniscus -0.0010,
Medial OA -0.0033, PF OA -0.0058, Lateral OA -0.0072; only Lateral Meniscus +0.0064). By structure scale,
focal +0.0001 against regional -0.0118 -- the graded regional findings a severity scale was built to
serve are exactly the ones that lost. The switch fired (the pattern is not uniform, so this is not a
no-op wearing an arm's name); it fired against its own prediction.

THIS BEAD IS BEING CLOSED NOW RATHER THAN ON THE DAY IT RAN because it sat in_progress with the verdict
already written in the ledger -- the same bead/ledger drift ledger_check exists to catch, found here by
reading the ledger rather than the bead.

THE HATCH IT LEFT OPEN IS NOW SHUT, and this is the reason the whole family can be summarised. The
ledger entry ended: 'an ordinal target or a graded head consumes that information without reweighting
the batch, and neither has been tried.' grade_ladder IS that ordinal target and was run 2026-08-21
(knee-t607, ledger 2026-08-21): mean -0.0013, and on the OA triple -- the only labels whose target shape
it changed -- three for three negative. So the severity information has now been spent three independent
ways against the same control:

  calib_span       rewrote the target VALUE   -0.0020   (and flipped sign on 6,363 mild cells)
  severity_weight  rewrote the loss WEIGHT    -0.0048   (regional -0.0118)
  grade_ladder     rewrote the target SHAPE   -0.0013   (OA triple 3/3 negative)

Three parameterisations, three negatives, none clearing the floor in the right direction. The reports do
carry a grade the binary targets discard -- that observation is still true and is not what these arms
refuted. What they refute is that the grade is RECOVERABLE BY SUPERVISION EDITS at this corpus size.

THE AXIS STAYS OPEN AS A BELIEF BY THE OWNER'S STANDING CALL (2026-08-20): 'severity weighting is the
right approach even if it doesnt win out on significant result.' That call is respected here -- nothing
about severity is being deleted, the switches all remain in the trainer and re-testable, and each arm's
mechanism is recorded so a later use is re-tested rather than assumed dead. What closes is the QUEUE
CLAIM: no further severity arm should take a card until something OTHER than a supervision edit is
proposed for it -- a graded HEAD (an output structure, not a target rewrite), or a corpus where the
grades are not already collapsed to binary before we see them.

title: The board frontier is FLAT at 0.952 over 37h; the pack is thickening and recombination is measured at 0.001
description:
RECORDED FRONTIER: 0.942, measured 2026-08-13. USER-REPORTED 2026-08-20: ~0.957, unverified.

If both are right the frontier moves +0.015/wk against our +0.005/wk and the gap has gone 0.014 -> 0.027 and is WIDENING. That changes what is worth queueing: a knob family returning -0.002 a run cannot close 0.027, and four consecutive decode/head knobs have now returned nothing.

WHY IT IS UNVERIFIED — four independent paths tried 2026-08-20, all dead:
  kaggle competitions leaderboard        EXIT 127, not on PATH
  uv run kaggle                          'program not found'
  uv run python -m kaggle                'No module named kaggle'; where.exe kaggle finds nothing
  direct REST, basic auth from ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json   HTTP 401 Unauthorized
KAGGLE_TOKEN is unset; the KGAT_* token survey.py wants expired 2026-07-23 and ~/.kaggle/access_token is stamped that date. WebFetch on /leaderboard and /discussion returns only the page title — Kaggle renders both client-side, so competition discussion has NEVER been readable from here.

WHAT THIS BLOCKS: every 'is our offline edge worth a submission slot' judgement is being made against a number a week old, and the discussion tab — where the frontier's method would be visible — has never been read at all.

FIX: refresh the Kaggle credential (manual, user-side) and re-run the frontier read; then decide whether the recorded 0.942 line in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md gets replaced or annotated.
notes:
2026-08-20 19:58Z FETCHED, and the CLI reads the board fine from here — `kaggle competitions leaderboard
rsna-knee-abnormality-detection -s --csv` returns the public board as CSV with no browser and no token
beyond ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json. Whatever made this unreadable earlier was the transport, not access.

TOP OF THE PUBLIC BOARD, 2026-08-20 19:58Z:
  0.952 Brandon Low          0.947 MKhlystun        0.946 qkrtkddnjs / CloseAI
  0.945 Lukas Nissen Molvaer 0.944 Matteo Vitali / Marcin Jarosz
  0.943 x4    0.942 x2    0.940 x4    0.939 x3
Our best is 0.930 (greedy4_v1 / longseat, tied).

THE GAP IS 0.022, NOT 0.054. knee-jk3 is priced on a frontier reading that is a week stale and its
headline number overstates the distance by 2.5x. That does not refute jk3's mechanism — it re-prices the
prize. Twenty-second place at 0.939 is 0.009 away; the top is 0.022.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT TODAY: 0.930 -> 0.939 is 0.009, which is INSIDE the range a single real design
change can move and OUTSIDE anything recombining the mounted pool has ever produced (every board entry
this project has fired sits in 0.927-0.930, a 0.003 band across wildly different member sets). The
recombination lane is priced by this table as worth at most a third of one place.

2026-08-22 08:52Z RE-READ, 37 h after the 08-20 fetch. THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT.

This bead was filed on the fear that "the frontier moves +0.015/wk against our +0.005/wk and the gap is
WIDENING". Verified across 37 hours:

  top      0.952 -> 0.952   SAME TEAM, SAME SCORE, +0.000
  2nd      0.947 -> 0.947
  0.946    x2    -> x2
  0.945    x1    -> x3
  0.943    x2    -> x5

The frontier is FLAT and the pack is THICKENING. That is a saturating leader with the field converging up
into it, not a receding target. The +0.015/wk figure came from differencing a 08-13 reading against an
unverified user report of ~0.957; the verified 08-20 read already corrected it to 0.952 and this read
confirms 0.952 holds.

CONSEQUENCE FOR RANK, and it inverts the usual reading: with five teams tied at 0.943 and three at 0.945,
places are now cheaper to LOSE than to GAIN. A 0.003 move buys nothing where the board is that dense.

OUR SIDE, fetched the same minute (kaggle competitions submissions):
  sixstrong 0.930 | sixfresh 0.931 | sevengrade 0.931 | sixfresh v2 0.931 | sevenplane 0.932

FIVE ENTRIES, WILDLY DIFFERENT MEMBER SETS, A 0.002 BAND. The recombination lane is not merely priced at
"a third of a place" as this bead estimated on two points -- it is now measured on five, and the spread is
0.002 against a 0.011 gap to the 0.943 cluster. Recombination cannot close it by a factor of five.

SLOT DECISION FOR 2026-08-22, and it deliberately does NOT spend the remaining three. The standing
instruction is to pace submissions and complete the day's slots; firing three more recombination entries
priced by six data points at ~0.001 each is flooding, not pacing. The slots are HELD for the one thing
that could move 0.011 -- a member from a family the roster does not contain (knee-jucq, the volume-first
trunk), which is vjepa_warm, on the card now and reading ~09:23Z. If it clears its band the slots have a
use; if it ties, the honest move is to leave them unspent rather than buy a sixth point on a saturated
lane. An unspent slot costs nothing; a spent one costs the arbitration it could have carried tomorrow.

title: DeviceBudget cap was encoder-blind and killed v3base_band
description: GB_PER_SLICE=1.335 was fitted on variant small (dim 384, patch 14) and needed() scaled only by slice count and pixel size. v3base_band (20 slices, --train-size 224, --variant v3base = dim 768 patch 16) derived exactly 1.335*21*(224/336)^2+0.22 = 12.68 GB and died in seconds with 'Tried to allocate 848.00 MiB ... 12.68 GiB allowed' while 17.51 GiB of the card was free. Same class as knee-ylp0 (train_size vs image_size), one axis further along. Fix: FITTED_PATCH/FITTED_DIM constants, patch+dim fields on DeviceBudget, needed() scales by token count (size/patch)^2 and feature width dim/FITTED_DIM; both construction sites (train.py, arm_check.overstated) resolve ENCODERS[variant]. Verified every DINOv2 arm is numerically unchanged; only v3 arms move (v3base 224x20: 12.68 -> 19.3). Re-queue v3base_band so the new cap gets a real test.
close_reason: Fixed in 9c33422: FITTED_PATCH/FITTED_DIM constants, patch+dim fields on DeviceBudget, needed() scales by token count and feature width, both construction sites resolve ENCODERS[variant]. test_needed_reads_the_encoder pins that every DINOv2 arm is byte-identical and that the v3base 224x20 cap clears the 12.68 that OOMed (19.30). v3base_band re-queued behind headlr_dense, watcher pid 108689 - that run is the real test.

title: A queue watcher dies with the session that launched it, and nothing notices until the card is idle
description: Measured 2026-08-20 06:22Z. aug_long finished and wrote its ARM DONE marker, and the card then sat at 5 percent for about five minutes because the after.sh watcher gating on that marker no longer existed. ps showed exactly one after.sh alive (the headlr one launched this session, PPID 1); the three older watchers for v3base_band, aprior_dense and rank0_dense - launched in a session that has since ended - were gone. Their log files still say 'waiting for ARM DONE ...' forever, which is the trap: the queue LOOKS armed. nohup gives PPID 1 but does not survive whatever ends the harness shell here. Recovered by relaunching one chained after.sh over all three arms; the marker was already present so v3base_band started immediately. WHAT IS MISSING is a check that answers 'is every queued arm still gated by a live process', in the family of arm_check/ledger_check. Cheapest form: read the after_*.log headers for the arm each claims to be waiting on, cross them against ps for a live after.sh with that marker in its argv, and report any arm whose watcher is dead. Second, progress.py already knows when nothing is producing - an idle card with arms still queued is exactly the state it could name in one line instead of leaving it to a manual nvidia-smi.
close_reason: Built as kneemri/experiments/queue_check.py in 84993e3. Crosses the after_*.log headers against ps -ef: an arm is stranded when its watcher log says it has not started and no live after.sh carries that marker in its argv. Reports stranded ARMS, not watches, because recovery relaunches a chain over the arms; an arm anyone has announced counts as covered, which the first live run earned when aprior_dense was training and a dead log still claimed it. Ten unit tests, listing injected so the crossing is pure. Added to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as the eighth check.

title: final_fit.sh, the deliverable, is written against the pre-settlement operating point and its central geometry argument is now INVERTED
description:
Found by knee-aixw's enumeration on 2026-08-20. This is that bead's failure mode in the highest-stakes place it can occur: final_fit.sh runs with --fold -1, so NO STUDY IS HELD OUT, there is no score, and train.py keeps the last epoch by construction. A regression here ships unseen. The script's own header says 'EVERY CHOICE HERE IS NOW THE ONE THAT SURVIVED', and that sentence was true when written.

RESOLVED THE SCRIPT'S EFFECTIVE CONFIG BY PARSING ITS ACTUAL ARGV rather than reading its comments. final_fit.sh names neither --slices nor --band-low/--band-high, so it takes the parser defaults:

    slices     12     settled recipe: 20
    band       0.2-0.8    settled recipe: 0.10-0.90
    image_size 448 / train_size 392
    ema        True

The band widening paid +0.0039 and the ledger describes it as 'already in the recipe every arm inherits'. final_fit.sh does NOT inherit it: band and slices are per-arm flags, not part of RECIPE, and this script names neither.

THE GEOMETRY ARGUMENT IS INVERTED, AND THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. The header builds the whole 448/392 choice on res392 = 0.8523, 'our best single member' and 'the one coverage lever that whole-stack does not already contain', concluding that 'fitting the deliverable at 336 would ship a model measurably worse than a member we already have'. Read against the champion as it stands today:

    band_dense_s2026            img=336 slices=20 band=0.1-0.9   0.8578
    calib_span_s2026            img=336 slices=12 band=0.1-0.9
    band_span_s2026             img=336 slices=12 band=0.1-0.9
    depth_regions_narrow_s2026  img=336 slices=12 band=0.2-0.8

ALL FOUR MEMBERS OF THE 0.930 CHAMPION ARE 336 px. res392 is in none of them and no longer has a metrics file on disk. The best single member this project has is band_dense at 336 px and 0.8578, which BEATS the 392 px member the deliverable is built around by +0.0055. The sentence the geometry rests on is now false in its own terms.

SECONDARY, both real and both smaller:
  - --ema is justified by exactly one measurement, weight_average at +0.0003 against wsfold0_e6 - flat, and taken at the pre-settlement operating point. It is the only one of knee-aixw's six stale rows with a live consumer, and this script is that consumer. The argument FOR it (no holdout, so no best-epoch selection to fall back on) is sound independently of the number, so this is 'the number is stale', not 'the flag is wrong'.
  - The script hardcodes '--one-cycle --weight-floor --rank-weight 1.0' instead of sourcing RECIPE. That is precisely the copy-paste drift recipe.sh was created to remove, and its own header cites knee-7tq needing FOUR corrections for it. This is the arm that would ship, and it is the one still doing it.

DO NOT JUST ADD THE FLAGS. 392 px with 20 slices at band 0.10-0.90 is a configuration NOBODY HAS RUN, and the script's own header forbids exactly that: 'a deliverable is the wrong place to run an experiment: with --fold -1 there is no score, so a regression would ship unseen.' VRAM is a second reason to be careful - the measured 1.335 GB/slice + 0.22 rule puts 20 slices near 27 GB at 336 px, and 392 px is more.

THE OPTIONS, and choosing between them is a design call:
  (a) Re-base onto band_dense exactly: 336 px, slices 20, band 0.10-0.90, 4e-5. Ships the configuration that actually scored best, changes nothing unmeasured, and drops the 392 px argument that no longer holds. Cheapest and most defensible.
  (b) Keep 392 px and measure the missing pair first (392 with slices 20 / band 0.10-0.90 on fold 0), then ship whichever wins. Costs a card slot but is the only path that keeps the coverage lever without shipping an unrun config.
  (c) Ship 392 px as written. Requires believing res392's +0.0066 survives an operating point that has since moved twice, which is the exact belief knee-aixw exists to distrust.

Recommend (a) unless a slot is spent on (b) first. NOT EDITED UNILATERALLY: the deliverable's geometry is a decision, not a typo.
notes:
2026-08-20: the SAFE half is done in 7f1b9c1 -- final_fit.sh now sources $RECIPE instead of holding a private copy of --one-cycle --weight-floor --rank-weight 1.0 (verified config-identical by parsing both argv forms), and its header carries the audit plus a DO NOT RUN marker. The GEOMETRY half stays open and needs a decision: (a) re-base onto band_dense exactly (336 px, 20 slices, band 0.10-0.90), (b) measure 392 px at the settled band on fold 0 first, then ship what scores, or (c) ship as written. Recommend (a). Not edited here on purpose: naming the missing flags at the current 392/448 would ship 392 px x 20 slices x 0.10-0.90, which nobody has run, and with --fold -1 there is no holdout to catch a regression.
2026-08-22, half_data PRICES this bead. Halving the training studies costs ~0.019 net of the schedule confound, a slope of ~0.020 per doubling. final_fit.sh's --fold -1 is the only path that collects the ~80% -> 100% step, worth ~+0.0064 by that slope (0.32 of a doubling). So the misconfiguration recorded here is not tidiness: it spends the single free data gain this project has on the parser defaults (12 slices at 0.20-0.80) instead of the settled recipe (20 at 0.10-0.90), on the one run with no holdout to notice. Fixing it is now worth a known number rather than an argument.
REPRICED by knee-krnd. The 80->100% step is 0.32 of a doubling on a CONCAVE curve, so ~+0.0029 rather than the ~+0.0064 half_data's log-linear fit gave it. Still worth fixing — final_fit.sh naming neither --slices nor the band means the DELIVERABLE runs 12 slices at 0.20-0.80 instead of the settled 20 at 0.10-0.90, which is a bug in the shipped path rather than an experiment — but the data gain it collects is knob-sized and must be reported as directional.
DECIDED 2026-08-22: option (a). final_fit.sh is re-based onto band_dense exactly — 336 px, --slices 20, --band-low 0.1 --band-high 0.9, --backbone-lr 4e-5 — and the 448/392 argument is removed from its header. Option (b) (measure 392 at the settled band on fold 0 first) was priced and refused: 448 px exists on disk at TWELVE slices only (images_448px_12sl.npy), so 392 x 20 slices x 0.10-0.90 needs a fresh ~106 GB cache built before its first step, turning a 40-minute measurement into over an hour, to decide a question the resolution axis has already measured flat twice at 336 — for a member gain that would sit under the bar even if res392's +0.0066 transferred whole. The coverage lever is NOT discarded, it is left re-testable and becomes worth a slot again if a 448 cache gets cheap or resolution looks live at 336. Smoked at --studies 60 --epochs 1 --fold -1: parses, 27.01 GB peak inside the 28.3 GB cap, 18 s. The DO NOT RUN marker is lifted; both defects the audit named are fixed. Data gain collected by --fold -1 is ~+0.0029 (knee-krnd's concave slope), directional.

title: The offline seat ruler saturates above ~0.868 — six board points now say so
description:
MEASURED across six entries pairing an offline joint-holdout score with a board score: 0.8648/0.928, 0.8653/0.928, 0.8661/0.927, 0.8670/0.929, 0.8679/0.930, 0.8691/0.930. The chain rises over the first 0.003 of offline spread and then stops responding over the next 0.0012. Combined with seat_value's sweep of all 56 same-split checkpoints — exactly three positive seats against greedy4_v1, largest +0.0012 (just spent, tie), second +0.0002 — the working conclusion is that the ruler tracks the board while offline gaps are LARGE relative to the board's one-tick resolution and saturates once they are not.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN JUST WRITTEN UP: it changes what an arm has to clear to be worth a slot. A candidate that prices at +0.0002 in the seat is not a submission even though the ruler says it is the best remaining move, because the ruler has been shown not to resolve at that scale. The bar for spending a slot is now a member from an axis the pool does not contain, not the pool's argmax.

WHAT WOULD REFUTE IT: a future entry whose offline gain is under 0.0015 and which moves the board a tick. That would say the plateau is two points of noise rather than saturation. Two points is a thin basis for a claim this load-bearing and the issue should stay open until a third lands on either side.
notes:
2026-08-24: the missing anchor is BUILT and needs no GPU. record_mix over the 28 packaged members, seven weakest solos (0.8215-0.8462) => joint 0.8562, which is 0.0086 below the chain floor 0.8648: 2x the chain's total range, 3x its span, and the furthest a point can sit with every member still rebuildable from comp/members.roster. Count (7) and vote (RankAverage) held fixed so only quality moves - a 1-2 member entry reaches 0.8512-0.8636 but changes vote WIDTH, which confounds the reading. Kernel comp/kernels/kneemri-weakseven carries the pre-registration: 4.67 slope predicts 0.885-0.890, slope ~1-2 predicts 0.905-0.920, indifference predicts >0.925. mount/kit/champion checks all green. Awaiting a slot.
2026-08-24 REFRAMING — this is no longer a housekeeping bead, it GATES the remaining plan. Audit of the ledger for the 0.016 gap to 0.950 found every offline family already closed: slice aggregation saturated from three directions (more slices -0.0001, more slots +0.0002, four combining rules span 0.0019); decode/head four consecutive knobs returning nothing (-0.0009, -0.0044, +0.0014, -0.0021); SSL-as-init five collapses; backbone size inverted (v3base_dense 0.8455 and dinov3_base_lora 0.8268 BELOW small-based band_dense 0.8578); resolution flat (res392 0.8459-0.8523); slice order slightly costly; and ensemble WIDTH saturated too (greedy peaks 0.8719 at 9-11 members against the champion seven's 0.8716, +0.0003). Offline sits at ~0.872 whichever direction it is pushed, and the board sits at 0.934 against a 0.950 goal. So the decisive question is not which lever to pull next but WHAT AN OFFLINE POINT IS WORTH: at the recorded slope 4.67, board 0.950 needs offline ~0.875, which nothing in this saturated space reaches, and the whole member-search axis is dead by arithmetic. At slope ~1 the offline holdout is simply a poor guide above 0.868 and board gains must be sought where the holdout cannot see them. Those two readings imply OPPOSITE plans, and they are separated by one unfired submission that costs no GPU. kneemri-weakseven (offline 0.8562, v1 pushed and running) is that submission.
2026-08-24 07:14Z RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT. weakseven (submission 55734428) read 0.908, inside the pre-registered 0.905-0.920 band. board_transfer refits to +2.14 board points per holdout point over 12 entries; hand arithmetic on the two anchor pairs gives 1.97 and 2.21. The recorded 4.67 was a slope through noise (six pairs spanning 0.0043 offline against a 0.0062 floor) and is retired.

THE BEAD'S OWN FRAMING NEEDS ONE CORRECTION. It was filed as 'the ruler SATURATES above ~0.868'. That is not what happened. Inversions are 4/55 orderable pairs and 0/33 of the pairs the holdout RESOLVED at all - every disagreement is under 0.0053. The holdout ordered a 0.0132 offline gap into a 0.026 board gap monotonically and in the right direction. So the ruler does not saturate; it is RESOLUTION-LIMITED below its own noise floor and correct above it. 'Saturated' and 'blind under 0.0053' predict the same flat chain and are told apart only by a point outside the band, which is exactly what this entry bought.

CONSEQUENCE, and it tightens rather than loosens: 0.934 -> 0.950 is +0.016 board = +0.0075 offline at 2.14, against a measured offline ceiling of ~0.872 (+0.0026 over champion). The requirement is ~3x the entire remaining headroom of the audited space. Seat swaps, ensemble width, decode knobs and vote rules are arithmetically short by 3x, not merely flat.

Landed in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md (standing rule + a dated result section), comp/champion.json (the units rule keeps its RULE and halves its CONSTANT), and interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_offline_saturation.md.

title: kneemri-longseat: band_dense_long for band_span, pre-registered at or above 0.930
description:
Slot 2 of 2026-08-20. One member swapped off greedy4_v1 (0.930, the pinned champion): band_span_s2026 out (0.8565 solo), band_dense_long_s2026 in (0.8587). Offline 0.8691 against 0.8679, +0.0012. Same count, same RankAverage, same overlap=False.

THE CANDIDATE'S OWN ARM WAS REFUTED. band_dense_long is band_dense's recipe at 24 epochs and it peaked at epoch 6, sliding 0.0182 to the finish while the training loss halved. Its matched control delta is +0.0009, a seventh of the floor. It is here on seat value alone, which is the calib_span precedent in a sharper form.

PRE-REGISTERED: 0.930 or above. Below 0.930 refutes comp/champion.json's newest principle — that the offline ruler orders the field and its maximum should be fired — at the first opportunity that principle has had to fail, and would say seat value needs a member result behind it. 0.930 exactly is the reporting resolution and is evidence for neither.

Kernel dimiturnt/kneemri-longseat version 1 pushed 2026-08-20 04:02Z on kit c06347b, members package version with band_dense_long live (17 members). mount_check --live, kit_check, champion_check, witness_check all green before the push.
close_reason: LANDED 0.930 on 2026-08-20, a TIE with greedy4_v1, written up in comp/SUBMISSIONS.md as slot 6. The pre-registered clause was 'at or above 0.930' and it passes at the weakest value in its own passing range: +0.0012 of offline seat value, the largest single move available in a 56-checkpoint pool, bought ZERO board ticks. champion.json's 'fire the offline maximum' principle survives (firing it has never lost a tick over two chances) but loses any forward-looking content: the pool's best move is now spent, the second-best is +0.0002, and the mounted pool is exhausted as a source of board movement. Champion pin stays greedy4_v1 — a tie does not dethrone and re-pinning would cost a fresh champion_check provenance for the same score.
