Do NOT widen the witness bound or weaken the UNVERIFIED verdict to make this go away. The 0.0312-class bounds are what separate this project from the 0.05-0.5 that every real reading defect has produced.
close_reason: Duplicate of knee-mwej, which already held the finding with better evidence. Its one novel item - that a witness is a fingerprint rather than a score, so an all-data member CAN carry one taken from its train set - is merged into knee-mwej's notes. Filed without grepping the ledger first, which is the exact failure CLAUDE.md warns about.

title: MemberDistance validated as a pair-gain ruler; raw distance is inverted without a quality control
description: fault_ruler measured all four candidate diversity statistics against measured offline pair gain over 166 members / 1200 pairs / 48000 discordance trials. Partial (quality held fixed): agreement/MemberDistance +0.7086, DER +0.6999, disagreement +0.6955, double-fault +0.5911. Pokhrel's ordering does NOT transfer. Raw, every statistic reads negative (agreement -0.5313) because this pool's distant members are its weak ones. MemberDistance.report ranks candidates across the whole quality range and is exposed to that confound - it should either restrict to comparable solo scores or residualise. Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_the-diversity-ruler-was-checked-and-the-citation-does-not-transfer.md

title: push.sh reports a false failure on a large dataset version
description: A 13G members push on 2026-09-04 ended with 'REFUSING to report success: the pushed version never read complete. Re-push before submitting.' The version had in fact landed: 'kaggle datasets status dimiturnt/kneemri-members' read 'ready', the files were stamped 00:48Z, and mount_check --live went from 83 ok / 8 refused to 90 ok / 1 refused. So the completion poll gives up before Kaggle finishes processing a version of this size, and the message tells the operator to RE-PUSH -- which would have spent another 13G of upload and another ~15 minutes to reach the state already reached. The failure mode is the expensive direction: a false failure that instructs a costly retry. Scale the poll window with the uploaded byte count, or re-read the status once after the window expires before writing the refusal.

title: roster_check does not catch a member named twice
description: comp/members.roster named certainty_ramp_s2026 and disagreed_ramp_s2026 twice each — a terse early row and a full 2026-09-02 block. roster_check passed it (179 scoreable, 0 undocumented) because it only asks whether every scoreable checkpoint is DOCUMENTED, never whether a name is documented ONCE. The collision was caught downstream by MemberManifest.document, which refuses because the second copy overwrites the first and the package would then list a member whose weights are another member's. That refusal is the right one, but it fires only when somebody rebuilds the package; the roster can carry the defect indefinitely between rebuilds, and the roster is the file a human edits. Add the duplicate-name assertion to roster_check so the defect is caught where it is introduced.

title: Sixteen arms across three trunk families trained plain cross-entropy under a ranking arm's name
description:
$RECIPE (experiments/recipe.sh:23) carries --rank-weight 1.0. RankedObjective.ranking forms pairs WITHIN the micro-batch, so at --batch 1 no pair forms and the term contributes exactly zero; --accumulate cannot repair it. knee-if3ze found this on ortho_stack and fixed that one arm. The census was never taken. It is sixteen arms, and none of them carries --pair-memory:

cnx_dense_448, cnx_mid_rate, cnx_warm_anneal, cnx_top_rate, cnx_own_recipe, cnx_distill_warm,
raptor_feat_fit, raptor_feat_pre, swin_toprate, swin_supervised, swin_open_half, swin_wholetop,
swin_distill_pre, swin_distill_fit, swin_calib_dense, radnet_family

That is the WHOLE ConvNeXt family, the WHOLE Swin family, the RadImageNet arm and the raptor feature-distillation pair. Every one was compared against a control that trained at batch 12 with the term ON, so every one moved TWO variables and every family was closed on that comparison. radnet_family 0.6716 is the number recorded in comp/members.declines closing the trunk-ARCHITECTURE-family lane, which the loop policy lists as CLOSED.

THE TERM IS PRICED, FREE, IN FLIGHT. The two ortho_stack runs differ by exactly --pair-memory 66:
  epoch 0  void 0.7389  |  term-on 0.7389  |  +0.0000
  epoch 1  void 0.7778  |  term-on 0.7837  |  +0.0059
  epoch 2  void 0.8010  |  term-on 0.8090  |  +0.0080
Growing with epoch. Do not re-run anything until this pair converges; it licenses or kills all sixteen at once and costs zero card.

WHAT THE ARITHMETIC ALREADY SAYS, so the re-runs are ranked before they are priced. Known void scores against band_dense 0.8578 and the 0.8459 seat bar: swin_toprate 0.8393, swin_wholetop 0.8331, swin_supervised 0.8192, cnx_own_recipe 0.8186, radnet_family 0.6716. If the term converges worth +0.010-0.015, only swin_toprate plausibly reaches the seat bar and none reaches the incumbent. So this is very likely a correctness debt rather than a rescued member - but the families were ABANDONED on these numbers, so what it re-opens is the DECISION to stop, not the members.

THE GUARD IS ALREADY WRITTEN: run_setup._check_pairs_can_form raises before the card is touched, so none of the sixteen can re-run as written. Fix is to add --pair-memory to each header with the derived capacity, not to relax the guard.
notes: PRICED 2026-09-04 01:05Z without waiting for a convergence that cannot arrive. The term-OFF half of the ortho_stack pair was KILLED at epoch 3 (four rows in ortho_stack_s2026.metrics.1.jsonl); the gate as written never opens. Matched-epoch delta e0-e3: +0.0000 / +0.0059 / +0.0080 / +0.0088, increments +0.0059 / +0.0021 / +0.0008 - saturating, asymptote ~+0.009-0.010, above the 0.0062 floor. DECISION: re-run NONE of the sixteen. At a generous +0.015 the best of them (swin_toprate 0.8393 -> 0.8543) is still under band_dense 0.8578, so eighty hours of card buys zero seats. What survives is the DECISION cost, not the members: the Swin family was closed at an apparent 0.0185 gap that is really ~0.0035. ONE corrected arm on swin_toprate's flags plus a derived --pair-memory is the only defensible spend, and its case is SEAT DIVERSITY in a DINOv2-monoculture pool, not solo quality. Gated behind ortho_stack and v3large_stack. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-04_three-trunk-families-were-closed-on-a-silenced-objective.md

title: mount_check refuses orthorehearse against the wrong package
description: mount_check --live REFUSES kneemri-orthorehearse: 'all_ours holds [...] and was asked for [ortho_dense_s2026]'. But that kernel mounts dimiturnt/kneemri-ortho-pkg, not the all_ours/kneemri-members package, and it has already RUN with run_check reading 'loaded 1 of 1 members'. So the check resolves the kernel's package from a default staging directory rather than from the kernel's own dataset_sources, and reports a false refusal on a kernel that demonstrably mounts. Risk is desensitisation: this is the gate that caught kneemri-solo's DINOv3 metadata drift, and a standing false refusal trains us to wave it off.

title: transduction: eight negative cells, axis NOT closed
description: kneemri/evaluation/transduction.py measured feature-space pseudo-label adaptation: two trunks x four tail sizes, every cell negative (-0.0020 to -0.0055). Shape contradicts its own pre-registration - smallest tail is worst, damage shrinks as the tail grows - which points at the labelling scheme forcing 'share' positives per finding regardless of prevalence. NOT a closure: the probe head is linear so pseudo-labels lie along the first fit's own decision direction (near-circular refit), and the holdout is drawn from the training corpus so shift is zero by construction while self-training is a shift remedy. Re-open by (a) prevalence-matched pseudo-labels and (b) a nonlinear head, both free on cached features.

title: Board-row fold counts are written from the _cf/_ff suffix, not read from the training log
description:
vjepaseat_v1's offline_scope says 'six of the eight seats are --fold -1'. Reading D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality/experiments/*.full.log for each named seat gives FIVE: final_ws_cf -1, calib_span_ff -1, grade_ladder_cf -1, lr4e-5_ws_cf -1, through_dense_cf -1, and merged_blend_cf is --fold 0. The _cf/_ff suffix is per-member and does NOT encode the fold; the row was written from the convention.

No verdict moves: one --fold -1 seat contaminates a pool as thoroughly as six, so 'no offline number is possible for this pool' stays true, and twinfive_v1's 0.8705 is CORRECT (all five of its seats really are --fold 0, merged_blend_cf included). Filed because the same habit written the other way round - calling a fold -1 member fold 0 - would manufacture an honest-looking offline number out of an in-sample pool, which is exactly the defect knee-nbk3 and the raptor_solo 0.8938 void were about.

FIX: board_check should read --fold from each member's full.log and assert the row's stated count, the way it already joins on the submission REF rather than a name. Cheap: the logs are on disk and the parse is one grep.

title: board_transfer's high-position slope rests on 3 pairs and the fit cannot see any fold -1 entry
description: board_transfer prints three compression bands: +1.25 whole record (436 pairs), +0.97 at >=0.8678 (13 resolved pairs), +0.71 at >=0.8694 (THREE resolved pairs). The +0.71 has been quoted as the operative constant -- holdfive_v1's board row prices its whole reading on it, and I priced four kill decisions on it on 2026-09-03 before checking. Two defects. (1) THIN: three pairs, non-independent (they share entries), and the printed '[+0.70, +0.89]' is a median range over those three, which reads as a confidence interval and is not one. (2) STRUCTURALLY BLIND: the run reports 43 one-sided entries -- every --fold -1 entry, the champion raptorweight_v1 among them -- because a fold -1 entry has no offline number by construction. So the fit is computed entirely on fold-0 entries, which occupy the 0.932-0.938 band of the board. 'Compression decreases at the top of the pool' is therefore a claim about the top of the FOLD-0 range, and the actual top of the board is unobservable to this instrument. CONSEQUENCE: any arm priced against a single slope is mispriced; quote the range +0.0064/+0.0082/+0.0113 for closing the 0.008 gap. WANTED: either an uncertainty on the band slopes that reflects pair non-independence, or a printed refusal when a band has fewer than N resolved pairs, plus a line naming how many entries the fit could not see.

title: merged3_corpus read -0.0024 and closes the corpus axis: slot coverage refuted, KIND does not compose
description: merged3_corpus_s2026 ran, landed at 0.8521 against merged_corpus's 0.8545, and was never written up. Reading now at interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-03_the-corpus-axis-saturates-at-two-sites.md. Mean -0.0024 inside the floor; the SPLIT is the result and it is merged_corpus's split inverted: Lateral Meniscus +0.0196* -> -0.0217*, Synovitis -0.0206* -> +0.0234*, focal/regional +0.0056/-0.0031 -> -0.0076/+0.0048. MRNet supervises ACL alone with 1,248 expert image reads and ACL moved -0.0013 -- the supervision landed and bought nothing. Closes slot-coverage (3 filled slots vs 1, negative), volume a third time (+24% studies, nothing), and KIND-composition (second image-read corpus cancelled the first's only starred gain). FLAT branch per the arm's own pre-registration, so MRNET_LEVEL is not implicated. Open successor: --corpus-oversample on a merged cache, never run, priced as an instrument not a gain.

title: ortho_lpft stage two, the number that prices the trunk, is truncated
description:
convergence_check reads ortho_lpft_s2026 as TRUNCATED: best e4 of 5 run, 12 asked. comp/members.declines:261 names this run as the one that prices the OrthoDiffusion trunk -- 'stage two (ortho_lpft_s2026, unfreeze_last 6, whole stack) is what prices the trunk; re-open on THAT number, never on this one' -- and under one_cycle a kill at 5 of 12 makes that number a floor.

Relevant now because Kimi Q-CO (2026-09-03) established there is NO published cross-family recipe-transfer rule (muP is within-family; LLRD and linear LR scaling are heuristics), so the trunk axis's re-open condition is only payable by a banned sweep. LP-FT (Kumar et al. 2022 ICLR) is the one exception: a DERIVED two-stage recipe, not a search. So the LP-FT triple is the only affordable route left onto that axis, and one of its three legs is a floor.

Lower priority than the fx re-run because ortholarge is licence-blocked (knee-nxthh, Kimi Q-CE outstanding), so even a good number ships nothing -- it is an instrument. The triple is also still one control short (ortho_fresh_lowlr, knee-6hfi).

title: Members specialise by finding: seven leaders across twelve columns, oracle ceiling +0.0094
description: First run of seat_profile over the ten holdout-readable pool members (2026-09-03, logs/seat_profile.txt). Seven DIFFERENT members lead the twelve findings: recal_dense 3 (Fracture .8322, Contusion .8867, Effusion .8633), stackfit 2 (PF OA .8733, ACL .8976), stack_increments 2 (Baker's .9237, MCL .8131), certainty_ramp 2 (Synovitis .8773, Medial Meniscus .9106), labelwise_dense 1 (Medial OA .8968), calib_dense_hold 1 (Lateral Meniscus .8700), stack_increments_base 1 (Lateral OA .8386). Best-per-column mean 0.8736 against best-single 0.8642 = +0.0094 ORACLE ceiling, and that ceiling is picked with hindsight on the same 909-study holdout, so real value is materially less. Above the 0.0062 floor, below the 1.5% bar: directional, composes, NOT a plan. SPREAD says where a seat can still pay: PF OA 0.0541, Baker's 0.0383, Fracture 0.0368 wide; Medial Meniscus 0.0137, Effusion 0.0164 narrow. MCL is the weakest column on 7 of 10 members (0.7800-0.8131) while spreading only 0.0331 - the pool is uniformly bad at it, which is a DATA or LABEL statement, not a seating one. CAVEAT THAT LIMITS ALL OF IT: all six champion seats are --fold -1 and have no record here, so this table describes the POOL, never the shipped entry.

title: seat_profile's missing-record error asserts a cause it never checked
description: kneemri/evaluation/seat_profile.py:37 raises 'left no holdout record - a --fold -1 member has none and can never have one' whenever HoldoutRecord.exists() is false. It never checks WHY. --members is type=Path, so passing a bare member name (rather than a checkpoint path) resolves against the repo root, the record is absent, and the tool blames --fold -1. On 2026-09-03 that message cost three calls and produced a false belief that slot_dropout_s2026 was dark - its .holdout.npz is on disk. Fix: distinguish 'checkpoint path does not exist' from 'checkpoint exists but kept no record', and only name --fold -1 in the second case. This is the harness-as-suspect failure the project keeps paying for, in miniature: a diagnostic that states a mechanism it did not measure.

title: Occlusion attribution is the less faithful readout — demote or fix attribution.py
description: knee-wgaa measured attention vs occlusion on attend_true_s2026, fold-0 holdout, 200 studies: attention wins on BOTH faithfulness metrics for 12/12 findings (infidelity 0.037-0.125 vs 0.052-0.188; sensitivity_max 0.70-0.90 vs 0.88-2.41). An occlusion sensitivity_max above 1.0 means the explanation moves more than the signal it explains. Any past reading that rested on an occlusion map should be re-read, and kneemri/evaluation/attribution.py should either be fixed or carry a docstring demoting it against attention_readout.py. Filed out of knee-wgaa's own FOLLOW-ON note.

title: Audit local vision-language models for report re-reading
description: Survey local VLMs that fit a 5090 (Qwen-VL, MedGemma, etc.) and estimate token cost for re-reading the 4,407 English/non-English reports against the published rubric. Realistic targets are Baker's and Contusion; Synovitis/Fracture reports are mostly silent. See comp/members.declines and research/2026-09-03_state_of_labels_and_model_axes.md.

title: Multilingual rubric re-read for subthreshold report vocabulary
description: English rubric correction touches 502 backed-contradiction cells; expanding to es/tr/hr/el/de/bg/nl reaches ~1,250 cells at zero GPU cost. Build per-language subthreshold vocabulary and run core.data.labels.table_correction. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-02_what-label-correction-is-actually-worth.md.

title: Fix missing gold-study row and targeted parser fixes for Effusion/Synovitis
description: report_labels_v2.csv is missing the gold study 1.2.826.0.1.3680043.8.498.73527530686853911124431549317032662220 (ACL/PF OA/Effusion/Contusion/Fracture positives). Audit also shows 70% Effusion false positives and 52% Synovitis false negatives. Fix the missing row and add targeted rules for trace/small effusion and implicit synovitis language. See interpretations/kneemri/2026-09-02_report-to-label_audit.md.

title: Scheme B: partial-label multi-task pretraining on MRNet+fastMRI++Rijeka
description: Shared trunk + task-specific heads with masked binary cross-entropy across RSNA, MRNet, fastMRI+ and Rijeka. Use LP-FT, L2-SP, external oversampling, MixStyle-style augmentation and an external validation split. Expected mean-AUC +0.005 to +0.012. See research/2026-09-02_using_external_knee_mri_data_to_improve_kaggle_score.md.

title: Arm a 224 px full-slice-coverage probe
description: Run a slice-coverage probe at 224 px that reads the full sagittal stack (36+ slices) instead of the current 12-20 slice cap. Measure per-label AUC and VRAM. Public frontier reads 64 slices/study; this project tops out at 20. See research/2026-08-31_public-frontier-sweep.md and research/2026-09-03_state_of_labels_and_model_axes.md.

title: Smoke-test OrthoDiffusion as a 3D knee-MRI member
description: Download HuggingFace weights for OrthoDiffusion, inspect checkpoint structure, extract sagittal/coronal/axial diffusion features for a batch of RSNA studies, pool/fuse, train a small 12-label head, and compare holdout AUC against the DINOv2/DINOv3 baseline. See research/2026-09-03_state_of_labels_and_model_axes.md and research/2026-09-02_sota_pretrained_knee_mri_models_2025_2026.md.

title: The UNK cells are a semi-supervised target, not a reading target — price it
description:
27.3% of supervision is the constant 0.28 with verdict UNK (14,445 of 52,872 cells), concentrated in Synovitis 84.2%, Fracture 56.4%, Baker's 45.9%. Two measurements now bracket what can be done with them.

report_reader (2026-08-27) closed READING them: on the UNK cells the report does not name the structure — Synovitis 1.8% of 1,424, Effusion 0 of 84. Only Baker's (30.8%) and Contusion (16.1%) have recoverable text, worth 1-3% of the matrix moving one rung, which that file already declines to arm.

supervision_gap on recal_dense (2026-09-03, knee-qxyj) says what the model does with them anyway: against radiologist truth on the 58 annotated studies the model beats its own labels by 0.047 [-0.0717,-0.0218], and the per-finding gaps are largest exactly where UNK is densest — Synovitis +0.1075 (label 0.687, model 0.794), Fracture +0.0715 (0.870, 0.942).

So on those cells the model is exceeding a ceiling made of constants, not out-reading a mis-read label. Targets already pulls an UNK cell weakly by its 0.05 confidence. The unasked question is whether pulling it toward the MODEL's own read — self-training restricted to verdict==UNK, confidence unchanged elsewhere — beats pulling it toward a constant.

NOT ARMED. Needs its own pre-registration before any card time: what the target is (a fixed teacher's read vs an EMA of the student), which cells (UNK only, or UNK above a confidence band), and the gate. The gate is the one report_reader already states for its own mechanism — score ON THE PAIRS THE LEXICON LEFT BLANK, since a win averaged over all pairs is a win over the denominator this would exist to correct. Control: band_dense_hold_s2026.
notes:
PLUMBING AUDIT 2026-09-03T10:33Z, before proposing an arm. core/data/labels/targets.py read in full.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS. Supervision.suspect takes a (StudyInstanceUID, target) csv and sets those cells' weight to 0.0 (targets.py:382), written by kneemri.evaluation.label_errors --flags. That is exactly the shape a cell-level UNK intervention needs, and it PRUNES. So one variant of this bead is ZERO new code: emit a flags table of every verdict==UNK cell and pass it as the suspect table.

WHY THAT VARIANT IS PROBABLY THE WRONG ONE, and the evidence is in the file. Every arm runs --weight-floor, so floor=0.25 and an UNK cell already pulls at 0.25 + 0.75*0.05 = 0.2875, with value 0.28 (0.136 calibrated). CONFIDENCE_FLOOR's docstring records that this project ORIGINALLY dropped unmentioned findings entirely at weight 0.0 and moved to the public baseline's floor: 'Silence in a radiology report is weak evidence of ABSENCE — a knee report lists what was checked and found intact — so dropping it discards evidence rather than declining to guess.' Pruning UNK is that decision run backwards. It is not identical (floor=0.0 leaves weight 0.05 on every cell, not 0.0 on UNK cells only) but it is close enough that it should be priced as a likely-negative instrument, not as a lever.

THE VARIANT WORTH THE CARD is the one with no plumbing: keep the weight, REPLACE THE VALUE on verdict==UNK cells with a teacher's read of the image. That is a new Supervision switch — a (study, target, value) table overwriting scores where suspect overwrites weights — roughly the pruned() method with an assignment instead of a mask, plus a supervised() key and the moves_the_ruler() clause (it moves the ruler, so --eval-labels must be pinned, as every calibrated arm already does).

WHY IT IS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY LABEL SWITCH ON THAT OBJECT. suspect's own docstring says the defect the other five cannot reach is the cell where the reader was confident and wrong. This is the complement: the cell where the reader said NOTHING. 14,445 cells, 27.3% of supervision, currently trained as 'weakly negative' on the strength of a lexicon's silence — where report_reader measured that the report genuinely never discusses the structure (Synovitis 1.8% of 1,424 UNK cells name it). A value that asserts weak-absence about something never examined is the one claim the annotations contradict: supervision_gap reads the model at 0.794 on Synovitis against the label's 0.687.

STILL NOT ARMED. Open: which teacher (a fixed rostered member's out-of-fold read vs an EMA of the student), whether to restrict to the three extreme-UNK findings or all twelve, and whether an annotated cell is exempt (it must be — suspect already exempts them at targets.py:382).
PRE-REGISTRATION, 2026-09-03T10:36Z. The three questions left open above, decided.

TEACHER: a FIXED out-of-fold read from one rostered member, not an EMA of the student. Three reasons. A moving target on 27% of cells through a shared trunk is a training-dynamics experiment wearing a label experiment's clothes, and it cannot be diffed, re-read or re-gated afterwards. Every label intervention this project has run is a static table on disk — that is why arm_check, the witness, run_comparison and the gold ruler all apply to them unchanged, and an EMA gives that up for nothing. And a table on disk composes with the plumbing that already exists.

WHICH MEMBER: calib_dense_hold_s2026 (0.8634, the best solo the project owns, and it carries --hold-annotations so the gold ruler will accept anything fitted from it). NAMED RISK: that member was itself trained with UNK cells at 0.28, so its read of an UNK cell is partly the prior it was pulled toward. That is the confirmation-collapse risk in its static form, and it is bounded rather than absent — the member reads PIXELS, and the gate below is radiologist truth it never saw.

SCOPE: every verdict==UNK cell, all twelve findings. NOT the four where supervision_gap measured the gap. Restricting to Synovitis / Fracture / Lateral Meniscus / Baker's would fit the intervention to a weakness measured on the same 58 studies it would then be gated on, which is unfalsifiable, and CLAUDE.md forbids shaping the objective to a specific weakness — needs come from balanced data, not from loss-engineering. The general version is also the honest one.

ANNOTATED CELLS EXEMPT, as Supervision.suspect already exempts them (targets.py:382). The radiologist reading is the truth the whole thing is gated against.

CONTROL: band_dense_hold_s2026, 0.8573 proxy / 0.8956 gold. Same recipe, same corner, already measured on both rulers, so only the arm costs card time.

RULER: --eval-labels PINNED. The switch moves the ruler (moves_the_ruler() must return True for it), so without the pin the arm scores against a table that moved with it — the exact defect recal_holdannot hit and knee-9198 exists for.

GATE: report_reader's own, because this shares its denominator problem. Score ON THE PAIRS THE LEXICON LEFT BLANK. A win averaged over all 52,872 pairs is a win over a denominator this exists to correct, since on the 72.7% the lexicon did read the two tables are identical by construction. Gold via annotated_readings against the control; floor 0.0062 on both.

PRE-REGISTERED SIZE, stated before running rather than after. Every measured label-lane delta in this project sits between +0.006 and +0.017, so the honest prediction here is sub-1.5% and this arm does NOT clear the house bar on precedent. What argues for it anyway is the only thing that is different about it: it moves 27.3% of the supervision, where every prior label arm moved a value or a weight on cells the reader had already read. A mechanism that touches a quarter of the training signal is the only label-side thing left that COULD be 1.5%, and if it lands at +0.01 like the rest, the lane is closed by exhaustion rather than by one more null.

BLOCKED ON: the card (owner's, 29.7 GB resident) and ~30 lines of new switch. Cost when armed: one 12-epoch arm, ~40 min, plus a CPU pass to write the teacher table.
2026-09-03 10:50Z DESIGN CHANGED, and the change is the whole point. The teacher is NOT our own member read in-sample. It is the PUBLISHED pool's out-of-fold arrays (PublishedRuler: 20 checkpoints, 5 folds x 4 seeds, partitioning all 4,407 studies), rank-averaged. Three reasons it is strictly better than the calib_dense_hold plan this bead was opened with: (a) every study has a prediction from a model that did not train on it, corpus-wide, with no folds of ours and no card hour; (b) it is the SAME array supervision_gap's labels-model = -0.0470 was measured with, so the mechanism and the evidence share a source rather than being argued across one; (c) our own member's read on its own training cells through a shared trunk is self-distillation, which is a training-dynamics experiment wearing a label experiment's clothes.

VALUES ARE MEAN-PRESERVING AND ORDER-ONLY. Rank is taken INSIDE each finding's UNK block, so it is uniform by construction and the band's mean is its centre; the centre is the constant those cells already carry, read off the table itself rather than stated (0.28 uncalibrated, 0.13559322 on v3). So the marginal each head sees is unchanged and the ONLY thing added is order - which is all the metric reads, and which keeps a prevalence shift (the one thing a twelve-head trunk transmits between heads) out of the arm.

THE BAND IS DERIVED. Half-width = the NEARER gap from the unread level to a neighbouring level in MEASURED_AGREEMENT. On the calibrated scale that is min(0.136-0.041, 0.378-0.136) = 0.095, band [0.041, 0.231]. So an override never asserts more about a cell than the reader's own adjacent verdict would have. The conservative side binds deliberately: the pool's discriminative power on UNK cells cannot be measured corpus-wide (58 annotated studies only), so the SIZE of the claim is capped by something that was measured rather than by a number chosen to make the arm interesting.

LANDED THIS WINDOW, all gated-pending: core/data/labels/targets.py Supervision.taught() + application in load() (scores only, after the loop, masked by ~read_by_radiologist so the radiologist still wins) + UNREAD in supervised(); --unread-targets in flag_vocabulary; unread_targets through options/landed/run_setup; kneemri/evaluation/unread_teacher.py (the generator) + its tests; 349 training/label unit tests green.

STILL BLOCKED ON THE CARD (owner's, 29.7 GB resident). Cost when it frees: one CPU pass to write the table, then one 12-epoch arm ~40 min. Control band_dense_hold_s2026, --eval-labels pinned, gate on the pairs the lexicon left blank plus gold via annotated_readings.
PRE-REGISTERED 2026-09-03T11:00Z, before any card time.

ARM: band_dense_hold recipe + --unread-targets <table>, 12 epochs, same split.
CONTROL: band_dense_hold_s2026, proxy 0.8573 / gold 0.8956.

THE PROXY IS UNINTERPRETABLE ON THIS ARM, and that is registered before the run rather than argued after
it. The report-holdout scores against report-derived labels, whose UNK cells ARE the constants this
treatment replaces. On 27.3% of cells the ruler and the treatment disagree by construction, so a proxy
DROP is the expected reading and is not evidence against the mechanism. Gold-58 via annotated_readings is
the only valid primary; paired half-width +/-0.015.

BRANCHES (gold delta vs control):
  >= +0.015  mechanism lives; roster it, and only then consider a slot.
  within +/-0.015  null on this ruler. Directional only, no slot, and do NOT tune the band - a band fitted
    to make the number move is the hack this project's own rules forbid.
  <= -0.015  refuted FOR THIS APPLICATION. Record what it does NOT rule out: (a) the weight-side variant,
    which reaches the same cells through --weight-floor rather than the score, and (b) restriction to the
    five findings where supervision_gap is positive (Synovitis +0.1075, Fracture +0.0715, Lateral Meniscus
    +0.0522, Baker's +0.0462), leaving MCL at -0.0692 alone.

The table is written by kneemri.evaluation.unread_teacher: values from the published out-of-fold pool,
mean-preserving and order-only inside each finding's UNK block, band half-width derived from
MEASURED_AGREEMENT (0.095 on the calibrated table).
PRICE, stated before the card is spent (knee-qxse). Cost: one 12-epoch fit, ~40 min, plus a CPU pass already done. P(clears the 1.5% house bar) = 0.12. Every measured label-lane delta in this project sits between +0.006 and +0.017, so precedent predicts sub-bar; the only thing arguing higher is that this moves 27.3% of the supervision where every prior label arm moved a value on cells the reader had already read. Armed as an INSTRUMENT: a null at +0.01 closes the label lane by exhaustion, which is worth the 40 min on its own.
RESULT 2026-09-03T18:13Z. NULL, middle pre-registered branch.

Run converged 12/12, peak e6 0.8577 (not truncated, convergence_check clean).
Gold-58 paired, both members --hold-annotations, neither trained on these cells:
  band_dense_hold_s2026 (control)  0.8956
  unread_dense_s2026               0.8976
  combined                         0.8994
  paired delta +0.0020 [-0.0155, +0.0200] INSIDE the interval, no pairwise claim.
Proxy 0.8577 peak vs control 0.8573 = +0.0004, and the proxy was pre-registered as uninterpretable.

THE LANE CLOSES BY EXHAUSTION, which is what the arm's own header said this outcome would mean. This
was the label lane's strongest possible shot: every prior label arm moved a value or a weight on cells
the reader had already read, this one replaced the constant on 27.3% of all (study, finding) pairs with
a corpus-wide out-of-fold teacher score. It moved the gold mean by 0.002.

BOTH NAMED FALLBACKS KILLED BY ARITHMETIC, not run. The header did not rule out (a) the weight-side
variant via --weight-floor and (b) restriction to the five findings with positive supervision_gap. Both
reach FEWER cells than the full application that just scored +0.0020, so both have a lower ceiling. An
80-minute arm whose ceiling is below +0.002 against a 0.015 bar is killed, not run.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. The teacher was the published pool's out-of-fold rank average. A materially
better teacher would re-open the mechanism -- but no such teacher exists in our reach, and building one
is the same problem as raising solo quality, which is the open question.

title: annotated_readings --against takes a PATH, and dies AFTER the whole read
description: --against is compared against per_member keys, which are WindowsPaths. Passing the member NAME (the spelling every other tool in this repo takes, and the spelling the flag's own help implies) raises KeyError: WindowsPath('band_dense_hold_s2026') at annotated_readings.py:171 — AFTER both encoder passes have run and every score has been computed, and before any of them is printed. On CPU that cost a 45s read; on a fourteen-member call it would cost an hour. Same class as the arm_read --arm <path> defect: an argument the tool cannot use, accepted silently, spending the work before it complains. Fix: resolve --against by stem against the checkpoint list, and validate it before the first read.

title: Control declaration is singular: cannot express an epoch-pinned, board-entry, or per-member control set
description:
Found while converting arm headers to declared controls (knee-sgzgc). Two classes of arm name their control correctly in prose but CANNOT be written as a '# control  <name> = <score>' line, and writing one anyway would be worse than silence.

EPOCH-PINNED CONTROL. mae_matched declares 'adapt_null 0.8240 @ e3 and band_dense 0.8232 @ e3, both already on the ledger, neither re-run' -- it reads a DIRECTION at the epoch its controls are already recorded at, not a final member. ArmRead.sibling matches a declared score against RunMetrics.best(), which is the run's PEAK, so a declared 0.8232 resolves to no sibling and the tool exits non-zero on an arm whose control is stated more precisely than most. Two controls in one header is the second half of the same gap: the line and the resolver are both singular.

BOARD-ENTRY CONTROL. packaged_seats and trio_seat_value both say 'THE CONTROL IS honest12, NOT THE PINNED CHAMPION' and argue for it at length -- honest12 is a twelve-member board entry at 0.937, every member fold-0 and scoreable, and trio_seat_value calls it 'the only scoreable control we own'. It is not a run, has no .metrics.jsonl, and RunComparison.resolved cannot reach it. Declaring it converts a silent arm into a hard SystemExit ('matches no single run'), which breaks --assert for a header that is doing the right thing.

So the census number is not purely a backlog: some fraction of the remaining 56 is arms the FORMAT excludes. Fix is one of: allow '@ e<N>' after the score and resolve against that epoch's row rather than best(); allow a board entry id as a control and resolve it through comp/board.jsonl; or accept both as legal-and-unresolvable so --assert counts them as declared while report() explains why it cannot draw the table. Until then do not hand-write lines for these two classes -- three arms were deliberately left silent for this reason.
notes:
2026-09-03 09:43Z: THIRD CLASS, found while sweeping the 'against `run` = score' phrasing. PER-MEMBER CONTROL SET. rampsix refits five of the champion's own-corpus seats with the curriculum ramp and nothing else; its pre-registration reads 'per-member solo: +0.004 to +0.008 over each seat's calibsix original'. So its denominator is FIVE runs, one per seat, and its second reading is an offline ensemble against the champion's own six. A single '# control  <name> = <score>' line cannot say either. Its header does contain two numbers in that shape — disagreed_ramp 0.8574 and certainty_ramp 0.8584 against disagreed_uniform 0.8507 — but those are the DOSE evidence from a different 2x2, not this arm's control, and declaring one would point arm_read at a run rampsix is not compared to. Left silent deliberately, same as mae_matched, packaged_seats and trio_seat_value.

So the format gap now has three shapes, not two: epoch-pinned, board-entry, and per-member-set. All three share one root — the line and ArmRead.sibling are both SINGULAR, and a control is not always one run at one epoch. Whatever fix lands should take a LIST, which subsumes the mae_matched two-control case as well.

WRITTEN THIS PASS instead (each verified on disk first, control name and score both taken from the arm's own prose): v3base_own_recipe -> v3base_dense = 0.8455, calibsix -> merged_blend_s2026 = 0.8587 (ledger reads 0.8589, inside the 5e-4 tolerance, still resolves).

Census note: 169 of 212 arms now carry a '# control  ' line, and 212-169=43 carry none at all — the ~49 the tool reports as undeclared is the 43 plus the handful whose line exists but lacks the '=' the parser requires (mae_matched is one). That difference is worth keeping straight: a header with a control line the regex rejects is a DIFFERENT defect from a header with no line, and only the second is an author's omission.

title: slices16_ws_s2026's weights and its predictions are different runs, and its decline quotes the wrong one
description:
Two defects found 2026-09-03 while triaging the convergence_check sweep.

(A) SEVEN of 195 metrics files under D:/models/rsna_knee_abnormality hold MORE THAN ONE training series appended into one file - the epoch number resets to 0 mid-file, because a relaunch appended instead of rotating. The recorder DOES rotate sometimes (depth_regions_span_s2026.metrics.1.jsonl, stack_increments_fx_s2026.metrics.1.jsonl, vjepa_member_s2026.metrics.{1,2}.jsonl exist), so the behaviour is inconsistent, and only the appending case is invisible.

  band_density_s2026        1ep/0.7487 then 12ep/0.8540
  dinov3_v3small_s2026     12ep/0.8080 then  3ep/0.7769
  lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026 4ep/0.7012 then 12ep/0.8217   (the knee-gnzx case)
  member_fold0              8 series, smoke
  pair_memory_s2026        12ep/0.8353 then  4ep/0.8155
  slices16_ws_s2026        12ep/0.8452 then  9ep/0.8411
  throughput_plain          2 series, throughput

RunMetrics.best() takes a max over the whole file, so it maxes ACROSS RUNS: pair_memory_s2026 reads 0.8353 where the artefact on disk is 0.8155 (+0.0198 of pure fiction). convergence_check reads the LAST row against the recipe's epoch budget, so it calls a file whose FIRST series ran 12 of 12 TRUNCATED - which is where the 2026-09-03 sweep's 13 truncated runs partly come from.

(B) THE WORSE HALF, and it is one member so far. slices16_ws_s2026.pt was written 2026-08-12 07:07; slices16_ws_s2026.holdout.npz was written 2026-08-19 12:31. 173 hours apart, and BOTH record epoch 6. The weights on disk are the first run (peak 0.8452); the holdout predictions every consumer scores that member from are the second run (peak 0.8411). MECHANISM: the checkpoint is saved ON IMPROVEMENT against a running best that the appended series never reset, so the retrain's 0.8411 never beat 0.8452 and never overwrote the .pt - while the holdout record is written UNCONDITIONALLY at the end. Conditional save beside unconditional record is the whole bug, and it is general: it would produce the same silent split for a ROSTERED member, where stacking, member_curve and every ensemble fit would pair one model's weights with another model's predictions.

BLAST RADIUS. 16 of 178 checkpoints have a >6h gap between .pt and .holdout.npz, but a large gap alone is NOT the defect - a later re-scoring pass from the same weights is legitimate and produces one. The defect is the CONJUNCTION of a large gap with a multi-series metrics file, and exactly two runs are in both sets: slices16_ws_s2026 and lora_r8_v3small_224_s2026. dinov3_v3small_s2026 has no holdout record at all.

NO VERDICT FLIPS. slices16_ws (true converged peak 0.8452 vs the 0.8411 its decline quotes) and pair_memory (0.8353 vs 0.8155) both still sit under the 0.8459 merit bar, so both declines survive - but slices16_ws misses by 0.0007 rather than by 0.0048, which is well inside the 0.0062 floor, and its decline should say so.

WHAT TO BUILD.
1. RunMetrics must SPLIT a metrics file into series at each epoch reset and never max across them. best() reads the LAST series, because that is the run that most recently wrote - and it must be able to say the file holds more than one.
2. A check asserting a run's checkpoint and its holdout record come from the SAME series. Cheapest form: refuse when a metrics file holds multiple series AND the .pt predates the .holdout.npz by more than the run's own epoch time.
3. Rewrite the slices16_ws_s2026 and pair_memory_s2026 decline lines with the corrected numbers and the reason they were wrong.
4. The recorder should rotate on relaunch always, never append - the rotated cases prove the path exists.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-09-03T09:24Z, BY ME, BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS ACTED ON. Half of what I filed above is wrong and it is wrong in the way CLAUDE.md names: I measured with my own loop instead of through the consumer, and I filed before reading the code that already owns the problem.

CLAIM (A) IS DEAD. RunMetrics.begin() has rotated epochs AND artefacts on relaunch since 2026-08-19, and rows() returns only the LAST group, so best() never maxes across runs. Read through the API the same five files give: band_density 0.8540@e6 (12 rows), dinov3_v3small 0.7769@e2 (3), lora_r8_v3small_224 0.8217@e8 (12), pair_memory 0.8155@e3 (4), slices16_ws 0.8411@e6 (9). Every one is a single series. The 'pure fiction +0.0198' I claimed for pair_memory does not exist - 0.8155 is exactly what the tool reports, and run_metrics.py:250-269 says so by name, with that number, in prose written before I got here. The seven multi-series files are LEGACY, from before rotation landed; no new one can form.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is one member. slices16_ws_s2026 holds a FINISHED 12-epoch run peaking 0.8452 and a KILLED 9-epoch rerun peaking 0.8411. Its .metrics rows and its .holdout.npz are both the KILLED run's (npz written 08-19 12:31, epoch 6, source trained) - self-consistent with each other. Its .pt is the FINISHED run's (08-12 07:07), because save-on-improvement never fired for a rerun that peaked lower. So predictions and weights are different models, and the tree carries two contradictory accounts of the member: comp/members.declines quotes 0.8411, while run_metrics.py:156-161 states that reading is WRONG and the member scores 0.8452. Both cannot be the number.

WHICH IS RIGHT DEPENDS ON THE CONSUMER, which is why it needs writing down rather than fixing: anything scoring the member from its STORED predictions gets 0.8411 and is self-consistent; anything re-running inference from the .pt gets 0.8452. A kit ships the .pt.

IT CHANGES NO VERDICT EITHER WAY - 0.8452 still misses the 0.8459 merit bar - but by 0.0007 rather than the 0.0048 the decline implies, which is inside the 0.0062 floor, and the decline should say that instead of the flat 'below the merit level' boilerplate. dinov3_v3small_s2026 is the same shape (finished 12ep/0.8080 under a killed 3ep/0.7769, no holdout npz at all) and also below bar.

title: Q-CG: ROI-crop gain against strong pretrained trunks in knee MRI
description: Claude asks whether the ROI/localization gain reported in knee-MRI literature is an information effect (crop raises tear's share of input for any classifier) or a model-capacity compensation effect (small CNNs need the crop; large pretrained transformers/ViTs do not). Need evidence: (1) ROI ablations with DINOv2/v3, SAM-derived, MRI-CORE, OrthoFoundation, or other foundation-model backbones; (2) whether ROI gain shrinks as backbone capacity/pretraining grows; (3) Astuto et al. discussion of why meniscus classification works despite low segmentation IoU; (4) where crop enters (input pixels vs ROI-pooled features); (5) SKM-TEA licence terms if a segmenter trained on SKM-TEA is used only to generate crop windows for classifier weights that would be re-hosted as Kaggle datasets. Cite clauses and licenses.

title: ROI crop family: gate it on the four crop members' focal columns before any segmenter build (SKM-TEA closed for shipping)
description:
THE ONLY OPEN LEVER THIS PROJECT HAS NEVER RUN THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY DELIVER 1.5%: an anatomy-aware ROI
member for the focal findings, with the ROIs supplied by a segmenter trained on SKM-TEA.

WHY IT IS NOT A REPEAT. Every crop arm here is a FIXED-GEOMETRY CENTRE CROP: crop80_tissue, crop80_span,
crop160_span, centre_tissue. The ledger closed that family and closed it correctly -- "at the control's
extent, centring alone is a null", and crop80_tissue's per-label pattern was attributable to the resolution
change it also carried. An ANATOMY-AWARE crop is a different mechanism: the window follows the structure
rather than the image, so it is not the arm that was refuted. Nothing in this repo has ever done it, and
the four crop arms are the reason it LOOKS done.

THE LITERATURE (Kimi, Q-CF, 2026-09-03T07:10Z, full write-up in research/):
  Astuto et al.  V-Net segments 11 knee ROIs (cartilage compartments, meniscus horns, ACL), each cropped
                 and fed to a dedicated 3D CNN.  meniscus 0.93, cartilage 0.93 -- and the meniscus
                 DETECTION IoU is tiny, so the gain does not need a good segmenter, only a roughly right
                 window.
  Gungor et al.  YOLOv8 -> EfficientNetV2 on 480x480 crops with weighted CE.  meniscus 0.97-0.98.
  Sun et al.     KneeXNet: 2D CNN meniscus 0.889 -> graph-CNN over slice-to-slice spatial dependency
                 0.968.  +0.079, LARGER than the same model's ACL gain.
  Nebelung       effusion 0.91, Baker's 0.93, MCL tear 0.95 against meniscus 0.88 -- the trade in the
                 direction our pool shows.  Astuto reads meniscus 0.93 against BME 0.83 -- the OPPOSITE
                 direction.  So the trade is real and NOT invariant; anatomy-awareness is what flips it.

WHY IT POINTS AT OUR WEAK COLUMNS SPECIFICALLY. The competence axis's negative loading is Baker's -0.400,
Medial Meniscus -0.340, MCL -0.297, Lateral Meniscus -0.145. Those are exactly the structures Astuto and
Gungor crop to. The positive end -- Effusion +0.539, Synovitis +0.534 -- is large and bright and needs no
window. The mechanism and the measured weakness name the same four labels.

THE ROI SOURCE, AND IT IS ALREADY OURS. SKM-TEA is knee MRI WITH SEGMENTATION LABELS (cartilage, meniscus)
and this project already holds a valid Azure SAS credential for it (D:/life/creds/machine/skmtea_url.txt,
fetch_skmtea.sh reads it, never embeds it). So the segmenter has a training corpus that needs no new
agreement and no new download negotiation. That is the piece that usually kills this idea and here it is
already paid for.

THE PRICE, stated before running anything. Multi-day, and the biggest single commitment on the board:
  - SKM-TEA fetch and decode                                  hours, no card
  - train a small segmenter on its meniscus/cartilage labels  a few hours of card
  - infer masks over 4407 RSNA studies, cache the ROI windows  hours of card
  - train ONE focal member on the ROI stack                    ~3.5 h of card, the arm itself
Against: the four focal labels are 4 of 12. If ROI cropping buys them what Astuto buys over a whole-image
baseline, even +0.05 on each of four columns is +0.017 on the mean, which CLEARS THE 1.5% BAR. If it buys
+0.02 each it is +0.0067 and does not. So this is priced as the one experiment on the board whose
mechanism could plausibly reach the bar, and it should be judged on the FOCAL COLUMNS, not the mean --
pre-register the four columns before it runs.

THE RISK THAT DECIDES IT, and it is asked of Kimi as Q-CG. Every ROI result above uses a SMALL CNN trained
from scratch or an EfficientNet. Cropping compensates for weak features: it hands a small model the
localisation it cannot learn. Our members are DINOv2/DINOv3-large with attention pooling over slices, which
may already attend to the structure. If the ROI gain is a small-model compensation, it does not transfer to
us and the whole build is wasted. No result in the letter separates those two explanations. That question
is the gate, and it should be answered before the SKM-TEA fetch, not after.

SEQUENCING. Do NOT start the build on Kimi's letter alone. Gate on Q-CG. If the answer is "the ROI gain is
measured against strong pretrained trunks too", this becomes the top of the queue and everything else waits.
If it is "only ever against small CNNs", the cheap version is a single arm that crops to a FIXED window
around the four structures' population-mean location -- which is close to what crop160_span already did and
would be expected to be null, so in that branch the lever closes without the SKM-TEA spend.
notes:
THE SKM-TEA ROUTE IS CLOSED FOR SHIPPING, AND THE LITERATURE CANNOT SETTLE THE GATE. Kimi, Q-CG,
2026-09-03T07:27Z, thirteen minutes after this bead was filed. Recording it against the bead rather than
letting the P1 stand on an argument that no longer holds.

1. THE ROI SOURCE IS GONE FOR ANYTHING THAT SHIPS. SKM-TEA is under a Stanford AIMI Research Use
Agreement: non-commercial research and education only, and it "prohibits distribution outside the existing
process." A Kaggle code submission runs OFFLINE, so a segmenter that makes crop windows on TEST studies has
to be re-hosted by us as a Kaggle dataset. That is redistribution of a derived artefact, and it is the same
shape as the fastMRI DSA 5(c) problem that closed fastMRI for shipping (knee-nxthh). Internal instrument
use is probably fine; a shipped member is not. The piece I priced as "already paid for" was the piece that
does not survive contact with the licence, which is the second time this project has made that exact error
in one week.

2. THE LITERATURE CANNOT ANSWER THE GATE QUESTION. There is NO published knee-MRI ablation comparing
whole-image against ROI-cropped input for DINOv2/v3, SAM-derived, MRI-CORE, OrthoFoundation-L or any
comparable large pretrained transformer. Every ROI gain in Q-CF is measured on a ResNet, an EfficientNet or
a 3D CNN. So the information-versus-compensation question is not settled anywhere, and the gate I set
cannot be cleared by reading.

3. MY EVIDENCE FOR THE INFORMATION EXPLANATION DID NOT HOLD. I read Astuto's tiny meniscus IoU with a good
AUC as showing the window only has to be roughly right. The authors explain the low IoU differently: "the
bounding box for the meniscus is much smaller than that for other ROIs" -- an artefact of the metric on a
small box, not evidence that a coarse crop suffices.

4. AND WE MAY ALREADY OWN THE ANSWER, FOR FREE. `crop80_tissue` is 80 mm about the TISSUE CENTRE -- a crude
anatomy prior, on a strong DINOv2 trunk. It sits at +0.008 on the competence axis and `crop80_tissue_full`
at +0.007: the REGIONAL side. `crop80_span` sits at -0.008 and `crop160_span` at -0.007, all four inside
0.016 of each other and none of them displaced toward the focal end. A crop on a strong trunk did not buy
focal findings in this repo's own data. That is the compensation explanation appearing in our measurements
rather than in a citation, and it is the cheapest evidence available on this question.

WHAT THIS BEAD BECOMES. Not a multi-day SKM-TEA build. Two things, in order:

  (a) READ THE FOUR CROP MEMBERS' FOCAL COLUMNS against their own controls, per-label, on the four labels
      the axis names (Baker's, Medial Meniscus, MCL, Lateral Meniscus). No card, no slot, arithmetic over
      cached holdout records. The ledger already warned that for `crop80_tissue` "mean is the WRONG read --
      gate is per-label", and that per-label gate was never actually run. If the focal columns are flat or
      negative, the ROI family closes on our own data without a segmenter, and the axis positions above
      become the confirmation rather than the evidence.
  (b) ONLY IF (a) shows focal gain: the surviving ROI source is MRI-CORE or MedSAM, both Apache 2.0 and
      therefore re-hostable, prompted rather than SKM-TEA-trained. That is a different and larger build and
      it is not justified before (a).

DEMOTE from P1. The 1.5%-reaching claim rested on Astuto's and Gungor's numbers transferring to a large
pretrained trunk, and there is no evidence that they do, one piece of our own evidence that they do not,
and no licensed path to ship the version I costed.

A SEPARATE MECHANISM WORTH KEEPING, from the same letter. Yiu et al. find ResNet50 beats ViT on MRNet
sagittal meniscus, 0.8184 against 0.74, and conclude transformers underfit without larger or domain-matched
pretraining. Every member this project owns is a ViT, and the axis's negative loading is exactly meniscus,
MCL and Baker's. That is a candidate mechanism for our focal weakness that is NOT about cropping at all,
and it predicts a CONVOLUTIONAL trunk should sit off-axis toward the focal end. We have convnext members:
cnx_dense +0.102, cnx_own_recipe +0.046, cnx_top_rate +0.051, cnx_mid_rate +0.089 -- all on the REGIONAL
side, which contradicts it, but all of them are also badly under-adapted (cnx_dense scored 0.7927), and the
positive end is where under-adapted trunks land regardless of architecture. So the prediction is untested
here, not refuted: it needs a convolutional trunk that actually converged. `cnx_rate_ladder`, running next
on the card, is the arm that produces one.
THE GATE THIS BEAD SET HAS NOW BEEN RUN, 2026-09-03T07:54Z. No card, no slot -- it is arithmetic over
holdout records that were already on disk, which is what the previous note said it would be. Four crop
members, read PER LABEL against their OWN declared controls with `arm_read`, focal/regional split as the
tool computes it:

  crop80_tissue       vs wholestack_s2026 0.8457   focal -0.0110  regional -0.0115   Baker's -0.0270
  crop80_tissue_full  vs crop80_tissue_s2026       focal -0.0016  regional +0.0018   nil either way
  crop80_span         vs band_span_s2026 0.8565    focal -0.0095  regional -0.0104   MCL -0.0265*,
                                                   ACL -0.0263*, Contusion -0.0198*, Baker's -0.0164*
  crop160_span        vs band_span_s2026 0.8565    focal +0.0016  regional -0.0024   Synovitis +0.0253*

  (* = the delta exceeds that label's own 95% sampling interval.)

THE READING. Tightening the physical window from 130 mm to 80 mm does not buy focal structures on this
trunk. It LOSES them, and on `crop80_span` it loses them significantly on MCL and Baker's -- which are two
of the four labels the competence axis names as our focal weakness and exactly the structures Astuto and
Gungor crop to. The single positive focal number in the table belongs to `crop160_span`, the arm that
WIDENED the window to 160 mm at 420 px: focal +0.0016 against regional -0.0024, the only row the tool
marks as a trade. So within this repo the crop axis runs the opposite way to the ROI literature: more
context helps the focal findings slightly, less context hurts them.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SETTLE. It settles the CHEAP version of the ROI idea -- the fixed-geometry,
tissue-centred crop -- and it settles it on four members rather than one. It does NOT refute an
anatomy-aware crop whose window follows the structure, because none of these four does that; that
mechanism is still formally untested here. But it removes the branch Q-CG left open as the affordable one
("a fixed window around the four structures' population-mean location"), because that is what
`crop80_tissue` and `crop80_span` already are, and it raises the prior on the COMPENSATION explanation:
cropping supplies localisation that a small CNN cannot learn and that a ViT-L/14 with slice attention
apparently already has, so removing context is a net loss for it. That is now our own measurement rather
than an inference from someone else's ablation, and it is the third independent thing pointing the same
way (the licence closing SKM-TEA, the absence of any ROI ablation on a strong trunk, and this table).

STATUS. The bead stays open at P2 but its remaining question is no longer "should we build a segmenter".
It is the narrower one: is there any mechanism by which a STRUCTURE-FOLLOWING window beats a
CONTEXT-PRESERVING one, given that on our data more context is worth more than less? Nothing on the board
answers that, and no card should be spent on it before something does. The Apache-2.0 route (MRI-CORE,
MedSAM) is still the only licensed one if it is ever re-opened.

A TOOL DEFECT FOUND WHILE RUNNING THE GATE, and it is why this read had never been done. `arm_read`
resolved run names against the PROCESSED root, and every `.metrics.jsonl` this project has ever written
lives under the MODELS root -- so every invocation failed with `control <name>.metrics.jsonl does not
exist`, which reads as a missing RUN rather than as a wrong ROOT. `run_comparison`, one layer down, passes
`root.models()` and always did. Fixed. Separately, `arm_read --assert` reports 110 of 213 arms declare no
`# control <name> = <score>` line at all, so half this project's arms cannot be read per-label even now;
three of the four crop arms were in that list and had to be given their control lines before this table
could exist. Both of those are filed separately.

title: holdout_record.read dies on a probe record with no epoch, killing every glob-the-root consumer
description:
`holdout_record.read` raises KeyError('epoch is not a file in the archive') on a record written by
`feature_probe`, and that one record kills the whole pool for every consumer that globs the processed root.

Found 2026-09-03T06:53Z running competence_axis over `*.holdout.npz`. Three of 207 records carry only
['predictions', 'studies', 'truth'] and no 'epoch':

  ortholarge@focal-attend_mean_probe.holdout.npz
  radnet121@focal-max_mean_probe.holdout.npz
  v3large@focal-attend_mean_probe.holdout.npz

They are not corrupt. A FROZEN PROBE HAS NO EPOCHS, so there is nothing for the field to hold — the
record is honest and the reader assumes every holdout record came from a trainer.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THREE FILES. `--largest-pool` exists precisely so a glob of the processed root is
runnable: it keeps the largest set that shares a split and a label table instead of refusing on the first
record that cannot be MIXED. But the read happens before the narrowing, so a record that cannot be READ
still takes the whole run down, and the flag's promise does not hold. The workaround is to know which
three files to exclude by name, which is the opposite of what the flag is for.

TWO WAYS TO FIX, and they are not equivalent:
  (a) make `epoch` optional on the record — absence is the right answer for a probe, and this module's
      neighbours already treat absence as a value rather than a hole.
  (b) have the narrowing catch an unreadable record and drop it with a counted reason, the way it already
      drops a foreign record ("someone else's weights through someone else's decode") and an unmixable one.

Both, probably: (a) because the probe records are legitimate and should be readable, and (b) because the
next unreadable record will be a different shape and a glob-the-root tool should survive it.

Worked around by hand for the competence_axis run (`grep -v '_probe.holdout'`), which is a fact about my
shell history and not about the repo.

Labels improvement: what the tables say versus what the reports say
description: Every member is fitted against a labels table derived from free-text reports, and there are 23 tables in the labels directory with 10 of them named by at least one arm. The finding columns carry value, __conf and __verdict, so label confidence is already a recorded axis and is used unevenly. Open questions worth a card or a CPU pass: which columns have the worst reader agreement and are therefore capped below the noise floor no matter what the model does; whether the confidence weights actually change a fitted member or are being multiplied into nothing; whether a re-read of the reports with a stronger extractor moves any column. Score argument: a column whose labels are 80 percent right has a ceiling below the frontier and no trunk change can reach past it, so measuring the ceiling per column tells us which columns are worth a model at all.

title: Other objectives: auxiliary heads on labels the score does not read
description: Mean AUC is rank-based and prevalence-invariant, so class balancing and reweighting move the loss and not the score - that lane is closed by the metric itself. Auxiliary heads are the lane that is open. Severity, sublabel, laterality, box area, plane and corpus of origin are all labels we hold or can derive, none of them scored, and each adds gradient signal on the shared trunk without changing the scored objective. Mechanism for gain: finer supervision per study makes a better representation for the 12 heads that are read. This is the general form of the aux-head design already priced under knee-n4ubq. Constraint from CLAUDE.md: keep the objective general, never fit the loss to a specific weakness. Blocked in part by the metadata frame - plane and corpus are not in the merged table any arm reads (knee-g39xh).

title: Grouped experts: one model per finding family, not per column
description: The cheaper half of the separate-experts idea. Instead of 12 experts, group the columns by what an image has to show for them: ligaments (ACL, MCL), menisci (Medial Meniscus, Lateral Meniscus), osteoarthritis (Medial OA, Lateral OA, PF OA), fluid (Effusion, Synovitis, Bakers), bone (Contusion, Fracture). Five models, not twelve, and each group shares an acquisition preference and a spatial scale, which is the reason to expect the compromise inside a shared trunk to be smaller within a group than across groups. Prices at 5x the card rather than 12x and the ensemble already knows how to combine members, so a group expert can enter the pool as an ordinary seat. Test cheaply: ONE group - fluid or ligaments - against the shared trunk on those columns only.

title: Separate experts: one model per finding column
description: Score is the mean AUC over 12 finding columns and every member so far is a single trunk with 12 heads, so one representation is asked to rank ACL tears, patellofemoral OA and Baker cysts at once. A separate expert per column trains each on its own positive set and its own hard negatives. Mechanism for gain: the columns disagree about what matters in an image - ligament tears are focal and sagittal, OA is textural and coronal, effusion is fluid-signal - and a shared trunk has to compromise. Cost is 12x the card, which is why the first test is NOT twelve models: take the two columns the pool is weakest on, train one expert each, and price the swap against the same seat in the champion. Open question the test must answer: does an expert beat the shared trunk ON ITS OWN COLUMN by more than the 0.0062 report floor. Related: grouped experts is the cheaper version of the same mechanism.

Trunk shelf from Q-CC: MRI-CORE and RadioDINO are redistributable and unregistered
description:
Kimi Q-CC (2026-09-03T05:12Z) surveyed publicly downloadable MRI-pretrained trunks with licences quoted. Two clear the redistribution test and are not in backbone.py.

MRI-CORE, mazurowski-lab/mri_foundation, MRI_CORE_vitb.pth, Apache 2.0, SAM ViT-B encoder, 110k MRI volumes across 18 body locations. Most architecture-distinct redistributable trunk on the shelf: SAM ViT rather than a DINO ViT. Needs an adapter and a read head, so it is not drop-in.

RadioDINO, HF hub Snarcy/RadioDino-b16 and -s16, CC-BY 4.0, ViT-S/16 and ViT-B/16 trained with DINO/DINOv2 on 1.35M RadImageNet images. Drop-in through the existing HF path. Weights fetched to D:/models/hf/ on 2026-09-03.

Note the distinction from radnet_family, which died at 0.6716: that was RadImageNet SUPERVISED DenseNet. RadioDINO is SSL on the same corpus, a different cell of the trunk 2x2, so it is not a repeat of a known result.

Ranked BELOW ortholarge, which is the knee-specific DINOv3-L continuation already on the card as ortho_pool_read and confirmed MIT by this survey. Do not arm either of these while that read is outstanding.

Also on the survey: MedSAM Apache 2.0 (segmentation, internal-only), and a watchlist of OmniMRI (weights unreleased), MedImageInsight (Azure catalog terms unclear), MedDINOv3 (CT-only).
notes:
RadioDINO-b16 REGISTERED in backbone.py 2026-09-03T05:23Z, ungated (card busy, cannot run uvx nox under a live arm). Constants RADIODINO_BASE=radiodinob16 and family RADIODINO=radiodino; entry is Snarcy/RadioDino-b16, width 768, patch 16, IMAGENET normalization, leaf radiodino-b16, params_m 86.6, no mount yet. Verified by constructing ENCODERS, which now holds 15.

The argument that earned it a card, recorded in the entry header: it isolates the PRETRAINING CORPUS with architecture and objective held. ViT-B/16, twelve blocks, 768 wide, DINO objective, same as v3base and vitin21k's twin, differing only in 1.35M RadImageNet images against LVD-1689M natural ones. No previous family change here moved one variable, which is why knee-m69u cannot be answered from the arms on disk.

It is also not a repeat of radnet_family. That arm closed the medical-SUPERVISED cell at 0.6716; these weights are self-supervised on the SAME corpus, a different cell. The pair separates 'RadImageNet is the wrong corpus' from '165-way supervision is the wrong objective', which the DenseNet result alone cannot say.

Priced as an INSTRUMENT, not a seat bid: knee-y59c measured distance-from-DINOv2 anti-correlating with solo strength, and a twin that is near on architecture and far on corpus tests which of those two distances that curve was measuring. No published knee number exists for these weights.

MRI-CORE remains unregistered and is a BUILD per Q-CD.
PRIOR ART PREDICTS THIS ARM LOSES (Kimi Q-CF, 2026-09-03T07:10Z). Frees et al. measured an ImageNet-initialised ResNet50 beating RadImageNet significantly on ACL (best AUC 0.9969). That is a direct prediction about this arm's corpus swap, from the medical-pretraining direction. It does not disarm the instrument -- the arm exists to say WHICH of architecture, objective and corpus carried radnet_family's 0.6716, and a predicted null on a pre-registered axis is still the answer to that question. It does mean the arm must NOT be sold as a seat bid, which its header already says, and that a loss here is a CONFIRMATION rather than a surprise. Record the prediction before the score lands.

title: Q-CC trunk shelf survey — musculoskeletal/knee MRI and general MRI vision trunks Claude asks for enumerated, downloadable, redistributable vision trunks pretrained/continued on knee/musculoskeletal MRI and general MRI. For each: name, download URL, licence (with redistribution clause), architecture+params, pretraining corpus, published knee MRI number. Rank by trunk-distinctness / lever size.
ortho_fresh_lowlr never trained: it timed out waiting for VRAM, and was filed as a failed arm
description:
Re-diagnosed 2026-09-03T04:16Z from its own log, which is 55 lines and contains NO epoch line at all. It ends:

  waiting for VRAM: 30.3 GB free, this run wants 31.9 - 1530 s of 1800
  ARM FAILED ortho_fresh_lowlr (trainer exit 127)

It asked for 31.9 GB on a 32607 MiB card, waited the full 1800 s wait for VRAM that was never going to arrive, and gave up having trained zero epochs. It is therefore evidence about NOTHING -- not about the ortholarge trunk, not about a low backbone rate, not about fine-tuning. It has been carried as a candidate silent-kill and as a possible method failure; it is neither.

WHY IT READ AS ONE. lib.sh's failure marker printed only 'trainer exit 127', and the environment note at the top of that file teaches exit 127 as the signature of a gates-rewritten venv. Both readings are wrong here and the correct one was the last line of the same file. Fixed in the same session: the marker now quotes the exception line, or the last non-marker line when there is no exception, which is exactly this case.

THE FIX FOR THE ARM ITSELF IS ALREADY VALIDATED. The over-reservation is the same one ortho_pool_read hit at --batch 12 (67549 MiB). Holding the EFFECTIVE batch with --batch 4 --accumulate 3 cut the reservation to 25737 MiB, which fits, and that configuration is on the card now. Re-arm ortho_fresh_lowlr the same way; no other variable moves, so its original pre-registration stands unchanged.

PRIORITISE AFTER ortho_pool_read reports. If the pool read transfers, the low-rate question is worth a card; if it does not, re-price this against the bands that arm selects.

PRICE: written before the arm runs (2026-09-03T07:40Z). The arm this bead now points at is
`ortho_slow_trunk` -- ortho_pool_read's recipe at 336 px with --backbone-lr 1e-5 instead of 4e-5, one
variable off a measured point. Its 224 px form is superseded: a null at 224 could not have separated the
rate from the resolution, because ortho_lpft already read 0.7537 at 224.

COST (wall-clock): ~3.5 h of card (12 epochs x ~1050 s), which is the whole of one arm slot on a single-card machine.

GAIN, bounded by the probe's own lead: frozen, `feature_probe --choose-penalty` read ortholarge at 0.8249
against dinov2-large 0.8048 and v3large 0.8046, so +0.0203. Fine-tuned at 4e-5 the same trunk peaked at
0.8464 against depth_regions_narrow_s2026 = 0.8554. Recovering ALL of the probe's lead reaches ~0.8664 and
clears the DINOv2 recipe; recovering half reaches ~0.856 and merely ties it. So the ceiling on this arm is
about +0.020 on ONE member, which is not 1.5% on the ensemble and is not sold as one.

P(clears the 1.5% bar) ~ 0.02. P(moves the member >= +0.009, i.e. back to the control) ~ 0.25. The counter-
evidence is strong and stated in the arm header: the encoder_adapt family runs at low rates and is among
the weakest work this project owns, and the competence-axis measurement says the encoder rate moves a
member 0.035 while resolution moves it 0.005 -- rate is the strongest single knob, and LOW is the weak end.

SO IT IS BOUGHT AS AN INSTRUMENT, not as an improvement, and that is the honest way to price it. What it
buys is the CLOSURE of the ortho trunk plus a verdict on `feature_probe` itself. If the probe-to-fine-tune
inversion reproduces at two rates an order of magnitude apart, then feature_probe -- the tool this project
has been using to RANK candidate trunks before spending a card on them -- is demoted to a floor that does
not predict fine-tuned order. That finding is worth more than the member, because it is upstream of every
future trunk decision, and it must be written into the probe's own docs rather than only this arm's row.
notes: READ 2026-09-05: ortho_slow_trunk = 0.8265, best epoch 11 of 12 (the LAST). convergence_check clean (1 converged). Pre-registered bottom branch (< 0.8402) = null on the RATE hypothesis only; the ortho trunk does not close by this arm. The curve is monotone to the end, so the budget bound the run - UNDERTRAINED, a faulty-TRAINING reading rather than a fact about the trunk. Slope over the last three epochs is +0.0007, so eight more epochs at 924 s (2.1 h) prices near zero and is NOT queued. Ledger section written.

title: Ordering.auc breaks ties by argsort order, which is wrong whenever the SCORE column is a label table
description:
protocol_prior.py:87 Ordering.auc ranks with Ordering.ranks, whose docstring justifies arbitrary tie-breaking: 'the members predictions are continuous floats, so exact ties are vanishing and a tie-aware rank would buy nothing for the cost of a second sort.' That is TRUE of a member and FALSE whenever the thing being ranked is a discrete column - a label table, a reader level, a vote count, a rank average over few members.

MEASURED 2026-09-03 on the annotated 58: report_labels_v2 takes SIX distinct values over 58 rows (four on Synovitis), and Ordering.auc reads it at 0.8690 against a tie-averaged 0.8658 - +0.0032 high, half the 0.0062 noise floor, and the sign depends on argsort order rather than on anything real. v3 reads +0.0014 high. On holdannot's continuous member predictions over the 909 the two agree to 0.000000, so the assumption holds exactly where the docstring claims it.

NOT a defect in any member number. Every holdout AUC in the ledger ranks continuous predictions and is unaffected. The exposure is anywhere a discrete column is passed as the SCORE argument - protocol_prior's own blending path mixes Ordering.ranks of one column into another, and foreign_gate/foreign_ruler rank foreign columns whose granularity is not checked.

FIX: make Ordering.auc tie-aware (average ranks over tied groups), which costs one extra sort and changes no continuous-column number by construction. Cheaper alternative if the sort cost matters: assert the score column has more than some fraction of distinct values and refuse otherwise, so the wrong use fails loudly instead of reading half a floor high.

title: a decline written em-dash style is silently swallowed as continuation prose
description: MemberDeclines.reasons() treats any line with no '#' and a space in it as a wrapped continuation of the previous entry. That discriminator is right for prose but it also eats a HEADER written in the file's other house style: 'ramp_dense_gate — 0.8578 at its peak epoch 7, against ...' registered as more text under ortho_lpft_head, so the member read as undocumented while a full, well-argued decline sat in the file. It did not fire as a finding only because no checkpoint on disk carries that exact stem. Found 2026-09-03 while filing the mrnet decline, which hit the same hole and DID fire. Both entries reformatted to 'name.pt  # reason'. Fix: accept a header whose FIRST token is a bare member name followed by a separator (' - ', ' — ', ':'), not only '#'.

title: seat_value drops a candidate given by BARE NAME and blames the run for it
description: `--candidates mrnet_warm_s2026` (no .pt) built a path that does not exist, so RecordMix hit its `not path.exists()` branch and logged 'a holdout record with no checkpoint — the run never reached its end, dropped'. The run had reached its end; the checkpoint is on disk; only the suffix was missing. The report then said 'no candidate carries a holdout record, so no seat can be priced' and printed a full, healthy-looking distance table with zero candidate rows. Passing the full path priced it fine. Two defects: the name->path resolution does not append .pt, and the drop message asserts a CAUSE it did not check. Fix: resolve a bare name to <models>/<name>.pt, and word the drop as 'checkpoint not found at <path>'.

title: queue_check counts DEAD watcher logs in its DOUBLE-QUEUED test and live ones everywhere else
description: On 2026-09-03 queue_check reported 'DOUBLE-QUEUED: experiments/arms/ortho_pool_read.sh' with only one live chain owing it. The second match was after_mrnet_rerun.log, whose first line reads "waiting for 'pid:66204' in logs/ortho_pool_read.log before running: experiments/arms/mrnet_warm.sh" - the arm name appears in the WATCH-FILE path, not in the owed-arm list. The check should parse the 'before running:' tail only. Consequence is the expensive direction: a false DOUBLE-QUEUED invites killing a chain that is the only one owing an arm, which strands it silently - the exact failure queue_check was built to block.
notes: CORRECTION 2026-09-03T01:52Z, my first diagnosis was wrong. I blamed after_mrnet_rerun.log, whose wait line names logs/ortho_pool_read.log in the watch-FILE path. Refuted by retiring the dead watcher logs: after_mrnet_rerun.log is STILL live and still names that path, both chains are still live, and queue_check now reads 'OK: every arm still owed is gated by exactly one live process'. So the second count came from after_ortho_pool_read.log - a DEAD watcher whose arm had already run. The defect is that the double-queue test scans logs the liveness pass has already excluded, which means the warning grows with the number of retired logs in logs/ rather than with anything true about the queue. It fired here at 43 stale logs. The expensive direction is unchanged: a false DOUBLE-QUEUED invites killing a chain that is the only one owing an arm.

Roster members whose image cache is gone cannot enter any offline pool, and nothing says so
description:
member_curve over the 101 roster members that have both a .pt and a .holdout.npz dies with FileNotFoundError on images_224px_12sl_adjacent.npy (adjacent224_s2026) and, after excluding that one, on images_336px_20sl_140mm_0.1-0.9band.npy. The second key is not named in ANY member's metrics.jsonl (grepped all 119 roster names for '140mm'), so the member that wants it cannot be identified from the ledger - the key is derived from recipe fields by core/data/corpus/study_cache.py:184, not recorded.

Consequence: a member can be on comp/members.roster, have a holdout npz, pass roster_check, and still be unable to participate in any offline pool computation - and the failure is a crash of the WHOLE run, not a skip of the one member. Any pool search over the roster is therefore blocked by the weakest member's missing cache.

Two things wanted:
1. member_curve should SKIP a member whose reading cache is absent, naming it, rather than aborting the run.
2. roster_check (or a new check) should assert every rostered member's cache key resolves to a file on disk, so the hole is found when the roster is edited rather than when a pool is searched.

Found 2026-09-02T23:09Z while pricing whether a 101-member greedy curve could beat the champion's pool. Not urgent for score - the seating axis is board-flat across seven entries - but it silently caps every offline pool study this project can run.

title: Pathology-specific knee MRI SOTA search is empty: no public weights, general models remain the only bet
description: Surveyed 2025-2026 literature per RSNA pathology. ACL: Xue et al. 2024 AUC 0.99 but private data/no weights. Meniscus: 3D mask-RCNN and YOLO segmentations, no public weights. OA/cartilage: radiograph KL-grading and OAI MRI segmentation, no public weights and no clean RSNA mapping. Synovitis/Baker's: no public models. No pathology-specific foundation model with public weights exists. The only actionable multi-pathology public models remain MRNet, Rijeka, fastMRI+, OrthoDiffusion and OrthoFoundation-L (declined). title: Test inference-time slot expectation to close train/test gap
description: Slot dropout in kneemri/training/augmentation.py:204-234 withholds present slots during training, but inference always sees all acquired slots. The head masks absent slots, yet the model was never trained on the inference absence distribution (~55-60% fill). Add an inference-time expectation: run multiple slot-dropout masks and average logits, or measure deterministic weakest-slot-drop.
