The cheap route is TWO PASSES with an intermediate scheme name: ours+Rijeka under a scheme, then that+MRNet under 'merged'. Two things make that non-trivial rather than a shell loop:

  * the intermediate cache is a full copy of the 71.6 GB base plus Rijeka, so the disk cost is paid twice and the intermediate has to be deletable without touching the base;
  * _disjoint's guarantee has to hold across all three identifier spaces, not pairwise. Ours are RSNA study ids, Rijeka's carry their own prefix, MRNet's carry 'mrnet-'. Pairwise checks do cover it here BY CONSTRUCTION of the prefixes, but nothing asserts the three-way case.

The alternative is to make build() take a LIST of foreign caches and write once. That costs one pass of disk instead of two and removes the intermediate scheme entirely. Prefer it unless the labels-column union turns out to be pairwise in a way that resists.

Do not start this before the merged_corpus arm reads. If a two-corpus merge does not beat lr4e-5_ws = 0.8525, a three-way merge is a bigger version of a mechanism that did not pay.

title: V-JEPA2 normalization constants are UNVERIFIED — check before arming any vjepa arm
description:
Every registry encoder now declares the mean/std it was pretrained under (Encoder.normalization, kneemri/models/backbone.py), and seven of eight were verified against the checkpoint's own preprocessor_config.json: DINOv2 small/base/large, DINOv3 vits16/vits16plus/vitb16 and ConvNeXtV2-base all declare the ImageNet pair; RAD-DINO declares 0.5307/0.2583 and was the defect knee-8wm6 fixed.

VJEPA2_LARGE could NOT be checked. facebook/vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256 is gated — the HF raw URL serves HTML, not JSON — and there is no local snapshot under D:/data or the HF hub cache. Its entry therefore keeps the IMAGENET default by inheritance, which is a GUESS, and tests/unit/kneemri/models/backbone.py marks it as such in test_every_encoder_declares_the_constants_it_was_pretrained_under.

Video trunks frequently ship their own constants, and vjepa_member (0.8343) is already in the ledger as a trunk that landed below its DINOv3 control — the same shape of reading RAD-DINO's arm turned out to carry. Resolve with the HF token at the machine creds path before any vjepa arm is armed or its solo number is quoted as evidence about video pretraining.

title: MEASURED_AGREEMENT pools one constant per level over twelve findings whose own rates run 0.000-0.778
description:
RECAST 2026-08-25 after reading the ledger, which had already spent this mechanism. The original framing (teach boundary effusions at 0.5) is NOT new: calibrated_targets / calib_span is exactly that lever, and calib_span measured -0.0020 against band_span on the shipped recipe. Do not re-run it as written.

WHAT IS NEW IS THAT OUR BOUNDARY MEASUREMENT EXPLAINS calib_span'S HEADLINE ANOMALY.

The ledger's calib_span row is emphatic that the arm INVERTED rather than missed: it predicted the gain would concentrate on the labels most skewed toward the 0.68 level, named MCL (495/219/53) and Effusion (1599/910/157), and Effusion came back -0.0212* — the worst row on the board — while PF OA, predicted to have nothing to gain, gained most at +0.0170*. The recorded mechanism sentence is 'the remap is not adding truth at this operating point, it is moving mass off the low-grade positives it was built to help.' It says WHAT happened, not WHY that label.

MEASURED_AGREEMENT remaps a 0.68 cell (a mild/low-grade YES) to 0.378 — across 0.5, inverting its sign, on 6,461 mild cells. That 0.378 is a CORPUS-WIDE rate over all twelve findings.

severity_boundary now measures Effusion's own rate at that boundary directly from the 58: a report whose effusion sentence carries a small-size qualifier is annotated positive 6 of 12, and one that mentions effusion with no size word 6 of 7. Effusion's own low-grade agreement is ~0.5, not 0.378 — and the free control says the tool is reading correctly, since denied effusions are 0 of 5 and moderate-or-larger 2 of 3.

So on the label holding the MOST mild cells in the corpus (1599 at the 0.68 level), the global constant pushes those cells to the negative side of 0.5 when their own measured rate sits on the line. calib_span's largest negative row is the label where its constant is furthest from that label's own rate. That is a mechanism for the inversion, and it is not in the ledger.

HONEST SIZE OF THE EVIDENCE — THIS IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER IT IS WORTH AN ARM. 6 of 12 is twelve English studies. Its binomial 95% interval is roughly [0.21, 0.79], which CONTAINS 0.378. So this measurement does NOT sharply refute the global constant for Effusion; it says the constant was never measured per-finding and that the one label we can check is not obviously at 0.378. The claim that stands is about the OBJECT being estimated (a per-finding rate), not about the specific number.

WHAT TO DO WITH IT, cheapest first, all CPU:
  1. Extend severity_boundary past Effusion. report_language.SEVERITY names eight graded findings; the same cross-tab runs on each. If several findings' own boundary rates spread widely around 0.378, the per-finding claim is supported by more than one label and the n problem shrinks by pooling.
  2. Compute each finding's 0.68-level agreement rate directly from the 58 annotations against the reader table — that is the same object MEASURED_AGREEMENT estimates, just not collapsed across findings, and it needs no size-word regex at all, so it works on the non-English 59.9% too. This is the real measurement; step 1 is the corroboration.
  3. ONLY IF the per-finding rates spread: an arm with a per-finding MEASURED_AGREEMENT, single-variable against band_span, so it is directly comparable to calib_span's -0.0020.

DO NOT run step 3 on step 1's evidence alone. The stale-operating-point lesson in calib_span's own row applies here too: a sign measured at one operating point is not a property of the lever.

Blocked on GPU only at step 3. Steps 1 and 2 cost nothing.
notes:
STEP 3 IS NOW LICENSED BUT ITS READING NEEDED A GUARD FIRST — 2026-08-26.

Steps 1 and 2 are done (level_agreement, above). The per-finding spread stands: at 0.68 the constant is
0.378 while the findings run 0.000 to 0.778. So step 3 — a per-finding MEASURED_AGREEMENT, single-variable
— is licensed by this bead's own gate.

Before spending it I asked a question this bead never asked: WHERE DO THE CONSTANTS COME FROM, and does
--hold-annotations hold them? It does not. MEASURED_AGREEMENT is fitted on the 696 annotation cells and is
a hardcoded module constant; the hold drops those cells from the training TABLE and leaves the CONSTANTS
carrying them. annotated_readings.withheld reads hold_annotations and nothing else, so a
--calibrated-targets --hold-annotations checkpoint passes the refusal while its targets still encode
annotation-derived rates, and is then scored against those annotations.

That threatened knee-bs4l's +0.0129 annotated / +0.0072 proxy — the number the whole calibration revival
rests on — and it threatened the refutation clause in calib_dense_hold.sh, which reads a proxy null with a
positive annotated read as the mechanism working when it is equally the signature of a contaminated ruler.

MEASURED, no GPU: LevelAgreement.stability refits the constants on disjoint interleaved halves and prices
the gap in its own binomial sigma. 1.1 / 1.5 / 0.9 / 2.0 / 0.7 across the five levels. Four settled; only
0.82 reaches the line. Five scalars over 72-196 cells each are a population estimate, not a fit to these
58, and cannot encode which study has an effusion.

SO THE VERDICT IS KEEP. The larger annotated gain is calibration moving targets out of report-space toward
annotation-space, which is the mechanism, and the board's ruler is annotation-like (0.8487 report / 0.8932
annotated, same weights). knee-bs4l survives; calib_dense_hold's clause survives; the queue is unchanged.

WHAT DOES NOT FOLLOW, and is now written at the guard and at the arm: the annotated read is a consistency
check between two rulers sharing an origin, NEVER an independent confirmation. Constants fitted on the
ruler they are scored against stay that way whatever the stability says. An independent annotated number
needs constants refitted on a held half and a retrain to go with them; no arm has spent one, and until one
does, no annotated delta from a calibrated arm goes into the ledger as a second independent reading.

WHERE THIS POINTS STEP 3. 0.82 is the level whose halves move (2.0 sigma) AND where four of the five
inversions sit (ACL 0.200, Contusion 0.458, Medial OA 0.500, Lateral OA 0.500 against a 0.688 constant).
One level is doing both jobs badly. A per-finding refit that touched only 0.82 would be a smaller, better-
argued change than refitting all five, and it is the one with 141 cells behind it.

MY OWN INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG FIRST. The stability tolerance shipped as a flat 0.05 and called three of five
levels MOVES when the largest was 0.9 sigma — a ruler legislated BELOW the noise it was judging, the exact
faulty-TEST failure mode. Halving a sample multiplies its SE by sqrt(2) and a gap between two halves
carries both terms, so a gap near 2x the full-sample SE is what a perfectly stable constant PRODUCES.
gap_sigma now derives it from the cell counts under the shipped rate. Commit 6fd27e5.

STEP 3 IS NOW UNLICENSED AT THE LEVEL THIS BEAD WAS BUILT ON — 2026-08-26.

This bead's gate was "ONLY IF the per-finding rates spread". They spread. What nobody asked is whether
they spread MORE THAN THIN CELLS ALONE WOULD MAKE THEM. LevelAgreement.heterogeneity now draws that null -
2000 corpora with each finding's own cell count, every cell genuinely drawn from the pooled constant -
and prices both the chi-square dispersion and the RANGE, because the range is the number the ledger
quoted.

  level   findings   chi2 / df    p       range vs chance
  0.08       11      8.1 / 10    0.615    0.105 vs 0.211   consistent with pooling
  0.28       12     26.1 / 11    0.021    0.341 vs 0.429   BEYOND POOLING
  0.68       12     18.0 / 11    0.100    0.778 vs 0.833   consistent with pooling
  0.82       12     22.9 / 11    0.024    0.800 vs 0.750   BEYOND POOLING
  0.94       11     20.3 / 10    0.135    0.400 vs 0.286   consistent with pooling

THE 0.68 LEVEL IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT OF THIS BEAD AND IT DOES NOT SURVIVE. 0.68 is where the 6,461 mild
cells are, where Effusion sits at 0.481 against 0.378 on 27 cells, where Synovitis reads 0.778, and its
"0.000 to 0.778" range is the sentence the calib_span ledger row quotes as mechanism. That range is
SMALLER than the 0.833 the same cells produce drawn from one constant. p 0.100. So the description above -
"on the label holding the MOST mild cells the global constant pushes those cells to the negative side
when their own measured rate sits on the line" - is a reading of sampling noise, not of a per-finding
rate. It should not be quoted again without this line beside it.

WHAT SURVIVES IS SMALLER AND SITS SOMEWHERE ELSE: 0.28 and 0.82. And 0.82 is the level whose POOLED
constant already fails split-half at 2.0 sigma, and where four of the five inversions sit (ACL 0.200,
Medial OA 0.500, Lateral OA 0.500, Contusion 0.458, all against 0.688). Contusion is the only thick one,
24 cells. So the defensible per-finding claim is now: ONE level, 0.82, where the pooled estimate is
unstable and the findings disagree beyond chance.

AND EVEN THAT IS UNCORRECTED. Five levels were tested; two at p ~ 0.02 do not survive Bonferroni at 0.01
individually. The joint statement does - expected count of p < 0.05 across five tests is 0.25 and seeing
two has probability ~0.023 - so per-finding structure exists SOMEWHERE while which level carries it rests
on one uncorrected test each.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ARM. A full per-finding MEASURED_AGREEMENT is estimating sixty numbers from 696 cells
on the strength of a spread that is chance at three of five levels. Do not run it. If the axis is ever
spent, the arm is a single-level one - 0.82 only, everything else left pooled, Contusion the pre-registered
riser at 24 cells - and it is worth ~a 40-minute fit only as an INSTRUMENT that retires the axis, never as
an improvement: no mechanism here plausibly delivers 1.5%.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH: calib_dense_hold stays queued exactly as written. Its constants are the POOLED
ones, level_agreement.stability already cleared them as a population estimate at four of five levels, and
this result strengthens rather than weakens the case for pooling.

title: Competitors independently report local OOF UNDERESTIMATING the LB - corroborates our compression constant from outside
description:
Read 2026-08-25 from the competition discussion via the Kaggle API. Topic 736635 'LB OOF relationship' (4 messages) and 735767 'What Could the Final Ceiling Be' (5 messages). No submission slot spent.

THE OOF->LB RELATIONSHIP, four independent reports:
- 'an UNDERestimation of my model performances in local OOF wrt LB ... for weak macro-AUC the relationship is particularly strange (looks nonlinear)'
- 'the public LB is simply quite a bit easier than our local validation' - from a run whose CV scheme makes leakage impossible
- 'nice that it is at least a somewhat consistent delta over time' - report-derived labels carry noise the image labels do not
- one dissent: 'gold at least for me is much more aligned with the LB, whereas val is quite noisy'

WHY THIS MATTERS HERE: board_transfer fits about +1.82 board points per offline point from our own 58-row record, and we have twice priced a gap wrong by taking that slope from the wrong half of our data. Outsiders seeing the SAME direction (offline under-reads the board) and calling it NONLINEAR is independent corroboration that the constant is a floor-and-slope, not a linear conversion. It does not give us a better number - it says nobody has one, so the caution stands rather than being ours alone.

SHAKEUP, from 735767 and 734681: '0.975 is the threshold of gold medal'; '#1 public LB is already around 0.951 while public solutions reach 0.92'; and an experienced competitor expecting 'a huge shakeup and lots of over fit models ... trusting your cv as a golden rule not very helpful' with 'private LB >0.94 would be gold, winner 0.96'. Also flagged: agents and autosubmissions polling the board fast make public-LB overfit easier than in past RSNAs.

The host has NOT answered whether the public/private split is stratified by site or holds entire sites out (734681, still open). That answer changes whether site-grouped CV is worth the OOF it costs. Until it lands, the honest position is that our public-board number is a noisy read on the thing being scored, which is the standing owner instruction anyway ('the real kaggle test dataset is NOT our dataset').
notes:
2026-08-25, discussion topic 735767 ('What Could the Final Ceiling Be'), read via kneemri.kaggle.discussion_read: the field's own expectation of the public-private split, which is the other half of this bead's compression argument.

  - 1,832 teams twelve days in, against 1,149 for all of RSNA 2025. Public #1 ~0.951, publicly shared solutions ~0.92.
  - Two competitors predict a large SHAKEUP: 'trusting your cv as a golden rule [is] not very helpful' because every team makes its own labels, and 'the public leaderboard will lie' with agents and autosubmissions polling it. One puts private-LB gold at >0.94 and the winner at 0.96 while expecting ~0.97 public.
  - One states 0.975 as the gold threshold; unsourced, and it is a prediction rather than a rule.

Consequence for us: it is corroboration for the direction this bead already records (local ruler and board do not move together), and it argues AGAINST buying board points with anything that fits the public split specifically. It does not change any number we hold - none of these are measurements.

title: champion_check cannot see a stale pin — assert the pinned board is still the board maximum
description: champion_check asserts REBUILDABILITY only; comp/champion.json's principle #39 states in the record that it 'cannot know the entry is still the best one' and that the pin must be updated in the same motion as reading the board. That motion is a human step and it was missed once already (basedense_v1 held the pin three hours after allfit scored) and has been missed again (allfit 0.937 pinned while votefit_v1 reads 0.938). It is one comparison against a file the check already knows about -- BOARD is a module constant there. Report it as a distinct complaint from drift: a stale pin is not an unbuildable pin, so decide deliberately whether it exits non-zero or logs a warning.

title: TrainingOptions is 693 of a 750 line ceiling and two thirds of it is argparse, not options
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-25 of the refactoring lane. kneemri/training/options.py is 693 lines against a file_max of 750 - 57 from the god-file gate, the same 'crept to within 44 lines' story run_setup.py's own docstring tells about the split that produced it. Of those 693, parser() spans 252-578 and _encoder_arguments 578-686: roughly 434 lines, two thirds of the file, are an argparse DECLARATION. The remaining ~250 are the dataclass and the eight methods that read flags as values (recipe, of_recipe, routing, crop, band, reading, cache, supervision, positions).

So the class answers two questions again, exactly as it did before the RunSetup split: what the command line ACCEPTS, and what a flag MEANS. Only the first grows every time a switch is added, which is why the file is at the ceiling. LCOM4 reads 6 on it, the lowest cohesion measured in either package, with six clusters that never touch: {band,crop,reading} {recipe} {routing} {cache} {supervision} {positions}. Six of those are inherent to a config object and are NOT the finding; the argparse half is.

THE MOVE: lift the vocabulary into kneemri/training/flag_vocabulary.py as FlagVocabulary.parser() plus its private encoder-argument helper. TrainingOptions.parse() stays as the public entry and calls it. TrainingOptions.parser() has exactly two callers outside the file, both tests (tests/unit/kneemri/experiments/switch_coverage.py, tests/unit/kneemri/training/options.py), so it can go rather than become a pass-through.

SAFE BY AUDIT: twenty modules import options and every one of them takes TrainingOptions itself - fields() in switch_coverage, parse() in arm_check/vram_need/train, of_recipe() in budget_residuals. Nothing outside options.py reaches for the parser except those two tests. No cycle: the new module builds an ArgumentParser and needs nothing from options.
close_reason: Split landed in 9c21220. options.py 693 -> 259; flag_vocabulary.py 461. The argparse declaration was two thirds of a file 57 lines under the 750 god-file ceiling, and it is the only half that grows when a switch is added. FlagVocabulary.parser() plus its private _encoder_arguments moved; TrainingOptions.parse() stays the public entry and is now the ONLY reach for the parser. TrainingOptions.parser() deleted rather than left a pass-through - its two outside callers were tests (switch_coverage, options), both repointed, and test_parser moved to tests/unit/kneemri/training/flag_vocabulary.py where hygiene.mirror wants it. The defaults-in-two-homes hazard the split creates was already pinned by test_parse_takes_every_default_from_the_dataclass, which compares a no-flag parse against the bare dataclass; a second test asserting the same thing was written and then dropped. Gates green, archmap regenerated in the same commit.

title: 54 kernels are one kernel plus a member tuple: fold the boilerplate, then fold the tuple
description:
FROM BIOHUB'S 2026-08-25 08:48Z LETTER (owner directive, cross-project): "Stop accreting from-scratch experiment scripts. Build ONE cumulative pyramid. Increasing codebase size WITHOUT restructuring/unifying is dangerous." Audited this repo's loose-script surface against that rule.

AUDIT. The package tree is CLEAN — no `_probe.py` sprawl, no notebooks, no root scripts; every entrypoint is a `python -m` module. The accretion is entirely in `comp/kernels/`: 54 kernel scripts, 7338 lines, one per submission attempt, against 37 board entries. That is the many-pyramids pattern in its purest form.

THEY ARE ALREADY HALF-UNIFIED, which is why this is a fold and not a rewrite. `kernel_bootstrap.py` is spliced into all 54 by `build_kernels.py` and gated by `--check`, so `find_kit`/`install_wheels` have one home. Stripping that region leaves 4317 lines.

LAYER ONE — THE BOILERPLATE THAT LEAKED OUTSIDE THE MARKERS. 16 lines appear in 40+ kernels outside the spliced region, ~850 duplicated instances: the six imports (logging/os/subprocess/sys/zipfile/Path), and `main`'s own opening — `logging.basicConfig`, `kit = find_kit()`, `install_wheels(kit)`, `sys.path.insert(0, str(kit))` — plus the `if __name__` tail. Each is a place a fix must land 54 times. FOLD: move the OPEN marker above the import block and add a `boot()` to `kernel_bootstrap` that does basicConfig + find_kit + install_wheels + sys.path. A kernel's own body then reads: docstring, region, `def main(): boot(); from ... import KernelRun; KernelRun(names=(...), overlap=False).run()`. ~750 lines go, `build_kernels --check` already gates the drift, and `kit_check` / `champion_check` / `witness_check` verify offline without a slot.

LAYER TWO — THE PART THAT IS DATA WEARING A SCRIPT. After layer one, what distinguishes one kernel from another is a member tuple and a serving config. That is exactly what `comp/board.jsonl` and `comp/champion.json` already record. 54 python files exist to hold 54 tuples. The pyramid move is ONE kernel that reads its entry, with the tuples living where the results live. NOT started here: the kernel is uploaded manually and a wrong turn costs a slot, so this wants its own plan and its own acceptance test (`champion_check` must still rebuild the pinned 0.937 entry from `chosen`).

RETENTION, the question that must be answered before anything is deleted: 17 of the 54 kernels have no board entry. Git history holds every one of them and `SUBMISSIONS.md` + `board.jsonl` hold the results, so a kernel file is not the record of a submission — but deleting shipped artifacts is outward-facing and is the owner's call, not a sweep's. Propose: a kernel with no board entry and no pending submission is a dead probe and goes; a kernel with a board entry survives layer one and is subsumed by layer two.

REPLY SENT to biohub's inbox naming this audit.
notes:
ORPHAN DELETION (the sweep layer) IS KILLED, and the census that would have driven it is wrong twice over.

Count: 21 orphan kernel dirs, not the 17 recorded here - joined on the canonical `kernel` field of comp/board.jsonl, 3237 lines total.

But deleting them is the wrong move on two grounds:

1. IT REMOVES NO BUG SURFACE. Not one of the 21 is imported or executed by anything in this repo. Every hit outside their own directory is a PROSE citation - kernel_run.py cites kneemri-encoder and kneemri-vote in docstrings, ensemble.py cites kneemri-views in a comment, mount_check.py and kernel_script.py cite kneemri-graft and kneemri-probe as the two cases they cannot see. Deleting the dirs orphans those citations and reduces the bug opportunity the owner asked about by zero.

2. THEY ARE THE ONLY SURVIVING RECORD OF WHAT SHIPPED, and the repo has already paid for that. comp/board.jsonl called fourteen entries permanently unpriceable for want of a script; joining on NAME rather than the kernel field found a surviving script for thirteen of them, all in these directories, and three rows were recovered from them on 2026-08-25 (chosen_v2, onedecode_v2, weakseven_v1 - named 33 -> 36). Deleting an orphan manufactures exactly the hole the file spent two sessions repairing.

Layers one (landed, b3a9aa3) and two (killed: a Kaggle kernel takes no arguments, and moving tuples into the kit makes an entry's identity depend on kit CONTENTS rather than its own text) stand as recorded. Follow-up on the recovery mechanism is knee-rmfa.

title: Reading an intermediate encoder layer costs memory DeviceBudget cannot see (+23.0%)
description:
MEASURED by `python -m kneemri.experiments.budget_residuals` (commit 1f79eca):

  encoder_layer_9_s2026  measured 19.97, derived 16.24  (+23.0%)  CAP UNDER DEMAND — allowed 17.57

THE DEFECT. `--encoder-layer 9` reads the residual stream at block 9 instead of the last block. The budget derives EXACTLY the same number as the default run at the same recipe (16.24, the fitted point) because `Encoder.activation_units(size)` sums tokens x width over every block and knows nothing about where the head reads from. But the measured peak is 3.73 GB higher than the run that reads the last layer.

THAT DIRECTION IS THE SURPRISE. Reading EARLIER should if anything cost LESS, since the blocks above the tap contribute no gradient path. Costing MORE by 23% says the tap is doing something the recipe does not describe — a candidate is that the hook keeps the intermediate activation alive across the whole forward (so both the tap's tensor and every later block's are resident at once), and another is that it defeats the encoder's activation checkpointing or its compiled graph, since `compile_encoder` is on by default and a hook in the middle is a graph break.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CAP. If the mechanism is a graph break or a defeated checkpoint, the arm also paid THROUGHPUT for it, and every intermediate-layer read in the ledger was measured on a slower loop than its comparison arm — which would be a confound in the layer-depth reading, not just a memory bug.

FIRST STEP IS DIAGNOSIS, NOT A CONSTANT: run the same recipe at --encoder-layer 9 with --eager-encoder and compare the peak. If the gap closes, it is the compiled graph and the fix is in the surgery, not the budget. If it does not, the budget needs to know that a tap holds its layer.

Found alongside knee-pf8b by the same instrument; both are CAP UNDER DEMAND rows, which is the failure DeviceBudget calls fatal.

title: mount_check.main is CC 18, the highest in the tree, and holds three separable concerns
description:
`kneemri/kaggle/mount_check.py` main() carries the tree's highest cyclomatic complexity (18, measured by the advisory cohesion.complexity report). It is under the enforced C901/PLR0912 ceiling only because those gates are configured at 10 for NEW code paths and this one predates the reading, so nothing blocks it today; it is a readability and test-surface problem, not a gate failure.

Three concerns sit in one function body:
1. LIVE ACQUISITION (--live/--settle): resolve the dataset identifier, read members, poll until settled, translate TruncatedListingError into the UNKNOWN exit-2 path.
2. MANIFEST ABSENCE: check.absent() and the package-wide refusal it implies for EVERY kernel.
3. THE PER-KERNEL SWEEP: entries -> verdicts -> the passed/skipped/refused buckets, the walked-vs-entries denominator line, and Denominator.refuse_empty().

Only (3) is reachable in a unit test today; (1) and (2) can only be exercised through the CLI, which is why the live path has no test at all.

DESIGN: lift (1) into a small class beside LiveDataset (a `LiveReading` holding `live` and `unsettled`, with the try/except and the exit-2 decision as a method returning a state rather than calling sys.exit), and lift (3) into a method on MountCheck returning a verdict summary object that owns the buckets and the walked count. main() then reads as: parse, acquire, absent, sweep, exit. Each lifted piece gets its hygiene.mirror test.

CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: the CC report drops main below 10 and the existing mount_check behaviour is unchanged — the same refusal codes on the same inputs (0 clean, 1 refused/absent/unsettled, 2 truncated). No new gate suppressions.

title: Fourteen entrypoints still hand-roll the CLI opening that core.cli.Command already owns
description:
AUDITED 2026-08-25 across kneemri/ and core/: 47 modules open their main() with cli.Command, and 14 still write the same four statements by hand — ArgumentParser(description=__doc__), a run of add_argument, parse_args(), logging.basicConfig(level=INFO, format='%(message)s').

The hand-rolled fourteen: core/data/labels/confident_labels.py, core/data/labels/label_power.py, kneemri/evaluation/{alignment_damage,board_transfer,encoder_drift,ordinal_signal,record_mix,side_blindness}.py, kneemri/experiments/{arm_check,card_check,queue_check,stale_gap}.py, kneemri/kaggle/champion_check.py, kneemri/training/fitted_encoder.py.

WHY IT MATTERS beyond line count: core/cli.py is the repo's ONLY CLI contract and it states the log format and where paths.yaml lives in one place. A module that re-decides those is a module that can drift from them silently — fitted_encoder.py already calls basicConfig BEFORE parse_args, which is the opposite order from every other entrypoint, and nothing would have caught it. The contract also gives every command a --paths a runner can redirect; the fourteen do not all have one.

NOT A FRAMEWORK MIGRATION. cli.Command exposes .parser, so each module keeps its own flags and its own main; what changes is four lines at the top. Watch for a module that already declares its own --paths (argparse raises on the duplicate) and for the two that pass a CLASS docstring rather than __doc__ (board_transfer, champion_check) — that is deliberate and must be preserved.

core/data/corpus/cache_flags.py is NOT in scope: it adds arguments to a parser someone else owns.

title: Two parameter clumps travel by hand through the objective and the coverage reports
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 by cohesion.data_clumps:

  4 sites, 4 params  normalise_by_count, per_label, structure, weight
                     kneemri/training/objective.py, kneemri/training/remembered_ranking.py
  6 sites, 3 params  normalise_by_count, per_label, structure   (same pair, the 3-param subset)
  5 sites, 3 params  batch, start, width
                     core/data/corpus/study_cache.py, core/data/corpus/window_reader.py
  4 sites, 3 params  corpus, measured, sampled
                     core/data/corpus/band_coverage.py, crop_alignment.py, crop_coverage.py

The first is the loss's own shape passed positionally between two files that must agree about it - the
clump most likely to cause a real bug, because a caller that swaps per_label and structure gets a loss
that trains rather than an error. The second is a read window. The third is a sampling denominator, which
is exactly the quantity this project has already mis-reported three times in one session.

Each becomes a frozen dataclass beside its producer. Small, mechanical, and each one deletes a repeated
signature rather than adding a layer.
notes:
2026-08-25 05:00Z progress.

DONE - clump 1 (the objective's shape). `Shaping` frozen dataclass added to kneemri/training/objective.py
beside `LabelStructure`, carrying normalise_by_count + per_label + structure. Six constructors converted
(Objective, RankedObjective, DistilledObjective, DecorrelatedObjective, MarginObjective, RememberedRanking),
run_setup.objective now builds ONE `shaping` and hands it to all six branches - 44 lines of repeated kwargs
became 19. cohesion.data_clumps re-run: 4 clumps -> 2, and both surviving ones are the OTHER two entries here,
so the 4-param and 3-param objective entries are gone rather than reshaped. Equality check held: the
settings() dict assertions in tests/unit/kneemri/training/objective.py pass unchanged, which is the switch
account a run is read against. 72 tests pass in the five affected files.

CLOSED WITHOUT WORK - clump 2 (batch, start, width). NOT a defect. core/data/corpus/window_reader.py:37
already argues the choice in prose: 'travels as three parameters rather than one request object
DELIBERATELY ... a slicing expression, not a noun the rest of the codebase says anything about ... would add
a type to name an argument list, on the inner loop, and would still be unpacked in the same two places.'
The detector cannot see an argued decision. Leaving it, and this note is so the next audit does not re-open it.

NEXT - clump 3 (corpus, measured, sampled). The real one: the shared part is the DENOMINATOR PAIR
(sampled, corpus), and the three tools word the same sentence three different ways. Plan is a
`CorpusSample(chosen, corpus)` that owns BOTH halves - the every-k-th draw (duplicated verbatim in
band_coverage.py:226, crop_coverage.py:195 and CropAlignment.sampled) and the denominator sentence - since
stating the denominator without owning the draw is exactly how a subset rate gets printed as a corpus rate.
crop_coverage.py and crop_alignment.py also still carry hand-rolled CLI preambles, so they take the
core.cli.Command port in the same edit.
DONE. Clump 3 (corpus/measured/sampled) closed by CorpusSample in core/data/corpus/study_cache.py — it owns the DRAW and the denominator sentence together, and CropAlignment.sampled/.named are deleted. Found a real bug doing it: all three audits printed a header, no rows, exit 0 on a wholesale decode failure; they now call CorpusSample.denominator().refuse_empty(). Denominator moved kneemri -> core (import-linter forbids core -> kneemri). crop_coverage + crop_alignment also took the core.cli.Command port. Clump 1 (Shaping) and 2 done in 8e2c788; clump 4 (batch,start,width in window_reader) is DELIBERATE and argued in its own docstring — do not re-open. data_clumps advisory now reports 2, both untouched entries. Commit 208f64d.

title: arm_check is 738 lines with a CC-21 main and three disjoint responsibilities
notes:
AUDITED, and the bead's proposal did not survive it. The proposal was to split LCOM group 2 out as a 'smoke cache decoding' side job; group 2 is {_parsed, decode_smoke_caches, overstated, readings, refused, uncached} and FOUR of those six are the module's PRIMARY checks (REFUSED, UNCACHED, OVERSTATED), clustered with decode_smoke_caches only because all six call _parsed. Executing it would have moved the tool's headline check into a class named for a side job. Second consecutive bead (after knee-rln3) whose proposal was wrong on reading the file.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT was in main, not in the class: seven checks each hand-rolling findings -> name-each-while-arming / count-otherwise -> contribute-to-exit-code, with two of them (report_prices, report_mismatch) already half-extracted and the pattern abandoned. CC 21, highest in the tree.

FIXED in e7bcd39. ArmVerdict (new module kneemri/experiments/arm_verdict.py) carries a finding, the two voices, and its own refusal policy; ArmCheck.verdicts states all eight beside the rules; main composes an exit code. main is off the complexity report entirely, tree max is now 15 (was 21). arm_check 738 -> 746 lines, plus 56 in arm_verdict.

WORTH KEEPING: the first pass looked like a fix and was not — it relocated the complexity into dict comprehensions and an or-chain, both of which radon counts as decision points, and main re-measured at 21 unchanged while the file GREW to 769. Only re-running --report cohesion.complexity caught it. Verify a refactor by the measurement it claims to move.

title: kneemri-count8 is not the eighth rung of the count curve it is named for
description: Its chosen tuple is the dark6 six plus band_dense_long_s2026 plus small_batch6_s2026 - the FOLD-0 twin, not small_batch6_ff. So it moves two variables against dark7 (a new member AND a fold-0 seat) and is shaped like lastseat 0.937 rather than like a count rung. It was written before dark7 existed. A true count-8 rung needs an eighth --fold -1 member, which does not exist yet and costs ~95 GPU-minutes. Either rename it to what it measures or rebuild the tuple as dark7 plus one converted member once the dose reading arrives.

title: Nothing in the repo reads the leaderboard, so the gap-to-leader decays silently in champion.json
description:
comp/champion.json pins the gap to the leader at 0.008. Read from the API on 2026-08-24 it was 0.015 and it is still 0.015 tonight. The pin was correct when written and decayed without anything noticing, because the only way to read the board here is to remember to type the kaggle CLI by hand.

kneemri/kaggle/ has no board reader at all — there is champion_check, mount_check, kit_check, seat_value, and nothing that asks what we are actually behind. 2026-08-24_the_goal_priced_against_the_inventory.md names this in its own words and it was never filed.

This is the same failure shape as board_transfer being quoted from prose at 4.67 / 2.14 / 1.92 for three months while the tool read +1.82: a number that lives in a document instead of a command goes stale and then gets planned against.

Scope: a kneemri.kaggle.board_read that fetches the top N and our own entry, prints the gap, and refuses quietly-stale reads; champion_check calls it so the pinned gap cannot rot unobserved. CPU-only, no slot cost. Remember the archmap regen in the same commit.
notes:
BUILT 2026-08-25: kneemri/kaggle/board_read.py, plus the wiring into champion_check.

SHAPE. LeaderboardRead(leader, ours, taken, rows) with gap as a SUBTRACTION rather than a stored field,
so the number cannot be edited to disagree with its own inputs. The live round trip is injected exactly
as board_check.LiveBoard and mount_check.LiveReading are — a path reachable only through real
credentials is a path with no test — and every one of the seven unit tests runs credential-free.

FIRST LIVE READ: leader 0.952, ours 0.938, gap 0.014 over 20 rows, recorded into comp/leaderboard.json
with the UTC instant. So the prose was wrong in the direction the bead predicted but only by a tick:
0.008 pinned, 0.015 quoted, 0.014 measured.

TWO THINGS FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, both recorded rather than smoothed over:
1. The API PAGINATES AT TWENTY and hands back a next-page token. My first version called the field
   `entries`, which would have written "entries: 20" into a record whose whole purpose is not to lie —
   reading as "twenty teams are competing". Renamed to `rows`, documented as one page, with the reason
   page one suffices for THIS question (Kaggle returns the board best-first, so the leader is on it) and
   does not suffice for a field size. The leader is taken as max() not [0], so the number does not depend
   on an ordering the API is free to change.
2. An absent record RAISES rather than reading as a gap of zero, and the message names the command that
   fixes it.

STALENESS IS THE HALF THAT MAKES IT A CHECK, and it is deliberately split: the live read needs
credentials, the age check does not. champion_check now refuses a recorded read older than STALE_DAYS=2,
which is derived and not chosen — five slots a day resetting at 00:00 UTC means a read from before
yesterday sits behind at least ten spent slots, ours and every rival<39>s. That is the same split
board_check draws with --live.

AND THE PROSE WAS FIXED AT SOURCE. comp/champion.json carried "the gap ... is 0.015" inside a principle;
that clause now points at the command and the record instead of holding a number. Otherwise this repeats
board_transfer, whose slope was quoted wrong from prose twice while the tool read it right.

Checks list in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md goes eleven -> twelve.

title: card_check argv preview truncates at the recipe defaults, hiding every override
description:
card_check prints the running process argv truncated to ~100 chars. For every arm in this repo that prefix is $RECIPE — the shared defaults — and the arm's own overrides come AFTER it. So the preview shows precisely the flags that are being overridden and never the ones that were moved.

Concretely, small_batch6_ff runs '$RECIPE $FIT' with FIT='--fold -1 --ema'. card_check displayed '--fold 0'. Reading that at face value says the one deliberate flag of the arm did not land, which would indict a 95-minute run mid-flight and could get a correct run killed.

It resolved to the opposite conclusion only by going around the tool: the arm script's flag ordering, the nan holdout AUC that only a --fold -1 run produces, and the 1.21x epoch-time ratio against the 1.26x study-count ratio.

Fix, in order of preference: (a) have run_train echo the fully resolved command into the arm log — no arm log currently records the flags it ran with, which is the deeper gap; (b) have card_check show the argv TAIL, or elide the middle, so overrides survive truncation.

title: queue_check advises relaunching a stranded arm that has already finished
description:
queue_check reported: STRANDED: experiments/arms/cnx_own_recipe.sh - owed by a dead watcher and by no live one, so relaunch after.sh over them; the marker they wait on may already be written.

cnx_own_recipe had already COMPLETED at that point - ARM DONE in its log, best 0.8186 at e6, checkpoint on disk, greedy seat 53 of 67, written up in the ledger. Obeying the advice would have put a finished 3.1 h arm back on the card, on top of small_batch6_ff which was 6/12 through it.

The check reasons about WATCHERS (who owes an arm) and not about ARMS (whether the arm's work is done). Its own hedge names the wrong hazard: it warns the MARKER may already be written, when the thing that matters is that the arm itself already ran to completion and its result is recorded.

FIX: before printing STRANDED for an arm, look for 'ARM DONE <stem>' in logs/<stem>.log, or for the checkpoint the arm writes. If the work landed, the strand is CLOSED, not stranded - report it as a watcher to clean up rather than an arm to relaunch. Two categories, two different actions, and only one of them touches the GPU.

This is the same family as the failure card_check was built for: two identical member_curve scans on one card for twenty-five minutes after a nohup relaunch landed on a job that had NOT failed. That one cost a reading; this one would have cost the card during a submission window.

title: vjepa_member 0.8343 is also a crash reading - trainer exit 127 at epoch 10 of 12
description:
Same shape as the raddino bead. logs/arm_vjepa_member.log ends 'ARM FAILED vjepa_member (trainer exit 127)'. Exit 127 is command-not-found, so the arm's own chain broke rather than the trainer - the same class of silent failure CLAUDE.md already records twice (bare 'nox', 'pkill').

The run reached epoch 9 of a 12-epoch one_cycle schedule at 0.8343 and was still climbing. Its full log also records a real STALL mid-run ('173 img/s against this run's own peak of 589'), diagnosed in-log as another process paging over PCIe - so this number was measured under card contention as well as truncated.

0.8343 is the second-best foreign trunk we have and sits only -0.017 from base_dense (0.8512), measured under two handicaps. Lower priority than raddino only because vjepa2l is heavier and its 2.64h for 10 epochs makes the finish more expensive.

Do not re-price the V-JEPA family off this number in either direction until it has run clean.

title: The ninth seat is dead: no member in a 33-candidate pool improves the 8-member peak, at any quality or distance
description:
Measured 2026-08-24, no card, from holdout arrays already on disk. 8-member greedy peak = 0.8731.

RESULT. 33 candidates added as a 9th member, spanning solo 0.79-0.857 and nearest-neighbour
agreement 0.769-0.951. NOT ONE reaches 0.8731. Best is intensity392_ws / attend_true at 0.8729;
worst 0.8706. The entire spread of outcomes is 0.0011, a sixth of the 0.0062 noise floor.

NOT AN APPEND-ONLY LIMIT. For 12 of the strongest and most distant candidates, the EXHAUSTIVE
best-8 over {peak8 + candidate} returns the ORIGINAL eight, unchanged, all 12 times. The peak set
is a local optimum under append AND under single-swap. Logs: floor_sweep.log, swap_sweep.log,
swap_sweep2.log.

THE OWNER'S PRINCIPLE - "it is about diversity, not averaging 7 copies of the same number" - shows
up in the SIGN and dies on the SIZE. spearman(delta, NEAREST) = -0.203: distant members DO help
more, and the two most distant of 28 are two of the best five. But spearman(delta, SOLO) = +0.477
is larger, and both live inside a 0.0011 band. Distance ORDERS the candidates; it pays none of them.

CONFOUND CHECKED AND CLOSED. RankAverage is equal-weight, which penalises the distant-but-weak case.
Under weighting the damage shrinks and does not reverse: QualityWeightedRank 0.8712, LogitAverage
0.8726, both under 0.8731.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. Not that diversity loses. margin_seat is solo 0.8525 and greedy takes it 2nd
of 65 on distance alone - distance BUILT this peak. What is exhausted is the POOL, not the
principle: every candidate here comes from one trunk family, one pipeline, one split, so a 34th
draw is a re-roll, not a new axis. Says nothing about a member from outside that space.

CONSEQUENCE. The pre-registered bar on knee-y59c (peak8 + it > 0.8731) is a test NOTHING passes -
it gates no decision. Replaced by a DISPLACEMENT test: put the new member in the full pool, re-run
the greedy from scratch, ask whether the NEW peak beats 0.8731. Solo AUC stops being a gate.

CORRECTION - two claims from the first five-point write-up are RETRACTED, both filed by me before
the wider sample existed, both now in the ledger as retractions:
1. "cnx_dense lost to matched-quality but much NEARER peers side_dense and quarter_data." Their
   distances were never looked up. Measured: cnx_dense 0.7686, quarter_data 0.7932, side_dense
   0.7961 - ALL far outside the roster spread. The comparison varied nothing.
2. "Damage is monotone in solo quality." Fails: deep24 (solo 0.8352, nearest 0.8342) scores 0.8727,
   above v3base_dense (solo 0.8455, nearest 0.8829) at 0.8721. Higher solo, closer, worse.

LIMITS. One peak set, one split, one fold. Swap test is SINGLE-swap over 12, not exhaustive over 33.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-24 18:02Z — the isolation claim in this issue is UNFOUNDED, the numbers are not.

This issue says cnx_dense 'lands 0.0004 BELOW its matched-quality but much nearer peers side_dense and
quarter_data', and concludes 'extreme distance bought no exemption at all'. The premise was never
checked. Measured with MemberDistance against the same 8-member peak (nearest-neighbour agreement, no
labels read):

  cnx_dense      nearest 0.7686
  quarter_data   nearest 0.7932
  side_dense     nearest 0.7961

All three are far outside the roster spread, not one distant member against two near ones. The three
weakest members in the pool are ALSO the three most distant, which is the anti-correlation the
architecture section already records - distance and strength are anti-correlated across the whole axis.
So the comparison held distance roughly FIXED and varied nothing; it cannot speak to whether distance
buys an exemption, in either direction.

What survives: the five ensemble numbers are real, every weak member cost the peak, and no vote rule
rescued cnx_dense. What does not survive: the inference that distance failed to pay. That was a claim
about a contrast that does not exist in the data.

A denser sweep is running (28 more members, delta against the same peak) together with both distance
axes for all 32, which is the reading that can actually separate the two. Early sign that the
monotone-in-solo claim also fails on the denser sample: deep24 (solo 0.8352, nearest 0.8342 - genuinely
distant) gives 0.8727, while v3base_dense (solo 0.8455, nearest 0.8829 - a near neighbour) gives 0.8721.
Higher solo, closer, WORSE. That is distance paying, in the band where the floor was bracketed.

The ledger entry and the letter already sent to celltrack carry the same unfounded sentence and both
need the same correction.

EXTENDED 2026-08-24 18:24Z - "the RECIPE SPACE is what saturated" TESTED, NOT ASSERTED.
Seven members outside the 33 run through the same displacement test: vjepa_warm, vjepa_member
(video pretrain), raddino_dense (medical pretrain), dinov3_base_lora, dinov3_v3small_224,
lora_r8_v3small_224, grade_ladder. ALL SEVEN return the original eight. 19 displacement tests,
0 passes, three separate pretrain corpora among them. So "an outside-corpus member gets in" is
NOT supported.

CONFOUND, checked rather than skipped - it is the same one that broke the five-point read.
Solo: dinov3_v3small_224 0.8057, raddino_dense 0.8137, lora_r8_v3small_224 0.8215,
dinov3_base_lora 0.8268, vjepa_warm 0.8337, vjepa_member 0.8343. Every outside-corpus member is
0.013-0.054 BELOW the seated band (0.8466-0.8598). Outside-corpus AND worse; the test cannot
separate them. The one candidate at parity is grade_ladder 0.8565 - above six of the eight seated
- and it is INSIDE-space (ordinal-target trick, same trunk, same corpus). It fails too.

STATE OF THE AXIS. No candidate has ever existed that is BOTH outside the pretrain corpus AND at
seated quality. Inside-at-parity fails (grade_ladder). Outside-below-parity fails (six members).
The deciding cell is EMPTY. cnx_own_recipe is the first candidate that could fill it, and that is
now the arm's whole value - not a ninth seat, but the measurement that separates corpus from quality.

title: PUSH DEBT: comp/members.roster names vjepa_warm_s2026, the live package does not hold it
description:
mount_check on 2026-08-24 reads '40 ok, 4 skipped, 1 refused' and the refusal is kneemri-farseat: its chosen tuple names vjepa_warm_s2026, and the all_ours dataset holds 34 checkpoints, none of them that one. A kernel that loads every member and then cannot build one fails AT RUNTIME on Kaggle, after the session has been allocated - the exact failure mode mount_check was written for (it caught kneemri-solo ranking over a package that had gained a DINOv3 member while its metadata still declared DINOv2 only).

TWO REPAIRS AND THEY ARE NOT EQUIVALENT. Packaging vjepa_warm would make the kernel runnable, but knee-053z has already priced that member: nearest seated neighbour 0.8210, the most distant member this project owns, seat value +0.0001 against a +0.0015 threshold, and the ledger row reads 'DISTANCE IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT'. So farseat is a kernel built to test a hypothesis that has since been refuted twice on two rulers. DELETING it is the honest repair; packaging a refuted member to make a dead kernel green is work spent to keep a gate quiet.

PRICE: ~5 min to delete, 0 to leave (the gate already refuses it, so it cannot ship by accident). P(clears 1.5% bar) 0.00 - it moves no score. It is hygiene, and the reason it is P3 rather than closed-as-wontfix is that a standing REFUSED line trains the eye to skim mount_check's verdict, which is the one gate whose whole value is that it is read.

DECIDE FIRST whether farseat is wanted at all before touching the package.
notes:
SELF-CORRECTION, same day, before any work was done on it. I filed this recommending DELETION of kneemri-farseat on the grounds that vjepa_warm is a refuted member. I had not read comp/members.roster, which is the file the description itself calls 'the package's only definition'. Reading it:

  Line 228 NAMES vjepa_warm_s2026.pt, added 2026-08-24, with thirty lines of argument, including that mounting it required first publishing dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf/vjepa2-vitl.

So the roster INTENDS to ship this member. The divergence is not a stale kernel -- it is that the ROSTER HAS BEEN EDITED AND THE PACKAGE HAS NOT BEEN PUSHED SINCE. mount_check is reporting a pending push, correctly, and my reading inverted which side was stale.

That also inverts my seat argument. I cited vjepa_warm's +0.0001 seat value as grounds to drop it; the roster states that same number and mounts the member BECAUSE of it -- '0 of 1 clearing the +0.0015 threshold, which by this roster's own rule means the offline ruler cannot tell it from the incumbent. That is the whole argument for mounting it, not against.' Precedents named there: calib_span mounted at -0.0020 carried 0.929; through_dense at -0.0020 is seated in the champion.

REVISED ACTION -- a push, not a deletion. The next package push should carry:
  vjepa_warm_s2026  -- roster-named since today, unmounted, gated on kneemri-augseat which has since read 0.936 (the roster's own gate said >=0.940 licenses naming it, <=0.935 says no kernel should; 0.936 falls between and leaves it mounted-but-unnamed, which is exactly what mounting-is-reversible is for)
  margin_seat_s2026 -- measured today into the strong-and-distant cell, not in the roster at all yet; needs a roster line with its numbers before it is pushed
  dissent_seat_s2026 -- if its seat read supports it; same objective axis, finishing ~17:40Z
One push, all of them, since mounting is reversible and a slot is not.

ALSO CORRECTED, from the same failure to read: I estimated the offline-to-board slope by hand at ~3.4 from the weakseven instrument. board_transfer reads +1.92 over 15 entries and 90 pairs. The roster warns in terms about this exact move -- 'Read it from board_transfer, never from prose' -- after the constant was wrong twice, both times quoted from prose. margin_seat's +0.0013 offline swap therefore prices at about +0.0025 board, not +0.004. Caveat the tool itself prints: +1.92 is fitted entirely at or below board 0.933 and is an extrapolation where we now live at 0.937.

What generalises: I filed a deletion recommendation against a file whose header says it is the only definition of the thing I was reasoning about, without opening it, and I hand-fitted a constant the repo has a tool for. Same shape as the two P0s on 2026-08-13 and yesterday's literature beads -- reciting a belief instead of reading the record.
2026-08-24 17:08Z — the SHIP-SIDE half of this debt, measured. `kit_check` says the mounted kit is at e7b65a0, 2 commits behind in the 33 files the kernel loads: cd661ab and 3108766. All three of today's board entries (allfit 0.937, lastseat 0.937, augseat 0.936) are stamped `kit e7b65a0`, so they ran two-commits-behind code.

Diffed both against HEAD, scoped to the kernel-loaded files, before calling it a defect:
- cd661ab -> kneemri/inference/vote.py: ADDS `RankAverage.agreement`, a staticmethod nothing on the serving path calls. Purely additive.
- 3108766 -> kneemri/models/backbone.py: ADDS `mount='dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf/vjepa2-vitl'` to the vjepa2-vitl encoder entry. Live ONLY for a member whose encoder is vjepa2-vitl — i.e. vjepa_warm_s2026, which is exactly the member this bead says is named-but-unmounted.

So the stale kit changed nothing about today's three scores. That is luck, not design: the one behavioural line it is missing is the one that the other half of this bead is about to make load-bearing. The moment vjepa_warm ships, an e7b65a0 kit is a kernel that mounts the member and cannot locate its weights.

CONSEQUENCE: the kit rebuild is not optional housekeeping to do eventually — it must go in the SAME manual upload as the member push, or the push lands a member the shipped code cannot resolve.

title: torch.backends is never touched: no cudnn.benchmark, no TF32, no channels_last — and the next arm is convolutional
description:
Audited the training pipeline for throughput on 2026-08-24. Most of it is already right and that is worth recording so nobody re-audits it: torch.compile on the encoder is the DEFAULT (--eager-encoder is the escape) after twenty-two of thirty-six arms forgot the old opt-in flag and paid 21% a step; bf16 is the DEFAULT (--fp16 is the escape) with the scaler dropped; gradient checkpointing rides in THROUGHPUT at a measured 19% a step for nearly all the encoder activation; and there is no DataLoader anywhere because the pixel cache is resident uint8 and divided on device, so there are no workers, no pin_memory and no prefetch to tune. Nothing to win there.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING. torch.backends is never touched anywhere in the tree. Three settings, none of them present:
  torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark - unset, so cuDNN re-picks a convolution algorithm by heuristic instead of autotuning once per shape. Our shapes are FIXED per run (resident cache, one read size, one slice count), which is the exact case benchmark is for. Irrelevant to a ViT, and the arm queued right now behind dissent_seat is ConvNeXtV2-base at 448 px.
  channels_last - unset. Convolutional trunks on tensor cores typically take 10-20% from the memory format alone, and again this only bites for the family knee-y59c is about to test.
  TF32 (set_float32_matmul_precision / allow_tf32) - unset, and this one is probably NOISE here rather than a win: autocast already runs the matmuls in bf16, so what is left in fp32 is small. Listed for completeness so the next audit does not re-derive it.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW AND NOT BEFORE. 189 of 202 checkpoints are ViT, and two of the three settings only pay on convolutions. The pipeline was optimised for the family we ran, which is the same shape as knee-zfgn's finding one layer down. cnx_own_recipe is about to spend ~2.6 h on a convolutional trunk with cuDNN autotuning off and the memory format wrong, and if it comes back slow that is OUR pipeline, not the architecture - the faulty-TRAINING suspect, again.

PRICE: ~10 min to add both settings plus a per-step timing read on the smoke, against a plausible 10-20% of every convolutional arm from here on. P(clears 1.5% bar) 0.00 - it moves no score at all and must never be sold as one. It buys WALL-CLOCK, which is this project's actual constraint, and it removes a confound from the trunk arms. Do NOT touch the running dissent_seat; land it before the NEXT convolutional arm, or after cnx_own_recipe so that arm keeps its control's conditions.

CAUTION: cudnn.benchmark makes the first step of each new shape slower and is only free when shapes are stable; whole-stack reading varies the slot count across studies, so verify the shape set is small before believing the win. channels_last must be applied to the model AND the input or it silently converts back every step.

title: max -> mean over the slice axis: the one-flag control the sequence-head bead depends on
description:
Our slice aggregation is amax. The MIL benchmark at arXiv 2604.26807 reports that simple MEAN pooling matches or outperforms recent MIL and 3D-CNN alternatives on 4 of 6 moderate-sized tasks while being ~25x cheaper, and that attention-MIL never gains more than 0.025 absolute AUROC over it. That literature is usually quoted as an argument against learned aggregation - but the baseline it beats things with is MEAN, and ours is MAX. Nobody here has ever compared the two.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN NUMBER. It is the control for knee-blvm. If mean already recovers most of what a GRU would, the sequence head is buying order rather than robustness and its arm must be read that way; if mean is flat or worse, then max is not the thing holding the stack back and knee-blvm's mechanism claim is cleaner. Either reading is worth more than the delta itself. Max is also the noisier estimator by construction - one outlier slice sets the feature - so a mean-pooled member may be a DIFFERENT error structure and therefore a seat candidate on the distance ruler even at equal quality (knee-053z).

PRICE: One entry in SLICE_POOLINGS (per_slice=True, aggregator=None currently means bare amax - a mean needs either a tiny module or a widening of that record), plus one ~2.5 h arm at the standing recipe against band_dense 0.8578 on the same split. Directional at best on its own: expected delta well inside the 0.0062 floor either way. Justified as an INSTRUMENT for knee-blvm, not sold as an improvement.

Do NOT run this before knee-blvm if only one card slot is free - the sequence head is the mechanism, this is its control, and a control run before the thing it controls for is a slot spent on a number nobody will act on alone.

PRICE: ~2.5 h of card. P(clears 1.5% bar) 0.05 on its own; it is an instrument for knee-blvm, not an improvement.
close_reason: Already measured, and the ledger holds the number. experiments/README.md rows slice_attention/attend_true: max 0.8457, unweighted mean 0.8473 on one recipe, i.e. max->mean is +0.0016 — a quarter of the 0.0062 floor. The row is even a natural experiment rather than a designed one: slice_attention's gate is zero-initialised and the optimiser never reached it (knee-7gyw), so that arm IS mean pooling, and attend_true re-ran it with the gate trained for +0.0003 more. This bead was filed against literature (arXiv 2604.26807, mean >= attention MIL) without grepping the ledger first, which is the exact failure CLAUDE.md names. The literature's ordering reproduces here; its SIZE does not survive our noise floor.

title: Distance as a seat rule: refuted, 0.8624 vs greedy 0.8719 over 70 members
description:
MemberCurve.diverse (forward selection by disagreement, parameter-free) run against the greedy on 70 same-split records / 909 shared studies, card-free. Diverse peaks 0.8624 at 62 seats; greedy peaks 0.8719 at 9. At matched nine seats diverse reads 0.8331. Loss 0.0095 at peak, past the 0.0062 floor.

WHY: in this pool distance and weakness are correlated - diverse's first five seats include quarter_data and half_data, members trained on a fraction of the corpus. The rule buys the correlation at full price. Refuted is 'distance is a seat rule', NOT 'a distant member can be worth a seat'.

AND: the greedy is not blind to distance. It seats vjepa_warm 12th and mae_matched (most distant in the pool, solo 0.6735) 18th, on a plateau flat to four decimals. It takes distant members late rather than never.

STILL OPEN, one cell: every distant member we own is also weak (the seven-trunk table orders solo exactly opposite to distance, no exception). The greedy has never been offered a distant-AND-strong member to refuse. knee-u0my (v3lora_dense) exists to build one.

Ledger: experiments/README.md, 'DISTANCE AS A SEAT RULE, RUN RATHER THAN ARGUED'. Commit cd661ab.

title: V-JEPA at a LARGER READ — the only untried combination of the two things that have moved
description:
THE RESIDUE ledger item (d) from vjepa_warm, priced. Every V-JEPA number this project holds was taken at 256 px with 20 slices. Nothing on this axis has varied the read.

WHY THIS AND NOT MORE EPOCHS. The other open residue is (a), a twelve-epoch schedule closing the 0.017 solo gap — 3.2 h of card, and the arm's OWN overfit signature argues against it (train loss fell monotonically 0.9198->0.6189 across all six epochs while holdout stopped improving at epoch 3 and drifted 0.8337->0.8311->0.8306; a schedule still generalising when it stops does not look like that). Call it 15-20% odds on ~0.003 board. Poor ratio.

WHAT MAKES THE READ AXIS DIFFERENT. Two things have actually moved a number on this project: whole-stack reading (+0.0147, the only lever that has cleared the noise floor) and DISTANCE (the axis the 2026-08-21 board split was decided on — lr4e-5_ws priced -0.0003 and took 0.931 while band_span priced +0.0002 and cost a tick). vjepa_warm is the most distant prediction family this project has ever produced: nearest seated neighbour 0.8210 against a seated spread whose most distant sits at 0.8801, a gap of 0.059, and it is a WORKING model that disagrees rather than a broken one (mae_matched's 0.4333 is what broken looks like). It bought +0.0002 only because distant-and-WEAK buys nothing: solo 0.8337 against roster members 0.8525-0.8578.

So the seat needs the solo gap closed WITHOUT spending the distance, and the untried lever is exactly the one that has produced this project's largest measured gain. A larger read on a tubelet trunk is also CHEAPER per token than on a 2D one — Stage.tubelet costs grid^2/tubelet per slice, and the direction was read backwards once already (knee-2nxh).

PRE-REGISTER BEFORE RUNNING: solo >= 0.85 with nearest still under 0.88 = the seat verdict is overturned and this is a new family in the roster. Solo up but nearest above 0.88 = the read bought quality by making it a twin, which is the whole trade and it fails. Solo flat = the trunk's ceiling on this task is real and V-JEPA is done as a member.

BLOCKED ON THE CARD, not on a decision: margin_seat then dissent_seat own it for ~2 h. Size the read against DeviceBudget before arming — 256 px was not necessarily a choice.

title: Training logs carry no config stamp, so a flag can only be verified after the run writes a checkpoint
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-24 on margin_seat. The arm log opens with a memory-gate line and then goes straight to 'epoch 0: loss ...'. Nothing in it says which flags the process actually parsed. The recipe stamp exists only inside the checkpoint, and the checkpoint is written at RUN END, so for the whole 84 minutes of a 12-epoch arm there is NO way to assert that --auc-margin (or any other flag) landed.

WHY IT MATTERS. The project rule is 'assert the flag LANDED, don't assume' — a value recorded in a config while the consumer reads a constant is one of the five named ways a well-argued idea dies on a harness bug rather than on its merits. Today that assertion could not be made: the smoke checkpoint that would have carried the stamp was deleted before it was read, so the only evidence --auc-margin fired was INDIRECT (margin loss 1.0150 vs cross-entropy's ~1.19 on the same shape). That is mechanism evidence, not a landed-flag assertion, and it is the weaker of the two by a lot.

FIX: emit the parsed config as the first line of the run log, before epoch 0 — the same dict the checkpoint stamps. One line, written once, and every arm's log becomes self-describing from second zero. It also makes a queued arm auditable without touching the card: the log answers 'what is this run' while it is still running.

title: vjepa2l has no Kaggle weights mount, so the recorded SHIPPABILITY PRE-CLEARED on knee-rpkw cleared only half of it
description:
knee-rpkw records, dated 2026-08-23 and written before the run rather than after it: 'SHIPPABILITY PRE-CLEARED. The mounted kit cf6a99f already carries BOTH pieces this member needs to load on Kaggle: backbone.py defines VJEPA2_LARGE and the facebook/vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256 entry, and volume_read.py defines VolumeRead. Verified by git show, not by assuming the kit tracks main. So if this arm returns a member worth a seat, it can be packaged and fired on the CURRENT kit.'

Both verified facts are true and the conclusion does not follow. Those two pieces are the CODE half. The other half is the WEIGHTS, and a Kaggle kernel has no internet, so an encoder reaches it only as a mounted dataset. Measured today: ENCODERS['vjepa2l'].mount is None, alongside cnxbase; every other encoder on the board carries one (dinov2 via metaresearch, the three DINOv3 variants via the private dimiturnt/dinov3-hf, raddino via dimiturnt/rad-dino).

The repo already knows this and says so at the exact spot. package_members.shippable() refuses a member whose encoder no Kaggle dataset mirrors, and its docstring names these members by name: 'three of the nine encoders carry no mount, two of them already have trained checkpoints on disk (cnx_dense, the V-JEPA2 members), and a roster line naming one of those used to package and push without a word.' So a roster line for vjepa_warm would be REFUSED at packaging today, and the recorded clearance says it would fire.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW rather than as bookkeeping. vjepa_warm (0.8337) is the most distant member this project has ever produced, nearest-neighbour 0.8210 against a seated band of 0.8801-0.9143, and knee-avzz's live augseat entry decides whether distance licenses a mount over the offline ruler's verdict. If augseat reads >= 0.940 the entry wants firing the same hour, and discovering the missing mount then costs the hour.

FIX, which is the one shippable() names: publish the weights and give the variant a mount. Weights are already on this machine at ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--facebook--vjepa2-vitl-fpc64-256 (1.3 GB, config.json + model.safetensors), and dimiturnt/dinov3-hf is the working precedent for a private per-variant snapshot dataset. Card-free; bandwidth only.

LESSON, which is the transferable part: a clearance that names the pieces it checked is only as good as its enumeration of the pieces that exist. This one enumerated two and there were three.
notes: FIXED in 3108766. Weights published as dimiturnt/vjepa2-hf/vjepa2-vitl (directory named for the leaf locates() matches on, not the bare variant name - staging it as 'vitl' would have uploaded 1.3 GB that locates() could never find). backbone.py's vjepa2l entry now carries mount=. Verified: locates('/kaggle/input/vjepa2-hf/vjepa2-vitl') True, locates on a dinov3 path False, ENCODERS['cnxbase'].mount still None so the unmounted-representative test stays valid, and a dry package_members build accepts 35 members with shippable() passing on vjepa_warm_s2026.

title: Six allfit seats carry no witness; their reading is proven only by twin transfer
description:
The pending kneemri-allfit entry seats six members with an EMPTY witness (five _ff plus final_ws_e12), all of them victims of the knee-52mu hole: --fold -1 took its fingerprint from a holdout it did not have. The fix in Fitting.witnessed only helps members fitted from 2026-08-24 on, so these six stay unwitnessed forever unless backfilled.

Closed for now by TWIN TRANSFER rather than by measurement on the weights themselves. Each of the six has a witnessed sibling whose reading config is IDENTICAL (verified key by key over the packaged configs; the only differences were ema, layer_decay, slice_regions and through_plane, of which ema and layer_decay are not reading axes and the other two matched their StudyDesign.from_config defaults, model.py:161-163):

  calib_span_ff    -> calib_span_s2026     ok 0.00158 of 0.0312, 8 of 12 labels
  grade_ladder_ff  -> grade_ladder_s2026   ok 0.0162  of 0.0312, 4 of 12 labels
  base_dense_ff    -> base_dense_s2026     ok 0.00908 of 0.0312, 5 of 12 labels
  lr4e-5_ws_ff     -> lr4e-5_ws_s2026      ok 0.00219 of 0.0312, 5 of 12 labels
  through_dense_ff -> through_dense_s2026  ok 0.01    of 0.0312, 6 of 12 labels
  final_ws_e12     -> grade_ladder_s2026   (same row; differs only in ema)

All five residuals spread across 4-8 of 12 labels, which is the arithmetic shape rather than the concentrated shape every real reading defect produced.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT BUY. A witness pass on config C proves the SERVING PATH reads config C the way training did, and every defect this check has ever caught was a consumer-side default disagreeing with a recorded value — which is a property of the config and the code, not of the weights. So the transfer covers exactly that defect class, and it is what licenses reading the pending allfit score as a fact about the all-data axis rather than about plumbing. It does NOT prove anything about the _ff weights themselves.

The real backfill (replay trainer.predict over 8 studies through a RunSetup rebuilt from the checkpoint recipe, compare against the serving path) is still worth building if a future entry seats an unwitnessed member whose config has NO witnessed twin. It was not built here because reconstructing the training path by hand risks a FALSE refusal, and the twin argument closed the question for these six at a fraction of the cost.

title: Slot availability is signal, not noise: per-stratum normalisation refuted 12/12
description: Hypothesis: SlotHead renormalisation + decoded_at zero-mask make prediction LEVEL depend on which of six primary slots a study presents; if that level shift were orthogonal to the label it would inject spurious population-wide ordering, recoverable by within-stratum rank normalisation. Measured on the 909-study fold-0 holdout over the six champion seats that keep a holdout.npz, rank-averaged. Result: normalising within slot-COUNT costs -0.0091 mean AUC, within presence-PATTERN -0.0209, negative on all twelve labels under both stratifications. Inverted reading: which sequences a study was scanned with records what the ordering clinician suspected, so the level shift is NOT orthogonal to the label and the ensemble already exploits it. Full account in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_slot_availability_is_signal.md, including the harness bug (continuous truth summed as a count, AUCs out of [0,1]) and the reconstruction check that licensed the numbers (0.8693 vs the champion's recorded 0.8694). Live descendant: whether the ensemble captures ALL the protocol signal or only part — fit a per-pattern per-label prior and ask whether blending moves the holdout. Card-free.

title: Serving reads all geometry from the member's own config, not a kernel literal — audited, and the residual hazard is an EDIT to a default
description:
Ported from a peer project's defect: their kernel pins the decode grid as a literal, so a checkpoint trained at another grid mounts clean and decodes wrong with no raise. Audited whether the same shape exists here. It does not, and the audit is recorded so nobody pays for it twice.

FINDING 1 — NO KERNEL-SIDE GEOMETRY LITERAL. A kernel script passes member names and 'overlap' and nothing else; KernelRun.__init__ (kernel_run.py:37-57) has no size/slices/band/pool parameter. Every geometry value is read from the member's own checkpoint config, which is copied wholesale into the manifest (package_members.py:69) and back out (members.py:505). So roster heterogeneity — 20 slices beside 12, band 0.10-0.90 beside 0.20-0.80 — is correct by construction rather than a hazard.

FINDING 2 — THE SHIPPED SEVEN ARE CLEAN. Checked every checkpoint on disk for key presence. The shipped seven carry every geometry key; the only absences are 'through_plane' and 'slice_regions', whose defaults (off, 1) are what the code did before those keys existed. So no shipped member is served off-grid.

FINDING 3 — greedy7 IS NOT PLUMBING. Its +0.0018 offline -> +0.000 board was the one inversion in an otherwise zero-inversion transfer, and this defect class was a candidate explanation for it. It is refuted: nothing in the serve path could have served a greedy7 member off-grid. Selection overfit (+0.0033 measured over subsets) stands as the read.

FINDING 4 — WHAT I GOT WRONG, AND THE REAL RESIDUAL. I first wrote a packaging gate refusing any member whose config omits a geometry key. Run against the committed roster it refused SEVEN members (res392_ws, calibrated_targets, sliceattn, intensity392_ws, extended_ws, lora_r8_v3small_224 on centre+tie; deep24 also on whole_stack) — all false positives, zero true positives, so it was reverted rather than shipped. The reason it has no true positive is worth stating: every default was chosen to reproduce the behaviour that existed before its key did, so an absent key means the member WAS trained at the default. deep24's config confirms it directly (12 slices, band 0.2-0.8, channels pooling — pre-settlement geometry throughout).

That guarantee holds only while nobody EDITS a default. Move SLICE_BAND and every keyless member is retro-served on a band it never saw; move LEGACY_SLICES and their stacks change depth. Nothing raises, and the fingerprint is taken over read_size and group alone (members.py:658) so it is blind to slices, band, crop and pooling by construction. That is the real instance of the peer's mechanism here, and it fires on edit rather than on any checkpoint now on disk.

DONE: a pin test in tests/unit/kneemri/inference/members.py asserts the eight default values with the argument attached, so changing one fails a test that explains what it retro-breaks. Zero false positives, catches the actual mechanism.

title: Serve-path routing asymmetry: training never routes, serving always does
description: TRAIN reads a memmap cache routed ONCE offline over train_series.csv (fitting.py, options.py, pretrain.py, trainer.py all consume CachedCorpus/StudyCache; no training module imports Study or SlotScheme). The Kaggle kernel routes EVERY hidden-test study live through core/data/corpus/slots.py predicates (submission.py:144-166). Five hazards sit on that seam. THREE ARE NOW EMPIRICALLY CLOSED: (1) plane vocabulary is closed and clean -- exactly {Sagittal,Coronal,Axial}, zero NaN, exact match to the slot predicates, on train_series.csv (24,371 rows) and test_series.csv (15 rows), so the silent-unroute hazard does not fire on any data we can see; (2) the duplicated plane lookups (study_cache.py:420-424 vs submission.py:328-331) are IDENTICAL -- 24,371 rows each, 0 mismatches, so drift is latent not live; (3) hidden-test fill is unmeasurable by construction -- test_series.csv is 2,213 bytes, the public sample. The FOURTH -- the serve path measured nothing -- is closed by SlotFill (commit 2db2389): per-slot fill and empty-study count now logged on every served split, with a legislated 5% zero-slot ceiling that refuses above FILL_WITNESS_FLOOR=100 studies. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: the two lookups should share one home rather than stay two identical copies, and there is no assertion tying the serve-time scheme to the scheme its members were CACHED under.

title: Lateral OA, PF OA, Baker's and Fracture have NO published comparator - our 0.7099 on Lateral OA is unpriceable
description:
A frontier sweep on 2026-08-23 found no published AUC for: compartment-specific (medial/lateral/patellofemoral) OA detection on MRI (located OAI/MOST work reports Dice/IoU or PF-OA incidence, not detection AUC); Baker's/popliteal cyst detection (nearest: SE-YOLOv5 cyst mAP 0.942); knee fracture on MRI (all located AUC figures are radiograph-based).

Consequence: Lateral OA at 0.7099 is our second-lowest annotation-ruler number and we cannot tell whether that is a large deficit or near the ceiling of a genuinely hard task. Same for PF OA at 0.8005. Together these two labels are 1/6 of the metric and are currently unpriceable, which means knee-9707's +0.025 ceiling is a LOWER bound on available headroom, not an upper one.

Cheapest way to price them: an internal oracle rather than a literature number - e.g. what does a model trained on Lateral OA alone reach, or what is the inter-annotator agreement on compartment OA in our own 58 annotated studies. Do not spend card time on this before knee-9707.

Source: research/2026-08-23_published-per-label-auc-vs-ours.md

title: Two live jobs on one card: queue_check guards watchers, nothing guards the card
description:
On 2026-08-23 two identical member_curve scans ran concurrently on the same GPU for 25 minutes (pids 40228/51260 at 13:22:33 and 52524/43408 at 13:23:26, same 15 checkpoints, same cache dir). A nohup relaunch landed on top of a job that had NOT failed; the launcher's own exit told me nothing, which is the documented nohup hole.

The cost was not only the wasted card. The contention made base_dense take 11 minutes instead of ~3, and I was one step from recording 'the DINOv2-base member is slow' as a fact about the member. A harness fault wearing a measurement's clothes -- exactly the class CLAUDE.md says to suspect first.

queue_check already blocks the symmetric holes for WATCHERS (zero watchers owing an arm, two watchers owing one arm). The card has no equivalent: nothing asks 'is a training or scoring job already holding the GPU?' before a launch.

Proposed: a card_check (or a flag on queue_check) that reads the process table for python.exe under this repo's venv running a card-taking module, and refuses/warns on a second. Cheap: one Win32_Process query. Should be in the eight-checks list in CLAUDE.md, which is where every other already-happened failure is written down.
notes:
BUILT 2026-08-23 as kneemri/experiments/card_check.py, and NOT the way this bead proposed. The bead
said "read the process table for python.exe under this repo's venv running a card-taking module" --
that needs a maintained list of which modules take the card, which is wrong the first time an arm is
renamed and wrong the other way for `member_curve --device cpu` (reads like a card job, takes no card).
It asks the DEVICE instead. nvidia-smi reports the pids actually computing; the process table is used
