title: Q-AA: metadata-conditioning seat for train_series.csv fields
description: Implement and evaluate a metadata-conditioning variant of a current whole-stack member. The per-series fields Fluid_Sensitive, Fat_Suppression and Anatomical_Plane are available in test_series.csv, clean, and literature (Meta-D, Dohmen et al. 2026) shows +2-3 pp gains from conditioning a vision model on analogous MRI metadata. Start with late concatenation or FiLM; control is the same member without metadata. Full audit in research/2026-09-02_series_metadata_axis_audit.md.
acceptance_criteria: A scored run and a seat comparison showing AUC delta vs image-only control; decision on whether to promote to a roster member.
notes: AUDIT BEFORE CLAIM, 2026-09-02: the premise is wrong by two thirds. kneemri/evaluation/study_series.py:8-11 records that Anatomical_Plane is CONSTANT (all 4,407 training studies carry Axial, Coronal and Sagittal alike) and Fat_Suppression EQUALS Fluid_Sensitive on all 24,371 rows; population_split.py:151 asserts the duplication at runtime. So the conditioning axis is ONE binary field, not three. That field is already consumed upstream by the slot router (raptor_feed.py:263,267; slot_fill.py:40; submission.py:346), so a FiLM head re-injects a bit the sampler already used to choose the slices. Kimi's citations do not reach the claim either: Dohmen +3pp and Liang >99.9% are series CLASSIFICATION (predicting sequence type from metadata naming it) - the redundant case, and Liang is evidence AGAINST since a fitted trunk reads sequence off pixels. Meta-D is the only real positive and is FiLM over sequence+PLANE, and plane is constant here. Sent 2026-09-02_0135z asking (1) for evidence on a single already-consumed binary flag improving DIAGNOSTIC classification, (2) Meta-D's plane-vs-sequence ablation split. Empty answer = decline. No card until then.
close_reason: DECLINED on mechanism, 2026-09-02. Two of three columns carry no information (study_series.py:8-11: Anatomical_Plane constant across all 4,407 studies; Fat_Suppression == Fluid_Sensitive on all 24,371 rows, asserted at population_split.py:151). The surviving binary field is already consumed by the slot router (raptor_feed.py:263,267, slot_fill.py:40, submission.py:346), so a FiLM/concat head re-injects a bit that already chose the input slices. Kimi's follow-up audit supplies the rule: Vincent 2020 conditioned a U-Net on T2 vs T2star and found INCONCLUSIVE gains because 'the modality-related features might already be encoded in the regular U-Net'; Lemay 2021's +5.1% Dice lands only when the metadata is TUMOR TYPE, a property not inferable from the image. Metadata conditioning pays only when the field carries information the pixels do not - Fluid_Sensitive fails that on both counts. Meta-D (the one positive precedent) never ablates plane vs sequence, and plane is constant here, so it cannot be assumed to transfer. Also declined the weaker StudySeries.counts()/.fluid() variant: series count proxies protocol length proxies site, which is a shortcut the hidden private split exists to punish - worse than null, not a weak positive.

title: Q-AC: text as privileged information (LUPI / distillation), not a text-branch member
description: The text-as-input branch is unshippable: the hidden test set has no Report column. The surviving text mechanism is privileged information: train a text-side model on reports, use only its output to shape the vision student. Question (Q-AC): when the hard labels were themselves extracted from the same reports, does a text teacher ever beat the extractor, or does it only reproduce it? Literature search; no card time.
notes:
DOWNGRADED to P3 at 2026-09-01 23:10Z, on Kimi's own Q-Z reply, before any card was spent. Two facts in that reply remove the reason the arm was filed P1.

THE 0.906 IS NOT THIS ARCHITECTURE'S NUMBER. It is the Kaggle Models tab 'best public score' for DINOv2-small across 40 users. The repo is a starter skeleton, does not claim to reproduce it, and its own default run is vision-only with the text branch listed as a later iteration. So there is no measured pairing of the two-branch design with 0.906 anywhere - the number that made this look like a 1.5% lever belongs to a backbone, not to a text branch. The whole P1 case was that arithmetic.

THE OBJECTIVE IS THE SHAPE THAT SHOULD BE EXPECTED TO HURT. No coupling loss: the report embedding is broadcast to the 12 target positions, concatenated with the per-target vision features, and ordinary BCE does all the work. The 12 labels were EXTRACTED from that same report text, and the test set has no Report column at all - so during training the model is handed a channel that nearly determines its target and is then absent at inference. The vision trunk is under less pressure to read the image for exactly the findings the metric scores, which is a stronger version of the mechanism that made report_supervision monotone in its weight rather than merely flat. A vision-ablation test is the only thing that would separate a supervision gain from that leakage, and it has not been run by anyone.

WHAT SURVIVES. The cheapness is real - training-only, no new loss, unchanged kernel runtime - so this stays as a P3 that a spare card slot could answer with a pre-registered vision-ablation, not as a night. The mechanism-(a) form on knee-iem6, contrastive image-report pretraining, is unaffected by this reply and remains the literature-backed member of the family. This is the third time the text axis has been re-opened by prose and closed by reading what the number actually measured.
Claude Q-AC mail 2026-09-02 0323z: re-scope from text-branch member to text-as-privileged-information. Input branch is dead because test set lacks Report column. Preliminary research note: research/2026-09-02_text_as_privileged_information_qac.md.

title: Transductive / test-time adaptation family DECLINED in writing
description:
Audited via Kimi Q-X (research/2026-09-01_transductive_test_time_adaptation_audit.md, knee-za1r). Declining the whole family; this bead is the written argument so it is re-opened by answering it rather than by re-asking the question.

WHY IT WAS ASKED. This is a CODE competition and the test set is present in full inside the kernel at inference. No entry this project has shipped uses that fact; every one treats each study as independent and stateless. With solo 0.859, ensemble 0.944 and the leader at 0.952, ensembling has already bought 0.085 and the leader sits 0.008 past where it buys out, so an axis nobody here has touched was worth pricing.

1. TEST-TIME PSEUDO-LABELING. 1-3 pp published, on small corpora or segmentation, and only with uncertainty filtering. Overfits the public split and can destroy the private score; rare positives get smoothed away by confident negatives. Needs a second training pass inside a 9 h kernel while we sit at efficiency rank 153. DECLINED on variance and runtime.

2. TEST-TIME NORMALIZATION / ALIGNMENT. Pays when recovering from a domain-shift DROP, small or negative when train and test are already close. Our trunks are LayerNorm/GroupNorm (DINOv2/v3, Swin, ConvNeXt), so TENT/AdaBN-style BN recalibration does not apply at all. Medeiros et al. 2026 measure standard TTA DEGRADING medical classification by up to 31.6 points on BN-statistic mismatch. DECLINED unless a systematic public/private shift is first diagnosed - it is a repair, not a lever.

3. NEIGHBOUR-GRAPH SMOOTHING. A few points in few-shot classification when the graph aligns with classes. Ours is ~1,300 test studies, 12 independent binary labels, severe imbalance: a similarity graph on frozen embeddings connects rare positives mostly to negatives and smoothing erodes the recall that carries the metric. Nearly free for us since embeddings are already cached, which is exactly why it is suspicious. DECLINED as a plan; admissible later as a low-probability side bet, never as the gap story.

4. THE COMPETITION RECORD. RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine top eight: 2.5D/3D CNNs, ensembles, 3-stage pipelines, no transductive training. RSNA 2019 ICH: 5-fold ensembles and ordinary TTA. Current public landscape here: best public score is DINOv2-small 0.906 with a 2.5D plus multilingual text branch. Nothing transductive is visible near the top of any of them.

WHAT WOULD RE-OPEN IT: a measured public/private distribution shift (which makes 2 a repair with a target), or a competition write-up showing a transductive method at the top of a comparable multi-label medical task.

title: MRNet architecture is already ours; both halves are answered
description: Stanford MRNet (2018): per-slice 2D feature extractor -> global average pool -> MAX pool across slices -> FC, then a separate CNN per (series, task) with a logistic regression weighting the three series. First half is slice_pooling.py MAXIMUM (SlicePooling(per_slice=True)), which this project has had all along - we have never used 3D convolutions, so 'volumetric' was never the bet. Second half is a per-view specialist stack combined by a fitted linear rule, which is exactly what vote/votefit measured at 0.938, flat. Filed to CLOSE the question rather than to open an arm: nothing in MRNet is untried here. Our LABELWISE slice attention is strictly richer than their max pool.

title: trajectory_check cannot arbitrate the warm lane until eight six-epoch runs exist
description: The floor fix (knee-e8sm) made short budgets READABLE; it did not make them READ. cnx_warm_anneal is the only 6-epoch run on disk, so spread() refuses with 'only 1 run(s) match a 6-epoch budget past epoch 3, and 8 are needed'. Every warm restart we run from here is unarbitrable mid-flight until the 6-epoch corpus reaches MIN_CORPUS = 8. Two ways out, and the choice is a design decision, not a default: (a) accumulate - warm arms are cheap (~20-80 min) and the lane is one we said we would run, so the corpus fills on its own and the gate switches on at the eighth; (b) band adjacent budgets - read a 6-epoch arm against, say, 5-8 epoch runs pooled, which is a WIDER instrument and must be argued for, because the whole reason gain() matches on the budget is that a 24-epoch one_cycle has twice the anneal left after the gate (median +0.0339 vs +0.0210) and a long schedule's headroom must not excuse a short arm. Do NOT pick (b) to make the current arm readable - that is fitting the instrument to the job it is refusing. Until one is chosen, a warm arm runs to completion and is read by convergence_check afterwards.

title: Captum for per-STUDY failure triage, and the standing argument in attribution.py it must answer first
description:
OWNER, 2026-08-30, named attribution (captum) as an analysis instrument. Synthesis: research/2026-08-30_analysis-instruments-distance-divergence-attribution.md.

THIS IS NOT A GAP, IT IS A POSITION ALREADY TAKEN. kneemri/evaluation/attribution.py already does attribution, by OCCLUSION, and its docstring argues against the gradient/saliency family by name: nothing in the supervision ever says WHERE a finding is, so a saliency map has no reason to look right and cannot be checked against anything, whereas an occlusion produces a NUMBER on the held-out score. It closes with: saliency is deliberately not here, the sibling cardiac project keeps captum behind an optional extra for the same reason, the always-on diagnostic has to be the one that yields a measurement. Three occlusion diagnostics exist and each returns a delta: slot importance, border-vs-centre, depth profile. That argument is correct and this bead does not discard it.

WHERE CAPTUM STILL ADDS SOMETHING. Occlusion is COARSE BY DESIGN (a whole acquisition slot, a border ring, a depth window) because it costs a forward pass per occlusion, so its resolution is bounded by card time. Integrated Gradients and GradientSHAP cost a fixed multiple of one backward pass regardless of spatial resolution, so they are cheaper PER UNIT OF DETAIL. The framings that survive the incumbent argument:
  - VALIDATE SALIENCY AGAINST OCCLUSION FIRST, then use it where occlusion is unaffordable. The three occlusion measurements are ground truth a saliency method can be SCORED against. Reproducing border-vs-centre and the depth profile is what licenses it to answer finer questions. This is the only framing in which a picture becomes a measurement.
  - ATTRIBUTE OVER SLOT ATTENTION rather than pixels. SlotHead per-diagnosis attention is small and checkable directly against the slot-importance occlusion.
  - PER-STUDY FAILURE TRIAGE, which is the owner actual framing: why a model does bad somewhere. Corpus-level attribution is what occlusion already does well. The unmet need is the individual failure: take the studies the ensemble is most wrong on and ask what the model looked at. Occlusion is too coarse and too slow for that.

THE HONEST COUNTER. The saliency reliability literature is unkind. Adebayo et al. sanity checks (randomise weights, randomise labels) show several popular methods produce near-identical maps for a trained and an untrained network. ADOPTION GATE: run that sanity check on OUR model first and report it, before any map is read as evidence. captum arrives as an OPTIONAL EXTRA matching the sibling cardiac project, never a declared dependency, never in the serving path or the kernel budget.

PRICE: ~half a day plus the sanity check. Zero card of consequence, 0 slots. Ranked LAST of the three instruments the owner named, because the incumbent argument is sound and this clears it only in the narrow per-study framing.
notes: Do not build before the sanity check is specified. Optional extra only; must not enter serving or the nine-hour kernel budget.

title: Budget-bound members are all mid-pack: extending epochs is not a score lever
description:
convergence_check reports 11 of 104 scored runs (10.6%) UNDERTRAINED, i.e. peaked on their final epoch, so their scores are floors set by the budget rather than ceilings set by the recipe. Five of them sit at e11 of a 12-epoch budget: cnx_dense, encoder_adapt, encoder_adapt_lower, mixup224_strong, mixup_dense.

Priced 2026-08-30 before running anything. Best holdout among the whole undertrained set:

  mixup_dense_s2026          0.8552
  wholestack_fold2           0.8518
  mixup224_strong_s2026      0.8516
  crop80_tissue_s2026        0.8345
  adapt_null_s2026           0.8240
  lora_r8_small_336_s2026    0.8127
  cnx_dense_s2026            0.7927
  encoder_adapt_lower_s2026  0.7309
  encoder_adapt_s2026        0.6902
  mae_matched_s2026          0.6735

Seated members on the roster read 0.88-0.89. The best budget-bound member is 0.03 BELOW the seating floor, so a budget extension has to buy more than 0.03 before the member is even a candidate for a seat, and the extension is a knob. Cost ~40 min of card per arm; plausible gain a mid-pack member that still does not seat. Ratio is poor against every open lever, so this is NOT run.

What would re-open it: a budget-bound run whose holdout lands INSIDE 0.88-0.89. Then the extension is cheap and the member is a seat candidate. Until then the 10.6% figure is a fact about the recipes, not a lever.

Separately, 8 runs remain TRUNCATED (died early); their scores are floors for a different reason and convergence_check keeps exiting 1 on them.
notes:
The 8 TRUNCATED runs price out the same way, checked 2026-08-30 00:13Z. Their scores are floors (the process died before the recipe finished; under one_cycle the anneal never ran), so relaunching them is the same shape of lever as extending a budget. Best holdout in the truncated set:

  dissent_seat_s2026          0.8509  (e6 of 9 run, 12 asked)
  depth_regions_span_s2026    0.8487  (e8/9)
  slices16_ws_s2026           0.8452
  pair_memory_s2026           0.8353
  vjepa_member_s2026          0.8343
  cnx_mid_rate_s2026          0.7177  (e0/1 — barely started)
  focus_latmen_s2026          0.4747  (e0/1 — barely started)
  v3_calib_ff                 nan

Top of the truncated set is 0.8509 against a seating floor of 0.88-0.89, so the same 0.03 gap applies and the same verdict follows: relaunching is not a score lever. The two barely-started runs (cnx_mid_rate, focus_latmen) are the only ones whose floor says nothing at all about their recipe — their scores are facts about a killed process at epoch 0, exactly the failure convergence_check was built for. If either recipe is ever wanted for another reason, it must be re-run rather than quoted; neither is wanted now.

So across BOTH under-trained families — 11 budget-bound and 8 truncated, 19 runs — not one sits inside the band where a seat is possible. The whole 'finish the unfinished runs' lever is closed on evidence rather than on preference.

title: The mounted package predates 30 new roster members — push it before any entry can seat them
description:
knee-0dtv added 30 members to comp/members.roster, stackfit_s2026 (0.8631 solo, second-best checkpoint the project owns) among them. The roster is the DEFINITION; the Kaggle dataset is the ARTEFACT, and the mounted one predates all thirty. So every one of them is still unseatable in a kernel today, for a different reason than yesterday: yesterday the roster did not name them, today the package does not carry them.

Until this is pushed, mount_check will read a roster the package cannot satisfy, and any entry chosen from a greedy over the full 123-member pool is unbuildable on Kaggle.

STEPS: python -m kneemri.kaggle.package_members (builds from the roster), then the manual upload, then python -m kneemri.kaggle.mount_check to assert Kaggle will actually serve what the roster names. Uploading is manual, so mount_check is the only thing that can tell us the artefact matches.

WATCH THE SIZE. Thirty more checkpoints is a materially bigger dataset; if it does not fit or the upload is too slow, the answer is a second package, not a silently trimmed roster.
notes:
DEMOTED P1 -> P3 the same evening, by the measurement that the roster fix made possible. This bead was filed on the assumption that thirty unshippable members meant thirty missing seats. The honest greedy over the full 111-member pool then read best honest count 28 at 0.8753, which is +0.0002 over the previous unrestricted honest12 at 0.8751. The thirty members buy nothing on the honest curve. So pushing a materially bigger dataset -- on a disk that is 95% full -- to seat them is paying a real cost for a measured null.

WHAT STAYS TRUE. The roster is still the definition and the artefact still lags it, so mount_check will report the divergence and should. This is now a hygiene item, not a lever.

WHAT WOULD RE-PROMOTE IT. Not a bigger pool. A member that is genuinely OFF this architecture -- a different decode or corpus (knee-ombx) -- would need packaging to be seated, and that is the case where the push buys something. Push then, with that member in it, rather than pushing thirty members that a measurement says are interchangeable with what is already mounted.

title: Seat swaps into the champion are closed: a +0.0045 member buys +0.0004

  member quality took 81.7% of the spread and was removed before the axis was read
  component 1: 45.7% of what is left, against a permutation null bar of 27.4%
  ONE shared axis: the pool's spread is a TRADE, and a permutation of it cannot move the mean

  loading, most negative first:
    Synovitis -0.454, Effusion -0.389, Medial OA -0.199, Lateral OA -0.181, Contusion -0.057,
    PF OA -0.003, ACL +0.015, Lateral Meniscus +0.032, MCL +0.060, Medial Meniscus +0.214,
    Fracture +0.313, Baker's +0.647
  by structure scale: focal -0.0086  regional +0.0121
  ends: depth_regions_span_run1 -0.158, mae_matched -0.137, encoder_adapt -0.117
        ... merged_blend +0.037, normcount224 +0.040, contrast_dense +0.041

WHAT IT MEANS. A member better at Synovitis and Effusion is measurably WORSE at Baker's, Fracture and Medial Meniscus. That is not noise: after member quality is removed the first component takes 45.7% of the remaining spread against a 27.4% null. The pool is NOT a flat monoculture on the competence axis, whatever it is on the architecture axis.

IT RESOLVES TODAY'S CONTRADICTION. Routed top-k per label measured NEGATIVE this morning, and a flat rank average, honest greedy seats and (knee-669u) learned weights all tie at the same ceiling. If a real per-label trade exists, routing should win. It does not, and the reason is the DENOMINATOR: the routing choice is made on 909 studies with as few as 62 Fracture positives, so the per-label ordering that the axis proves exists in aggregate cannot be recovered per label at this sample size. The axis is real AND our ruler cannot pick along it.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE CEILING MECHANISM. Averaging members that sit at opposite ends of a trade cancels the trade. That is why four aggregation strategies sharing nothing but the pool land within 0.003 of each other: they are all averaging along an axis whose ends subtract.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT LICENSE. Not a per-label loss and not a focus-label member: the house rule is to keep the objective general and fix needs with balanced data, not loss-engineering, and per_label_loss and focus_label are both already flags this project has. Nor does it license a diversity-seeking seat search - that is what has already been measured flat, four ways.

WHAT IT DOES LICENSE, and it needs its own pre-registration before anything is armed: a member deliberately placed OFF this axis rather than at an end of it. The ends are populated (depth_regions_span at -0.158, contrast_dense at +0.041); what the pool has never held is a member whose competence profile is orthogonal to the trade.

IMMEDIATE USE: this is a THIRD read for raddino_dense when it lands, and a better one than the two on knee-fzpy. Re-run competence_axis with the new checkpoint present and read WHERE IT SITS. At an end of the existing axis it is another draw from the pool whatever its solo score. Off the axis - a member whose loading is small on component 1 while its own quality is high - is the first genuinely new competence profile this pool has held, and that is the finding the seat and distance rulers cannot report.
notes:
2026-08-29 17:20Z — RETRACTED, by an instrument added one tick after the finding.

AxisReading.maturity correlates each member's axis position with its own holdout mean. Over the same 109-member pool: r = +0.90.

The axis is very largely MEMBER QUALITY. Row-centring removes each member's LEVEL — that is the 81.7% the reading already reported — but it cannot remove the SHAPE of being under-fitted, and that shape is a direction in this matrix: the high-prevalence large-signal findings (Synovitis, Effusion) come first in training and the rare focal ones (Baker's, Fracture, Medial Meniscus) come last. So the first component is mostly the FITTING GRADIENT read back as pool structure. The tail widened to 15 a side put lr2e-4_ws (a learning-rate knob) and quarter_data (a data fraction) at the diffuse end, which is what prompted the check.

Retracted: (1) the pool spans one competence trade; (2) the aggregation ceiling is that trade cancelling under averaging; (3) the pre-registered target of a member at +0.15 toward the focal end. A focal-end member is just a better member; seating the opposite end seats a worse one.

Survives, and duller: the ceiling still has an explanation — the pool is ONE QUALITY LADDER with a long weak tail, so every strategy that averages it averages strong with weak and they land together. The four-strategy tie (knee-669u) and the closed vote axis are untouched; those were measured on held-out score, not on this decomposition.

Priority dropped P1 -> P3: the module and its guard are worth keeping, the finding is not. General lesson now in the module docstring: removing a confound's LEVEL is not removing the confound, and a decomposition that reports how much quality it stripped can still be reporting quality afterwards. Any future reading of a resolved axis quotes maturity beside it or means nothing.

title: mount_check exits 1 on kneemri-blendall — it asks for blend_through/blend_base, neither is in all_ours
description:
`python -m kneemri.kaggle.mount_check` reports 58 ok, 4 skipped, 1 REFUSED of 63 kernel directories, and
exits 1 on the refusal. The refused one is `kneemri-blendall`:

  D:\data\...\all_ours holds [56 members] and was asked for ['blend_through', 'blend_base']

Neither name is in the packaged roster. `kneemri-calibsolo` — the kernel slot 5 is pinned to — reads `ok`.

WHY THIS IS FILED AND NOT FIXED TONIGHT. The check is doing exactly its job: it names a kernel that would
load a member the package cannot build. The cost is that a NON-ZERO exit is now the tool's normal answer,
which is the shape that gets a real refusal waved through later — this project has paid twice for a green
reading over a broken one. It is not on the submission path, so it does not block slot 5, and the fix is
either repackaging those two members or retiring the kernel.

DECIDE WHICH before fixing: `blend_through` / `blend_base` may be names from an earlier roster generation
that the kernel was never updated past, in which case retiring it is correct and repackaging would resurrect
a member nothing else references. Check the ledger for both names first.
notes: Duplicate of knee-2jfx, which filed the same refusal first and at the right priority. Closed unworked. I filed it without searching the board — the same mistake this session already paid for once (re-deriving knee-o3a1's raptor correlations). Search before filing, not after.

title: Graduate ledger_check's unattributed advisory: 13 runs quote a number another run provably owns
description:
`ledger_check` now reports, advisory and never blocking, the runs whose score never shares a LINE with their own name. Today: 46 of 156 loose, and 13 of those quote a number a DIFFERENT finished run demonstrably owns — the reader following that number lands on the wrong row.

The philosophy is graduated gates: a check starts advisory and becomes enforced once the code is clean. The 13 collided rows are the clean-able subset. Fix them (give each run a same-line row of its own), then the collided count is the thing to enforce — `if collided: raise SystemExit(1)` — while the plain 46-loose count stays advisory, because a gate failing on a third of a correct-enough ledger is one the reader learns to skip.

The 46 are printed as one line, the 13 individually, so the actionable subset is already separated in the output. Blocked on nothing; it is bounded reading work.

title: Arm a band_wide twin at the champion fit regime — a seat covering the resolved deficit axis
description:
First card arm when the GPU returns; better argued than the calibrated-blend cross (knee-brkd's neighbour) because it aims at a BOUNDED weakness.

MECHANISM, measured today at zero cost from records already on disk. The supervision gap resolves three deficit findings (ACL, MCL, Lateral Meniscus) whose paired bands exclude zero while the aggregate does not (knee-yx0n). In-plane resolution does not reach them: lr4e-5 vs res392 reads ACL +0.0109, MCL -0.0088, LatMen -0.0001, nothing marked. THROUGH-PLANE DOES, and in the wrong direction for us: band_wide_s2026 (16 slices) vs band_dense_s2026 (20), the only diff 'slices 16->20', reads PF OA +0.0194*, Medial OA +0.0122*, Synovitis +0.0135 against MCL -0.0111, ACL -0.0037, LatMen -0.0007. All three deficit findings move negative TOGETHER, MCL the largest negative on the table, against a +/-0.0315 band.

So band_dense's +0.0025 is a TRADE (centre bought with collaterals and cruciates), and the champion family is dense - it holds the losing side of exactly the three findings the gap resolves as its deficit. band_wide is a diversity seat with a mechanism: worse on the mean, better where the roster is measurably weak.

WHY IT IS NOT A SLOT. band_wide_s2026 is _s2026 and the champion's seats are _cf/_ff; swapping across fit regimes gives back the +0.004 the regime is worth, more than this axis could pay. It needs a TWIN trained at the champion's regime.

DISCOUNT, pre-registered: every seat permutation on this board prices between -0.004 and +0.001 (see 2026-08-27_every-no-card-axis-is-priced-and-flat.md). What is new is the selection RULE - a resolved per-finding deficit rather than the offline mean - which is a different die, not a better roll. Three same-sign moves on three findings named in advance by an unrelated measurement is a pattern; no single one of them is marked.

See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-supervision-gap-is-four-findings-not-an-average.md.
notes:
REFUTED ON ITS CONTENT, 2026-08-27, by the instrument this bead asked for. kneemri/evaluation/competence_axis.py reads 105 members x 12 findings over 909 shared studies: double-centred (by finding, then by member), first component against a column-shuffle null.

READING. Member QUALITY takes 81.7% of the spread and is removed before the axis is read. Component 1 then takes 45.9% of what is left against a null bar of 27.7% - so a shared axis exists, but it carries about 8% of the total member-to-member variation.

The axis is NOT centre-vs-periphery. Loadings: Synovitis -0.451, Effusion -0.388, Medial OA -0.198, Lateral OA -0.181 at one end; Baker's +0.649, Fracture +0.316, Medial Meniscus +0.215 at the other. A fluid-and-inflammation axis. The centre/periphery hypothesis in this bead was generalised from ONE controlled pair (band_wide vs band_dense) and 105 members disagree with it.

WHAT REPLACES IT, and it is better. The flat seat search is explained by the 81.7%: a pool that differs almost entirely by uniform quality has nothing to trade, so no selector can extract diversity from it. And the three resolved deficit findings - ACL, MCL, Lateral Meniscus - load +0.014, +0.053, +0.028 (near zero) while their own spreads read 0.0141, 0.0165, 0.0183 (ordinary, above Contusion's 0.0097). They vary across members as much as anything else, ORTHOGONALLY to the shared axis. Idiosyncratic variation is exactly what a flat rank-average destroys and exactly what a targeted selector could keep.

Full reading: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_the-pool-is-82-percent-one-number.md

title: The vote rule is the one ensemble axis never measured offline, and the champion disagrees with the ruler
description:
Every offline reading in experiments/README.md was taken under RankAverage - the Pool.vote default - while the shipped champion kneemri-calibsix combines with LogitAverage, and has since kneemri-vote. So the ruler and the entry have never agreed on the combination rule, which makes every offline->board transfer this project quotes carry an unmeasured rule change on top of the population mismatch already recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-27_seat-count-is-flat-both-rulers.md.

record_mix --vote now offers rank, logit and median (MedianLogit has never been submitted at all). The axis is zero-training and zero-upload: it changes one line of the kernel's combine step, not a member. Price all three on the largest agreeing pool with LabelScores.paired_mean_interval, which can now bound a named pair on the competition metric directly.

Caveat that bounds what it buys: the offline pool is the _s2026 family and the champion is _cf/_ff, so a rule result transfers only if the rule is family-independent. A combination rule is far more plausibly family-independent than member identity is, but that is an argument, not a measurement.
notes:
CORRECTED before any compute was spent. The central claim - that the vote axis was never measured - is WRONG, and comp/board.jsonl says so in two CONTROLLED single-variable pairs:

  2 seats:  efficient_v4 0.919 -> vote_v2    0.919  ( 0.000)
  6 seats:  dark6_v1     0.937 -> votefit_v1 0.938  (+0.001)

Both are the same six/two members with LogitAverage swapped for RankAverage and every other variable held. Rank->logit buys zero to one board tick, at or under BOARD_RESOLVABLE = 0.0015, and the champion already serves the better side of it. So the offline ruler defaulting to RankAverage while the champion serves LogitAverage is a documentation discrepancy worth one line, NOT the unmeasured axis this bead claimed, and it does not license a submission slot.

What survives, much smaller: MedianLogit has never been submitted and appears in no board row, so it is the only untried member of VOTE_RULES. Given the two measured points bracket the axis at ~0.001, its prior is a null too - price it offline on the pool with paired_mean_interval if the pool is being read anyway, never as a slot of its own.

Third false start this session caught by reading the record before spending. The first two were the fit-regime 'discovery' and the seat-count transfer; the rule that catches them is CLAUDE.md's read-the-ledger-and-the-board-first, and it has now paid three times in one window.

title: smallseat: swap lr4e-5_ws_ff for small_batch6_ff, the quality-positive twin of tonight's bet
description:
The natural next entry after kneemri-resseat, and the counter-bet to it. Both replace the champion's lr4e-5_ws_ff seat; they differ in which axis they move.

resseat (fired 2026-08-26) enters res392_ws_s2026: quality-NEUTRAL by construction (twin solos 0.8523 vs the outgoing 0.8525) so only the decode path changes, but it introduces a SECOND fold-0 seat into a six that otherwise runs full-fit.

smallseat would enter small_batch6_ff: quality-POSITIVE by +0.0073 on the fold-0 twins (small_batch6_s2026 0.8598 vs lr4e-5_ws_s2026 0.8525, the second-best solo this project owns), and it keeps every seat full-fit, so the fold-0 confound resseat carries is absent. Cost: no decode-path diversity — both read 336 px — and small_batch6 measured only +0.0005 as an EIGHTH seat, which is not the same measurement as a replacement.

Both checkpoints are already mounted (comp/members.roster lines 184 and 379). No training, no packaging, one slot.

Why it matters more than a knob: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-26_our-model-is-past-its-teacher.md and research/2026-08-26_rival_single_models_and_the_label_bottleneck.md both say the gap is MEMBER QUALITY, not ensembling — rivals self-report SINGLE models at 0.926-0.942 against our six-member 0.939. resseat bets on diversity; smallseat bets on quality. Firing both, one slot each, is the only way this project has to separate the two axes on the board, and the offline ruler cannot (eleven variations spanned 0.8687-0.8705 against a 0.0062 noise floor).

Do NOT fire without asking — knee-pubw holds the first slot of the day.
notes:
DEFECTIVE AGAINST THE CURRENT CHAMPION, found 2026-08-27 19:45Z without spending anything.

Two independent reasons, either sufficient.

(1) THE SEAT IT WOULD ENTER IS UNCALIBRATED. This bead was written 2026-08-26 against the blendseat champion, whose seats were _ff. The champion is now calibsix, whose six seats are _cf/_ff and which got its 0.938->0.941 climb from --calibrated-targets on every seat at once. comp/members.roster carries small_batch6 as _s2026 and _ff only - there is no small_batch6_cf. So the swap would put the one uncalibrated seat into a fully calibrated six, undoing the single treatment this project has measured positive three times, to gain a quality delta measured on the UNCALIBRATED fold-0 twins (+0.0073).

(2) THE AXIS CLOSED WHILE THE BEAD SAT. Seven board entries now span 0.937-0.941 across seven seatings: honest12 0.937 (12), resseat 0.938 (6), blendseat 0.939 (7), blendthree 0.939 (7), pixgroup 0.940 (8), calibsix 0.941 (6), calibmix 0.941 (11 names / 5 recipes). Against the 0.0053 Hanley-McNeil floor that is one number read seven times. The bead's own framing - 'firing both, one slot each, is the only way to separate diversity from quality on the board' - was right when two seatings had been read; resseat fired and read 0.938, and the five entries after it closed the question the counter-bet was meant to answer.

NOT A CLEAN KILL OF THE MEMBER. small_batch6_s2026 is still the second-best solo we own (0.8598; calib_dense_hold_s2026 0.8634 leads - the roster comment claiming small_batch6 was best was stale and is corrected in this commit). What died is this SWAP at this champion, not the member and not the quality-over-diversity thesis, which pixgroup and honest12 independently support.

WHAT WOULD REVIVE IT: a calibrated full-fit twin (small_batch6_cf), which is a card question and cheap - it is one flag on an existing recipe. Rolled into knee-wbwq's lane rather than kept as a slot plan. Slot 5 goes to knee-d500 instead.

title: crop_alignment.dump writes spread, not the centroid offset magnitude — the clipping claim is unmeasurable
description:
tissue224 (knee-2zbi) came out flat and refuted the COMMON-MODE mechanism, leaving CLIPPING alive but untested. Clipping is a subpopulation claim: only studies whose tissue centroid sits further than the ~15 mm margin from the image centre actually lose anatomy to the image-centred crop, which crop_coverage puts at roughly the worst tenth (p90 offset 18 mm, max 32 mm). An effect confined to 10% of the corpus moves the mean by about a tenth of its own size, so it produces a flat mean BY CONSTRUCTION and can only be read in an offset split.

THE GAP: crop_alignment.dump() writes `spread` — the disagreement BETWEEN slots — not the centroid's offset MAGNITUDE from the image centre. Those are different quantities: a study whose joint sits 25 mm off-centre in every slot identically has a large offset and zero spread. So the decile the split needs does not exist on disk.

THE FIX IS A DUMP COLUMN, NOT A FIT. tissue224 and native224 both read the SAME studies and both kept per-study predictions, so the split is a re-read of two existing checkpoints once the offset column exists. No card time for the fit; the dump is CPU.

PRICE HONESTLY BEFORE ANYONE SPENDS ON IT: the mean is flat and the surviving claim is worth at most a tenth of its own size on the corpus mean, i.e. below the 0.0062 floor even if the mechanism is entirely real. This is an INSTRUMENT that closes the crop/centre axis cleanly, never an improvement. It is P3 for exactly that reason. Do not promote it on the strength of the mechanism being sound.

title: The public Synovitis hole is not our hole - RadImageNet declined, and the read is evidence our reader is ahead of the floor
description:
Forum topic 737566, posted 2026-08-26 0442z, four hours before this was written: 'Why everyone's Synovitis AUC is stuck around 0.6-0.7 (its not your model)'. The poster measures 0.62-0.72 on Synovitis across FOUR architectures, finds only ~16% of the 4407 reports mention any synovitis term across the nine report languages, prices the public label tables at ~0.79 AUC on Synovitis against ~0.99 on ACL, and reports that a RadImageNet-pretrained encoder took them to 0.78 where every ImageNet-pretrained model sat at 0.62-0.72.

TWO THINGS, AND THEY POINT OPPOSITE WAYS.

(1) The DIAGNOSIS confirms ours, by a route that shares no denominator. Our unsure_cost run on the 58 annotated studies found Synovitis is the most-unsure finding by a distance (41 of 58 cells UNK, 34.1% of those actually positive, the only POSITIVE taught error at +0.061), and reader_disagreement over 4406 studies ranked Synovitis top of twelve on cross-reader spread (0.2995, split rate 0.175). They counted report TERMS across nine languages; we counted reader VERDICTS and cross-reader SPREAD. Three instruments, same finding: the reports genuinely do not say much about synovitis. That is now externally confirmed and can be quoted as such.

(2) The PRESCRIPTION does not transfer, because we do not have their number. experiments/README.md:473 puts our Synovitis holdout AUC at 0.8456/0.8764 depending on the member. That is not 0.62-0.72; it is above our corpus mean and roughly a fifth of a point above the ceiling they reached WITH RadImageNet. Our two worst labels are MCL 0.7745 and Fracture 0.7922 — Synovitis is not close to the bottom for us.

CONSEQUENCE: DECLINE the RadImageNet member on this evidence. It is offered as a fix for a hole we do not have, and the price would be a fresh encoder family plus a pretrain-weights dependency for a label already 0.10-0.15 above the number that motivates it. Revisit only if a medically-pretrained encoder is argued on the FOCAL findings (knee-lxi1) instead, where our deficit actually lives — and note that is a different argument needing its own evidence, not this thread's.

SECOND CONSEQUENCE, and it is the more useful one: this is the first outside measurement of the PUBLIC label floor on a finding where we can compare directly. Their tables read Synovitis at ~0.79 against the annotated studies; ours trains a model to 0.85-0.88 on it. Our reader pipeline is ahead of the public floor on the hardest-to-read finding in the set, which is a concrete answer to 'are the public tables better than ours' — on this finding, no. Related: table_separation (recomposing the blend is not a lever, every recipe inside the gold ruler's +/-0.008), knee-1ww2 and knee-uahl (both closed 2026-08-26).

title: STUDY_RESAMPLES=1000 has never had the measurement RESAMPLES=1500 got
description:
core/bootstrap.py now holds two draw counts. RESAMPLES=1500 is MEASURED: its docstring records that at 300 draws the Lateral Meniscus lower bound moved 0.0063 across three resample seeds - enough to flip whether it cleared zero - and that 1500 brings that spread to 0.0015. STUDY_RESAMPLES=1000, the count behind the paired 0.0062 floor, the +/-0.0106 absolute band and every per-label interval in the ledger, has had no such check. Its old docstring asserted 1000 was 'stable to about a thousandth', which is the SAME claim 300 made and lost.

The test is cheap and spends no card: run paired_interval and mean_interval at three different resample SEEDS on a recorded pair of arms and read how far each bound moves. If the Monte Carlo spread is near 0.0015 the count is fine and the docstring can say so with evidence. If it is nearer 0.006 then the floor this project quotes everywhere is partly a seed.

DO NOT simply raise it to 1500. Changing the count moves every interval already published in experiments/README.md and interpretations/, so the measurement comes first and any change is a separate, deliberate re-read of those numbers.

title: CoPAS correlation-mining head: inter-label co-occurrence term, the surviving half of knee-0a9c
description:
Split out of knee-0a9c when its cross-plane-attention half was killed on the paper's own supplementary table (the CPA row is built on the no-crop baseline, so no clean step exists, and the whole stack over the ROI-cropped baseline is +0.031 against +0.038 for the two clean modules - the crop and the attention substitute for each other, and we already crop to 130mm).

WHAT SURVIVES. Correlation mining (CRM) is a clean +0.013 step in their Table 10: a 12-channel conv plus SENet-style attention over the per-label logits, modelling which abnormalities co-occur. Our head emits twelve INDEPENDENT logits with no inter-label term, and knee MRI has strong real co-occurrence (ACL tear / bone contusion / effusion is the classic triad).

WHY IT IS CHEAP. Head-only: it changes the readout, not the input distribution, so a member can be WARM-STARTED rather than refit. And the co-occurrence structure can be read off the 4,349 report-derived targets rather than the 58 annotations, so it is not blocked behind the 58-study ruler the rest of the label-side family sits behind.

WHY IT IS P3 ANYWAY. +0.013 is on THEIR corpus and THEIR ruler, before any transfer to ours, and it is under the 1.5 pct house bar. Directional at best. Take it only if something else opens the head anyway - never as its own arm, and never as a reason to spend a submission slot.

Source table and arithmetic: research/2026-08-24_published_knee_mri_multilabel_sota.md.

title: Param-group dict {lr, params} is built at three sites — a dataclass with one home
description:
devtools.cohesion.data_clumps (advisory, run 2026-08-26 00:29Z over core + kneemri) reports the dict
key-set {lr, params} constructed at three sites:

  kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py:215
  kneemri/models/encoder_surgery.py:231
  kneemri/models/model.py:472

This is the optimiser param-group shape. Three hand-built dicts of the same shape is the Fowler clump the
detector is for, and the house rule is one home per thing. A small frozen dataclass beside its PRODUCER
(encoder_surgery, which builds two of the three) with model.py importing it removes the third hand-build
and makes the shape checkable rather than conventional.

SIZE, STATED HONESTLY: this is a handful of lines and touches no behaviour. It is lane-2 bug-surface work,
not a score lever, and it is filed at P3 so it is not confused with one. The reason to do it at all is that
param groups are exactly where a silent lr mistake hides -- a wrong key or a missing group fails no gate
and shows up as a training curve nobody can explain.

DO NOT bundle this with a behaviour change. If the refactor is done, the printed recipe and the first
epoch's loss must be identical to a run from before it, and that equality IS the test.

Other advisory findings from the same sweep, recorded so the audit is not paid for twice and thrown away:
  - repeated key-set {bg, de, el, en, es, hr, nl, tr} at core/data/labels/report_language.py:41 and :54 --
    a language table written twice; lower value, same shape of fix.

title: KneeCoT is DISALLOWED as external data — host ruled, do not spend on it
description:
Discussion 734109, read live 2026-08-25. Host reply, quoted:

  'After deliberation, we decided to not allow the use of KneeCoT dataset due to the required data agreement with dataset institution. In our interpretation of the rules, this can make the playing field uneven for participants who can complete the formal agreement to seek approval compared those that cannot... For now, the KneeCoT dataset is not allowed in this competition.'

The dataset is gated CC BY-NC 4.0 at huggingface.co/datasets/YiHui0124/KneeCoT and was never in our plan, but the RULING generalises and that is why this is written down: the bar is not licence permissiveness, it is EQUAL AND REASONABLE ACCESSIBILITY. A corpus behind a formal institutional agreement is out even when the agreement is grantable.

READ IT ONTO WHAT WE DO HOLD:
  * MRNet (knee-dnhd) — Stanford RUA, click-through, no institutional review. Reasonably accessible; survives this ruling on its face.
  * fastMRI+ (knee-3oy8) — annotations MIT and free, but the IMAGES need the NYU data sharing agreement. That is the same shape as KneeCoT and is now a SHIPPING risk, not merely a download chore. Ask the host in-thread before building on the images; the annotations alone are fine.
  * Rijeka — public, already merged.

The host also left the door open ('if the situation changes... we may change our stance'), so this is a ruling to re-read before the deadline, not a permanent fact.

title: CoPAS (Nat Commun 2024) fuses planes at FEATURE level; we fuse at context level only
description:
Frontier gather, 2026-08-25, no GPU spent. CoPAS - 'Learning co-plane attention across MRI sequences for diagnosing twelve types of knee abnormalities', Nat Commun 15 (2024), HKUST, PMC11368947. Same task shape as ours: twelve knee abnormalities, multi-sequence MRI, 1748 subjects. Their headline is 0.812 mean AUC on THEIR OWN dataset and is NOT comparable to our 0.938 board or our holdout - different corpus, different label definitions, different denominator. Read for MECHANISM only.

WHAT THEY DO THAT WE ALREADY DO, and arguably better: 'each knee abnormality has its optimal diagnostic MRI plane' is their motivating claim, and they cash it as a plane-aware matrix built by element-wise multiplication of three branch predictions. SlotHead already gives every diagnosis its own query over the acquisition slots AND seeds those logits with an anatomical prior (slot_head.py:60-72). That axis is closed here; do not re-open it.

THE GENUINE GAP - WHERE THE FUSION HAPPENS. CoPAS enhances one plane's FEATURES using another plane's features: the main plane supplies queries, synthetic volumes rotated into the orthogonal orientations supply keys and values, through weight-shared ResNet3D-18 encoders, before any readout. Our slot embeddings are each computed independently by the encoder and only ever meet inside SlotHead's attention - which combines CONTEXTS, not features. No slot's representation is ever conditioned on another slot's. through_plane is not this: it gives a slice its two DEPTH neighbours in the RGB channels (model.py:85-89), which is within-plane, not cross-plane.

Note their reason for SYNTHESISING the orthogonal volumes does not apply to us. They rotate the high-res PDW volume because they want its in-plane detail expressed in other orientations; our slots are the planes the study actually acquired, so we already hold real orthogonal information and would attend across acquired slots rather than rendered ones. That makes our version CHEAPER than theirs, not more expensive - no rotation, no synthetic volume, no second encoder pass.

SECOND, CHEAPER LEVER - inter-label correlation. Their correlation mining module (12-channel conv + SENet-style attention over the plane-aware matrix) explicitly models which abnormalities co-occur. Our head emits twelve INDEPENDENT logits with no inter-label term, and knee MRI has strong real co-occurrence (ACL tear with bone contusion with effusion is the classic triad). Head-only, no encoder change. It is a LABEL-side mechanism, which interpretations/kneemri record as blocked behind the 58-study ruler - but co-occurrence structure can be read off the 4,349 report-derived targets rather than the 58 annotations, which is what makes it worth pricing separately from the rest of that family.

NEITHER IS PRICED YET and neither is armed - the card is biohub's and the owner has ruled out GPU work. Cross-plane feature attention is an ENCODER change and therefore a full refit of every member that would use it, so it must be priced as wall-clock-per-member before anything is queued. The correlation head is cheap enough to warm-start, since it changes the readout and not the input distribution. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11368947/ and https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-51888-4
notes:
PRICED AND LARGELY KILLED, 2026-08-25, from the supplementary ablation (Table 10) rather than the article - the article defers it and never shows it.

The cross-plane-attention lever this bead filed CANNOT be priced at all from their own table: the paper builds the CPA row on the NO-crop baseline while comparing its multitask row against the CROPPED one, so every subtraction reaching CPA also crosses the ROI crop or the single-to-multitask change. There is no clean CPA step. The +0.049 that has been quoted here twice is (iv)-(ii), which skips (iii).

What the table does say, and it goes against this bead: the two CLEAN steps sum to +0.038 (CSA +0.025, CRM +0.013) while the WHOLE stack over the ROI-cropped baseline is +0.031. The crop and the attention modules substitute for each other, which their own text states outright - 'cropping along ROI can align the spatial position across sequences'. We already crop to 130mm, so we sit at their row (i) and the residual for cross-plane feature attention is near zero BY THEIR NUMBERS. An encoder change plus a refit of every member for that is a bad ratio; do not queue it.

Note the reasoning correction in both directions: the earlier kill ('our slots are already orthogonal within 87.3 deg, so it does not transfer') was also invalid. Orthogonality is the PRECONDITION their module operates on, not a substitute for it. The table kills this, the geometry does not.

SURVIVING HALF, kept and downgraded: correlation mining (CRM) is a clean +0.013 step, head-only, warm-startable, readable off the 4349 report-derived targets. Under the 1.5 pct bar on their own ruler before any corpus transfer, so it is directional at best - worth taking only if something else opens the head anyway, never as its own arm.

Full table and the arithmetic: research/2026-08-24_published_knee_mri_multilabel_sota.md, which had already argued the plane axis was spent on 2026-08-24. This bead re-opened it a day later without reading that note - the failure CLAUDE.md names.
close_reason:
Priced and closed 2026-08-25/26. The cross-plane feature-attention half - the lever this bead was filed for - cannot be priced from CoPAS's own supplementary Table 10 at all: the CPA row is built on the NO-crop baseline while the multitask row is compared against the CROPPED one, so every subtraction reaching CPA also crosses the ROI crop. There is no clean CPA step, and the +0.049 quoted here twice is (iv)-(ii), which skips (iii). What the table does say goes against the bead: the two clean steps sum to +0.038 while the whole stack over the ROI-cropped baseline is +0.031, so the crop and the attention modules substitute for each other - their own text says cropping along ROI aligns spatial position across sequences. We already crop to 130mm, so we sit at their row (i) and the residual is near zero by their numbers. An encoder change plus a refit of every member for that is a bad ratio.

The surviving half - correlation mining, +0.013, head-only, warm-startable - is re-filed as knee-c4x7 so closing this does not lose it.

Recorded for a future re-test: the EARLIER kill of this axis (our slots are already orthogonal within 87.3 deg) was also invalid reasoning. Orthogonality is the precondition their module operates on, not a substitute for it. The table kills this lever; the geometry does not. If a corpus ever gives us planes their crop cannot align, this is re-openable.

title: Code-reduction axis measured across the whole tree: nothing to reduce
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-25, run under the standing refactor instruction (lower the amount of code, make it easier to keep in order). Three instruments over kneemri + core, and all three come back clean. Recording it so the next session does not pay for the same scan.

DUPLICATION. jscpd at min-tokens 35 - BELOW the gate own 50 - over 160 files, 29918 lines: 25 clones, 167 duplicated lines, 0.56 percent. Read every clone. They fall into three kinds and none is a reduction target:

  IMPORT BLOCKS. band_coverage/crop_coverage/crop_alignment/crop_laterality share 5 clones that are
  literally the same import run plus the logger line. Deduplicating imports is not a thing.

  STRATEGY SIBLINGS. token_pooling has two self-clones which are the @override decorator, the
  signature and the patch-slice line shared by ClassAndPatchMeanAndTail and ClassAndSidedMean. That
  boilerplate IS the strategy pattern the house style mandates; collapsing it collapses the pattern.

  THE CORPUS-WALKING CLI PREAMBLE. slot_ties and tie_divergence share three clones, the largest single
  one in the tree at 92 tokens, and they are the same idiom: --split/--workers/--studies, rooted().raw(),
  StudyCache.planes_of, sorted directories, an optional head, then a ProcessPoolExecutor over
  ((directory, planes) for directory in directories). Twelve modules use a pool and ten of them are in
  corpus. This is the ONE case with a real shared responsibility, and it is still not worth a type: only
  three modules call planes_of at all, and the rest differ in what the worker returns and how the flags
  are named. A CorpusScan value type would buy ~15 lines and pay an import edge in ten modules.

COHESION. cohesion.lcom reports 44 low-cohesion classes, 41 of them at LCOM4=2 which is one method
touching one other field - noise. The one real outlier, TrainingOptions at 6, is correct by design and
now says so in its own docstring (commit 19da8be): the fields are flat because parse builds the
dataclass from argparse dest names, so the grouping is properties over disjoint scalars, which is
exactly what LCOM4 counts as six responsibilities.

DATA CLUMPS. One, {batch, start, width} across study_cache and window_reader, already argued as
deliberate at window_reader.py:37.

COMPLEXITY. radon ranks 15 at the top but the fixed gate is ruff C901 at >10, and the two count
differently by design - ruff counts branches, radon also counts boolean operators and comprehensions.
No pyproject max-complexity override, so ruff is at its default 10 and passes. Nothing is over.

FILE SIZE. Largest module is arm_check at 701 against file_max 750; see knee-0ox0, whose own
measurement already refused the split.

WHAT THIS MEANS. The tree is not carrying redundant code. If the amount of code is to come down it has
to come down by deleting a CAPABILITY nobody uses, not by deduplicating - and the only such candidate on
record is knee-xh96 layer three, the 17 board-less kernels, which is the owner call.

title: arm_check is 701 of 750 lines and holds three responsibilities behind one class
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-25. kneemri/experiments/arm_check.py is 701 lines against the [tool.structure] file_max of 750 - 3.5x the next-largest module in the package (queue_check at 280) and the only one anywhere near the ceiling. It passes every gate today, including god-file, so this is pressure and not a failure.

ArmCheck itself is ~480 lines over ~20 methods, and reading them they fall into three groups that do not talk to each other much:

  READING what the arms declare - _environment, queued, invocations, _printed, selected, _parsed,
  carriage_returns. Runs the shell arms under git-bash, captures the invocation each prints, parses
  the flags into TrainingOptions.

  JUDGING what was declared - refused, mismatched, _flag_values, _same, unpriced, _descriptions,
  prices, verdicts, overstated, unstated. Every one of these takes an invocations mapping and
  returns complaints; none of them needs to know how the invocation was obtained.

  SMOKING - readings, uncached, decode_smoke_caches, plus the ArmReading dataclass.

THE PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN THE TREE: arm_smoke.py exists as a 195-line module carved out of exactly
this file, so the seam has been cut once before and held.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, which is why this is a bead and not a commit: LCOM reports the class cohesive,
and a split that just relocates methods LOWERS no code - it buys a smaller file and pays an import
edge plus a second mirror test file. The standing instruction is to lower the amount of code, not to
redistribute it. So the split is only worth doing if the READING half can take the shell-running
machinery with it whole (GIT_BASH, TIMEOUT_SECONDS, STUB, SHELLS, _environment, _printed) and leave
the judging half a pure function of a mapping - that is a genuine interface, and it would also make
the judging half testable without git-bash on the machine.

NEXT STEP is measurement, not editing: count what actually moves and what each half would still
import from the other. If the two halves share more than the ArmVerdict type, leave it alone.
notes:
MEASURED the same day, and the measurement REFUSES the split on this bead's own stated criterion.

Per-method audit of what each half reaches for through self:

  verdicts (JUDGE, 76 lines) calls carriage_returns (READ).
  refused, overstated (JUDGE) and readings (SMOKE) all call _parsed (READ).
  self.headers is read by both halves - _printed and queued on the READ side, mismatched, prices and
  verdicts on the JUDGE side.

So the two halves share three things, not one type: the flag parser, the CR scan, and the headers
path. A split would either duplicate _parsed, or leave the JUDGE module importing the READ module for
it - which is the import edge this bead already said is the cost, bought for nothing. LEAVE THE CLASS
WHOLE. Its stated pre-condition ('only if the judging half becomes a pure function of a mapping') is
measurably false.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT DID FIND, and the reason this stays open at P3 rather than closing: SIX methods
touch no self at all - selected, _parsed, _flag_values, _same, unpriced, _descriptions, unstated (and
_parsed only fails the count because it is called as self._parsed). That is ~105 lines of pure
function sitting inside a class as staticmethods. Moving them to module level, or onto a small value
type that owns a flag string, takes the CLASS well under 400 lines and costs no import edge, because
they already depend on nothing. It shrinks the file honestly; it does not lower the amount of code, so
it is worth doing only alongside a change that already touches them.

title: uv cannot build the devtools git dep while the git-shim blocks reset --hard
description:
Every devtools_ref bump (copier update) makes uv re-fetch sdlc-devtools from git. uv builds a git dependency by checking it out into its own cache and running 'git reset --hard <sha>'. The global git-shim blocks reset-hard, so 'nox -s gates' dies at the first devtools-using session with:

  BLOCKED by git-shim [reset-hard] in global scope

The failure names the shim but reads like a repo problem, and it lands mid-gate-run (after ruff/vulture/import-linter pass), so it is easy to misread as a gate regression. It is neither - the target is uv's cache checkout, never this tree.

WORKAROUND that works: install the dep once with the shim in log-only mode, then run gates normally (the build is cached, no further git op):

  GIT_SHIM_LOG_ONLY=1 uv sync --extra dev --extra devtools
  uvx nox -s gates

Log-only rather than GIT_SHIM=off so the operation is still recorded. Decide whether this belongs in the shim as a scoped allowance for uv's cache path, or in the repo README as the documented step after a copier update.
notes:
Hit for real 2026-08-25 during the v1.28.0 update; workaround applied and it works.
DECIDED 2026-08-25: documented in the repo, not fixed in the shim. The scoped allowance is the better permanent fix and loses no protection - uv only ever resets its OWN cache checkout, never a work tree - but the shim is machine-global and lives outside this repo, so changing it is the owner s call rather than something a session edits blind. What landed: the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md Scaffolding section now carries the mechanism, the misreading it causes (dies mid-gate-run after three gates print clean, so it reads as a gate regression), and the two-command workaround with GIT_SHIM_LOG_ONLY=1 rather than GIT_SHIM=off so the op is still recorded. Closing as documented; re-open only to take the shim-side allowance.

title: run_setup's two exclusivity guards are one loop written twice
description:
_check_margin_alone and _check_dissent_alone differ only in which flag is being refused, its value, the flags it conflicts with, and the trailing clause of the message. The body of each is the same three steps: name the given conflicts, and if any, raise a ValueError spelling the flag, its value, the conflicting flags with their values, and why they do not compose.

THE MOVE: extract _check_alone(flag, value, conflicts, reason) holding the loop and the raise. Both callers keep their own method and their own docstring - those carry the MECHANISM (why the margin objective replaces cross-entropy, why the dissent term is the label ranking at a re-weighted pair mass) and are the reason the guards exist at all; only the plumbing is shared. conflicts is typed Mapping[str, float], not dict, because a literal mixing int and float values is not assignable to an invariant dict.

WHY IT MATTERS beyond line count: a third exclusive objective flag is the obvious next one, and today that means a third copy of the loop. The message FORMAT is the thing that would drift - one guard listing values and another not, one saying 'is not composed with' and another 'cannot be used with', in errors a reader hits at queue time with the card already held.
close_reason:
Tried it and MEASURED it: run_setup.py went 393 -> 403. The extraction is a net LOSS of ten lines and I am closing it as not worth doing, not deferring it.

THE ARITHMETIC, so nobody re-opens this on the same reasoning I did. The shared body is five lines standing twice, so ten lines are available. Against that: the helper signature and its four-line body, a docstring that has to say why a private helper exists at all, and two call sites that grow because the conflicts dict and the trailing message clause become spelled-out arguments where they used to be locals. The duplication is real and the removal still costs more than it saves - two instances of a five-line loop is under the size where extraction pays.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: a THIRD exclusive objective flag. At three instances the arithmetic flips, and the drift risk the original description named (one guard listing values and another not, in an error read at queue time) becomes worth paying for. Until then the two guards stay as they are.

Filed and closed inside one sitting under a refactoring directive that says lower the amount of code; a change that adds ten lines does not clear that bar on a P3 drift risk.

title: batch/start/width travel together through study_cache and window_reader as three loose ints
description:
AUDIT (2026-08-25, cohesion.data_clumps): the triple `batch, start, width` is passed as three separate arguments across core/data/corpus/study_cache.py and core/data/corpus/window_reader.py. Three ints in a fixed order is the shape that lets a caller swap start and width silently - both are non-negative, both index the same axis, and neither a type checker nor a shape contract can see the swap.

DESIGN: one frozen value beside its producer (a window's placement in a cached array), constructed once where the arithmetic that derives it lives, passed whole thereafter.

CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT: no call site passes the three as positionals any more, the existing window_reader tests pass unchanged, and a swapped-argument test that used to read as a valid call no longer type-checks or no longer constructs.
close_reason: Fixed by keyword-only start/width rather than the value object: window_reader.WindowReader.read, MappedReader.read, FileReader.read/_fill, study_cache.CachedCorpus.window. The reader's own docstring already argued against a request type (nothing stores/returns/decides from the triple) and the call-site audit backed it - two read() sites, four window() sites. Keyword-only kills the swap-silence, which was the whole risk, and adds no type on the inner loop. Constraint met: pyrefly rejects a positional extent (it found comp/witness_check.py, a caller outside core/kneemri/tests the greps missed), a negative test asserts TypeError, and the pre-existing window_reader/prefetch/study_cache tests pass unchanged. 195 tests green, uvx nox -s gates successful. Commit e39ec3d.

title: Sixteen vulture findings sit under the enforced gate's confidence floor
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 with vulture 2.16 at --min-confidence 60 over kneemri/ + core/ (the gate itself
runs at the same floor, so these are AT the boundary, not below it):

  oof_oracle.py:71,72,83   unused variables ids / pred / oof
  switch_coverage.py:82    unused method unaccounted
  members.py:47,116        unused variables img / annot
  members.py:431           unused property pixel_group
  kernel_run.py:34         unused class KernelRun
  kit_wheels.py:30         unused class KitWheels
  backbone.py:30,31        unused DINOV2 / DINOV3
  member_record.py:19,33   unused RECORDED_AS / NOT_IN_CONFIG
  run_metrics.py:78,79     unused vram_peak_gb / vram_alloc_gb
