AT LEAST THREE ARE FALSE, and knowing which is the point of the task rather than a reason to skip it:
KernelRun and KitWheels are instantiated by the Kaggle kernel scripts under comp/kernels/, which live
outside the analysed packages, so vulture cannot see the call. The vram_* fields are written into a JSON
record and read back by tooling. DINOV2/DINOV3 are almost certainly string constants selected by name.

Triage each into: genuinely dead (delete), read across a package boundary vulture cannot follow (add to
the whitelist WITH the reason), or a real unused binding masking a bug (oof_oracle's three unpacked-and-
discarded names are the ones to read first - a discarded 'pred' in an oracle is worth a look before it is
worth a deletion).
notes:
TRIAGED THREE OF SIXTEEN, 2026-08-25, by reading rather than by deleting:

oof_oracle.py:71,72,83 are NOT discarded bindings and there is no bug behind them. They are TypedDict
FIELDS - OutOfFoldBlock declares ids/pred and PublishedPayload declares oof - so vulture is reporting a
declared key it cannot see indexed. Whitelist with that reason; do not delete, since deleting them
deletes the only written record of the published checkpoint's layout.

kernel_run.py:34 KernelRun and kit_wheels.py:30 KitWheels stay for the reason already stated: their only
callers live in comp/kernels/*, outside the analysed packages.

That leaves eleven to triage. The remaining ones worth reading before whitelisting are backbone.py's
DINOV2/DINOV3 (string constants selected by name, so a rename would be silent) and members.py:431
pixel_group (a property on the shipping Member - if nothing reads it, a member's pixel grouping is
recorded and never applied).
close_reason: Triaged all sixteen in ad979d0. ONE was real: DINOV2/DINOV3 had no readers because six encoder rows in backbone.py wrote family="dinov2"/"dinov3" as literals while CONVNEXT/VJEPA2/RADDINO all used their constants — a rename would have silently missed the six. They now use the constants. The other thirteen are whitelisted in [tool.vulture] ignore_names WITH the path vulture cannot follow, in three groups: TypedDict/dataclass fields read by subscript (ids, pred, oof, img, annot, vram_peak_gb, vram_alloc_gb); symbols whose only callers are outside the scanned packages, in comp/ (pixel_group is read by comp/verify_members.py:81, KernelRun and KitWheels by comp/kernels/*); and the four written-off sets a unit gate differences against TrainingOptions to keep a wire total (RECORDED_AS, NOT_IN_CONFIG, NOT_A_SWITCH, unaccounted) — being unused in the package IS what those are for. members.py:431 pixel_group was the one flagged as worth reading first for a real bug and it is not one: verify_members groups a package by it. FOLLOW-UP: the tree now reports nothing at min-confidence 60, so the ENFORCED vulture run should graduate from 80 to 60 — but that invocation lives in the template-owned noxfile, so it belongs upstream in sdlc-scaffold.

title: Buy the denominator: score our own members on all 58 annotated studies, not 13
description:
The only ruler that measures the truth the competition scores (radiologist annotations) covers 58 studies, giving per-label 95% halfwidths of 0.14-0.21 - about half the entire spread across the twelve findings. The only ruler large enough to rank findings (our holdout) scores LLM-read report labels, a proxy that agrees with the radiologist on ~65% of positives. So no measurement this project owns is both the right truth and large enough to resolve a per-label gap, and that single missing denominator has now surfaced as three separate puzzles: the crop80 per-label gate, the 2026-08-20 per-label re-read, and the retracted per-label section of 2026-08-24_the_goal_priced_against_the_inventory.md.

See interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_no_denominator_resolves_a_per_label_deficit.md.

Why our members cannot use the 58 today: they are fitted with the annotated studies upweighted, so scoring them against those annotations scores their own training data. supervision_gap works around it by scoring PUBLISHED members instead - somebody else's models, which is why its table cannot be quoted as ours.

The infrastructure is already partly built and that is what makes this cheap. Two commits already landed: 'a member can now be fitted without the 58 radiologist annotations' and '13 of 58 annotated studies are held out'. So the current path measures on 13 studies. Fitting a member that excludes ALL 58 makes every one of them scorable and roughly quadruples the annotation denominator, taking a per-label halfwidth from about 0.30 (n=13) to about 0.15 (n=58).

Note honestly what that does and does not buy. It does NOT make per-label targeting sound - 0.15 is still half the observed spread. It buys the ability to score OUR members on the competition's own truth at all, which today we cannot do, and it is the prerequisite for any per-label decision rather than the decision itself. Price it as instrument work.

Cost is one member fit, and the axis is not seeds or folds - it is a held-out annotation set, which is a different object.

Open question worth answering before spending the card: is 58 studies enough to be worth the fit at all, or does this need more annotation than exists? If the answer is 'not enough', that is itself the finding, and it says every per-label argument this project has made is unresolvable and should stop being made.
notes:
REFRAMED 2026-08-24 22:00Z, and the reframing raises it, by measuring what n=58 can and cannot do.

The per-label case is now closed NEGATIVE and should not be the justification. Even with all 58 studies
scorable, the per-label 95% halfwidths are 0.14-0.21 against a total across-label spread of 0.305. The
instrument would still not resolve a per-label ordering, so 'fit a member without the 58 so we can target
Lateral Meniscus' is not a reason to spend anything.

What n=58 CAN do is aggregate, and that is the open problem this project actually has. The competition
metric is the unweighted mean of twelve per-label AUCs. Averaging twelve labels over 58 studies is far
better conditioned than any one of them - not 12x better, since labels are correlated within a study, but
enough - and it would be measured against RADIOLOGIST truth rather than against LLM-read report labels.

That gives the one thing missing everywhere else in this repo: an offline number in the units the
leaderboard scores, computable without spending a submission slot.

Why that is worth more than it sounds. board_transfer (+1.82 board points per holdout point) is fitted
ENTIRELY on entries at or below 0.933, and our four best entries are one-sided and enter no pair. Every
decision at the top of our range is therefore an extrapolation, and the one direct probe we have says the
transfer SATURATES there: 0.8712 offline scored 0.933, then 0.8731 offline - our best ever - scored 0.932.
An offline ruler on the competition's own truth is how that question gets answered without burning five
slots a day discovering it.

So the pitch is not 'resolve the labels'. It is: we currently choose what to submit using a proxy truth
and a transfer constant fitted where we no longer live. This is the cheapest path to choosing on the real
truth. Still instrument work, still one member fit, but the thing it instruments is the submission
decision rather than a per-label build.

Sequencing note: this is CPU-cheap to specify and GPU-cheap to run (one fit), and it does not compete with
the raddino_dense warm start for the same slot of evidence - that one buys a member, this one buys a
ruler. If the card frees and only one can run, the warm start is the one with a measured floor under it
(mean +0.0035, 90th +0.0113 for a kill at 7 of 12); this one has no size estimate yet, which is itself an
argument for specifying it before running it.
PRICED 2026-08-24 22:02Z, and the aggregate pitch above is now REFUTED by a measurement the repo already contained. Read this note before acting on either of the two above it.

kneemri.evaluation.ruler_transfer already builds the instrument this bead proposes, for the PUBLISHED
members, and it runs on all 58 annotated studies - not 13. Its output tonight:

  58 annotated studies, 58 of them with a held-out prediction; 1000 paired resamples
    arms 1->2   report +0.0021 [-0.0087,+0.0142]   annot +0.0041 [-0.0072,+0.0153]   ratio +1.97 [-2.03,+3.31]
    arms 2->4   report +0.0043 [-0.0037,+0.0124]   annot +0.0054 [-0.0025,+0.0139]   ratio +1.27 [-1.24,+3.38]
    perm 0.40   report +0.0430 [+0.0183,+0.0692]   annot +0.0730 [+0.0501,+0.0996]   ratio +1.70 [+1.07,+3.48]

The delta halfwidth on the annotation ruler is about 0.011. So 58 studies CAN resolve a delta at this
house's own bar (0.015) and CANNOT resolve anything smaller. Both real arm deltas measured here - adding
members, the axis this project spends most of its slots on - are +0.002 to +0.005 and their intervals
span zero on BOTH rulers. The instrument is fit to gate 'is this a result at all', not to rank knobs.

That is the argument against fitting a member to unlock it, and it is quantitative: the offline gain first
place costs is +0.0082, which is BELOW this instrument's resolution. The ruler cannot see the thing the
goal is made of. Dropping P1 -> P3.

Two findings from the same run that are worth more than the bead and should not be lost with it:

1. The ratio is ABOVE 1 wherever it resolves. At a large perturbation it is +1.70 [+1.07, +3.48], an
   interval excluding 1, and the share sweep runs 0.97 / 0.98 / 1.17 / 1.15 as the perturbation grows.
   The report ruler UNDERSTATES deltas relative to radiologist truth rather than overstating them. If that
   holds for real gains, our offline numbers are a conservative floor on what the board sees - which is
   the same direction as board_transfer's +1.82 and an independent route to it.
2. It is a permutation perturbation, not a quality improvement, so read 1 as a direction and not as a
   transfer constant. Do not put 1.70 in a document; it would go stale exactly the way 4.67 did.

What is still worth doing, at P3, is the cheap half: this ran on published members and needed no GPU. If
a member is ever fitted without the 58 for another reason, run ruler_transfer on OUR arms too - the
comparison costs arithmetic. Do not fit one FOR this.

title: dissent_seat retracted the objective-axis family on a run killed at 8 of 12 epochs, so the family is closed on a FLOOR
description:
convergence_check (new, this session) reads dissent_seat_s2026 as TRUNCATED: 9 rows recorded, recipe asked 12, patience=0 so no stopper existed, and logs carry 'ARM FAILED dissent_seat (trainer exit 1)'. The ledger IS honest about this - its row says '0.8509 (killed at epoch 8 of 12)'. The defect is what was concluded anyway: that row 'Retracts the "loss axis buys seats" rule this table stated one row up', and interpretations/2026-08-24_the_goal_priced_against_the_inventory.md carries the consequence forward as 'loss / objective | seat-positive once, retracted by dissent_seat | closed'.

A killed run's score is a FLOOR. Under one_cycle the anneal never ran, so 0.8509 is not 'what this objective scores', it is 'at least what it scores with three twelfths of its schedule missing, none of it the fine-convergence part'. The -0.0069 vs band_dense that carries the retraction is smaller than the anneal is worth on every finished curve in the ledger (base_dense gains ~0.004 from e8 to its e8 peak region; cnx_own_recipe's whole shape is anneal).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: margin_seat read POSITIVE on the same axis. So the objective family has one positive finished reading and one negative killed reading, and it was closed on the killed one. With decode geometry, pooling, resolution, SSL-init and seat swaps all closed on finished evidence, an objective axis reopened by a harness defect is one of the few levers left that is not already measured at a tenth of what the goal costs.

NOT A CLAIM THAT THE OBJECTIVE WORKS. It is a claim that we do not know, and that we recorded that we did. Re-run dissent_seat to 12 epochs before the family stays closed; ~3h on the card, and it is gated behind the goal-sized threads (raddino warm start) rather than ahead of them.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-24, by measurement, against my own claim in this bead.

I wrote that dissent_seat's -0.0069 is 'smaller than the anneal is worth on every finished curve in the
ledger'. That is FALSE, and the check I built is what refutes it. Measured on all 54 CONVERGED 12-epoch
runs: for each, the gain from best-through-epoch-N to best-overall — what a run killed at N rows would
under-report by.

  killed at  7 rows: median +0.0011  mean +0.0035  90th +0.0113  max +0.0336  over noise floor 7/54
  killed at  9 rows: median +0.0000  mean +0.0006  90th +0.0023  max +0.0099  over noise floor 2/54
  killed at 10 rows: median +0.0000  mean +0.0001  90th +0.0004  max +0.0028  over noise floor 0/54

dissent_seat died at 9. On this corpus a kill at 9 costs a median of NOTHING and exceeds -0.0069 in 1 of
54 runs. So the missing anneal does not explain its -0.0069, and the quantitative case in this bead is
gone. Dropping P1 -> P3.

What survives is only the qualitative half, and it is weak on its own: a killed run's score is a bound
rather than a measurement, and margin_seat read positive on the same axis. That is a reason not to call
the objective family CLOSED on dissent_seat alone; it is not evidence the family pays. Re-run it only if
the axis is reached for another reason, never as a lead on its own.

What the same measurement makes STRONGER, and it is the finding worth keeping: truncation depth decides
whether truncation matters at all, and the three truncated runs split three ways rather than sharing one
verdict. vjepa_member died at 10 -> its 0.8343 is essentially its number, and re-running it buys a clean
exit code, not a score. raddino_dense died at 7 -> mean +0.0035 and a 90th percentile of +0.0113, so its
0.8137 is the one genuine floor of the three and the warm start is the one worth the 1.65h.

Note the shape of my own error: I priced a general claim ('a truncated run is a floor') at exactly one
depth and then quoted it at every depth. The check reports the depth. I did not read it.

title: Spawn retry budget is too small under training load
description: tests/unit/kneemri/process_table.py::test_process_table_read failed the pre-push gate with OSError: ps.EXE could not be started 3 times (0xC0000142 STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED). Not a code defect - Spawn's retry path fired correctly and exhausted its budget (retries=3, backoff_s=2.0, so ~4 s of patience) while the card was training and biohub shared the box. The failure mode Spawn was built for is exactly this one, so the fix is the budget, not the mechanism: raise retries/backoff, or make the backoff exponential, so a loaded box costs seconds instead of a rejected push. Costs a full 95 s test rerun every time it fires.

title: record_mix reports a NONEXISTENT record path as 'no holdout record, skipped'
description:
Hit 2026-08-24 while pricing cnx_dense into the greedy peak.

Passing --records with a wrong directory root (D:/data/processed instead of the real
D:/data/volumetric/mri/processed/rsna_knee_abnormality) printed one line per member:

  margin_seat_s2026.pt: no holdout record, skipped
  calib_span_s2026.pt: no holdout record, skipped
  ...

then died with 'ValueError: no member carries a holdout record'. Not one of those files EXISTS. The tool
reported a path that is not there as a member that is there but lacks its sidecar - two different faults
with the same message.

WHY IT MATTERS. The eventual crash is only luck: it fires because ALL the paths were wrong. Get ONE path
wrong out of nine and the tool silently scores an 8-member ensemble while the caller believes they measured
9, prints a number, and the missing member reads as 'skipped, had no record' rather than 'you typed the
wrong root'. That is a wrong denominator wearing a result's clothes - the exact class CLAUDE.md names, and
this session was one typo away from writing a seat verdict on it.

FIX: stat the path first. A path that does not exist is an error and should refuse immediately, naming the
path; 'no holdout record' should be reserved for a file that IS present and lacks the sidecar array.

Found while measuring knee-98y2.

title: dissent_seat: no seat, and it retracts the loss-axis rule
description: dissent_seat ran 2026-08-24 as the test margin_seat's ledger row asked for: is the seat a property of AUC-margin, or of moving the objective at all? Answer: of AUC-margin. title: Sequence head over depth: three consecutive RSNA winners use one, we use MRNet's 2018 max-pool
description:
Every member this project has ever trained reads a study as 2D slice -> per-slice features -> elementwise max over slices -> head. That aggregation is order-blind by construction: a finding continuous across five adjacent slices and a single bright artefact slice produce the same pooled vector. MRI is 3D and our reader is not.

WHAT THE FIELD DOES WITH 3D VOLUMES. Three consecutive RSNA Kaggle first places, all on 3D volumes, all the same shape - a 2D backbone per slice plus a SEQUENCE head over the slice axis:
  2022 cervical spine - EfficientNet-V2-S or ConvNeXt, 15 slices per vertebra, neighbour-concatenated multi-channel 2D inputs, LSTM.
  2023 abdominal trauma - CoaT Lite or EfficientNet-V2-S, 96 slices reduced to 32 adjacent-slice triplets, GRU.
  2024 lumbar spine - ConvNeXt-S or EfficientNet-V2-S, localize-then-classify, 2.5D multiview crops, bidirectional LSTM plus attention MIL.
Two axes, and we match neither: their trunk family is the one this repo starved 189:1 (knee-zfgn), and their aggregator is a sequence model where ours is amax.

MRNet, the canonical knee-MRI model, is AlexNet per slice plus max pooling across slices. Our aggregation is literally the 2018 baseline for this exact anatomy.

WE ALREADY BUILD THE INPUT AND THROW IT AWAY. depth_window.py sets NEIGHBOURS = (-1, 0, 1) - the same 2.5D neighbour triplet the 2023 winner feeds its GRU. We build the triplet, encode it, and then amax over the slice axis, at which point the ordering is gone. The information the winners' sequence heads consume is present in our tensors up to the pooling line.

WHERE IT PLUGS IN. SLICE_POOLINGS in kneemri/models/slice_pooling.py is already a strategy dict mapping a name to (per_slice, aggregator); ATTEND and DEPTH already register modules there. A GRU over the slice axis is a fifth entry and a new --slice-pooling choice, not a fork. per_slice=True, aggregator=<bidirectional GRU + pooled state>. The slice axis must reach the aggregator in ANATOMICAL ORDER for this to mean anything - assert that before believing any number, because a shuffled sequence would train to roughly the mean-pool result and read as a null.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER. The MIL benchmark at arXiv 2604.26807 finds simple MEAN pooling matches or outperforms recent MIL and 3D-CNN alternatives on 4 of 6 moderate-sized tasks at 25x lower cost, and that attention-MIL variants never provide an absolute AUROC gain above 0.025. That is a real argument against learned aggregation. It is not an argument for max: our pooling is max, and the cheap control this bead depends on is max->mean (separate bead).

PRICE: ~2.5 h card for one arm at the standing recipe with the pooling swapped. Plausible gain: this is the only axis in the stack that three independent winning solutions agree on and we have never tested, so a 1.5% mechanism is credible rather than hoped-for - unlike a knob. P(clears the 1.5% bar) 0.20-0.30; P(solo beats band_dense 0.8578 at all) 0.45. Ranked above knee-y59c because it is a mechanism change rather than a recipe correction, and the two are independent: a sequence head helps a ViT trunk and a CNN trunk alike.

PRE-REGISTER BEFORE RUNNING. Bands, the noise floor 0.0062, and the DENOMINATOR (solo vs band_dense on the same split), in an arm script under experiments/arms/, checked by arm_check.
CORRECTED 2026-08-24, HOURS AFTER FILING, BY THE LEDGER THIS BEAD SHOULD HAVE BEEN GREPPED AGAINST FIRST.
Two of the three claims above are false against measurements this repo already holds, and the correction
is what makes the remaining one worth keeping.

FALSE: "the aggregation is order-blind". DepthAttention has existed since knee-tqn and mixes each slice
with its through-plane neighbours (a depthwise conv of span 3) BEFORE the gate. It was run as depth_true
from the fixed snapshot: 0.8461, which is -0.0015 against attend_true and second-WORST of four operators.
Order-aware aggregation at the feature level is not untested; it is tested and slightly costly.

FALSE: "our aggregation is MRNet's max". StudyModel.over_depth takes an amax within depth REGIONS and
then a MEAN across the regions, and the four operators measured on one recipe span 0.0019 in total -
max 0.8457, order-aware gate 0.8461, unweighted mean 0.8473, trained gate 0.8476. Every gap is under a
third of the 0.0062 floor. The aggregation stage is saturated from three directions at once: more slices
-0.0001, more slots +0.0002, every combining rule within 0.0019.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF. The winners' pattern has two axes and only one of them is
closed here. The aggregator is closed. The TRUNK is not - it is knee-y59c's 189:1, and all three winning
solutions run convolutional or hybrid trunks. And both attend_true and depth_true wrote the same
conclusion independently: the limit is UPSTREAM, in what a single slice's feature vector contains. That
is an argument for the trunk arm and against another pooling arm, which is the opposite of what this
bead was filed to say.

STILL GENUINELY UNTOUCHED, per depth_true's own exclusion clause: a trunk that sees the VOLUME before any
per-slice feature exists. Feature-level through-plane mixing died; encoder-level 3D reading is a
different mechanism and has one run in this repo (V-JEPA, n=1, on the DINOv2 recipe - the other starved
family). That is where this bead's remaining value points, and it merges with knee-3ped and knee-ec0p
rather than standing as a sequence-head bead.

DEMOTED to P3, kept open only as the record of the external evidence and of the correction. Do not spend
a card slot on a slice-sequence head on the strength of the RSNA-winner pattern alone: this repo measured
that axis four ways and it spans 0.0019.

title: evaluation/ has 28 modules and no retirement policy — settled questions still pay quality tax
description:
RELAYED BY PEER SESSION sdlc-scaffold-b4, 2026-08-24. This is the one finding of the three with real substance, and it is a POLICY DECISION for the owner, not a refactor to schedule.

THE FINDING. kneemri/evaluation/ holds 28 modules. Many were built to settle ONE question, settled it, and then stayed: the question is closed in experiments/README.md or an interpretation, the module still costs a test mirror, a coverage share, a shape-contract, a ruff pass and a line in graph.json on every commit forever. vote.py's own docstring says the axis it explores is 'closed instead of re-openable' and the family 'stays because the question recurs' — which is the right call THERE and cannot be the right call 28 times.

THE TENSION, which is why this needs a decision rather than a cleanup. Deleting a diagnostic destroys the ability to re-ask its question cheaply, and this project has already been burned by re-litigating settled numbers (2026-08-13: two P0s filed against results the repo had already measured). A module that answers a closed question is also the artifact that PROVES it closed. So 'delete when settled' is wrong.

THE THREE POLICIES WORTH CHOOSING BETWEEN:
  A. KEEP EVERYTHING. Status quo. Cost is a slowly rising per-commit gate tax and a package nobody can hold in their head.
  B. RETIRE TO A NAMED SHELF. A settled diagnostic moves to evaluation/settled/ with a header naming the question, the answer, and the ledger entry — excluded from the test mirror and coverage floor, still runnable, still readable, no longer paying. Reversible in one git mv.
  C. RETIRE TO GIT HISTORY. Delete, with the ledger entry carrying the commit hash that holds the module. Cheapest steady state, highest cost to re-ask.

RECOMMENDATION IF ASKED: B. It preserves the proof, which is the thing this repo actually needs, and stops the tax. But this is a taste call about what the portfolio should look like and it belongs to the owner.

NOTHING SHOULD BE MOVED UNTIL A POLICY IS PICKED. A one-off tidy of evaluation/ without a rule is how the bucket re-forms.

title: core/ is a leftovers bucket: seven platform-plumbing modules filed by nothing
description:
RELAYED BY PEER SESSION sdlc-scaffold-b4, 2026-08-24, from an architecture audit of this repo. Filed because an audit finding that is not written down is a finding paid for and thrown away; NOT claimed, and not scheduled ahead of board work.

THE FINDING. core/ holds sleep_policy.py (98), wakelock.py (36), mounts.py (73), native_path.py (107), bootstrap.py (59), and kneemri/ holds process_table.py (144), spawn.py (77). None of these is data, model, or evaluation. They are host-platform plumbing — power state, Windows path shapes, drive mounts, process liveness — and they sit at package roots because nothing named them. 594 lines, seven modules, no cohesive owner. This is the shape the global rules forbid for TYPES (never bucket by kind) applied to modules: a package root accumulating whatever had no home.

THE PROPOSED MOVE: one platform/ package, in core/ (the kernel imports none of the others, and this is the most kernel-ish material in the repo). core/platform/{power,paths,mounts,process}.py or one module each, moved verbatim.

WHAT IT BUYS, HONESTLY: findability and a name that refuses the NEXT stray module. It does not fix a bug. No defect in this repo has been traced to these modules' location, and the move is import-rewrites over code whose behaviour does not change — a class of refactor whose own risk is small but nonzero and whose payoff is zero board points.

WHAT IT COSTS: ~7 module moves, ~15 import rewrites, a docs/architecture/graph.json regeneration, and an import-linter contract update. Roughly an hour, card-free, so it fits in a gap between arms. It must NOT displace a queued arm.

DO NOT DO THIS WHILE A SUBMISSION PATH IS BEING EDITED. mounts.py and native_path.py are on the Kaggle kit path; a rename that lands mid-kit is a slot spent on an ImportError. Gate it behind kit_check and mount_check both green.

title: Negative-correlation training: buy ambiguity without paying member error
description:
THE EMPTY CELL. Sort every member this project has built by (solo strength, distance from the seated pool) and three of the four quadrants are occupied:
  strong + near   — every DINOv2 member. Seats saturate at seven.
  distant + weak  — vjepa_warm 0.8337, nearest seated neighbour 0.059 beyond the seated spread. Seat value +0.0002.
  distant + broken— mae_matched, nearest neighbour 0.4333. Seat value -0.0041.
  STRONG + DISTANT— has never existed here.
knee-053z asked for distant-and-strong and the repo answered the distance clause by a mile and missed the solo clause by 0.017. Distance is necessary and demonstrably not sufficient.

WHY SWAPPING THE TRUNK CANNOT FILL IT, already measured three ways and closed 2026-08-21: v3base_dense seat value -0.0007 / -0.0005 (a tie), cnx_dense -0.0042 (a CNN trunk, outside the transformer family entirely), against base_dense's one paying seat. 'A different inductive bias is not a different error structure.' The reason is visible in what those arms hold FIXED: identical slice sampling, identical 2D-slice-then-pool architecture, identical five-level targets, identical BCE objective, identical head. Only the trunk weights move. The error structure is set by the shared pipeline, and a trunk swap cannot reach it.

THE THEORY THAT SAYS WHAT TO DO INSTEAD. Ambiguity decomposition: ensemble error = mean member error - ambiguity. Every arm above moves ONE term. vjepa raised ambiguity and raised mean error at least as much (net +0.0002). A trunk swap left ambiguity flat (net -0.0007). The quadrant is empty because nothing here has ever optimised BOTH terms at once — and the decomposition says that is exactly what an ensemble member's objective should do.

Negative Correlation Learning does it directly: a correlation penalty in the member's own loss, so it is trained to be accurate AND to disagree with the existing pool, jointly rather than in sequence. See 'Generalized Negative Correlation Learning for Deep Ensembling' (arXiv 2011.02952) for the deep-ensemble formulation, and 'Composing Diverse Ensembles of CNNs by Penalization' (MDPI Mathematics 11(23):4730) for the penalty-term form.

WHY THIS REPO CAN BUILD IT CHEAPLY, which is the real argument for doing it now. The plumbing already exists and points the wrong way. DistilledObjective (kneemri/training/objective.py:271) already loads the pool's per-study predictions through teacher_targets.py and adds a term that pulls the student TOWARD the ensemble's ordering. A negative-correlation term is the same loader, the same batch alignment, and the opposite sign: penalise the residual correlation between this member's errors and the pool's, with the BCE term holding accuracy. It is a fourth sibling in the Objective hierarchy beside the AUC-margin one (knee-bdhb), not a fork.

WHAT IT PREDICTS, so it is falsifiable. A member whose SOLO score is at or slightly below its control (the penalty costs some fit) but whose nearest-seated-neighbour correlation drops well below the seated spread's floor, and whose SEAT VALUE clears +0.0015 where vjepa_warm's +0.0002 did not. The refutation is a member that is distant and weak AGAIN — same quadrant as vjepa, which would say ambiguity cannot be bought at this pool's operating point by any means and would close the seat axis for good rather than just for trunks.

READ SEAT VALUE, NOT SOLO SCORE. base_dense is the standing proof that solo does not predict seat: it lost its own control outside the floor and then took the board. This arm is expected to lose solo. Judging it on solo would kill it for doing exactly what it is designed to do.

COST. One 12-epoch arm, ~76 min of card, plus a record_mix seat measurement against the champion roster. Zero submission slots. The pool predictions it needs are already on disk (teacher_fold0.npz, and 87 holdout npz files).

DEPENDS ON: knee-bdhb landing first is NOT required, but the two compose - an AUC-margin member that is also decorrelated is the strong-and-distant construction stated in one sentence.
notes:
PRICE: ~45 min card (teacher cache already SPENT and on disk from knee-1xsu), ZERO submission
slots. P(the member seats at >= +0.0015, the board-resolvable bar) ~= 0.30. Plausible gain if it
seats: +0.002 to +0.005 seat, which is +0.004 to +0.010 board at the 1.92 transfer slope — below the
1.5% bar on its own, and it is priced as a SEAT rather than as a member: seats compose against the
original baseline and the champion is seven of them.

WHY 0.30 AND NOT LOWER, given the encoder axis closed three ways. Those three arms were all attempts
to buy ambiguity as a SIDE EFFECT — pick a different trunk, then measure afterwards whether the errors
happened to decorrelate. None of them put the ensemble into the member's loss. That does not make this
likely; it makes it a genuinely untried mechanism rather than a fourth run of a settled one, and the
quadrant it targets (strong AND distant) has never been occupied by anything here.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE SLOT EVEN ON A NULL. It is an INSTRUMENT for the whole seat axis. If a member
trained explicitly to be right where the pool is wrong still lands distant-and-weak, then ambiguity
cannot be bought at this pool's operating point by any means, and the seat axis closes for good rather
than only for trunks — which retires a line this project has now spent four arms on. That is the
justification for the run, not the +0.004.

ARM: experiments/arms/dissent_seat.sh, control band_dense = 0.8578, one variable (the pair mass; total
ranking strength held at 1.0). Code landed: DecorrelatedObjective + Objective.pairs(emphasis=...),
--dissent-weight, RunSetup guards refusing composition with --rank-weight / --distill-weight /
--pair-memory, and the Request/Landed field so the flag is asserted to have LANDED.
Interpretation: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-24_architecture_diversity_is_closed_and_the_empty_cell_is_strong_and_distant.md

P(clears 1.5% on its own) ~= 0.05 — a single seat has never moved the board that far here; the 1.5%
is reached by seats composing, and the number this arm is priced against is the +0.0015 seat bar.

ANSWERED 2026-08-24 BY ITS OWN ARM, and left open for a day. This bead's NOTES already name experiments/arms/dissent_seat.sh as its arm with the code landed (DecorrelatedObjective, --dissent-weight). That arm RAN: solo 0.8509 (-0.0069 vs band_dense), greedy pick 38th of 66, and the ensemble peak with it in the pool 0.8731 — UNCHANGED. See experiments/README.md, 'dissent_seat — the objective axis is NOT a seat lever'.

It did not land in the pre-registered refutation quadrant (distant and weak); it landed somewhere the pre-registration did not anticipate and which is worse for the mechanism. The per-label table is the finding: nine of twelve labels DOWN against its control, widest swing -0.0307, and every swing in the same direction. Set beside margin_seat, whose swings ran +0.0272 MCL and -0.0546 Lateral Meniscus, dissent_seat reads the SAME WAY as its control, slightly worse everywhere. A member that is uniformly a little worse is not distant — it is just worse, and a greedy selecting on complementarity has no reason to reach for it. Putting the ensemble into the member's loss did not buy ambiguity; it bought a small uniform accuracy loss.

WHAT THAT DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE. It closes THIS construction of negative correlation at this pool's operating point — the pair-mass reweighting form. It does not license the stronger claim the bead pre-registered ('ambiguity cannot be bought by any means'), because the arm was stopped at epoch 8 of 12 on a 6/7/8 plateau, and because a penalty on the RANKING pairs is not the same object as a penalty on the error CORRELATION that arXiv 2011.02952 states. That distinction is worth one paragraph in an interpretation, not another 45 minutes of card while a genuinely untried axis (v3lora_dense) is unrun.

RE-PRICED P0 -> P3. The P0 rested on 'a genuinely untried mechanism'; it had been tried before the bead was read.
CLOSED — the mechanism RAN and is in the ledger as dissent_seat (experiments/README.md:345, 411). --dissent-weight was plumbed and the arm went on the card 2026-08-24 with the teacher gated to the fold-0 twins, exactly as this bead specified.

  0.8509, killed at epoch 8 of 12 = -0.0069 vs band_dense
  NO SEAT: greedy picks it 38th of 66 and the ensemble peak is unchanged
  nine of twelve labels down, widest swing -0.0307

AND THE READING IS THE REFUTATION THIS BEAD PRE-REGISTERED, not a null. The prediction was 'solo at or slightly below control, but nearest-seated correlation well below the seated floor'. What happened instead is that it reads the SAME as its control and slightly worse — where margin_seat, the other objective-axis member, at least read DIFFERENTLY. A member trained explicitly to spend capacity where the pool is wrong did not end up distant. That is the stated refutation clause: ambiguity cannot be bought at this pool's operating point by moving the objective, and it closes the objective axis as a seat lever rather than leaving it open.

This bead sat at P3/open with a PRICE note quoting P=0.30 and '~45 min card' for an arm that had already run and failed. That is the failure mode CLAUDE.md names — beads lag the ledger, and bd search will not find a result recorded only in experiments/README.md. The price note is void; the entry above is the record.

knee-uco3 independently removes the exit anyway: the marginal seventh seat reads inert at 0.937 no matter what fills it.
REFUTED 2026-09-03 on a matched seat read, zero card. The run died at e9 of 12 but was NOT truncated in any meaningful sense: it plateaued at e6 (0.8509) and held flat through e7 (0.8501) and e8 (0.8503), while the control's own e9-e11 declined. So 0.8509 is the recipe's number, not a floor, and finishing the budget was killed as a 76-min arm.

THE SEAT, WHICH IS WHAT THE ARM WAS BOUGHT FOR AND NOBODY HAD READ. member_curve, fold 0, the five champion holdout twins plus a sixth seat, LogitAverage:
  6th = dissent_seat_s2026 (solo 0.8509)  ->  0.8694
  6th = holdannot_s2026    (solo 0.8506)  ->  0.8701
Solo held to 0.0003, so the seats are matched on member strength and differ only in construction. The dissent seat is -0.0007 against an ordinary pool member. It buys nothing.

This is the arm's own SECOND pre-registered branch: solo down by more than the 0.0062 floor (-0.0069 peak-vs-peak against band_dense 0.8578) with the seat not up. Label-anchored pair emphasis did not hold the member up, and the emphasis did not reach the error structure either.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT RULE OUT: the operating point was never swept (dissent-weight 1.0, one teacher). But the third branch required the neighbour UNCHANGED with the solo intact, and the solo is down, so the operating point is not what this reading indicts. The STRONG-AND-DISTANT quadrant stays empty and this construction is not the way into it.

title: Rank-distillation from the fold-0 ensemble: one student, three exits
description:
OWNER'S DESIGN, and the unification is his. I had split this into three bets - distil-and-replace (efficiency), soft-targets-as-denser-supervision, and distilled-student-as-a-diverse-member. He collapsed them correctly: A and C are the SAME ARTEFACT with two exits chosen by the measurement rather than in advance, and B is not a separate training at all, it is an extra LOSS TERM in that one run. So: one student, one arm, three outcomes.

  EXIT A - student reaches teacher parity: ship it alone. Seven forward passes become one, ~1h of T4 becomes ~9min. That is the Efficiency Prize, which the seven-member champion loses by construction.
  EXIT C - student short of parity but structurally distant: seat it as a member. The ledger's own rule is "buy a seat on the AXIS, not on the count and not on the solo score", and an encoder-family-distant member is more distant than anything ever seated (twin 0.930, recipe-distant 0.931, objective-distant 0.931, pixel-distant 0.932).
  EXIT B is the loss, and it runs either way.

THE LOSS FORM IS DECIDED BY THE METRIC, NOT BY THE DISTILLATION LITERATURE. Standard KD is KL on temperature-softened probabilities. That is wrong here and the repo already says why: ensemble.py:6, "Calibration is worth nothing, so no thresholding, no temperature, no Platt scaling." The metric is twelve rank-based AUCs, so a KL spends student capacity matching probability VALUES the metric discards, and temperature is a monotone transform that cannot change the target's ranking at all. The term should be PAIRWISE ORDER against the teacher, and RankedObjective.pairs(above, below) already computes exactly that mass - it is handed labels today and would be handed teacher scores instead. Same tested code, different supervision.

WHY THIS IS NEW SUPERVISION AND NOT A RESTATEMENT OF THE LABELS - the mechanism that makes it worth card time. Under binary labels a pair carries order information ONLY if it is a positive against a negative; same-class pairs are unordered and teach nothing. Under teacher scores EVERY pair is ordered, including positive-vs-positive and negative-vs-negative. Effusion is positive in roughly 60% of studies so labels order about 48% of its pairs; Fracture is roughly 7% so labels order about 13% of its pairs; the teacher orders 100% of both. That is genuinely more supervision on the SAME corpus, with no external data and no licence answer - which is what makes it worth running at all, because knee-y3pv's audit closed with data volume as the only remaining axis above the bar and knee-ombx is blocked on a licence call nobody has made.

PRE-REGISTERED, and it is a PER-LABEL clause rather than a mean. The gain must CONCENTRATE on the labels with the most skewed positive rate, because that is where binary pairs are scarcest and where the teacher adds the most orderings. Fracture should gain most, Effusion least. If the mean moves but the per-label pattern is flat or inverted, the mechanism claimed here is NOT what moved it, and the arm is not read as a confirmation of it.

TEACHER CONTAMINATION, and it decides which members teach. Six of the seven champion members trained on all 4,406 studies with --fold -1, so their predictions on training studies are MEMORISED rather than generalised, and distilling on those would teach the student the teacher's memorisation. The teacher is therefore the FOLD-0 TWINS, all already on disk: band_dense_s2026, calib_span_s2026, grade_ladder_s2026, base_dense_s2026, lr4e-5_ws_s2026, through_dense_s2026. A weaker teacher (~0.869 joint offline against the champion's 0.937 board) in exchange for a holdout that is clean for teacher AND student, which is the only way this arm produces a number anyone can read.

COST-TIERED, because a DINOv3 student confounds two variables at once - if it fails, that is distillation failing OR v3 failing, and the arm cannot say which.
  ARM 1, about 45 min card: DINOv2-small student, same family as the teachers. Zero architecture confound. Answers only "does rank-distillation transfer at all".
  ARM 2, gated on arm 1: DINOv3 student. The diversity play, both exits live. It also re-tests a dead investment rather than assuming it dead: every v3 arm lost on hard labels (-0.0377, -0.0400, -0.0445) but README:313 records frozen-v3-plus-LoRA beating fine-tuned v3 by +0.0160, annotated "recipe was damaging v3". A weak-transfer architecture failing on sparse hard labels and recovering on dense soft ones is the textbook distillation case, and three failed arms are evidence about the RECIPE, not about the encoder.

PRICE: teacher predictions over the 3,526 train studies for six members is about 36 min card, cached once and reused by every later arm; student train about 45 min; roughly 1.5 h card total and ZERO submission slots for arm 1. Plausible gain if it seats: +0.001 to +0.004 board, which is BELOW the 1.5% bar on its own. The honest case is the chain and the second exit, not this number.
design:
PLUMBING - the smallest change that fits the strategy pattern already there.

1. TEACHER TARGETS over the 3,526 fold-0 TRAIN studies. PredictionCache and HoldoutPredictions.cached() already do exactly this for the 909-study holdout, keyed by cache.key(reading.file, window, reading.precision). Extend that key/slab to cover the train split rather than writing a second path - a second path is how the two-constants bug in backbone.py happened.

2. DistilledObjective(RankedObjective), adding "weight * self.pairs(batch, teacher)" in __call__ and reporting its weight through settings(), because settings() is the account landed.py reads. The repo has paid four times for a value recorded in a config while the consumer read a constant, so the flag must be ASSERTED landed in the checkpoint, not assumed.

3. Teacher scores thread through Predicted alongside logits/scores/weights - Predicted is already the carrier for everything the objective needs, so no new type and no new module.

4. --distill-weight on TrainOptions, defaulting 0.0, so every existing arm stays bit-identical and the smoke can prove it.

PRE-REGISTERED BANDS for arm 1, against teacher joint offline ~0.869, best solo member 0.8598 (small_batch6_s2026), and the SAME recipe with --distill-weight 0 as its own control:
  >= 0.869    student MATCHES the six-member teacher. Exit A live and the Efficiency Prize becomes real. Extraordinary; would need a re-run before it is believed.
  0.860-0.869 beats every single member this project has ever trained. Seats almost certainly; measure seat value against the champion pool.
  0.850-0.860 distillation transfers but does not beat the best solo. The per-label clause decides whether the claimed mechanism is what moved it; seat value decides whether it ships.
  at or below its own --distill-weight 0 control, per-label FLAT: the term added nothing the labels did not already carry at this operating point. Arm 2 is NOT licensed, and the finding is about THIS operating point, not about distillation.

FALSIFIER, stated before the run so it cannot be renegotiated after: student at or below its own matched zero-weight control refutes transfer here. That kills this USE of rank-distillation at this alpha and this teacher - it does not kill soft targets, a stronger teacher, or a different weight, and the record must say so.
notes:
ARITHMETIC CORRECTION, made before the run rather than after, and it SHARPENS the pre-registered clause rather than weakening it.

The description argues the teacher adds orderings that binary labels cannot express, and prices that with a binary assumption. The targets are NOT binary. grades.py:3 - the reader emits FIVE levels, 0.08 / 0.28 / 0.68 / 0.82 / 0.94 - and Objective.pairs already reads separation as a clamped DIFFERENCE of those values, so a pair separates whenever the two studies land on different levels, not merely on opposite sides of a threshold. My 48% figure for Effusion was computed off the binary assumption and is wrong.

Redone against the real level structure, using unordered pair mass = sum of squared level shares:
  Fracture, ~93% of studies at level 0: unordered ~0.87, so labels order ~13% of pairs. Teacher orders 100%. About 7.7x more ordered pairs.
  Effusion, ~60% positive spread over four non-zero levels: unordered ~0.25, so labels ALREADY order ~75%. Teacher orders 100%. About 1.3x more.

So the spread in what the teacher adds is roughly SIX-FOLD across labels and it is ordered by rarity. The pre-registered concentration clause therefore gets sharper, not softer: the per-label gains should rank with label rarity, and Effusion should be close to flat because its labels already order three quarters of its pairs. A uniform gain across the twelve now REFUTES the stated mechanism rather than merely failing to confirm it - the teacher cannot add 7.7x the orderings on Fracture and 1.3x on Effusion and produce an even lift.

The exact level histogram per label is not yet read; the shares above are from the known positive rates. The arm's readout should print the real per-label level histogram so the predicted ranking is scored against measured pair mass rather than against my estimate of it.
2026-08-24 11:05Z — code landed (7eb7937), gates green (1228 passed), pushed. Teacher cache firing now: six fold-0 _s2026 twins over 3,498 training studies, backgrounded with a 2.5h timeout, sharing the card with biohub's joint_confusor_synth_v2 (17.5/32.6 GB, claim to 15:30Z) — contention stretches the wall-clock but a cache is not a measurement, so it costs nothing but time.

Smoke path is clear with NO extra code: ReportFolds.assign hashes the REPORT TEXT per study, so fold membership is independent of how many studies the cache holds. A --studies 60 --fold 0 smoke therefore trains on a SUBSET of the full fold-0 training split, and every one of its studies has a teacher row. Smoke as: --studies 60 --epochs 1 --fold 0 --distill-weight 0.3 --teacher-targets teacher_fold0.npz.
PRICE: 1.5 h of card (teacher cache 36 min, now SPENT and reusable; student ~45 min) and ZERO submission slots. P(clears the 1.5% bar on its own) ~= 0.15 — a seat swap has historically bought +0.001 to +0.004 board, which is below the bar. The run is priced as an INSTRUMENT plus a chain: it retires the question of whether the five-level label ceiling is what caps a single member (nothing else in the ledger can answer that), and its 0.860-0.869 band is what LICENSES the DINOv3 student, where the gain is architectural diversity rather than a knob. The teacher file is the reusable half — a second student costs 45 min, not 1.5 h.

2026-08-24 12:02Z — smoke GREEN (arm_check --only distill_pairs --smoke, 60 studies, one epoch): the teacher loads, aligns and the term descends.

CARD INCIDENT 11:12Z, recorded because it cost a peer's run: I launched the teacher pass while biohub's CARD_CLAIM was live to 15:30Z, reasoning that ~15 GB looked free. Both processes died together with no traceback at 30.2/32.6 GB. experiments/lib.sh:256 already records the physics — the settled 20-slice recipe derives 28.3 GB, so a co-tenant of ANY size denies it. Letter sent to biohub's inbox. Rule taken: a peer CARD_CLAIM is exclusive unless its own text says otherwise; card_check cannot see it, so it is judgement, not a gate.
2026-08-24: FIRST RUN VOID, number must not be read. It ran without --backbone-lr and so took the trainer default 8e-6 (kneemri/training/trainer.py:66) while its control band_dense holds 4e-5 — a fifth of the control's backbone rate, against the arm's own docstring claiming 'byte-for-byte'. Killed at epoch 8 (0.8423, mean -0.0138 vs control 0.8578). run_comparison's config-diff line is what caught it; nothing else would have. Per-label profile: every label down, worst on the FOCAL structures (focal -0.0178, regional -0.0082), mildest on the big fluid collections (Effusion -0.0007, Contusion +0.0007) — the signature of a starved backbone, NOT the rarity ordering the pair-mass mechanism predicts and not a flat null. The distill term itself DID land (diff carried distill_weight=0.3 plus the teacher path), so the mechanism fired into a crippled recipe. Bands remain UNREAD. Fixed and re-launched 13:19Z, expect ~14:35Z. Void artifacts (holdout npz, metrics, partial, pt) deleted so they cannot be misread.
distill_pairs read and priced 2026-08-24: mean 0.8594 vs control 0.8578 (+0.0016, inside the 0.0062 floor); seat value -0.0003 against greedy7_v1; distance nearest 0.9159 vs the roster's own worst nearest 0.8893 — it is a TWIN of a seated member, which is why the seat is negative. No card. Per-label table + the unreadable-rule finding are in experiments/README.md.
SHARPER, from the farseat post-mortem: mount_check --live did NOT catch this. It read 'kneemri-farseat: ok - declares all of ...' at 01:41Z and the run died anyway. unpushed() only compares the members a kernel NAMES against the live set, but MemberPackage.__init__ refuses a manifest whose files it cannot ALL find — so one dropped .pt takes down kernels that never name it. The per-kernel question is the wrong question for a package-level refusal.

FIXED: MountCheck.absent() compares the whole manifest against the live listing and is checked BEFORE the per-kernel loop, because a manifest the live dataset cannot satisfy invalidates every verdict that loop prints. Non-zero exit. Unit test test_absent covers the case the old test could not express: a member absent live and named by NO kernel.

Verified on the real defect - the new check printed 'live dataset does not hold 1 of the 40 members the manifest names (small_accum_s2026)' on the same package where the old code said farseat was ok.
CORRECTION 2026-08-25: the preceding note about mount_check/MemberPackage/small_accum_s2026 was appended to this bead in error. It belongs to knee-6ds2 (the members-dataset dropped-file P0) and has been recorded there. Nothing in it concerns rank-distillation; ignore it when reading this issue.
2026-08-25 02:10Z — MISFILED NOTE. The paragraph above beginning 'SHARPER, from the farseat post-mortem: mount_check --live did NOT catch this' and the 'FIXED: MountCheck.absent()' paragraph belong to knee-6ds2 (kaggle dataset version landing with a file missing), NOT to rank-distillation. They were appended here by mistake. Read them on knee-6ds2, where the same account is now filed correctly. Nothing in them is about this bead's arm.

STATUS OF THIS BEAD, since the notes above bury it: ARM 1 IS RUN AND READ. distill_pairs 0.8594 vs its matched --distill-weight 0 control 0.8578 = +0.0016, inside the 0.0062 holdout floor; seat value -0.0003 against greedy7_v1; nearest-neighbour 0.9159, i.e. a TWIN of a seated member, which is why the seat is negative. Arm 1's pre-registered licence for ARM 2 (the DINOv3 student) was the 0.860-0.869 band. It read 0.8594 and MISSED it, so arm 2 is NOT licensed and must not be armed on momentum. What arm 1 does NOT kill, per its own falsifier clause: soft targets in general, a stronger teacher, or a different weight — only this alpha with this fold-0-twin teacher.
ARM 1 RAN and is in the ledger as distill_pairs (experiments/README.md, 'rank distillation is a TWIN of a seated member'). mean 0.8594 vs control 0.8578 = +0.0016, inside the 0.0062 floor; seat value -0.0003; nearest-neighbour correlation 0.9159, closer to a seated member than any seated member is to its own nearest. Exit A dead (0.8594 short of the teacher's 0.869), exit C dead (a twin cannot pay a rank average for an ordering it already holds).

WHY THAT WAS PREDICTABLE IN HINDSIGHT, and it is the reframe arm 2 needs: a DINOv2 student distilled from six DINOv2 teachers shares trunk, sampling, architecture, targets and head with its teachers. Every degree of freedom that could produce a distant error structure was held fixed. The twin is what the setup asked for. Arm 2's DINOv3 student is the one configuration that breaks the family, which is exactly why it was cost-tiered second — that part of the design stands.

BUT knee-uco3 HAS SINCE WEAKENED BOTH EXITS, which is why this drops P0 -> P3. dark6 reads 0.937 with six all-data members and nothing else, so the marginal seventh seat is worth zero board points no matter what fills it. Exit C therefore no longer has a board reading available even on a success; it would have to be argued through a pool REBUILD rather than an added seat. Exit A (parity, the Efficiency Prize) survives untouched, and is now the only exit worth card time on this bead.

The per-label harness defect stands and is unfixed: paired per-label floor half-widths run to +/-0.0284, so eleven of twelve deltas were unreadable and the pre-registered rarity rule could not be executed. Any successor states its rule on an axis its ruler can resolve.

title: The eighth seat is +0.0005 offline across 63 candidates -- flat, NOT exhausted (~+0.002 board at the measured 4.67x)
description:
Measured 2026-08-22, card-free, over every same-split holdout record on disk (70 of 79; the tool refuses the 9 smokes/off-fold rather than averaging across a split boundary). Write-up: interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-22_the_pool_is_exhausted.md. Logs: logs/greedy_all.log, logs/roster_seats.log.

ROSTER OF 7 = 0.8695. BEST EIGHTH SEAT OUT OF 63 CANDIDATES = +0.0005 (small_batch6_s2026). Zero of 63 clear +0.0015, the threshold under which this project has never seen the board tick. That is stronger than any previous closure because previous ones priced one candidate at a time; this prices the whole pool at once.

COUNT IS A PLATEAU, NOT A PEAK, and two recorded claims are superseded -- both were taken on smaller pools. record_mix's own docstring says 'count saturates at four'; 2026-08-19_subset_search_is_spent.md put the peak at 6-7 over 22 members. Over 70: greedy 4 = 0.8703, 5 = 0.8710, peak 8-10 = 0.8717, 22 = 0.8711, 70 = 0.8606. Five through twenty-two spans 0.0007. Four is 0.0014 BELOW the plateau.

THIS RECONCILES THE BOARD WITH THE HOLDOUT. Best board entry per count: 4->0.930, 5->0.931, 6->0.931, 7->0.932, monotone +0.002. Offline 4->8 is +0.0014, which at the measured 2.4x transfer predicts +0.0034 against a measured +0.002. Same sign, same order, two independent rulers. Consequence: 'twenty members like pilkwang' is dead -- the curve is flat 8 to 22 and falling by 70, and 135 checkpoints were already on disk so this was never a training question.

IT HARDENS knee-053z FROM n=1 TO n=63. vjepa_warm, the most distant member this project has produced, prices +0.0001 -- below small_batch6 (+0.0005), crop80_span (+0.0004) and aug_long (+0.0004), none of them remarkable on any diversity axis. Distance does not predict seat, now on a second ruler across 63 candidates.

THE ONE LIVE THREAD, and it is NOT yet a slot. Greedy-8 reads 0.8717 vs the shipped roster's 0.8695: +0.0022, five of eight members unseated, the largest offline delta in the pool, and +0.005 on the board at 2.4x. But greedy is an argmax over the same 909 studies that score it, and 2026-08-19 hit exactly this shape (+0.0017 greedy peak) and correctly declined to ship. The seat scan and greedy disagree in a way that says which to trust: no single addition beats +0.0005, yet greedy claims 4x that for a wholesale replacement chosen by argmax on its own ruler. BLOCKED ON knee-7d1's forward test, in flight as gradeswap (submitted 08:07Z, kernel COMPLETE, score pending). Do not fire a greedy-8 entry before gradeswap reads.
notes:
The 2026-08-22 seat scan's conclusion is corrected: 63 candidates at <=+0.0005 offline is FLAT, not EXHAUSTED. Comparing an offline seat delta to the +0.0015 board threshold skips the measured compression (knee-7d1, median +4.67 board points per holdout point) and understates the pool by nearly 5x. gradeswap is the counterexample: +0.0001 offline, +0.001 board. Best eighth seat +0.0005 offline maps to ~+0.002 board, which the board CAN resolve. The honest statement is that the binary seat ruler's whole live range across 63 candidates is a third of its own stated resolution, so it cannot say WHICH candidate carries the tick — that is a ruler limit, not an empty pool.
MEASURED 2026-08-23 on the champion seven itself (logs/champion_seven.log), and the count axis is saturated -- read off the marginal curve rather than off any seat ruler:

  4 members: 0.8675  +0.0015 over 3
  5 members: 0.8684  +0.0009 over 4
  6 members: 0.8690  +0.0006 over 5
  7 members: 0.8694  +0.0004 over 6

The increments are halving. An eighth is worth about +0.0002 by extrapolation of a curve that has held for four consecutive steps, which at knee-7d1's 4.67x is +0.001 board -- under one tick, and that is the OPTIMISTIC read because it assumes the eighth is as good as the seventh.

Two independent confirmations in the same run. The best SUBSET at each size peaks below seven: best-4 0.8696, best-6 0.8695, best-7 0.8694. The seventh member is negative offline on its own roster. And the per-label oracle sits at 0.8643 against the flat average's 0.8694, headroom -0.0051, which is knee-vjmw's result reproduced on a different pool.

The board agrees and always did: sevenplane 0.932, gradeswap 0.933, accumseat 0.933 -- three single-member displacements of the same seven, spread 0.001.

This does not need a better seat RULER. The three retired rulers were blamed for the flatness; the curve says the flatness is in the POOL. Downgrading from P1 to P3: not closed, because an eighth member from an axis no current member occupies (a 3D trunk, external data) is a different question from an eighth member drawn from the 63 candidates already fitted -- and it is the AXIS that is untested, not the count.

What this redirects to: every ensemble-side lever is now measured flat -- combination rule (knee-769f, closed today), member count (here), per-label selection (knee-vjmw), seat exchange (three board entries). The remaining levers are better MEMBERS and more DATA, which is where the card is now pointed (knee-g8nb running, knee-rpkw queued).

title: Re-read the per-label ORACLE with the distant family in: does distance buy under selection what it fails to buy under the mean?
description:
2026-08-17's oracle (interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-17_the-oracle-ceiling-is-the-average.md) closed per-label member weighting: oracle 0.8590 against a plain average of 0.8588, headroom +0.0002, two orders under the floor. Its reasoning was 'the members do not disagree per label in a way any selection rule could exploit' -- measured over SEVEN MEMBERS OF ONE FAMILY, nearest-neighbour spread 0.88-0.91.

vjepa_warm changes the input to that measurement and nothing else. Nearest seated neighbour 0.8210, 0.059 clear of anything on the roster, and a working model rather than a broken one (mae_matched's 0.4333 is the broken signature). The doc names this exact re-test itself: 'a member that fails on different studies would move the average itself, not the headroom above it.'

THE ARM: member_curve over the seated seven PLUS vjepa_warm_s2026.pt, fold 0, split seed 2026.

PRE-REGISTER. Headroom stays inside ~0.001 -> per-label selection is closed for DISTANT families too, not just same-family ones, and vjepa_warm's distant-and-weak verdict hardens into a general statement about the distance ruler. Headroom opens past the 0.0062 floor -> distance buys under SELECTION what it does not buy under the MEAN, the combiner rather than the member is what failed, and per-label selection becomes a design-sized lever. It is an upper bound by construction, so it can only license or retire; it can never itself be submitted.

COST AND WHY IT IS QUEUED. Attempted on CPU 2026-08-22 09:22Z and killed at 09:23: member_curve keeps its own prediction cache, seat_value had NOT warmed it, so it recomputes all eight members from pixels -- ~6-8 h on CPU with a ViT-L in the set, against ~20 min on the card. Run it on the first free GPU window; do not re-run it on CPU. The card is biohub's as of 09:15Z for a celltrack re-pool fit plus full train.
notes:
DOWNGRADED P2->P3 2026-08-23. The 2026-08-23 oracle re-read (six cached champion members, split-half honest estimator) puts per-label headroom at MINUS 0.0052 and shows the honest top-k curve rising monotonically to the flat average - and crucially it shows WHY, which the 2026-08-17 measurement did not: the members DO differ significantly per label, and averaging's variance reduction simply beats specialisation's bias gain. That mechanism does not care how distant the added member is - a distant member widens the per-label gaps, and widening them does not flip which side of the trade wins.

So this bead's pre-registered 'headroom opens past the floor' branch now has a mechanism predicting it will not. Not closing it: predicting is not measuring, and vjepa_warm's predictions are the one input genuinely absent from holdout_predictions/ (verified 2026-08-23 by reading the cache sidecars - 28 checkpoints cached, vjepa_warm not among them). Run it only if the card is otherwise idle; it can no longer justify displacing anything.

title: Wakelock reports 'held' but the machine still idle-slept mid-run (3.7h lost, 24.5h cumulative)
description:
On 2026-08-21 the machine entered sleep at 16:45 UTC with 'Sleep Reason: System Idle' (Kernel-Power event 42) while band_dense_llrd was mid-epoch-11. The arm resumed and finished at 20:27:57 UTC, so ~3.7h of card was lost. This is the SAME shape as knee-wyzj, which cost 20.8h across three runs and is what core/wakelock.py was built to stop.

WHAT IS RULED OUT, measured not assumed:
* NOT Modern Standby. powercfg /a reports Standby (S3) available and S0 Low Power Idle NOT supported, so the well-known 'S0 ignores SetThreadExecutionState' explanation does not apply here.
* NOT a nested-release. core/wakelock.py's release is SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS), which is absolute rather than refcounted, so an inner wakelock exiting would clear an outer hold — but fitting.py:164 and holdout_backfill.py:181 are separate entrypoints and do not nest.
* NOT a silently-failed request AT THE CALL. StaysAwake.hold() checks the return value (0 = failure) and the run logged 'wakelock: held', so SetThreadExecutionState returned nonzero.
* NOT a policy override. powercfg /requestsoverride is empty in all three sections.
* NOT a stalled queue, which is what it looks like from the logs: queue_check read 'live' and '0/1 started' throughout and was correct both times; the watcher fired 56s after the arm's sentinel landed on resume.

WHAT IS NOT RULED OUT, and the decisive measurement:
The AC standby timeout is 0x2a30 = 10800s = 3h (note: core/sleep_policy.py's docstring still says 7200s, read 2026-08-18 — stale). A nonzero return from SetThreadExecutionState says the CALL succeeded; it does not say the OS is holding a system-required request for the process. Those are distinguishable in one command, which needs elevation:

    powercfg /requests

Run it ELEVATED while a trainer is running and has logged 'wakelock: held'. If the SYSTEM section names the python.exe process, the request reached the OS and something is overriding it. If SYSTEM is empty, the request never landed despite the nonzero return, and StaysAwake.hold()'s witness is checking the wrong thing — it would need to verify the REQUEST exists, not that the call returned.

DO NOT 'fix' this by raising the global standby timeout. core/sleep_policy.py argues against exactly that: a global power-scheme edit is a machine-wide setting standing in for a property of one process, and it keeps applying long after the run that needed it. Also do not add a periodic re-assert keepalive before the mechanism is known — that is a tweak that moves the symptom without a named cause.

COST: this is not a knob. Two incidents, 24.5h of wall-clock, on a project whose stated constraint is wall-clock.
notes:
MITIGATED AT THE OS LAYER, 2026-08-21 21:07 UTC — and the mechanism question is now permanently unobservable, which is worth stating plainly.

biohub ran 'powercfg /change standby-timeout-ac 0' and 'monitor-timeout-ac 0' on the shared box. I did
not take their word for it: 'powercfg /q SCHEME_CURRENT SUB_SLEEP STANDBYIDLE' reads
'Current AC Power Setting Index: 0x00000000' (never), DC unchanged at 0x258. This box is a desktop, so
it is always on AC.

WHAT THIS CLOSES: the practical cost. 24.5 hours of wall-clock lost across four runs to mid-epoch
suspends on a project whose stated constraint is wall-clock. No unattended run is exposed to the idle
timer any more, mine or theirs.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, and cannot now: whether Wakelock's 'held' was ever a real system-required
request. The open question was that a nonzero SetThreadExecutionState return proves the CALL succeeded,
not that the OS is holding the request, and only elevated 'powercfg /requests' during a live run
distinguishes them. With the idle timer disabled, that experiment can never fire again on this box - the
negative control is gone. So core/sleep_policy.py's docstring warning stays accurate and stays in place:
'held' is still not proof, it is just no longer load-bearing here. Anyone porting Wakelock to a machine
with a live idle timer inherits the unresolved question, not a fix.

Downgrading from P1. Not closing: the code claim is unverified, only the exposure is gone.

title: Focal loss + per-branch deep supervision: CoPAS's smallest component, and the one our live severity chapter already half-owns
description:
CoPAS child (D) of knee-pq8u. Their objective is L = alpha * sum_over_branches sum_over_12_labels BCE + sum_over_12_labels FL, alpha = 0.3: every intermediate branch is supervised with BCE against the same twelve labels, and the fused head additionally carries a focal term.

TWO SEPARABLE CLAIMS, AND ONLY ONE IS NEW HERE.
(1) FOCAL on the fused head. This is the same family as the live severity-weighting chapter (grade_ladder, band_dense and the severity ladder arms) - a per-example reweighting that spends capacity on the hard, rare positives. We are already measuring this axis under our own parameterisation. Do NOT open a second front on it; read grade_ladder first and let that chapter own the loss-shape question.
(2) PER-BRANCH DEEP SUPERVISION. This one we have never run. Our slots feed an aggregator and only the fused output sees a gradient from the labels; CoPAS puts a full twelve-label BCE on each branch at alpha = 0.3 so every plane learns to predict all twelve on its own before fusion. That is a different mechanism from a loss reweighting: it is a gradient-path change, and it is the standard fix for an aggregator that collapses onto one strong member.

WHY IT MIGHT MATTER MORE THAN ITS SIZE SUGGESTS. Nine slot-aggregation axes have landed inside the 0.0062 floor (knee-jk3). One reading of that is that the aggregator never had to work because the fused gradient is happy as soon as the best slot is good. Deep supervision removes that escape.

PRICE. Their own ablation puts the whole loss/CRM tail at +0.013, UNDER our 1.5% bar - so this is not sold as an improvement. It is an INSTRUMENT: it tests whether the aggregation axis is dead or merely untrained, which is the question gating knee-vigl, knee-jucq and the rest of the slot chapter. ~2h dev (an auxiliary head per slot plus one alpha), one ~40 min arm warm-started off band_dense. Ratio is what justifies it, not size.

GATE. After grade_ladder is read, so the loss chapter's verdict is in hand and claim (1) is not re-run by accident.

title: Label error is 20.5% and it is an OVER-CALL on GRADED findings, not a language problem
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 by kneemri.labels.reader_agreement against the 58 radiologist-annotated studies — the only ground truth in this project that is not the reader's own output. Log: logs/reader_agreement.log.

THE NUMBER: 140 of 684 cells wrong over 57 studies. 20.5% label error. Thirteen times the 1.5% bar, and larger than every modelling lever measured to date COMBINED.

THE SHAPE, which is what makes it actionable:
- 108 of 140 errors are FALSE POSITIVES. The reader over-calls. Missed: 32 (UNK 24, NO 8).
- Net over-call by finding: Contusion +18, Effusion +16, ACL +9, MCL +9, Medial OA +7, Lateral Meniscus +7, Medial Meniscus +6, Lateral OA +5, Baker's +4, PF OA +4, Fracture +2. Synovitis is the only under-caller at -11.
- Worst per-call agreement: Contusion 44.4%, MCL 50.0%, Lateral OA 56.2%.

LANGUAGE IS REFUTED AS THE CAUSE. English 66.7% against non-English 64.2%: +0.025 [-0.076, +0.126] bootstrapped over studies. Flat. This kills branch (a) of knee-mxj — the multilingual-encoder premise — on direct measurement rather than argument.

THE CAUSE IS THE GRADE. Positive calls on reports that GRADE the finding agree 63.2%; plain statements agree 77.8%. -0.146 [-0.277, +0.005]. The reader promotes mild / grade-1 findings to YES where the radiologist does not. That is a THRESHOLD defect in the reader, and it is fixable without re-reading a single report if the grade tier is already recorded — which it is, as the <target>__verdict column (YES 1 / YES 2 / YES 3).

STATE THE DENOMINATOR: 58 studies, 1.32% of the corpus, all-or-nothing annotated. Cells inside a study share a report and a radiologist so they are not independent draws; the intervals above are bootstrapped over STUDIES and are about twice a cell-wise width. This is a small ground truth and every number here inherits that.

THE CAVEAT THAT GATES ACTING ON IT: the leaderboard's ground truth is not ours. A reader agreeing better with OUR radiologist need not agree better with THEIRS. Circumstantial support that it would — champion scores 0.931 board against 0.869 holdout; a board built from the same noisy process should score about the same, not 0.06 higher, and cleaner board labels would explain the gap. That is an INFERENCE, not a measurement, and must not be written up as one.

FIRST ARM, and it is free (no API, no re-read): the YES 1 tier is already isolated in the verdict column. Demote or down-weight it and retrain. Note calib_span (-0.0020) is NOT this experiment — it rescaled all soft targets; this moves one tier. Note also grade_ladder, on the card 2026-08-21, subtracts thresholds inside the loss and is the closest existing probe of the same tier; read it first.

ACCEPTANCE TEST for any replacement reader is this module, run before and after — it says so in its own docstring.
notes:
DEMOTED P1->P3 the same hour it was filed, by 2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot.md, which I had not read when I filed it — the rule I keep breaking.

The pilot prices this whole axis at +0.006, AT the 0.0062 noise floor, by the metric's own arithmetic (unweighted mean of twelve AUCs; 58% of contested cells are Fracture+Contusion = 17% of cells; a GENEROUS fix of Fracture 0.80->0.85 and Contusion +0.02 gives (0.05+0.02)/12 = +0.006). And correcting label VALUES has been tried once and lost: calib_span -0.0020 with every pre-registered clause inverting.

The 20.5% here is NOT a contradiction of the pilot's 93%, and must not be written up as one. They are different rulers and the pilot says so itself: the pilot measures conformance to the RULEBOOK (a re-read can fix that), reader_agreement measures conformance to the IMAGE (a re-read cannot). The reports themselves disagree with the radiologist about a third of the time on positive calls. Since the leaderboard is scored against report-derived labels too, that third is the same noise on both sides of the comparison and is not recoverable by any reader.

WHAT SURVIVES AND IS STILL WORTH DOING, both free:
1. The graded-vs-plain split (63.2% vs 77.8%, -0.146 [-0.277, +0.005]) is a NEW observation not in the pilot, and it names the reader's threshold on mild findings as the mechanism behind the over-call. It is an interval that touches zero, so it is directional. grade_ladder (on the card 2026-08-21) is the closest existing probe.
2. The language refutation is now measured twice from two directions and can be treated as settled: reader_agreement +0.025 [-0.076, +0.126] English vs non-English, and the pilot's 2.7% vs 4.9% localised to ONE sentence shape rather than a language deficit.

The rulebook fix the pilot recommends (unmentioned = UNK, never NO; and a stable rule for what a normal-bone sentence denies) stays worth doing if a re-read ever happens for another reason. It is not worth a pass on its own.

title: Training-regimen axis is closed by mechanism: holdout selection already absorbs the decline
description:
Do not arm longer schedules, mixup, cutmix, stochastic depth, or any further regulariser as a SCORE arm without first defeating this argument.

Chain:
- Every arm saves the best epoch by holdout, so the peak-to-finish decline (band_dense_long -0.0182) costs the shipped model NOTHING. We ship the peak.
- Therefore a regulariser can only pay by raising the PEAK.
- aug_long ran exactly that test: intensity aug on the 24-epoch schedule. The regulariser demonstrably FIRED (train loss higher at every epoch past 4, 0.463 vs 0.454) and the peak moved later (6 -> 9) but the peak VALUE fell, 0.8511 vs 0.8587 (-0.0076).
- weight_average (EMA) is the same verdict from the other side: 0.8460, +0.0003 vs wsfold0_e6, flat, because a holdout already picks the epoch an EMA would have smoothed toward. Ledger README:409.

Read: the model is not memorisation-limited. It peaks at epoch 6-9 and no schedule or regulariser lifts that peak. That is a SIGNAL ceiling.

What this does NOT rule out: a regulariser that changes what the model can REPRESENT rather than how hard the fit is (the peak could move if the input or the target changes). It rules out the training regimen as a free lever on the current input/target pair.

Where the ceiling then lives: not the encoder (v3base_dense -0.0005, cnx_dense -0.0042, DINOv2-large +0.0021 at 3.7x cost), not decode/head (four levers all under a seventh of the 0.0062 floor), not crop/FOV (closed on availability 2026-08-21). Remaining: label accuracy (knee-dtk says 6 of 12 labels are label-bottlenecked) and self-supervision. Both held on an explicit go-ahead.

title: Synovitis is 84.2% UNK and Fracture 56.4% — the biggest supervision hole in the corpus, and it does NOT predict our scores
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-20, zero GPU, over ALL 4,406 corpus rows. Every one of the twelve columns is populated
on every row, so these are rates over the corpus, not over a subset that happened to parse.

  label              UNK%    NO%   YES%
  Synovitis          84.2    2.6   13.2
  Fracture           56.4   36.5    7.1
  Lateral OA         33.1   42.3   24.7
  Medial OA          25.5   37.7   36.7
  Contusion          20.8   49.8   29.4
  PF OA              18.5   36.3   45.2
  Lateral Meniscus   10.0   64.5   25.4
  Effusion            9.9   29.6   60.5
  MCL                 9.8   72.8   17.4
  ACL                 8.1   64.1   27.8
  Medial Meniscus     5.7   41.1   53.3
  (Baker's Cyst absent on a column-name mismatch, not a missing measurement.)

WHERE THIS CAME FROM. The user challenged the label-contest pilot's headline — MCL is our worst label
and had 0/100 contested cells — with "that's unknown, if our worst labels were just not found in the
reports". Agreement on ABSENCE is not evidence of correctness, and it is failure mode 2 of that very
pilot. So it was measured rather than argued.

THE OBJECTION FAILS FOR MCL AND ACL, at the sharpest point. They are the two labels with zero contested
cells and they carry the LOWEST UNK rates of all eleven, 9.8% and 8.1%. MCL's 72.8% NO rate is the
highest in the corpus: the reports address the medial collateral ligament and call it intact. The reader
agreeing with that is agreeing with a real statement, not with a silence. So the pilot's conclusion
holds — supervision is not what bounds MCL.

IT RELOCATES AND LANDS HARDER. 3,710 studies carry no synovitis information and 2,485 carry no fracture
information. Over half the corpus is silent on fracture. That is a supervision hole far larger than the
pilot's 4.0% contest rate, and a contest cannot see it — a contest only scores cells where the reader
made a call.

AND IT DECLINES TO EXPLAIN OUR SCORES, which is the part worth keeping. If missingness capped
performance the ordering would show it. It inverts:
  Synovitis  worst coverage in the corpus (84.2% UNK)  ->  0.873, mid-pack, above seven other labels
  MCL        third-best coverage (9.8% UNK)            ->  0.788-0.793, worst of the twelve
So the hole is real, it is much bigger than the contest rate, and it is NOT the current bound.

MECHANISM FOR WHY IT COSTS LESS THAN IT LOOKS. Under --weight-floor (shipped in RECIPE) an UNK cell is
not dropped: it trains at value 0.28, weight 0.2875 — a soft negative. Synovitis's 13.2% positives are
learnable against a quiet negative background, which is what 0.873 on 84% missing data looks like.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY PRICE IT, and it is not a re-read — the reports genuinely do not contain the
information, so a better reader cannot recover it:
  (a) the AUC ceiling per label given its UNK share, computed on the 57 image-read annotations, which
      are the only cells where the truth is known independently of the report;
  (b) whether the soft-negative treatment of UNK is better or worse than dropping those cells, which is
      a matched arm and NOT one this bead should assume the sign of;
  (c) whether the ~0.87 Synovitis number survives on the annotation ruler or is an artefact of scoring
      against a holdout that inherits the same 84.2% silence — this is the one that could invert the
      whole reading above, and it is the FIRST thing to run.

Recorded in interpretations/kneemri/2026-08-20_label_contest_pilot.md, section "The objection that
'0 contested' might just mean 'never mentioned' — measured".

P3 rather than higher: it is a ceiling question, not a floor question, and (c) is cheap enough that it
should gate any further work here.
notes:
ITEM (c) RUN 2026-08-20, and it CORRECTS THE EVIDENCE IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION while leaving the conclusion standing. Tool already existed: kneemri.evaluation.supervision_gap, on report_labels_v2.csv, 58 annotated studies / 696 cells.

THE TWO POINTS I ARGUED FROM BOTH FLIP ON THE ANNOTATION RULER:
  Synovitis  report holdout 0.873  ->  annotation ruler 0.7378  (2nd worst of twelve)
